portal.name: usefulapi
portal.tagline: Hosted MCP servers for the tools you already use.

servers.name: Ably
servers.description: MCP server for Ably — channel history, presence, occupancy, stats, publish, and app management.

tools.name: ably_get_channel_history
tools.title: Get channel message history
tools.description: Retrieve historical messages published to a channel, newest-first by default. REST: GET /channels/{channel}/messages.

tools.name: ably_get_presence
tools.title: Get channel presence set
tools.description: List the members currently present on a channel (who is online now). REST: GET /channels/{channel}/presence.

tools.name: ably_get_presence_history
tools.title: Get channel presence history
tools.description: Retrieve historical presence events (enter/leave/update) for a channel. REST: GET /channels/{channel}/presence/history.

tools.name: ably_get_channel_details
tools.title: Get channel details / occupancy
tools.description: Get status and occupancy metrics for a single channel (connections, publishers, subscribers, presence members). REST: GET /channels/{channel}.

tools.name: ably_list_channels
tools.title: List active channels
tools.description: Enumerate channels that are currently active in the app. Requires the API key to have the 'channel-metadata' capability. REST: GET /channels.

tools.name: ably_get_stats
tools.title: Get app statistics
tools.description: Retrieve message/connection/channel usage statistics for the app tied to the API key, bucketed by time. REST: GET /stats.

tools.name: ably_get_service_time
tools.title: Get Ably service time
tools.description: Return the current Ably service time in ms since epoch. Useful for aligning start/end windows to the server clock. REST: GET /time.

tools.name: ably_publish_message
tools.title: Publish a message to a channel
tools.description: WRITE: publish a message to a channel. Every connected subscriber receives it in real time. This is a real, outward-facing side effect — confirm the channel and payload before calling. REST: POST /channels/{channel}/messages.

tools.name: ably_whoami
tools.title: Get control token / account info
tools.description: Return details about the configured control token: the account and user it belongs to and its capabilities. Good first call to confirm control-plane access. Control API: GET /me.

tools.name: ably_list_apps
tools.title: List Ably apps
tools.description: List all apps in the account (id, name, status, tls-only). Account id is resolved automatically from the control token when ABLY_ACCOUNT_ID is unset. Control API: GET /accounts/{account_id}/apps.

tools.name: ably_list_keys
tools.title: List an app's API keys
tools.description: List the API keys for an app, including their capabilities (but not the full secret). Control API: GET /apps/{app_id}/keys.

tools.name: ably_list_namespaces
tools.title: List an app's channel namespaces
tools.description: List the channel namespaces (channel-rule prefixes) configured for an app, e.g. persistence and push settings. Control API: GET /apps/{app_id}/namespaces.

tools.name: ably_list_queues
tools.title: List an app's queues
tools.description: List the Ably Queues (AMQP/STOMP message queues) provisioned for an app, with their state and messaging stats. Control API: GET /apps/{app_id}/queues.

tools.name: ably_list_rules
tools.title: List an app's integration rules
tools.description: List the integration rules (reactor rules: webhooks, AWS Lambda/SQS/Kinesis, Kafka, Pulsar, etc.) configured for an app. Control API: GET /apps/{app_id}/rules.

tools.name: ably_get_account_stats
tools.title: Get account-level statistics
tools.description: Retrieve aggregated usage statistics across the whole account, bucketed by time. Account id is resolved from the control token when ABLY_ACCOUNT_ID is unset. Control API: GET /accounts/{account_id}/stats.

tools.name: ably_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: ably_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Ably tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: ably_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Ably (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: ably_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Ably Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run ably_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find your **API key** in Ably → **your app → API Keys** (full `appId.keyId:keySecret`). The optional **Control API token** lives under **Account → Control API tokens** and powers the management tools (apps, keys, namespaces, queues, rules, account stats). Your credentials are used only to call Ably on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

examples: Which of our live channels have people connected right now?
Show the last 20 messages sent on our orders channel today.
How many messages did our app handle each day this past week?
Show the last 20 messages sent on our test channel today.

servers.name: Accelo
servers.description: Manage Accelo companies, contacts, jobs, tasks, tickets and time.

tools.name: accelo_list_companies
tools.title: List companies
tools.description: List companies (client organizations). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/companies. Supports _page/_limit/_fields/_filters/_search. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_get_company
tools.title: Get a company
tools.description: Fetch a single company (client organization). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/companies/{id}. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts (people at companies). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/contacts. Supports _page/_limit/_fields/_filters/_search. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: Fetch a single contact (a person). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/contacts/{id}. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_list_jobs
tools.title: List jobs (projects)
tools.description: List jobs — Accelo "jobs" are projects. Accelo API: GET /api/v0/jobs. Supports _page/_limit/_fields/_filters/_search. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_get_job
tools.title: Get a job (project)
tools.description: Fetch a single job (project). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/jobs/{id}. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List tasks (units of work logged against an object such as a job or company). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/tasks. Supports _page/_limit/_fields/_filters/_search. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_get_task
tools.title: Get a task
tools.description: Fetch a single task. Accelo API: GET /api/v0/tasks/{id}. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_list_activities
tools.title: List activities
tools.description: List activities — notes, emails, calls, and meetings logged against objects. Accelo API: GET /api/v0/activities. Supports _page/_limit/_fields/_filters/_search. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_get_activity
tools.title: Get an activity
tools.description: Fetch a single activity (note/email/call/meeting). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/activities/{id}. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices. Accelo API: GET /api/v0/invoices. Supports _page/_limit/_fields/_filters/_search. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_get_invoice
tools.title: Get an invoice
tools.description: Fetch a single invoice. Accelo API: GET /api/v0/invoices/{id}. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_list_prospects
tools.title: List prospects (sales)
tools.description: List prospects — sales opportunities in the pipeline. Accelo API: GET /api/v0/prospects. Supports _page/_limit/_fields/_filters/_search. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_get_prospect
tools.title: Get a prospect (sale)
tools.description: Fetch a single prospect (sales opportunity). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/prospects/{id}. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_list_staff
tools.title: List staff
tools.description: List staff (Accelo users in your deployment). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/staff. Supports _page/_limit/_fields/_filters/_search. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_get_staff
tools.title: Get a staff member
tools.description: Fetch a single staff member. Accelo API: GET /api/v0/staff/{id}. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_list_issues
tools.title: List issues (tickets)
tools.description: List issues — support/service tickets. Accelo API: GET /api/v0/issues. Supports _page/_limit/_fields/_filters/_search. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_get_issue
tools.title: Get an issue (ticket)
tools.description: Fetch a single issue (support/service ticket). Accelo API: GET /api/v0/issues/{id}. Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_request
tools.title: Raw read request
tools.description: Power-user escape hatch: GET any Accelo API path not wrapped by a dedicated tool. READ-ONLY — only GET is allowed. Pass the FULL API path after the host, starting with a slash, INCLUDING any query string, e.g. "/api/v0/companies?_limit=1&_filters=status(1)" or "/api/v0/tasks/123". Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_create_company
tools.title: Create a company
tools.description: MUTATES Accelo data: creates a new company (client organization). Accelo API: POST /api/v0/companies (form-encoded). Returns { meta, response } with the created company. (Accelo has no separate delete tool here; to UPDATE, POST to /api/v0/companies/{id}.)

tools.name: accelo_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: MUTATES Accelo data: creates a new contact (a person). Accelo API: POST /api/v0/contacts (form-encoded). NOTE: a contact's company affiliation is set separately via an affiliation (POST /api/v0/contacts/{id}/affiliations), not on creation. Returns { meta, response } with the created contact.

tools.name: accelo_create_task
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: MUTATES Accelo data: creates a new task. Accelo tasks are always logged AGAINST an object (a job, company, issue, etc.), so against_type + against_id are required. Accelo API: POST /api/v0/tasks (form-encoded). Returns { meta, response }.

tools.name: accelo_create_activity
tools.title: Create an activity (log a note/email/call)
tools.description: MUTATES Accelo data: logs an activity (a note, email, call, or meeting) against an object. This is the highest-value safe write — e.g. add a note/comment to a job or company. against_type + against_id say what it is logged against (required). Accelo API: POST /api/v0/activities (form-encoded). Returns { meta, response }.

Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: accelo_cancel_subscription

tools.description: Cancel the caller's Accelo Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). tools.name: allquiet_get_incident_markdown
tools.title: Get incident as markdown
tools.description: Get a markdown rendering of a single incident by its id (useful for pasting into a doc or chat). All Quiet: GET /v1/incident/search/{incidentId}/markdown.

tools.name: allquiet_who_is_on_call
tools.title: Who is on call
tools.description: Get who is currently (or at a given point in time) on call, optionally filtered by team/user. All Quiet: GET /v1/on-call.

tools.name: allquiet_on_call_report
tools.title: On-call report
tools.description: Get a summed on-call duration report over a time window, optionally filtered by user/team/escalation tier. All Quiet: GET /v1/on-call-report/sum.

tools.name: allquiet_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: Search/list teams, optionally filtered by display name. All Quiet: GET /v1/team/search/list.

tools.name: allquiet_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: Search/list users, optionally filtered by email or display name. All Quiet: GET /v1/user/search/list.

tools.name: allquiet_list_on_call_overrides
tools.title: List on-call overrides
tools.description: Search/list on-call overrides for a given user. All Quiet: GET /v1/on-call-override/search/list.

tools.name: allquiet_create_incident
tools.title: Create incident
tools.description: Creates a new incident on the LIVE account (may trigger alerting/paging). `status` and `severity` are free-form strings the API validates against your account's configuration — common `severity` values include "Warning", "Minor", "Major", "Critical", and `status` reflects the incident lifecycle (e.g. "Open"/"Resolved"); confirm the valid values for your account before calling. All Quiet: POST /v1/incident.

tools.name: allquiet_update_incident
tools.title: Update incident
tools.description: Applies an operation to an existing LIVE incident: change its severity and/or append an intent (a lifecycle action such as acknowledge/resolve/reopen/snooze — a status transition). At least one of `changeSeverity` or `appendIntent` is required. All Quiet: PATCH /v1/incident/{incidentId}.

tools.name: allquiet_create_on_call_override
tools.title: Create on-call override
tools.description: Creates an on-call override for a user on the LIVE account (temporarily changes who is on call). `type` is a free-form override kind and `start`/`end` govern the override window — confirm the valid `type` values for your account. All Quiet: POST /v1/on-call-override.

tools.name: allquiet_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: allquiet_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the All Quiet tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: allquiet_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on All Quiet (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: allquiet_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's All Quiet Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run allquiet_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find it in All Quiet → **Settings → API keys** (the Public API requires a Pro or Enterprise plan). Your key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Who is on call for the support team right now?
List the open incidents from the past 7 days, most serious first.
How many hours was the support team on call last week in total?
Who has an on-call override scheduled for Jane Smith?

servers.name: Amberflo
servers.description: Query and manage Amberflo metering & billing: customers, meters, usage, plans, invoices, prepaid.

tools.name: amberflo_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List all customers registered in your Amberflo account (id, name, email, traits, enabled). Good first call to discover customer ids. API: GET /customers/.

tools.name: amberflo_get_customer
tools.title: Get a customer
tools.description: Fetch a single customer by its Amberflo customerId. API: GET /customers/?customerId=<id>.

tools.name: amberflo_list_meters

tools.name: amberflo_get_usage

tools.description: Query aggregated usage for a single meter over a time range, optionally grouped/filtered. API: POST /usage/.

tools.name: amberflo_get_all_usage
tools.title: Get all usage
tools.description: Get total usage across all meters over a time range, optionally grouped by customer or filtered to one customer. API: GET /usage/all.

tools.name: amberflo_explain_usage
tools.title: Explain usage
tools.description: Explain/drill into the raw meter events behind a meter's usage over a time range — useful to debug why a number looks off. API: POST /usage/explain.

tools.name: amberflo_get_customer_plan
tools.title: Get customer plan
tools.description: Get a customer's LATEST assigned product plan (pricing). API: GET /payments/pricing/amberflo/customer-pricing?CustomerId=<id>.

tools.name: amberflo_list_customer_plan_history

tools.description: List the full history of product plans assigned to a customer over time. API: GET /payments/pricing/amberflo/customer-pricing/list?CustomerId=<id>.

tools.name: amberflo_list_customer_invoices

tools.name: amberflo_get_customer_invoice

tools.name: amberflo_list_prepaid_orders

tools.name: amberflo_assign_customer_plan

tools.name: amberflo_ingest_usage

servers.name: Anvil
servers.description: Hosted MCP server for Anvil — fill & generate PDFs and run Etch e-signature packets for AI agents.

tools.name: anvil_current_user
tools.title: Current Anvil user
tools.description: Get the authenticated Anvil user (from the API key) and the organizations they belong to (eid, name, slug). Good first call to discover org slugs/eids for other tools. GraphQL query: currentUser.

tools.name: anvil_get_organization
tools.title: Get organization
tools.description: Fetch an Anvil organization and its PDF templates (casts) and workflows (welds). Provide either its slug or its eid (at least one is required). GraphQL query: organization.

tools.name: anvil_get_cast
tools.title: Get cast (PDF template)
tools.description: Fetch a cast — an Anvil PDF template — by its eid: title, version number, and whether it is a template. Use the returned eid as the cast_eid for anvil_fill_pdf. GraphQL query: cast.

tools.name: anvil_get_etch_packet
tools.title: Get Etch e-signature packet
tools.description: Fetch an Etch e-signature packet by eid: its status, details URL, document group, and every signer (eid, aliasId, name, email, status, routing order). Use this to check signature progress. GraphQL query: etchPacket.

tools.name: anvil_get_weld
tools.title: Get weld (workflow)
tools.description: Fetch a weld — an Anvil workflow — by eid, including its forges (the individual form steps: eid, name, slug). GraphQL query: weld.

tools.name: anvil_get_weld_data
tools.title: Get weld data (workflow submission)
tools.description: Fetch a weldData record — a single submission to a weld (workflow) — by eid: completion state, test flag, and creation time. GraphQL query: weldData.

tools.name: anvil_fill_pdf
tools.title: Fill a PDF template
tools.description: Fill an Anvil PDF template (cast) with data and return the finished PDF as base64. REST: POST /fill/{castEid}.pdf. Returns { filename, byteLength, pdfBase64 }. The `data` object's keys are the template's field aliases.

tools.name: anvil_generate_pdf
tools.title: Generate a PDF from HTML or Markdown
tools.description: Generate a brand-new PDF from HTML or Markdown and return it as base64. REST: POST /generate-pdf. For type=html, pass data = { html, css? }. For type=markdown, pass data = [ { label, content }, ... ]. Returns { filename, byteLength, pdfBase64 }.

tools.name: anvil_create_etch_packet
tools.title: Create Etch e-signature packet
tools.description: Create an Etch e-signature packet (documents + signers). GraphQL mutation: createEtchPacket. IMPORTANT: isDraft defaults to true (a safe draft that sends nothing). Setting isDraft=false with real signers SENDS signature-request emails to those signers. Use isTest=true while developing.

tools.name: anvil_generate_etch_sign_url
tools.title: Generate Etch signing URL
tools.description: Generate a one-time embedded signing URL for a specific signer in an Etch packet (for iframe/redirect signing flows). GraphQL mutation: generateEtchSignURL. Returns { url }.

tools.name: anvil_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)

Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: anvil_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Anvil (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: anvil_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription

servers.name: Api2Pdf
servers.description: MCP server for Api2Pdf — generate PDFs & images from HTML, URLs or office files; merge, barcodes.

tools.name: api2pdf_html_to_pdf
tools.title: HTML to PDF (Chrome)
tools.description: Render an HTML string to a PDF using the headless-Chrome engine. Returns a { FileUrl } link (valid ~24h) by default. Great for invoices, reports, and letters produced as HTML. BILLED per document. Api2Pdf API: POST /chrome/pdf/html.

tools.name: api2pdf_url_to_pdf
tools.title: URL to PDF (Chrome)
tools.description: Fetch a web page by URL and render it to a PDF using headless Chrome. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). Use extraHTTPHeaders to pass auth for a protected page. BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /chrome/pdf/url.

tools.name: api2pdf_markdown_to_pdf
tools.title: Markdown to PDF (Chrome)
tools.description: Render a Markdown string to a PDF using headless Chrome. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /chrome/pdf/markdown.

tools.name: api2pdf_html_to_image
tools.title: HTML to image (Chrome)
tools.description: Render an HTML string to an image using headless Chrome. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h) by default, or base64 bytes with output_binary:true. BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /chrome/image/html.

tools.name: api2pdf_url_to_image
tools.title: URL to image / screenshot (Chrome)
tools.description: Take a screenshot of a live web page by URL using headless Chrome. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /chrome/image/url.

tools.name: api2pdf_wkhtml_to_pdf
tools.title: HTML to PDF (wkhtmltopdf)
tools.description: Render an HTML string to a PDF using the wkhtmltopdf engine — an alternate to Chrome that supports a table of contents (pass enableToc / tocOptions inside `options`). Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /wkhtml/pdf/html.

tools.name: api2pdf_office_to_pdf
tools.title: Office document to PDF (LibreOffice)
tools.description: Convert an office document (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, ODT, and many more) at a URL to a PDF using LibreOffice. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /libreoffice/any-to-pdf.

tools.name: api2pdf_merge_pdfs
tools.title: Merge PDFs (PDFSharp)
tools.description: Merge several existing PDFs (given as URLs, in order) into a single PDF. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /pdfsharp/merge.

tools.name: api2pdf_compress_pdf
tools.title: Compress PDF (PDFSharp)
tools.description: Compress an existing PDF (given as a URL) to reduce its file size. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /pdfsharp/compress.

tools.name: api2pdf_extract_pages
tools.title: Extract PDF pages (PDFSharp)
tools.description: Extract a range of pages from an existing PDF (given as a URL) into a new PDF. `start`/`end` are 0-based page indices; omit `end` to extract a single page. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /pdfsharp/extract-pages.

tools.name: api2pdf_add_password
tools.title: Password-protect PDF (PDFSharp)
tools.description: Encrypt an existing PDF (given as a URL) with a user password (required to open) and an optional owner password (controls permissions). Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /pdfsharp/password.

tools.name: api2pdf_convert_to_markdown
tools.title: Convert document to Markdown (MarkItDown)
tools.description: Convert a document or file (given as a URL — PDF, Office docs, and more) to Markdown text via MarkItDown. Great for feeding a document's contents back to an agent. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h). BILLED. Api2Pdf API: POST /markitdown.

tools.name: api2pdf_generate_barcode
tools.title: Generate barcode / QR code (Zebra)
tools.description: Generate a barcode or QR code image. `format` is the symbology (e.g. 'QRCode', 'Code128', 'PDF417', 'DataMatrix') and `value` is the string to encode. Returns a { FileUrl } (valid ~24h) by default, or base64 with output_binary:true. BILLED. Api2Pdf API: GET /zebra.

tools.name: api2pdf_get_balance
tools.title: Get account balance
tools.description: Return the remaining balance / usage for the configured Api2Pdf account. Api2Pdf API: GET /balance.

tools.name: api2pdf_get_status
tools.title: Get service status
tools.description: Return the current Api2Pdf service / health status. Api2Pdf API: GET /status.

tools.name: api2pdf_delete_file
tools.title: Delete a generated file
tools.description: Delete a previously generated file by its ResponseId (the `ResponseId` returned in a generation response). Api2Pdf API: DELETE /file/{ResponseId}.

tools.name: braintree_find_transaction
tools.title: Find a transaction
tools.description: Fetch one transaction by its GraphQL global ID (the opaque `id` returned by braintree_search_transactions, NOT the short legacy id). Uses the GraphQL `node` query. Returns amount, status, timestamps, order id, and the linked customer.

tools.title: Search transactions
tools.description: Search transactions by created-at date range, status, and/or customer. Builds a TransactionSearchInput (operators: status `in`, createdAt `greaterThanOrEqualTo`/`lessThanOrEqualTo`, customer.id `is`). Returns a page of transaction nodes (id, legacyId, amount, status, createdAt). GraphQL `search { transactions }`.

tools.name: braintree_find_customer
tools.title: Find a customer
tools.description: Fetch one customer by GraphQL global Customer ID via the `node` query. Returns id, legacyId, name, company, and created-at. To also enumerate stored cards/PayPal accounts use braintree_customer_payment_methods.

tools.name: braintree_customer_payment_methods
tools.title: List a customer's payment methods
tools.description: List the vaulted payment methods (credit cards, PayPal accounts, etc.) for one customer, by GraphQL global Customer ID. Returns each method's id, legacyId, usage, created-at, and detail type. GraphQL `node { ... on Customer { paymentMethods } }`.

tools.name: braintree_list_subscriptions
tools.title: List a customer's subscription activity
tools.description: List a customer's recurring / subscription payment activity. IMPORTANT: Braintree's GraphQL API does NOT expose native Subscription objects (recurring-billing management is still legacy-API only — see braintree/graphql-api issue #1). This tool therefore returns the customer's transactions (the observable evidence of subscription charges) via a TransactionSearchInput scoped to the customer; inspect each node's status/amount/createdAt to trace recurring charges. For full subscription CRUD you must use Braintree's legacy server SDK / REST API.

tools.name: braintree_refund_transaction
tools.title: Refund a transaction
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Refund a SETTLED (or settling) transaction, returning money to the customer. Use the GraphQL global transaction ID. Omit `amount` for a full refund, or pass a decimal string for a partial refund. GraphQL mutation `refundTransaction`. For transactions not yet settled, use braintree_void_transaction instead.

tools.name: braintree_void_transaction
tools.title: Void a transaction
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Void (cancel) a transaction that has NOT yet settled — e.g. an authorization or one submitted-for-settlement. Use the GraphQL global transaction ID. GraphQL mutation `voidTransaction`. For already-settled transactions use braintree_refund_transaction instead.

tools.name: clinicaltrialsgov_search_studies

tools.description: Search the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 study registry. Provide any combination of query terms (condition, intervention, title, location, sponsor, general term) — multiple query.* terms are ANDed together — plus optional filters (status, geo, advanced Essie expression, explicit NCT ids). Returns { totalCount?, studies: [...], nextPageToken? }. Use `fields` to trim the response to specific fields/modules, `sort` to order (e.g. '@relevance', 'LastUpdatePostDate:desc', 'EnrollmentCount:desc'), and pageSize/pageToken to page. GET /studies.

tools.name: clinicaltrialsgov_get_study
tools.title: Get a clinical trial by NCT ID
tools.description: Fetch a single ClinicalTrials.gov study by its NCT id (format NCT######## — the letters 'NCT' followed by digits, e.g. NCT00841061). Returns the full study object { protocolSection, derivedSection?, hasResults? }. Use `fields` to return only specific fields/modules. GET /studies/{nctId}.

tools.title: Count matching clinical trials
tools.description: Return only the total NUMBER of studies matching a query, without fetching any records. Accepts the same query terms and filters as clinicaltrialsgov_search_studies (term, condition, intervention, title, location, sponsor, status, geoFilter, advanced). Returns { totalCount }. tools.name: clinicaltrialsgov_get_studies_stats

tools.description: Return overall study-size statistics across the registry: { totalStudies, averageSizeBytes, percentiles, ranges, largestStudies }. Useful for understanding data volume. GET /stats/size.

servers.name: Codat
servers.description: MCP server for Codat — companies, connections, invoices, bills and financial statements.

tools.name: codat_get_profile
tools.title: Get account profile
tools.description: Fetch the authenticated Codat account's profile (organization name, redirect URLs, features) — a quick way to verify the API key works. Codat API: GET /profile.

tools.name: codat_list_companies
tools.title: List companies
tools.description: List the companies in your Codat account. A company represents one of your customers' businesses and holds its data connections. Codat API: GET /companies. Returns the paged envelope { results, pageNumber, pageSize, totalResults, _links }.

tools.name: codat_get_company
tools.title: Get a company
tools.description: Fetch a single company by id (name, platform, dataConnections, created/lastSync). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}.

tools.name: codat_list_connections
tools.title: List data connections
tools.description: List a company's data connections (each links the company to one source platform, e.g. QuickBooks, Xero). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/connections. Returns the paged envelope.

tools.name: codat_get_connection
tools.title: Get a data connection
tools.description: Fetch a single data connection by id (platformKey, status, sourceType, lastSync). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/connections/{connectionId}.

tools.name: codat_get_data_status

tools.name: codat_get_data_info

tools.name: codat_list_accounts

tools.description: List a company's chart of accounts (id, name, nominalCode, type, status, currency, currentBalance). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/accounts. Returns the paged envelope.

tools.name: codat_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List a company's accounts-receivable invoices (id, invoiceNumber, customerRef, issueDate, dueDate, currency, totalAmount, amountDue, status, lineItems). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/invoices. Returns the paged envelope. Tip: filter with query, e.g. "status=Submitted&&amountDue>0".

tools.name: codat_get_invoice
tools.title: Get an invoice
tools.description: Fetch a single AR invoice by id (full object incl. lineItems, paymentAllocations). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/invoices/{invoiceId}.

tools.name: codat_list_bills
tools.title: List bills
tools.description: List a company's accounts-payable bills (id, reference, supplierRef, issueDate, dueDate, currency, totalAmount, amountDue, status, lineItems). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/bills. Returns the paged envelope.

tools.name: codat_list_bill_payments
tools.title: List bill payments
tools.description: List a company's bill payments (money paid out to suppliers) — id, supplierRef, date, currency, totalAmount, lines. Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/billPayments. Returns the paged envelope.

tools.name: codat_list_credit_notes
tools.title: List credit notes
tools.description: List a company's credit notes (id, creditNoteNumber, customerRef, issueDate, currency, totalAmount, remainingCredit, status). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/creditNotes. Returns the paged envelope.

tools.name: codat_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List a company's customers (id, customerName, contactName, emailAddress, addresses, status, defaultCurrency). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/customers. Returns the paged envelope.

tools.name: codat_list_suppliers
tools.title: List suppliers

tools.name: codat_list_payments
tools.title: List payments

tools.name: codat_list_journal_entries
tools.title: List journal entries
tools.description: List a company's journal entries (id, postedOn, createdOn, journalLines with accountRef/netAmount/currency). Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/journalEntries. Returns the paged envelope.

tools.name: codat_get_balance_sheet
tools.title: Get balance sheet
tools.description: Get a company's balance sheet, broken into periods. periodLength (months per period) and periodsToCompare are BOTH required by Codat. Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/financials/balanceSheet.

tools.name: codat_get_profit_and_loss
tools.title: Get profit & loss
tools.description: Get a company's profit and loss (income statement), broken into periods. periodLength and periodsToCompare are BOTH required by Codat. Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/financials/profitAndLoss.

tools.name: codat_get_cash_flow_statement
tools.title: Get cash flow statement
tools.description: Get a company's cash flow statement, broken into periods. periodLength and periodsToCompare are BOTH required by Codat. Codat API: GET /companies/{companyId}/data/financials/cashFlowStatement.

tools.name: codat_list_direct_costs

servers.name: EmailOctopus
servers.description: Manage lists, contacts and campaigns, and read campaign performance reports on EmailOctopus.

tools.name: emailoctopus_list_lists
tools.title: List lists
tools.description: List all lists in the account. Returns {data:[...],paging:{...}} — each list's id, name, contact counts by status, and created_at. Paginate with `limit` (max 100) and `starting_after` (cursor from the previous page). EmailOctopus: GET /lists.

tools.name: emailoctopus_get_list
tools.title: Get list
tools.description: Get a single list by its id. Returns the list's full state — name, contact counts by status, and created_at. EmailOctopus: GET /lists/{list_id}.

tools.name: emailoctopus_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List the contacts in a list. Returns {data:[...],paging:{...}} — each contact's id, email_address, fields, tags, status, and created_at. Paginate with `limit` (max 100) and `starting_after`. EmailOctopus: GET /lists/{list_id}/contacts.

tools.name: emailoctopus_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: Get a single contact in a list. Returns email_address, fields, tags, status, and created_at. `contact_id` is the MD5 hash of the lowercased email address, or the `id` returned by emailoctopus_list_contacts. EmailOctopus: GET /lists/{list_id}/contacts/{contact_id}.

tools.name: emailoctopus_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: List all campaigns in the account. Returns {data:[...],paging:{...}} — each campaign's id, name, status, subject, and created_at. Paginate with `limit` (max 100) and `starting_after`. EmailOctopus: GET /campaigns.

tools.name: emailoctopus_get_campaign
tools.title: Get campaign
tools.description: Get a single campaign by its id. Returns the campaign's full state — name, status, subject, from, content, and created_at. EmailOctopus: GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}.

tools.name: emailoctopus_get_campaign_report
tools.title: Get campaign report
tools.description: Get a campaign's aggregate performance report — sent, opened, clicked, bounced, unsubscribed, complained, and related counts. EmailOctopus: GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}/reports/summary.

tools.name: emailoctopus_get_campaign_links_report
tools.title: Get campaign links report
tools.description: Get a campaign's per-link click report — for each link in the campaign, the URL and its click counts. EmailOctopus: GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}/reports/links.

tools.name: emailoctopus_create_list
tools.title: Create list
tools.description: CREATES a new list — this MODIFIES live data. Provide a `name`. EmailOctopus: POST /lists. Returns the created list.

tools.name: emailoctopus_update_list
tools.title: Update list
tools.description: UPDATES an existing list by id — this MODIFIES live data. Sets the list's `name`. EmailOctopus: PUT /lists/{list_id}. Returns the updated list.

tools.name: emailoctopus_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: CREATES a new contact in a list — this MODIFIES live data (adds a subscriber). `email_address` is required; optionally set `fields` (keyed by field tag), `tags`, and `status`. EmailOctopus: POST /lists/{list_id}/contacts. Returns the created contact.

tools.name: emailoctopus_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: UPDATES an existing contact in a list — this MODIFIES live data. Send only the fields you want to change (email_address, fields, tags, status). `contact_id` is the MD5 hash of the lowercased email address, or the id from list_contacts. EmailOctopus: PUT /lists/{list_id}/contacts/{contact_id}. Returns the updated contact.

tools.name: emailoctopus_delete_contact
tools.title: Delete contact
tools.description: PERMANENTLY REMOVES a contact from a list — this MODIFIES live data and cannot be undone. `contact_id` is the MD5 hash of the lowercased email address, or the id from list_contacts. EmailOctopus: DELETE /lists/{list_id}/contacts/{contact_id}.

tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: emailoctopus_request_feature

servers.name: Estuary Flow
servers.description: Inspect Estuary Flow captures, materializations, collections and stats.

tools.name: estuary_list_catalog
tools.title: List catalog entities
tools.description: List live catalog entities (captures, collections, materializations, tests) the user can read, with connector + last-publication metadata. Optionally filter by a catalog-name prefix and spec_type. Estuary control-plane view live_specs_ext. PostgREST: GET /live_specs_ext.

tools.name: estuary_get_catalog_spec
tools.title: Get catalog spec
tools.description: Get one live catalog entity by its exact catalog_name, including the full serialized `spec` and compiled `built_spec`. Estuary control-plane view live_specs_ext. PostgREST: GET /live_specs_ext?catalog_name=eq.<name>&limit=1.

tools.name: estuary_get_catalog_stats
tools.title: Get catalog stats
tools.description: Get usage/throughput stats for one catalog entity — bytes & docs read/written (both directions), usage_seconds, warnings/errors/failures, and txn_count — per time grain. tools.name: estuary_list_drafts
tools.title: List drafts

tools.name: estuary_list_draft_specs
tools.title: List draft specs
tools.description: List the staged spec entries within a draft (each an insert/replace of a catalog entity pending publication). Estuary control-plane table draft_specs. PostgREST: GET /draft_specs.

tools.title: List publications

tools.name: estuary_list_discovers
tools.title: List discovers
tools.description: List connector discovery jobs (auto-detecting bindings/resources for a capture). Estuary control-plane table discovers. PostgREST: GET /discovers.

tools.name: estuary_list_roles

tools.title: List models
tools.description: List or search fal.ai models in the registry (paginated). fal.ai API: GET /models (query: keywords, page, total).

tools.title: Get model schema
tools.description: Get the OpenAPI 3 schema for a model — its input/output fields (components.schemas). Use this to learn what inputs a model accepts before submitting. fal.ai API: GET /openapi/queue/openapi.json?endpoint_id={model_id}.

tools.title: Get request status
tools.description: Get the status of a queued request (IN_QUEUE | IN_PROGRESS | COMPLETED). fal.ai queue: GET {queue}/{model_id}/requests/{request_id}/status (optional logs=1).

tools.name: falai_get_request_result
tools.title: Get request result
tools.description: Get the final output of a COMPLETED queued request. fal.ai queue: GET {queue}/{model_id}/requests/{request_id}.

tools.name: falai_submit_request
tools.title: Submit request
tools.description: Submit an inference request to the queue and return immediately (async — does NOT wait for completion). Returns { request_id, response_url, status_url, cancel_url, queue_position }. Consumes fal credits when the model runs. fal.ai queue: POST {queue}/{model_id} with body = the model input.

tools.name: falai_run_model
tools.title: Run model (subscribe)
tools.description: Convenience 'subscribe': submit a request, poll its status until COMPLETED, then return the result. Consumes fal credits. If it does not complete within the wait budget, returns a { status, request_id, status_url, note } object (NOT an error) so you can keep polling with falai_get_request_status / falai_get_request_result.

tools.title: Cancel request
tools.description: Request cancellation of a queued (not-yet-started) request. Returns 202 { status: 'CANCELLATION_REQUESTED' }. fal.ai queue: PUT {queue}/{model_id}/requests/{request_id}/cancel.

tools.title: Get default store

tools.title: Get store
tools.description: Get a single store resource by id, including its settings and _links to sub-collections. Foxy hAPI: GET /stores/{store_id}.

tools.description: List a store's transactions (orders), newest first. Returns a HAL collection embedding fx:transactions. Foxy hAPI: GET /stores/{store_id}/transactions.

tools.name: foxy_get_transaction
tools.title: Get transaction
tools.description: Get a single transaction by id, optionally zooming related resources (items, customer, payments, applied_taxes…). Foxy hAPI: GET /transactions/{id}.

tools.name: foxy_list_subscriptions
tools.title: List subscriptions

tools.title: Get customer

tools.title: List carts

tools.title: Update subscription
tools.description: UPDATES a subscription — reschedule its next run (next_transaction_date), change its frequency, or activate/pause it (is_active). This MODIFIES live store data and affects future billing. Foxy hAPI: PATCH /subscriptions/{id}. Provide only the fields you want to change.

tools.name: harvest_upgrade

servers.name: Health Gorilla
servers.description: Query Health Gorilla FHIR patients, conditions, medications and lab results.

tools.name: healthgorilla_find_patients
tools.title: Find patients
tools.description: Search for patients by demographics. FHIR: GET /Patient?given=&family=&birthdate=&identifier=. Returns a FHIR searchset Bundle. Use the returned Patient id with the other tools.

tools.name: healthgorilla_get_patient
tools.title: Get patient
tools.description: Read a single patient by id. FHIR: GET /Patient/{id}. Returns a FHIR Patient resource.

tools.name: healthgorilla_get_patient_everything
tools.title: Get patient $everything
tools.description: Fetch the comprehensive record for a patient as a FHIR Bundle. FHIR: GET /Patient/{id}/$everything. Optionally scope by _since and page with _count.

tools.name: healthgorilla_list_conditions
tools.title: List conditions
tools.description: List a patient's conditions/problems. FHIR: GET /Condition?patient={id}. Returns a FHIR searchset Bundle.

tools.name: healthgorilla_list_medications
tools.title: List medications
tools.description: List a patient's medication requests/prescriptions. FHIR: GET /MedicationRequest?patient={id}. Returns a FHIR searchset Bundle.

tools.name: healthgorilla_list_allergies
tools.title: List allergies
tools.description: List a patient's allergies/intolerances. FHIR: GET /AllergyIntolerance?patient={id}. Returns a FHIR searchset Bundle.

tools.name: healthgorilla_list_immunizations
tools.title: List immunizations
tools.description: List a patient's immunizations. FHIR: GET /Immunization?patient={id}. Returns a FHIR searchset Bundle.

tools.name: healthgorilla_list_observations
tools.title: List observations
tools.description: List a patient's observations (labs, vitals). FHIR: GET /Observation?patient={id}. Filter by category (e.g. laboratory, vital-signs), LOINC code, or date. Returns a FHIR searchset Bundle.

tools.name: healthgorilla_list_diagnostic_reports
tools.title: List diagnostic reports
tools.description: List a patient's diagnostic reports (lab panels, imaging). FHIR: GET /DiagnosticReport?patient={id}. Returns a FHIR searchset Bundle.

tools.name: healthgorilla_list_documents
tools.title: List documents
tools.description: List a patient's document references (C-CDA, notes, etc). FHIR: GET /DocumentReference?patient={id}. Each entry points at a Binary you can fetch with healthgorilla_get_binary.

tools.name: healthgorilla_get_coverage
tools.title: Get coverage
tools.description: List a patient's insurance coverage. FHIR: GET /Coverage?patient={id}. Returns a FHIR searchset Bundle.

tools.name: healthgorilla_get_binary
tools.title: Get binary (document content)
tools.description: Retrieve raw document content by Binary id. FHIR: GET /Binary/{id}. Content may be a FHIR Binary JSON resource, XML C-CDA, or base64 — returned as-is (raw text if not JSON).

tools.name: healthgorilla_poll_query_status
tools.title: Poll query status
tools.description: Poll a RequestResult URL returned by healthgorilla_start_patient360_query. HTTP 202 = still processing, 200 = done (returns retrieval metrics: organizationsTotal, documentsFound, documentsImported, documentsSkipped, documentsFailed). Returns { status, body }.

tools.name: healthgorilla_fhir_search

tools.description: Escape hatch: run an arbitrary FHIR search. GET /{resource_type}?{query}. e.g. resource_type='Observation', query='patient=123&category=laboratory&_count=5'. Use when a dedicated tool does not cover your query.

tools.name: healthgorilla_create_patient

tools.name: healthgorilla_start_patient360_query

servers.name: Healthchecks.io
servers.description: Manage cron/heartbeat checks, read pings and flips, pause/resume/delete on Healthchecks.io.

tools.name: healthchecksio_list_checks
tools.title: List checks
tools.description: List all checks in the project, optionally filtered by slug and/or tags. Returns {checks:[...]} — each check's status, schedule, last ping, and ping URL. Healthchecks: GET /checks/.

tools.name: healthchecksio_get_check
tools.title: Get check
tools.description: Get a single check by its UUID (or its unique read-only key). Returns the check's full state — status, timeout/schedule, grace, tags, last ping. Healthchecks: GET /checks/{uuid}.

tools.name: healthchecksio_list_pings
tools.title: List pings
tools.description: List a check's logged pings (100 on the free plan, 1000 on paid), most recent first. Each ping: type, date, n, scheme, remote_addr, method, ua, rid, duration, body_url. Healthchecks: GET /checks/{uuid}/pings/.

tools.name: healthchecksio_get_ping_body
tools.title: Get ping body
tools.description: Get the logged request body of a single ping, returned as PLAIN TEXT (verbatim, not JSON). Healthchecks: GET /checks/{uuid}/pings/{n}/body.

tools.name: healthchecksio_list_flips
tools.title: List flips
tools.description: List a check's status changes ("flips") over time — [{timestamp, up}]. Optionally scope by a lookback window or an explicit start/end range. Healthchecks: GET /checks/{uuid}/flips/.

tools.name: healthchecksio_list_integrations
tools.title: List integrations
tools.description: List the project's notification integrations ("channels") — {channels:[{id, name, kind}]}. The ids are what you assign to a check's `channels` field. Healthchecks: GET /channels/.

tools.name: healthchecksio_list_badges
tools.title: List badges
tools.description: List the project's status-badge URLs per tag (plus "*" for the overall status) — {badges:{...}}. Healthchecks: GET /badges/.

tools.name: healthchecksio_create_check
tools.title: Create check
tools.description: CREATES a new check — this MODIFIES live monitoring config. Provide a `timeout` (simple period-based check) OR a `schedule` + `tz` (cron-based check); the two are mutually exclusive. Use `unique` to avoid creating duplicates. Assign notifications via `channels`. Healthchecks: POST /checks/. Returns the created check (201) or the existing match (200).

tools.name: healthchecksio_update_check
tools.title: Update check
tools.description: UPDATES an existing check by UUID — this MODIFIES live monitoring config. Send only the fields you want to change (timeout and schedule remain mutually exclusive). Healthchecks: POST /checks/{uuid}. Returns the updated check.

tools.name: healthchecksio_pause_check
tools.title: Pause check
tools.description: PAUSES a check — disables monitoring without deleting it (it stops going down for missed pings until it next receives a ping or is resumed). This MODIFIES live monitoring config. Healthchecks: POST /checks/{uuid}/pause (empty body).

tools.name: healthchecksio_resume_check
tools.title: Resume check
tools.description: RESUMES a paused check — re-enables monitoring. This MODIFIES live monitoring config. Returns HTTP 409 (surfaced cleanly) if the check is not currently paused. Healthchecks: POST /checks/{uuid}/resume (empty body).

tools.name: healthchecksio_delete_check
tools.title: Delete check
tools.description: PERMANENTLY DELETES a check by UUID — this MODIFIES live monitoring config and cannot be undone. Healthchecks: DELETE /checks/{uuid}. Returns the deleted check's last known state.

tools.name: healthchecksio_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: healthchecksio_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Healthchecks.io tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: healthchecksio_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Healthchecks.io (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: healthchecksio_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Healthchecks.io Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run healthchecksio_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: hetzner_list_servers
tools.title: List servers
tools.description: List the servers in the token's project, optionally filtered by name, status or a label selector. Hetzner Cloud: GET /servers.

tools.name: hetzner_get_server

tools.name: hetzner_get_server_metrics
tools.title: Get server metrics

tools.name: hetzner_list_server_types
tools.title: List server types
tools.description: List the available server types with their cores, memory, disk and hourly and monthly prices — read this before creating a server. Hetzner Cloud: GET /server_types.

tools.name: hetzner_list_images
tools.title: List images
tools.description: List OS images, snapshots and backups you can boot or restore from. Hetzner Cloud: GET /images.

tools.name: hetzner_list_locations
tools.title: List locations

tools.name: hetzner_get_pricing
tools.title: Get pricing

servers.name: Hypertune
servers.description: Evaluate and inspect your Hypertune feature flags from your AI assistant.

tools.name: hypertune_evaluate
tools.title: Evaluate feature flags
tools.description: Evaluate one or more feature flags for a given context and get their resolved values. Builds `query { root(context: <context>) { <selection> } }`. Provide `selection` = the flag fields to read (e.g. `exampleFlag anotherFlag { nestedField }`) and `context` = the evaluation context (environment + user/attributes). Every field must supply all of its arguments (Hypertune reduces the flag logic to a JSON result). Use hypertune_list_flags / hypertune_introspect first if you don't know the flag names.

tools.name: hypertune_get_logic
tools.title: Get flag logic (unreduced)
tools.description: Fetch the underlying LOGIC of flags without reducing them — i.e. `query { root { <selection> } }` with no context. Returns the flag's conditional expression / rules rather than a single resolved value, useful for inspecting how a flag is configured. If the schema requires a context arg you can still pass a partial one via `context`.

tools.name: hypertune_query
tools.title: Run a raw GraphQL query
tools.description: Run an arbitrary GraphQL query (and optional variables) against the Hypertune edge endpoint. Power-user escape hatch for full control — each Hypertune project has its own generated schema, so this handles any flag shape, nested selections, inline enum literals, or variables the convenience tools can't express. The query root field is `root(context: ...)`.

tools.name: hypertune_introspect
tools.title: Introspect the GraphQL schema
tools.description: Run a GraphQL introspection query to discover the project's schema — all types and fields, including the available flags and the shape of the evaluation context. Best-effort: some edge deployments disable introspection, in which case this returns a clear error (use hypertune_query with a known flag name instead).

tools.name: hypertune_list_flags
tools.title: List feature flags
tools.description: List the project's top-level feature flags (the fields of the query root type) with their return types and descriptions, derived from GraphQL introspection. A convenient first call to see what flags exist before evaluating. Requires introspection to be enabled on the edge endpoint.

servers.name: Instatus

tools.name: instatus_list_pages

tools.name: instatus_list_components
tools.title: List components

tools.name: instatus_get_component
tools.title: Get component
tools.description: Get a single component by id — its full state (name, description, status, order, showUptime, grouped, archived). Instatus: GET /v2/{page_id}/components/{component_id}.

tools.name: instatus_list_incidents
tools.title: List incidents
tools.description: List a status page's incidents, most recent first — optionally filtered by status. Each incident: id, name, status, impact, affected components, updates, timestamps. Instatus: GET /v1/{page_id}/incidents.

tools.name: instatus_get_incident
tools.title: Get incident
tools.description: Get a single incident by id — its full state including its update timeline and affected components. Instatus: GET /v1/{page_id}/incidents/{incident_id}.

tools.name: instatus_list_maintenances
tools.title: List maintenances

tools.name: instatus_get_maintenance
tools.title: Get maintenance
tools.description: Get a single scheduled maintenance by id — its full state including its update timeline and affected components. Instatus: GET /v1/{page_id}/maintenances/{maintenance_id}.

tools.name: instatus_update_component
tools.title: Update component
tools.description: UPDATES a component by id — this MODIFIES live status-page data. The key way to set a component's operational status (OPERATIONAL, UNDERMAINTENANCE, DEGRADEDPERFORMANCE, PARTIALOUTAGE, MAJOROUTAGE). Send only the fields you want to change. Instatus: PUT /v2/{page_id}/components/{component_id}. Returns the updated component.

tools.name: instatus_create_incident
tools.title: Create incident
tools.description: CREATES a new incident — this MODIFIES live status-page data and can notify subscribers. Provide `name` (required); optionally set the initial `message`, affected `components`, per-component impact via `statuses`, `status`, `started`, `notify`, and `shouldPublish`. Instatus: POST /v1/{page_id}/incidents. Returns the created incident.

tools.name: instatus_update_incident
tools.title: Update incident
tools.description: UPDATES an existing incident by id — this MODIFIES live status-page data and can notify subscribers (e.g. move it to MONITORING or RESOLVED). Send only the fields you want to change. Instatus: PUT /v1/{page_id}/incidents/{incident_id}. Returns the updated incident.

tools.name: instatus_delete_incident
tools.title: Delete incident
tools.description: PERMANENTLY DELETES an incident by id — this MODIFIES live status-page data and cannot be undone. Instatus: DELETE /v1/{page_id}/incidents/{incident_id}.

tools.name: instatus_create_maintenance
tools.title: Create maintenance
tools.description: CREATES a new scheduled maintenance — this MODIFIES live status-page data and can notify subscribers. Provide `name` (required); optionally set `message`, affected `components`, per-component impact via `statuses`, `status`, `start`/`end`, `duration`, and `notify`. Instatus: POST /v1/{page_id}/maintenances. Returns the created maintenance.

tools.name: instatus_update_maintenance
tools.title: Update maintenance
tools.description: UPDATES an existing scheduled maintenance by id — this MODIFIES live status-page data and can notify subscribers. Send only the fields you want to change. Instatus: PUT /v1/{page_id}/maintenances/{maintenance_id}. Returns the updated maintenance.

tools.name: instatus_delete_maintenance
tools.title: Delete maintenance
tools.description: PERMANENTLY DELETES a scheduled maintenance by id — this MODIFIES live status-page data and cannot be undone. Instatus: DELETE /v1/{page_id}/maintenances/{maintenance_id}.

tools.name: instatus_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: instatus_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Instatus tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: instatus_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Instatus (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). tools.name: knack_get_application
tools.title: Get application schema
tools.description: Fetch a Knack application's full schema/metadata — its objects (tables), fields, and scenes. Knack API: GET /applications/{app_id}. Returns the raw JSON as-is. app_id defaults to the configured KNACK_APPLICATION_ID.

tools.name: knack_list_objects
tools.title: List objects (tables)
tools.description: List an application's objects (tables) as a compact array [{ key, name, fieldCount }]. Convenience over GET /applications/{app_id}. app_id defaults to the configured KNACK_APPLICATION_ID.

tools.name: knack_list_fields
tools.title: List fields for an object
tools.description: List the fields of ONE object as [{ key, name, type, required }]. Fetches GET /applications/{app_id} and returns the fields of the object whose key === objectKey (e.g. "object_1"). app_id defaults to the configured KNACK_APPLICATION_ID.

tools.name: knack_list_records
tools.title: List records
tools.description: List an object's records. Knack API: GET /objects/{object_key}/records. Returns the paged envelope { total_pages, current_page, total_records, records: [...] } as-is. Records carry both field_x (formatted) and field_x_raw (structured) values. Page with page / rows_per_page (max 1000), sort with sort_field / sort_order, and filter with the `filters` object.

tools.name: knack_get_record
tools.title: Get a record
tools.description: Fetch a single record by id. Knack API: GET /objects/{object_key}/records/{record_id}. Returns the bare record (with both field_x and field_x_raw values).

tools.name: knack_request
tools.title: Raw Knack API GET
tools.description: Power-user escape hatch: GET any Knack API path not wrapped by a dedicated tool (e.g. view-based reads). READ-ONLY — only GET is allowed. Path starts with a slash (e.g. "/objects/object_1/records"). Knack API: GET {path}.

tools.name: knack_create_record
tools.title: Create a record
tools.description: MUTATES Knack data — creates a new record in an object. Knack API: POST /objects/{object_key}/records. Provide `fields` as an object keyed by field key, e.g. { "field_1": "Acme", "field_2": 100 }. Auto Increment / Formula / Equation fields are read-only and cannot be set. Returns the created record.

tools.name: knack_update_record
tools.title: Update a record
tools.description: MUTATES Knack data — updates a record. Knack API: PUT /objects/{object_key}/records/{record_id}. Provide `fields` as an object keyed by field key; only the included fields change, e.g. { "field_1": "Acme Inc" }. Auto Increment / Formula / Equation fields are read-only. Returns the updated record.

tools.name: knack_delete_record
tools.title: Delete a record
tools.description: MUTATES Knack data — permanently DELETES a record (irreversible). Knack API: DELETE /objects/{object_key}/records/{record_id}. Knack returns { delete: true } on success.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_request
tools.title: Raw read request
tools.description: Power-user escape hatch: GET any KnowledgeOwl API path not wrapped by a dedicated tool. READ-ONLY — only GET is allowed. Pass the FULL API path after the base, starting with a slash, INCLUDING any query string, e.g. "/article.json?_page=2" or "/category/abc123.json". Returns the parsed JSON.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_create_article
tools.title: Create an article
tools.description: MUTATES KnowledgeOwl data: creates a new article. KnowledgeOwl API: POST /article.json (JSON). Required by the API: project_id, name, status, url_hash, visibility, and current_version (a nested object `{ <lang>: { title, body, ... } }` — pass it via the `fields` passthrough). Returns the created article.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_update_article
tools.title: Update an article
tools.description: MUTATES KnowledgeOwl data: updates an existing article. KnowledgeOwl API: PUT /article/{id}.json (JSON — only included fields change). Use the `fields` passthrough for current_version (title/body) and any other documented field. The path id is never sent in the body.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_create_category
tools.title: Create a category
tools.description: MUTATES KnowledgeOwl data: creates a new category (a node in the article tree). KnowledgeOwl API: POST /category.json (JSON). Required by the API: type, project_id, url_hash, name, visibility, status. Pass extra documented fields via `fields`. Returns the created category.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_update_category
tools.title: Update a category
tools.description: MUTATES KnowledgeOwl data: updates an existing category. KnowledgeOwl API: PUT /category/{id}.json (JSON — only included fields change). Use the `fields` passthrough for any other documented field. The path id is never sent in the body.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_create_snippet
tools.title: Create a snippet
tools.description: MUTATES KnowledgeOwl data: creates a reusable content snippet. KnowledgeOwl API: POST /snippet.json (JSON). Pass the snippet body/content and any other documented field via `fields` (e.g. snippet_text/body). Returns the created snippet.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_create_glossary_term
tools.title: Create a glossary term
tools.description: MUTATES KnowledgeOwl data: creates a glossary term and definition. KnowledgeOwl API: POST /glossaryterm.json (JSON). Pass extra documented fields via `fields`. Returns the created glossary term.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the KnowledgeOwl tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on KnowledgeOwl (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: knowledgeowl_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's KnowledgeOwl Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run knowledgeowl_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: List the articles in the Billing category that we have not updated this year.
Show the comments that readers left on articles this month.
Draft a new article "How to reset your password" in the Account category.
Show the revision history of the Getting started article.

login.hint: Find it in KnowledgeOwl → **Account → API keys**. Your key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: mailchimp_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: Get the API Root — the authenticated Mailchimp account: account name, total subscribers, contact info, plan and industry stats. REST: GET /.

tools.name: mailchimp_list_audiences
tools.title: List audiences (lists)
tools.description: List the account's audiences — Mailchimp's `/lists` resource (an audience is a list of subscribers). Paginated, with optional sort. REST: GET /lists.

tools.name: mailchimp_get_audience
tools.title: Get audience (list)
tools.description: Get a single audience (list) by id, including subscriber stats, default from-name/email and settings. REST: GET /lists/{list_id}.

tools.name: mailchimp_list_members
tools.title: List members
tools.description: List members of an audience (list). Paginated, with an optional status filter and sort. REST: GET /lists/{list_id}/members.

tools.title: Get member
tools.description: Get a single audience member (subscriber) by email or subscriber_hash, including status, merge fields, tags and stats. REST: GET /lists/{list_id}/members/{subscriber_hash} (email → MD5 hash).

tools.name: mailchimp_search_members
tools.title: Search members

tools.title: List campaigns

tools.title: List reports

tools.name: mailchimp_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: mailchimp_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Mailchimp tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: mailchimp_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Mailchimp (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: mailchimp_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Mailchimp Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run mailchimp_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find it in Mailchimp → **Account & billing → Extras → API keys**. Copy the whole key including the trailing datacenter suffix (`-us21`) — it tells us which Mailchimp server your account lives on. Your key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: How many subscribers are in each of my audiences?
What were the open and click rates of my last campaign?
Show my 25 most recently sent campaigns with their send dates.
Is jane@acme.example subscribed, and which tags does she have?

servers.name: Memberful
servers.description: Manage Memberful members, subscriptions, plans, passes and coupons via the GraphQL API.

tools.name: memberful_get_member
tools.title: Get a member
tools.description: Fetch one Memberful member by id: profile, Stripe customer id, unrestricted-access flag, total spend, metadata, address, and their subscriptions (each with plan). Memberful GraphQL: member(id).

tools.name: memberful_list_members
tools.title: List members
tools.description: List members (Relay connection): each edge has a cursor + node (profile, Stripe customer id, unrestricted-access flag, total spend, and their subscriptions). Paginate with `first` + `after` (pass the last edge's `cursor`); `first` defaults to 50. Set `activeOnly` to return only members with an ACTIVE membership state. For member-state filters beyond active, use memberful_query. Memberful GraphQL: members connection.

tools.name: memberful_get_subscription
tools.title: Get a subscription
tools.description: Fetch one subscription by id: status, activated/expires/trial timestamps, plan, member, orders, coupon. Memberful GraphQL: subscription(id).

tools.name: memberful_list_subscriptions
tools.title: List subscriptions
tools.description: List subscriptions (Relay connection): each edge has a cursor + node (status, expires/created timestamps, plan, member). Paginate with `first` + `after` (pass the last edge's `cursor`); `first` defaults to 50. NOTE: this uses the top-level `subscriptions` connection, which is sourced from the community SDK — validate against a live account. Memberful GraphQL: subscriptions connection.

tools.name: memberful_list_plans
tools.title: List plans
tools.description: List all plans (Memberful dashboard 'Prices'): name, interval, price (cents), for-sale flag, plan group. Memberful GraphQL: plans.

tools.name: memberful_list_passes
tools.title: List passes
tools.description: List all passes (Memberful dashboard 'Plans' — the access groups a member subscribes to): id, name. Memberful GraphQL: passes.

tools.name: memberful_query
tools.title: Run a GraphQL query (read-only)
tools.description: Escape hatch: run an arbitrary Memberful GraphQL QUERY (read-only) against your account's /api/graphql endpoint with optional variables. Mutations are REJECTED — use the dedicated write tools or memberful_graphql for those. Useful for fields not covered by the curated read tools (e.g. member-state filters beyond active).

tools.name: memberful_create_member
tools.title: Create a member
tools.description: MUTATES Memberful data: create a new member with an email (and optional full name). Memberful GraphQL: memberCreate(email, fullName).

tools.name: memberful_update_member
tools.title: Update a member
tools.description: MUTATES Memberful data: update a member's metadata (a JSON string; max 50 keys, 40-char keys, 500-char values). Only metadata is supported here; for other inline member fields use memberful_graphql. Memberful GraphQL: memberUpdate(id, metadata).

tools.name: memberful_change_subscription_expiration
tools.title: Change subscription expiration
tools.description: MUTATES Memberful data: change WHEN a subscription expires (extend or shorten access). expiresAt is a Unix timestamp in SECONDS (Int). Memberful GraphQL: subscriptionChangeExpirationTime(id, expiresAt).

tools.name: memberful_create_coupons
tools.title: Create coupons
tools.description: MUTATES Memberful data: create one or more coupon codes for a discount. Provide the discount id (discountId) and the coupon code strings. Memberful GraphQL: createCoupons(discountId, coupons).

tools.name: memberful_graphql
