tools.description: MUTATES Memberful data (potentially): escape hatch to run an arbitrary Memberful GraphQL operation — including any mutation — against your account's /api/graphql endpoint with optional variables. Prefer memberful_query for read-only calls.

tools.name: nomic_get_user

tools.description: Fetch an organisation by slug, with the datasets it holds. Atlas: GET /v1/organization/{slug}.

tools.name: nomic_get_dataset
tools.title: Get a dataset by id
tools.description: Fetch a dataset (Atlas calls it a project) by id — its schema, size, indices and projections. Atlas: GET /v1/project/{id}.

tools.name: nomic_get_dataset_by_slug
tools.title: Get a dataset by name
tools.description: Fetch a dataset by organisation slug and dataset slug — the human-readable path, and usually easier than finding the UUID. Atlas: GET /v1/project/{organization_slug}/{project_slug}.

tools.name: nomic_nearest_neighbors_by_id
tools.title: Find similar records
tools.description: Semantic search: given the ids of records already in a dataset, return their nearest neighbours in embedding space, with distances. This is what Atlas is for — finding what resembles what across unstructured data. Needs a BUILT index; if the map is still building the call fails with a 500, so check nomic_get_index_job. Atlas: POST /v1/project/data/get/nearest_neighbors/by_id.

tools.name: nomic_get_index_job

tools.description: Fetch the status of an index-building job. Atlas indexes take time to build, and a vector search against an unbuilt map fails — this is how you tell which it is. Atlas: GET /v1/project/index/job/{job_id}.

tools.name: nomic_get_projection_schema

tools.name: nomic_list_tags

tools.name: nomic_get_tag_status
tools.title: Get a tag's status

servers.description: Calculate sales tax & VAT, record transactions and refunds, manage products and customers.

tools.description: Health check — verifies the API key works and reports the environment (test/prod), api_version, and server timestamp. Numeral: GET /tax/ping.

tools.description: Calculate sales tax / VAT for an order — a STATELESS quote that persists nothing (record it later with numeral_create_transaction using the returned calculation id). Returns per-jurisdiction rates, total_tax_amount, and totals. Provide a customer address and one or more line items (each needs reference_product_id OR product_category). tools.name: numeral_get_transaction

tools.description: List all refunds recorded against a transaction. Returns {refunds:[...]}. Numeral: GET /tax/transactions/{transaction_id}/refunds.

tools.title: List products
tools.description: List your Numeral products (up to 50 per page), each with its reference id, name, and product_category. Use `cursor` (the last_product_id from a previous page) to paginate; has_more indicates more pages. Numeral: GET /tax/products.

tools.name: numeral_get_product

tools.description: Get a single product by its reference_product_id (your id). Returns the product's name, product_category, and timestamps. Numeral: GET /tax/products/{reference_product_id}.

tools.name: numeral_get_customer

tools.name: nylas_create_event

tools.name: nylas_create_draft

tools.name: nylas_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: nylas_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Nylas tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: nylas_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Nylas (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: nylas_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Nylas Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run nylas_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find your API key in the Nylas dashboard → **API keys**, and pick the region your Nylas application lives in. A default grant id is optional — you can set one now or pass `grant_id` per call (list connected accounts with `nylas_list_grants`). Your API key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Show me the emails that I received in my inbox today.
What meetings do I have on my calendar this week?
Show the latest emails from jane@acme.example and summarize what she wants.
Draft an email to jane@acme.example confirming our meeting on Thursday at 2pm.

servers.name: openFDA
servers.description: Search openFDA drug, device, food and adverse-event datasets.

tools.name: openfda_search_drug_events
tools.title: Search drug adverse-event reports (FAERS)
tools.description: Search the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS): reports of drug side effects, adverse reactions and medication errors submitted to the FDA. Returns individual case reports. openFDA drug/event endpoint.

tools.name: openfda_search_drug_labels
tools.title: Search drug product labels (SPL)
tools.description: Search Structured Product Labeling (SPL): the official prescribing information for drugs — indications, warnings, dosage, adverse reactions, drug interactions and more. openFDA drug/label endpoint.

tools.name: openfda_search_drug_recalls
tools.title: Search drug recall enforcement reports
tools.description: Search drug recall enforcement reports: recalled drug products with the reason, classification (Class I/II/III), recalling firm, distribution and status. openFDA drug/enforcement endpoint.

tools.name: openfda_search_drug_shortages
tools.title: Search drug shortages

tools.name: orb_upgrade

List all unpaid invoices and which customers they belong to.
Preview the next invoice for subscription ID sub-1042.
Create a new customer called Northwind Traders with the email billing@northwind.example.

tools.name: oura_get_personal_info

tools.name: oura_list_documents

tools.name: oura_get_document

tools.name: oura_get_heartrate
tools.title: Get heart-rate samples

tools.name: oura_get_ring_battery_level

tools.name: oura_create_webhook_subscription

tools.name: oura_renew_webhook_subscription

tools.name: oura_delete_webhook_subscription

servers.name: OwnerRez
servers.description: Manage OwnerRez properties, bookings, guests, quotes and inquiries.

tools.name: ownerrez_get_me
tools.title: Get current user
tools.description: Return the authenticated OwnerRez user (verifies your credentials). OwnerRez API: GET /v2/users/me.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_properties
tools.title: List properties
tools.description: List rental properties. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/properties. Returns the pageable envelope { items, count, limit, offset, next_page_url }.

tools.name: ownerrez_get_property
tools.title: Get a property
tools.description: Fetch a single property by id (includes time_zone). OwnerRez API: GET /v2/properties/{id}.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_bookings
tools.title: List bookings
tools.description: List bookings (reservations). OwnerRez API: GET /v2/bookings. Filter by property, date range, changed-since, and status; opt into embedded charges/guest/tags. Returns { items, count, limit, offset, next_page_url }.

tools.name: ownerrez_get_booking
tools.title: Get a booking
tools.description: Fetch a single booking by id. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/bookings/{id}. Opt into embedded charges/guest/tags.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_guests
tools.title: List guests
tools.description: List guests (contacts). OwnerRez API: GET /v2/guests. NOTE: OwnerRez REQUIRES either `q` (search) or `created_since_utc` on this endpoint. Returns { items, count, limit, offset, next_page_url }.

tools.name: ownerrez_get_guest
tools.title: Get a guest
tools.description: Fetch a single guest (contact) by id. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/guests/{id}.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_quotes
tools.title: List quotes
tools.description: List quotes. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/quotes. Returns { items, count, limit, offset, next_page_url }. Use the `params` passthrough for documented filters (e.g. property_id, guest_id).

tools.name: ownerrez_get_quote
tools.title: Get a quote
tools.description: Fetch a single quote by id. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/quotes/{id}.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_listings
tools.title: List listings
tools.description: List channel listings (a property's presence on a listing site such as Airbnb/Vrbo). OwnerRez API: GET /v2/listings. Returns { items, count, limit, offset, next_page_url }.

tools.name: ownerrez_get_listing
tools.title: Get a listing
tools.description: Fetch a single channel listing by id. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/listings/{id}.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_listing_sites
tools.title: List listing sites
tools.description: List the listing sites (channels, e.g. Airbnb, Vrbo) known to OwnerRez. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/listingsites.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_owners
tools.title: List owners
tools.description: List property owners. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/owners. Returns { items, count, limit, offset, next_page_url }.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_inquiries
tools.title: List inquiries
tools.description: List guest inquiries (pre-booking leads). OwnerRez API: GET /v2/inquiries. Use `params` for documented filters.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_messages
tools.title: List messages
tools.description: List messages from guest-communication threads. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/messages. Use `params` for documented filters (e.g. booking_id).

tools.name: ownerrez_list_payments
tools.title: List payments
tools.description: List payments. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/payments. Use `params` for documented filters (e.g. booking_id, since_utc).

tools.name: ownerrez_get_payment
tools.title: Get a payment
tools.description: Fetch a single payment by id. OwnerRez API: GET /v2/payments/{id}.

tools.name: ownerrez_list_field_definitions
tools.title: List custom-field definitions
tools.description: List custom-field definitions available in the account (the schema for custom fields on properties/bookings/guests). OwnerRez API: GET /v2/fielddefinitions.

tools.name: ownerrez_request
tools.title: Raw read request
tools.description: Power-user escape hatch: GET any OwnerRez API path not wrapped by a dedicated tool. READ-ONLY — only GET is allowed. Pass the FULL API path after the host, starting with a slash, INCLUDING any query string, e.g. "/v2/propertysearch?query=beach" or "/v2/bookings/123". Returns the parsed JSON.

tools.name: ownerrez_create_guest
tools.title: Create a guest
tools.description: MUTATES OwnerRez data: creates a new guest (contact). OwnerRez API: POST /v2/guests (JSON). Emails/phones/addresses are arrays of objects — pass them via the `fields` passthrough (e.g. email_addresses:[{address:"a@b.com"}]). Returns the created guest.

tools.name: ownerrez_update_guest
tools.title: Update a guest
tools.description: MUTATES OwnerRez data: updates an existing guest. OwnerRez API: PATCH /v2/guests/{id} (JSON — only included fields change). Use the `fields` passthrough for arrays (email_addresses/phones/addresses) and any other documented field.

tools.name: ownerrez_create_booking
tools.title: Create a booking
tools.description: MUTATES OwnerRez data: creates a new booking (reservation). OwnerRez API: POST /v2/bookings (JSON). A booking ties a guest to a property for a date range; the exact charge/quote shape is account-specific, so pass extra documented fields via `fields`. Returns the created booking.

tools.name: ownerrez_update_booking
tools.title: Update a booking
tools.description: MUTATES OwnerRez data: updates an existing booking. OwnerRez API: PATCH /v2/bookings/{id} (JSON — only included fields change). Use the `fields` passthrough for any documented field (dates, guest counts, notes, status).

tools.name: ownerrez_create_quote
tools.title: Create a quote
tools.description: MUTATES OwnerRez data: creates a quote for a property + date range (the pre-booking pricing document). OwnerRez API: POST /v2/quotes (JSON). The full quote/charge shape is account-specific — pass extra documented fields via `fields`. Returns the created quote.

tools.name: ownerrez_create_message
tools.title: Create a message
tools.description: MUTATES OwnerRez data: posts a message into a guest-communication thread. OwnerRez API: POST /v2/messages (JSON). The exact thread/booking linkage is account-specific — pass extra documented fields (e.g. thread_id, booking_id) via `fields`. Returns the created message.

servers.name: Parabol
servers.description: Start Parabol retrospectives, standups and sprint poker; read teams/meetings/tasks; create tasks.

tools.name: parabol_get_viewer
tools.title: Get current user (viewer)
tools.description: Fetch the authenticated Parabol user (the token owner): id, preferredName, email, tier, and the team ids (tms) they belong to. Parabol GraphQL: query { viewer { ... } }. Requires the USERS_READ scope. Start here to discover your identity and team ids.

tools.name: parabol_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: List the teams the viewer belongs to, with each team's id, name, orgId, tier, and team lead. Parabol GraphQL: viewer.teams. Requires the TEAMS_READ scope.

tools.name: parabol_get_team
tools.title: Get a team
tools.description: Fetch one team by id: metadata, its team members (with each member's user), active meetings, and organization. Parabol GraphQL: viewer.team(teamId). Requires TEAMS_READ (+ MEETINGS_READ for activeMeetings, ORGS_READ for organization).

tools.name: parabol_list_team_members
tools.title: List team members
tools.description: List the members of a team, each with role flags (isLead, isOrgAdmin) and the underlying user (preferredName, email). Parabol GraphQL: viewer.team(teamId).teamMembers. Requires TEAMS_READ.

tools.name: parabol_list_organizations
tools.title: List organizations
tools.description: List the organizations the viewer belongs to: id, name, tier, billingTier. Parabol GraphQL: viewer.organizations. Requires ORGS_READ.

tools.name: parabol_get_organization
tools.title: Get an organization
tools.description: Fetch one organization by id, including its teams. Parabol GraphQL: viewer.organization(orgId). Requires ORGS_READ (+ TEAMS_READ for teams).

tools.name: parabol_list_organization_users
tools.title: List organization users
tools.description: List the users in an organization (Relay connection): each org-user's role, joinedAt, tier, and underlying user (preferredName, email). Paginate with `first` + `after` (pass the last edge's `cursor`). Parabol GraphQL: viewer.organization(orgId).organizationUsers. Requires ORGS_READ + USERS_READ.

tools.name: parabol_list_meetings
tools.title: List meetings (history)
tools.description: List past/ongoing meetings for one or more teams (Relay connection), newest first. `teamIds` is required. `meetingTypes` defaults to all four (retrospective, action, poker, teamPrompt). `before` bounds the window (defaults to now); paginate older with `after`. Parabol GraphQL: viewer.meetings. Requires MEETINGS_READ.

tools.name: parabol_get_meeting
tools.title: Get a meeting
tools.description: Fetch one meeting by id with its phases and stages. For a retrospective it also returns the reflection groups and reflections plus vote/topic/task/comment counts. Uses __typename so you can tell meeting types apart. Parabol GraphQL: viewer.meeting(meetingId). Requires MEETINGS_READ.

tools.name: parabol_list_active_meetings
tools.title: List active meetings
tools.description: List a team's currently-active (in-progress) meetings. Parabol GraphQL: viewer.team(teamId).activeMeetings. Requires TEAMS_READ + MEETINGS_READ.

tools.name: parabol_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List the viewer's tasks (Relay connection), optionally filtered by team, user, status, archived state, or a text query. Paginate with `first` + the `after` DateTime cursor. Parabol GraphQL: viewer.tasks. Requires TASKS_READ.

tools.name: parabol_query
tools.title: Run a GraphQL query (read-only)
tools.description: Escape hatch: run an arbitrary Parabol GraphQL QUERY (read-only) against action.parabol.co/graphql with optional variables. Mutations are REJECTED — use the dedicated write tools or parabol_graphql for those. Useful for fields not covered by the curated read tools. Requires the matching read scope(s) on your token.

tools.name: parabol_create_task
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: MUTATES Parabol data: create a task on a team. Required: teamId and status (active|stuck|done|future). Provide `plaintextContent` for the task text (and/or `content`, which is a stringified TipTap/ProseMirror JSON document). Optionally assign to a userId or link to a meetingId/discussionId. Parabol GraphQL: createTask(newTask, area). Requires TASKS_WRITE.

tools.name: parabol_update_task
tools.title: Update a task
tools.description: MUTATES Parabol data: update an existing task. Required: id. Optionally change content (stringified TipTap JSON), status, assignee (userId), or sortOrder. Only included fields change. Parabol GraphQL: updateTask(updatedTask, area). Requires TASKS_WRITE.

tools.name: parabol_create_reflection
tools.title: Create a reflection
tools.description: MUTATES Parabol data: add a reflection card to a running retrospective's reflect phase. Required: meetingId, promptId (the reflect-prompt/column), sortOrder (Float). `content` (optional) is a stringified TipTap/ProseMirror JSON document (<=2000 chars). Parabol GraphQL: createReflection(input). Requires MEETINGS_WRITE.

tools.name: parabol_add_comment
tools.title: Add a comment
tools.description: MUTATES Parabol data: add a comment to a meeting discussion thread. Required: content (stringified TipTap/ProseMirror JSON document), discussionId, threadSortOrder (Int). Optionally isAnonymous or threadParentId (to reply). Parabol GraphQL: addComment(comment) → union. Requires COMMENTS_WRITE.

tools.name: parabol_start_retrospective
tools.title: Start a retrospective
tools.description: MUTATES Parabol data: start a new retrospective meeting for a team (returns the new meetingId). Required: teamId. Optionally name it. Parabol GraphQL: startRetrospective → union. Requires MEETINGS_WRITE.

tools.name: parabol_start_checkin
tools.title: Start a check-in meeting
tools.description: MUTATES Parabol data: start a new Check-in (Action) meeting for a team (returns the new meetingId). Required: teamId. Optionally name it. Parabol GraphQL: startCheckIn → union. Requires MEETINGS_WRITE.

tools.name: parabol_start_team_prompt
tools.title: Start a standup (team prompt)
tools.description: MUTATES Parabol data: start a new async Standup (Team Prompt) meeting for a team. Required: teamId. Optionally name it (default 'Standup'). Parabol GraphQL: startTeamPrompt → union. Requires MEETINGS_WRITE.

tools.name: parabol_invite_to_team
tools.title: Invite users to a team
tools.description: MUTATES Parabol data: send team invitations by email. Required: teamId and invitees (an array of email addresses). Optionally scope to a meetingId. Parabol GraphQL: inviteToTeam(teamId, invitees). Requires TEAMS_WRITE.

tools.name: parabol_graphql
tools.title: Run a GraphQL operation (query or mutation)
tools.description: MUTATES Parabol data (potentially): escape hatch to run an arbitrary Parabol GraphQL operation — including any mutation — against action.parabol.co/graphql with optional variables. Use for operations not covered by the curated tools. Your token must carry the scope the operation requires. Prefer parabol_query for read-only calls.

tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Parabol (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: parabol_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Parabol Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run parabol_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

What tasks came out of our last three retrospectives?
Create a task "Fix the flaky deploy test" for my team.
Start a standup for my team named Weekly check-in.

servers.name: Particle Health
servers.description: Query Particle Health patient records across connected clinical networks.

tools.name: particle_get_patient
tools.title: Get patient record
tools.description: Fetch a single patient record by its Particle patient id. Endpoint: GET /api/v2/patients/{particle_patient_id}.

tools.name: particle_search_patient
tools.title: Search for a patient
tools.description: Search for an existing patient by demographics (non-mutating). Returns an array of matching patient objects (or a 204 message when none match). Endpoint: POST /api/v2/patients/search.

tools.name: particle_get_query_status
tools.title: Get query status
tools.description: Get the status of a clinical-record retrieval query (state, timing, demographics, files). Omit query_id to get the latest COMPLETE query. Endpoint: GET /api/v2/patients/{particle_patient_id}/query.

tools.name: particle_get_fhir
tools.title: Get FHIR bundle
tools.description: Retrieve the patient's complete clinical record as a FHIR searchset Bundle. Supports incremental sync and pagination. Endpoint: GET /api/v2/patients/{particle_patient_id}/fhir.

tools.name: particle_get_fhir_by_type
tools.title: Get FHIR resources by type
tools.description: Retrieve only one FHIR resource type for a patient (e.g. Condition, MedicationRequest, Observation) as a Bundle. Supports the same pagination as particle_get_fhir. Endpoint: GET /api/v2/patients/{particle_patient_id}/fhir/{type}.

tools.name: particle_get_flat
tools.title: Get flattened clinical data
tools.description: Retrieve the patient's clinical data in Particle's flattened (de-nested) format, easier to read than raw FHIR. Optionally filter to one domain. Endpoint: GET /api/v2/patients/{particle_patient_id}/flat.

tools.name: particle_get_ccda
tools.title: Get C-CDA document(s)
tools.description: Retrieve the patient's C-CDA clinical document(s). May be large and returned as XML/text — parsed if JSON, otherwise passed through as-is. Endpoint: GET /api/v2/patients/{particle_patient_id}/ccda.

tools.name: particle_search_network_participants
tools.title: Search network participants
tools.description: List the health-data network participants (organizations Particle can query). Optionally filter by state or zipcode, and page with continuation_token. Endpoint: GET /api/v1/networkparticipants (with /state/{state} and /zipcode/{zip} variants).

tools.name: particle_get_patient_documents
tools.title: List patient documents
tools.description: List the documents uploaded / available for a patient. Endpoint: GET /api/v1/documents/{patient_id}.

tools.name: particle_submit_patient
tools.title: Submit (register) patient (WRITE)

tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: particlehealth_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Particle Health tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). tools.name: particlehealth_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Particle Health (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: particlehealth_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription

Show the status of the latest completed record retrieval for patient ID patient-1042.
List the medications and conditions recorded for patient ID patient-1042.
Show the available documents for patient ID patient-1042.

servers.name: People Data Labs
servers.description: Enrich and search people and companies, resolve identities, and enrich IP addresses.

tools.name: pdl_person_enrich
tools.title: Enrich a person
tools.description: Find the single best-matching person profile for a set of identifying attributes (name, email, phone, profile URL, company, etc.). Returns one record plus a likelihood score (1-10), or a 404 'no match' body. Use uniquely-identifying inputs for best results. API: GET /person/enrich.

tools.name: pdl_person_identify
tools.title: Identify a person
tools.description: Given broad, possibly-ambiguous attributes about a person, return up to 20 strongly-related profiles ranked by match score. Sits between enrich (1:1) and search (open-ended) — ideal when you can't uniquely resolve someone. API: GET /person/identify.

tools.name: pdl_person_search
tools.title: Search people
tools.description: Search the full PDL Person Dataset with an Elasticsearch query object OR a SQL string over the Person Schema (e.g. everyone with job_title_role='engineering' at a company). Returns matching profiles sorted by completeness; paginate with scroll_token. Each returned record costs 1 credit. API: POST /person/search.

tools.name: pdl_company_enrich
tools.title: Enrich a company
tools.description: Find the single best-matching company record. Requires a non-ambiguous input — name OR website OR ticker OR profile (website/ticker/profile resolve more reliably than name). Returns firmographics (industry, size, location, etc.) or a 404 'no match' body. API: GET /company/enrich.

tools.name: pdl_company_search

tools.description: Search the full PDL Company Dataset with an Elasticsearch query object OR a SQL string over the Company Schema (e.g. all SaaS companies with 50-200 employees in the US). Paginate with scroll_token. Each returned record costs 1 credit. API: POST /company/search.

tools.name: pdl_ip_enrich
tools.title: Enrich an IP address
tools.description: Enrich an IP address with its location, company, and (optionally) associated person data via a 1:1 match against PDL's IP dataset. API: GET /ip/enrich.

tools.name: pdl_autocomplete
tools.title: Autocomplete search values
tools.description: Get suggested values for a search field along with the number of available records for each — useful for building valid Person/Company Search queries. Free on all plans. API: GET /autocomplete.

tools.name: pdl_job_posting_search
tools.title: Search job postings
tools.description: Search PDL's Job Posting Dataset (millions of active & historical postings sourced from company career pages) with an Elasticsearch query object OR a SQL string. Beta — may require plan access (HTTP 403 if not enabled). Each returned posting costs 1 credit. API: POST /job_posting/search.

servers.name: Persona
servers.description: Read Persona inquiries, accounts, verifications and reports.

tools.name: persona_list_inquiries
tools.title: List inquiries
tools.description: List identity-verification inquiries (an end-user's KYC verification session). Optionally filter by status, account_id, reference_id, inquiry_template_id, and a created-at date range, and paginate via the JSON:API links.next cursor (page_after) / links.prev (page_before). Returns JSON:API { data:[...], links } — objects contain PII. Persona REST: GET /inquiries.

tools.name: persona_get_inquiry
tools.title: Get inquiry
tools.description: Get a single identity-verification inquiry by id, including its status, template, and relationships (verifications, account). Returns JSON:API { data } containing PII. Persona REST: GET /inquiries/{inquiry_id}.

tools.name: persona_list_accounts
tools.title: List accounts
tools.description: List accounts (a persistent identity record for an end user, linking their inquiries/verifications over time). Optionally filter by reference_id and paginate via the JSON:API links.next cursor (page_after) / links.prev (page_before). Returns JSON:API { data:[...], links } — objects contain PII. Persona REST: GET /accounts.

tools.name: persona_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: Get a single account by id — the persistent identity record for an end user. Returns JSON:API { data } containing PII. Persona REST: GET /accounts/{account_id}.

tools.name: persona_get_verification
tools.title: Get verification
tools.description: Get a single verification by id — one identity check within an inquiry (e.g. government-id, selfie, database, document). Returns JSON:API { data } with check results and PII. Persona REST: GET /verifications/{verification_id}.

tools.name: persona_list_reports
tools.title: List reports
tools.description: List reports (screening/monitoring results such as watchlist, adverse-media, or business lookups). Paginate via the JSON:API links.next cursor (page_after) / links.prev (page_before). Returns JSON:API { data:[...], links } — objects may contain PII. Persona REST: GET /reports.

tools.name: persona_get_report
tools.title: Get report
tools.description: Get a single report by id — a screening/monitoring result (e.g. watchlist, adverse-media, business lookup). Returns JSON:API { data } containing PII. Persona REST: GET /reports/{report_id}.

tools.name: persona_list_cases
tools.title: List cases
tools.description: List cases (manual-review workflow items grouping inquiries/reports for an analyst to adjudicate). Optionally filter by status, case_template_id, account_id, reference_id, inquiry_id, report_id, and paginate via the JSON:API links.next cursor (page_after) / links.prev (page_before). Returns JSON:API { data:[...], links } — objects contain PII. Persona REST: GET /cases.

tools.name: persona_get_case
tools.title: Get case
tools.description: Get a single case by id — a manual-review workflow item. Returns JSON:API { data } containing PII. Persona REST: GET /cases/{case_id}.

tools.name: persona_list_transactions
tools.title: List transactions
tools.description: List transactions (records submitted for transaction fraud/monitoring analysis). Optionally filter by reference_id and transaction_type_id, and paginate via the JSON:API links.next cursor (page_after) / links.prev (page_before). Returns JSON:API { data:[...], links } — objects may contain PII. Persona REST: GET /transactions.

tools.name: persona_get_transaction
tools.title: Get transaction
tools.description: Get a single transaction by id — a record submitted for transaction fraud/monitoring analysis. Returns JSON:API { data } containing PII. Persona REST: GET /transactions/{transaction_id}.

tools.name: persona_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: Get a single audit-trail event by id, including its name and payload. Returns JSON:API { data } — payloads may reference PII. Persona REST: GET /events/{event_id}.

tools.description: WRITE: adds a tag to an account (mutates state). Tags label/segment accounts for review and automation. Sends JSON body { meta: { "tag-name": <tag_name> } }. Persona REST: POST /accounts/{account_id}/add-tag.

servers.name: Printify
servers.description: Read shops, catalog blueprints, print providers, products and orders; create and publish products.

tools.name: printify_copy_products
tools.title: Copy products between shops
tools.description: Preview or copy selected products or a complete catalog between two Printify shops in the same account. Preserves title, description, blueprint/provider, variant IDs/prices/enabled flags, artwork IDs and print-area transforms. Preserves canvas side printing and image pattern rotation. This initial workflow does not copy tags, SKUs, channel IDs, publication state or generated mockups. Products with text/personalization layers are explicitly refused because their creation fields are read-only. Preview by default. confirm:true starts/resumes a durable bounded job; save job_id and keep calling with that job_id and confirm:true until complete. Duplicate prevention remembers copies made by this connector, including across restarts/jobs; pre-existing copies made elsewhere are not detected. An uncertain create is never automatically retried: inspect the target and use printify_resolve_copy. Do not change the source catalog during an all-products run. Requires shops.read/products.read/products.write. Confirmed copying requires the hosted connector's durable coordinator.

tools.name: printify_copy_status
tools.title: Check product copy progress
tools.description: Read a durable product-copy job's progress, target mappings, failures and uncertain writes. Verifies that the current token can access both shops. Does not create or retry products.

tools.name: printify_resolve_copy
tools.title: Resolve an uncertain product copy
tools.description: Resolve one failed or uncertain source product in a durable copy job. Provide an existing target_product_id to verify the exact supported fields against the checkpoint and record it as copied. Or set verified_not_created:true only after checking the target shop manually; this allows one future retry through printify_copy_products. Requires confirm:true, never creates/publishes/deletes anything itself. An ambiguous write must never be blindly retried.

tools.description: List products in a shop (paginated). Printify REST: GET /v1/shops/{shop_id}/products.json.

tools.name: printify_calculate_shipping

tools.description: Get a shipping price quote for a set of line items to a destination address. Non-destructive — it only prices, it does NOT place an order. `line_items` is an array where each item is one of {product_id, variant_id, quantity}, {print_provider_id, blueprint_id, variant_id, quantity}, or {sku, quantity}. `address_to` is the destination (first_name, last_name, email, phone, country, region, address1, address2, city, zip, company). Printify REST: POST /v1/shops/{shop_id}/orders/shipping.json.

tools.name: raisely_get_user

tools.name: raisely_list_subscriptions

tools.name: raisely_get_subscription
tools.title: Get a subscription

tools.name: raisely_list_posts
tools.title: List posts

tools.title: List tags

tools.name: raisely_list_campaign_donations
tools.title: List a campaign's donations
tools.description: Convenience: list donations for a specific campaign. Raisely API: GET /campaigns/{campaign}/donations. Returns { data:[...], pagination }.

tools.name: raisely_list_campaign_profiles
tools.title: List a campaign's profiles
tools.description: Convenience: list fundraising profiles for a specific campaign. Raisely API: GET /campaigns/{campaign}/profiles. Returns { data:[...], pagination }.

tools.name: raisely_list_user_donations
tools.title: List a user's donations
tools.description: Convenience: a donor's giving history. Raisely API: GET /users/{uuid}/donations. Returns { data:[...], pagination }.

tools.name: raisely_request
tools.title: Raw read request
tools.description: Power-user escape hatch: GET any Raisely API path not wrapped by a dedicated tool. READ-ONLY — only GET is allowed. Pass the FULL API path after the base, starting with a slash, INCLUDING any query string, e.g. "/subscriptions/{uuid}/donations" or "/donations?limit=50". Returns the parsed JSON.

tools.name: raisely_create_donation
tools.title: Record a donation
tools.description: MUTATES Raisely data: records a donation (use for OFFLINE/manual donations — e.g. cash or cheque). Raisely API: POST /donations with the body wrapped as { data: {...} }. Required by the API: amount (integer, in cents/smallest currency unit), currency (3-letter code), email (donor), type (ONLINE or OFFLINE), method (payment gateway, e.g. OFFLINE). Link it to a campaign/profile via campaignUuid/profileUuid. Everything else (firstName, lastName, message, date, items, public, private, ...) goes through `fields`. Returns the created donation.

tools.name: raisely_upsert_user
tools.title: Upsert a user
tools.description: MUTATES Raisely data: creates OR updates a supporter/donor, matched by email (safer than a plain create — no duplicates). Raisely API: POST /users/upsert with the body wrapped as { data: {...} }. Typed: email (the match key), firstName, lastName; everything else (phoneNumber, address, public, private, ...) via `fields`. Returns the upserted user.

tools.name: raisely_update_profile
tools.title: Update a fundraising profile
tools.description: MUTATES Raisely data: updates a fundraising profile's goal/name/story. Raisely API: PATCH /profiles/{path} with the body wrapped as { data: {...} } (only included fields change). Use `fields` for goal, name, description/story, public, private, and any other documented field. Set overwriteCustomFields:true to overwrite (rather than preserve) unspecified custom fields. The path is never sent in the body.

tools.name: raisely_create_post
tools.title: Create a post
tools.description: MUTATES Raisely data: publishes a post (a campaign/profile update). Raisely API: POST /posts with the body wrapped as { data: {...} }. Required by the API: path (the post's URL slug), body (the content), photoUrl. Link it to a profile via profileUuid (pass through `fields`). Extra fields (title, date, ...) via `fields`. Returns the created post.

tools.name: raisely_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: raisely_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Raisely tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: raisely_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Raisely (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: raisely_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Raisely Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run raisely_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find it in Raisely campaign admin → **Settings → Developers**. Your key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: How much has each of our campaigns raised so far?
List the donations received in the last 7 days with donor names and amounts.
Show the giving history for donor Jane Smith.
Add a supporter named Jane Smith with the email jane.smith@example.com.

tools.name: recharge_list_customers

servers.description: Correlate GitHub releases with Sentry issues and PagerDuty incidents.

tools.name: release_radar_whats_broken_since_last_deploy
tools.title: What's broken since the last deploy?
tools.description: COMPOSITE. Finds the latest GitHub deployment/release for a repo, then queries Sentry for unresolved issues SINCE that deploy's timestamp (the deploy time drives the Sentry window), then looks up who's currently on-call in PagerDuty — and synthesizes one situational-awareness object. Degrades gracefully: if Sentry or PagerDuty creds are absent it returns what it can plus a note. GitHub is required (it's the anchor).

tools.name: release_radar_incident_snapshot
tools.title: Current incident snapshot
tools.description: COMPOSITE. A right-now on-call picture: top unresolved Sentry issues + active (triggered/acknowledged) PagerDuty incidents + who's currently on-call, fused into one snapshot with a human summary. Each service degrades independently if its creds are missing.

tools.name: release_radar_oncall_handoff
tools.title: On-call handoff briefing
tools.description: COMPOSITE. A start-of-shift briefing for whoever is currently on call, fusing all three services: (a) PagerDuty current on-call + any active (triggered/acknowledged) incidents they're inheriting, (b) the GitHub deployment/release that most recently shipped (what's live), and (c) Sentry's top unresolved errors. Correlates them into one object — including a heads-up when a fresh deploy coincides with active incidents (a likely culprit). Degrades gracefully: every service is optional; whatever's unconfigured or failing is named in `notes` and the briefing still returns. Never crashes.

tools.description: Low-level building block: the latest GitHub deployment for a repo (falls back to the latest release), returning sha + timestamp. Used internally by release_radar_whats_broken_since_last_deploy. GitHub: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/deployments.

servers.name: Scalingo
servers.description: Manage Scalingo PaaS apps, deployments, containers, logs and env vars from your AI assistant.

tools.name: scalingo_list_apps
tools.title: List apps
tools.description: List all Scalingo apps you can access in the current region. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps. Returns { apps: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_app
tools.title: Get an app
tools.description: Fetch a single app's details (region, stack, status, URLs, flags). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}. Returns { app }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_containers
tools.title: List containers (formation)
tools.description: List an app's container formation — the running process types with their amount and size (the current scaling). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/containers. Returns { containers: [{ name, amount, size }] }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_app_stats
tools.title: Get container stats
tools.description: Real-time per-container resource stats (CPU / memory / swap usage) for an app. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/stats. Returns { stats: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_deployments
tools.title: List deployments
tools.description: List an app's deployments (most recent first), paginated. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/deployments. Returns { deployments: [...], meta: { pagination } }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_deployment
tools.title: Get a deployment
tools.description: Fetch a single deployment's details (status, git_ref, pusher, image size, timestamps). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/deployments/{deployment_id}. Returns { deployment }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_app_logs
tools.title: Get recent app logs
tools.description: Fetch recent application log lines. Scalingo returns an authenticated logs_url (GET /v1/apps/{app}/logs → { logs_url }); this tool then downloads the last N lines from it (dump mode) and returns them as text. Returns { logs_url, lines }. If the follow-up download fails, only logs_url is returned so you can fetch it yourself.

tools.name: scalingo_list_variables
tools.title: List environment variables
tools.description: List an app's environment variables. WARNING: this exposes secret VALUES (API keys, database URLs, etc.). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/variables. Returns { variables: [{ id, name, value }] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_collaborators
tools.title: List collaborators
tools.description: List an app's collaborators (users invited to the app) and their status. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/collaborators. Returns { collaborators: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_domains
tools.title: List domains
tools.description: List an app's custom domains and their TLS/canonical status. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/domains. Returns { domains: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_addons
tools.title: List addons
tools.description: List the addons (databases, services) provisioned on an app. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/addons. Returns { addons: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_addon_providers
tools.title: List addon providers
tools.description: List the addon providers available on Scalingo (databases, monitoring, etc.) with their plans embedded. Scalingo API: GET /v1/addon_providers. Returns { addon_providers: [{ ..., plans: [...] }] }.

tools.name: scalingo_list_app_events
tools.title: List app events
tools.description: List an app's activity events (deployments, scaling, restarts, collaborator changes, etc.), paginated. Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/events. Returns { events: [...], meta: { pagination } }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_operation
tools.title: Get an operation
tools.description: Poll the status of an asynchronous operation (e.g. a scale or restart returns an operation to track). Scalingo API: GET /v1/apps/{app}/operations/{operation_id}. Returns { operation } with status pending|running|done|error.

tools.name: scalingo_list_regions
tools.title: List regions
tools.description: List the Scalingo regions available to your account, each with its API/dashboard/database hosts. Useful to discover the right SCALINGO_REGION. Scalingo API: GET (auth host) /v1/regions. Returns { regions: [...] }.

tools.name: scalingo_get_account
tools.title: Get current account
tools.description: Fetch the authenticated user's account (id, email, username, fullname, company). Scalingo API: GET /v1/users/self. Returns { user }.

tools.name: scalingo_request
tools.title: Raw read request
tools.description: Power-user escape hatch: GET any Scalingo API path not wrapped by a dedicated tool. READ-ONLY — only GET is allowed. Path is taken after /v1 (e.g. "/apps/my-app/alerts"). By default hits the regional API; set on_auth_host:true for auth-host resources (regions, scm_integrations, tokens). Scalingo API: GET {path}.

tools.name: scalingo_restart_app
tools.title: Restart app
tools.description: MUTATES Scalingo infrastructure — restarts an app's containers. Optionally restart only specific process types via scope; omit scope to restart everything. Returns 202 Accepted (track via scalingo_get_operation). Scalingo API: POST /v1/apps/{app}/restart.

tools.name: scalingo_scale_app
tools.title: Scale app
tools.description: MUTATES Scalingo infrastructure — sets the container formation (number and/or size of each process type). Only the container types you include are changed. Returns 202 Accepted (track via scalingo_get_operation). Scalingo API: POST /v1/apps/{app}/scale.

tools.name: scalingo_set_variables
tools.title: Set environment variables (bulk)
tools.description: MUTATES Scalingo infrastructure — creates or updates environment variables in bulk (each { name, value } is created if new or updated if it exists). This usually triggers a restart to apply the new env. Names ≤64 chars, values ≤8192 chars. Scalingo API: PUT /v1/apps/{app}/variables. Returns { variables }.

tools.name: scalingo_trigger_deployment

tools.description: MUTATES Scalingo infrastructure — triggers a new deployment from a source archive URL (a tar.gz reachable by Scalingo). To roll back, re-deploy a previous git_ref/archive — there is no separate rollback endpoint. Scalingo API: POST /v1/apps/{app}/deployments. Returns { deployment }.

tools.title: List teams

tools.description: List incidents for a team — {incidents:[...], totalIncidents, totalOpenIncidents, pagination}. Each incident carries title, status, priority, severity, and timing. Spike: GET /incidents (team-scoped).

tools.name: spike_list_triggered_incidents

tools.description: List currently TRIGGERED (open, unacknowledged) incidents for a team — the active fire-fighting queue. Spike: GET /incidents/triggered (team-scoped).

tools.title: Get on-call schedule

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Squadcast (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: squadcast_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription

Requires confirm: true. Run squadcast_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: What incidents were triggered in the last 24 hours?
Show the timeline of events for our latest incident.
Which on-call schedules does our platform team have set up?
Add a note to our latest open incident saying the database restart is underway.

servers.name: StatusPal
servers.description: Read status-page status, services, incidents and metrics; create, update and publish incidents.

tools.name: statuspal_get_summary
tools.title: Get status page summary
tools.description: Get the FULL status-page summary — status_page, services[], incidents[], maintenances[], upcoming_maintenances[], info_notices[], and current_status_type. StatusPal: GET /status_pages/{subdomain}/summary.

tools.name: statuspal_get_status
tools.title: Get overall status
tools.description: Get the current overall status of the status page (the aggregate status type). StatusPal: GET /status_pages/{subdomain}/status.

tools.name: statuspal_list_services
tools.title: List services
tools.description: List the services on a status page — each with {id, name, current_incident_type, children[]}. StatusPal: GET /status_pages/{subdomain}/services.

tools.name: statuspal_get_service_status
tools.title: Get service status
tools.description: Get the current status of a single service by its id. StatusPal: GET /status_pages/{subdomain}/services/{service_id}/status.

tools.name: statuspal_list_incidents
tools.title: List incidents
tools.description: List incidents for a status page. Returns {incidents[], links:{next,prev}, meta:{total_count}}. Use `before`/`after` cursors to paginate and `type` to filter. StatusPal: GET /status_pages/{subdomain}/incidents.

tools.name: statuspal_get_incident
tools.title: Get incident
tools.description: Get a single incident by its id. StatusPal: GET /status_pages/{subdomain}/incidents/{incident_id}.

tools.name: statuspal_list_metrics
tools.title: List metrics
tools.description: List the metrics configured on a status page. Use `before`/`after` cursors to paginate. StatusPal: GET /status_pages/{subdomain}/metrics.

tools.name: statuspal_create_incident
tools.title: Create incident
tools.description: PUBLISHES a new incident to the LIVE public status page (and, with notify=true, emails/notifies subscribers). type="major" or "minor" is an outage incident; type="scheduled" creates a scheduled maintenance window. StatusPal: POST /status_pages/{subdomain}/incidents.

tools.name: statuspal_update_incident
tools.title: Update incident
tools.description: UPDATES an existing incident on the LIVE public status page (title/type/services/timing). StatusPal: PUT /status_pages/{subdomain}/incidents/{incident_id}.

tools.name: statuspal_create_incident_update
tools.title: Post incident update
tools.description: POSTS an update (e.g. investigating → identified → monitoring → resolved) to an existing incident on the LIVE public status page (and, with notify=true, notifies subscribers). StatusPal: POST /status_pages/{subdomain}/incidents/{incident_id}/updates.

tools.name: statuspal_delete_incident
tools.title: Delete incident
tools.description: DELETES an incident from the LIVE public status page — this permanently removes it. StatusPal: DELETE /status_pages/{subdomain}/incidents/{incident_id}.

tools.name: statuspal_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: statuspal_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the StatusPal tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: statuspal_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's StatusPal Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run statuspal_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find it in StatusPal → **Account settings → API**. Your key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

List the incidents on our status page and show their current state.
Show whether any maintenance is coming up.
What metrics do we show on our status page?

servers.name: Stream
servers.description: Query channels, search messages, and read threads, users and reactions in your Stream Chat app.

tools.name: stream_get_app
tools.title: Get app settings
tools.description: Fetch the Stream app's settings and configured channel types. Good first call to confirm credentials and discover available channel types. GET /api/v2/app.

tools.name: stream_query_channels
tools.title: Query channels
tools.description: List/filter channels by a Stream query filter. e.g. filter {"type":"messaging"} or {"members":{"$in":["user-1"]}}. Returns channels with recent state. POST /api/v2/chat/channels.

tools.name: stream_get_channel
tools.title: Get channel state + recent messages
tools.description: Fetch a single channel's state (config, members) and its most recent messages. Note: uses Stream's get-or-create endpoint — for an existing channel it reads; if the type/id does not exist it may be created empty. POST /api/v2/chat/channels/{type}/{id}/query.

tools.name: stream_search_messages
tools.title: Search messages
tools.description: Search messages across channels. Scope with a channel filter (filter, e.g. {"type":"messaging"}) plus EITHER a full-text `query` OR a `message_filter` object (e.g. {"text":{"$q":"refund"}}). GET /api/v2/chat/search.

tools.name: stream_get_message
tools.title: Get a message
tools.description: Fetch a single message by its id. GET /api/v2/chat/messages/{id}.

tools.name: stream_get_replies
tools.title: Get thread replies
tools.description: Fetch the reply messages in a thread, given the parent message id. GET /api/v2/chat/messages/{parent_id}/replies.

tools.name: stream_get_reactions
tools.title: Get message reactions
tools.description: List the reactions on a message. GET /api/v2/chat/messages/{id}/reactions.

tools.name: stream_query_members
tools.title: Query channel members
tools.description: List/filter the members of one channel. Requires the channel type + id. Optional member filter, e.g. {"name":{"$autocomplete":"jo"}}. GET /api/v2/chat/members.

tools.name: stream_query_users
tools.title: Query users
tools.description: List/filter users in the app. e.g. filter {"role":{"$eq":"admin"}} or {"id":{"$in":["u1"]}}. GET /api/v2/users.

tools.name: stream_query_threads
tools.title: Query threads
tools.description: List threads (messages with replies). Server-side calls should pass a user_id to scope thread read-state to that user. POST /api/v2/chat/threads.

tools.name: stream_get_unread_counts
tools.title: Get unread counts for a user
tools.description: Fetch total and per-channel unread message/mention counts for one user. GET /api/v2/chat/unread.

tools.name: stream_send_message
tools.title: Send a message (WRITE — posts to Stream)
tools.description: ⚠️ WRITE: post a new message to a channel, attributed to user_id (must be an existing user in the app). POST /api/v2/chat/channels/{type}/{id}/message.

tools.name: stream_send_reaction
tools.title: Send a reaction (WRITE — posts to Stream)
tools.description: ⚠️ WRITE: add a reaction (e.g. "like", "love") to a message, attributed to user_id (must be an existing user). POST /api/v2/chat/messages/{id}/reaction.

tools.name: stream_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: stream_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Stream tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: stream_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Stream (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: stream_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Stream Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run stream_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find both in the Stream dashboard → **App → API keys**. Your key and secret are used only to call the API on your behalf (the secret signs a server-side token) and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

examples: Find chat messages that mention 'refund' across our channels.
How many unread messages does user jane_smith have?
Which channels exist in our app right now?
Show me the replies in the thread under our latest announcement.

servers.name: Svix
servers.description: Send and debug webhooks — applications, endpoints, messages, delivery attempts and replays.

tools.name: svix_list_applications
tools.title: List applications
tools.description: List the applications (your tenants/customers) in the Svix environment. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app.

tools.name: svix_get_application
tools.title: Get one application
tools.description: Fetch a single application by its Svix id or your own uid. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app/{app_id}.

tools.name: svix_list_endpoints
tools.title: List endpoints
tools.description: List the webhook endpoints registered for one application. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app/{app_id}/endpoint.

tools.name: svix_get_endpoint
tools.title: Get one endpoint
tools.description: Fetch a single webhook endpoint, including its URL, subscribed event types and channels. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app/{app_id}/endpoint/{endpoint_id}.

tools.name: svix_get_endpoint_stats
tools.title: Get endpoint delivery stats
tools.description: Read delivery statistics for one endpoint — counts of success, pending, sending and fail. The fastest way to see whether an endpoint is healthy. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app/{app_id}/endpoint/{endpoint_id}/stats.

tools.name: svix_list_messages
tools.title: List messages
tools.description: List the webhook messages sent for one application, newest first. Filter by event type, channel, tag or time window. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app/{app_id}/msg.

tools.name: svix_get_message
tools.title: Get one message
tools.description: Fetch a single message, including its event type and payload. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app/{app_id}/msg/{msg_id}.

tools.name: svix_list_attempts_by_message
tools.title: List delivery attempts for a message
tools.description: List every delivery attempt Svix made for one message, across endpoints — status, response code and body. This is the tool for answering 'why did this webhook not arrive?'. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app/{app_id}/attempt/msg/{msg_id}.

tools.name: svix_list_attempts_by_endpoint
tools.title: List delivery attempts for an endpoint
tools.description: List delivery attempts against one endpoint, newest first. Filter by status to find the failures. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app/{app_id}/attempt/endpoint/{endpoint_id}.

tools.name: svix_list_endpoint_messages
tools.title: List messages for an endpoint
tools.description: List the messages destined for one endpoint, with each message's delivery status. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/app/{app_id}/endpoint/{endpoint_id}/msg.

tools.name: svix_list_event_types
tools.title: List event types
tools.description: List the event types defined in the environment — the catalogue endpoints can subscribe to. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/event-type.

tools.name: svix_get_event_type
tools.title: Get one event type
tools.description: Fetch a single event type by name, including its description and JSON schema. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/event-type/{event_type_name}.

tools.name: svix_list_background_tasks
tools.title: List background tasks
tools.description: List Svix background tasks (bulk replays, expunges, imports) with their status. Use it to follow up a recover or replay. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/background-task.

tools.name: svix_health
tools.title: Check API health
tools.description: Check that the Svix API is reachable and the API key works. Returns 200 with an empty body when healthy. Svix REST: GET /api/v1/health.

tools.name: svix_create_application
tools.title: Create an application
tools.description: Create a new application (one tenant/customer of yours) in the Svix environment. Svix REST: POST /api/v1/app.

tools.name: svix_create_endpoint
tools.title: Create an endpoint
tools.description: Register a webhook endpoint URL for one application, optionally scoped to specific event types and channels. Svix REST: POST /api/v1/app/{app_id}/endpoint.

tools.name: svix_send_message
tools.title: Send a message
tools.description: Send a webhook message to every endpoint of an application subscribed to the event type. This delivers real traffic to your customers' URLs. Svix REST: POST /api/v1/app/{app_id}/msg.

tools.name: svix_resend_message
tools.title: Resend a message to one endpoint
tools.description: Queue one message for redelivery to one endpoint. The usual fix after a customer's endpoint was down. Svix REST: POST /api/v1/app/{app_id}/msg/{msg_id}/endpoint/{endpoint_id}/resend.

tools.name: svix_recover_endpoint
tools.title: Recover an endpoint's failed messages
tools.description: Replay every failed message for one endpoint since a timestamp. Runs as a background task — follow it with svix_list_background_tasks. Svix REST: POST /api/v1/app/{app_id}/endpoint/{endpoint_id}/recover.

tools.name: svix_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: svix_request_feature

tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Svix tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: svix_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Svix (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: svix_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Svix Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run svix_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create one in the Svix dashboard → **API Access**. Your token is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Which webhook deliveries failed for our customer Acme Ltd recently?
What are the delivery success and failure counts for Acme Ltd's endpoint?
Which event types can customers subscribe to?
Show the latest failed delivery and its response for our first customer endpoint.

servers.name: Swell
servers.description: Manage your Swell headless-commerce store — products, orders, customers, and subscriptions.

tools.name: swell_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products in the store, with MongoDB-style filtering, sorting, search, field selection, and expansion. Swell backend REST API: GET /products.

tools.name: swell_get_product
tools.title: Get a product
tools.description: Fetch a single product by its record id or its slug. Supports `expand` and `fields`. Swell backend REST API: GET /products/{id}.

tools.name: swell_list_categories
tools.title: List categories
tools.description: List product categories, with filtering, sorting, search, and expansion. Swell backend REST API: GET /categories.

tools.name: swell_list_orders
tools.title: List orders
tools.description: List orders, with MongoDB-style filtering, sorting, search, and expansion. Swell backend REST API: GET /orders.

tools.name: swell_get_order
tools.title: Get an order
tools.description: Fetch a single order by its record id or its order number. Supports `expand` and `fields`. Swell backend REST API: GET /orders/{id}.

tools.name: swell_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List customers. In Swell, customers are the `accounts` model — this queries GET /accounts, with filtering, sorting, search, and expansion.

tools.name: swell_get_customer
tools.title: Get a customer
tools.description: Fetch a single customer (Swell `accounts` model) by id. Supports `expand` and `fields`. Swell backend REST API: GET /accounts/{id}.

tools.name: swell_list_carts
tools.title: List carts
tools.description: List shopping carts (including abandoned carts), with filtering, sorting, and expansion. Swell backend REST API: GET /carts.

tools.name: swell_list_subscriptions
tools.title: List subscriptions
tools.description: List subscriptions, with filtering, sorting, and expansion. Swell backend REST API: GET /subscriptions.

tools.name: swell_get_subscription
tools.title: Get a subscription
tools.description: Fetch a single subscription by id. Supports `expand`. Swell backend REST API: GET /subscriptions/{id}.

tools.name: swell_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices (typically subscription invoices), with filtering, sorting, and expansion. Swell backend REST API: GET /invoices.

tools.name: swell_list_coupons
tools.title: List coupons
tools.description: List discount coupons, with filtering and sorting. Swell backend REST API: GET /coupons.

tools.name: swell_query
tools.title: Query any collection (read-only)
tools.description: Power tool: read-only (GET only) access to ANY Swell model not covered by a dedicated tool — e.g. stock, promotions, giftcards, payments, shipments, settings. Supply the collection name plus the usual list params (limit, page, where, sort, expand, fields, search). Swell backend REST API: GET /{collection}.

tools.name: swell_create_product
tools.title: Create a product
tools.description: MUTATES LIVE STORE DATA. Create a new product in the store. Provide the common fields directly (name is required); anything else goes in `fields`, which is merged into the request body. Swell backend REST API: POST /products.

tools.name: swell_update_product
tools.title: Update a product
tools.description: MUTATES LIVE STORE DATA. Partially update an existing product by id. Provide the id plus a `fields` object of attributes to change. Swell backend REST API: PUT /products/{id}.

tools.name: swell_update_order
tools.title: Update an order
tools.description: MUTATES A LIVE ORDER. Partially update an existing order by id — e.g. change status, fulfillment, or notes. Provide the id plus a `fields` object of attributes to change, e.g. {"status":"complete"}. Swell backend REST API: PUT /orders/{id}.

tools.name: swell_usage_status

Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. tools.name: swell_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Swell Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run swell_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find both in the Swell dashboard → **Developer → API keys** (use a **secret** key, not a public one). Your credentials are used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

servers.name: Tailscale
servers.description: Read devices, users, keys, ACLs and DNS for a tailnet; manage devices, routes and auth keys.

tools.name: tailscale_list_devices
tools.title: List devices
tools.description: List all devices in the tailnet (name, addresses, OS, last seen, tags, etc.). Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/devices.

tools.name: tailscale_get_device
tools.title: Get device
tools.description: Get a single device by id. Tailscale REST: GET /device/{deviceId}.

tools.name: tailscale_list_device_routes
tools.title: List device routes
tools.description: List the subnet routes a device advertises and which are enabled. Tailscale REST: GET /device/{deviceId}/routes.

tools.name: tailscale_list_keys
tools.title: List keys
tools.description: List auth keys and API access tokens for the tailnet. Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/keys.

tools.name: tailscale_get_key
tools.title: Get key
tools.description: Get details of a single auth key / API access token by id (capabilities, expiry, usage). Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/keys/{keyId}.

tools.name: tailscale_get_policy_file
tools.title: Get policy file
tools.description: Get the tailnet's ACL / policy file (returned as JSON via the Accept header, not HuJSON). Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/acl.

tools.name: tailscale_list_dns_nameservers
tools.title: List DNS nameservers
tools.description: List the global DNS nameservers configured for the tailnet. Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/dns/nameservers.

tools.name: tailscale_get_dns_preferences
tools.title: Get DNS preferences
tools.description: Get the tailnet's DNS preferences (e.g. whether MagicDNS is enabled). Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/dns/preferences.

tools.name: tailscale_list_dns_searchpaths
tools.title: List DNS search paths
tools.description: List the DNS search paths (search domains) configured for the tailnet. Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/dns/searchpaths.

tools.name: tailscale_get_split_dns
tools.title: Get split DNS
tools.description: Get the tailnet's split-DNS configuration — a map of domain → nameservers. Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/dns/split-dns.

tools.name: tailscale_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List users of the tailnet, optionally filtered by type, role or status. Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/users.

tools.name: tailscale_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: Get a single user by id. Tailscale REST: GET /users/{userId}.

tools.name: tailscale_list_webhooks
tools.title: List webhooks
tools.description: List the webhook endpoints configured for the tailnet. Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/webhooks.

tools.name: tailscale_get_tailnet_settings
tools.title: Get tailnet settings
tools.description: Get the tailnet's settings (device approval, key expiry, posture, etc.). Tailscale REST: GET /tailnet/{tailnet}/settings.

tools.name: tailscale_authorize_device
tools.title: Authorize device
tools.description: Authorize or de-authorize a device (only relevant when device approval is enabled for the tailnet). Tailscale REST: POST /device/{deviceId}/authorized.

tools.name: tailscale_set_device_name
tools.title: Set device name
tools.description: Set (rename) a device's name. Tailscale REST: POST /device/{deviceId}/name.

tools.name: tailscale_set_device_tags
tools.title: Set device tags

tools.name: tailscale_expire_device_key
tools.title: Expire device key
