tools.name: tailscale_set_device_routes
tools.title: Set device routes
tools.description: Set the subnet routes ENABLED for a device (from the routes it advertises). REPLACES the enabled set. Tailscale REST: POST /device/{deviceId}/routes.

tools.name: tailscale_create_auth_key
tools.title: Create auth key
tools.description: Create a new auth key for the tailnet (used to register new devices). Tailscale REST: POST /tailnet/{tailnet}/keys.

tools.name: tailscale_delete_key
tools.title: Delete key
tools.description: Delete (revoke) an auth key or API access token by id — a security response. Tailscale REST: DELETE /tailnet/{tailnet}/keys/{keyId}.

tools.name: tailscale_delete_device
tools.title: Delete device
tools.description: Delete a device, removing it from the tailnet. Tailscale REST: DELETE /device/{deviceId}.

tools.name: tailscale_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: tailscale_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Tailscale tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: tailscale_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Tailscale (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). tools.name: tailscale_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Tailscale Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run tailscale_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

List the users on our network and their roles.

Rename the device 'laptop-3' to 'front-desk-pc'.

servers.name: Text-Em-All
servers.description: Send and track Text-Em-All broadcasts, texts and contact lists.

tools.name: text_em_all_get_account
tools.title: Get account settings
tools.description: Fetch your Text-Em-All account settings — company/billing info plus credit balances (AvailableCallUnits, CallBalance) used for sending. Text-Em-All API: GET /v1/account. Use this first to confirm your credentials work.

tools.name: text_em_all_list_broadcasts
tools.title: List broadcasts
tools.description: List broadcasts (text + voice campaigns) as a paged Feed { Size, Items:[...], Previous, Next }. Text-Em-All API: GET /v1/broadcasts. Filter with equals-style `params` (e.g. BroadcastStatus=Complete) and order with `sortby`. For date-range operators (StartDate~gte~2024-01-01) use the text_em_all_request escape hatch.

tools.name: text_em_all_get_broadcast
tools.title: Get a broadcast
tools.description: Fetch a single broadcast by id, including its status and summary. Text-Em-All API: GET /v1/broadcasts/{id}.

tools.name: text_em_all_get_broadcast_details
tools.title: Get broadcast delivery details
tools.description: Fetch per-contact delivery details/results for a broadcast (who was reached, delivery status). Text-Em-All API: GET /v1/broadcasts/{id}/details.

tools.name: text_em_all_list_text_numbers
tools.title: List text numbers
tools.description: List the toll-free text (SMS) numbers on your account as a Feed. Each TextNumber has a TextNumberID you need to send a 1:1 conversation text (see text_em_all_send_text_message). Text-Em-All API: GET /v1/textnumbers.

tools.name: text_em_all_list_lists
tools.title: List contact lists
tools.description: List saved contact lists (groups you can broadcast to) as a Feed; each List has a ListID/ListName. Text-Em-All API: GET /v1/lists. NOTE: inferred from the API's List model — if your account/endpoint differs, use the text_em_all_request escape hatch.

tools.name: text_em_all_get_authorization_token
tools.title: Get a user authorization token
tools.description: Exchange a Text-Em-All account username + PIN/password for that user's authorization token (the value you set as TEXTEMALL_AUTH_TOKEN). Text-Em-All API: POST /v1/user/login. Signed with your App/Secret key only (no user token yet). Returns { AuthToken }. Use this once to bootstrap; store the token in config thereafter.

tools.name: text_em_all_get_conversations_sso_url
tools.title: Get a single-sign-on conversations URL
tools.description: Generate a single-sign-on URL to the Text-Em-All conversations UI (open in a browser/iframe). Optionally scope it to one conversation thread by passing a toll-free textNumber + the other phoneNumber. Text-Em-All API: POST /v1/singlesignon/conversations. Returns { Url }. No account data is changed.

tools.name: text_em_all_request
tools.title: Raw read request
tools.description: Power-user escape hatch: GET any Text-Em-All API path not wrapped by a dedicated tool. READ-ONLY — only GET is allowed. Pass the FULL API path after the origin, starting with a slash, INCLUDING any query string, e.g. "/v1/broadcasts?StartDate~gte~2024-01-01&sortby=-StartDate" or "/v1/textnumbers". Returns the parsed JSON.

tools.name: text_em_all_create_broadcast
tools.title: Send a broadcast
tools.description: MUTATES Text-Em-All data AND SENDS MESSAGES (spends account credits): creates + sends a broadcast to the given contacts. Text-Em-All API: POST /v1/broadcasts. Set broadcastType to 'SMS' (a text broadcast — provide textMessage) or 'Announcement' (a voice broadcast — provide voiceText for text-to-speech, or a pre-recorded AudioID via `fields.Audio`). Contacts is a list of { primaryPhone, firstName?, lastName?, notes? }. Extra documented fields (CallerID, TextNumberID, Lists, RetryTimes, CallThrottle, MaxMessageLength, StartDate, CheckCallingWindow) go through `fields` (PascalCase). Returns the created broadcast.

tools.name: text_em_all_send_text_message
tools.title: Send a conversation text
tools.description: MUTATES Text-Em-All data AND SENDS A TEXT (spends credits): sends a 1:1 conversation text message immediately from one of your toll-free text numbers to a single contact. Text-Em-All API: POST /v1/conversations. You need a textNumberId (from text_em_all_list_text_numbers). Returns the conversation.

tools.name: text_em_all_create_draft_broadcast
tools.title: Create a draft broadcast
tools.description: MUTATES Text-Em-All data (creates a DRAFT — does NOT send anything): stages a broadcast with the given contacts and returns a single-sign-on URL to finish + send it in the Text-Em-All UI. Safer than text_em_all_create_broadcast when a human should review before sending. Text-Em-All API: POST /v1/draftbroadcasts. Returns { SingleSignOnUrl, ... }.

tools.name: text_em_all_add_account_user
tools.title: Add an account user
tools.description: MUTATES Text-Em-All data: adds a new user to your account (a master user can do this). Text-Em-All API: POST /v1/account/users. Provide the user's fields via `fields` using the API's PascalCase names (e.g. UserName, FirstName, LastName, EmailAddress, Permissions). Returns the created user.

tools.name: text_em_all_update_account_user
tools.title: Update an account user
tools.description: MUTATES Text-Em-All data: updates an existing account user. Text-Em-All API: PUT /v1/account/users/{user_id}. Provide the fields to change via `fields` (PascalCase, e.g. FirstName, LastName, EmailAddress, Permissions). The user_id is never sent in the body. Returns the updated user.

servers.name: Trigger.dev
servers.description: Debug background jobs — runs, traces, spans, schedules, queues and deployments.

tools.name: trigger_list_runs
tools.title: List runs
tools.description: List task runs, filtered by status, task, tag, queue, schedule or a time window. This is the main read for 'what ran, and what failed?'. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/runs.

tools.name: trigger_get_run
tools.title: Get one run
tools.description: Fetch a single run's outcome — its status, output, error and attempts. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/runs/{runId}/result.

tools.name: trigger_get_run_trace
tools.title: Get a run's trace
tools.description: Fetch the full execution trace of a run — every span, with timings and nesting. The tool for 'where did this run spend its time, and where did it break?'. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/runs/{runId}/trace.

tools.name: trigger_get_run_span
tools.title: Get one span of a run
tools.description: Fetch a single span from a run's trace, with its own logs and attributes. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/runs/{runId}/spans/{spanId}.

tools.name: trigger_list_run_events
tools.title: List a run's events
tools.description: List the lifecycle events of one run — queued, dequeued, started, retried, completed. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/runs/{runId}/events.

tools.name: trigger_get_run_metadata
tools.title: Get a run's metadata
tools.description: Fetch the mutable metadata a run has written about itself — progress, checkpoints and custom state. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/runs/{runId}/metadata.

tools.name: trigger_get_batch_results
tools.title: Get a batch's results
tools.description: Fetch the outcome of every run in a batch. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/batches/{batchId}/results.

tools.name: trigger_list_schedules
tools.title: List schedules
tools.description: List the cron schedules configured for tasks, with their next run times. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/schedules.

tools.name: trigger_get_schedule
tools.title: Get one schedule
tools.description: Fetch a single schedule with its cron expression, timezone and active state. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/schedules/{scheduleId}.

tools.name: trigger_list_queues
tools.title: List queues
tools.description: List task queues with their concurrency limits and current depth — where you look when work is backing up. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/queues.

tools.name: trigger_get_queue
tools.title: Get one queue
tools.description: Fetch a single queue's concurrency limit, running count and queued count. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/queues/{queue}.

tools.name: trigger_get_current_deployment
tools.title: Get the current deployment
tools.description: Fetch the deployment currently serving the key's environment — its version, git ref and status. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/deployments/current.

tools.name: trigger_list_env_vars
tools.title: List environment variables
tools.description: List the environment variables configured for a project environment. Values may be redacted depending on the key's permissions. READ ONLY — this server exposes no env-var writes. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/projects/{projectRef}/envvars/{env}.

tools.name: trigger_list_waitpoint_tokens
tools.title: List waitpoint tokens
tools.description: List outstanding waitpoint tokens — runs paused waiting for an external signal. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/waitpoints/tokens.

tools.name: trigger_list_bulk_actions
tools.title: List bulk actions
tools.description: List bulk replay and cancel operations and their progress. Trigger.dev: GET /api/v1/bulk-actions.

tools.name: trigger_cancel_run
tools.title: Cancel a run
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight run. Note this is the one endpoint on API v2, not v1. Trigger.dev: POST /api/v2/runs/{runId}/cancel.

tools.name: trigger_replay_run
tools.title: Replay a run
tools.description: Re-run one specific past run with the same payload. This EXECUTES your production task again — the same side effects it had the first time. Trigger.dev: POST /api/v1/runs/{runId}/replay.

tools.name: trigger_reschedule_run

tools.name: trigger_activate_schedule

tools.description: Resume a paused schedule so it fires again. Trigger.dev: POST /api/v1/schedules/{scheduleId}/activate.

tools.name: trigger_deactivate_schedule

tools.name: trigger_pause_queue

tools.name: unkey_list_api_keys

tools.name: unkey_list_identities

tools.name: unkey_get_identity

tools.name: unkey_list_permissions

tools.title: List roles
tools.description: List the roles defined in the workspace. Read-only despite being a POST. Unkey: POST /v2/permissions.listRoles.

tools.name: unkey_list_ratelimit_overrides
tools.title: List rate-limit overrides
tools.description: List the per-identifier overrides in one rate-limit namespace. Read-only despite being a POST. Unkey: POST /v2/ratelimit.listOverrides.

tools.name: unkey_get_ratelimit_override
tools.title: Get one rate-limit override
tools.description: Fetch the override for one identifier in a namespace. Read-only despite being a POST. Unkey: POST /v2/ratelimit.getOverride.

tools.name: unkey_query_verification_analytics
tools.title: Query key-verification analytics
tools.description: Run a read-only SQL query over key-verification analytics. The query must use one of the public aliases: key_verifications_v1, key_verifications_per_minute_v1, key_verifications_per_hour_v1, key_verifications_per_day_v1 or key_verifications_per_month_v1. Physical default.* table names are rejected, and results are scoped to your workspace. Unkey: POST /v2/analytics.getVerifications.

tools.name: unkey_create_api
tools.title: Create an API
tools.description: Create a new API namespace to issue keys under. Unkey: POST /v2/apis.createApi.

tools.name: unkey_create_key
tools.title: Create an API key
tools.description: Issue a new API key under an API. The plaintext key is returned ONCE in the response and cannot be retrieved later unless recoverable is set. Unkey: POST /v2/keys.createKey.

tools.name: unkey_update_key
tools.title: Update a key
tools.description: Change a key's name, owner, metadata, expiry, roles, permissions or enabled state. Unkey: POST /v2/keys.updateKey.

tools.name: unkey_update_key_credits
tools.title: Update a key's credits
tools.description: Set, increment or decrement a key's remaining credits. Use set with no value for unlimited. Unkey: POST /v2/keys.updateCredits.

tools.name: unkey_delete_key
tools.title: Delete a key
tools.description: Revoke a key. By default this is a soft delete the key stops working but stays queryable; pass permanent to erase it. Unkey: POST /v2/keys.deleteKey.

tools.name: unkey_create_identity
tools.title: Create an identity
tools.description: Create an identity — an end user or organisation that keys and shared rate limits attach to. Unkey: POST /v2/identities.createIdentity.

tools.name: unkey_set_ratelimit_override
tools.title: Set a rate-limit override
tools.description: Set a custom rate limit for one identifier in a namespace — how you raise or lower a single customer's limit. Unkey: POST /v2/ratelimit.setOverride.

tools.name: unkey_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: unkey_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Unkey tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: unkey_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Unkey (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: unkey_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Unkey Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run unkey_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create one in Unkey → **Settings → Root Keys**. Your token is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: List the customer identities we have set up, with their saved details.
How many verifications did our keys have in the last 7 days?
Show how many key checks passed or failed in the last seven days.
List the roles and permissions we have set up for customer access.

servers.name: YouCanBook.me
servers.description: Manage YouCanBook.me bookings, booking pages, appointment types, team members and locations.

tools.name: youcanbookme_list_bookings
tools.title: List bookings
tools.description: List bookings (appointments) on the YouCanBookMe account. YCBM API: GET /v1/bookings. Filter by profileId (booking page), an after/before time window, cancelled status, and a free-text searchText; select fields with `fields`. Paginated via page (0-based) + maxResults. Returns a JSON array of bookings.

tools.name: youcanbookme_get_booking
tools.title: Get a booking
tools.description: Fetch a single booking (appointment) by id. YCBM API: GET /v1/bookings/{bookingId}. Use `fields` to select which fields to return. Returns the booking object.

tools.name: youcanbookme_list_profiles
tools.title: List profiles (booking pages)
tools.description: List all profiles (booking pages) on the account. YCBM API: GET /v1/profiles. A profile is a bookable page with its own subdomain, appointment types, team members, and locations. Use `fields` to select fields (e.g. "id,title,subdomain"). Paginated via page (0-based) + maxResults. Returns a JSON array of profiles.

tools.name: youcanbookme_get_profile
tools.title: Get a profile (booking page)
tools.description: Fetch a single profile (booking page) by id. YCBM API: GET /v1/profiles/{profileId}. Use `fields` to select fields, including nested sub-resources (appointmentTypes, teamMembers, locations). Returns the profile object.

tools.name: youcanbookme_list_team_members
tools.title: List a profile's team members
tools.description: List the team members configured on a profile (booking page). YCBM API: GET /v1/profiles/{profileId} with a teamMembers field selection. Returns the profile's teamMembers block (each member has id, name, email, description, pic, calendarId).

tools.name: youcanbookme_list_appointment_types
tools.title: List a profile's appointment types
tools.description: List the appointment types configured on a profile (booking page). YCBM API: GET /v1/profiles/{profileId} with an appointmentTypes field selection. Returns the profile's appointmentTypes block (each with id, name, description, slotLength, price).

tools.name: youcanbookme_list_locations
tools.title: List a profile's locations
tools.description: List the locations configured on a profile (booking page). YCBM API: GET /v1/profiles/{profileId} with a locations field selection. Returns the profile's locations block (each with id, kind, value, notes, strategy).

tools.name: youcanbookme_list_available_accounts
tools.title: List available accounts (calendars)
tools.description: List the accounts/calendars available to your account — used to find the calendarId for a team member. YCBM API: GET /v1/{accountId}/availableAccounts (accountId is taken from your configured credentials). Returns a JSON array.

tools.name: youcanbookme_request
tools.title: Raw read request
tools.description: Power-user escape hatch: GET any YCBM API path not wrapped by a dedicated tool. READ-ONLY — only GET is allowed. Pass the FULL API path after the origin, starting with a slash, INCLUDING any query string, e.g. "/v1/bookings?maxResults=5" or "/v1/profiles". Returns the parsed JSON.

tools.name: youcanbookme_create_booking
tools.title: Create a booking
tools.description: MUTATES YouCanBookMe data: creates a booking (appointment) on a profile. YCBM API: POST /v1/bookings (JSON). Required: profileId, startsAt, endsAt (ISO 8601 times). Optional: title, timeZone, locale, units. Complex fields like `answers` (form-field answers) and `linkFields` should be passed via the `fields` passthrough. Returns the created booking.

tools.name: youcanbookme_update_booking
tools.title: Update a booking
tools.description: MUTATES YouCanBookMe data: updates an existing booking (reschedule, rename, mark cancelled/no-show). YCBM API: PATCH /v1/bookings/{bookingId} (JSON, partial update). Set any of title/startsAt/endsAt/cancelled/noShow/timeZone/locale/units; use the `fields` passthrough for answers/linkFields or other documented fields. The path id is never sent in the body.

tools.name: youcanbookme_cancel_booking
tools.title: Cancel a booking
tools.description: MUTATES YouCanBookMe data: cancels a booking. Convenience wrapper for PATCH /v1/bookings/{bookingId} with { cancelled: true } — safer and reversible (re-activate via youcanbookme_update_booking cancelled=false) versus deleting. Returns the updated booking.

tools.name: youcanbookme_update_profile
tools.title: Update a profile (booking page)
tools.description: MUTATES YouCanBookMe data: updates a profile's (booking page) configuration. YCBM API: PATCH /v1/profiles/{profileId} (JSON, partial update). Pass the fields to change via the `fields` passthrough (e.g. { title, subdomain, ... }) — profile fields are numerous and use YCBM's own names. The path id is never sent in the body.

tools.name: youcanbookme_create_appointment_type
tools.title: Create an appointment type
tools.description: MUTATES YouCanBookMe data: adds an appointment type to a profile. YCBM API: POST /v1/profiles/{profileId}/appointmenttypes/items (JSON). Required: name; use the `fields` passthrough for description, slotLength, price, etc. The path profileId is never sent in the body.

tools.name: youcanbookme_update_appointment_type
tools.title: Update an appointment type
tools.description: MUTATES YouCanBookMe data: updates an appointment type on a profile. YCBM API: PATCH /v1/profiles/{profileId}/appointmenttypes/items/{appointmentTypeId} (JSON, partial update). Pass changed fields (name, description, slotLength, price, ...) via the `fields` passthrough. Path ids are never sent in the body.

tools.name: youcanbookme_create_team_member
tools.title: Add a team member
tools.description: MUTATES YouCanBookMe data: adds a team member to a profile. YCBM API: POST /v1/profiles/{profileId}/teammembers/items (JSON). Required: name; calendarId links the member to a calendar (find it via youcanbookme_list_available_accounts). Use the `fields` passthrough for email, description, pic, etc. The path profileId is never sent in the body.

tools.name: youcanbookme_update_team_member

Pass changed fields (name, email, description, calendarId, ...) via the `fields` passthrough. Path ids are never sent in the body.

tools.name: youcanbookme_create_location

tools.name: zendesk_search

servers.name: Fillout
servers.description: Read Fillout forms and submissions, export responses, and create submissions and webhooks.

tools.name: fillout_list_forms
tools.title: List forms
tools.description: List every form in the Fillout account — each form's name and formId. Start here to find the formId the other tools need. Fillout: GET /forms.

tools.name: fillout_get_form
tools.title: Get form questions and metadata
tools.description: Fetch one form's metadata: every question (id, name, type), calculations, URL parameters, scheduling and payment fields, and quiz settings. Use the question ids to read answers or to create submissions. Fillout: GET /forms/{formId}.

tools.name: fillout_list_submissions
tools.title: List submissions
tools.description: List one page of a form's submissions (answers to every question, calculations, URL parameters, scheduling, payments, quiz score, login email), filtered by date range, status or free-text search. Offset pagination: the response carries totalResponses and pageCount. Fillout: GET /forms/{formId}/submissions.

tools.name: fillout_get_submission
tools.title: Get one submission
tools.description: Fetch a single submission by id, with every answer. Fillout: GET /forms/{formId}/submissions/{submissionId}.

tools.name: fillout_count_submissions
tools.title: Count submissions
tools.description: Count a form's submissions matching the same filters as fillout_list_submissions (date range, status, search) without pulling the answers — e.g. 'how many responses this week?' or 'how many partial submissions?'. Reads totalResponses from GET /forms/{formId}/submissions with limit=1.

tools.name: fillout_export_submissions
tools.title: Export submissions
tools.description: Fetch many submissions in one call by walking the offset pagination (150 per page, paced under Fillout's 5 requests/second limit), up to max_submissions. Same filters as fillout_list_submissions. Use this for analysis across a whole response set; the result says whether it was truncated. Fillout: GET /forms/{formId}/submissions (repeated).

tools.name: fillout_create_submissions
tools.title: Create submissions
tools.description: Create up to 10 new submissions on a form, as if respondents had filled it in — e.g. to import responses collected elsewhere. Each submission needs its question answers (question ids from fillout_get_form); URL parameters, scheduling, payments, login email and timestamps are optional. Creates real records that trigger the form's integrations. Fillout: POST /forms/{formId}/submissions.

tools.name: fillout_create_webhook
tools.title: Create a submission webhook
tools.description: Subscribe a URL to a form's new submissions: Fillout will POST each submission (same shape as a fillout_list_submissions entry) to it. Returns the webhook id — keep it, it is the only handle for removing the webhook later. Fillout: POST /webhook/create.

tools.name: fillout_remove_webhook
tools.title: Remove a submission webhook
tools.description: Stop a webhook from receiving submissions. Recoverable: create it again with fillout_create_webhook (it gets a new id). Fillout: POST /webhook/delete.

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Fillout (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). servers.name: Checkfront
servers.description: Check Checkfront availability and rates, and manage booking sessions, bookings, customers and notes.

tools.name: checkfront_get_company
tools.title: Get company settings
tools.description: Fetch the connected Checkfront account's company configuration — name, URL, plan, currency, timezone, locale and date/time formats. A cheap way to confirm the host and credentials work. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/company.

tools.name: checkfront_list_categories
tools.title: List item categories
tools.description: List the inventory categories (e.g. Tours, Rentals, Accommodations) with their ids, names, display order and item counts. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/category.

tools.name: checkfront_list_items
tools.title: List inventory items (optionally with availability and rates)
tools.description: List the enabled inventory items (tours, activities, rentals, rooms). With NO dates this is the plain catalogue. Pass start_date (and end_date / param quantities) to get a RATED response: per-item availability, pricing and a SLIP token — the SLIP is what checkfront_add_to_booking_session needs to book the item. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/item.

tools.name: checkfront_get_item
tools.title: Get an item (optionally with availability and rates)
tools.description: Fetch one inventory item's details. Pass start_date / end_date and param quantities (e.g. {"adults": 2}) for a RATED response with availability (rate.status, rate.available), the price breakdown and the SLIP used to book it. For parent/child grouped items, rate the CHILD item. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/item/{item_id}.

tools.name: checkfront_get_availability_calendar
tools.title: Get an availability calendar
tools.description: Day-by-day available inventory over a date range — for one item (item_ids with a single id), several items, or a whole category. Use it to answer 'which days next month still have space?'. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/item/{item_id}/cal or GET /api/3.0/item/cal.

tools.name: checkfront_list_bookings
tools.title: List bookings
tools.description: List bookings, newest filters first — by status, customer, dates, item or partner. Each row has the booking code, status, totals (total, tax_total, paid_total), customer name/email, summary and date_desc. Paged (default 100/page); the response's request.pages tells you how many pages exist. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/booking/index.

tools.name: checkfront_get_booking
tools.title: Get a booking
tools.description: Fetch extended information on one booking — status, dates, customer, form fields, line items and totals. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/booking/{booking_id}.

tools.name: checkfront_list_booking_notes
tools.title: List booking notes
tools.description: List the notes left on bookings across the account (default: the past 30 days), each with its booking code, author account id (0 = customer), date, body and whether it is private. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/booking/notes.

tools.name: checkfront_get_booking_form
tools.title: Get the booking form fields
tools.description: Fetch the customer-details form for a booking (booking_form_ui): every field id (customer_name, customer_email, …), its label, type and whether it is required. Call this before checkfront_create_booking to know which `form` fields to send. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/booking/form.

tools.name: checkfront_get_booking_session
tools.title: Get a booking session (cart)
tools.description: Read a booking session — the in-progress 'cart' — with its line items (keyed by line_id), dates, sub_total, tax, total and amount due. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/booking/session.

tools.name: checkfront_search_customers
tools.title: Search customers
tools.description: Look up customers by exact email, full name or phone number (exact matches; non-unique fields such as name can return several). Results are in the `customers` object. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/customer.

tools.name: checkfront_get_customer
tools.title: Get a customer
tools.description: Fetch one customer's contact details and their bookings (codes with created dates). Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/customer/{customer_id}.

tools.name: checkfront_list_events
tools.title: List events (seasons, specials, closures, discounts)
tools.description: List the date-based events that change price or availability — seasonal rates (SE), specials (SP), discounts (DC), closures (status U) — with their dates, recurrence, pricing rule and the items/categories they apply to. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/event.

tools.name: checkfront_list_staff_accounts
tools.title: List staff accounts
tools.description: List the staff (and partner) accounts on the Checkfront account — ids, names, emails, login ids and whether enabled. The account_id is what CHECKFRONT_ON_BEHALF takes. Checkfront: GET /api/3.0/account.

tools.name: checkfront_add_to_booking_session
tools.title: Add items to a booking session (cart)
tools.description: Start or modify a booking session: add one or more SLIPs (from a rated checkfront_get_item / checkfront_list_items call), replace a line with a new SLIP (line_id + slip), or alter lines (quantity, 'remove', 'optin'/'optout' for package add-ons). Holds the inventory while the session is open; NOTHING is booked until checkfront_create_booking. Returns the session_id to reuse. Checkfront: POST /api/3.0/booking/session.

tools.name: checkfront_end_booking_session
tools.title: End or clear a booking session
tools.description: Abandon a booking session: 'clear' empties its items, 'end' closes it. Releases the inventory it was holding; no booking is affected. Checkfront: POST /api/3.0/booking/session/clear or /booking/session/end.

tools.name: checkfront_create_booking
tools.title: Create a booking
tools.description: Commit a booking: from a session_id (built with checkfront_add_to_booking_session) or directly from SLIPs, plus the customer form fields (see checkfront_get_booking_form for which are required — typically customer_name and customer_email). Creates a real reservation that consumes inventory and may notify the customer; change it later with checkfront_update_booking_status. Returns the new booking's ids and any invoice/payment URL. Checkfront: POST /api/3.0/booking/create.

tools.name: checkfront_update_booking_status
tools.title: Change a booking's status
tools.description: Set a booking's status — e.g. confirm a pending booking (PAID/PART), put it on HOLD or WAIT(list), or cancel it (VOID/STOP). Reversible: set it back to the previous status the same way. Does NOT record a payment. Optionally triggers the account's customer notifications. Checkfront: POST /api/3.0/booking/{booking_id}/update.

tools.name: checkfront_add_booking_note
tools.title: Add a note to a booking
tools.description: Add a note to a booking, logged under the staff account the API acts on behalf of. Checkfront: POST /api/3.0/booking/{booking_id}/note.

tools.name: checkfront_check_in_booking
tools.title: Check a booking in or out
tools.description: Mark a guest as arrived (check in) or departed (check out). Checkfront adds a note under the acting account. VOID and cancelled bookings cannot be checked in or out. Checkfront: POST /api/3.0/booking/{booking_id}/checkin or /checkout.

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Checkfront (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Checkfront Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). servers.name: Breeze ChMS
servers.description: Manage Breeze ChMS people, tags, events, check-ins, volunteers and contributions.

tools.name: breeze_get_account_summary
tools.title: Get the account summary
tools.description: The church account this key belongs to: name, subdomain, status, timezone and country/currency. A cheap way to confirm BREEZE_SUBDOMAIN and BREEZE_API_KEY are right. Breeze: GET /api/account/summary.

tools.name: breeze_list_people
tools.title: List people
tools.description: List people in the church database, optionally filtered (by tag, status, gender, etc.) and paginated with limit/offset. Without details you get id, first_name, last_name and photo path; with details=true every profile field is returned keyed by field_id (slower). Filter keys are profile field_ids (see breeze_list_profile_fields) or special keys, e.g. {"tag_contains":"y_16681"} for people in a tag, or {"2000138015":"226-227"} for a Status field matching options 226 or 227. Breeze: GET /api/people.

tools.name: breeze_get_person
tools.title: Get a person
tools.description: Fetch one person's profile by id, including address and — by default — every profile field keyed by field_id, plus family members. Pair with breeze_list_profile_fields to label the field ids. Breeze: GET /api/people/{person_id}.

tools.name: breeze_list_profile_fields
tools.title: List profile fields
tools.description: The church's profile layout: sections, each with its fields (field_id, field_type, name) and, for multiple-choice fields, their options (option_id, name). Needed to read person details, to build list_people filters, and to write fields with breeze_add_person / breeze_update_person. Breeze: GET /api/profile.

tools.name: breeze_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: List tags (Breeze's groups/lists) with id, name, created_on and folder_id, optionally only those in one folder. To list the people in a tag, call breeze_list_people with filter {"tag_contains":"y_<tag_id>"}. Breeze: GET /api/tags/list_tags.

tools.name: breeze_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List event instances in a date range (default: the current month), optionally on one calendar. Each row's `id` is the INSTANCE id used by attendance, volunteer and get_event tools; `event_id` is the series. Responses are cached by Breeze and may lag up to 15 minutes. Breeze: GET /api/events.

tools.name: breeze_get_event
tools.title: Get an event instance
tools.description: Fetch one event instance, optionally with the other instances in its series (then the response is an array of {id, start} only). Cached by Breeze, may lag up to 15 minutes. Breeze: GET /api/events/list_event.

tools.name: breeze_list_calendars
tools.title: List calendars
tools.description: List the church's event calendars (id, name, color and iCal feed address). The id is the category_id for breeze_list_events and breeze_add_event. Breeze: GET /api/events/calendars/list.

tools.name: breeze_list_attendance
tools.title: List attendance
tools.description: Who checked in to one event instance (person_id, check-in time created_on, check_out), optionally with each person's details, or the anonymous head count instead. Breeze: GET /api/events/attendance/list.

tools.name: breeze_list_forms
tools.title: List forms
tools.description: List the church's online forms (id, name, url_slug, is_archived) — active ones by default, or archived ones. Breeze: GET /api/forms/list_forms.

tools.name: breeze_list_form_fields
tools.title: List form fields
tools.description: The fields of one form (field_id, field_type, name, options). Form entry responses are keyed by these field_ids. Breeze: GET /api/forms/list_form_fields.

tools.name: breeze_list_form_entries
tools.title: List form entries
tools.description: Submissions to one form (id, created_on, person_id), and with details=true each entry's responses keyed by form field_id (see breeze_list_form_fields). Breeze: GET /api/forms/list_form_entries.

tools.name: breeze_list_volunteers
tools.title: List volunteers
tools.description: Volunteers scheduled for one event instance: person_id, response, comment, rsvped_on and role_ids. Breeze: GET /api/volunteers/list.

tools.name: breeze_list_account_log
tools.title: List the account log
tools.description: The account's audit log for one action type (e.g. person_updated, tag_assign, contribution_added), optionally within a date range or by one user. Good for 'what changed since…' and incremental sync. Breeze: GET /api/account/list_log.

tools.name: breeze_list_funds
tools.title: List funds
tools.description: List giving funds (id, name, tax_deductible, is_default), optionally with the total given to each. Legacy endpoint: no longer shown on Breeze's current API reference; churches whose giving runs through Tithely may get an error. Breeze: GET /api/funds/list.

tools.name: breeze_list_contributions
tools.title: List contributions
tools.description: List recorded contributions (gifts) given within a date range, optionally narrowed by giver (with their family), amount, payment method, fund, envelope, batch or form. Read-only: this server never adds, edits or deletes gifts. Legacy endpoint: no longer shown on Breeze's current API reference; churches whose giving runs through Tithely may get an error. Breeze: GET /api/giving/list.

tools.name: breeze_add_person
tools.title: Add a person
tools.description: WRITE: create a new person profile with a first and last name, and optionally set profile fields in the same call (same field shape as breeze_update_person). Check breeze_list_people first to avoid duplicates. Returns the new profile including its id. Breeze: GET /api/people/add.

tools.name: breeze_update_person
tools.title: Update a person
tools.description: WRITE: set profile fields on an existing person — email, phone, address, dates, multiple-choice options, family role, and custom fields. Only the fields you pass change; the previous values are overwritten (read them first with breeze_get_person if you may need to restore them). field_id and option ids come from breeze_list_profile_fields. Breeze: GET /api/people/update.

tools.name: breeze_add_tag
tools.title: Create a tag
tools.description: WRITE: create a new tag, at the top level or inside a folder. Returns the new tag with its id. Breeze: GET /api/tags/add_tag.

tools.name: breeze_assign_tag
tools.title: Assign a tag to a person
tools.description: WRITE: add a tag to one person (e.g. put them in a small group or list). Undo with breeze_unassign_tag. Breeze: GET /api/tags/assign.

tools.name: breeze_unassign_tag
tools.title: Remove a tag from a person
tools.description: WRITE: remove a tag from one person. The person and the tag both remain; re-assign with breeze_assign_tag. Breeze: GET /api/tags/unassign.

tools.name: breeze_add_event
tools.title: Add an event
tools.description: WRITE: create an event on the church calendar, optionally as another instance of an existing series. Times are Unix timestamps in seconds. This server cannot delete events, so a mistaken event must be removed in the Breeze app. Breeze: GET /api/events/add.

tools.name: breeze_record_attendance
tools.title: Check a person in or out
tools.description: WRITE: record attendance for one person at one event instance — check them in (default) or check them out (records when they left; checking out someone not checked in creates a record with matching in/out times). Breeze: GET /api/events/attendance/add.

tools.name: breeze_schedule_volunteer
tools.title: Schedule a volunteer
tools.description: WRITE: schedule one person as a volunteer for one event instance. Breeze: GET /api/volunteers/add.

tools.name: breeze_chms_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: breeze_chms_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Breeze ChMS tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: breeze_chms_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Breeze ChMS (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: breeze_chms_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Breeze ChMS Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run breeze_chms_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: The subdomain is the part before `.breezechms.com` in your Breeze web address. Find the API key in Breeze → **Extensions → API** (API access comes with a paid Breeze subscription). Your key is used only to call the Breeze API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: How many people attended last Sunday's service?
Show the total giving for the past month by fund.
Who is scheduled to volunteer at this Sunday's service?
Add a new person named John Brown to the church database.

servers.name: Neon CRM
servers.description: Search Neon CRM accounts, donations, memberships and events; create accounts and activities.

tools.name: neon_get_organization_profile
tools.title: Get the organization profile
tools.description: Fetch the Neon CRM organization these credentials belong to — its name, org ID and app URL. A cheap way to confirm the org ID and API key work. Neon: GET /properties/organizationProfile.

tools.name: neon_list_accounts
tools.title: List accounts
tools.description: List constituent accounts (individuals and companies), optionally filtered by email, first or last name, or type. Returns accountId, names, email and userType. For richer queries use neon_search. Neon: GET /accounts.

tools.name: neon_get_account
tools.title: Get one account
tools.description: Fetch one account in full — returned as individualAccount or companyAccount with its primary contact, addresses, consent, custom fields, current membership status and timestamps. Neon: GET /accounts/{id}.

tools.name: neon_list_search_fields
tools.title: List search or output fields
tools.description: Discover the field names neon_search accepts for a resource: kind=searchFields gives filterable fields with their allowed operators; kind=outputFields gives the columns you can return (standard field names plus custom fields with numeric ids). Call this before neon_search. Neon: GET /{resource}/search/searchFields or /outputFields.

tools.name: neon_search
tools.title: Search records
tools.description: Report-style search over accounts, donations (includes pledges and pledge payments), activities or events. Give filter criteria (field + operator + value), the output columns to return (standard field NAMES as strings, or custom-field IDS as integers — both from neon_list_search_fields), and 0-based pagination. Results come back as searchResults rows keyed by output field name, plus pagination totals. Neon allows only ONE concurrent search per endpoint. Neon: POST /{resource}/search.

tools.name: neon_list_account_donations
tools.title: List an account's donations
tools.description: List one account's donations (amount, date, fund, campaign, purpose, status, payments), newest first by default. Neon: GET /accounts/{id}/donations.

tools.name: neon_list_account_memberships
tools.title: List an account's memberships
tools.description: List one account's membership history — level, term, start and end dates, fee, status (e.g. SUCCEEDED/FAILED) and auto-renewal. Filter to active or the primary active membership. Neon: GET /accounts/{id}/memberships.

tools.name: neon_list_account_event_registrations
tools.title: List an account's event registrations
tools.description: List the event registrations one account has made, optionally for a single event. Neon: GET /accounts/{id}/eventRegistrations.

tools.name: neon_get_donation
tools.title: Get one donation
tools.description: Fetch one donation — amount, date, fund, campaign, purpose, source, tribute, soft-credit solicitor, payments and status. Neon: GET /donations/{id}.

tools.name: neon_get_membership
tools.title: Get one membership
tools.description: Fetch one membership — level, term, dates, fee, status, auto-renewal, sub-members and payments. Neon: GET /memberships/{membershipId}.

tools.name: neon_list_membership_levels
tools.title: List membership levels
tools.description: List the organization's membership levels (id, code, description, rank, type, status). Neon: GET /memberships/levels.

tools.name: neon_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List events, filterable by name, category, date window, published or archived state. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Only Neon's legacy events are exposed by the API. Neon: GET /events.

tools.name: neon_get_event
tools.title: Get one event
tools.description: Fetch one event — name, summary, dates, location, capacity, category, campaign, registration and financial settings. Neon: GET /events/{id}.

tools.name: neon_list_event_registrations
tools.title: List an event's registrations
tools.description: List the registrations for one event — registrant account, tickets and attendees, amount, payments. Optionally only one registrant. Neon: GET /events/{id}/eventRegistrations.

tools.name: neon_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: List fundraising campaigns (id, code, name, status). Neon: GET /campaigns.

tools.name: neon_get_campaign
tools.title: Get one campaign
tools.description: Fetch one campaign — dates, goal, fund, purpose, parent campaign, status, page URLs and fundraising statistics. Neon: GET /campaigns/{id}.

tools.name: neon_get_activity
tools.title: Get one activity
tools.description: Fetch one activity (a logged interaction or task) — subject, note, dates, linked accounts, assigned users, status and priority. Neon: GET /activities/{id}.

tools.name: neon_list_properties
tools.title: List lookup values
tools.description: List one of the organization's lookup lists — the ids other tools need: funds, purposes, sources, solicitation methods, activity statuses and system time zones (for neon_create_activity), system users, individual and company types, event categories, countries, states/provinces, genders, prefixes. Neon: GET /properties/{name}.

tools.name: neon_create_account
tools.title: Create an account
tools.description: Create a constituent account: an INDIVIDUAL (a person) or a COMPANY (with company_name, plus an optional primary contact). Neon's Account Match may merge it into an existing account with the same name and email, so check neon_list_accounts by email first. Returns the new id. Neon: POST /accounts.

tools.name: neon_update_account
tools.title: Update an account
tools.description: Change an account's name, email, job title, company name or do-not-solicit / email opt-out flags. Only the fields you pass are changed (PATCH). The type must match the account (see neon_get_account). Addresses are not edited here. Neon: PATCH /accounts/{id}.

tools.name: neon_create_activity
tools.title: Log an activity
tools.description: Create an activity — log an interaction with a constituent (call, meeting, note) or schedule a task. Needs a subject, a start date, a time zone id (neon_list_properties name=systemTimezones), a status id (name=activityStatuses) and a priority; link it to accounts and assign it to system users. Returns the new id. Neon: POST /activities.

tools.name: neon_update_activity
tools.title: Update an activity
tools.description: Change an activity's subject, note, status (e.g. mark it completed) or priority. Only the fields you pass are changed (PATCH). Neon: PATCH /activities/{id}.

tools.name: neon_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: neon_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Neon CRM tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: neon_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Neon CRM (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: neon_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Neon CRM Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run neon_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: **Organization ID:** Neon CRM → **Settings → Organization Profile**. **API key:** Neon CRM → **Settings → User Management** → open a user → enable **API Access** and copy the key (the key inherits that user’s permissions). Your credentials are used only to call the Neon CRM API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

examples: Show the donations Jane Smith has made this year.
List the events coming up in the next 30 days.
Which membership levels do we offer, and which of them are currently active?
Log a call with Jane Smith asking about her membership renewal.

servers.name: Insightly
servers.description: Read and write Insightly contacts, organisations, leads, opportunities, tasks and notes.

tools.name: insightly_get_current_user
tools.title: Get the current user
tools.description: Fetch the user the API key belongs to (USER_ID, name, email, admin flag). A cheap way to confirm the key and pod are right, and to get your own id for owner fields. Insightly: GET /Users/Me.

tools.name: insightly_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the users in the Insightly instance — needed to resolve OWNER_USER_ID / RESPONSIBLE_USER_ID. Insightly: GET /Users.

tools.name: insightly_list_records
tools.title: List or search records
tools.description: List records of one type — Contacts, Organisations, Leads, Opportunities, Projects, Tasks, Events or Notes — optionally filtered by one field value and/or last-updated time. With field_name + field_value (both required together) or updated_after_utc this uses GET /<Object>/Search; otherwise GET /<Object>. Field names are Insightly's UPPER_SNAKE names, e.g. EMAIL_ADDRESS, LAST_NAME, ORGANISATION_NAME, OPPORTUNITY_STATE, LEAD_RATING, or a custom field such as Industry__c.

tools.name: insightly_get_record
tools.title: Get one record
tools.description: Fetch a single Contact, Organisation, Lead, Opportunity, Project, Task, Event or Note by id, with its custom fields, tags and links. Insightly: GET /<Object>/{id}.

tools.name: insightly_list_record_activity
tools.title: List a record's notes, tasks or events
tools.description: List the Notes, Tasks or Events attached to one Contact, Organisation, Lead, Opportunity or Project — the activity history of that record. Insightly: GET /<Object>/{id}/Notes | Tasks | Events.

tools.name: insightly_search_by_tag
tools.title: Find records by tag
tools.description: List Contacts, Organisations, Leads, Opportunities or Projects carrying a tag. Insightly: GET /<Object>/SearchByTag?tagName=.

tools.name: insightly_list_pipelines
tools.title: List pipelines
tools.description: List the sales and project pipelines (PIPELINE_ID, name, whether for opportunities or projects). Insightly: GET /Pipelines.

tools.name: insightly_list_pipeline_stages
tools.title: List pipeline stages
tools.description: List every pipeline stage (STAGE_ID, PIPELINE_ID, name, order) — map an opportunity's or project's STAGE_ID to a stage name. Insightly: GET /PipelineStages.

tools.name: insightly_list_lead_statuses
tools.title: List lead statuses
tools.description: List the lead statuses defined in the instance (LEAD_STATUS_ID, name, type). Insightly: GET /LeadStatuses.

tools.name: insightly_list_lead_sources
tools.title: List lead sources
tools.description: List the lead sources defined in the instance (LEAD_SOURCE_ID, name). Insightly: GET /LeadSources.

tools.name: insightly_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: Create a contact (first_name is required). Insightly: POST /Contacts.

tools.name: insightly_update_contact
tools.title: Update a contact
tools.description: Update a contact. Only the fields you pass are changed (v3.1 partial update). Insightly: PUT /Contacts with CONTACT_ID.

tools.name: insightly_create_organisation
tools.title: Create an organisation
tools.description: Create an organisation (company). Insightly: POST /Organisations.

tools.name: insightly_update_organisation
tools.title: Update an organisation
tools.description: Update an organisation. Only the fields you pass are changed. Insightly: PUT /Organisations with ORGANISATION_ID.

tools.name: insightly_create_lead
tools.title: Create a lead
tools.description: Create a lead (last_name is required). Insightly's schema also marks lead_status_id and lead_source_id as required — get valid ids from insightly_list_lead_statuses / insightly_list_lead_sources. Insightly: POST /Leads.

tools.name: insightly_update_lead
tools.title: Update a lead
tools.description: Update a lead. Only the fields you pass are changed. Insightly: PUT /Leads with LEAD_ID.

tools.name: insightly_create_opportunity
tools.title: Create an opportunity
tools.description: Create a sales opportunity (opportunity_name is required). Insightly: POST /Opportunities.

tools.name: insightly_update_opportunity
tools.title: Update an opportunity
tools.description: Update an opportunity's value, probability, dates, owner or details. Only the fields you pass are changed. Insightly: PUT /Opportunities with OPPORTUNITY_ID.

tools.name: insightly_create_task
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: Create a task (title is required). Insightly requires OWNER_USER_ID and COMPLETED on a task: if owner_user_id is omitted it is filled with the API key's own user (via GET /Users/Me), and completed defaults to false. Insightly: POST /Tasks.

tools.name: insightly_update_task
tools.title: Update a task
tools.description: Update a task — mark it completed, change due date, status, assignee or details. Only the fields you pass are changed. Insightly: PUT /Tasks with TASK_ID.

tools.name: insightly_add_note
tools.title: Add a note to a record
tools.description: Add a note (title + body) to a Contact, Organisation, Lead, Opportunity or Project. Insightly: POST /<Object>/{id}/Notes.

tools.name: insightly_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: insightly_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Insightly tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: insightly_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Insightly (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: insightly_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Insightly Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run insightly_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Both are in Insightly → your avatar → **User Settings → API**: copy the **API key**, and read the pod from the **API URL** shown there (e.g. `https://api.**eu1**.insightly.com` → `eu1`). Your key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Which opportunities are open and what are they worth in total?
Show the leads that have been updated since the start of this month.
Show the notes and tasks on the organisation Acme Ltd.
Create a task 'Follow up with Acme Ltd' for the owner.

servers.name: Bookeo
servers.description: Check Bookeo availability and manage bookings, holds and customers; read payments.

tools.name: bookeo_get_api_key_info
tools.title: Get API key info
tools.description: Show which Bookeo account the credentials belong to and which permissions were granted (e.g. bookings_rw_all, customers_r_all, availability_r). A cheap way to confirm the setup works. Bookeo: GET /settings/apikeyinfo.

tools.name: bookeo_get_business
tools.title: Get the business
tools.description: Get the business's name, contact details, address, website and description. Bookeo: GET /settings/business.

tools.name: bookeo_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List the bookable products (tours, classes, courses, appointments) with their ids, type (fixed, fixedCourse, flexibleTime), duration, participant limits per people category, default rates and options. Bookeo: GET /settings/products.

tools.name: bookeo_list_people_categories
tools.title: List people categories
tools.description: List the participant categories the account uses (default Adults/Children/Infants plus custom ones like Students), with their ids and seats taken. Needed for peopleNumbers. Bookeo: GET /settings/peoplecategories.

tools.name: bookeo_list_resources
tools.title: List resources
tools.description: List resource types and their resources (guides, instructors, rooms, boats...) with ids. Bookeo: GET /settings/resources.

tools.name: bookeo_get_availability_slots
tools.title: Get availability slots
tools.description: List available slots (eventId, start/end, seats available) for fixed and fixedCourse products in a time window of at most 31 days. Not for flexibleTime products — use bookeo_search_matching_slots for those. Bookeo: GET /availability/slots.

tools.name: bookeo_search_matching_slots
tools.title: Search matching slots
tools.description: Find slots that can take a given party (participant counts per category, options, resources), with an estimated price. Works for all product types, including flexibleTime appointments. Window max 31 days. To page through results pass only pageNavigationToken (+ pageNumber). Read-only. Bookeo: POST /availability/matchingslots, GET /availability/matchingslots/{pageNavigationToken}.

tools.name: bookeo_list_bookings
tools.title: List bookings
tools.description: List bookings by start time (startTime+endTime) and/or by last change (lastUpdatedStartTime+lastUpdatedEndTime) — at least one pair is required, each spanning at most 31 days. Optionally filter by product, include canceled bookings, and expand customer/participant details. Bookeo: GET /bookings.

tools.name: bookeo_get_booking
tools.title: Get a booking
tools.description: Get one booking by its booking number: product, times, participants, options, price, paid amount, status (canceled/accepted/noShow). Bookeo: GET /bookings/{bookingNumber}.

tools.name: bookeo_list_booking_payments
tools.title: List a booking's payments
tools.description: List the payments (and refunds, as negative amounts) received for one booking. Bookeo: GET /bookings/{bookingNumber}/payments.

tools.name: bookeo_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List or search customers — by name, firstName, lastName or emailAddress — optionally only members/non-members or those created since a date. Bookeo: GET /customers.

tools.name: bookeo_get_customer
tools.title: Get a customer
tools.description: Get one customer: contact details, next/previous booking, number of bookings, cancellations and no-shows, membership and store credit. Bookeo: GET /customers/{id}.

tools.name: bookeo_list_customer_bookings
tools.title: List a customer's bookings
tools.description: List one customer's bookings, optionally between two dates. Bookeo: GET /customers/{id}/bookings.

tools.name: bookeo_list_payments
tools.title: List payments
tools.description: List payments received in a time period, optionally by payment method. Refunds are included with a negative amount. Bookeo: GET /payments.

tools.name: bookeo_get_payment
tools.title: Get a payment
tools.description: Get one payment: amount, method, reason, received time, customer and gateway transaction id. Bookeo: GET /payments/{id}.

tools.name: bookeo_create_hold
tools.title: Hold seats (price check)
tools.description: Temporarily reserve the seats/resources for a draft booking (default 300 s, max 600 s) and get the FINAL price, taxes and amount payable. The recommended step before bookeo_create_booking: pass the returned hold id as previousHoldId there. Holds expire automatically. Bookeo: POST /holds.

tools.name: bookeo_create_booking
tools.title: Create a booking
tools.description: Create a confirmed booking for an existing customer (customerId) or a new one (customer). fixed/fixedCourse products need an eventId from the availability tools; flexibleTime products take eventId or startTime. Pass previousHoldId to convert a hold. Does NOT record any payment. Reversible with bookeo_cancel_booking. Bookeo: POST /bookings.

tools.name: bookeo_update_booking
tools.title: Update a booking
tools.description: Change an existing booking — reschedule (eventId or startTime/endTime), change participant counts, options, resources or external reference. Fetches the current booking and sends it back with only your changes applied (Bookeo's PUT takes the full booking). Bookeo: GET then PUT /bookings/{bookingNumber}.

tools.name: bookeo_cancel_booking
tools.title: Cancel a booking
tools.description: Cancel a booking. It stays in the system (visible with includeCanceled) but frees its seats. The account's cancellation policy is NOT applied, so no cancellation fee is charged. Bookeo: DELETE /bookings/{bookingNumber}.

tools.name: bookeo_create_customer
tools.title: Create a customer
tools.description: Create a customer record. Not needed before booking — bookeo_create_booking can create the customer inline. Bookeo: POST /customers.

tools.name: bookeo_update_customer
tools.title: Update a customer
tools.description: Update a customer's contact details. Fetches the current record and sends it back with only your changes applied (Bookeo's PUT takes the full customer). Bookeo: GET then PUT /customers/{id}.

tools.name: bookeo_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: bookeo_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Bookeo tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: bookeo_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Bookeo (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: bookeo_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Bookeo Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run bookeo_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: The Bookeo API needs a paid Bookeo subscription. To get both keys: **1)** create a free Bookeo [developer account](https://www.bookeo.com/api/setup/) and register an application — its **secret key** is shown there; **2)** have the business account owner open the app's **Authorization URL** and grant permissions (e.g. `bookings_rwd_all,customers_rw_all,payments_r_all,availability_r`) — Bookeo then issues the per-account **API key**. Your keys are used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

examples: Which of my tours have open seats next Saturday?
List all bookings starting this week with the customer names.
How much payment did we receive last month, split by payment method?
Find the customer Jane Smith and show her past bookings and any no-shows.

servers.name: Bloomerang
servers.description: Search Bloomerang constituents and donations; log interactions, notes and tasks.

tools.name: bloomerang_get_current_user
tools.title: Get the current user
tools.description: Fetch the Bloomerang user the API key belongs to — name, email and permission level. A cheap way to confirm the key works and see what it may do. Bloomerang: GET /user/current.

tools.name: bloomerang_search_constituents
tools.title: Search constituents
tools.description: Full-text search across constituents (individuals and organizations) and households by name, email, etc. Start here to find a donor's Id. Bloomerang: GET /constituents/search.

tools.name: bloomerang_list_constituents
tools.title: List constituents
tools.description: List constituents with filters — by Id, type, favorites, last-modified date, or a custom field value — and sorting. Good for syncing recent changes. Bloomerang: GET /constituents.

tools.name: bloomerang_get_constituent
tools.title: Get one constituent
tools.description: Fetch one constituent's full profile — names, primary and secondary contact details, household, communication preferences, engagement score and custom values. Bloomerang: GET /constituent/{id}.

tools.name: bloomerang_get_constituent_timeline
tools.title: Get a constituent's timeline
tools.description: The activity timeline for a constituent — gifts, interactions, notes, tasks and more, newest first. Pass a household Id to get the timeline of every member. Bloomerang: GET /constituent/{id}/timeline.

tools.name: bloomerang_list_constituent_relationships
tools.title: List a constituent's relationships
tools.description: Relationships between this constituent and others (spouse, employer, board member ...), with the role on each side. Bloomerang: GET /constituent/{id}/relationships.

tools.name: bloomerang_get_household
tools.title: Get one household
tools.description: Fetch a household — its names, head of household (HeadId) and member constituent Ids. A constituent's HouseholdId points here. Bloomerang: GET /household/{id}.

tools.name: bloomerang_list_transactions
tools.title: List transactions (gifts)
tools.description: List transactions — donations, pledges, pledge payments, recurring donations and their payments — with their designations (fund, campaign, appeal). Filter by constituent, amount range, type or last-modified date. Read only. Bloomerang: GET /transactions.

tools.name: bloomerang_get_transaction
tools.title: Get one transaction
tools.description: Fetch one transaction with its payment method, amounts, refund status and every designation (fund, campaign, appeal, tribute, acknowledgement status). Bloomerang: GET /transaction/{id}.

tools.name: bloomerang_list_funds
tools.title: List funds
tools.description: List the funds gifts can be designated to (e.g. General Operating, Scholarship). Bloomerang: GET /funds.

tools.name: bloomerang_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: List fundraising campaigns with their goals and dates. Bloomerang: GET /campaigns.

tools.name: bloomerang_list_appeals
tools.title: List appeals
tools.description: List appeals — the specific asks (a year-end letter, a gala invitation) that gifts are attributed to. Bloomerang: GET /appeals.

tools.name: bloomerang_list_interactions
tools.title: List interactions
tools.description: List logged interactions (calls, emails, meetings, letters ...) — filter by constituent, channel or purpose. Bloomerang: GET /interactions.

tools.name: bloomerang_list_notes
tools.title: List notes
tools.description: List notes, optionally for specific constituents. Bloomerang: GET /notes.

tools.name: bloomerang_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List tasks (follow-ups) — filter by status, due-date range, assignee user, constituent, channel or purpose. Bloomerang: GET /tasks.

tools.name: bloomerang_create_constituent

tools.name: bloomerang_update_constituent

tools.name: bloomerang_create_interaction
tools.title: Log an interaction
tools.description: WRITE: log an interaction with a constituent — a call, email, meeting, letter, etc. — on their timeline. Bloomerang: POST /interaction.

tools.name: bloomerang_create_note
tools.title: Add a note
tools.description: WRITE: add a note to a constituent's record. Bloomerang: POST /note.

tools.name: bloomerang_create_task
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: WRITE: create a follow-up task, optionally tied to a constituent and assigned to a user (find user Ids via bloomerang_get_current_user or existing tasks). Bloomerang: POST /task.

tools.name: bloomerang_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.
