tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Eventbrite (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: eventbrite_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Eventbrite Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run eventbrite_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find it in Eventbrite → **Account Settings → Developer Links → API Keys** (or [eventbrite.com/platform/api-keys](https://www.eventbrite.com/platform/api-keys)) — copy the **Private token**, not the API key or client secret. Create an API key first if you have none. Your token is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: How many tickets have I sold for each of my upcoming events?
Show gross and net sales for my spring workshop over the last month.
Who has registered for my next event, with their email addresses?
Which discount codes have been used, and how many times each?

servers.name: Less Annoying CRM
servers.description: Read and write Less Annoying CRM contacts, notes, tasks, events, pipelines and groups.

tools.name: lacrm_get_user
tools.title: Get the current user
tools.description: Return the user who owns this API key — UserId, name, email and timezone. A cheap way to confirm the key works, and the UserId to use for AssignedTo. LACRM: GetUser.

tools.name: lacrm_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the users on the account that you can see (admins see all), with their UserIds — needed to assign contacts, tasks or filter by owner. LACRM: GetUsers.

tools.name: lacrm_search_contacts
tools.title: Search contacts and companies
tools.description: Search (or list) contacts and companies. With no search_terms, returns everything visible, paged. Returns { HasMoreResults, Results }. LACRM: GetContacts.

tools.name: lacrm_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact or company
tools.description: Fetch one contact or company record with all its fields (emails, phones, addresses, custom fields, owner). LACRM: GetContact.

tools.name: lacrm_list_notes
tools.title: List notes
tools.description: List notes, newest first by default — across the whole CRM, or for one contact. Filter by date range and author. LACRM: GetNotes.

tools.name: lacrm_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List tasks due in a date range, optionally only incomplete/complete, for given users. If contact_id is given, ALL of that contact's tasks are returned regardless of dates or status. LACRM: GetTasks.

tools.name: lacrm_list_events
tools.title: List calendar events
tools.description: List calendar events in a date range, filterable by user or calendar. If contact_id is given, all events attached to that contact are returned and other filters are ignored. LACRM: GetEvents.

tools.name: lacrm_list_pipelines
tools.title: List pipelines
tools.description: List the account's pipelines (e.g. Sales Leads) with their statuses (StatusId, Name, IsActive) and optionally their custom fields. This is the setup, not the items — use lacrm_list_pipeline_items for those. LACRM: GetPipelines.

tools.name: lacrm_list_pipeline_items
tools.title: List pipeline items
tools.description: List the items in one pipeline (deals, leads...), optionally only in given statuses or for given users. An empty status filter returns items in all ACTIVE statuses. LACRM: GetPipelineItems.

tools.name: lacrm_get_contact_pipeline_items
tools.title: Get a contact's pipeline items
tools.description: All pipeline items attached to one contact or company, grouped by pipeline. LACRM: GetPipelineItemsAttachedToContact.

tools.name: lacrm_list_groups
tools.title: List groups
tools.description: List the contact groups you can see (GroupId, Name, Sharing, Color), optionally with member counts. LACRM: GetGroups.

tools.name: lacrm_list_contacts_in_group
tools.title: List contacts in a group
tools.description: List the contacts that are members of one group. Identify the group by group_id (preferred) or group_name — not both. LACRM: GetContactsInGroup.

tools.name: lacrm_get_contact_groups
tools.title: Get a contact's groups
tools.description: List the groups one contact or company belongs to. LACRM: GetGroupsAttachedToContact.

tools.name: lacrm_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List custom fields
tools.description: List the account's field definitions (name, type, options) for contacts, companies or pipelines — use the Name values as keys in custom_fields when creating/editing contacts. LACRM: GetCustomFields.

tools.name: lacrm_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact or company
tools.description: Create a new contact (person) or company record. For a person, company_name links them to that company (creating it if needed). Company names must be unique. If assigned_to is omitted, the record is assigned to the API key's own user (one extra GetUser call). Returns { ContactId }. LACRM: CreateContact.

tools.name: lacrm_edit_contact
tools.title: Edit a contact or company
tools.description: Update fields on an existing contact or company. Only the fields you pass change; omitted fields are left alone. Multi-value fields (email, phone, address, website) are REPLACED by the list you pass. Set is_company=true when renaming a company. LACRM: EditContact.

tools.name: lacrm_create_note
tools.title: Add a note to a contact
tools.description: Attach a plain-text note to a contact or company's history (newlines kept, HTML/markdown escaped). Returns { NoteId }. LACRM: CreateNote.

tools.name: lacrm_create_task
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: Create a to-do on a user's task list (date only, no time — use lacrm_create_event for timed things). Optionally attach it to a contact. Returns { TaskId }. LACRM: CreateTask.

tools.name: lacrm_edit_task
tools.title: Edit or complete a task
tools.description: Update a task — including marking it complete (is_complete=true) or re-opening it (false). Only passed fields change. LACRM: EditTask.

tools.name: lacrm_create_event
tools.title: Schedule a calendar event
tools.description: Create a timed (or all-day) event on your calendar, optionally with contacts/users as attendees. The timezone of start_date becomes the event's timezone. Returns { EventId }. LACRM: CreateEvent.

tools.name: lacrm_create_pipeline_item
tools.title: Add a contact to a pipeline
tools.description: Create a pipeline item (deal, lead...) on a contact in a given pipeline and status, with an optional note. Returns { PipelineItemId }. LACRM: CreatePipelineItem.

tools.name: lacrm_update_pipeline_item
tools.title: Move or annotate a pipeline item
tools.description: Move a pipeline item to another status (e.g. Prospect → Won) and/or add a note to its history. LACRM: EditPipelineItem.

tools.name: lacrm_add_contact_to_group
tools.title: Add a contact to a group
tools.description: Add a contact or company to a group (creates a group membership). Identify the group by group_id (preferred) or group_name — not both. LACRM: CreateGroupMembership.

tools.name: lacrm_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lacrm_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Less Annoying CRM tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lacrm_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Less Annoying CRM (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lacrm_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Less Annoying CRM Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run lacrm_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create one in Less Annoying CRM → **Settings → Programmer API**. The key's read/create/edit permissions apply, and API access requires a paid plan (or trial). Your key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Which tasks are due this week and haven't been completed yet?
Show me all the deals currently in my sales pipeline by stage.
Find Acme Ltd and show me their latest notes.
Add a note to Jane Smith saying we sent the revised quote today.

servers.name: Workiz
servers.description: Manage Workiz jobs and leads: create, update, assign team members and convert leads to jobs.

tools.name: workiz_list_jobs
tools.title: List jobs
tools.description: List jobs, most recently scheduled first (sorted by JobDateTime, descending). Filter by start date, open-only, and status; page with offset/records (max 100). Without start_date Workiz returns the last 14 days. Workiz: GET /job/all/.

tools.name: workiz_get_job
tools.title: Get one job
tools.description: Fetch one job by UUID: schedule, status, client contact and address, totals and amount due, notes, tags and assigned team. Workiz: GET /job/get/{UUID}/.

tools.name: workiz_list_leads
tools.title: List leads
tools.description: List leads, most recent first (sorted by LeadDateTime, descending). Filter by start date, open-only, and status; page with offset/records (max 100). Workiz: GET /lead/all/.

tools.name: workiz_get_lead
tools.title: Get one lead
tools.description: Fetch one lead by UUID: schedule, status, client contact and address, source, notes and assigned team. Workiz: GET /lead/get/{UUID}/.

tools.name: workiz_list_team
tools.title: List team members
tools.description: List the account's active team members: id, name, role, whether they are a field tech, email, service areas and skills. Use the name to assign people to jobs or leads. Workiz: GET /team/all/.

tools.name: workiz_get_team_member
tools.title: Get one team member
tools.description: Fetch one team member by user id: name, role, field-tech flag, email, service areas, skills and active status. Workiz: GET /team/get/{USER_ID}.

tools.name: workiz_list_time_off
tools.title: List upcoming time off
tools.description: List FUTURE time off (start, end, userName — 'Entire Business' for company-wide closures). Set all=true to include every user and company time off. Useful before scheduling. Workiz: GET /TimeOff/get/.

tools.name: workiz_get_user_time_off
tools.title: Get a team member's time off
tools.description: List one team member's FUTURE time off, by their name. Workiz: GET /TimeOff/get/{USER_NAME}.

tools.name: workiz_create_job
tools.title: Create a job
tools.description: WRITE: create a new job (schedule, client contact and address, type, source, notes). Returns the new job's UUID, ClientId and app link. Workiz: POST /job/create/.

tools.name: workiz_update_job
tools.title: Update a job
tools.description: WRITE: update fields on an existing job — status/sub-status, reschedule (JobDateTime/JobEndDateTime), contact, address, type, source, notes, tags. Only the fields you pass are sent. Workiz: POST /job/update/.

tools.name: workiz_assign_job
tools.title: Assign a team member to a job
tools.description: WRITE: assign a team member (by name) to a job. Reversible with workiz_unassign_job. Workiz: POST /job/assign/.

tools.name: workiz_unassign_job
tools.title: Unassign a team member from a job
tools.description: WRITE: remove a team member (by name) from a job. Reversible with workiz_assign_job. Workiz: POST /job/unassign/.

tools.name: workiz_create_lead
tools.title: Create a lead
tools.description: WRITE: create a new lead (client contact and address, requested time, job type, source, notes). Returns the new lead's UUID, ClientId and app link. Workiz: POST /lead/create/.

tools.name: workiz_update_lead
tools.title: Update a lead
tools.description: WRITE: update fields on an existing lead — status, schedule, contact, address, type, source, notes, tags. Only the fields you pass are sent. Workiz: POST /lead/update/.

tools.name: workiz_assign_lead
tools.title: Assign a team member to a lead
tools.description: WRITE: assign a team member (by name) to a lead. Reversible with workiz_unassign_lead. Workiz: POST /lead/assign/.

tools.name: workiz_unassign_lead
tools.title: Unassign a team member from a lead
tools.description: WRITE: remove a team member (by name) from a lead. Reversible with workiz_assign_lead. Workiz: POST /lead/unassign/.

tools.name: workiz_convert_lead_to_job
tools.title: Convert a lead to a job
tools.description: WRITE (no API undo): convert a lead into a job. Creates a new job from the lead and returns its UUID and link; the API cannot reverse the conversion. Workiz: POST /lead/convert/.

tools.name: workiz_mark_lead_lost
tools.title: Mark a lead as lost
tools.description: WRITE: mark a lead as lost. Reversible with workiz_activate_lead. Workiz: POST /lead/markLost/{UUID}/.

tools.name: workiz_activate_lead
tools.title: Reactivate a lost lead
tools.description: WRITE: change a lost lead back to active. Workiz: POST /lead/activate/{UUID}/.

tools.name: workiz_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: workiz_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Workiz tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: workiz_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Workiz (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: workiz_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Workiz Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run workiz_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find both in Workiz → **Settings → Integrations → Developer** (requires the Workiz **Developer API add-on** on a paid plan). Your credentials are used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

examples: Show my open jobs with their scheduled times and assigned team members.
Which open leads came in during the last 7 days?
Who on my team has time off coming up in the next month?
Mark the lead for Jane Smith as lost, she chose another company.

servers.name: Depot
servers.description: Inspect Depot builds, CI runs, job logs and Actions runners; retry or cancel CI runs.

tools.name: depot_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the organization's Depot projects. A project is an isolated container-build cache (region, hardware, cache policy). Use the returned projectId with the build and registry tools. Depot: ProjectService/ListProjects.

tools.name: depot_get_project
tools.title: Get a project
tools.description: Get one Depot project — name, region, hardware size, cache policy, build timeout and autoscaling. Depot: ProjectService/GetProject.

tools.name: depot_list_builds
tools.title: List builds for a project
tools.description: List container builds in a project, newest first: status (STATUS_RUNNING / FAILED / SUCCESS / ERROR / CANCELED), timestamps, build duration, time saved by cache, and cached vs total steps. Depot: core BuildService/ListBuilds.

tools.name: depot_get_build
tools.title: Get a build
tools.description: Get one container build's status, timestamps, duration, time saved and cached/total step counts. Depot: core BuildService/GetBuild.

tools.name: depot_get_build_steps
tools.title: List a build's steps
tools.description: List the BuildKit steps of a container build: name, digest, start/end time, cache state (CACHED / UNCACHED), any error, and whether it has logs. Find the failing step here, then pass its digest to depot_get_build_step_logs. Depot: build.v1 BuildService/GetBuildSteps.

tools.name: depot_get_build_step_logs
tools.title: Get a build step's logs
tools.description: Get the log lines (message + timestamp) of one container-build step, identified by its digest from depot_get_build_steps. Depot: build.v1 BuildService/GetBuildStepLogs.

tools.name: depot_list_registry_images
tools.title: List registry images
tools.description: List the images stored in a project's Depot Registry: tag, digest, pushedAt and sizeBytes. Depot: build.v1 RegistryService/ListImages.

tools.name: depot_get_usage
tools.title: Get organization usage
tools.description: Get the organization's Depot usage over a window: container builds per project (build count, minutes saved, minutes billed), GitHub Actions jobs per repo/workflow/runner (minutes elapsed and billed), storage, and agent sandboxes. Depot: UsageService/GetUsage.

tools.name: depot_ci_list_runs
tools.title: List Depot CI runs
tools.description: List Depot CI runs, newest first. Filter by status (default: running + queued — pass ["failed"] to find failures), repo, commit SHA prefix, trigger event, or pull request number (requires repo). Depot: CIService/ListRuns.

tools.name: depot_ci_get_run_status
tools.title: Get a CI run's status tree
tools.description: Get a Depot CI run's status with its nested workflows, jobs and attempts (ids, keys, statuses, error messages). This is how to find the workflowId / jobId / attemptId for the log, diagnosis and retry tools. Depot: CIService/GetRunStatus.

tools.name: depot_ci_list_workflows
tools.title: List Depot CI workflows
tools.description: List Depot CI workflows across runs, newest first, with per-status job counts. Filter by name/path text, repo, status, trigger, SHA prefix or PR number. Depot: CIService/ListWorkflows.

tools.name: depot_ci_get_job
tools.title: Get a CI job
tools.description: Get one Depot CI job: status, conclusion, error message, timestamps, runner config (labels, image, CPUs, memory), matrix values, parent run/workflow context, dependencies and attempt history. Depot: CIService/GetJob.

tools.name: depot_ci_get_job_logs
tools.title: Get a CI job's logs
tools.description: Get persisted log lines for a Depot CI job attempt, oldest first (step key/name, timestamp, line number, body). Pass job_id to read the job's latest attempt, or attempt_id for a specific one — exactly one. Pass nextPageToken back as page_token for more lines. Depot: CIService/GetJobAttemptLogs.

tools.name: depot_ci_get_failure_diagnosis
tools.title: Diagnose a CI failure
tools.description: Get Depot's failure diagnosis for a CI run, workflow, job or attempt. For runs and workflows, identical failures are grouped by error fingerprint; for a job or attempt it is a focused diagnosis with evidence. Empty when no failure evidence is found. The best first call when a run failed. Depot: CIService/GetFailureDiagnosis.

tools.name: depot_gha_list_jobs
tools.title: List GitHub Actions jobs on Depot runners
tools.description: List GitHub Actions jobs that ran on Depot-managed runners, newest first: status, conclusion, runner label, requested CPU/memory, duration, billable time and GitHub URL. Defaults to the last 30 days (max window 90 days). Depot: GithubActionsService/ListGithubActionsJobs.

tools.name: depot_gha_search_logs
tools.title: Search GitHub Actions logs
tools.description: Search GitHub Actions log lines from Depot runners, newest match first (job, workflow, step, timestamp, body, lineId). Defaults to the last hour (max window 30 days). Filter by repository, workflow, runner label, action or compute id. Depot: GithubActionsService/SearchGithubActionsLogs.

tools.name: depot_gha_get_analytics
tools.title: Get GitHub Actions analytics
tools.description: Get time-bucketed GitHub Actions analytics for Depot runners: job counts (successful/failed/cancelled), failure rate, elapsed and billable seconds, average duration — as totals plus hourly or daily buckets. Defaults to the last 30 days (max 90). Depot: GithubActionsService/GetGithubActionsAnalytics.

tools.name: depot_gha_list_recommendations
tools.title: List runner-size recommendations
tools.description: List Depot's runner-size recommendations from job CPU and memory metrics: SIZE_UP when average CPU or memory reaches 90%, SIZE_DOWN when both averages stay ≤30% and peaks ≤70%, with current vs suggested size and per-minute price. Defaults to the last 30 days. Depot: GithubActionsService/ListGithubActionsRecommendations.

tools.name: depot_cache_list_entries
tools.title: List cache entries
tools.description: List Depot Cache entries of one type, optionally by key prefix: key, size in bytes, name and creation time (Depot returns no last-access time and no repository). Retention and size limits are set only in the dashboard (Organization Settings), not through the API. Depot: CacheService/ListEntries on cache.depot.dev.

tools.name: depot_cache_delete_entries
tools.title: Delete cache entries
tools.description: WRITE — deletes cached build data; a later build rebuilds it. Delete Depot Cache entries by exact key. Without confirm it only previews: it shows which keys exist, with their size, and deletes nothing. Show the preview to the user, then call again with confirm: true. Depot: CacheService/DeleteEntry on cache.depot.dev.

tools.name: depot_create_project
tools.title: Create a project
tools.description: WRITE. Create a Depot container-build project (an isolated build cache). Idempotent by name: if an active project with the same name exists, that project is returned. Defaults: cache 50 GB / 14 days, hardware HARDWARE_16X32 on AWS builders. Depot: ProjectService/CreateProject.

tools.name: depot_ci_retry_job
tools.title: Retry a CI job
tools.description: WRITE — starts compute. Retry one failed or cancelled Depot CI job, plus any skipped jobs that depend on it. Fails if a dependent job already started; use depot_ci_retry_failed_jobs then. Depot: CIService/RetryJob.

tools.name: depot_ci_retry_failed_jobs
tools.title: Retry a workflow's failed jobs
tools.description: WRITE — starts compute. Retry only the failed and cancelled jobs in a Depot CI workflow, plus skipped jobs that depend on them. Jobs that succeeded are left alone. Depot: CIService/RetryFailedJobs.

tools.name: depot_ci_cancel_run
tools.title: Cancel a CI run
tools.description: WRITE — stops work in progress. Cancel a queued or running Depot CI run and all of its unfinished workflows, jobs and attempts. Cancelled jobs can be retried afterwards with depot_ci_retry_failed_jobs. Depot: CIService/CancelRun.

tools.name: depot_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: depot_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Depot tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: depot_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Depot (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: depot_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Depot Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run depot_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create one in the [Depot dashboard](https://depot.dev/orgs) → **Organization Settings → API Tokens**. Depot derives the organization from the token. Your token is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Which CI runs failed recently and what was the diagnosis?
How many container builds did we run this month and how many minutes did caching save?
Show me the latest failed build steps for my main project.
Show the failed jobs in my latest failed run and their error messages.

servers.name: Mindbody
servers.description: Read Mindbody classes, schedules, clients, staff and sales; book clients and appointments.

tools.name: mindbody_list_sites
tools.title: List sites
tools.description: List the Mindbody sites (businesses) your developer account can access, or details for specific site ids. A cheap way to confirm the API key works. Mindbody: GET /site/sites.

tools.name: mindbody_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List the business's locations (studios / branches) with address, phone and amenities. Location ids are needed to book appointments. Mindbody: GET /site/locations.

tools.name: mindbody_list_session_types
tools.title: List session types
tools.description: List the session types (the bookable kinds of class or appointment, e.g. '60-min massage') used at the site. Session type ids drive appointment availability and booking. Mindbody: GET /site/sessiontypes.

tools.name: mindbody_list_classes
tools.title: List scheduled classes
tools.description: List scheduled class occurrences in a date range — time, class description, teacher, location, capacity, booked/waitlist counts and cancellation status. Mindbody: GET /class/classes.

tools.name: mindbody_list_class_schedules
tools.title: List class schedules
tools.description: List recurring class schedules (the templates that generate class occurrences) — days, times, teacher, location and date span. Mindbody: GET /class/classschedules.

tools.name: mindbody_get_class_visits
tools.title: Get a class's visits (roster)
tools.description: Get one class with its visits — the roster of clients booked into it, with sign-in / late-cancel status. Mindbody: GET /class/classvisits.

tools.name: mindbody_list_bookable_items
tools.title: Find bookable appointment slots
tools.description: Find appointment availability — which staff can deliver the given session types, where, and in which time windows. Use before mindbody_add_appointment. Mindbody: GET /appointment/bookableitems.

tools.name: mindbody_list_staff_appointments
tools.title: List appointments
tools.description: List booked appointments in a date range, by staff member, client or appointment id — the appointment book. Mindbody: GET /appointment/staffappointments.

tools.name: mindbody_list_clients
tools.title: Search clients
tools.description: Search or fetch client records by name/email text or by client ids (max 20 ids) — contact details, status, alerts, home location. Requires a staff user token. Mindbody: GET /client/clients.

tools.name: mindbody_list_client_visits
tools.title: List a client's visits
tools.description: List a client's past and scheduled visits (class and appointment attendance) in a date range, optionally only unpaid ones. Mindbody: GET /client/clientvisits.

tools.name: mindbody_list_client_memberships
tools.title: List a client's active memberships
tools.description: List a client's active memberships (auto-renewing pricing options) with remaining counts and expiry. Mindbody: GET /client/activeclientmemberships.

tools.name: mindbody_get_client_account_balances
tools.title: Get client account balances
tools.description: Get the account balance for one or more clients (what they owe or hold in credit), optionally as of a date. Mindbody: GET /client/clientaccountbalances.

tools.name: mindbody_list_staff
tools.title: List staff
tools.description: List staff members (instructors, practitioners). Filter by role, or find who is available for a session type at a location and time (session_type_id + location_id + start_date_time together). Without a staff token only public fields return. Mindbody: GET /staff/staff.

tools.name: mindbody_list_services
tools.title: List pricing options
tools.description: List the pricing options (services — class packs, drop-ins, intro offers) for sale at the site, with price, online price, count and expiry. Read only. Mindbody: GET /sale/services.

tools.name: mindbody_list_sales
tools.title: List sales
tools.description: List completed sales at the site in a date/time range — purchased items, payments and client. Read only. Mindbody: GET /sale/sales.

tools.name: mindbody_add_client_to_class
tools.title: Book a client into a class
tools.description: Book a client into a class (or onto its waiting list). Does not take payment: by default no pricing option is required; set require_payment to insist the client has a usable one on account. Undo from the Mindbody front desk. Pass test: true to validate only. Mindbody: POST /class/addclienttoclass.

tools.name: mindbody_add_appointment
tools.title: Book an appointment
tools.description: Book an appointment for a client with a staff member at a location. Find a slot first with mindbody_list_bookable_items. No card is charged; apply_payment (Mindbody's default is true) only applies a pricing option already on the client's account. Pass test: true to validate only. Requires a staff user token. Mindbody: POST /appointment/addappointment.

tools.name: mindbody_update_appointment
tools.title: Update an appointment
tools.description: Reschedule or edit an appointment (start/end time, staff, session type, notes — the only fields Mindbody lets you change) and/or move it through its status: confirm, unconfirm, arrive, unarrive, complete. Cancel and late-cancel are deliberately not offered (a late cancel can charge the client). Pass test: true to validate only. Requires a staff user token. Mindbody: POST /appointment/updateappointment.

tools.name: mindbody_add_client
tools.title: Add a client
tools.description: Create a new client record (first and last name required; the site may require more — Mindbody reports which). No card or billing data is accepted. Pass test: true to validate only. Mindbody: POST /client/addclient.

tools.name: mindbody_update_client
tools.title: Update a client
tools.description: Update fields on an existing client record — only the fields you pass change. No card or billing data is accepted. cross_regional_update (Mindbody default: true) also updates the client's profiles at the region's other sites. Pass test: true to validate only. Mindbody: POST /client/updateclient.

tools.name: mindbody_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: mindbody_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Mindbody tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: mindbody_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Mindbody (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: mindbody_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Mindbody Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run mindbody_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Your credentials are used only to call the Mindbody API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone. Note: Mindbody meters and bills API calls to your developer account.

examples: Which classes are on the schedule tomorrow and how full is each one?
Who is booked into this Friday's evening yoga class?
Show me all the sales we rang up last week with the totals.
Which memberships does Jane Smith currently hold and how many visits are left?

servers.name: Buildium
servers.description: Read Buildium properties, units, leases, tenants, balances and bills; manage work orders.

tools.name: buildium_list_rental_properties
tools.title: List rental properties
tools.description: List rental properties (buildings) with address, unit count, type/subtype and manager. Filter by location (city/state contains), type, subtype, status, rental owner or property ids. Buildium: GET /v1/rentals.

tools.name: buildium_get_rental_property
tools.title: Get a rental property
tools.description: Fetch one rental property by id. Buildium: GET /v1/rentals/{propertyId}.

tools.name: buildium_list_rental_units
tools.title: List rental units
tools.description: List rental units with unit number, bedrooms/bathrooms, size, market rent and whether each unit is listed or occupied. Filter by property. Buildium: GET /v1/rentals/units.

tools.name: buildium_get_rental_unit
tools.title: Get a rental unit
tools.description: Fetch one rental unit by id. Buildium: GET /v1/rentals/units/{unitId}.

tools.name: buildium_list_rental_owners
tools.title: List rental owners
tools.description: List rental owners (the landlords you manage for) with contact details, management-agreement dates and the property ids they own. Buildium: GET /v1/rentals/owners.

tools.name: buildium_list_leases
tools.title: List leases
tools.description: List leases with unit, dates, lease type/status, current tenants, rent/deposit account details and eviction flag. Filter by property, owner, unit number, tenant name, dates, lease type or status (Active/Past/Future). Buildium: GET /v1/leases.

tools.name: buildium_get_lease
tools.title: Get a lease
tools.description: Fetch one lease by id, including tenants, cosigners, account details and move-out data. Buildium: GET /v1/leases/{leaseId}.

tools.name: buildium_list_outstanding_balances
tools.title: List lease outstanding balances
tools.description: Delinquency report: leases that owe money, with aged buckets (0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+ days), total balance, past-due-email and eviction-pending dates. Leases with zero or credit balances are not returned. Buildium: GET /v1/leases/outstandingbalances.

tools.name: buildium_list_lease_transactions
tools.title: List lease transactions
tools.description: Read a lease's ledger: charges, payments, credits, refunds, deposits and other transactions with date, type, total amount and journal lines. Read-only — this server never posts to a ledger. Buildium: GET /v1/leases/{leaseId}/transactions.

tools.name: buildium_list_tenants
tools.title: List tenants
tools.description: List rental tenants with contact details, emergency contact, address and leases. Filter by name, email, phone, unit number, property, owner, unit ids or lease term status. Buildium: GET /v1/leases/tenants.

tools.name: buildium_get_tenant
tools.title: Get a tenant
tools.description: Fetch one rental tenant by id. Buildium: GET /v1/leases/tenants/{tenantId}.

tools.name: buildium_list_applicants
tools.title: List applicants
tools.description: List rental applicants with contact details, status and their applications. Filter by application status, unit, name, email, submission date or entity. Buildium: GET /v1/applicants.

tools.name: buildium_list_work_orders
tools.title: List work orders
tools.description: List work orders with title, status, priority, due date, vendor, amount, line items, linked task and bill ids. Filter by entity, status, priority, task type, unit, vendor, assignee, dates, amount, billed flag or title. Buildium: GET /v1/workorders.

tools.name: buildium_get_work_order
tools.title: Get a work order
tools.description: Fetch one work order by id. Buildium: GET /v1/workorders/{workOrderId}.

tools.name: buildium_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List all tasks/requests — contact requests, resident requests, rental owner requests and to-dos — with category, property, unit, requester, assignee, status, priority and due date. Buildium: GET /v1/tasks.

tools.name: buildium_list_vendors
tools.title: List vendors
tools.description: List vendors (contractors, suppliers) with contact details, category, insurance and default expense GL account. Filter by name, email, phone, website, status or insurance expiration. Buildium: GET /v1/vendors.

tools.name: buildium_list_bills
tools.title: List bills
tools.description: List vendor bills (accounts payable) with dates, memo, vendor, linked work order, reference number, approval status and lines. Read-only. Buildium: GET /v1/bills.

tools.name: buildium_list_gl_accounts
tools.title: List general ledger accounts
tools.description: List the chart of accounts: GL accounts with number, name, type/subtype, sub-accounts and bank/credit-card flags. Useful for finding the gl_account_id for work order line items. Buildium: GET /v1/glaccounts.

tools.name: buildium_list_associations
tools.title: List associations
tools.description: List community/HOA associations with address, manager, reserve, fiscal year and operating bank account. Buildium: GET /v1/associations.

tools.name: buildium_create_work_order
tools.title: Create a work order
tools.description: Create a work order for a vendor. Attach it to an existing task (task_id) or create a new task with it (task: title, priority, status, assigned staff user, optional due date/property/unit). vendor_id and entry_allowed are required. Line items are optional (quantity x unit price, optional GL account). Buildium: POST /v1/workorders.

tools.name: buildium_update_work_order
tools.title: Update a work order
tools.description: Update a work order's details. Buildium's PUT replaces the whole record, so this reads the current work order first and only changes the fields you pass — everything else (including line items and entry contacts) is preserved. Passing line_items REPLACES all existing line items. Status/priority/due date live on the linked task. Buildium: GET then PUT /v1/workorders/{workOrderId}.

tools.name: buildium_create_todo_task
tools.title: Create a to-do task
tools.description: Create an internal to-do task assigned to a staff user, optionally tied to a property/unit and category, with a due date. Buildium: POST /v1/tasks/todorequests.

tools.name: buildium_update_todo_task
tools.title: Update a to-do task
tools.description: Update a to-do task — change status (e.g. mark Completed), priority, assignee, due date, title or category, optionally with an update message. Buildium's PUT replaces the whole record, so this reads the current task first and only changes the fields you pass. Buildium: GET then PUT /v1/tasks/todorequests/{toDoTaskId}.

tools.name: buildium_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: buildium_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Buildium tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: buildium_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Buildium (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: buildium_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Buildium Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run buildium_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: An administrator first enables the API in Buildium → **Settings → Application settings → Api settings** (toggle Open API), then creates a key under **Settings → Developer Tools → Create API Key**, choosing which data it may read. The secret is shown only once, at creation. Keys are environment-bound: pick Sandbox for a sandbox account's key. Your credentials are used only to call the Buildium API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

examples: Which tenants currently owe rent, and how overdue are they?
Which open work orders are high priority right now?
List the leases for my properties and when each one ends.
Which to-do tasks are still open and due this month?

servers.name: Housecall Pro
servers.description: Manage Housecall Pro customers, jobs, estimates and leads; schedule and dispatch jobs.

tools.name: housecall_get_company
tools.title: Get the company
tools.description: Fetch the Housecall Pro company this key belongs to — name, contact details, address, time zone, service-area zip codes and (multi-location) its locations. A cheap way to confirm the key works. Housecall Pro: GET /company.

tools.name: housecall_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List or search customers, with their phone numbers, tags and addresses. `q` searches name, email, mobile number and address. Housecall Pro: GET /customers.

tools.name: housecall_get_customer
tools.title: Get one customer
tools.description: Fetch a single customer by id, including their addresses (whose ids you need to create a job or estimate). Housecall Pro: GET /customers/{customer_id}.

tools.name: housecall_list_jobs
tools.title: List jobs
tools.description: List jobs, filterable by scheduled window, customer, assigned employees and work status. Each job carries its customer, address, notes, schedule, assigned employees and totals. Housecall Pro: GET /jobs.

tools.name: housecall_get_job
tools.title: Get one job
tools.description: Fetch a single job by id — customer, address, work status and timestamps, schedule, assigned employees, notes and totals. Housecall Pro: GET /jobs/{id}.

tools.name: housecall_list_job_line_items
tools.title: List a job's line items
tools.description: List the line items (services, materials, labor, discounts) on one job, with unit price, cost, quantity and amount in cents. Housecall Pro: GET /jobs/{job_id}/line_items.

tools.name: housecall_list_job_invoices
tools.title: List a job's invoices
tools.description: List the invoices raised for one job, with status, amounts, due and paid dates, items, taxes, discounts and payments. Housecall Pro: GET /jobs/{job_id}/invoices.

tools.name: housecall_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices across the company, filterable by status, customer, and created / due / paid date ranges — e.g. everything open and overdue. Amounts are in cents. Housecall Pro: GET /invoices.

tools.name: housecall_list_estimates
tools.title: List estimates
tools.description: List estimates, filterable by scheduled window, customer, assigned employees and work status. Each carries its customer, address, schedule and options. Housecall Pro: GET /estimates.

tools.name: housecall_get_estimate
tools.title: Get one estimate
tools.description: Fetch a single estimate by id, including its options and each option's approval status. Housecall Pro: GET /estimates/{estimate_id}.

tools.name: housecall_list_employees
tools.title: List employees
tools.description: List the company's active employees with their role, contact details and permissions. Use their ids to assign or dispatch jobs. Housecall Pro: GET /employees.

tools.name: housecall_list_leads
tools.title: List leads
tools.description: List leads, filterable by status (open / won / lost), customer, assigned employees, tags and lead source. Housecall Pro: GET /leads.

tools.name: housecall_get_lead
tools.title: Get one lead
tools.description: Fetch a single lead by id — its customer, address, lead source, tags, assigned employee, status and pipeline status. Housecall Pro: GET /leads/{id}.

tools.name: housecall_list_job_types
tools.title: List job types
tools.description: List the company's job types (e.g. Repair, Install, Maintenance). Use an id as job_type_id when creating a job or estimate. Housecall Pro: GET /job_fields/job_types.

tools.name: housecall_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: List the tags defined in the company. Housecall Pro: GET /tags.

tools.name: housecall_list_price_book_services
tools.title: List price book services
tools.description: List or search the price book's services — name, task number, price and cost (cents), taxable and online-booking flags; optionally with their materials and labor rates. Housecall Pro: GET /api/price_book/services.

tools.name: housecall_create_customer
tools.title: Create a customer
tools.description: Create a new customer, optionally with one or more addresses. Housecall Pro: POST /customers.

tools.name: housecall_update_customer
tools.title: Update a customer
tools.description: Change a customer's name, contact details, tags, lead source, notes or notification setting. Only the fields you pass are sent. Housecall Pro: PUT /customers/{customer_id}.

tools.name: housecall_create_customer_address
tools.title: Add an address to a customer
tools.description: Add a service address to an existing customer. Returns the address id to use when creating a job or estimate. Housecall Pro: POST /customers/{customer_id}/addresses.

tools.name: housecall_create_job
tools.title: Create a job
tools.description: Create a job for an existing customer at one of their existing addresses, optionally scheduled, assigned, tagged and with line items (prices in cents). Get address ids from housecall_get_customer. Housecall Pro: POST /jobs.

tools.name: housecall_update_job_schedule
tools.title: Reschedule a job
tools.description: Set or change a job's scheduled start/end and arrival window, optionally dispatching employees and notifying the customer and/or the pro. Jobs with more than one appointment (multi-day) cannot be rescheduled here. Housecall Pro: PUT /jobs/{job_id}/schedule.

tools.name: housecall_dispatch_job
tools.title: Dispatch a job to employees
tools.description: Set which employees a job is dispatched to. This REPLACES the current dispatch list — pass everyone who should be on the job. Housecall Pro: PUT /jobs/{job_id}/dispatch.

tools.name: housecall_add_job_note
tools.title: Add a note to a job
tools.description: Add a text note to a job. Housecall Pro: POST /jobs/{job_id}/notes.

tools.name: housecall_create_estimate
tools.title: Create an estimate
tools.description: Create an estimate for a customer with one or more options (e.g. Good / Better / Best), each with line items priced in cents. Give an existing address_id or a new address. Housecall Pro: POST /estimates.

tools.name: housecall_create_lead
tools.title: Create a lead
tools.description: Create a lead, either for an existing customer (customer_id) or with a new customer inline (customer). Optionally with an address, lead source, assigned employee, tags, note and line items priced in cents. Housecall Pro: POST /leads.

tools.name: housecall_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: housecall_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Housecall Pro tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: housecall_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Housecall Pro (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: housecall_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Housecall Pro Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run housecall_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find the key in Housecall Pro → **My Apps → All Apps → API Key Management → Generate API Key** (account admins only; API access requires the **MAX plan**). The company ID is only for multi-location accounts, to pin one location (sent as `X-Company-Id`); leave it blank otherwise. Your key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: What jobs are scheduled for this week and who are they dispatched to?
Which invoices are still unpaid and how old are they?
Show my newest estimates with each option's approval status.
Add a note to Jane Smith's latest job saying the gate code is 4521.

servers.name: Hostaway
servers.description: Manage Hostaway listings, reservations, calendar, guest messages, reviews and tasks.

tools.name: hostaway_list_listings
tools.title: List listings
tools.description: List the account's properties (listings) with name, address, capacity, base price, fees and check-in times. Filter by name, city, country, property type, availability for a date range and guest count, or active/archived status. Hostaway: GET /v1/listings.

tools.name: hostaway_get_listing
tools.title: Get one listing
tools.description: Fetch a single listing by id — full details including description, house rules, amenities, images, fees, taxes, cancellation policy and access info (door code, wifi). Hostaway: GET /v1/listings/{listingId}.

tools.name: hostaway_list_reservations
tools.title: List reservations
tools.description: List reservations across all channels (Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, direct…) with guest, dates, status, price and channel. Filter by listing, channel, arrival/departure window, guest name or email, unread messages, and more. Default order is newest first; for large accounts page with afterId (the id of the last reservation on the previous page). Channel ids: 2000 direct, 2018 airbnbOfficial, 2002 homeaway/Vrbo, 2005 bookingcom, 2007 expedia, 2013 bookingengine, 2019 marriott, 2020 partner, 2022 google. Hostaway: GET /v1/reservations.

tools.name: hostaway_get_reservation
tools.title: Get one reservation
tools.description: Fetch a single reservation by its Hostaway id — guest contact details, dates, guest counts, price breakdown, payment state, door code, notes, channel and cancellation policy. Hostaway: GET /v1/reservations/{reservationId}.

tools.name: hostaway_get_reservation_logs
tools.title: Get reservation change history
tools.description: The audit trail for one reservation: every field change with previous and new value, when, and by which user (most recent first). Useful for 'who changed these dates / this price?'. Hostaway: GET /v1/reservations/{reservationId}/logs.

tools.name: hostaway_get_calendar
tools.title: Get listing calendar
tools.description: Day-by-day availability and pricing for one listing over a date range: status (available, blocked, reserved, pending), nightly price, min/max stay, closed-to-arrival/departure and notes. Set includeResources to see the reservations occupying each day. Hostaway: GET /v1/listings/{listingId}/calendar.

tools.name: hostaway_calculate_price
tools.title: Quote a stay
tools.description: Calculate what a stay at a listing would cost — total price plus the component breakdown (base rate, cleaning fee, taxes, discounts). A calculation only: nothing is booked or held. Hostaway: POST /v1/listings/{listingId}/calendar/priceDetails (version 2).

tools.name: hostaway_list_conversations
tools.title: List guest conversations
tools.description: List guest conversations (the unified inbox across channels), each with its latest message and linked reservation. Filter to one reservation. Hostaway: GET /v1/conversations.

tools.name: hostaway_list_conversation_messages
tools.title: Read a conversation
tools.description: The messages in one guest conversation — body, direction (isIncoming), channel/email/SMS type, send status and timestamps. By default only sent messages; set includeScheduledMessages to also see scheduled, paused or failed ones. Hostaway: GET /v1/conversations/{conversationId}/messages.

tools.name: hostaway_list_reviews
tools.title: List reviews
tools.description: List guest-to-host and host-to-guest reviews with rating (0-10), public review, private feedback and the host's reply. Filter by listings, reservation, type, status, rating range, dates, guest name, or whether the host has replied. Hostaway: GET /v1/reviews.

tools.name: hostaway_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List operational tasks (cleaning, maintenance, check-in/out) with assignee, status, time window and cost. Filter by reservation, status, text match, channel, or start/deadline windows. Hostaway: GET /v1/tasks.

tools.name: hostaway_list_expenses
tools.title: List expenses and extras
tools.description: List expenses (negative amounts) and extras (positive amounts) recorded against listings and reservations, with date, concept, categories and the owner statements they appear on. Hostaway: GET /v1/expenses.

tools.name: hostaway_list_owner_statements
tools.title: List owner statements
tools.description: List the account's owner statements (id and name). Hostaway: GET /v1/ownerStatements.

tools.name: hostaway_get_owner_statement
tools.title: Get one owner statement
tools.description: Fetch one owner statement — the filter it was generated with (listings, date range), summary and per-reservation financial data, grand totals, expenses, and owner / property-manager details. Hostaway: GET /v1/ownerStatement/{ownerStatementId}.

tools.name: hostaway_create_reservation
tools.title: Create a reservation
tools.description: Create a new reservation on a listing (it blocks the calendar and syncs to connected channels). Only channelId 2000 (direct, the default), 2002 (homeaway) or 2020 (partner) are accepted. To price it correctly, call hostaway_calculate_price first and pass its total as totalPrice. Overbooking protection is always left on. Hostaway: POST /v1/reservations.

tools.name: hostaway_update_reservation
tools.title: Update a reservation
tools.description: Change fields on an existing reservation — guest details and counts, dates, check-in/out hours, door code, host note or comment. Send only the fields to change. The listing cannot be changed, and this tool never cancels or reprices a booking. Date changes on channel bookings may be overwritten by the channel. Hostaway: PUT /v1/reservations/{reservationId}.

tools.name: hostaway_update_calendar
tools.title: Update listing calendar
tools.description: Change availability and/or pricing for a date range on one listing, pushed to every connected channel: block (isAvailable=false) or open days, set the nightly price, min/max stay, closed-to-arrival/departure, or a note. For multi-unit listings set desiredUnitsToSell instead of isAvailable (0 blocks). Hostaway: PUT /v1/listings/{listingId}/calendar.

tools.name: hostaway_send_message
tools.title: Send a guest message
tools.description: Send a message to the guest in a conversation — it is delivered immediately and cannot be recalled. Delivered by email by default, or via the booking channel, SMS or WhatsApp. Attachments are not supported. Rate-limited by Hostaway to 30 messages per minute. Hostaway: POST /v1/conversations/{conversationId}/messages.

tools.name: hostaway_create_task
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: Create an operational task — e.g. a cleaning after a checkout or a maintenance job — optionally tied to a listing and reservation, assigned to a user, with a time window, category and cost. Hostaway: POST /v1/tasks.

tools.name: hostaway_update_task
tools.title: Update a task
tools.description: Update a task — change its status (e.g. completed), reassign it, move its window, or add a resolution note. Send only the fields to change. Hostaway: PUT /v1/tasks/{taskId}.

tools.name: hostaway_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: hostaway_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Hostaway tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: hostaway_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Hostaway (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: hostaway_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Hostaway Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run hostaway_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find both in the Hostaway dashboard → **Settings → Hostaway API**: your numeric Account ID is shown there, and you can create an API key. Connecting takes a couple of seconds while we check the pair with Hostaway. Your credentials are used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

examples: Which guests check in over the next 7 days, and at which properties?
Show me the latest guest reviews and their ratings across my listings.
What would a 5-night stay for 2 guests at my beach house cost starting June 12?
Create a cleaning task for the lake cabin on the day after checkout.

servers.name: Invoice Ninja
servers.description: Manage Invoice Ninja clients, invoices, quotes, expenses, tasks and projects.

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_clients
tools.title: List clients
tools.description: List clients with balances and contacts, optionally searched by name, email or number. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/clients.

tools.name: invoiceninja_get_client

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_invoices

tools.name: invoiceninja_get_invoice
tools.title: Get one invoice
tools.description: Fetch one invoice by id — line items, totals, balance, dates, status and invitations. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/invoices/{id}.

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_quotes
tools.title: List quotes
tools.description: List quotes (estimates), filterable by client and quote status. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/quotes.

tools.name: invoiceninja_get_quote
tools.title: Get one quote
tools.description: Fetch one quote by id — line items, totals, status and the invoice it was converted to (invoice_id), if any. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/quotes/{id}.

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products / services in the catalog with price, cost and default taxes. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/products.

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_payments
tools.title: List payments
tools.description: List payments received, with amount, date, refunded/applied totals and the invoices each was applied to (paymentables). Read-only: this server never records or refunds payments. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/payments.

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_expenses
tools.title: List expenses
tools.description: List expenses, filterable by client and invoicing/payment state. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/expenses.

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_vendors
tools.title: List vendors
tools.description: List vendors (suppliers) with contacts and address. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/vendors.

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List tasks / time entries with their time_log, duration, rate and linked client, project and invoice. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/tasks.

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_projects

tools.description: List projects with client, budgeted hours, task rate, current hours and due date. Invoice Ninja: GET /api/v1/projects.

tools.name: invoiceninja_list_recurring_invoices

tools.name: invoiceninja_create_client

tools.name: invoiceninja_update_client

tools.name: invoiceninja_create_invoice

tools.name: invoiceninja_update_invoice

tools.name: invoiceninja_mark_invoice_sent

tools.name: invoiceninja_email_invoice

tools.name: invoiceninja_create_quote

tools.name: invoiceninja_convert_quote_to_invoice

tools.name: invoiceninja_create_expense

tools.description: Log an expense, optionally tied to a vendor, client or project and flagged to be re-invoiced. Invoice Ninja: POST /api/v1/expenses.

tools.name: invoiceninja_create_task
tools.title: Create a task / log time
tools.description: Create a task, optionally with logged time entries, for a client or project. Invoice Ninja: POST /api/v1/tasks.

tools.name: invoiceninja_create_project

servers.name: Atera
servers.description: Check devices, alerts and tickets in Atera, and open tickets, comment or resolve alerts.

tools.name: atera_get_account
tools.title: Get the account
tools.description: Fetch the Atera account this key belongs to — company name, plan, country and timezone. A cheap way to confirm the key works. Atera: GET /api/v3/account.

tools.name: atera_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List the customers (client companies) managed in Atera, paginated. Atera: GET /api/v3/customers.

tools.name: atera_get_customer
tools.title: Get one customer
tools.description: Fetch a single customer by id — address, domain, phone, notes. Atera: GET /api/v3/customers/{customerId}.

tools.name: atera_list_agents
tools.title: List agents (devices)
tools.description: List Atera agents — the managed machines — with online status, last seen, OS, hardware and logged-in user. Pass customer_id to list only one customer's devices. Atera: GET /api/v3/agents or GET /api/v3/agents/customer/{customerId}.

tools.name: atera_get_agent
tools.title: Get one agent (device)
tools.description: Fetch a single agent by its AgentID — full device inventory, online status, IPs, OS build and last reboot. Atera: GET /api/v3/agents/{agentId}.

tools.name: atera_find_agents_by_machine
tools.title: Find agents by machine name
tools.description: Find the agent(s) installed on a machine by its machine name, e.g. DESKTOP-4F2K9. Atera: GET /api/v3/agents/machine/{machineName}.

tools.name: atera_get_agent_patches
tools.title: Get an agent's patches
tools.description: List the Windows/OS patches on one device — either those still AVAILABLE (missing) or those already INSTALLED. Takes the device's DeviceGuid (from atera_list_agents / atera_get_agent), not the AgentID. Atera: GET /api/v3/agents/{deviceGuid}/available-patches or /installed-patches.

tools.name: atera_list_alerts
tools.title: List alerts
tools.description: List monitoring alerts (disk, CPU, availability, hardware...) with severity, device, customer and linked ticket. Filter by status. Atera: GET /api/v3/alerts.

tools.name: atera_list_tickets
tools.title: List tickets
tools.description: List helpdesk tickets with priority, status, type, end user, technician, SLA durations and last comments. Filter by customer and/or status. Atera: GET /api/v3/tickets.

tools.name: atera_get_ticket
tools.title: Get one ticket
tools.description: Fetch a single ticket by its TicketID. Atera: GET /api/v3/tickets/{ticketId}.

tools.name: atera_list_ticket_comments
tools.title: List a ticket's comments
tools.description: List the comment thread on one ticket — end-user and technician replies, with internal notes flagged. Atera: GET /api/v3/tickets/{ticketId}/comments.

tools.name: atera_list_ticket_work_hours
tools.title: List a ticket's work hours
tools.description: List the time entries logged on one ticket — technician, start/end, billable, on-site, rate. Atera: GET /api/v3/tickets/{ticketId}/workhoursrecords.

tools.name: atera_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List end-user contacts, optionally searching by whole or partial email or phone number. Atera: GET /api/v3/contacts.

tools.name: atera_list_contracts
tools.title: List contracts
tools.description: List service contracts (retainer, block hours, hourly, remote monitoring...) with their rates and billing periods. Pass customer_id for one customer's contracts. Atera: GET /api/v3/contracts or GET /api/v3/contracts/customer/{customerId}.

tools.name: atera_list_kb_articles
tools.title: List knowledge-base articles
tools.description: List knowledge-base articles with their product, keywords, section, category and ratings. Atera: GET /api/v3/knowledgebases.

tools.name: atera_create_ticket
tools.title: Create a ticket
tools.description: Open a new helpdesk ticket. Give either end_user_id (an existing contact's EndUserID) or all of end_user_first_name, end_user_last_name and end_user_email to create a new contact with it. Atera: POST /api/v3/tickets.

tools.name: atera_update_ticket
tools.title: Update a ticket
tools.description: Change a ticket's title, status, type, priority, impact or assigned technician. Only the fields you pass are sent. Atera: PUT /api/v3/tickets/{ticketId}.

tools.name: atera_add_ticket_comment
tools.title: Comment on a ticket
tools.description: Add a comment to a ticket, either as a technician (technician_id, with is_internal=true for a private note or false for a reply the end user sees) or on behalf of an end user (enduser_id). Atera: POST /api/v3/tickets/{ticketId}/comments.

tools.name: atera_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: Create a new end-user contact under an existing customer (give customer_id or customer_name). Atera: POST /api/v3/contacts.

tools.name: atera_resolve_alert
tools.title: Resolve an alert
tools.description: Mark one monitoring alert as resolved. If the underlying condition persists, Atera raises it again on the next check. Atera: PUT /api/v3/alerts/{alertId}.

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Atera (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

The key is account-wide; this server only reads data and writes tickets, comments, contacts and alert resolutions — it never deletes anything or runs scripts on devices.
