tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Rewardful tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: rewardful_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Rewardful (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: rewardful_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Rewardful Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run rewardful_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find it in Rewardful → **Company settings** ([app.getrewardful.com/company/edit](https://app.getrewardful.com/company/edit)), in the API section: copy the **API Secret**, not the public API Key used by the tracking snippet. Your secret is used only to call the Rewardful API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: List my affiliates with their visitor, lead and conversion counts.
How much commission is currently owed to my affiliates?
Show my latest payouts and the amounts paid.
What reward rules do my affiliate campaigns use?

servers.name: sevdesk
servers.description: Look up contacts, invoices, vouchers, orders, bank transactions and parts, and create drafts.

tools.name: sevdesk_get_bookkeeping_system_version
tools.title: Get the bookkeeping system version
tools.description: Return whether the account runs sevdesk bookkeeping 1.0 or 2.0 (2.0 uses taxRule instead of taxType on invoices). Also a cheap way to confirm the API token works. sevdesk: GET /Tools/bookkeepingSystemVersion.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts (customers, suppliers, partners, prospects). By default sevdesk returns only organisations; set include_persons to also get individual persons. sevdesk: GET /Contact.

tools.name: sevdesk_get_contact
tools.title: Get one contact
tools.description: Fetch a single contact by id. sevdesk: GET /Contact/{contactId}.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_communication_ways
tools.title: List contact emails, phones and websites
tools.description: List communication ways (email addresses, phone and mobile numbers, websites), optionally for one contact. sevdesk: GET /CommunicationWay.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_communication_way_keys
tools.title: List communication way keys
tools.description: List the labels a communication way can carry (1 Privat, 2 Arbeit, 3 Fax, 4 Mobil, 6 Autobox, 7 Newsletter, 8 Rechnungsadresse). Needed for sevdesk_add_communication_way. sevdesk: GET /CommunicationWayKey.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices, filterable by status, number, date range and contact. Status: 50 deactivated recurring, 100 draft, 200 open/due, 750 partially paid, 1000 paid. sevdesk: GET /Invoice.

tools.name: sevdesk_get_invoice
tools.title: Get one invoice
tools.description: Fetch a single invoice by id — totals, status, dates, contact and contact person. sevdesk: GET /Invoice/{invoiceId}.

tools.name: sevdesk_get_invoice_positions
tools.title: Get an invoice's line items
tools.description: List the positions (line items) of one invoice: name, quantity, price, tax rate, sums. sevdesk: GET /Invoice/{invoiceId}/getPositions.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_vouchers
tools.title: List vouchers (receipts)
tools.description: List vouchers — receipts and incoming/outgoing bills. Status: 50 draft, 100 unpaid/due, 1000 paid. credit_debit C = credit (revenue), D = debit (expense). sevdesk: GET /Voucher.

tools.name: sevdesk_get_voucher
tools.title: Get one voucher
tools.description: Fetch a single voucher (receipt) by id. sevdesk: GET /Voucher/{voucherId}.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_credit_notes
tools.title: List credit notes
tools.description: List credit notes (Gutschriften), filterable by status, number, date range and contact. Status: 100 draft, 200 open/delivered, 750 partially paid, 1000 paid. sevdesk: GET /CreditNote.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_orders
tools.title: List orders and quotes
tools.description: List orders — quotes (Angebote), order confirmations and delivery notes — filterable by status, number, date range and contact. Status: 100 draft, 200 delivered, 300 rejected, 500 accepted, 750 partially calculated, 1000 calculated. sevdesk: GET /Order.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_parts
tools.title: List parts (products)
tools.description: List parts — the products and services in the sevdesk inventory, with prices, tax rate and stock. sevdesk: GET /Part.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_check_accounts
tools.title: List payment accounts
tools.description: List check accounts — the bank accounts, cash registers and clearing accounts sevdesk tracks payments on, with IBAN, type and sync status. sevdesk: GET /CheckAccount.

tools.name: sevdesk_get_check_account_balance
tools.title: Get a payment account's balance at a date
tools.description: Balance of one check account as the sum of every transaction sevdesk knows up to and including the given date. May differ from the real bank balance if older transactions were never imported. sevdesk: GET /CheckAccount/{checkAccountId}/getBalanceAtDate.

tools.name: sevdesk_list_transactions
tools.title: List bank transactions
tools.description: List check-account transactions (bank payments in and out), filterable by account, booking state, date range, payee/payer and purpose. sevdesk: GET /CheckAccountTransaction.

tools.name: sevdesk_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: Create a contact. Give `name` for an organisation, or `surename`/`familyname` for a person. Addresses and emails are separate (use sevdesk_add_communication_way). sevdesk: POST /Contact.

tools.name: sevdesk_update_contact
tools.title: Update a contact
tools.description: Update fields on an existing contact; only the fields you pass are sent. sevdesk: PUT /Contact/{contactId}.

tools.name: sevdesk_add_communication_way
tools.title: Add an email, phone or website to a contact
tools.description: Attach an email address, phone/mobile number or website to a contact. key_id labels it (2 Arbeit/work is a good default; see sevdesk_list_communication_way_keys). sevdesk: POST /CommunicationWay.

tools.name: sevdesk_create_draft_invoice
tools.title: Create a draft invoice
tools.description: Create a normal invoice (type RE) with its line items, ALWAYS saved as a DRAFT (status 100): it is not sent, not booked and stays editable in sevdesk. contact_person_id is the sevdesk USER responsible for it — copy contactPerson.id from any existing invoice (sevdesk_get_invoice). Bookkeeping 2.0 accounts use tax_rule_id (1 = taxable sales in Germany, the usual choice); 1.0 accounts pass tax_type instead (check sevdesk_get_bookkeeping_system_version). sevdesk: POST /Invoice/Factory/saveInvoice.

Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sevdesk_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's sevdesk Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run sevdesk_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find it in sevDesk → **Settings → Users → your user → API token** (32 hex characters). API access requires a **paid sevDesk plan**. Your token is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Which invoices are still unpaid, and how much do customers owe?
What is the current balance of my business bank account?
Show me the bank payments that came in last month.
Which receipts and bills did I record this month?

servers.name: Shopmonkey
servers.description: Look up shop customers, vehicles, work orders and parts, and create orders or book appointments.

tools.name: shopmonkey_get_current_user
tools.title: Get the current user
tools.description: Fetch the user this API key acts as — id, name, company, default location and permissions. A cheap way to confirm the key works and to find your locationId. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/user/me.

tools.name: shopmonkey_search_customers
tools.title: Search customers
tools.description: Search customers with a server-side filter, sort and paging. Returns customers with their emails and phone numbers. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/customer/search.

tools.name: shopmonkey_find_customers_by_phone
tools.title: Find customers by phone number
tools.description: Find the customers that own any of the given phone numbers — the usual way to identify a caller. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/customer/phone_number/search.

tools.name: shopmonkey_find_customers_by_email
tools.title: Find customers by email
tools.description: Find the customers that own any of the given email addresses. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/customer/email/search.

tools.name: shopmonkey_get_customer
tools.title: Get one customer
tools.description: Fetch a single customer by id — contact details, emails, phone numbers, counts of vehicles/orders/appointments. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/customer/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_list_customer_vehicles
tools.title: List a customer's vehicles
tools.description: List the vehicles owned by a customer (year/make/model, VIN, plate, mileage). Shopmonkey: GET /v3/customer/:id/vehicle.

tools.name: shopmonkey_list_customer_orders
tools.title: List a customer's orders
tools.description: List a customer's work orders (estimates, repair orders, invoices) — their service history. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/customer/:id/order.

tools.name: shopmonkey_get_vehicle
tools.title: Get one vehicle
tools.description: Fetch a single vehicle by id, including its mileage and tire-pressure logs. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/vehicle/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_list_orders
tools.title: List orders
tools.description: List work orders for the shop, paged. Use orderBy: {createdDate: 'desc'} for newest first. Each order carries its number, status flags, totals in cents, workflow status and assigned technicians. For name/date filters use shopmonkey_search_orders; for one customer's orders use shopmonkey_list_customer_orders. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/order.

tools.name: shopmonkey_search_orders
tools.title: Search orders by name and creation date
tools.description: Find work orders by case-insensitive name substring, creation date, customer or status. Reads pages and checks filters locally because some shops ignore GET filters. Matches are sorted by createdDate, newest first, then paged with limit/matchSkip (default 100 results). complete: false means only a segment was scanned: newer matches may exist outside it; continue with nextScanSkip or increase maxOrders. scanSkip is a scan offset, not a matched-result offset. A changing order list can shift offsets; restart from 0 for a fresh search. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/order.

tools.name: shopmonkey_list_purchase_orders
tools.title: List purchase orders
tools.description: Read purchase orders with parts, tires, received quantities, inventory links and Draft/Ordered/Received/Fulfilled/Cancelled status. Paged; use orderBy for sorting. The public API documents reads and deletions, but no create/update/receive endpoints: change status, Receive All and inventory linking in the Shopmonkey UI. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/purchase_order.

tools.name: shopmonkey_get_purchase_order
tools.title: Get a purchase order
tools.description: Read one purchase order, including its status, vendor, parts/tires, ordered and received quantities, inventory links and associated work order. Purchase-order creation, status changes and receiving are not documented public API operations; use the Shopmonkey UI for those writes. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/purchase_order/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_get_order
tools.title: Get one order
tools.description: Fetch a single work order by id — customer, vehicle, complaint, totals (parts/labor/tax in cents), payment state and profitability. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/order/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_find_order_by_number
tools.title: Find an order by its number
tools.description: Find a work order by the number the shop sees (e.g. 1042 or #1042), also matching an overridden external number. Tries Shopmonkey's server-side filter first, then reads the order list page by page (newest first) and compares each number exactly, up to maxOrders orders. Returns the order (use its id with the other order tools) or found: false with how many orders were read. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/order.

tools.name: shopmonkey_list_order_services
tools.title: List an order's services
tools.description: List the services (jobs) on a work order with their line items — labor, parts, tires, fees, subcontracts — authorization status and totals. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/order/:orderId/service.

tools.name: shopmonkey_search_appointments
tools.title: Search appointments
tools.description: Search the appointment calendar by date range, customer, order or technician. Returns appointments with their customer. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/appointment/search.

tools.name: shopmonkey_search_inventory_parts
tools.title: Search inventory parts
tools.description: Search the parts inventory — name, part number, SKU, quantity on hand/available/reserved, retail and wholesale cost in cents, bin location, brand and vendor. Filter e.g. {"sku": "ABC-123"}. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/inventory_part/search.

tools.name: shopmonkey_list_canned_services
tools.title: List canned services
tools.description: List the shop's canned services (reusable job templates like 'Oil change') with their labor, parts and fees and total in cents. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/canned_service.

tools.name: shopmonkey_list_workflow_statuses
tools.title: List workflow statuses
tools.description: List the workflow statuses (the columns of the shop's work-order board) with their position. Use the id to move an order with shopmonkey_update_order. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/workflow_status.

tools.name: shopmonkey_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the shop's users (service writers, technicians, admins) — the ids to use for technicians and service writers. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/user.

tools.name: shopmonkey_create_customer
tools.title: Create a customer
tools.description: Create a customer (a person) or a fleet account. Add an email afterwards with shopmonkey_add_customer_email. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/customer.

tools.name: shopmonkey_update_customer
tools.title: Update a customer
tools.description: Update a customer's name, address, note or preferences. Only the fields you pass are sent. Shopmonkey: PUT /v3/customer/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_add_customer_email
tools.title: Add an email to a customer
tools.description: Add an email address to an existing customer, optionally as their primary address. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/customer/:id/email.

tools.name: shopmonkey_create_vehicle
tools.title: Create a vehicle
tools.description: Create a vehicle, optionally attached to a customer. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/vehicle.

tools.name: shopmonkey_create_order
tools.title: Create an order
tools.description: Open a new work order (it starts as an estimate) for a customer and vehicle. Add services and labor with shopmonkey_add_service. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/order.

tools.name: shopmonkey_update_order
tools.title: Update an order
tools.description: Update a work order — move it to another workflow status, change its status (Estimate, RepairOrder, Invoice), edit complaint/recommendation, due date, service writer, or archive it. Only the fields you pass are sent. Shopmonkey: PUT /v3/order/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_create_appointment
tools.title: Book an appointment
tools.description: Book an appointment on the shop calendar, optionally for a customer, vehicle and order and assigned to technicians. Confirmation/reminder messages are only sent if you ask. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/appointment.

tools.name: shopmonkey_update_appointment
tools.title: Update or reschedule an appointment
tools.description: Change an existing appointment — move it (new startDate/endDate), rename it, change its note, color, technicians, customer, vehicle or linked order, or set its confirmation status. Only the fields you pass are sent, so nothing is duplicated. Find the id with shopmonkey_search_appointments. Shopmonkey: PUT /v3/appointment/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_delete_appointment
tools.title: Delete (cancel) an appointment
tools.description: WRITE — removes an appointment from the shop calendar. To move it instead, use shopmonkey_update_appointment. Without confirm it only previews: it reads the appointment and deletes nothing. Show the preview to the user, then call again with confirm: true. After the delete the appointment is read again to verify it is gone. Shopmonkey: DELETE /v3/appointment/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_add_service
tools.title: Add a service (job) to an order
tools.description: Add a new service (job) to a work order, e.g. 'Road Call', optionally with labor lines (name, hours, hourly rate in cents). The service is created first, then each labor line is added to it. Find the order id with shopmonkey_find_order_by_number. To add labor to a service that exists, use shopmonkey_add_labor. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/order/:orderId/service, then POST /v3/order/:orderId/service/:serviceId/labor.

tools.name: shopmonkey_apply_canned_service
tools.title: Apply a canned service to an order
tools.description: Copy a saved canned service onto an existing work order in one vendor request, including its labor, parts and fees. Use shopmonkey_list_canned_services for cannedServiceId. Creates a new service each time; check shopmonkey_list_order_services before retrying an uncertain result. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/order/:orderId/service with fromCannedServiceId.

tools.name: shopmonkey_add_fee
tools.title: Add a flat fee to a service
tools.description: Add a fixed-cent fee/surcharge to an existing work order service, e.g. amountCents: 3000 for a $30 fuel or on-site fee. Uses the vendor's FixedCents fee type, not a labor line. Get serviceId with shopmonkey_list_order_services. Each call creates a fee; check the service before retrying an uncertain result. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/order/:orderId/service/:serviceId/fee.

tools.name: shopmonkey_send_message
tools.title: Send a customer SMS or email
tools.description: Send a free-form customer message by Email, SMS or All through Shopmonkey messaging. This sends the supplied text without sharing an estimate or changing order authorization. Contact ids must belong to customerId; omitted ids use the primary or only contact (or the selected order contact when orderId is given). Optional orderId must belong to this customer. Returns message delivery statuses; creation does not guarantee delivery. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/customer/:id, optionally GET /v3/order/:id, then POST /v3/message.

tools.name: shopmonkey_add_labor
tools.title: Add a labor line to a service
tools.description: Add a labor line (name, hours, hourly rate in cents, technician) to a service on a work order. Get the service id with shopmonkey_list_order_services; to start a new service, use shopmonkey_add_service. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/order/:orderId/service/:serviceId/labor.

tools.name: shopmonkey_send_estimate
tools.title: Send an estimate for customer authorization
tools.description: Share a work order's estimate through Shopmonkey messaging by Email, SMS or All. Reads the order and customer, enables customer authorization on the order, then creates an Order share message. This requests the customer's approval; it does not record approval. Supply the message text. Contact ids must belong to the order's customer; omitted ids use the order's selected contact, the primary contact, or the only contact. Returns Shopmonkey's message and delivery statuses (creation does not guarantee delivery). Invoiced or deleted orders cannot be sent. Shopmonkey: GET /v3/order/:id, GET /v3/customer/:id, PUT /v3/order/:id, POST /v3/message.

tools.name: shopmonkey_add_part
tools.title: Add a part to a work order service
tools.description: Add a part line to an existing service on a work order. Use shopmonkey_list_order_services for serviceId and shopmonkey_search_inventory_parts for inventoryPartId. Prices are per unit in cents; quantity may be fractional. Inventory reservation and reduction happen only if explicitly requested. Returns data.part with the new part id. This does not create or fulfill a vendor purchase order: those writes are not documented in Shopmonkey's public API. Shopmonkey: POST /v3/order/:orderId/service/:serviceId/part.

tools.name: shopmonkey_delete_service
tools.title: Remove a work order service and its lines
tools.description: Preview then remove one service and all its labor, parts, fees, tires and subcontract lines. Show the cascade preview before confirming with its fingerprint. Refuses authorized/invoiced/paid/archived/deleted/read-only orders, orders with payments or a non-Unlocked invoiceLockState, authorized services and inventory/PO-linked parts or tires. Verifies absence after deletion. DELETE /v3/order/:orderId/service/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_delete_labor
tools.title: Remove a labor line
tools.description: Preview then remove one labor line belonging to this work order service. Show the preview, then confirm with its fingerprint. Refuses authorized/invoiced/paid/archived/deleted/read-only orders, orders with payments or a non-Unlocked invoiceLockState, and authorized services. Verifies absence. DELETE /v3/order/:orderId/service/:serviceId/labor/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_delete_part
tools.title: Remove a part line
tools.description: Preview then remove one part line belonging to this work order service. Show the preview, then confirm with its fingerprint. Refuses authorized/invoiced/paid/archived/deleted/read-only orders, orders with payments or a non-Unlocked invoiceLockState, authorized services and inventory/PO-linked parts. Verifies absence. DELETE /v3/order/:orderId/service/:serviceId/part/:id.

tools.name: shopmonkey_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: shopmonkey_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Shopmonkey tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: shopmonkey_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Shopmonkey (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: shopmonkey_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Shopmonkey Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run shopmonkey_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: A shop admin creates it in Shopmonkey → **Settings → Integration → API Keys**. The key has the same permissions as the user who created it and is shown only once. It is used only to call the Shopmonkey API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: List the shop's work orders with their status and assigned technicians.
Which vehicles has Jane Smith brought in, and what was done?
What appointments are on the calendar for tomorrow?
Which brake pads do we have in stock and how many?

servers.name: Smile.io
servers.description: Look up loyalty customers, points history, rewards and VIP tiers, and add points or activities.

tools.name: smile_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List loyalty-program customers, newest first, with their points balance, state and VIP tier id. Look a customer up by exact email, or filter by state or last-updated time. Cursor-paginated (metadata.next_cursor). Smile: GET /customers.

tools.name: smile_get_customer
tools.title: Get a customer
tools.description: Fetch one customer by Smile customer ID: name, email, state, points_balance, referral_url, vip_tier_id, and optionally their VIP status with current and next tier. Smile: GET /customers/{id}.

tools.name: smile_list_points_transactions
tools.title: List points transactions
tools.description: List points transactions (every earn, spend and manual adjustment), newest first — e.g. a customer's full points history. Each has points_change (+/-), a customer-visible description and a merchant internal_note. Cursor-paginated. Smile: GET /points_transactions.

tools.name: smile_get_points_transaction
tools.title: Get a points transaction
tools.description: Fetch one points transaction by ID. Smile: GET /points_transactions/{id}.

tools.name: smile_list_points_products
tools.title: List points products (ways to redeem)
tools.description: List points products — the rewards customers can buy with points. 'fixed' products cost points_price; 'variable' products trade variable_points_step points for variable_points_step_reward_value, between variable_points_min and variable_points_max. Each embeds its reward. Page-numbered (page, page_size); a page shorter than page_size is the last. Smile: GET /points_products.

tools.name: smile_get_points_product
tools.title: Get a points product
tools.description: Fetch one points product (a way to redeem points) by ID, including its reward. Smile: GET /points_products/{id}.

tools.name: smile_list_reward_fulfillments
tools.title: List reward fulfillments
tools.description: List rewards that have been issued to customers — usually discount codes — with code, fulfillment_status (pending/issued/cancelled/failed), usage_status (used/unused/untracked), used_at and expires_at. Use customer_id to answer 'what codes does this customer have?'. Cursor-paginated. Smile: GET /reward_fulfillments.

tools.name: smile_list_earning_rules
tools.title: List earning rules (ways to earn)
tools.description: List the enabled earning rules — the ways customers earn points or rewards (placing an order, signing up, birthdays, custom activities), with reward, reward_value, earning_limit and any VIP-tier restriction. Cursor-paginated. Smile: GET /earning_rules.

tools.name: smile_list_vip_tiers
tools.title: List VIP tiers
tools.description: List the VIP program's tiers, sorted by milestone (the threshold to reach each tier), optionally with each tier's perks and entry rewards. Smile: GET /vip_tiers.

tools.name: smile_get_points_settings
tools.title: Get points settings
tools.description: Fetch the points program's configuration, e.g. the points currency label ("Points", "Stars"). Smile: GET /points_settings.

tools.name: smile_get_referral_settings
tools.title: Get referral settings
tools.description: Fetch the referral program's configuration: whether it is active, and the sender (advocate) and receiver (friend) rewards. Smile: GET /referral_settings.

tools.name: smile_create_points_transaction
tools.title: Adjust a customer's points balance
tools.description: WRITE: add or deduct points from a customer's balance (a manual adjustment, e.g. a goodwill credit or a correction). points_change > 0 adds, < 0 deducts; Smile rejects a deduction that would make the balance negative. Undo by creating an opposite adjustment. `description` is shown to the customer; `internal_note` is merchant-only. To reward a customer for completing an action, prefer smile_create_activity. Requires the points_transaction:write scope. Smile: POST /points_transactions.

tools.name: smile_create_activity
tools.title: Record a customer activity
tools.description: WRITE: record that a customer performed an action (identified by an activity type token configured in Smile Admin, e.g. a custom 'newsletter signup' activity). Smile then asynchronously applies the store's earning rules and may issue points or rewards. Identify the customer by customer_id OR customer_email (exactly one). Pass distinct_id (e.g. an order number) to make it idempotent — a second activity with the same token + distinct_id is rejected. Custom activity types need Smile's Plus/Enterprise plan. Requires the activity:write scope. Smile: POST /activities.

tools.name: smile_purchase_points_product
tools.title: Redeem a customer's points for a reward
tools.description: WRITE — SPENDS THE CUSTOMER'S POINTS: redeem points on the customer's behalf by purchasing a points product; Smile deducts the points and issues the reward (the response's points_purchase.reward_fulfillment usually holds a discount code). Only do this when the customer asked for it. For a 'variable' product pass points_to_spend; leave it out for 'fixed' products. There is no API to cancel a redemption — a mistaken one can only be compensated with smile_create_points_transaction. Requires the points_purchase:write scope. Smile: POST /points_products/{id}/purchase.

tools.name: smile_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smile_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Smile.io tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smile_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Smile.io (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smile_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Smile.io Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run smile_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create one in Smile Admin → **Settings → Developer tools → API keys**. Merchant API keys require Smile's **Plus or Enterprise** plan. Grant the read scopes you want (customer read is required), plus `points_transaction:write`, `activity:write` and `points_purchase:write` if you want the write tools. Your key is used only to call the Smile.io API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Show the 10 most recently joined loyalty members and their points balances.
What rewards can customers redeem with their points?
Show the points history for the customer with email jane.smith@example.com.
Add 100 bonus points to jane.smith@example.com as a thank-you.

servers.name: Smoobu
servers.description: Check vacation-rental reservations, rates, availability and guest messages, and update bookings.

tools.name: smoobu_get_user
tools.title: Get the current user
tools.description: Fetch the Smoobu user these credentials belong to (id, name, email). A cheap way to confirm the setup works; the id is the customerId used by availability checks. Smoobu: GET /api/me.

tools.name: smoobu_list_apartments
tools.title: List properties
tools.description: List every property (Smoobu calls them apartments) in the account, with id and name. Start here to get apartment ids. Smoobu: GET /api/apartments.

tools.name: smoobu_get_apartment
tools.title: Get one property
tools.description: Fetch one property's details: location, time zone, rooms and beds, max occupancy, amenities, currency, min/max nightly price and type. Smoobu: GET /api/apartments/{apartmentId}.

tools.name: smoobu_list_reservations
tools.title: List reservations
tools.description: List reservations across all channels (Airbnb, Booking.com, direct, ...), paginated, with guest, dates, channel, price and payment status. Filter by stay range, arrival, departure, creation or modification date, and property. Smoobu: GET /api/reservations.

tools.name: smoobu_get_reservation
tools.title: Get one reservation
tools.description: Fetch one reservation by id: guest, dates, check-in/out times, channel and its reference id, price, prepayment and deposit status, and the guest-app URL. Smoobu: GET /api/reservations/{reservationId}.

tools.name: smoobu_list_price_elements
tools.title: List a reservation's price elements
tools.description: List the financial breakdown of one reservation: base price, cleaning fee, add-ons, long-stay discounts and coupons, with amounts, tax and currency. Smoobu: GET /api/reservations/{reservationId}/price-elements.

tools.name: smoobu_get_reservation_placeholders
tools.title: Get a reservation's message placeholders
tools.description: Get every placeholder value Smoobu would substitute into a message for this reservation: guest name, dates and times, nights, price and balance, online check-in link, guest-app link, door PIN codes and more. Useful for drafting a guest message. Smoobu: GET /api/reservations/{reservationId}/placeholders.

tools.name: smoobu_get_rates
tools.title: Get rates and availability
tools.description: Get the nightly price, minimum length of stay and availability (0 = not available) for each date in a range, for one or more properties. Smoobu: GET /api/rates.

tools.name: smoobu_check_availability
tools.title: Check availability and quote a stay
tools.description: Check which properties can be booked for an arrival/departure pair and get the total price for each; unavailable ones come back with the reason (minimum stay, too many guests, arrival day, lead time...). Read-only, books nothing. Smoobu: POST /booking/checkApartmentAvailability.

tools.name: smoobu_list_message_threads
tools.title: List inbox threads
tools.description: List the unified guest inbox: one thread per booking with guest name, property and the latest message, plus the unread count. Smoobu: GET /api/threads.

tools.name: smoobu_list_reservation_messages
tools.title: List a reservation's messages
tools.description: Get the full conversation for one reservation, paginated. Each message has a subject, plain-text and HTML body, and type (1 = inbox / from guest, 2 = outbox / sent). Smoobu: GET /api/reservations/{reservationId}/messages.

tools.name: smoobu_list_guests
tools.title: List guests
tools.description: List guests from the Smoobu CRM with their emails, phone numbers, address, notes and bookings; optionally search. Smoobu: GET /api/guests.

tools.name: smoobu_get_guest
tools.title: Get one guest
tools.description: Fetch one guest by id (the guestId on a reservation) with contact details, notes and every booking they have made. Smoobu: GET /api/guests/{guestId}.

tools.name: smoobu_list_addons
tools.title: List add-ons
tools.description: List the bookable add-ons (towels, breakfast, late check-out...) with amount, tax, calculation type (0 per booking, 1 per person, 2 per night, 3 per person and night) and the properties they apply to; optionally for one property. Smoobu: GET /api/addons[/{apartmentId}].

tools.name: smoobu_list_custom_placeholders
tools.title: List custom placeholders
tools.description: List the account's custom message placeholders (key, default value, and whether they are global, per booking or per property). Smoobu: GET /api/custom-placeholders.

tools.name: smoobu_create_reservation
tools.title: Create a reservation
tools.description: Create a reservation (or a blocked period) on a property. Smoobu treats it like a booking from a channel and SYNCS the blocked dates to every connected channel (Airbnb, Booking.com, ...). Fails if the dates overlap an existing booking. This server offers no cancel — cancel it in Smoobu if needed. Which guest fields are mandatory depends on your booking-tool 'Form Content' settings. Smoobu: POST /api/reservations.

tools.name: smoobu_update_reservation
tools.title: Update a reservation
tools.description: Update an existing reservation's times, guest contact, notes, guest counts, language, or price / prepayment / deposit amounts and paid status. Only the fields you pass are sent. Dates and property cannot be changed here. Smoobu: PUT /api/reservations/{reservationId}.

tools.name: smoobu_set_rates
tools.title: Set rates and minimum stays
tools.description: Set the nightly price and/or minimum length of stay for dates on one or more properties. Smoobu PUSHES these to every channel with price sync enabled, so this changes live prices guests see. Reversible by setting the old values again — read them first with smoobu_get_rates. Each operation needs daily_price, min_length_of_stay, or both (a minimum stay alone needs an existing price). Smoobu: POST /api/rates.

tools.name: smoobu_send_message_to_guest
tools.title: Send a message to a guest
tools.description: Send a message to the guest of a reservation through Smoobu (it goes out on the booking's channel, e.g. the Airbnb or Booking.com inbox, or email). Delivered IMMEDIATELY and cannot be unsent — confirm the text with the user first. Smoobu: POST /api/reservations/{reservationId}/messages/send-message-to-guest.

tools.name: smoobu_send_message_to_host
tools.title: Post a message to the host
tools.description: Post a message on a reservation's thread addressed to the Smoobu user (the host). With internal=true it is an internal note hidden from the guest — handy for logging. Cannot be unsent. Smoobu: POST /api/reservations/{reservationId}/messages/send-message-to-host.

tools.name: smoobu_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smoobu_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Smoobu tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smoobu_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Smoobu (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smoobu_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Smoobu Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run smoobu_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create both in Smoobu → **Settings → Advanced → API Keys**. The secret is shown only once, when the key is created. Both are required: every request is HMAC-signed, and Smoobu switches off the old key-only access on 2026-10-31. Your credentials are used only to call the Smoobu API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

examples: Which guests arrive over the next 7 days, and at which properties?
Which of my properties are free from August 3 to August 8, and at what price?
Show me the latest guest messages across my bookings.
Show the check-in time on Jane Smith's booking for Friday.

servers.name: Sortly
servers.description: Search inventory items and folders, low-stock alerts, jobs and purchase orders, and update stock.

tools.name: sortly_list_items
tools.title: List items and folders
tools.description: List items and folders, newest first. By default the root level; pass folder_id for a folder's direct contents, plus include_subfolders for everything nested under it. Paginated via meta.next_page_url / total_pages. Sortly: GET /api/v1/items.

tools.name: sortly_get_item
tools.title: Get one item or folder
tools.description: Fetch a single item or folder by numeric id: quantity, min_quantity, price, tags, sid, barcodes, and optionally custom field values and photos. Sortly: GET /api/v1/items/{item_id}.

tools.name: sortly_search_items
tools.title: Search inventory
tools.description: Search items and folders by name, optionally limited to items or folders and scoped to specific folders. Read-only despite being a POST. Paginated: send the same arguments with the next page number. Sortly: POST /api/v1/items/search.

tools.name: sortly_list_recently_updated_items
tools.title: List recently updated items
tools.description: List items and folders changed since a Unix timestamp — the incremental-sync read ('what moved since yesterday?'). Without updated_since it behaves like sortly_list_items. Sortly: GET /api/v1/items/recent.

tools.name: sortly_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List custom fields
tools.description: List the account's custom fields (id, name, type, applies_to). Call this before writing custom_attribute_values to get the right custom_attribute_id. Sortly: GET /api/v1/custom_fields.

tools.name: sortly_list_units
tools.title: List units of measure
tools.description: List the units of measure available to the account (unit_name, unit_type, scale) — the values measured_quantity and purchase-order lines expect. Sortly: GET /api/v1/units.

tools.name: sortly_list_alerts
tools.title: List alerts
tools.description: List stock (Quantity) and date (DateReminder) alerts, with is_fired showing which have already triggered — the quick way to find low-stock items. Sortly: GET /api/v1/alerts.

tools.name: sortly_list_jobs
tools.title: List jobs
tools.description: List jobs (work orders that pull stock out), most recently updated first, filterable by name prefix and status. Paginated via meta.pagination.has_next. Sortly: GET /api/v1/jobs.

tools.name: sortly_get_job
tools.title: Get one job
tools.description: Fetch a single job: status, folder_id (where its pulled items sit), dates, notes, custom field values and the version needed for updates. Sortly: GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}.

tools.name: sortly_list_purchase_orders
tools.title: List purchase orders
tools.description: List purchase orders, most recently updated first, filterable by PO number and status. The list leaves out notes, terms, sub_total and line_items — use sortly_get_purchase_order for those. Needs Purchase Orders on the plan (else 402). Sortly: GET /api/v1/purchase_orders.

tools.name: sortly_get_purchase_order
tools.title: Get one purchase order
tools.description: Fetch a single purchase order with its line_items (quantity vs received_quantity), vendor, addresses, charges, totals and version. Sortly: GET /api/v1/purchase_orders/{purchase_order_id}.

tools.name: sortly_get_purchase_order_receive_status
tools.title: Get a purchase order's receive status
tools.description: Report the most recent receive against a purchase order: pending / completed / failed, with the line ids received, pending and failed (and why). Returns 404 until something has been received. Sortly: GET /api/v1/purchase_orders/{purchase_order_id}/receive/status.

tools.name: sortly_create_item
tools.title: Create an item or folder
tools.description: Create a trackable item (type item) or a folder (type folder), optionally inside a folder via parent_id, with quantity, price, tags, custom fields, barcodes and a measured quantity. WRITE. Sortly: POST /api/v1/items.

tools.name: sortly_update_item
tools.title: Update an item or folder
tools.description: Change fields on an existing item or folder — e.g. set a new quantity after a stock count, rename it, or relocate a folder via parent_id. Only the fields you pass change; pass null to clear a nullable field. Sending tags or custom_attribute_values replaces them. WRITE. Sortly: PUT /api/v1/items/{item_id} (returns 204).

tools.name: sortly_move_item
tools.title: Move stock to another folder
tools.description: Move some or all of an item's quantity to another folder (items only — relocate a folder with sortly_update_item parent_id). A partial move splits off a new item with the same sid; a full move relocates the item; a matching item at the destination is merged, and the returned id is the destination's. Undo by moving it back. WRITE. Sortly: POST /api/v1/items/{item_id}/move.

tools.name: sortly_create_alert
tools.title: Create an alert
tools.description: Create a stock alert on an item (type Quantity, e.g. threshold_method quantity_less_than with threshold_value 5, or less_than_or_equal_to_min_quantity), or a DateReminder on a datetime custom field (custom_attribute_id + before/after/same_day + threshold_interval). WRITE. Sortly: POST /api/v1/alerts.

tools.name: sortly_create_job
tools.title: Create a job
tools.description: Create a job (and its job folder) in not_started status. Name must be unique in the company. Then use sortly_pull_items_into_job to record the stock it uses. WRITE. Sortly: POST /api/v1/jobs.

tools.name: sortly_pull_items_into_job
tools.title: Pull items into a job
tools.description: Move quantities of existing items (from any folders) into a job's folder — how usage on a job is recorded. Up to 100 items per call; items are processed independently, so ALWAYS check data.errors (a partial failure still returns 200). Undo with sortly_return_items_from_job. Returns 403 on a completed job. WRITE. Sortly: POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/items.

tools.name: sortly_return_items_from_job
tools.title: Return items from a job
tools.description: Move items off a job's folder back into inventory (destination_folder_id, or All Items if omitted). Up to 100 per call; check data.errors — items are processed one by one. WRITE. Sortly: POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/items/return.

tools.name: sortly_create_purchase_order
tools.title: Draft a purchase order
tools.description: Create a purchase order in draft status (no stock or ordering happens until it is moved on in Sortly). Sortly computes amounts, sub_total and total from the lines; omit purchase_order_number to have one generated. Needs Purchase Orders on the plan (else 402). WRITE. Sortly: POST /api/v1/purchase_orders.

tools.name: sortly_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sortly_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Sortly tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sortly_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Sortly (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sortly_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Sortly Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run sortly_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Generate one in Sortly at [app.sortly.com/public-api](https://app.sortly.com/public-api) (Settings → Public API; Enterprise plan only). Your key is used only to call the Sortly API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Which items in my inventory are running low on stock right now?
Show me everything in the Warehouse folder with its current quantity.
List my open purchase orders and which ones are still waiting to be received.
Set the quantity of Blue Widgets to 120 after today's stock count.

servers.name: StatusCake
servers.description: Review uptime, SSL, pagespeed and heartbeat checks, alerts and maintenance windows; create checks.

tools.name: statuscake_list_uptime_checks
tools.title: List uptime checks
tools.description: List uptime checks with their current status (up/down), type, URL, check rate, tags and uptime percentage. Filter by status or tags. StatusCake: GET /uptime.

tools.name: statuscake_get_uptime_check
tools.title: Get one uptime check
tools.description: Fetch one uptime check in full — settings, current status, last test time, next location and the monitoring servers it runs on. StatusCake: GET /uptime/{test_id}.

tools.name: statuscake_get_uptime_history
tools.title: Get uptime check history
tools.description: Individual test runs for one uptime check — when, from which location, the status code and the response time (ms). Newest first; follow links.next (or pass before) to page back. StatusCake: GET /uptime/{test_id}/history.

tools.name: statuscake_get_uptime_periods
tools.title: Get uptime check up/down periods
tools.description: The up and down periods of one uptime check — when each started and ended and how long it lasted (ms). The direct answer to 'how long was it down?'. StatusCake: GET /uptime/{test_id}/periods.

tools.name: statuscake_list_uptime_alerts
tools.title: List uptime check alerts
tools.description: Alerts triggered by one uptime check — when, the status it changed to and the status code. StatusCake: GET /uptime/{test_id}/alerts.

tools.name: statuscake_list_ssl_checks
tools.title: List SSL checks
tools.description: List SSL certificate checks with the certificate's validity window (valid_from/valid_until), issuer, cipher and score, and flags such as expired, broken, revoked or mixed content. StatusCake: GET /ssl.

tools.name: statuscake_get_ssl_check
tools.title: Get one SSL check
tools.description: Fetch one SSL certificate check in full — expiry, issuer, cipher, scores, flags and any mixed-content resources found. StatusCake: GET /ssl/{test_id}.

tools.name: statuscake_list_pagespeed_checks
tools.title: List pagespeed checks
tools.description: List pagespeed checks with their location, alert thresholds and latest stats (load time ms, page size kb, request count, latest issue). StatusCake: GET /pagespeed.

tools.name: statuscake_get_pagespeed_history
tools.title: Get pagespeed check history
tools.description: Past runs of one pagespeed check — load time (ms), file size (kb), request count, throttling and the saved HAR file location. StatusCake: GET /pagespeed/{test_id}/history.

tools.name: statuscake_list_heartbeat_checks
tools.title: List heartbeat checks
tools.description: List heartbeat (push) checks — jobs that must ping a StatusCake URL within a period — with their status, period and ping URL. StatusCake: GET /heartbeat.

tools.name: statuscake_get_heartbeat_check
tools.title: Get one heartbeat check
tools.description: Fetch one heartbeat check in full, including its ping URL, period, status and when it last received a ping. StatusCake: GET /heartbeat/{test_id}.

tools.name: statuscake_list_contact_groups
tools.title: List contact groups
tools.description: List contact groups — who gets alerted: email addresses, mobile numbers, integration ids and ping URL. Use their ids in a check's contact_groups. StatusCake: GET /contact-groups.

tools.name: statuscake_list_maintenance_windows
tools.title: List maintenance windows
tools.description: List maintenance windows (scheduled alert silences) with their start/end, timezone, repeat interval, state and the checks or tags they cover. Only works on accounts using the newer maintenance-windows feature. StatusCake: GET /maintenance-windows.

tools.name: statuscake_get_maintenance_window
tools.title: Get one maintenance window
tools.description: Fetch one maintenance window by id. StatusCake: GET /maintenance-windows/{window_id}.

tools.name: statuscake_list_uptime_locations
tools.title: List uptime monitoring locations
tools.description: List StatusCake's uptime monitoring servers — region, region code, IPv4/IPv6 and status. Use region codes in a check's regions; use the IPs for firewall allowlists. StatusCake: GET /uptime-locations.

tools.name: statuscake_list_pagespeed_locations
tools.title: List pagespeed monitoring locations
tools.description: List StatusCake's pagespeed monitoring servers — region, IPs and status. StatusCake: GET /pagespeed-locations.

tools.name: statuscake_create_uptime_check
tools.title: Create an uptime check
tools.description: Start monitoring a URL, host or IP. Returns the new check's id as data.new_id. Faster check rates and some regions depend on the plan. StatusCake: POST /uptime.

tools.name: statuscake_update_uptime_check
tools.title: Update an uptime check
tools.description: Change an uptime check's settings. Only the fields you pass are changed; list fields (tags, contact_groups, regions, dns_ips) are REPLACED, and an empty list clears them. Pass paused=true to pause a check and paused=false to resume it. StatusCake: PUT /uptime/{test_id}.

tools.name: statuscake_create_ssl_check
tools.title: Create an SSL check
tools.description: Start monitoring a site's SSL certificate for expiry and problems. Returns the new id as data.new_id. StatusCake: POST /ssl.

tools.name: statuscake_create_heartbeat_check
tools.title: Create a heartbeat check
tools.description: Create a heartbeat (push) check for a cron job or worker: it goes down if StatusCake is not pinged within `period` seconds. Returns the new id as data.new_id; fetch it with statuscake_get_heartbeat_check to get the ping URL. StatusCake: POST /heartbeat.

tools.name: statuscake_create_maintenance_window
tools.title: Create a maintenance window
tools.description: Schedule a maintenance window that silences alerts for the given uptime checks (by id and/or tag). start_at/end_at are RFC3339; only the date and time are used and are read as local time in `timezone`. At least one of tests or tags is required. Only works on accounts using the newer maintenance-windows feature. StatusCake: POST /maintenance-windows.

tools.name: statuscake_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: statuscake_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the StatusCake tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: statuscake_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on StatusCake (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: statuscake_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's StatusCake Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run statuscake_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create or copy one in the StatusCake app under **Account → API Keys**. Your key is used only to call the StatusCake API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Are any of my website uptime checks down right now?
Which SSL certificates on my sites expire in the next 30 days?
How did my main website's uptime look over the last week?
Create an uptime check for https://acme-example.com that tests every 5 minutes.

servers.name: Tito
servers.description: Look up events, releases, tickets, registrations and discount codes, and edit tickets and codes.

tools.name: tito_whoami
tools.title: Check the API token
tools.description: Confirm the API token works and list the account slugs it can reach, plus its lookup mode (live or test — a token only sees tickets and registrations of its own mode). Call this first to discover account_slug. Tito: GET /hello.

tools.name: tito_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List an account's events: upcoming (default), past or archived. Each has its slug, title, dates, location, currency, live/test_mode flags and public URL. Tito: GET /:account/events, /events/past, /events/archived.

tools.name: tito_get_event
tools.title: Get one event
tools.description: Fetch a single event by slug: title, description, dates and times, time zone, location, currency, live/test_mode, and its releases. Tito: GET /:account/:event.

tools.name: tito_list_releases
tools.title: List releases (ticket types)
tools.description: List an event's releases — Tito's ticket types — with price, quantity, tickets_count sold, sold_out / off_sale / secret flags, sale window and share_url. Tito: GET /:account/:event/releases.

tools.name: tito_get_release
tools.title: Get one release
tools.description: Fetch a single release (ticket type) by slug, with pricing, capacity, sales counts (full-price, discounted, free, voided), questions and activities. Tito: GET /:account/:event/releases/:release_slug.

tools.name: tito_list_tickets
tools.title: List tickets (attendees)
tools.description: List an event's tickets — one per attendee — newest first, with name, email, company, reference, release, price paid and state. Filter by free text (name, email, phone, reference, company, tag), state, type, release, activity, and created/updated time. Void tickets are excluded unless states includes 'void'. Tito: GET /:account/:event/tickets.

tools.name: tito_get_ticket
tools.title: Get one ticket
tools.description: Fetch a single ticket by slug (ti_...), with the attendee, registration, release, question answers, tags and amounts paid. Tito: GET /:account/:event/tickets/:ticket_slug.

tools.name: tito_list_registrations
tools.title: List registrations (orders)
tools.description: List an event's registrations — Tito's orders — newest first, with buyer name/email, reference, total, state, paid/refunded flags, discount code and ticket quantities. Filter by free text (email, name, slug, reference, company, discount code), state, and created/updated time. Cancelled ones are excluded unless states includes 'cancelled'. Tito: GET /:account/:event/registrations.

tools.name: tito_get_registration
tools.title: Get one registration
tools.description: Fetch a single registration (order) by slug (reg_...), with its tickets, receipts, refunds, line items, billing address and payment details. Tito: GET /:account/:event/registrations/:registration_slug.

tools.name: tito_list_discount_codes
tools.title: List discount codes
tools.description: List an event's discount codes with code, type (PercentOffDiscountCode / MoneyOffDiscountCode), value, quantity and quantity_used, validity window and attached releases. Tito: GET /:account/:event/discount_codes.

tools.name: tito_get_discount_code
tools.title: Get one discount code
tools.description: Fetch a single discount code by its numeric id, including how many times it has been used. Tito: GET /:account/:event/discount_codes/:discount_code_id.

tools.name: tito_list_activities
tools.title: List activities
tools.description: List an event's activities — sessions, workshops or dinners beyond the ticket itself — with capacity, allocation_count, sold_out, date/times and attached releases. Tito: GET /:account/:event/activities.

tools.name: tito_list_questions
tools.title: List questions
tools.description: List the custom questions an event asks attendees (e.g. dietary requirements, t-shirt size) with slug, field_type, required flag and answers_count. Use a question's slug with tito_list_answers. Tito: GET /:account/:event/questions.

tools.name: tito_list_answers
tools.title: List answers to a question
tools.description: List every attendee's answer to one question, each with its ticket_id and the response text. Tito: GET /:account/:event/questions/:question_slug/answers.

tools.name: tito_list_checkin_lists
tools.title: List check-in lists
tools.description: List an event's check-in lists (the door lists used at the venue) with title, slug, the releases/activities they cover and which attendee fields they show. Tito: GET /:account/:event/checkin_lists.

tools.name: tito_list_refunds
tools.title: List refunds
tools.description: List the refunds recorded for an event, each with amount, created_at, whether it was manual, and the registration it belongs to. Read-only: this server never issues refunds. Tito: GET /:account/:event/refunds.

tools.name: tito_create_discount_code
tools.title: Create a discount code
tools.description: Create a discount code for an event. type is PercentOffDiscountCode (value = percent) or MoneyOffDiscountCode (value = flat amount off per ticket, in the event currency). Undo by editing it (e.g. quantity or end_at) with tito_update_discount_code. Tito: POST /:account/:event/discount_codes.

tools.name: tito_update_discount_code
tools.title: Update a discount code
tools.description: Change an existing discount code — its code, value, quantity, validity window or attached releases. Only the fields you pass are sent. To retire a code without deleting it, set end_at to now. Tito: PATCH /:account/:event/discount_codes/:discount_code_id.

tools.name: tito_create_ticket
tools.title: Issue a ticket manually
tools.description: Issue a ticket for a release without a checkout — e.g. a speaker, sponsor or comp ticket. Tito creates a manual registration for it. This creates a real ticket that counts against the release's capacity (undo only by voiding it in the Tito dashboard). Tito: POST /:account/:event/tickets.

tools.name: tito_update_ticket
tools.title: Update a ticket's attendee details
tools.description: Correct a ticket's attendee details — name, email, company, phone, tags or metadata. Only the fields you pass are sent, and no email is sent to anyone (unlike a reassignment, which this server does not do). Tito: PATCH /:account/:event/tickets/:ticket_slug.

tools.name: tito_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: tito_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Tito tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: tito_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Tito (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: tito_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Tito Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run tito_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create a token at [id.tito.io](https://id.tito.io) → **API access → Generate New Token** and copy the **secret** token. A token is either **live** or **test** mode and only sees tickets and registrations of that mode. The account slug is the first part of your event URL `ti.to/<account>/<event>`; set it so tools can omit `account_slug`. Your token is used only to call the Tito API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: How many tickets have we sold so far for our next upcoming event?
List the ticket types for my next event with how many of each are sold.
Which discount codes have been used the most for my upcoming event?
Show the latest 10 registrations for my next event with buyer names and emails.

servers.name: Trengo
servers.description: Work tickets and messages, look up contacts and teams, pull reports, and reply, assign or close.

tools.name: trengo_list_tickets
tools.title: List tickets
tools.description: List tickets (conversations) visible to the token's user, newest activity first, with channel and latest message. Filter by status, contact, assignee, channel, label, last message direction or update time. Trengo: GET /tickets.

tools.name: trengo_list_ticket_messages
tools.title: List a ticket's messages
tools.description: List the messages of one ticket — inbound, outbound and internal notes — with the contact or agent behind each. Trengo: GET /tickets/{ticket_id}/messages.

tools.name: trengo_get_email_message
tools.title: Get an email message
tools.description: Fetch the full email behind one message of a ticket: original HTML body, from, to, subject and Message-ID. The message must be an email message. Trengo: GET /tickets/{ticket_id}/full_email_messages/{message_id}.

tools.name: trengo_list_contacts
tools.title: List or search contacts
tools.description: List contacts, or search them by name, email or phone number. Trengo: GET /contacts.

tools.name: trengo_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: Fetch one contact with name, email, phone and custom field data, optionally with notes. Trengo: GET /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: trengo_list_contact_groups
tools.title: List contact groups
tools.description: List the contact groups in the account — use their ids with trengo_update_contact. Trengo: GET /contact_groups.

tools.name: trengo_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the agents (users) in the Trengo account — use their ids to assign tickets or filter. Trengo: GET /users.

tools.name: trengo_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: List the teams in the account — use their ids to assign tickets to a team. Trengo: GET /teams.

tools.name: trengo_list_labels
tools.title: List labels
tools.description: List the ticket labels (tags) in the account, for filtering tickets and reports. Trengo: GET /labels.

tools.name: trengo_list_ticket_results
tools.title: List ticket results
tools.description: List the ticket results (closing outcomes, e.g. 'Resolved', 'Sale') that can be applied when closing a ticket. Trengo: GET /ticket_results.

tools.name: trengo_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List custom fields
tools.description: List the custom fields defined for tickets, contacts and profiles. Trengo: GET /custom_fields.

tools.name: trengo_list_quick_replies
tools.title: List quick replies
tools.description: List the saved quick replies (canned responses), optionally only the messaging or email ones — useful for drafting consistent answers. Trengo: GET /quick_replies.

tools.name: trengo_get_reporting_metrics
tools.title: Get reporting metrics
tools.description: Aggregate support metrics over a period: new, created, assigned, closed and reopened tickets, average first response time and average total resolution time (seconds). Filter by team, channel, label or direction. Trengo: GET /reporting/metrics.

tools.name: trengo_get_agent_performance
tools.title: Get agent performance
tools.description: Per-agent performance over a period: messages sent, notes, tickets assigned and closed, average first response and resolution times (with and without business hours). Trengo: GET /reporting/agent_performance.

tools.name: trengo_get_ticket_details_report
tools.title: Get ticket details report
tools.description: Per-ticket reporting rows: status, assignee, labels, first reply, first resolution and total resolution times (with and without business hours). Filter by team, channel, label, direction, status and created/closed/assigned date ranges; sort by a timing metric. For large accounts page with start_after_ticket_id instead of page. Trengo: GET /reporting/details/ticket.

tools.name: trengo_create_ticket
tools.title: Create a ticket
tools.description: Open a new ticket for an existing contact on a channel. Nothing is sent to the customer until you post a message with trengo_send_ticket_message. Trengo: POST /tickets.

tools.name: trengo_assign_ticket
tools.title: Assign a ticket
tools.description: Assign a ticket to a user or a team, with an optional assignment note. Reversible by reassigning. Trengo: POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/assign.

tools.name: trengo_close_ticket
tools.title: Close a ticket
tools.description: Close a ticket, optionally applying a ticket result (see trengo_list_ticket_results). Reversible with trengo_reopen_ticket. Trengo: POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/close.

tools.name: trengo_reopen_ticket
tools.title: Reopen a ticket
tools.description: Reopen a closed ticket. Trengo: POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/reopen.

tools.name: trengo_send_ticket_message
tools.title: Send a ticket message
tools.description: Post a message on a ticket. With internal_note=true it is an internal note visible only to agents. OTHERWISE IT IS DELIVERED TO THE CUSTOMER on the ticket's channel (email, WhatsApp, chat...) and cannot be recalled — confirm the text first. Trengo: POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/messages.

tools.name: trengo_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: Create a contact on a channel. The identifier is the contact's address on that channel: an email address for email channels, a phone number for WhatsApp/SMS/voice. Trengo: POST /channels/{channel_id}/contacts.

tools.name: trengo_update_contact
tools.title: Update a contact
tools.description: Rename a contact and/or set the contact groups it belongs to. contact_group_ids REPLACES the contact's groups. Trengo: PUT /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: trengo_create_board_card
tools.title: Create a board card
tools.description: Create a card (e.g. a deal or task) in a stage of a Trengo board. The board id is in the board's URL in Trengo. Trengo: POST /boards/{boardId}/cards.

tools.name: trengo_update_board_card
tools.title: Update a board card
tools.description: Partially update a board card: rename it, move it to another stage, or set its users (owners) and contacts (leads). user_ids / contact_ids replace the current sets. Trengo: PUT /boards/{boardId}/cards/{cardId}.

tools.name: trengo_upgrade

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Trengo (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: trengo_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Trengo Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run trengo_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create one in Trengo → **Settings → Apps & integrations → Rest API** → new personal access token. It acts with your own Trengo permissions, channels and teams. Your token is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.
