Show me my newest open tickets and who they are from.
Which agent closed the most tickets this month?
Close the ticket from Jane Smith about her late delivery.

servers.name: Unleashed Software
servers.description: Check products, stock on hand, customers, orders, invoices and quotes, and create records.

tools.name: unleashed_get_company
tools.title: Get the company
tools.description: Fetch the Unleashed company these credentials belong to — name, base currency and default tax rate. A cheap way to confirm the API id, key and signature are right. Unleashed: GET /Companies.

tools.name: unleashed_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products, optionally searched by code/description or filtered by code prefix, group, brand, barcode or modification date. Unleashed: GET /Products/{page}.

tools.name: unleashed_get_product
tools.title: Get one product
tools.description: Fetch a single product by Guid — prices, units, stock alert levels, group, brand, supplier. Unleashed: GET /Products/{productGuid}.

tools.name: unleashed_list_stock_on_hand
tools.title: List stock on hand
tools.description: List stock on hand per product — QtyOnHand, AllocatedQty, AvailableQty, OnPurchase, AvgCost — optionally for one warehouse or as at a past date. Unleashed: GET /StockOnHand/{page}.

tools.name: unleashed_get_product_stock
tools.title: Get a product's stock
tools.description: Stock on hand for one product — totals, or broken down per warehouse with allWarehouses=true. The direct answer to 'how many do we have and where?'. Unleashed: GET /StockOnHand/{productGuid}[/AllWarehouses].

tools.name: unleashed_list_customers

tools.name: unleashed_list_suppliers

tools.name: unleashed_list_warehouses
tools.title: List warehouses
tools.description: List warehouses (code, name, default flag, address). Warehouse codes are what other tools filter by. Unleashed: GET /Warehouses/{page}.

tools.name: unleashed_list_product_groups
tools.title: List product groups
tools.description: List product groups (name, Guid, parent group) — the category tree products are filed under. Unleashed: GET /ProductGroups/{page}.

tools.name: unleashed_list_sales_orders

tools.description: List sales orders, filtered by status, customer, order number, warehouse or date range. Deleted orders are excluded unless asked for. Unleashed: GET /SalesOrders/{page}.

tools.name: unleashed_get_sales_order

tools.name: unleashed_list_purchase_orders

tools.name: unleashed_get_purchase_order

tools.description: Fetch a single purchase order by Guid, with its lines, supplier and totals. Unleashed: GET /PurchaseOrders/{orderGuid}.

tools.name: unleashed_list_invoices

tools.description: List sales invoices, filtered by status, customer, invoice number, sales order number or date range. Unleashed: GET /Invoices/{page}.

tools.name: unleashed_list_sales_quotes

tools.description: List sales quotes, filtered by status, customer, quote number or date range. Unleashed: GET /SalesQuotes/{page}.

tools.name: unleashed_list_stock_adjustments
tools.title: List stock adjustments
tools.description: List stock adjustments (write-offs, recounts, corrections) with reason, status and lines, filtered by warehouse, product or date. Unleashed: GET /StockAdjustments/{page}.

tools.name: unleashed_create_product

tools.description: Create a DRAFT sales order with status Parked (reserves no stock, posts nothing to accounting — a person places or completes it in Unleashed). servers.name: UpCloud
servers.description: Inspect servers, storage, networks, databases and billing, and start, stop or back up servers.

tools.name: upcloud_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The calling account: username, remaining credits and resource limits (cores, memory, storage per tier, IPs, networks, managed services). A cheap way to confirm the token works. UpCloud: GET /1.3/account.

tools.name: upcloud_list_zones
tools.title: List zones
tools.description: Available zones (data centres) with id (e.g. fi-hel1, de-fra1, us-chi1), description and whether they are public or private-cloud. Zone ids are used by every other resource. UpCloud: GET /1.3/zone.

tools.name: upcloud_list_plans
tools.title: List server plans
tools.description: Fixed-price server plans: name (e.g. 2xCPU-4GB), cores, memory, included storage size/tier and transfer, plus GPU model/amount for GPU plans. UpCloud: GET /1.3/plan.

tools.name: upcloud_list_prices
tools.title: List prices
tools.description: The price list per zone in the account's currency: per-hour prices for plans, cores, memory, storage tiers, backups, IPv4 addresses and traffic. UpCloud: GET /1.3/price.

tools.name: upcloud_get_billing_summary
tools.title: Get monthly billing summary
tools.description: Billing summary for one month with per-resource details (servers, storages, managed databases, object storage, …: amount, hours, plan, zone, labels) and totals. Needs an account allowed to read billing. UpCloud: GET /1.3/account/billing/summary/{yearmonth}.

tools.name: upcloud_list_servers
tools.title: List servers
tools.description: Cloud servers on the account (summary: uuid, title, hostname, zone, plan, cores, memory, state, tags, labels). Filter by state, a free-text search (name, title, uuid, zone, IP, hostname, tag or template), tags or labels. Use upcloud_get_server for IPs and disks. UpCloud: GET /1.3/server.

tools.name: upcloud_get_server
tools.title: Get server details
tools.description: Full details of one server: state, plan, cores/memory, network interfaces and IP addresses, attached storage devices, firewall on/off, simple-backup schedule, labels, tags and remote-access settings. UpCloud: GET /1.3/server/{uuid}.

tools.name: upcloud_list_storages
tools.title: List storages
tools.description: Storage devices: disks, backups, CD-ROM images and OS templates (uuid, title, type, tier, size GB, state, zone, labels). Narrow by `kind`: private (yours), public (UpCloud-provided), normal (disks), backup, cdrom, template or favorite. UpCloud: GET /1.3/storage[/{kind}].

tools.name: upcloud_get_storage
tools.title: Get storage details
tools.description: Details of one storage: size, tier, state (e.g. online, backuping), encryption, the servers it is attached to, its backups and backup_rule. Poll this to follow a backup started with upcloud_create_storage_backup. UpCloud: GET /1.3/storage/{uuid}.

tools.name: upcloud_list_ip_addresses
tools.title: List IP addresses
tools.description: Every IP address on the account: address, family (IPv4/IPv6), access (public/utility/private), the server it is assigned to, zone, PTR record, floating flag and release policy. UpCloud: GET /1.3/ip_address.

tools.name: upcloud_list_firewall_rules
tools.title: List server firewall rules
tools.description: The firewall rules of one server in evaluation order (position, direction, action, family, protocol, address and port ranges, comment). Whether the firewall is enabled at all is the `firewall` field of upcloud_get_server. UpCloud: GET /1.3/server/{uuid}/firewall_rule.

tools.name: upcloud_list_networks
tools.title: List networks
tools.description: Networks visible to the account — public, utility and private SDN networks — with their IP subnets, DHCP settings, routes, attached servers and peerings. Optionally only one zone. UpCloud: GET /1.3/network/.

tools.name: upcloud_list_databases
tools.title: List managed databases
tools.description: Managed Database services (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Valkey, OpenSearch): uuid, title, type, plan, zone, state, component hosts/ports, backups and labels. Note the response can include connection URIs with credentials. UpCloud: GET /1.3/database.

tools.name: upcloud_list_load_balancers
tools.title: List managed load balancers
tools.description: Managed Load Balancer services with their frontends, backends and members, networks, plan, zone, configured status and operational state. UpCloud: GET /1.3/load-balancer.

tools.name: upcloud_list_kubernetes_clusters
tools.title: List Kubernetes clusters
tools.description: Managed Kubernetes clusters: name, uuid, zone, plan, state, network/CIDR, control-plane IP filter, labels and node groups (plan, count, state). UpCloud: GET /1.3/kubernetes.

tools.name: upcloud_list_object_storages
tools.title: List managed object storages
tools.description: Managed Object Storage (S3-compatible) services: uuid, name, region, configured status and operational state, public/private endpoints, custom domains and labels. UpCloud: GET /1.3/object-storage-2.

tools.name: upcloud_list_audit_logs
tools.title: List audit logs
tools.description: Security audit trail of the account (up to 180 days): who did what to which resource, when, from which IP and via API or Hub. Filter by action, origin, resource type, time window or a keyword (UUID, username or IP). Returns total_count for paging. UpCloud: GET /1.3/audit-logs.

tools.name: upcloud_start_server
tools.title: Start a server
tools.description: Start a stopped server (billing for a started server resumes). Fails with 409 if it is not stopped. `async` returns immediately — poll upcloud_get_server for state=started. UpCloud: POST /1.3/server/{uuid}/start.

tools.name: upcloud_stop_server
tools.title: Stop a server
tools.description: DISRUPTIVE: stop a running server — it goes offline until started again with upcloud_start_server. soft (default) sends an ACPI shutdown; with a timeout, a hard stop follows if it is still running. hard is like pulling the plug and can lose unsaved data. UpCloud: POST /1.3/server/{uuid}/stop.

tools.name: upcloud_restart_server
tools.title: Restart a server
tools.description: DISRUPTIVE: stop and start a running server. soft (default) needs a timeout: after it, timeout_action=destroy hard-stops and restarts, ignore (API default) aborts and leaves the server running. hard power-cycles immediately. UpCloud: POST /1.3/server/{uuid}/restart.

tools.name: upcloud_create_storage_backup
tools.title: Back up a storage
tools.description: Take an on-demand, point-in-time backup of a storage device. Additive (nothing is overwritten) but backups are billed per GB. Asynchronous: the storage goes to a backuping/maintenance state and back to online — poll upcloud_get_storage. UpCloud: POST /1.3/storage/{uuid}/backup.

tools.name: upcloud_modify_server
tools.title: Rename a server / set its backup schedule
tools.description: Change a server's title, hostname and/or simple-backup schedule. Only these reversible fields are exposed — no resizing or plan change (billing) and no firewall toggle. simple_backup is `HHMM,daily|dailies|weeklies|monthlies` (UTC time) or `no` to disable. UpCloud: PUT /1.3/server/{uuid}.

What did my hosting bill come to last month, by resource?
List the firewall rules on my web server.
Show the disks and existing backups attached to my main web server.

servers.name: updown.io
servers.description: Check updown.io uptime checks, downtimes, response metrics and status pages, and create checks.

tools.name: updown_list_checks
tools.title: List checks
tools.description: List all monitoring checks on the account with their status (down, uptime, last_status, error), period, SSL certificate and domain-expiry info. Optionally filter client-side by status or a text match on URL/alias. updown: GET /api/checks.

tools.name: updown_get_check
tools.title: Get one check
tools.description: Fetch a single check by token, optionally with the last hour of performance metrics and/or the detailed results of the last 5 requests. updown: GET /api/checks/:token.

tools.name: updown_list_downtimes
tools.title: List a check's downtimes
tools.description: List the downtimes of one check, newest first, 100 per page: error, started_at, ended_at, duration (seconds) and a details URL. updown: GET /api/checks/:token/downtimes.

tools.name: updown_get_check_metrics
tools.title: Get a check's metrics
tools.description: Get aggregated metrics for one check over a time range: uptime, apdex, timings (redirect/namelookup/connection/handshake/response/total, ms) and request counts by response time. Optionally group by 'time' or by 'host' (monitoring location). Data is hourly (daily after 2 days, monthly after 40 days); the range must span at least one hour. Uptime is not returned when grouping. updown: GET /api/checks/:token/metrics.

tools.name: updown_find_problems
tools.title: Find checks with problems
tools.description: One-call health overview across every check: which are DOWN (since when, error), which have an invalid SSL certificate, which certificates or domains expire within N days, and which checks are paused or muted. Built from GET /api/checks.

tools.name: updown_list_recipients
tools.title: List alert recipients
tools.description: List the alert recipients/channels on the account (email, sms, slack, telegram, webhook, zapier, ...). The `id` (e.g. email:3719031852) is what check `recipients` take. updown: GET /api/recipients.

tools.name: updown_list_status_pages
tools.title: List status pages
tools.description: List the account's status pages: token, public URL, name, description, visibility (public/protected/private) and the ordered check tokens shown. updown: GET /api/status_pages.

tools.name: updown_list_nodes
tools.title: List monitoring nodes
tools.description: List updown.io's monitoring/webhook servers keyed by location code (lan, mia, tor, rbx, fra, cap, hel, sin, tok, syd) with IPv4, IPv6, city, country and coordinates. Public — no API key needed. updown: GET /api/nodes.

tools.name: updown_list_node_ips
tools.title: List monitoring node IPs
tools.description: List updown.io's server IP addresses — e.g. to allowlist the monitors in a firewall. Choose all, ipv4 or ipv6. Public — no API key needed. updown: GET /api/nodes/ips, /api/nodes/ipv4, /api/nodes/ipv6.

tools.name: updown_create_check
tools.title: Create a check
tools.description: Add a new monitoring check. The type (http, https, tcp, tcps, icmp) is inferred from the URL scheme; pass type 'pulse' (and no URL) for a cron/heartbeat check. Each check consumes updown credits while enabled. Requires the read/write API key. updown: POST /api/checks.

tools.name: updown_update_check
tools.title: Update a check
tools.description: Change a check's settings — URL, period, alias, string match, recipients, headers, locations — or pause/resume it (enabled) or mute its alerts (mute_until). Only the fields you pass are changed. Caution: URLs returned by a read-only key hide basic-auth credentials; re-sending such a URL erases them. Requires the read/write API key. updown: PUT /api/checks/:token.

tools.name: updown_add_recipient
tools.title: Add an alert recipient
tools.description: Add an alert recipient: an email address, phone number (sms), webhook URL, Slack-compatible incoming-webhook URL, or Microsoft Teams webhook URL. Returns the new (or already-existing) recipient with its id. By default it is selected on ALL existing checks; pass selected=false to add it unattached. Slack/Telegram/Zapier/Statuspage integrations must be set up in the web UI. Requires the read/write API key. updown: POST /api/recipients.

tools.name: updown_create_status_page
tools.title: Create a status page
tools.description: Create a status page showing the given checks, in order. Returns its token and URL. Requires the read/write API key. updown: POST /api/status_pages.

tools.name: updown_update_status_page
tools.title: Update a status page
tools.description: Change a status page's checks (replaces the list, order respected), name, description, visibility or access key. Only the fields you pass are changed. Requires the read/write API key. updown: PUT /api/status_pages/:token.

tools.name: updown_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: updown_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the updown.io tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: updown_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on updown.io (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: updown_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's updown.io Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run updown_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find it at [updown.io → **Settings → API keys**](https://updown.io/settings/edit). The **read-only** key is enough for every read tool (checks, downtimes, metrics, problems, recipients, status pages); to create/update checks, add recipients or edit status pages, paste the **read/write** key instead. Your key is used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Is anything on my account down right now?
What was the uptime of my website over the last 30 days?
Which of my checks have had downtime this week and for how long?
Add an uptime check for https://acme-example.com/ every minute.

servers.name: Virtuous
servers.description: Search donors and contacts, giving history, notes and projects, and log notes, tags and gifts.

tools.name: virtuous_get_current_organization
tools.title: Get the current organization
tools.description: Fetch the Virtuous organization this API key acts in — its name, time zone and culture, and whether the key's user is an administrator. A cheap way to confirm the key works. Virtuous: GET /api/Organization/Current.

tools.name: virtuous_search
tools.title: Global search
tools.description: Full-text search across contacts, individuals and entities (campaigns, projects, segments, tags) — the same search as the Virtuous search bar. Returns hits with highlights, grouped by kind. Virtuous: POST /api/Search.

tools.name: virtuous_search_contacts
tools.title: Search contacts
tools.description: Find contacts whose name, email, phone or address fully or partially matches a search string. Returns id, name, contact type, email, phone and address per match. Virtuous: POST /api/Contact/Search.

tools.name: virtuous_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: Fetch one contact (household, organization, foundation ...) with its address, giving summary (life-to-date, year-to-date, last gift), individuals and their contact methods, and custom fields. Virtuous: GET /api/Contact/{contactId}.

tools.name: virtuous_find_contact
tools.title: Find a contact by email or reference
tools.description: Look up a single contact by email address, or by an external reference (reference source + id, e.g. Stripe customer id). Give either email, or both reference_source and reference_id; if both are given Virtuous prioritises the reference. Virtuous: GET /api/Contact/Find.

tools.name: virtuous_list_contact_individuals
tools.title: List a contact's individuals
tools.description: List the individuals (people) that belong to a contact/household, with names, birth dates, and their emails and phones (contact methods). Virtuous: GET /api/ContactIndividual/ByContact/{contactId}.

tools.name: virtuous_list_contact_notes
tools.title: List a contact's notes
tools.description: List the notes logged on a contact — calls, meetings, emails and other touchpoints — with type, date, text and author. Virtuous: GET /api/ContactNote/ByContact/{contactId}.

tools.name: virtuous_list_contact_note_types
tools.title: List contact note types
tools.description: List the note types this organization accepts on a contact note (e.g. Call, Email, Visit; admins can add custom ones). Call it before virtuous_create_contact_note and pass one of these names as its type. Virtuous: GET /api/ContactNote/Types.

tools.name: virtuous_list_contact_tags
tools.title: List a contact's tags
tools.description: List the tags applied to a contact (contactTagId, tagId, name). Virtuous: GET /api/ContactTag/ByContact/{contactId}.

tools.name: virtuous_list_contact_gifts
tools.title: List a contact's gifts
tools.description: List a contact's giving history: gift id, type, date, amount, segment and batch. Use virtuous_get_gift for designations and full detail. Virtuous: GET /api/Gift/ByContact/{contactId}.

tools.name: virtuous_get_gift
tools.title: Get a gift
tools.description: Fetch one gift in full: contact, type, date, amount and currency, batch, segment, grant, tribute, receipt date, designations to projects, premiums and custom fields. Virtuous: GET /api/Gift/{giftId}.

tools.name: virtuous_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: List the organization's tags (id, name, tag group). Use this to find a tagId before virtuous_add_contact_tag. Virtuous: GET /api/Tag.

tools.name: virtuous_search_projects
tools.title: Search projects
tools.description: Find projects (funds / designations gifts are given to) by name or code, with their balances, financial need and life-to-date giving. Virtuous: POST /api/Project/Search.

tools.name: virtuous_get_project
tools.title: Get a project
tools.description: Fetch one project: code, type, status, balances, financial need, date range, life-to-date and calendar-year giving and gift/giver counts. Virtuous: GET /api/Project/{projectId}.

tools.name: virtuous_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List the organization's events: name, type, location, start/end, invite and RSVP counts, attendance and total giving. Virtuous: GET /api/Event.

tools.name: virtuous_get_query_options
tools.title: Get query options
tools.description: List the parameters, their types, allowed operators and value options that virtuous_query accepts for one record type. Call this BEFORE building a query. Virtuous: GET /api/<Resource>/QueryOptions.

tools.name: virtuous_query
tools.title: Query records
tools.description: Run a Virtuous query-builder query against one record type (contacts, gifts, campaigns, projects, tasks, grants, pledges, recurring gifts, events ...). Conditions use parameter/operator names from virtuous_get_query_options. Returns { list, total }. For Contact and Gift, full_details returns full records instead of the abbreviated view. Virtuous: POST /api/<Resource>/Query.

tools.name: virtuous_create_contact_note
tools.title: Log a note on a contact
tools.description: Add a note to a contact's timeline — a call, meeting, visit or other touchpoint. Writes to the donor record. Get the valid type names from virtuous_list_contact_note_types first. Virtuous: POST /api/ContactNote.

tools.name: virtuous_add_contact_tag
tools.title: Tag a contact
tools.description: Apply an existing tag to a contact (find the tagId with virtuous_list_tags). Virtuous: POST /api/ContactTag.

tools.name: virtuous_create_contact_transaction
tools.title: Submit a contact for import
tools.description: Submit a new or updated contact through Virtuous's import pipeline (the recommended way to add contacts). It is matched against existing contacts by name, email, phone, address and reference, bundled into an import at midnight, and only committed when a user reviews the import and clicks Run — so nothing is created in real time and no duplicates are forced. Virtuous: POST /api/Contact/Transaction.

tools.name: virtuous_create_gift_transaction
tools.title: Submit a gift for import
tools.description: Record a gift (donation already received) through Virtuous's gift import pipeline — the method Virtuous recommends. The gift is matched to a contact, recurring gift or pledge, held until the nightly import, and only created when a user reviews the import and clicks Run. This records a gift; it does NOT charge anyone. Identify the donor with contact.id, contact.referenceId, or name/email details. Virtuous: POST /api/v2/Gift/Transaction.

tools.name: virtuous_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: virtuous_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Virtuous tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: virtuous_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Virtuous (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: virtuous_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Virtuous Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run virtuous_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Create one in Virtuous → **Settings → API Keys** (the key acts with the permission group you assign it). Your key is used only to call the Virtuous API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Find the contact record for jane.smith@example.com and show her giving history.
What gifts has the Smith household given us, and when?
Which of our upcoming events have the most RSVPs?
Add a note to Jane Smith's record: called to thank her for her gift.

servers.name: When I Work
servers.description: Check shifts, time clock entries, time-off requests, swaps and availability, and manage shifts.

tools.name: wheniwork_get_account
tools.title: Get the account
tools.description: Fetch the When I Work account (workplace) the token acts on — company name, plan and settings; for a parent account also its child accounts. A cheap way to confirm the credentials work. When I Work: GET /2/account.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the employees, supervisors, managers and admins in the account, optionally limited to some schedules or searched by name/email. Role codes: 1 admin, 2 manager, 3 employee, 5 supervisor. When I Work: GET /2/users.

tools.name: wheniwork_get_user
tools.title: Get one user
tools.description: Fetch one user by id — name, email, role, positions, schedules, wage. When I Work: GET /2/users/{id}.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_locations
tools.title: List schedules (locations)
tools.description: List the schedules in the account. The API calls a schedule a "location"; its id is the location_id every shift belongs to. When I Work: GET /2/locations.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_positions
tools.title: List positions
tools.description: List the positions (job roles such as Cashier or Dishwasher) in the account. When I Work: GET /2/positions.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_shifts
tools.title: List shifts
tools.description: List scheduled shifts in a time window — who works when, where and in which position — optionally including open shifts and unpublished drafts. Answers "who is on on Friday?" and "what open shifts are left?". When I Work: GET /2/shifts.

tools.name: wheniwork_get_shift
tools.title: Get one shift
tools.description: Fetch one shift by id, including its breaks and publish state. When I Work: GET /2/shifts/{id}.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_eligible_users_for_shift
tools.title: List users eligible for an open shift
tools.description: Find who could take an open shift — either an existing shift (shift_id) or a hypothetical one (start, end, position_id and location_id all required). When I Work: GET /2/shifts/eligible.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_times
tools.title: List clocked times (timesheets)
tools.description: List clocked time entries — actual hours worked, clock-in/out times, length and approval state. Use only_open to see who is clocked in right now. When I Work: GET /2/times.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_time_off_requests
tools.title: List time-off requests
tools.description: List time-off requests in a date range, with the requesting users. Status: 0 pending, 1 canceled, 2 accepted, 3 expired, 4 denied. When I Work: GET /2/requests.

tools.name: wheniwork_get_time_off_request
tools.title: Get one time-off request
tools.description: Fetch one time-off request by id, with its message thread and users. When I Work: GET /2/requests/{request_id}.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_time_off_types
tools.title: List time-off types
tools.description: List the time-off types (e.g. Personal, Sick, Holiday) and whether each allows paid time. Their ids are the type_id for a new request. When I Work: GET /2/requesttypes.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_shift_swaps
tools.title: List shift swaps and drops
tools.description: List shift requests: swaps, drops and alerts, with the shifts and users involved. Status: 0 pending, 1 approved, 2 declined, 3 completed, 4 canceled, 5 expired. Type: 1 swap, 2 drop, 3 alert. start and end must be given together. When I Work: GET /2/swaps.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_availability
tools.title: List availability
tools.description: List availability events — when people said they can or cannot work, including recurring patterns that fall in the window. Defaults to the caller, from now to two weeks out. When I Work: GET /2/availabilityevents.

tools.name: wheniwork_list_annotations
tools.title: List schedule annotations
tools.description: List schedule annotations — announcements, business-closed days and blackout dates when time off is not allowed. Defaults to today through one year out. When I Work: GET /2/annotations.

tools.name: wheniwork_create_shift
tools.title: Create a shift
tools.description: Create one shift on a schedule — assigned to a user, or open (user_id 0). Created as a draft unless published is true. Undo by editing it or unpublishing. When I Work: POST /2/shifts.

tools.name: wheniwork_update_shift
tools.title: Update a shift
tools.description: Change a shift — reassign it, move it, change position or notes. When I Work requires start_time, end_time and location_id on every update, so fetch the shift first and pass them back. This tool never sends a breaks array; When I Work documents that breaks omitted from an update's breaks list are removed, so re-check the shift's breaks afterwards. When I Work: PUT /2/shifts/{id}.

tools.name: wheniwork_publish_shifts
tools.title: Publish shifts
tools.description: Publish draft shifts so employees can see them. Publishing does not itself send notifications. Undo with wheniwork_unpublish_shifts. When I Work: POST /2/shifts/publish.

tools.name: wheniwork_unpublish_shifts
tools.title: Unpublish shifts
tools.description: Return published shifts to draft, hiding them from employees. Undo with wheniwork_publish_shifts. When I Work: POST /2/shifts/unpublish.

tools.name: wheniwork_create_time_off_request
tools.title: Create a time-off request
tools.description: Create a time-off request for a user (default the calling user). It starts pending; cancel it with wheniwork_update_time_off_request (status 1). Get type ids from wheniwork_list_time_off_types. When I Work: POST /2/requests.

tools.name: wheniwork_update_time_off_request
tools.title: Approve, deny or change a time-off request
tools.description: Change a time-off request: set its status (0 pending, 1 canceled, 2 accepted/approved, 3 expired, 4 denied) and/or its dates or hours. Reversible — set the status back. start_time and end_time must be given together. When I Work: PUT /2/requests/{request_id}.

tools.name: wheniwork_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wheniwork_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the When I Work tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wheniwork_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on When I Work (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wheniwork_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's When I Work Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run wheniwork_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Who works tomorrow, and which shifts are still open?
List the pending time-off requests for next week.
Approve Alex's time-off request for Friday.
Show the clocked hours for each employee last week.
Create an open 9 am–5 pm cashier shift on Saturday as an unpublished draft.
servers.keyHelp: When I Work issues the **developer key** (W-Key). If you do not have one, ask When I Work support for an API developer key. Then use the email and password that you use at app.wheniwork.com.

login.hint: Your developer key, email and password are stored **encrypted** in this connection's authorization grant and used **only** to log in to When I Work and call the When I Work API on your behalf. They are never shown to anyone; the key and email are also hashed into a private account id for usage metering.

servers.name: Wild Apricot
servers.description: Look up members, events, registrations, invoices and payments, and add contacts or check in guests.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_accounts
tools.title: List accounts
tools.description: List the Wild Apricot accounts this API key can reach — id, name, primary domain, currency, contact limit. A cheap way to confirm the key works. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts.

tools.name: wildapricot_get_account
tools.title: Get the account
tools.description: Fetch the current account's details (name, primary domain, time zone, currency, billing plan, contact limit). Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_contacts
tools.title: Search contacts and members
tools.description: Search contacts and members. Use simple_query for a substring match on name, organization, email or phone, or filter for an OData-style expression over field names/system codes (e.g. "'Membership status' eq 'Active'", "'Profile last updated' gt 2026-01-01"). Runs synchronously ($async=false). Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/contacts.

tools.name: wildapricot_get_contact
tools.title: Get one contact
tools.description: Fetch one contact or member with all field values, membership level and status. Set extended_membership_info for the pending membership order, its invoice and allowed actions. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/contacts/{contactId}.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_contact_fields
tools.title: List contact fields
tools.description: List the contact and membership field definitions — names, system codes, types, allowed values, whether each is searchable ($filter) and editable. Use it to build filters and field_values. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/contactfields.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_membership_levels
tools.title: List membership levels
tools.description: List membership levels — name, fee, renewal period, individual vs bundle, whether the public can apply. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/membershiplevels.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_member_groups
tools.title: List member groups
tools.description: List ad hoc member groups (id, name, description). Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/membergroups.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_saved_searches
tools.title: List saved searches
tools.description: List the contact saved searches defined by admins (id, name, description). Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/savedsearches.

tools.name: wildapricot_get_saved_search
tools.title: Run a saved search
tools.description: Run one saved search and return the ids of the contacts it currently matches. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/savedsearches/{savedSearchId}.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List events. filter supports e.g. "IsUpcoming eq true", "StartDate gt 2026-01-01", "RegistrationEnabled eq true", "Tags in [workshop]", "Id in [1,2]". Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/events.

tools.name: wildapricot_get_event
tools.title: Get one event
tools.description: Fetch one event with its details — description, registration types, registration fields, sessions, registration counts and totals paid/due. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/events/{eventId}.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_event_registration_types
tools.title: List event registration types
tools.description: List an event's registration types (ticket types) — price, availability, limits, waitlist. You need a type id to register someone. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/EventRegistrationTypes?eventId=.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_event_registrations
tools.title: List event registrations
tools.description: List registrations for an event (attendee list) or for a contact (what they signed up for) — registration type, fee, paid, checked in, waitlist. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/eventregistrations.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices, optionally for one contact, event or event registration, paid/unpaid only, or within a created-date range. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/invoices.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_payments
tools.title: List payments
tools.description: List payments received, optionally for one contact or event, unsettled only, or within a created-date range. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/payments.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_donations
tools.title: List donations
tools.description: List donations — donor, amount, date, comments and donation field values — optionally within a date range. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/donations.

tools.name: wildapricot_list_audit_log
tools.title: List audit log items
tools.description: List audit log items (membership changes, payments, invoices and other admin/member activity) within a date range. Wild Apricot: GET /accounts/{accountId}/auditLogItems.

tools.name: wildapricot_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact or member
tools.description: Create a contact. To make them a member set membership_enabled=true and membership_level_id (Wild Apricot may create a membership invoice unless recreate_invoice=false). Custom fields go in field_values. Wild Apricot: POST /accounts/{accountId}/contacts.

tools.name: wildapricot_update_contact
tools.title: Update a contact or member
tools.description: Update an existing contact: names, email, membership level/status, or custom field values. Only the fields you pass are sent. Wild Apricot: PUT /accounts/{accountId}/contacts/{contactId}.

tools.name: wildapricot_create_event_registration
tools.title: Register a contact for an event
tools.description: Register an existing contact for an event under one registration type (from wildapricot_list_event_registration_types). Can add to the waitlist instead. Wild Apricot: POST /accounts/{accountId}/eventregistrations.

tools.name: wildapricot_check_in_attendee
tools.title: Check an attendee in or out
tools.description: Mark an event registration as checked in (checked_in=true) or undo it (false); for anonymous guests, set how many are checked in. Wild Apricot: POST /rpc/{accountId}/CheckInEventAttendee.

tools.name: wildapricot_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wildapricot_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Wild Apricot tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wildapricot_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Wild Apricot (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wildapricot_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Wild Apricot Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run wildapricot_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: Find the key in Wild Apricot → **Settings → Integration → Authorized applications** → authorize a **Server application** → copy its **API key**. The account ID is only needed if the key reaches more than one account (it is the number in your admin URLs). Your key is used only to call the Wild Apricot API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

examples: Which events are coming up, and how many people have registered for each?
Which invoices are still unpaid, and how much is outstanding in total?
Find the member record for Jane Smith and show her membership level.
What payments did we receive this month?

servers.name: Wufoo
servers.description: Read forms, fields, entries, reports and comments by field title, and submit entries.

tools.name: wufoo_list_forms
tools.title: List forms
tools.description: List the forms the API key's user can access: name, description, hash (permanent identifier), URL title, public/private, start/end dates, entry limit, created/updated timestamps. Set includeTodayCount to add EntryCountToday. Wufoo: GET /forms.json.

tools.name: wufoo_get_form
tools.title: Get one form
tools.description: Fetch one form's settings by hash or URL title — name, description, confirmation message, notification emails, public flag, language, start/end dates, entry limit and links. Wufoo: GET /forms/{identifier}.json.

tools.name: wufoo_get_form_fields
tools.title: Get form fields
tools.description: The field structure of a form: each field's Title, Type, API ID (Field###, used for filters, sorting and submissions), required flag, default value and page. Checkbox, name, address and likert fields list SubFields with their own IDs; multiple-choice, dropdown and likert fields list Choices. Admin-only fields are not returned. Wufoo: GET /forms/{identifier}/fields.json.

tools.name: wufoo_list_form_entries
tools.title: List form entries
tools.description: List a form's submitted entries (as in the Entry Manager), keyed by field API ID (Field105…) plus EntryId, DateCreated, CreatedBy, DateUpdated, UpdatedBy. Filter like the Entry Manager (Filter1=Field105 Contains foo, combined with match AND/OR), sort by any field ID, and page with pageStart/pageSize (max 100). For entries keyed by human field titles use wufoo_get_labeled_entries. Wufoo: GET /forms/{identifier}/entries.json.

tools.name: wufoo_get_labeled_entries
tools.title: Get entries keyed by field title
tools.description: Fetch a page of a form's entries with every Field### key replaced by the field's human title — e.g. "Email", or "Title — Label" for sub-fields of checkbox, name, address and likert fields ("Name — First", "Address — City"). EntryId, DateCreated and the other default/system keys stay as they are. Empty values are dropped unless includeEmpty is set. Also returns fieldIds (title → API ID) for building filters or submissions. Takes the same paging, sorting and filter arguments as wufoo_list_form_entries. Wufoo: GET /forms/{identifier}/fields.json + /entries.json.

tools.name: wufoo_count_form_entries
tools.title: Count form entries
tools.description: Count a form's entries — all of them, or only those matching filters (same filter format as wufoo_list_form_entries). Useful to plan paging. Returns {EntryCount}. Wufoo: GET /forms/{identifier}/entries/count.json.

tools.name: wufoo_list_form_comments
tools.title: List entry comments
tools.description: List the comments team members left on a form's entries in the Entry Manager: CommentId, EntryId, Text, CommentedBy, DateCreated. Optionally only for one entry. Page with pageStart/pageSize (max 100). Wufoo: GET /forms/{identifier}/comments.json.

tools.name: wufoo_count_form_comments
tools.title: Count entry comments
tools.description: Count all comments on a form's entries. Returns {Count}. Wufoo: GET /forms/{identifier}/comments/count.json.

tools.name: wufoo_list_reports
tools.title: List reports
tools.description: List the reports the API key's user can access: name, description, hash, URL title, public flag and created/updated timestamps. Wufoo: GET /reports.json.

tools.name: wufoo_get_report
tools.title: Get one report
tools.description: Fetch one report by hash or URL title. Wufoo: GET /reports/{identifier}.json.

tools.name: wufoo_get_report_fields
tools.title: Get report fields
tools.description: The field structure of the form a report is built on (same shape as wufoo_get_form_fields). Wufoo: GET /reports/{identifier}/fields.json.

tools.name: wufoo_list_report_entries
tools.title: List report entries
tools.description: The entries that make up a report — what its datagrid widget or an export would show, keyed by field API ID. Wufoo documents no paging or filter parameters for this endpoint. Wufoo: GET /reports/{identifier}/entries.json.

tools.name: wufoo_count_report_entries
tools.title: Count report entries
tools.description: Count the entries in a report. Returns {EntryCount}. Wufoo: GET /reports/{identifier}/entries/count.json.

tools.name: wufoo_list_report_widgets
tools.title: List report widgets
tools.description: The chart, graph (pie/bar/line) and big-number widgets on a report: Name, Type, TypeDesc, Size and Hash (the hash embeds the widget). Text and datagrid widgets are not returned. Wufoo: GET /reports/{identifier}/widgets.json.

tools.name: wufoo_list_users
tools.title: List account users
tools.description: List the account's users: name, email, timezone, company, owner/admin flags and create-forms/reports/themes permissions. Each user's API key is redacted from the result. Wufoo: GET /users.json.

tools.name: wufoo_submit_entry
tools.title: Submit a form entry
tools.description: WRITE: submits a new entry to a form, exactly as if someone filled it in — it is stored and triggers the form's notifications, webhooks and integrations. Keys are field API IDs from wufoo_get_form_fields (Field1, Field105…); fields with sub-fields (name, address, checkbox) take one key per sub-field ID. Dates must be YYYYMMDD. Field validation and form limits still apply: a rejected submission returns each field error. Limited by Wufoo to 50 submissions per user per 5 minutes. Wufoo: POST /forms/{identifier}/entries.json.

tools.name: wufoo_add_webhook
tools.title: Add a webhook
tools.description: WRITE: adds a webhook to a form, so Wufoo POSTs every new entry to the given URL. Idempotent per URL: calling again with the same URL updates its handshake key / metadata setting instead of adding a duplicate. Forms allow at most 10 integrations. Returns WebHookPutResult.Hash — keep it, it is needed to delete the webhook. Wufoo: PUT /forms/{identifier}/webhooks.json.

tools.name: wufoo_delete_webhook
tools.title: Delete a webhook
tools.description: WRITE: removes a webhook from a form; the receiving URL stops getting new entries immediately. Needs the webhook hash returned by wufoo_add_webhook (Wufoo has no endpoint to list webhooks). Wufoo: DELETE /forms/{identifier}/webhooks/{webhookHash}.json.

tools.name: wufoo_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wufoo_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Wufoo tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wufoo_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Wufoo (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wufoo_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Wufoo Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run wufoo_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: The subdomain is the first part of your Wufoo address (`fishbowl` in `fishbowl.wufoo.com`). Find the API key in Wufoo → **Form Manager → Account → API Information** (or a form's **More → API Information**). Your credentials are used only to call the API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

examples: How many entries has my contact form received so far?
Show the latest 10 entries on my event signup form with readable field names.
How many signups came in on my newsletter form this month?
What comments has my team left on entries of my order form?

servers.name: Lightspeed Retail (R-Series)
servers.description: Read Lightspeed R-Series items, stock, sales, customers and POs; create customers and set stock.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The connected Lightspeed Retail (R-Series) account: id, name, status, employee count/limit, default and purchasing currencies. Good first call. GET /Account/{accountID}.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_list_shops
tools.title: List shops
tools.description: List the account's shops (store locations): shopID, name, time zone, archived flag. Use shopID to filter sales, inventory and purchase orders. GET /Account/{accountID}/Shop.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_list_items
tools.title: List items
tools.description: Search the product catalog. Each item has itemID, description, SKUs (systemSku, customSku, upc, ean, manufacturerSku), defaultCost, categoryID and its Prices (price levels). Set include_stock to add per-shop quantities (ItemShops; shopID 0 = all shops). Paginate with next_url. GET /Account/{accountID}/Item.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_get_item
tools.title: Get an item
tools.description: One item by itemID with its prices, per-shop stock (ItemShops), category and other related records. GET /Account/{accountID}/Item/{itemID}.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_list_inventory
tools.title: List inventory levels
tools.description: Stock levels per item per shop (ItemShop records): qoh (quantity on hand), sellable, backorder, reorderPoint, reorderLevel, costs and values. shopID 0 is the all-shops summary. Paginate with next_url. GET /Account/{accountID}/ItemShop.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_list_categories
tools.title: List categories
tools.description: Item categories (hierarchical): categoryID, name, fullPathName, parentID, nodeDepth. GET /Account/{accountID}/Category.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_list_sales
tools.title: List sales
tools.description: Sales history: saleID, completed/voided flags, completeTime, totals (calcSubtotal, calcTax1/2, total, balance), customerID, employeeID, shopID, registerID. Filter by a date range on completeTime (default) or timeStamp, shop, customer, employee. Set include_lines for SaleLines (items sold). Paginate with next_url. GET /Account/{accountID}/Sale.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_get_sale
tools.title: Get a sale
tools.description: One sale by saleID with its line items (SaleLines with Item), payments (SalePayments with PaymentType) and customer. GET /Account/{accountID}/Sale/{saleID}.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: Search customers by name, company or email: customerID, firstName, lastName, company, customerTypeID, createTime. Email search loads the Contact relation (emails, phones, addresses). Paginate with next_url. GET /Account/{accountID}/Customer.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_get_customer
tools.title: Get a customer
tools.description: One customer by customerID with Contact (emails, phones, addresses), customer type and notes. GET /Account/{accountID}/Customer/{customerID}.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_list_vendors
tools.title: List vendors
tools.description: Suppliers: vendorID, name, accountNumber, archived. GET /Account/{accountID}/Vendor.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_list_purchase_orders
tools.title: List purchase orders
tools.description: Purchase orders to vendors: orderID, vendorID, shopID, orderedDate, arrivalDate, receivedDate, complete, totalQuantity, shipCost. GET /Account/{accountID}/Order.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_get_purchase_order
tools.title: Get a purchase order
tools.description: One purchase order by orderID with its lines (OrderLines: itemID, quantity, numReceived, price), vendor and shop. GET /Account/{accountID}/Order/{orderID}.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_list_employees
tools.title: List employees
tools.description: Employees: employeeID, firstName, lastName, lockOut, archived, employeeRoleID, limitToShopID. Use employeeID to filter sales. GET /Account/{accountID}/Employee.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_create_customer
tools.title: Create a customer
tools.description: Create a new customer, optionally with a primary email and one phone number (stored in the customer's Contact). Give at least a first name, last name or company. Returns the new customer with its customerID. POST /Account/{accountID}/Customer.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_update_item
tools.title: Update an item
tools.description: Change fields of an existing item: description, default cost, SKUs, category. Only the fields you pass are changed. Prices and stock are not changed here (use lightspeedrseries_update_stock for quantities). PUT /Account/{accountID}/Item/{itemID}.json.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_update_stock
tools.title: Set stock level
tools.description: CHANGES STOCK COUNTS: sets (does not add to) the quantity on hand of one item in one shop to `qoh`, by updating the item's ItemShop record. Use for correcting a few items; for many items use an inventory count in Lightspeed. Identify the shop by shop_id, or by item_shop_id from lightspeedrseries_get_item's ItemShops. Not for shopID 0 (the all-shops summary). PUT /Account/{accountID}/Item/{itemID}.json with ItemShops.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Lightspeed Retail (R-Series) tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Lightspeed Retail (R-Series) (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lightspeedrseries_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Lightspeed Retail (R-Series) Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run lightspeedrseries_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

login.hint: This server reads your items, stock levels, sales, customers, vendors, purchase orders and employees, and can create customers, edit items and set stock levels when you ask it to. It can do only what the Lightspeed employee who signs in is allowed to do. You can revoke access any time from your Lightspeed Retail account settings.

examples: Which items are low on stock at my main store?
What were my total sales yesterday across all of my stores?
Show the purchase orders still waiting to arrive from our vendors.
Look up the customer Jane Smith and show her contact details.

servers.name: Lightspeed Retail (X-Series)
servers.description: Read Lightspeed X-Series products, stock, sales, customers, stock orders; one-call sales reports.
examples: What were my total sales yesterday, by outlet and payment type?
Which products are below their reorder point at my main outlet?
Show the supplier stock orders that have not arrived yet.
Find the customer jane@example.com and add a note to her record.

login.hint: This server reads your products, stock levels, sales, customers, suppliers, stock orders, outlets, registers and staff, and can create and update customers, set product prices and set stock levels when you ask it to. You can remove its access any time in your Lightspeed Retail back office.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_retailer
tools.title: Get retailer
tools.description: The connected store: id, name, domain prefix, store URL, country, currency, time zone, tax-exclusive setting, loyalty and gift-card settings. Good first call (use the time zone to turn a local day into UTC for sales searches). GET /retailer.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_outlets
tools.title: List outlets
tools.description: List the store's outlets (locations): id, name, address, currency, time zone, default tax. Use the outlet id to filter sales, stock and stock orders. Paginate with next_after. GET /outlets.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_outlet
tools.title: Get outlet
tools.description: One outlet by id. GET /outlets/{outlet_id}.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_registers
tools.title: List registers
tools.description: List registers (tills): id, name, outlet_id, is_open, open/close times and invoice numbering. Paginate with next_after. GET /registers.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_register_payments_summary
tools.title: Get register payments summary
tools.description: Payment totals by payment type for one register since it was opened (the end-of-day / cash-up view). GET /registers/{register_id}/payments_summary.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_taxes
tools.title: List taxes
tools.description: List tax groups and their rates (id, name, is_default, rates). The vendor returns the whole list in one reply (no cursor). GET /taxes.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the store's users (staff): id, username, display name, email, account type (cashier, manager, admin), enabled flag, restricted outlets. Paginate with next_after. GET /users.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_user_sale_totals
tools.title: Get user sale totals
tools.description: Sales totals for one staff user, as the vendor computes them (no date filter; use sales_summary for a period). GET /users/{user_id}/sale_totals.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products (variants) in the catalog: id, family_id, sku, variant_name, prices (price_excluding_tax / price_including_tax), active flags, codes, suppliers, version. The product NAME lives on the product family: add includes=["families"] to get it. Paginate with next_after (stop when data is empty). With sku set, only that SKU is looked up and the other filters are ignored. For text/brand/supplier filters use search_products; for stock use get_inventory_levels. GET /products.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_product
tools.title: Get product
tools.description: One product (variant) by id, with its prices, codes, suppliers and outlet taxes. GET /products/{product_id}.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_search_products
tools.title: Search products
tools.description: Filter products by SKU, brand, supplier, tag, product type or variant parent. Uses offset paging: pass next_offset to continue (null = last page). GET /search?type=products.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_inventory_levels
tools.title: Get inventory levels
tools.description: Stock on hand per product per outlet: product_id, location_id (= outlet id), current_inventory_level, reorder threshold/amount, quantity_to_procure, average cost, total cost, supplier. Filter by outlet_ids, product_ids (or root_product_ids for variant families), supplier_ids; to_be_procured_only keeps products with a positive quantity_to_procure (the vendor's re-order suggestion, which accounts for open orders); for a plain below-reorder-point list, compare current_inventory_level with reorder_threshold yourself. Offset paging: pass next_offset to continue (null = last page). Read-only even though the vendor takes the filter as a POST body. POST /inventory_levels.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_brands
tools.title: List brands
tools.description: List product brands (id, name). Paginate with next_after. GET /brands.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: List product tags (id, name). Paginate with next_after. GET /tags.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_suppliers
tools.title: List suppliers
tools.description: List suppliers: id, name, default markup and contact details. Paginate with next_after. GET /suppliers.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_consignments
tools.title: List stock orders (consignments)
tools.description: List consignments: supplier stock orders (type SUPPLIER), transfers between outlets (OUTLET), stocktakes (STOCKTAKE) and returns (RETURN), with status (OPEN, SENT, DISPATCHED, RECEIVED, STOCKTAKE_*, CLOSED, CANCELLED), outlet, supplier, due and received dates, totals. Paginate with next_after. GET /consignments.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_consignment
tools.title: Get consignment
tools.description: One consignment (stock order, transfer, stocktake or return) by id. GET /consignments/{consignment_id}.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_consignment_products
tools.title: List consignment products
tools.description: The product lines of one consignment: product_id, SKU, ordered count, received quantity, cost. Paginate with next_after (stop when data is empty). GET /consignments/{consignment_id}/products.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_sales
tools.title: List sales (change feed)
tools.description: Sales in version order, oldest changes first: the way to sync everything that changed. It has NO date filter: for a period use search_sales or sales_summary. Each sale: id, date, invoice_number, state, customer_id, source (outlet, register, user), payments, line_items, totals. Paginate with next_after (stop when data is empty). GET /sales.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_sale
tools.title: Get sale
tools.description: One sale by id with its line items, payments, taxes and totals. GET /sales/{sale_id}.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_search_sales
tools.title: Search sales
tools.description: Find sales by date range (UTC), state, outlet, register, user, customer, payment type, product or invoice number. Uses offset paging: pass next_offset to continue (null = last page). Replies can be large: for totals over a period use sales_summary instead of paging through this. GET /search?type=sales.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_sales_summary
tools.title: Sales summary (totals for a period)
tools.description: Totals for a period computed here from up to max_pages x page_size sales, so a report needs ONE tool call instead of dozens: sale count and net / tax / gross (tax-inclusive) totals, plus breakdowns by state, UTC day, outlet and payment type name, and the top products by quantity. By default only closed sales are counted (states containing 'closed'); set counted_states to change that. Dates are UTC (convert local days with the retailer's time zone). If the reply says truncated, call again with offset = next_offset and add the figures up. Uses GET /search?type=sales.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List customers in version order: id, customer_code, name, email, phone, balance, loyalty_balance, year_to_date, customer group. To find one by name or email use search_customers. Paginate with next_after (stop when data is empty). GET /customers.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_search_customers
tools.title: Search customers
tools.description: Find customers by email, first name, last name, company name, phone, mobile or customer code. Uses offset paging: pass next_offset to continue (null = last page). GET /search?type=customers.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_customer
tools.title: Get customer
tools.description: One customer by id: contact details, addresses, customer group, balance, loyalty balance, year-to-date spend. GET /customers/{customer_id}.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_customer_groups
tools.title: List customer groups
tools.description: List customer groups (id, name). Use the id as customer_group_id when creating or updating a customer. Paginate with next_after. GET /customer_groups.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_create_customer
tools.title: Create customer
tools.description: WRITE: create a new customer. Give at least a first name, last name or company name. Check search_customers first so you do not create a duplicate. POST /customers.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_update_customer
tools.title: Update customer
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing customer. Only the fields you pass change: the tool first reads the customer and sends the vendor its full record with your changes applied (the vendor's update is a full PUT). Cannot delete a customer or change balances. Lightspeed offers no partial update for customers, so a change made by someone else in the moments between the tool's read and its write can be overwritten. PUT /customers/{customer_id}.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_update_product_prices
tools.title: Update product prices
tools.description: WRITE: set the selling price of one product (variant). Pass price_excluding_tax or price_including_tax as a decimal string such as "24.99" (set one; the store's tax setting decides which the till uses). Nothing else on the product changes. Read the product first and confirm the new price with the user. PATCH /products/{product_id}.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_set_product_stock
tools.title: Set product stock and reorder levels
tools.description: WRITE: set the stock on hand (current_amount) and/or the reorder point and reorder amount of ONE product at ONE outlet. current_amount is the NEW TOTAL on hand, not a change: it overwrites the count, so sales made since you last read it are lost from the count. Read get_inventory_levels first and confirm the number with the user. Other outlets and all other product fields stay as they are. PATCH /products/{product_id} (outlet_inventories).

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Lightspeed Retail (X-Series) tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Lightspeed Retail (X-Series) (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Lightspeed Retail (X-Series) Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run lightspeedxseries_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: FreeAgent
servers.description: Read FreeAgent contacts, invoices, bills, banking and reports; add contacts, draft invoices, time.

tools.name: freeagent_get_company
tools.title: Get the company
tools.description: Fetch the FreeAgent company these credentials belong to — name, type (e.g. UkLimitedCompany), currency, start date and VAT registration status. A cheap way to confirm the setup works. FreeAgent: GET /v2/company.

tools.name: freeagent_get_current_user
tools.title: Get the current user
tools.description: Fetch the FreeAgent user the token acts as, including their URL (needed for freeagent_create_timeslip) and permission level. FreeAgent: GET /v2/users/me.

tools.name: freeagent_get_tax_timeline
tools.title: Get the tax timeline
tools.description: List upcoming tax deadlines and amounts due — VAT returns, corporation tax, self assessment and so on. FreeAgent: GET /v2/company/tax_timeline.

tools.name: freeagent_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts (clients and suppliers), with their account balance. FreeAgent: GET /v2/contacts.

tools.name: freeagent_get_contact

tools.description: Fetch a single contact by id or URL. FreeAgent: GET /v2/contacts/:id.

tools.name: freeagent_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List sales invoices, optionally for one contact or project, filtered by status. FreeAgent: GET /v2/invoices.

tools.name: freeagent_get_invoice

tools.name: freeagent_list_bills

tools.description: List supplier bills (purchases), optionally by date range, contact or project, filtered by status. FreeAgent: GET /v2/bills.

tools.name: freeagent_list_expenses
tools.title: List expenses
tools.description: List expense claims (out-of-pocket spending and mileage), optionally by date range or project. FreeAgent: GET /v2/expenses.

tools.name: freeagent_list_bank_accounts
tools.title: List bank accounts

tools.name: freeagent_list_bank_transactions

tools.name: freeagent_list_projects

tools.name: freeagent_list_tasks

tools.name: freeagent_list_timeslips

tools.name: freeagent_get_profit_and_loss

tools.name: freeagent_get_balance_sheet

tools.name: freeagent_create_contact

tools.name: freeagent_update_contact

tools.name: freeagent_create_draft_invoice

tools.name: freeagent_create_timeslip

login.hint: This server reads your contacts, invoices, bills, expenses, bank accounts and transactions, projects, timeslips and reports. It can create and update contacts, create draft invoices (never sent) and log timeslips when you ask it to; it never deletes anything. It can do only what your FreeAgent user is allowed to do.
