servers.name: Pirsch Analytics
servers.description: Read Pirsch web analytics: visitors, pages, referrers, UTM, events, funnels and sessions.

login.hint: In Pirsch open **Account Settings** (all your dashboards) or, on a dashboard you own, **Integration Settings**, click **Add Client**, choose the type **oAuth** and turn off every write scope. The secret is shown once. Access keys (pa_...) cannot read statistics. Your credentials are used only to call the Pirsch API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone. The Pirsch API needs a paid Pirsch plan.

tools.name: pirsch_list_domains
tools.title: List domains (dashboards)
tools.description: List the Pirsch dashboards (domains) the OAuth client can read: id, hostname, display name, time zone and role. Use the id as domain_id in every other tool. A dashboard-level client sees one domain; an account-level client sees all. GET /api/v1/domain.

tools.name: pirsch_get_domain
tools.title: Get domain
tools.description: One Pirsch dashboard (domain) by id, with its time zone, hostname, role and subscription state. GET /api/v1/domain?id=.

tools.name: pirsch_get_overview
tools.title: Get overview
tools.description: Quick overview of a dashboard: visitors, views, growth compared with the previous period, a visitors time series and the number of team members. Cached by Pirsch; takes no date range or filters. GET /api/v1/statistics/overview.

tools.name: pirsch_get_totals
tools.title: Get total visitors
tools.description: Totals for a period: visitors, views, sessions, bounces, bounce rate and conversion rate. Not grouped by day, so returning visitors are counted once. GET /api/v1/statistics/total.

tools.name: pirsch_get_visitors_time_series
tools.title: Get visitors time series
tools.description: Visitors, views, sessions, bounces and bounce rate per day, week, month or year (see scale). Use it for traffic charts and trends. GET /api/v1/statistics/visitor.

tools.name: pirsch_get_growth
tools.title: Get growth rates
tools.description: Growth of visitors, views, sessions, bounces, time spent and conversion rate compared with the previous period of the same length. GET /api/v1/statistics/growth.

tools.name: pirsch_get_active_visitors
tools.title: Get active visitors
tools.description: Visitors on the site right now (or in the past n seconds), with the pages they are on and their countries. GET /api/v1/statistics/active.

tools.name: pirsch_get_time_distribution
tools.title: Get visitors by time
tools.description: Visitors by hour of the day, by minute (only when from and to are the same day), or by weekday and hour (Monday is 0). Shows when traffic peaks. GET /api/v1/statistics/hours, /minutes or /weekdays.

tools.name: pirsch_get_duration
tools.title: Get time spent
tools.description: Average session duration over time, or average time on page over time, in seconds. GET /api/v1/statistics/duration/session or /duration/page.

tools.name: pirsch_list_pages
tools.title: List pages
tools.description: Top pages with visitors, views, sessions, bounces, bounce rate and average time on page. type=entry lists landing pages, type=exit lists exit pages. Filters narrow the data (for example country=de, path=~blog). Results are rows with visitors, views, sessions, bounces and relative shares. GET /api/v1/statistics/page, /page/entry or /page/exit.

tools.name: pirsch_list_hostnames
tools.title: List hostnames
tools.description: Traffic per hostname. Mostly useful for rollup views that combine several hostnames. GET /api/v1/statistics/hostname.

tools.name: pirsch_list_referrers
tools.title: List referrers
tools.description: Where visitors come from: referrers (by=referrer) or traffic channels such as Organic Search and Paid Search (by=channel). Filters narrow the data (for example country=de, path=~blog). Results are rows with visitors, views, sessions, bounces and relative shares. GET /api/v1/statistics/referrer or /channel.

tools.name: pirsch_list_utm
tools.title: List UTM parameters
tools.description: Visitors per UTM source, medium, campaign, content or term. Filters narrow the data (for example country=de, path=~blog). Results are rows with visitors, views, sessions, bounces and relative shares. GET /api/v1/statistics/utm/{dimension}.

tools.name: pirsch_list_geography
tools.title: List countries, regions, cities and languages
tools.description: Visitors per country, region, city or language. Filters narrow the data (for example country=de, path=~blog). Results are rows with visitors, views, sessions, bounces and relative shares. GET /api/v1/statistics/country, /region, /city or /language.

tools.name: pirsch_list_devices
tools.title: List browsers, operating systems and screens
tools.description: Visitors per browser, browser version, operating system or screen class (XXL to S). Filters narrow the data (for example country=de, path=~blog). Results are rows with visitors, views, sessions, bounces and relative shares. GET /api/v1/statistics/browser, /browser/version, /os or /screen.

tools.name: pirsch_get_platforms
tools.title: Get platform split
tools.description: Visitors on desktop, mobile and unknown platforms, as counts and shares. GET /api/v1/statistics/platform.

tools.name: pirsch_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: Custom events with count, visitors, views, conversion rate, average duration and their metadata keys. Use pirsch_get_event_breakdown for the values of one metadata key. GET /api/v1/statistics/events.

tools.name: pirsch_get_event_breakdown
tools.title: Get event metadata breakdown
tools.description: The values of one metadata key of one event, with count, visitors and conversion rate. Both event and event_meta_key are required. GET /api/v1/statistics/event/meta.

tools.name: pirsch_list_event_pages
tools.title: List pages of an event
tools.description: The pages on which an event was triggered, with visitors and views. The event name is required. GET /api/v1/statistics/event/page.

tools.name: pirsch_list_goals
tools.title: List conversion goals
tools.description: Conversion goals with their definition (page pattern, event, targets) and the visitors, views and conversion rate for the period. GET /api/v1/statistics/goals.

tools.name: pirsch_list_funnels
tools.title: List funnels
tools.description: The funnels defined for a dashboard, with their steps and step filters. Use a funnel id in pirsch_get_funnel. GET /api/v1/funnel.

tools.name: pirsch_get_funnel
tools.title: Get funnel statistics
tools.description: Visitors per funnel step for a period: visitors, share of the first step, drop-off between steps. The filter applies to the first step. GET /api/v1/statistics/funnel.

tools.name: pirsch_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: Tag keys with views and share. Use pirsch_get_tag_breakdown to see the values of one key. GET /api/v1/statistics/tags.

tools.name: pirsch_get_tag_breakdown
tools.title: Get tag breakdown
tools.description: The values of one tag key with views and share. The tag filter (the key) is required. GET /api/v1/statistics/tag/details.

tools.name: pirsch_list_sessions
tools.title: List sessions
tools.description: Individual visitor sessions: start, duration, entry and exit page, page views, bounce, country, city, referrer, browser, OS and UTM data. visitor_id is a string (a 64-bit number). Use pirsch_get_session for one session's page views and events. GET /api/v1/statistics/session/list.

tools.name: pirsch_get_session
tools.title: Get session details
tools.description: All page views and events of one session in time order. Both ids come from pirsch_list_sessions. GET /api/v1/statistics/session/details.

tools.name: pirsch_list_filter_values
tools.title: List filter values
tools.description: The values that exist for a filter in a period, such as all page paths, referrers, countries, browsers or event names. Use it to find valid values before filtering. GET /api/v1/statistics/options/{dimension}.

Does not count against the meter.

Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: pirsch_cancel_subscription

servers.name: Exoscale
servers.description: Inspect Exoscale: instances, volumes, SKS, DNS, IPs, quotas and usage; start, stop, reboot VMs.

login.hint: In the Exoscale portal open **IAM → API Keys** and create a key. A role limited to read access (it must allow reading the organization) is enough for every tool except start, stop and reboot of instances. The secret is shown only once. Pick the zone where most of your resources live; every tool can still ask for another zone. Your key and secret are used only to sign requests to the Exoscale API on your behalf; the secret is never sent and never shown to anyone.

tools.name: exoscale_list_zones
tools.title: List zones
tools.description: List the Exoscale zones (data centers) with their API and object-storage endpoints. Compute, storage and network resources live in one zone each. GET /zone.

tools.name: exoscale_get_organization
tools.title: Get organization
tools.description: The Exoscale organization of the API key: id, name, address, country, account balance and currency. GET /organization.

tools.name: exoscale_list_quotas
tools.title: List quotas
tools.description: Resource quotas of the organization: for each resource its current usage and limit (instances, volumes, elastic IPs, and so on). GET /quota.

tools.name: exoscale_get_quota
tools.title: Get quota
tools.description: Usage and limit of one quota entity, for example 'instance'. Use exoscale_list_quotas for the names. GET /quota/{entity}.

tools.name: exoscale_get_usage_report
tools.title: Get usage report
tools.description: Aggregated usage of the organization for one month: product, variable, quantity and unit per line. GET /usage-report.

tools.name: exoscale_list_instances
tools.title: List compute instances
tools.description: List the compute instances of one zone: id, name, state, instance type, template, IP addresses and security groups. Call once per zone for a full inventory. GET /instance.

tools.name: exoscale_get_instance
tools.title: Get compute instance
tools.description: Details of one compute instance: state, type, template, disk size, networks, security groups, elastic IPs, snapshots. The cloud-init user-data is never returned. GET /instance/{id}.

tools.name: exoscale_start_instance
tools.title: Start compute instance
tools.description: WRITE: start a stopped compute instance (normal boot, no rescue profile). Billing for the instance resumes. Returns an operation; poll it with exoscale_get_operation. PUT /instance/{id}:start.

tools.name: exoscale_stop_instance
tools.title: Stop compute instance
tools.description: WRITE: stop a running compute instance. Running services go down and the public IP may change unless it is an elastic IP. Returns an operation; poll it with exoscale_get_operation. PUT /instance/{id}:stop.

tools.name: exoscale_reboot_instance
tools.title: Reboot compute instance
tools.description: WRITE: reboot a running compute instance. Running services restart and unsaved data in memory is lost. Returns an operation; poll it with exoscale_get_operation. PUT /instance/{id}:reboot.

tools.name: exoscale_get_operation
tools.title: Get operation
tools.description: State of an asynchronous operation (pending, success, failure, timeout), for example the reply of a start, stop or reboot. Use the same zone as the call that created it. GET /operation/{id}.

tools.name: exoscale_list_instance_types
tools.title: List instance types
tools.description: List the compute instance types: family, size, CPUs, GPUs, memory and the zones that offer them. GET /instance-type.

tools.name: exoscale_get_instance_type
tools.title: Get instance type
tools.description: Details of one instance type: family, size, CPUs, GPUs, memory, zones. GET /instance-type/{id}.

tools.name: exoscale_list_templates
tools.title: List templates
tools.description: List the compute templates (OS images) of a zone: name, family, version, default user, size, visibility. The public list is long: filter by family or page with limit/offset. GET /template.

tools.name: exoscale_get_template
tools.title: Get template
tools.description: Details of one template: name, family, version, default user, size, boot mode, checksum, zones. GET /template/{id}.

tools.name: exoscale_list_security_groups
tools.title: List security groups
tools.description: List the security groups of a zone: id, name, description and external sources (firewall), with the rules when the API includes them. GET /security-group.

tools.name: exoscale_get_security_group
tools.title: Get security group
tools.description: Details of one security group: description and external sources, with the rules (protocol, ports, network, direction) when the API includes them. GET /security-group/{id}.

tools.name: exoscale_list_elastic_ips
tools.title: List elastic IPs
tools.description: List the elastic IP addresses of a zone with description, address family, health-check settings and labels. GET /elastic-ip.

tools.name: exoscale_get_elastic_ip
tools.title: Get elastic IP
tools.description: Details of one elastic IP: address, CIDR, family, description, health check and labels. GET /elastic-ip/{id}.

tools.name: exoscale_list_block_storage_volumes
tools.title: List block storage volumes
tools.description: List the block storage volumes of a zone: name, size, state, the instance each is attached to, encryption and snapshots. GET /block-storage.

tools.name: exoscale_get_block_storage_volume
tools.title: Get block storage volume
tools.description: Details of one block storage volume: size, block size, state, attached instance, encryption, labels and snapshots. GET /block-storage/{id}.

tools.name: exoscale_list_sks_clusters
tools.title: List SKS clusters
tools.description: List the Scalable Kubernetes Service (SKS) clusters of a zone: name, version, state, level, CNI, endpoint and node pools. GET /sks-cluster.

tools.name: exoscale_get_sks_cluster
tools.title: Get SKS cluster
tools.description: Details of one SKS cluster: version, state, level, CNI, add-ons, OIDC settings (no secrets), endpoint and node pools. GET /sks-cluster/{id}.

tools.name: exoscale_list_dns_domains
tools.title: List DNS domains
tools.description: List the DNS domains (zones) hosted at Exoscale: id, unicode name, creation date. DNS is the same in every zone. GET /dns-domain.

tools.name: exoscale_get_dns_domain
tools.title: Get DNS domain
tools.description: Details of one DNS domain. GET /dns-domain/{id}.

tools.name: exoscale_list_dns_records
tools.title: List DNS records
tools.description: List the records of one DNS domain: name, type, content, TTL, priority. Use exoscale_list_dns_domains for the domain id. GET /dns-domain/{domain-id}/record.

tools.name: exoscale_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: exoscale_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Exoscale tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: exoscale_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Exoscale (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: exoscale_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Exoscale Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run exoscale_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which of my cloud instances are running in the Frankfurt zone?
How close am I to my cloud instance quota and my other resource limits?
What was my cloud usage for last month, broken down by product?
Which DNS records do I have for my domain acme-example.com?

servers.name: Pipeline CRM
servers.description: Manage Pipeline CRM deals, people, companies, notes and calendar entries.

fields.label: App key — only with a legacy api_key

login.hint: Create the token in Pipeline CRM under your **profile → API tokens** (an account admin may first need to grant you access). Choose Read only if you only need reports. With an older **api_key** (Admin → API Keys), also enter the **app key** from Admin → API Integrations; with an API token, leave the app key empty. Your credentials are used only to call the Pipeline CRM API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_get_profile
tools.title: Get my profile
tools.description: The Pipeline CRM user this credential acts as: id, name and whether they are an account admin. The user's api_key is never returned. GET /profile.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_users
tools.title: List users

tools.name: pipelinecrm_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: One user of the account by id. The user's api_key is never returned. GET /users/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_deals
tools.title: List deals
tools.description: List or search deals with stage, owner, company, primary contact, value, probability and expected close date. Filter by name, stage, pipeline, status, owner, company, contact, archived flag, value range and created, expected-close, closed or modified dates. Money values come back as decimal strings. GET /deals.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_get_deal
tools.title: Get deal
tools.description: One deal by id with owner, company, people, stage, status, loss/won reasons, tags, custom fields and the next task. GET /deals/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_deal_totals_by_stage
tools.title: Deal totals by stage
tools.description: Count and total value of the deals visible to the user in every deal stage: the pipeline summary. GET /deals/totals_by_stage.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_deal_notes
tools.title: List notes on a deal
tools.description: List the notes (activities) logged on one deal, with author, category and content. GET /deals/{id}/notes.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_create_deal
tools.title: Create deal
tools.description: WRITE: create a deal. Give the owner (user id), stage id, value, expected close date and company or primary contact when known; a new company is created from company_name if no company_id is given. No email is sent to the owner. POST /deals.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_update_deal
tools.title: Update deal
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of a deal; only the fields you pass change. Move it to another stage with stage_id. Setting probability to 100 or 0 closes the deal as won or lost; give won/loss reason ids when you do. Archive with archived: true. No email is sent to a new owner. PUT /deals/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_people
tools.title: List people (leads and contacts)
tools.description: List or search people (leads and contacts) with email, phones, position, company, owner, lead status and tags. Use search for a quick match on name, email or company name, or filter precisely. GET /people.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_get_person
tools.title: Get person
tools.description: One person (lead or contact) by id with all contact details, company, owner, tags and custom fields. GET /people/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_person_deals
tools.title: List deals of a person
tools.description: List the deals one person is associated with. GET /people/{id}/deals.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_person_notes
tools.title: List notes on a person
tools.description: List the notes (activities) logged on one person. GET /people/{id}/notes.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_create_person
tools.title: Create person
tools.description: WRITE: create a lead or contact. Pass at least a first or last name or an email. No email is sent to the owner. POST /people.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_update_person
tools.title: Update person
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of a person; only the fields you pass change. Pass type Contact to convert a lead. PUT /people/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_companies
tools.title: List companies
tools.description: List or search companies with address, website, phones, owner, tags and pipeline totals. GET /companies.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_get_company
tools.title: Get company
tools.description: One company by id with address, phones, website, owner, tags and custom fields. GET /companies/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_company_people
tools.title: List people at a company
tools.description: List the people (leads and contacts) who work at one company. GET /companies/{id}/people.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_create_company
tools.title: Create company
tools.description: WRITE: create a company. POST /companies.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_update_company
tools.title: Update company
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of a company; only the fields you pass change. PUT /companies/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_notes
tools.title: List notes
tools.description: List notes (called activities in the Pipeline CRM app) attached to a deal, person or company. Pass at least one of deal_id, person_id, company_id. Filter by text, category, author and created date. GET /notes.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_get_note
tools.title: Get note
tools.description: One note (activity) by id with its content, author, category, associations and comments. GET /notes/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_add_note
tools.title: Add note
tools.description: WRITE: log a note (activity) on a deal, person or company. Pass at least one of deal_id, person_id, company_id. POST /notes.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_calendar_entries
tools.title: List tasks and events
tools.description: List calendar entries: tasks (a due date) and events (a start and end time) tied to deals, people or companies. Filter by kind, owner, a date range, and completed, incomplete or late. GET /calendar_entries.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_get_calendar_entry
tools.title: Get task or event
tools.description: One calendar entry (task or event) by id. GET /calendar_entries/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_create_calendar_entry
tools.title: Create task or event
tools.description: WRITE: create a task (CalendarTask, optional due date) or an event (CalendarEvent, start_time and end_time required), optionally tied to a deal, person or company. POST /calendar_entries.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_update_calendar_entry
tools.title: Update task or event
tools.description: WRITE: change a task or event; only the fields you pass change. Pass complete: true to mark a task done. PUT /calendar_entries/{id}.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_deal_stages
tools.title: List deal stages
tools.description: List the deal stages with id, name, default win probability and the pipeline each belongs to. Use the ids to filter or move deals. GET /admin/deal_stages.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_deal_pipelines
tools.title: List deal pipelines
tools.description: List the deal pipelines (each has its own stages) with id, name and which one is the default. GET /admin/deal_pipelines.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_list_lookup
tools.title: List lookup values
tools.description: List one set of account lookup values to get ids for filters and writes. kind: deal_statuses, deal_loss_reasons, deal_won_reasons, deal_tags, lead_statuses, lead_sources, contact_tags, company_tags, note_categories, event_categories, task_priorities, task_statuses, teams. GET /admin/<kind>.

Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: pipelinecrm_cancel_subscription

examples: How many deals do I have in each stage and what is their total value?
Show my open deals expected to close this month.
Find the contact Jane Smith and show her notes.

tools.name: homebase_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List the locations (stores or sites) of the account with uuid, name, address, phone, website and time zone. The uuid is the id every other Homebase tool needs. GET /locations.

tools.name: homebase_get_location
tools.title: Get location
tools.description: One location by uuid: name, address, phone, website, time zone and POS merchant id. GET /locations/{location_uuid}.

tools.name: homebase_get_location_plan
tools.title: Get location plan
tools.description: The Homebase subscription plan of a location: plan number, price, last update and trial state. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/plan.

tools.name: homebase_list_employees
tools.title: List employees
tools.description: List the employees of a location with contact details and their job: level, default role, additional roles, wage type and rate, payroll id and archive date. The time-clock PIN is never returned. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/employees.

tools.name: homebase_get_employee
tools.title: Get employee
tools.description: One employee of a location by user id, with contact details and job (role, wage type and rate, payroll id). The id is the job's user id from homebase_list_employees. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/employees/{id}.

tools.name: homebase_list_shifts
tools.title: List shifts
tools.description: List the scheduled shifts of a location in a date range: employee, role, department, start and end, published/open state, wage rate and scheduled labor hours (regular, overtime). Filter open shifts only. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/shifts.

tools.name: homebase_get_shift
tools.title: Get shift
tools.description: One shift of a location by id, with its labor data and optional note. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/shifts/{id}.

tools.name: homebase_list_deleted_shifts
tools.title: List deleted shifts
tools.description: The ids of shifts deleted in a date range at a location, with their start, end and deletion time. Use it to keep a copy of the schedule in sync. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/shifts/deleted.

tools.name: homebase_list_timecards
tools.title: List timecards
tools.description: List the timecards (worked time) of a location in a date range: employee, role, clock in and out, breaks, hours, labor cost, tips and approval state. Time-off hours are always 0 on timecards; use homebase_get_labor_by_employee for totals with time off. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/timecards.

tools.name: homebase_get_timecard
tools.title: Get timecard
tools.description: One timecard of a location by id: clock in and out, breaks, labor hours and cost, tips, approval state. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/timecards/{id}.

tools.name: homebase_list_deleted_timecards
tools.title: List deleted timecards
tools.description: The ids of timecards deleted in a date range at a location, with clock in, clock out and deletion time. Use it to keep a copy of the timecards in sync. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/timecards/deleted.

tools.name: homebase_get_labor
tools.title: Get labor report
tools.description: Aggregate labor for a location in a date range, grouped by day or by hour: regular, overtime and paid hours, labor cost, tips, breaks and time off. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/labor.

tools.name: homebase_get_labor_by_role
tools.title: Get labor report by role
tools.description: Aggregate labor (hours, cost, tips, overtime) for a location in a date range, grouped by role. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/labor/by_role.

tools.name: homebase_get_labor_by_employee
tools.title: Get labor report by employee
tools.description: Aggregate labor (hours, cost, wage rate, tips, overtime, time off) for a location in a date range, grouped by employee. Use it for payroll totals. GET /locations/{location_uuid}/labor/by_employee.

tools.name: homebase_get_timeclock_status
tools.title: Get time clock status
tools.description: The current time-clock state of one job (employee at a location): clocked_in, on_break or clocked_out, the current shift, the shifts that can be clocked into and the breaks that can be started. The job id is the `job.id` of an employee from homebase_list_employees. GET /timeclock/status.

tools.name: homebase_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: homebase_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Homebase tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: homebase_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Homebase (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: homebase_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Homebase Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run homebase_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Who is scheduled to work at my main location this week?
What was my total labor cost last week at my main location, by day?
Who is clocked in right now at my store?
Show total hours worked by each employee last week.

servers.name: Benchmark Email
servers.description: Manage Benchmark Email lists and contacts, and read campaign reports: opens, clicks, bounces.

login.hint: Find it in Benchmark Email under **Integrations** ([ui.benchmarkemail.com/Integrate](https://ui.benchmarkemail.com/Integrate#AP)) in the **API** tab. Any account type, including the free plan, has an API token. The token acts as the account owner; it is used only to call the Benchmark Email API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: benchmark_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The Benchmark Email account this token belongs to: client id, name, company, email, status, plan products, contact count and emails sent. GET /Client/ProfileDetails.

tools.name: benchmark_get_plan
tools.title: Get plan and usage
tools.description: The account's email plan, add-ons and contact usage (active, account and total contacts, percent used). GET /Client/Plan.

tools.name: benchmark_get_settings
tools.title: Get account settings
tools.description: Default sender settings: from name and email, signature, footer, time zone, language and company address. The API token in the reply is removed. GET /Client/Setting.

tools.name: benchmark_list_lists
tools.title: List contact lists
tools.description: List contact lists with id, name, description, contact count and dates. Use the ids with the contact tools. GET /Contact/.

tools.name: benchmark_get_list
tools.title: Get contact list
tools.description: One contact list: name, description, active contact count and its custom field names (Field1Name ...). GET /Contact/{list_id}.

tools.name: benchmark_get_list_fields
tools.title: Get contact list fields
tools.description: The column names of a contact list (email, firstname, lastname and the custom fields). GET /Contact/{list_id}/Fields.

tools.name: benchmark_create_list
tools.title: Create contact list
tools.description: WRITE: create an empty contact list. POST /Contact/.

tools.name: benchmark_list_segments
tools.title: List segments
tools.description: List the saved segments (filtered subsets of lists) with id and name. GET /Contact/Segments.

tools.name: benchmark_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts in a list
tools.description: List the contacts of one list with email, name, dates and id. Filter by status (subscribed, unsubscribed, hard_bounced) or search a column. GET /Contact/{list_id}/ContactDetails.

tools.name: benchmark_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact of a list with all its fields (Field1 ... Field24 hold the custom columns). GET /Contact/{list_id}/ContactDetails/{contact_id}.

tools.name: benchmark_search_contacts
tools.title: Search contacts by email
tools.description: Find an email address across all lists: one row per list it is on, with the list name, contact id and master-unsubscribe flag. GET /Contact/ContactDetails.

tools.name: benchmark_add_contact
tools.title: Add contact to a list
tools.description: WRITE: add one contact to a list (or update it if the email is already there, as the vendor decides). It does not send any email. Only add people who agreed to get email. POST /Contact/{list_id}/ContactDetails.

tools.name: benchmark_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of one contact in one list. Only the fields you pass are sent. PATCH /Contact/{list_id}/ContactDetails/{contact_id}.

tools.name: benchmark_unsubscribe_contact
tools.title: Unsubscribe contact
tools.description: WRITE: move a contact to the Do Not Contact (master unsubscribe) list, so no campaign reaches it again. The API has no undo for this. DELETE /Contact/{list_id}/MoveToDNC/{contact_id}.

tools.name: benchmark_list_emails
tools.title: List emails (campaigns)
tools.description: List email campaigns with id, name, subject, type, status, dates and target lists. GET /Emails/.

tools.name: benchmark_get_email
tools.title: Get email (campaign)
tools.description: One email campaign: subject, sender, target and excluded lists, dates and settings. GET /Emails/{email_id}.

tools.name: benchmark_list_email_reports
tools.title: List email report summaries
tools.description: Report summaries of sent emails: sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes and complaints per campaign. GET /Emails/Report.

tools.name: benchmark_get_email_report
tools.title: Get email report
tools.description: The report summary of one email: recipients, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, forwards, complaints and rates. GET /Emails/{email_id}/Report.

tools.name: benchmark_get_email_opens
tools.title: Get email opens
tools.description: Who opened an email: contact, email address, time and device. GET /Emails/{email_id}/Report/Opens.

tools.name: benchmark_get_email_clicks
tools.title: Get email clicks
tools.description: Who clicked a link in an email: contact, email address and time. GET /Emails/{email_id}/Report/Clicks.

tools.name: benchmark_get_email_bounces
tools.title: Get email bounces
tools.description: Which addresses bounced for an email: contact, email address, time and bounce type. GET /Emails/{email_id}/Report/Bounces.

tools.name: benchmark_get_email_unsubscribes
tools.title: Get email unsubscribes
tools.description: Who unsubscribed after an email: contact, email address, time and reason, with a count per reason. GET /Emails/{email_id}/Report/Unsubscribes.

tools.name: benchmark_list_signup_forms
tools.title: List signup forms
tools.description: List signup forms with id, name, date and the lists they feed. GET /SignupForm/.

tools.name: benchmark_get_signup_form
tools.title: Get signup form
tools.description: One signup form with its settings and target lists. GET /SignupForm/{form_id}.

tools.name: benchmark_get_signup_form_link
tools.title: Get signup form link
tools.description: The public link of a signup form. GET /SignupForm/{form_id}/Link.

tools.name: benchmark_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: benchmark_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Benchmark Email (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: benchmark_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Benchmark Email Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run benchmark_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: How many contacts do I have on each email list?
How did my last email campaign do for opens and clicks?
Which email addresses bounced on my latest campaign?
Add jane.smith@example.com to my Newsletter list.

servers.name: eDesk
servers.description: Work with eDesk support tickets, replies, internal notes, contacts and sales orders.

login.hint: Create it at **dashboard.edesk.com/api-token**. The eDesk API is part of the Enterprise plan. The token acts with the permissions of the user who created it. Your token is used only to call the eDesk API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: edesk_whoami
tools.title: Who am I
tools.description: The eDesk user the API token belongs to: id, name, email, username, role and active flag. GET /whoami.

tools.name: edesk_list_users
tools.title: List users (agents)
tools.description: List the eDesk users (support agents) with id, name, email, username, role and active flag. Use the ids as ticket owners. GET /users.

tools.name: edesk_list_channels
tools.title: List channels
tools.description: List the sales channels connected to eDesk (Amazon, eBay, Shopify, email, ...) with id, type, name, country and currency. Use the ids to filter tickets and orders. GET /channels.

tools.name: edesk_list_tag_groups
tools.title: List tag groups
tools.description: List the tag groups that organize ticket tags. GET /tag-groups.

tools.name: edesk_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: List ticket tags with id, name, color, active flag and tag group id. Use the ids in edesk_update_ticket (tag_ids). GET /tags.

tools.name: edesk_list_templates
tools.title: List reply templates
tools.description: List saved reply templates (id, name, subject, body text, channels, usage). GET /templates.

tools.name: edesk_get_template
tools.title: Get reply template
tools.description: One reply template by id. GET /templates/{id}.

tools.name: edesk_list_tickets
tools.title: List tickets
tools.description: List support tickets from all channels with subject, type, status, channel, owner, contact, linked sales order id, tag ids, message ids, reply count and AI classification. Filter by status, type, channel, contact, owner, sales order, seller (marketplace) order id and last-updated date. GET /tickets.

tools.name: edesk_get_ticket
tools.title: Get ticket
tools.description: One ticket by id with its status, owner, tags, custom fields, linked sales order and the ids of its messages (read each with edesk_get_message). GET /tickets/{id}.

tools.name: edesk_get_message
tools.title: Get message
tools.description: One ticket message or internal note by id (from a ticket's message ids): body, direction, type (Message or Note), author and attachments. GET /messages/{id}.

tools.name: edesk_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: Search the contacts (customers) of the helpdesk by free text, email, name, phone number or consumer id. Returns id, channel, full name, email and phone. GET /contacts.

tools.name: edesk_list_sales_orders
tools.title: List sales orders
tools.description: List the marketplace/store orders that eDesk holds, with status, items, amounts, addresses, tracking codes and the linked ticket id. Filter by status, channel, contact, marketplace order id, id range and created/updated dates. GET /sales-orders.

tools.name: edesk_get_sales_order
tools.title: Get sales order
tools.description: One sales order by id with items, amounts, ship-to and bill-to addresses, tracking codes, delivery dates, the linked ticket id and order note ids. GET /sales-orders/{id}.

tools.name: edesk_list_order_notes
tools.title: List order notes
tools.description: List the internal notes attached to sales orders (id, sales order id, author, text, attachments). GET /order-notes.

tools.name: edesk_update_ticket
tools.title: Update ticket
tools.description: WRITE: change a ticket's status, owner (assignee), tags or subject. Only the fields you pass are sent. tag_ids is sent as given: read the ticket first (tags_ids) and include the tags to keep. Nothing is sent to the customer. PUT /tickets/{id}.

tools.name: edesk_add_ticket_note
tools.title: Add internal ticket note
tools.description: WRITE: add an internal note to a ticket. The note is for the team only and is never sent to the customer. POST /messages with type Note.

tools.name: edesk_reply_to_ticket
tools.title: Reply to customer
tools.description: WRITE, CUSTOMER-VISIBLE: send a reply on a ticket. eDesk queues it for delivery to the marketplace or email channel, so it cannot be recalled once queued. The audience is the channel's default: on a Mirakl channel it is the channel's "Default messages recipients" setting (customer, operator or both), and this API cannot choose recipients (use the eDesk reply box when they matter). Only call this when the user has approved the exact text and audience. If the call fails in transit, the reply may still be queued: check the ticket before retrying. Use edesk_add_ticket_note for an internal note. POST /messages with type Message.

tools.name: edesk_add_order_note
tools.title: Add order note
tools.description: WRITE: add an internal note to a sales order (never sent to the customer). POST /order-notes.

tools.name: edesk_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: edesk_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the eDesk tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: edesk_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on eDesk (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: edesk_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's eDesk Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run edesk_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: List open support tickets and the owner assigned to each one.
What are the latest tickets from my marketplace channels about?
Find the order for customer Jane Smith and tell me its tracking code.
Add an internal note on Jane Smith's latest ticket saying the refund was approved.

servers.name: Encharge
servers.description: Manage Encharge people, tags, segments and fields, and track events for email automation.

login.hint: Find the API key and the write key in Encharge → **Account → Account info**. The API key needs a plan with API access. The write key is optional: only the event tracking tool uses it. Your keys are used only to call the Encharge API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: encharge_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The Encharge account behind the API key: account id, name, site, status, timezone, people count and active services. GET /accounts/info.

tools.name: encharge_get_people
tools.title: Get people
tools.description: Look up people (contacts) by email, userId or Encharge id. Pass up to 20 people, each with at least one identifier. Returns each person with all fields, tags and segment data; a person that does not exist is left out. GET /people.

tools.name: encharge_list_segment_people
tools.title: List people in a segment
tools.description: People in one dynamic segment, with paging (limit/offset), optional sort and a choice of person fields (attributes). Use encharge_list_segments for segment ids and encharge_list_fields for field names. GET /segments/{segmentId}/people.

tools.name: encharge_upsert_person
tools.title: Create or update a person
tools.description: WRITE: create a person, or update the one that already has this email, userId or Encharge id. Only the fields you pass are set. Use encharge_add_tags for tags. POST /people.

tools.name: encharge_unsubscribe_person
tools.title: Unsubscribe a person
tools.description: WRITE: unsubscribe one person so Encharge sends them no more email. The person stays in Encharge. Identify them by email, userId or Encharge id. POST /people/unsubscribe.

tools.name: encharge_add_tags
tools.title: Add tags to a person
tools.description: WRITE: add one or more tags to an existing person. Tags that do not exist yet are created. POST /tags.

tools.name: encharge_remove_tags
tools.title: Remove tags from a person
tools.description: WRITE: remove one or more tags from an existing person. The tags themselves are not deleted. DELETE /tags.

tools.name: encharge_list_segments
tools.title: List segments
tools.description: List the dynamic segments of the account with id, name and conditions. Use the ids with encharge_list_segment_people. GET /segments.

tools.name: encharge_list_fields
tools.title: List person fields
tools.description: List all person fields (built-in and custom) with name, title, type and whether the field is read-only. Use the names in encharge_upsert_person. GET /fields.

tools.name: encharge_track_event
tools.title: Track an event
tools.description: WRITE: record an event for a person through the Ingest API, for example "Registered user" or "Created Page". The person is created or updated from `user`. Use the event name "identify" to only create or update a person. Needs the account write key. POST https://ingest.encharge.io/v1/.

tools.name: encharge_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: encharge_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Encharge tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: encharge_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Encharge (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: encharge_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Encharge Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). examples: Look up jane@acme.com and tell me which tags she has.
Which segments do we have set up and what are their conditions?
List all the custom fields we collect about our contacts.
Add the tag webinar-attendee to john@acme.com.

servers.name: Sendlane
servers.description: Manage Sendlane lists, contacts, tags and custom fields; read campaign and SMS reports.

login.hint: In Sendlane open the **API** section, choose **Generate a v2 access token** and copy it (it is shown once). Your token is used only to call the Sendlane API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: sendlane_list_lists
tools.title: List lists
tools.description: List the audience lists of the account: id, name, description, status, created date. GET /lists.

tools.name: sendlane_get_list
tools.title: Get list
tools.description: One audience list by id. GET /lists/{listId}.

tools.name: sendlane_list_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts of a list
tools.description: Contacts on one list: email, name, phone, subscribed/suppressed state, tags, custom fields, lifetime value. GET /lists/{listId}/contacts.

tools.name: sendlane_list_list_unsubscribed
tools.title: List unsubscribed contacts of a list
tools.description: Contacts that unsubscribed from one list. GET /lists/{listId}/unsubscribed.

tools.name: sendlane_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: All contacts of the account: email, name, phone, lists, tags, custom fields, subscribed/suppressed state. Filter by creation time with from/to. GET /contacts.

tools.name: sendlane_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact by id, with lists, tags, custom fields, consent, lifetime value and subscribed/suppressed state. GET /contacts/{contactId}.

tools.name: sendlane_list_unsubscribed_contacts
tools.title: List unsubscribed contacts
tools.description: Contacts that unsubscribed from the account. GET /contacts/unsubscribed.

tools.name: sendlane_get_contact_subscriptions
tools.title: Get contact subscriptions
tools.description: The list subscriptions of one contact: list, subscribed/suppressed state, who added it and when. GET /contacts/{contactId}/subscriptions.

tools.name: sendlane_get_contact_tags
tools.title: Get contact tags
tools.description: The tags on one contact. GET /contacts/{contactId}/tags.

tools.name: sendlane_get_contact_custom_fields
tools.title: Get contact custom fields
tools.description: The custom field values of one contact. GET /contacts/{contactId}/custom-fields.

tools.name: sendlane_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: The contact tags of the account: id, name, audience count. GET /tags.

tools.name: sendlane_get_tag
tools.title: Get tag
tools.description: One tag by id. GET /tags/{tagId}.

tools.name: sendlane_list_tag_contacts
tools.title: List contacts with a tag
tools.description: Contacts that carry one tag. GET /tags/{tagId}/contacts.

tools.name: sendlane_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List custom fields
tools.description: The custom contact fields of the account: id, name, type. Use the ids when setting field values. GET /custom-fields.

tools.name: sendlane_list_segments
tools.title: List segments
tools.description: The segments of the account: id, name, list, match rule, last count. GET /segments.

tools.name: sendlane_list_segment_contacts
tools.title: List contacts of a segment
tools.description: Contacts in one segment: id, email, name, phone. GET /segments/{segmentId}/contacts.

tools.name: sendlane_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: Email campaigns: id, name, status, scheduled and sent time, automation. GET /campaigns.

tools.name: sendlane_get_campaign
tools.title: Get campaign
tools.description: One email campaign by id. GET /campaigns/{campaignId}.

tools.name: sendlane_get_campaign_report
tools.title: Get campaign report
tools.description: Statistics of one email campaign: sent, opens, clicks (unique too), bounced, suppressed, unsubscribed, spam, revenue. from/to limit the period. GET /campaigns/{campaignId}/report.

tools.name: sendlane_list_sms_messages
tools.title: List SMS messages
tools.description: SMS messages (campaign and automation): id, name, campaign status, automation. GET /sms-messages.

tools.name: sendlane_get_sms_report
tools.title: Get SMS report
tools.description: Statistics of one SMS message: sent, delivered, clicks, failed, replies, unsubscribed, credits, revenue. from/to limit the period. GET /sms-messages/{messageId}/report.

tools.name: sendlane_list_sender_profiles
tools.title: List sender profiles
tools.description: The sender profiles (from name, from/reply email, postal address, default flag). GET /senders.

tools.name: sendlane_create_list
tools.title: Create list
tools.description: WRITE: create an audience list. Not idempotent: calling it twice makes two lists. POST /lists.

tools.name: sendlane_update_list
tools.title: Update list
tools.description: WRITE: rename a list and/or change its description (a full update: name is required, an omitted description may be cleared). PUT /lists/{listId}.

tools.name: sendlane_add_contacts_to_list
tools.title: Add contacts to a list
tools.description: WRITE: add one or more contacts (up to 100) to a list; a contact that does not exist is created. Each needs an email or a phone. Sendlane accepts the request for processing (HTTP 202). Only add people who agreed to receive marketing. POST /lists/{listId}/contacts.

tools.name: sendlane_remove_contact_from_list
tools.title: Remove a contact from a list
tools.description: WRITE: remove one contact from one list (the contact stays in the account). DELETE /lists/{listId}/contacts/{contactId}.

tools.name: sendlane_unsubscribe_contact
tools.title: Unsubscribe a contact
tools.description: WRITE: unsubscribe one contact from email marketing. The contact stops receiving campaigns. POST /contacts/{contactId}/unsubscribe.

tools.name: sendlane_create_tag
tools.title: Create tag
tools.description: WRITE: create a contact tag. POST /tags.

tools.name: sendlane_add_contact_tags
tools.title: Tag a contact
tools.description: WRITE: put one or more existing tags on a contact. POST /contacts/{contactId}/tags.

tools.name: sendlane_remove_contact_tag
tools.title: Untag a contact
tools.description: WRITE: remove one tag from a contact (the tag itself is kept). DELETE /contacts/{contactId}/tags/{tagId}.

tools.name: sendlane_set_contact_custom_fields
tools.title: Set contact custom fields
tools.description: WRITE: add custom field values to a contact. Field ids come from sendlane_list_custom_fields. POST /contacts/{contactId}/custom-fields.

tools.name: sendlane_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sendlane_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Sendlane tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sendlane_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Sendlane (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sendlane_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Sendlane Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run sendlane_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Show opens, clicks and unsubscribes for email campaign ID 1042.
Which contacts joined my newsletter list in the last 7 days?
Who unsubscribed from my main list recently?
Which tags do we have and how many contacts carry each one?

servers.name: Simple Analytics
servers.description: Read Simple Analytics stats: pageviews, visitors, pages, referrers, events and data exports.

login.hint: Find both in Simple Analytics → **Account settings**: the key starts with `sa_api_key_`, the user id with `sa_user_id_`. They are used only to call the Simple Analytics API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone. Your plan must include API access.

tools.name: simpleanalytics_list_websites
tools.title: List websites
tools.description: List the websites of the Simple Analytics account (hostnames to use in the other tools). Good first call. Admin API: GET /api/websites.

tools.name: simpleanalytics_get_stats
tools.title: Get traffic summary
tools.description: Aggregated traffic for one website and date range: total pageviews, unique visitors and the median seconds on page. Optional filters narrow it to a page, country, referrer, UTM value, browser, OS, device or metadata value. Stats API: GET /<hostname>.json.

tools.name: simpleanalytics_get_timeseries
tools.title: Get traffic over time
tools.description: Pageviews and visitors per hour, day, week, month or year for one website and date range (time series for charts and trends). Optional filters as in simpleanalytics_get_stats. Stats API: GET /<hostname>.json?fields=histogram.

tools.name: simpleanalytics_get_breakdown
tools.title: Get top pages, referrers, countries or devices
tools.description: Top values of one dimension for one website and date range, each with pageviews and visitors: pages, countries, referrers, UTM sources/mediums/campaigns/contents/terms, browsers, operating systems or device types. Optional filters as in simpleanalytics_get_stats. Stats API: GET /<hostname>.json?fields=<dimension>.

tools.name: simpleanalytics_get_events
tools.title: Get event counts
tools.description: How often custom events happened on one website in a date range. Pass event names, or leave names out for all events (up to 1000). Stats API: GET /<hostname>.json?events=...

tools.name: simpleanalytics_export_datapoints
tools.title: Export raw data points
tools.description: Raw, unsampled page views or events of one website for a date range, as rows with only the fields asked for. The reply is capped at max_rows (default 100, max 1000) rows and 2 MB; "truncated" says more exist, so narrow the range. Rows are cut to about 40 000 characters of JSON. Dates: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH for one hour (start and end the same day). Robots are left out unless asked. Needs the user id too. Export API: GET /api/export/datapoints.

Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: simpleanalytics_cancel_subscription

servers.name: Hint Health
servers.description: Read Hint Health patients, memberships, plans, invoices and payments for direct primary care.

login.hint: In Hint go to **Admin → Developers → API Keys** and create a key (live keys stay locked until your practice signs Hint's API Access Agreement; the sandbox panel on the same page creates sandbox keys). A key works only in the environment where it was created: pick **Production** for your live practice and **Sandbox** for a key from the sandbox panel. Your key is used only to call the Hint API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: hinthealth_get_practice
tools.title: Get practice
tools.description: The practice this API key belongs to: id, name, address, email, phones, website and logo. GET /provider/practice.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List the practice's locations with address, phone, virtual flag and location group. Optionally search near a postal code. GET /provider/locations.

tools.name: hinthealth_get_location
tools.title: Get location
tools.description: One location by id (for example loc-ab12C345DeF6). GET /provider/locations/{id}.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_practitioners
tools.title: List practitioners
tools.description: List the practice's practitioners with bio, NPI, specialties, panel size and limit, enrollment settings and locations. Optionally search near a postal code. GET /provider/practitioners.

tools.name: hinthealth_get_practitioner
tools.title: Get practitioner
tools.description: One practitioner by id. GET /provider/practitioners/{id}.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_patients
tools.title: List patients
tools.description: List patients (protected health information) one page at a time: name, date of birth, contact, address, membership status, autopay, past-due balance, practitioner and location. Archived patients are left out unless archived is true. The Social Security number is never returned. There is no bulk export: page with limit and offset. GET /provider/patients.

tools.name: hinthealth_get_patient
tools.title: Get patient
tools.description: One patient by id (for example pat-ab12C345DeF6), protected health information: identity, contact, address, insurance, consents, memberships, sponsorships, emergency contact. The Social Security number is never returned. GET /provider/patients/{id}.

tools.name: hinthealth_match_patients
tools.title: Find patients by name
tools.description: Find existing patients that match a first and last name, optionally narrowed by email, date of birth or middle name. Reads only: nothing is created. Use it to look a patient up by name. POST /provider/patients/matching.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_patient_credits
tools.title: List patient credits
tools.description: List a patient's account credits: amount, remaining balance, category and reason. GET /provider/patients/{patient_id}/credits.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_memberships
tools.title: List memberships
tools.description: List memberships: status, enrollment status, dates, rates in cents, plan, coupon, owner, member patients and upcoming bills. Filter by created or updated time (ISO 8601). GET /provider/memberships.

tools.name: hinthealth_get_membership
tools.title: Get membership
tools.description: One membership by id: plan, rates, dates, owner, member patients, cancellation and upcoming bills. GET /provider/memberships/{id}.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_plans
tools.title: List plans
tools.description: List the practice's membership plans (id, name, type: company, retail or sponsor_fixed_fee). GET /provider/plans.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_coupons
tools.title: List coupons
tools.description: List membership coupons: code, discount (cents or percent), duration, redeemable window and archive state. GET /provider/coupons.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_charge_items
tools.title: List charge items
tools.description: List the practice's charge item catalog (the services and products a charge is made of): code, name, price in cents, category, stock. GET /provider/charge_items.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List customer invoices (what patients are billed) with number, date, status, amounts in cents (total, due, paid), charges, location and owner. Filter by owner patient, location, status or created/updated time. GET /provider/customer_invoices.

tools.name: hinthealth_get_invoice
tools.title: Get invoice
tools.description: One customer invoice by id with its charges, location, owner, amounts in cents and payment status. GET /provider/customer_invoices/{id}.

tools.name: hinthealth_list_invoice_payments
tools.title: List invoice payments
tools.description: List the payments made on one customer invoice: amount in cents, date, status, error message, memo, source and whether it was recorded outside Hint. GET /provider/customer_invoices/{id}/payments.

tools.name: hinthealth_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: hinthealth_request_feature

tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Hint Health tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. tools.name: hinthealth_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Hint Health (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: hinthealth_cancel_subscription

tools.description: Cancel the caller's Hint Health Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). examples: How many active memberships do we have and on which plans?
Which invoices are still unpaid this month?

List all our membership plans and any active coupons.

servers.name: Elation Health
servers.description: Read Elation Health patients, appointments, problems, allergies, medications, notes and vitals.

login.hint: A practice admin creates the key pair in Elation → **Settings → API Access** (choose **Elation APIv2**, not FHIR) and can narrow its scopes to read-only. Sandbox keys only work with Sandbox, production keys only with Production. Your credentials are used only to call the Elation API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_patients
tools.title: List patients
tools.description: Search the practice's patient charts (PHI): id, name, date of birth, sex, contact details, address, status. First and last name match exactly (case-insensitive, no partial names). The SSN is redacted. Elation: GET /patients/.

tools.name: elationhealth_get_patient
tools.title: Get a patient
tools.description: Get one patient chart header by id (PHI): demographics, contact details, address, insurance, emergency contact, primary physician, tags. The SSN is redacted. Elation: GET /patients/{id}/.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_appointments
tools.title: List appointments
tools.description: List appointments and calendar time slots, filterable by date range, patient, physician and practice. Each has the scheduled date, duration, status, reason, patient, physician and service location. Elation: GET /appointments/.

tools.name: elationhealth_get_appointment
tools.title: Get an appointment
tools.description: Get one appointment by id: scheduled date, duration, status, reason, instructions, patient, physician, practice, service location, telehealth and billing details. Elation: GET /appointments/{id}/.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_appointment_types
tools.title: List appointment types
tools.description: List the appointment types (visit reasons with default duration) a practice offers. Elation: GET /appointment_types/.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_practices
tools.title: List practices
tools.description: List the practices this API key can access: id, name, address, status, time zone, physicians and service locations. Elation: GET /practices/.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_physicians
tools.title: List physicians
tools.description: List the practice's physicians (providers): id, name, NPI, specialty, credentials, license, practice, user id. Elation: GET /physicians/.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_problems
tools.title: List a patient's problems
tools.description: List one patient's problem list (PHI): description, ICD-9/ICD-10/SNOMED codes, status (Active, Controlled, Resolved), start and resolved dates, synopsis. Elation: GET /problems/?patient=.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_allergies
tools.title: List a patient's allergies
tools.description: List one patient's allergies (PHI): allergen name, reaction, severity, status, start date. Elation: GET /allergies/?patient=.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_medications
tools.title: List a patient's medications
tools.description: List one patient's medication documents (PHI): drug name, strength, directions, quantity, authorized refills, prescribing physician, start date, and the discontinue order if any. Current and discontinued entries both appear unless you filter. Elation: GET /medications/?patient=.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_visit_notes
tools.title: List a patient's visit notes
tools.description: List one patient's visit notes (PHI): visit date, type, physician, signed state and the note body (bullets by category such as Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan). Filter by signed date or last change. Elation: GET /visit_notes/?patient=.

tools.name: elationhealth_get_visit_note
tools.title: Get a visit note
tools.description: Get one visit note by id (PHI): visit date, type, physician, signed state and the full note body. Elation: GET /visit_notes/{id}/.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_non_visit_notes
tools.title: List a patient's non-visit notes
tools.description: List one patient's non-visit notes (PHI): free-text chart notes outside a visit, such as phone calls and administrative notes. Elation: GET /non_visit_notes/?patient=.

tools.name: elationhealth_list_vitals
tools.title: List a patient's vitals
tools.description: List one patient's vital signs (PHI): height, weight, BMI, blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature, oxygen saturation, pain, with chart dates. Elation: GET /vitals/?patient=.
