examples: How many SMS credits do I have left on my account today?
How many texts did I send last month and how many credits did they use?
Who has opted out of receiving my text messages so far?
Which messages are scheduled to go out later?

servers.name: Megaventory
servers.description: Read Megaventory products, stock, orders and partners; create clients, sales and purchase orders.

login.hint: Find it in Megaventory: click your **profile icon → My Profile**, then the **key icon** to generate a key, and choose **Update**. The API is part of the paid Megaventory plans. The key acts with that user's permissions (a dedicated user makes its activity easy to track). It is used only to call the Megaventory API on your behalf, sent in the request body, and never shown to anyone.

tools.name: megaventory_get_current_user
tools.title: Get current user
tools.description: The Megaventory user this API key belongs to (user name and whether they are an administrator). The key itself and the mobile PIN are never returned. POST /User/UserGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: Search the product catalog: SKU, description, category, prices (selling, purchase, unit cost), dimensions, main supplier, sellable/purchasable flags and more. Filter by id, exact SKU, category, main supplier or words in the description. Empty text fields are omitted. POST /Product/ProductGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_product_categories
tools.title: List product categories
tools.description: List product categories (id, name, description). Use the ids to filter products. POST /ProductCategory/ProductCategoryGet.

tools.name: megaventory_get_product_bom
tools.title: Get product bill of materials
tools.description: The bill of materials (BOM) of a manufactured product: its raw materials (id, SKU, description, quantity per unit). POST /ProductBOM/ProductBOMGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_product_bundles
tools.title: List product bundles
tools.description: List product bundles (a bundle sells several products together). Filter by bundle id or SKU, or by a product the bundle includes. POST /Product/ProductBundleGetAll.

tools.name: megaventory_get_stock
tools.title: Get stock levels
tools.description: Stock per product per inventory location: physical stock, on hand, on hold, not yet shipped (open sales orders), not yet received (open purchase orders / work orders) and the alert level. Filter by product ids, SKU, category, location or supplier, or show only products below their alert level. POST /InventoryLocationStock/InventoryLocationStockGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_inventory_locations
tools.title: List inventory locations
tools.description: List inventory locations (warehouses, shops, transit): id, abbreviation, name, address. Use the ids for stock filters and order locations. POST /InventoryLocation/InventoryLocationGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_clients_suppliers
tools.title: List clients and suppliers
tools.description: List clients and suppliers (one record type in Megaventory): id, type, name, addresses, phone, email, tax id, currency, payment terms and contacts. Filter by type or words in the name. POST /SupplierClient/SupplierClientGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_product_suppliers
tools.title: List product supplier prices
tools.description: Which suppliers sell which products: supplier SKU, description and purchase price per product-supplier pair. POST /ProductSupplier/ProductSupplierGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_sales_orders
tools.title: List sales orders
tools.description: List sales orders with client, dates, totals (subtotal, tax, discount, grand total), status and the order rows (SKU, quantity, shipped/invoiced quantity, unit price). Filter by order number or status. POST /SalesOrder/SalesOrderGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_purchase_orders
tools.title: List purchase orders
tools.description: List purchase orders with supplier, dates, totals, status and the order rows (SKU, quantity, received/invoiced quantity, unit price). Filter by order number, status or supplier. POST /PurchaseOrder/PurchaseOrderGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_sales_quotes
tools.title: List sales quotes
tools.description: List sales quotes with client, totals, status and rows. Filter by quote number or status. POST /SalesQuote/SalesQuoteGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_work_orders
tools.title: List work orders
tools.description: List work (production) orders: finished product, quantity, location, status, priority and the materials allocated. Filter by work order number or status. POST /WorkOrder/WorkOrderGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_documents
tools.title: List documents
tools.description: List transaction documents of any type: shipments, invoices, receipts, credit notes, returns, adjustments and so on, with totals and status. Narrow by document type ids (megaventory_list_document_types), document number or status. POST /Document/DocumentGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_document_types
tools.title: List document types
tools.description: List the document types of the account (sales order, purchase order, shipment, invoice and so on) with their ids and abbreviations. POST /DocumentType/DocumentTypeGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_taxes
tools.title: List taxes
tools.description: List the tax rates defined in the account (id, name, rate). POST /Tax/TaxGet.

tools.name: megaventory_list_currencies
tools.title: List currencies
tools.description: List the currencies of the account (code, description, exchange rate to the default currency, default flag). POST /Currency/CurrencyGet.

tools.name: megaventory_create_client_or_supplier
tools.title: Create client or supplier
tools.description: WRITE: create a NEW client, supplier or both in Megaventory (Insert only: an existing record is never updated, nothing is deleted). Creating the same name twice creates two records, so search with megaventory_list_clients_suppliers first. POST /SupplierClient/SupplierClientUpdate.

tools.name: megaventory_create_sales_order
tools.title: Create pending sales order
tools.description: WRITE: create a NEW sales order for an existing client in the PENDING status. A pending order is only a draft document: it is not verified, nothing is shipped, invoiced or paid, and stock is not touched. Verifying, shipping and invoicing happen in Megaventory, not through this server. POST /SalesOrder/SalesOrderUpdate.

tools.name: megaventory_create_purchase_order
tools.title: Create pending purchase order
tools.description: WRITE: create a NEW purchase order to an existing supplier in the PENDING status. A pending order is only a draft document: it is not verified or sent, nothing is received, invoiced or paid, and stock is not touched. Verifying and receiving happen in Megaventory, not through this server. POST /PurchaseOrder/PurchaseOrderUpdate.

tools.name: megaventory_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: megaventory_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Megaventory tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: megaventory_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Megaventory (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: megaventory_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Megaventory Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run megaventory_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: How much stock do we have of each product in the main warehouse?
Which sales orders are still pending this month?
Which purchase orders have we placed with our suppliers recently?
Create a new client record for Acme Ltd with email buyer@acme.com.

servers.name: REVIEWS.io
servers.description: Read REVIEWS.io product and company reviews, ratings, UGC, surveys; tag reviews; invite one buyer.

login.hint: Both are in the REVIEWS.io dashboard ([dash.reviews.io](https://dash.reviews.io)) under **Integrations > API**. The API is available on the **Plus** package. Your key is used only to call the REVIEWS.io API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: reviewsio_list_reviews
tools.title: List reviews and questions
tools.description: The recommended way to read reviews: company (store) reviews, product reviews, third-party reviews and product questions in one filterable timeline, with the account's private data (reviewer e-mail, order). Filter by type, SKU/MPN/GTIN, tag, branch, keyword, date range, minimum rating, photos/videos; sort newest-first by default. Pages are 1-based; next_page is set when more results remain. GET /reviews.

tools.name: reviewsio_list_company_reviews
tools.title: List company reviews
tools.description: Company (store) reviews with private data (order number, reviewer details, tags) and optionally the replies. Filter by rating range, dates, order number, branch, invitation id; order by date or rating. Pages are 0-based; next_page is set when more remain. GET /merchant/reviews.

tools.name: reviewsio_get_review_stats
tools.title: Get review statistics
tools.description: Basic review statistics: average rating and review count for product reviews, company reviews and third-party reviews. GET /stats/all.

tools.name: reviewsio_get_product_ratings
tools.title: Get product ratings
tools.description: Average rating and review count for one or more products by SKU (batch). GET /product/rating-batch.

tools.name: reviewsio_get_review_nuggets
tools.title: Get review nuggets
tools.description: Short, highlight-worthy review snippets (nuggets) of company and/or product reviews, for marketing. Filter by SKU, tags, branch, minimum rating. GET /review-nuggets/data.

tools.name: reviewsio_list_ugc
tools.title: List user generated content
tools.description: Customer photos/videos (UGC) collected through REVIEWS.io, filterable by SKU, tag, category or videos only. GET /ugc.

tools.name: reviewsio_list_surveys
tools.title: List surveys
tools.description: The store's surveys (campaigns) with their ids; use an id with reviewsio_list_survey_responses. GET /widget/surveys.

tools.name: reviewsio_list_survey_responses
tools.title: List survey responses
tools.description: The responses submitted to one survey. Get the survey id from reviewsio_list_surveys. GET /widget/survey-responses.

tools.name: reviewsio_list_product_invitations
tools.title: List product invitations
tools.description: Product review invitations that are queued or sent (customer, order, send date, status); filter by SKU, order id or sent state, and page through with page/limit. GET /product/invitation.

tools.name: reviewsio_list_company_invitations
tools.title: List company invitations
tools.description: Company review invitations that are queued or sent (customer, order, send date, status); filter by order id or sent state, and page through with page/limit. GET /merchant/invitations.

tools.name: reviewsio_list_unsubscribed_users
tools.title: List unsubscribed users
tools.description: E-mail addresses that unsubscribed from (or were unsubscribed from) REVIEWS.io invitation e-mails. GET /unsubscribe/list.

tools.name: reviewsio_list_webhooks
tools.title: List webhooks
tools.description: The review-submitted webhooks registered for the store (read-only; this server never adds or removes webhooks). GET /webhook/list.

tools.name: reviewsio_tag_company_review
tools.title: Tag a company review
tools.description: WRITE: adds a tag to one company review (visible in your REVIEWS.io dashboard and usable as a filter). Adding the same tag twice changes nothing. Nothing is sent to the customer. POST /review/tag/{id}.

tools.name: reviewsio_tag_product_review
tools.title: Tag a product review
tools.description: WRITE: adds a tag to one product review (visible in your REVIEWS.io dashboard and usable as a filter). Adding the same tag twice changes nothing. Nothing is sent to the customer. POST /product-review/tag/{id}.

tools.name: reviewsio_unsubscribe_user
tools.title: Unsubscribe a user from invitation e-mails
tools.description: WRITE: stops REVIEWS.io sending review invitation e-mails to one e-mail address. Use it for a customer who asked not to be contacted. This server has no tool to re-subscribe an address; it can only be undone in the REVIEWS.io dashboard. Nothing is sent to the customer. POST /unsubscribe/email.

tools.name: reviewsio_queue_company_invitation
tools.title: Queue one company review invitation (e-mails a customer)
tools.description: WRITE - SENDS A MESSAGE TO A REAL CUSTOMER: queues ONE company review invitation e-mail to the given customer address; REVIEWS.io then e-mails that person (when and with which template follows your Flow Sequence / template_id, usually within hours or days). It cannot be recalled from this server. Only call it when the user has explicitly asked to invite this exact customer, and pass confirm_send_email: true. There is no bulk or SMS invitation tool. POST /merchant/invitation.

Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: Voodoo SMS
servers.description: Read Voodoo SMS credits, reports, inbox and lists; send one SMS; manage the opt-out blacklist.

login.hint: Create it in the Voodoo SMS portal under **Send SMS → API SMS → RESTful API → Create New API Key** and copy it when it is shown (it is shown only once). Choose **Read-only** if you only want reports and lists, or **Read-write** to let the AI send SMS (which uses your credits). Do not lock the key to an IP address. Your key is used only to call the Voodoo SMS API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: voodoosms_get_credits
tools.title: Get credit balance
tools.description: Get the SMS credit balance of the account. One credit pays for one 160-character SMS part (153 characters per part in a long message). Voodoo SMS REST: GET /credits.

tools.name: voodoosms_list_delivery_reports
tools.title: List delivery reports
tools.description: List delivery reports of sent messages (message_id, sender_id, to, sent_at, delivered_at, price, status), optionally filtered. Use it to check whether a message was delivered. Dates accept a UNIX timestamp, ISO 8601 (2026-10-01T09:00:00+00:00) or plain English ('yesterday', '2 weeks'). Voodoo SMS REST: GET /report.

tools.name: voodoosms_list_scheduled_messages
tools.title: List scheduled messages
tools.description: List SMS that were scheduled through the send API and are still waiting to go out (messages scheduled in the portal's Web SMS are not shown). Voodoo SMS REST: GET /schedule.

tools.name: voodoosms_list_inbox
tools.title: List received SMS
tools.description: List SMS received on the account's Virtual Mobile Numbers (replies and keyword messages). Needs a purchased number; an empty inbox returns an empty result. Dates accept a UNIX timestamp, ISO 8601 or plain English. Voodoo SMS REST: GET /inbox.

tools.name: voodoosms_list_numbers
tools.title: List virtual mobile numbers
tools.description: List the Virtual Mobile Numbers (VMNs) the account has purchased, used to receive SMS. Returns an empty result if there are none. Voodoo SMS REST: GET /numbers.

tools.name: voodoosms_list_contact_lists
tools.title: List contact lists
tools.description: List the account's contact lists (id, name, status, size, created/updated times) without their contacts. Returns an empty result if there are none. Voodoo SMS REST: GET /contacts.

tools.name: voodoosms_get_contact_list
tools.title: Get contacts in a list
tools.description: Get one contact list including its contacts (id, number, status, dynamic_data, created_at). Voodoo SMS REST: GET /contacts?contact_list_id=.

tools.name: voodoosms_list_blacklist
tools.title: List blacklisted numbers
tools.description: List the numbers on the account's opt-out blacklist (no SMS is ever sent to them), or look up one number (`{empty: true}` means it is not on the list). Returns an empty result when the blacklist is empty. Voodoo SMS REST: GET /blacklist.

tools.name: voodoosms_send_sms
tools.title: Send an SMS to one recipient
tools.description: WRITE: SENDS A REAL SMS to ONE recipient and USES THE ACCOUNT'S CREDITS (1 credit per message part, charged whether or not it is delivered; it cannot be undone). `sandbox` is required: true validates and prices the message without sending or charging, false sends it for real. Optional `schedule` queues it for later (cancel with cancel_scheduled_message). Do not retry after an error or timeout without checking list_delivery_reports / list_scheduled_messages, or the recipient may get it twice. One recipient per call; there is no bulk or list send. Voodoo SMS REST: POST /sendsms.

tools.name: voodoosms_cancel_scheduled_message
tools.title: Cancel a scheduled SMS
tools.description: WRITE: cancels one SMS that was scheduled through the send API, so it will not be sent. A message that has already gone out cannot be cancelled. Whether credits are refunded for a cancelled message is not documented by the vendor. Voodoo SMS REST: DELETE /schedule/{id}.

tools.name: voodoosms_add_to_blacklist
tools.title: Add a number to the blacklist
tools.description: WRITE: adds one number to the account's opt-out blacklist; from then on no SMS is sent to it (sends to it fail with error 20). Use it for a recipient who asked to stop. This tool cannot remove a number again. Voodoo SMS REST: POST /blacklist.

tools.name: voodoosms_create_contact_list
tools.title: Create a contact list
tools.description: WRITE: creates a new contact list with up to 500 contacts (the list name must be unique, at most 32 characters). It does not send anything. Voodoo SMS REST: POST /contacts.

tools.name: voodoosms_update_contact_list
tools.title: Rename a contact list or add contacts
tools.description: WRITE: renames a contact list and/or adds up to 500 contacts to it (existing contacts are not removed). Adding dynamic data needs a list created as dynamic. It does not send anything. Voodoo SMS REST: PUT /contacts/{contact_list_id}.

tools.name: voodoosms_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Voodoo SMS tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Voodoo SMS (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: voodoosms_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Voodoo SMS Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run voodoosms_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: How many SMS credits do I have left on my account today?
Show delivery reports for the texts I sent recently.
Which phone numbers are currently on my opt-out blacklist?
What replies have come into my inbox this week?

servers.name: Eventzilla
servers.description: Read Eventzilla events, tickets, orders, attendees and users; open or close ticket sales.

login.hint: Create it in Eventzilla under **Settings → Developers → API Credentials**. Your key is used only to call the Eventzilla API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: eventzilla_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List the events in the Eventzilla account: id, title, dates and times, venue, status, tickets sold and total, categories and the public URL. Use the id (and dateid) in the other tools. Filter by status and category name. GET /events.

tools.name: eventzilla_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event by id: title, description, dates, time zone, venue, status, tickets sold/total, URL, categories. GET /events/{eventid}.

tools.name: eventzilla_list_event_transactions
tools.title: List event transactions
tools.description: List the orders (transactions) of one event: order reference, checkout id, date, amount, number of tickets and status. Read-only. GET /events/{eventid}/transactions.

tools.name: eventzilla_list_event_attendees
tools.title: List event attendees
tools.description: List the attendees (registrations) of one event: name, ticket type, barcode, check-in status, order reference and answers to registration questions. The API returns the whole list in one reply (no paging). GET /events/{eventid}/attendees.

tools.name: eventzilla_list_ticket_types
tools.title: List ticket types
tools.description: List the ticket types of one event: id, title, price, quantity, sales window and limits, plus its donation ticket options (donation_options). GET /events/{eventid}/tickets.

tools.name: eventzilla_list_categories
tools.title: List event categories
tools.description: List the event categories (names to use as the category filter in eventzilla_list_events). GET /categories.

tools.name: eventzilla_get_attendee
tools.title: Get attendee
tools.description: One attendee by id: name, ticket type, barcode, check-in status, order reference, registration answers. GET /attendees/{attendeeid}.

tools.name: eventzilla_get_transaction
tools.title: Get transaction
tools.description: One transaction (order) by checkout id or order reference number: amount, ticket count, status, event date. Read-only. GET /transactions/{identifier}.

tools.name: eventzilla_list_users
tools.title: List organizers
tools.description: List the account's organizer and sub-organizer users: name, company, contact details, time zone, user type. GET /users.

tools.name: eventzilla_get_user
tools.title: Get organizer
tools.description: One organizer or sub-organizer by user id. GET /users/{userid}.

tools.name: eventzilla_toggle_event_sales
tools.title: Turn ticket sales on or off
tools.description: WRITE: publish (status true) or unpublish (status false) ticket sales of one event. Unpublishing stops attendees from buying tickets on the event page; publishing starts public sales again. Existing orders are not touched and no money moves through this tool. Idempotent. POST /events/togglesales.

tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: eventzilla_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Eventzilla (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: eventzilla_cancel_subscription

How many tickets have been sold for my next event?
List the attendees registered for my spring workshop.

servers.name: Finale Inventory
servers.description: Read Finale Inventory products, stock, orders and shipments; create draft purchase orders.

login.hint: The account is the part after `app.finaleinventory.com/` in your Finale address. Create the key in Finale: gear icon → **Application settings → Users → API keys** (you need the Manage users and permissions permission) and copy the secret right away, it is shown only once. Finale keys have full access to the account, and direct API use depends on your Finale subscription tier. Your key is used only to call the Finale API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: finale_list_facilities
tools.title: List locations (facilities)
tools.description: List Finale locations and sublocations: facilityName, facilityUrl (use it in other tools), parentFacilityUrl (set for sublocations), status. GET /{account}/api/facility/.

tools.name: finale_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products (SKUs): productId, internalName, status, productUrl, manufacturer, UPC, packing. Optional exact filters on productId and status. Collections come back ordered by lastUpdatedDate; for large catalogs narrow with updated_since or page with next_updated_since. GET /{account}/api/product/.

tools.name: finale_get_product
tools.title: Get a product
tools.description: One product in full: ids, description, UPC/ASIN, dimensions and weight, cost, supplier list, reorder guidelines, price list, custom fields. GET /{account}/api/product/{id} (falls back to a productId filter when the resource URL differs).

tools.name: finale_list_orders
tools.title: List orders (sales and purchase)
tools.description: List orders without their line items: orderId, type (SALES_ORDER or PURCHASE_ORDER), status (ORDER_CREATED, ORDER_LOCKED = committed, ORDER_COMPLETED, ORDER_CANCELLED), dates, origin/destination facility, reference number, total. Get the items with finale_get_order. For a large order history always pass updated_since (Finale cuts unfiltered collections at 120,000 rows before applying other filters). GET /{account}/api/order/.

tools.name: finale_get_order
tools.title: Get an order
tools.description: One order in full: header, line items (productUrl, quantity, unitPrice), roles (customer or supplier), adjustments, shipment and invoice URLs, notes. GET /{account}/api/order/{orderId}.

tools.name: finale_list_shipments
tools.title: List shipments
tools.description: List shipments (sales shipments, purchase receipts, transfers): shipmentId, type, status (for example SHIPMENT_INPUT, SHIPMENT_PACKED, SHIPMENT_SHIPPED), order, origin/destination, dates, tracking code. GET /{account}/api/shipment/.

tools.name: finale_get_shipment
tools.title: Get a shipment
tools.description: One shipment in full, including its shipment items (product, facility, quantity), packages and transfers. GET /{account}/api/shipment/{shipmentId}.

tools.name: finale_list_parties
tools.title: List customers and suppliers
tools.description: List party groups (customers, suppliers, carriers): partyId (derived from partyUrl; use it as supplier_party_id when drafting a purchase order), name (description), type, roles, status. GET /{account}/api/partygroup/.

tools.name: finale_list_inventory_items
tools.title: List stock entries
tools.description: Current stock as Finale stores it: one entry per product, location, lot and order with quantityOnHand, quantityOnOrder (committed purchase orders) and quantityReserved (committed sales orders). The inventoryitem collection has no server-side filter, so the WHOLE collection is downloaded (one collection read of the 300 per hour; can be large on big accounts, up to the 50,000 character result cap) and filtered here: pass product_id or facility_url. For per-product totals use finale_get_product_stock. GET /{account}/api/inventoryitem/.

tools.name: finale_get_product_stock
tools.title: Get stock levels of a product
tools.description: Stock of one product summed over Finale's stock entries: totals for quantityOnHand, quantityOnOrder and quantityReserved, and the same per location/sublocation. Downloads the WHOLE inventoryitem collection (Finale offers no filter; large on big accounts), so it counts as one collection read of the 300 per hour: avoid calling it in a loop. GET /{account}/api/inventoryitem/.

tools.name: finale_list_inventory_transfers
tools.title: List stock transfers
tools.description: List stock transfers between locations: product, from/to facility, quantity, lot, send and receive dates. GET /{account}/api/inventorytransfer/.

tools.name: finale_list_stock_changes
tools.title: List stock changes (inventory variances)
tools.description: List stock changes (physical counts and adjustments already recorded in Finale): id, type, date, status, location, comments. Read-only history. GET /{account}/api/inventoryvariance/.

tools.name: finale_create_draft_purchase_order
tools.title: Create a draft purchase order (WRITE)
tools.description: WRITE. Creates a purchase order for a supplier in status ORDER_CREATED, i.e. an editable draft. It is NOT locked (committed), received, completed or emailed, no stock changes and no money moves: review and commit it in Finale. Products are looked up first (one single read each; products whose resource URL differs from the SKU cost collection reads, bounded to 3 or one full product-list read), then ONE POST creates the order; the call is never retried, so check finale_list_orders before repeating it after an error. POST /{account}/api/order/.

tools.name: finale_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: finale_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Finale Inventory tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: finale_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Finale Inventory (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: finale_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Finale Inventory Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run finale_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: How much stock do we have of SKU WIDGET-01 across locations?
Which purchase orders are open with our suppliers?
Show sales orders updated this week with their dates and totals.
List recent stock adjustments from our physical counts.

servers.name: ClassMarker
servers.description: Read ClassMarker groups, links, exams and recent results; manage question bank and access codes.

login.hint: Create a key in ClassMarker under **My Account → Webhooks / API Keys** (see the [API docs](https://www.classmarker.com/online-testing/docs/api/)); give it access to the groups and links you want to use. API access needs an upgraded ClassMarker account. ClassMarker allows **30 requests per hour per key**, so connecting uses one of them. Results contain test-taker names and emails; your key and secret are used only to call the ClassMarker API on your behalf and are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: classmarker_list_groups_links_exams
tools.title: List groups, links and exams
tools.description: List the groups, links and exams (tests) this API key can access, with the ids the other tools need (group_id, link_id, link_url_id, test_id, and access_list_id for links with an access-code list). Good first call. Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: GET /v1.json.

tools.name: classmarker_recent_group_results
tools.title: Recent results across all groups
tools.description: Recent finished test results taken in the key's groups (all groups, all exams), oldest first, PAGED by finish time: test-taker name, email, score, percentage, pass/fail, timing, certificate. Contains personal data: use small pages. Max look-back 3 months. Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: GET /v1/groups/recent_results.json.

tools.name: classmarker_recent_link_results
tools.title: Recent results across all links
tools.description: Recent finished test results taken through the key's links (all links, all exams), oldest first, PAGED by finish time: test-taker name, email, score, pass/fail, timing, access code, extra tracking fields, IP address, certificate. Contains personal data: use small pages. Max look-back 3 months. Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: GET /v1/links/recent_results.json.

tools.name: classmarker_recent_group_exam_results
tools.title: Recent results for one group exam
tools.description: Recent finished results for ONE exam in ONE group (ids from classmarker_list_groups_links_exams), oldest first, PAGED by finish time. Contains personal data: use small pages. Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: GET /v1/groups/{group_id}/tests/{test_id}/recent_results.json.

tools.name: classmarker_recent_link_exam_results
tools.title: Recent results for one link exam
tools.description: Recent finished results for the exam of ONE link (ids from classmarker_list_groups_links_exams), oldest first, PAGED by finish time. Contains personal data: use small pages. Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: GET /v1/links/{link_id}/tests/{test_id}/recent_results.json.

tools.name: classmarker_list_categories
tools.title: List question categories
tools.description: List the question-bank categories with their parent categories and ids (needed for creating and updating questions). Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: GET /v1/categories.json.

tools.name: classmarker_list_questions
tools.title: List question-bank questions
tools.description: List the questions of the question bank, 200 per page (page 1, 2, ...): question text, type, category, points, options, correct options, status. A full page means more may follow, so ask for the next page. Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: GET /v1/questions.json?page=N.

tools.name: classmarker_get_question
tools.title: Get a question
tools.description: Get one question-bank question by id (ids from classmarker_list_questions). Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: GET /v1/questions/{question_id}.json.

tools.name: classmarker_add_access_codes
tools.title: Add access codes to a list
tools.description: WRITE: add access codes (1-100 per call, up to 255 characters each; a list holds at most 20,000) to a link's access-code list, so those people can start the exam. The access_list_id comes from classmarker_list_groups_links_exams (links[].access_list_id). Only adds; removing codes is not offered. Does not count against the 30 requests per hour limit. API: POST /v1/accesslists/{access_list_id}.json.

tools.name: classmarker_create_parent_category
tools.title: Create a parent category
tools.description: WRITE: create a new top-level question category. Returns its parent_category_id. Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: POST /v1/categories/parent_category.json.

tools.name: classmarker_update_parent_category
tools.title: Rename a parent category
tools.description: WRITE: rename an existing parent category (overwrites its name). Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: PUT /v1/categories/parent_category/{parent_category_id}.json.

tools.name: classmarker_create_category
tools.title: Create a category
tools.description: WRITE: create a question category under a parent category. Returns its category_id. Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: POST /v1/categories/category.json.

tools.name: classmarker_update_category
tools.title: Update a category
tools.description: WRITE: rename a category and/or move it to another parent (overwrites both fields: send the name and parent_category_id you want it to have). Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: PUT /v1/categories/category/{category_id}.json.

tools.name: classmarker_create_question
tools.title: Create a question
tools.description: WRITE: add a new question to the question bank. Only multiplechoice, multipleresponse, truefalse and essay can be created. Returns the new question_id. For truefalse, give only correct_options ["A"] (True) or ["B"] (False). Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: POST /v1/questions.json.

tools.name: classmarker_update_question
tools.title: Update a question
tools.description: WRITE (overwrites): replace an existing question-bank question. Send the COMPLETE question (type, text, options, correct options, points, feedback), not only the changed fields; read it first with classmarker_get_question. Only multiplechoice, multipleresponse, truefalse and essay questions can be updated. Counts as one of ClassMarker's 30 requests per hour per API key. API: PUT /v1/questions/{question_id}.json.

Does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on ClassMarker (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: classmarker_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's ClassMarker Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). servers.name: SupportBee
servers.description: Read SupportBee tickets, replies and reports; reply, comment, label, assign and archive tickets.

login.hint: The company is the first part of your desk address (`acme` for acme.supportbee.com). Find the API token in SupportBee under your **profile menu → API Token**; it acts with that user's permissions, so a dedicated agent makes its activity easy to track. A reply you send through this server is e-mailed to the customer. Your token is used only to call the SupportBee API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: supportbee_list_tickets
tools.title: List tickets
tools.description: List tickets of the shared inbox, newest activity first, with filters (assignee, team, label, requester, dates, spam/trash/archived). By default archived, spam and trashed tickets are left out. Each ticket has id, subject, labels, requester, assignee, replies_count, comments_count, unanswered, archived and the first message text (cut). With total_only=true only the number of matching tickets comes back. GET /tickets.

tools.name: supportbee_search_tickets
tools.title: Search tickets
tools.description: Full-text search over tickets (subject, body, requester) with SupportBee's search syntax, newest activity first. Spam and trash are excluded unless asked. GET /tickets/search.

tools.name: supportbee_get_ticket
tools.title: Get a ticket
tools.description: One ticket with subject, requester, labels, assignees, state and the first message text. Replies and comments are separate calls. GET /tickets/{id}.

tools.name: supportbee_list_replies
tools.title: List the replies of a ticket
tools.description: The public replies (the conversation with the customer) of a ticket, oldest first, as text. GET /tickets/{id}/replies.

tools.name: supportbee_get_reply
tools.title: Get one reply of a ticket
tools.description: One reply of a ticket (text, replier, cc/bcc). GET /tickets/{ticket_id}/replies/{id}.

tools.name: supportbee_list_comments
tools.title: List the internal comments of a ticket
tools.description: The internal comments (visible to agents only, never e-mailed) of a ticket, oldest first, as text. GET /tickets/{id}/comments.

tools.name: supportbee_get_ticket_audit
tools.title: Get the audit trail of a ticket
tools.description: What happened to a ticket and who did it (assignments, label changes, replies, archiving) with timestamps. GET /tickets/{id}/audit.

tools.name: supportbee_list_labels
tools.title: List labels
tools.description: All custom labels of the company (name and color). Use a label name with supportbee_add_label or the label filter. GET /labels.

tools.name: supportbee_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: The teams of the company (id, name), optionally only those that have users in them, or only the token user's teams. GET /teams.

tools.name: supportbee_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: The agents, admins and collaborators of the desk (id, name, e-mail, role, teams), or customer groups. Use the id as assigned_user or user_id. GET /users.

tools.name: supportbee_get_user
tools.title: Get a user
tools.description: One user or customer with role, teams, ticket counts and a few of their recent tickets. GET /users/{id}.

tools.name: supportbee_list_snippets
tools.title: List snippets
tools.description: The canned replies (snippets) of the company: name, tags and text, to reuse in a reply. GET /snippets.

tools.name: supportbee_list_forwarding_addresses
tools.title: List forwarding addresses
tools.description: The support e-mail addresses (forwarding addresses) of the desk: id, name, the address tickets arrive at and the from address. GET /emails.

tools.name: supportbee_get_report
tools.title: Get a report
tools.description: A report as time-series data points (value, timestamp): tickets_count, replies_count or avg_first_response_time, optionally for one agent, team or label. Needs an admin token. GET /reports/{report}.

tools.name: supportbee_reply_to_ticket
tools.title: Reply to a ticket (sends an e-mail)
tools.description: WRITE: SENDS AN E-MAIL to the customer. Posts a public reply on ONE ticket; SupportBee e-mails it to the ticket's requester and to the cc/bcc addresses you list (at most 10 addresses in total). It cannot be recalled. The reply comes from the token's user. For a note only your team sees, use supportbee_add_comment. POST /tickets/{id}/replies.

tools.name: supportbee_add_comment
tools.title: Add an internal comment to a ticket
tools.description: WRITE: adds an internal comment to a ticket. Comments are visible to your agents only and are never e-mailed to the customer. POST /tickets/{id}/comments.

tools.name: supportbee_add_label
tools.title: Add a label to a ticket
tools.description: WRITE: adds an existing label to a ticket (404 if the label does not exist; names come from supportbee_list_labels). Safe to repeat. POST /tickets/{id}/labels/{label}.

tools.name: supportbee_remove_label
tools.title: Remove a label from a ticket
tools.description: WRITE: removes a label from a ticket (the label itself stays; 404 if the ticket does not have it). DELETE /tickets/{id}/labels/{label}.

tools.name: supportbee_assign_ticket
tools.title: Assign a ticket to a user or a team
tools.description: WRITE: assigns a ticket to ONE agent (user_id) or ONE team (team_id), not both. A ticket that belongs to a team can only go to a member of that team; assigning to another team removes the user assignee. The customer is not e-mailed (SupportBee may notify the assigned agent). POST /tickets/{id}/user_assignment or /team_assignment.

tools.name: supportbee_unassign_ticket
tools.title: Remove the user or team assignment of a ticket
tools.description: WRITE: clears the user assignee or the team assignee of a ticket. DELETE /tickets/{id}/user_assignment or /team_assignment.

tools.name: supportbee_set_ticket_archived
tools.title: Archive or un-archive a ticket
tools.description: WRITE: archives a ticket (archived=true, it leaves the open inbox) or moves it back (archived=false). Nothing is deleted or sent. POST/DELETE /tickets/{id}/archive.

tools.name: supportbee_set_ticket_answered
tools.title: Mark a ticket answered or unanswered
tools.description: WRITE: marks a ticket as answered (answered=true) or unanswered (answered=false) without sending anything. POST/DELETE /tickets/{id}/answered.

tools.name: supportbee_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: supportbee_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the SupportBee tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: supportbee_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on SupportBee (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: supportbee_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's SupportBee Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run supportbee_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

Search tickets from jane@acme.com and summarize her issue.

servers.name: Tokeet
servers.description: Read Tokeet rentals, rates, guests, tasks and expenses; add guests, notes and tasks.

login.hint: In Tokeet open **Settings → Account Info**. The API key (click **Generate Key** if there is none; a new key disables the old one) and the account id are shown at the top of the first table. They are used only to call the Tokeet API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: tokeet_get_current_user
tools.title: Get current user
tools.description: The Tokeet user the API key belongs to (name, email, role). Login data is never returned. GET /user/me.

tools.name: tokeet_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the team members (users) of the Tokeet account. GET /user.

tools.name: tokeet_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: One team member by id. GET /user/{user_pkey}.

tools.name: tokeet_list_rentals
tools.title: List rentals
tools.description: List the rental properties in the account, sorted by name. GET /rental.

tools.name: tokeet_get_rental
tools.title: Get rental
tools.description: One rental property by id (its pkey from tokeet_list_rentals). GET /rental/{rental_pkey}.

tools.name: tokeet_list_rentals_by_owner
tools.title: List rentals by owner
tools.description: List the rentals assigned to one owner. GET /rental/owner/{owner_pkey} (Tokeet documents no paging for it: all of the owner's rentals come back).

tools.name: tokeet_get_rental_availability
tools.title: Get rental availability
tools.description: The open and blocked dates of one rental over the next two years. GET /rental/{rental_pkey}/availability.

tools.name: tokeet_list_rates
tools.title: List rental rates
tools.description: All standard, dynamic and promotional rates of one rental. Read-only: rates cannot be changed with this server. GET /rate/{rental_pkey}.

tools.name: tokeet_list_guests
tools.title: List guests
tools.description: List guests (personal data: name, emails, phones, address, notes, interactions), one page at a time. Filter by partial name, booking source/channel, and whether they have bookings. GET /guest.

tools.name: tokeet_get_guest
tools.title: Get guest
tools.description: One guest by id: contact details, notes, interactions and preferences. GET /guest/{pkey}.

tools.name: tokeet_get_guest_by_email
tools.title: Get guest by email
tools.description: The guest whose primary email is exactly this address. GET /guest/email/{email}.

tools.name: tokeet_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List the tasks (to-dos, e.g. cleanings and check-ins) in the account, sorted by task name. GET /task.

tools.name: tokeet_get_task
tools.title: Get task
tools.description: One task by id. GET /task/{task_pkey}.

tools.name: tokeet_list_expenses
tools.title: List expenses
tools.description: List the expenses recorded in the account (date, rental, category, amount, paid/unpaid status), by creation date. Read-only. GET /expense.

tools.name: tokeet_get_expense
tools.title: Get expense
tools.description: One expense by id. GET /expense/{expense_pkey}.

tools.name: tokeet_list_templates
tools.title: List message templates
tools.description: List the message/email templates in the account, optionally of one type. GET /template.

tools.name: tokeet_get_template
tools.title: Get message template
tools.description: One message template by id. GET /template/{template_pkey}.

tools.name: tokeet_list_triggers
tools.title: List automation triggers
tools.description: List the automation triggers (event, rental, template, delay) in the account. Read-only: triggers cannot be changed with this server. GET /trigger.

tools.name: tokeet_create_guest
tools.title: Create guest
tools.description: WRITE: create a guest record (name and email required, the rest optional). Nothing is sent to the guest. Tokeet cannot recover deleted data and this server cannot delete guests. POST /guest.

tools.name: tokeet_update_guest
tools.title: Update guest
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of a guest (name, address, birthday, spouse, kids, drink, hobby, sport). Only the fields you pass are sent, and each one OVERWRITES the stored value (an address object replaces the whole address). Emails and phones have their own endpoints and are not changed here. PUT /guest/{guest_pkey}.

tools.name: tokeet_add_guest_note
tools.title: Add guest note
tools.description: WRITE: add an internal note to a guest record (not visible to or sent to the guest). POST /guest/{guest_pkey}/note.

tools.name: tokeet_record_guest_interaction
tools.title: Record guest interaction
tools.description: WRITE: log an interaction you had with a guest (phone call, meeting or comment) in the guest's history. Nothing is sent to the guest. `date` is an epoch timestamp: use the same unit as the dates you see on existing interactions from tokeet_get_guest. POST /guest/{guest_pkey}/interaction.

tools.name: tokeet_create_task

tools.description: WRITE: create a task (to-do) in the account, optionally linked to an inquiry and assigned to a user. `due` is an epoch timestamp: use the same unit as the `due` of existing tasks from tokeet_list_tasks. No message is sent to anyone by this call. POST /task.

tools.name: tokeet_update_task
tools.title: Update task
tools.description: WRITE: change a task: rename, move to another list, reschedule, edit notes, reassign, or mark it completed (status 2) or active (1). Only the fields you pass are sent and each OVERWRITES the stored value. PUT /task/{task_pkey}.

Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: Inventory Planner
servers.description: Read Inventory Planner forecasts, replenishment and purchase orders; create draft purchase orders.

login.hint: In Inventory Planner open **Account → Settings → API** and click **Generate key** (the key works only for a user with full access to the account); the account id is shown on the same page. Your key is used only to call the Inventory Planner API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone. This server can create draft purchase orders but never sends an order to a vendor.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_list_variants
tools.title: List variants (forecast and replenishment)
tools.description: List product variants with Inventory Planner's computed metrics (forecast, replenishment, days to sell out, lost revenue, lead time, review period and ~200 more). Always pass `fields` to pick the metrics you need (default: id,sku,lead_time,review_period,replenishment,oos,under_value; oos = forecasted days to sell out, under_value = forecasted lost revenue, replenishment = recommended order quantity). Use `filters` and `sort` for questions like "which SKUs need reordering". Removed variants are excluded unless include_removed. GET /api/v1/variants.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_get_variant
tools.title: Get variant
tools.description: One variant by its Inventory Planner id, with the metrics named in `fields` (default: id,sku,lead_time,review_period,replenishment,oos,under_value). GET /api/v1/variants/{id}.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_list_variant_vendors
tools.title: List a variant's vendors
tools.description: The vendors a variant can be ordered from, with cost_price, landing_cost_price, vendor_reference (vendor SKU), vendor_name, vendor_packaging (MOQ) and uom_ordering. GET /api/v1/variants/{id}/vendors.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_get_variant_vendor
tools.title: Get a variant's vendor terms
tools.description: One vendor's terms for a variant: cost_price, landing_cost_price, vendor_reference, vendor_name, vendor_packaging (MOQ), uom_ordering. vendor_id is the vendor name in lowercase. GET /api/v1/variants/{id}/vendors/{vendor_id}.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_list_purchase_orders
tools.title: List purchase orders (and transfers, assembly orders)
tools.description: List stock orders: purchase orders, transfers and assembly orders (the `type` field is "po"/empty, "transfer" or "assembly"). Filter with `filters`, e.g. {"status": "OPEN", "vendor": "Acme", "expected_date_lt": "2026-11-01"}. Default fields: id,reference,status,type,vendor,warehouse,source,created_date,expected_date,received_date,currency,total,total_ordered,total_received. GET /api/v1/purchase-orders.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_get_purchase_order
tools.title: Get purchase order
tools.description: One purchase order, transfer or assembly order by id, with its header fields (reference, status, vendor, warehouse, dates, addresses, totals, notes) and line items. GET /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id}.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_list_purchase_order_items
tools.title: List purchase order line items
tools.description: The line items of a purchase order: variant id, sku, title, ordered quantity (replenishment), received quantity and received_history, cost price, tax, discount and stock snapshots. GET /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id}/items.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_get_purchase_order_connections
tools.title: Get purchase order connection status
tools.description: Whether and how a purchase order was saved to connected systems (ERP, accounting): per connection the status (success, error, run, queued), save_po flag and the PO's id and reference there. Read-only. GET /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id}/connections.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_get_purchase_order_stock_update
tools.title: Get purchase order stock update (preview)
tools.description: The stock updates a purchase order has computed: per warehouse (wh) the items with stock_before, delta and error. for_destination false reads the source warehouse of a transfer. Read-only: nothing is pushed. GET /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id}/stock-update.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_create_draft_purchase_order
tools.title: Create a draft purchase order
tools.description: WRITE: create a purchase order with status "draft" in Inventory Planner (POST /api/v1/purchase-orders). A draft is only a plan inside Inventory Planner: it is NOT sent to the vendor, NOT saved to any connected system and moves no stock or money. Purchase orders only (no transfers or assembly orders). Each line item is a variant id plus the quantity to order (replenishment).

tools.name: inventoryplanner_update_draft_purchase_order
tools.title: Edit a draft purchase order
tools.description: WRITE: change the reference, expected date or notes of a purchase order that is still a draft (PATCH /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id}). The order is read first and refused unless its status is "draft". It never changes the status, sends the order, or touches line items or received quantities.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: inventoryplanner_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Inventory Planner tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Inventory Planner (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. servers.name: Tick
servers.description: Read Tick clients, projects, tasks, users and time entries; log and edit time entries.

login.hint: Both values are in Tick under **My Profile** (the subscription id is also the number in your Tick address, `https://www.tickspot.com/**12345**/...`). The token belongs to one user and one subscription and acts with that user's rights. Your token is used only to call the Tick API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: tick_list_clients
tools.title: List clients
tools.description: List Tick clients. By default only clients that have open projects; set include_all=true for every client (also archived or without projects). 100 per page. GET /clients.json or /clients/all.json.

tools.name: tick_get_client
tools.title: Get client
tools.description: One client by id, with a summary of its projects (count and URL). GET /clients/{id}.json.

tools.name: tick_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List Tick projects with budget (hours or money), billable flag, client_id and owner_id. Open projects by default; status=closed for closed ones. 100 per page. GET /projects.json or /projects/closed.json.

tools.name: tick_get_project
tools.title: Get project
tools.description: One project by id, with total_hours entered, a summary of its tasks (count and URL) and its client. GET /projects/{id}.json.

tools.name: tick_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List Tick tasks (the budget lines that time entries are logged against). Across all projects, or for one project when project_id is given. Open tasks by default; status=closed for closed ones. You need a task id to log time. 100 per page. GET /tasks.json, /tasks/closed.json, /projects/{id}/tasks.json or /projects/{id}/tasks/closed.json.

tools.name: tick_get_task
tools.title: Get task
tools.description: One task by id, with total_hours entered, a summary of its entries (count and URL) and its project. GET /tasks/{id}.json.

tools.name: tick_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the users of the Tick subscription (id, name, e-mail, timezone). A non-administrator sees only themself. Use deleted=true for removed users who still have time entries (administrators only). GET /users.json or /users/deleted.json.

tools.name: tick_list_entries
tools.title: List time entries
tools.description: List time entries. Tick requires EITHER start_date AND end_date (entries dated in that range) OR updated_at (entries created or changed after that time). Optional filters: project_id, task_id, user_id, billable, billed. Each entry has date, hours, notes, task_id, user_id. 100 per page. GET /entries.json.

tools.name: tick_get_entry
tools.title: Get time entry
tools.description: One time entry by id, with its task. GET /entries/{id}.json.

tools.name: tick_create_entry
tools.title: Log time entry
tools.description: WRITE: log a new time entry on a task (POST /entries.json). Needs the task id (see tick_list_tasks). hours is a decimal (1.5 = 1h30m). user_id is only honored for administrators (otherwise the entry is yours). Creates a new entry every call; nothing is sent to anyone.

tools.name: tick_update_entry
tools.title: Update time entry
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing time entry (PUT /entries/{id}.json): hours, notes, date, task, or mark it billed. Only the fields you pass change; the previous values are overwritten.

tools.name: tick_create_client
tools.title: Create client
tools.description: WRITE: create a new client (POST /clients.json). Tick administrators only (403 otherwise). Creates a new client every call.

tools.name: tick_create_project
tools.title: Create project
tools.description: WRITE: create a new project (POST /projects.json). Tick administrators only. The project has no tasks: create at least one with tick_create_task before time can be logged. Creates a new project every call.

tools.name: tick_create_task
tools.title: Create task
tools.description: WRITE: create a new task on a project (POST /tasks.json). Tick administrators only. Creates a new task every call.

servers.name: SIGNL4
servers.description: Read SIGNL4 alerts, teams, users and duty schedules; raise, acknowledge, close and annotate alerts.

login.hint: Create it in the SIGNL4 web portal under **Integrations → API Keys**. The key is used only to call the SIGNL4 API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: signl4_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: List the SIGNL4 teams the API key can access: id, name, description, time zone and member ids. Team ids are needed to raise alerts and to look up categories and duties. GET /v3/teams.

tools.name: signl4_get_team
tools.title: Get team
tools.description: One SIGNL4 team: name, description, time zone, member ids. GET /v3/teams/{teamId}.

tools.name: signl4_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the SIGNL4 users the key can access with name, e-mail, contact addresses, activation state and duty status per team (dutyMode, onDutyTime). User ids are needed to acknowledge/close/annotate alerts. GET /v3/users.

tools.name: signl4_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: One SIGNL4 user: name, e-mail, contact addresses, time zone and duty status per team. GET /v3/users/{userId}.

tools.name: signl4_list_team_users
tools.title: List users of teams
tools.description: List the users of the given teams (all accessible teams by default) with duty status. Teams that cannot be read are reported under `errors`. GET /v3/teams/users.

tools.name: signl4_list_categories
tools.title: List alert categories
tools.description: List the alert categories of a team (name, color, keywords used to auto-classify alerts). The category name can be passed to signl4_raise_alert. GET /v3/categories/{teamId}.

tools.name: signl4_list_alerts
tools.title: List alerts
tools.description: Search SIGNL4 alerts (signls), newest first, with status, severity, category and history (created, acknowledged, closed). Filter by team, status, creation time, text or external id. Up to 100 per page; pass the returned continuation_token to get the next page. POST /v3/signls/paged (a read).

tools.name: signl4_get_alert
tools.title: Get alert
tools.description: Full detail of one alert: title, text, severity, category, status and delivery status, history (who acknowledged/closed it and when), parameters, attachments and escalations with per-user delivery. GET /v3/signls/{signlId}/details.

tools.name: signl4_get_alert_timeline
tools.title: Get alert timeline
tools.description: The ordered timeline of an alert: creation, notifications, acknowledgements, annotations, escalations and remote actions. GET /v3/signls/{signlId}/timeline.

tools.name: signl4_get_alert_report
tools.title: Get alert report
tools.description: Alert volume and response statistics per team over several time periods: acknowledged, closed and unhandled counts, overall and per category (optionally for one user). Teams that cannot be read are reported under `errors`. GET /v3/signls/report.

tools.name: signl4_raise_alert
tools.title: Raise alert
tools.description: WRITE: raise a new alert in a SIGNL4 team. THIS NOTIFIES REAL PEOPLE: every team member currently on duty is paged (push, SMS and/or voice call according to their settings) and the alert escalates if nobody acknowledges it. Only use it when the user clearly asked to alert the team; never for tests unless they said so. Not idempotent: a second call pages the team again. Returns the new alert incl. its id. POST /v3/signls.

tools.name: signl4_acknowledge_alert
tools.title: Acknowledge alert
tools.description: WRITE: acknowledge an alert on behalf of a SIGNL4 user (recorded in its history under that user). Stops escalation to further tiers for that alert. POST /v3/signls/{signlId}/acknowledge.

tools.name: signl4_close_alert
tools.title: Close alert
tools.description: WRITE: close (resolve) an alert on behalf of a SIGNL4 user; it leaves the open list and stops all further notifications. POST /v3/signls/{signlId}/close.

tools.name: signl4_annotate_alert
tools.title: Annotate alert
tools.description: WRITE: add a text note to an alert's timeline on behalf of a SIGNL4 user. The note is visible to the team in the app. It does not page anyone by itself. POST /v3/signls/{signlId}/annotate.

tools.name: signl4_list_duty_schedules
tools.title: List duty schedules
tools.description: Planned on-call duty schedules (who is on duty when): start/end, team, user, tier, stand-in and shift info. Filter by team, user and time window. POST /v3/schedules (a read).

tools.name: signl4_get_duty_status
tools.title: Get user duty status
tools.description: Whether a user is currently on or off duty in each of their teams (dutyMode, onDutyTime, tier). GET /v3/users/{userId}/dutyStatus.

tools.name: signl4_get_duty_summary
tools.title: Get duty summary
tools.description: Duty assistant info per team: whether it is enabled and the last two (or all) duty periods. GET /v3/duties/summary.

tools.name: signl4_list_audit_logs
tools.title: List audit logs
tools.description: Audit log of changes and events in the SIGNL4 subscription (who changed what, when). Filter by team, time window and message text; pass the returned continuation_token for the next page. GET /v3/audits.

tools.name: signl4_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on SIGNL4 (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: SpinupWP
servers.description: Read SpinupWP servers, sites and events; purge caches, restart services, run git deploys.

login.hint: Create a token in SpinupWP under **My Account → API Tokens** (or **Team Settings → API Tokens** for team owners and admins) at [spinupwp.app](https://spinupwp.app). The API needs an active SpinupWP plan. This connection cannot create or delete servers or sites. Your token is used only to call the SpinupWP API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: spinupwp_list_servers
tools.title: List servers
tools.description: List the servers in your SpinupWP team: name, provider, region, size, IP, Ubuntu version, disk space, connection status and whether a reboot or upgrade is required. GET /servers.

tools.name: spinupwp_get_server
tools.title: Get server
tools.description: One server by id: provider, size, disk usage, database server, connection status, reboot/upgrade-required flags and install notes. GET /servers/{id}.

tools.name: spinupwp_list_sites
tools.title: List sites
tools.description: List sites across your servers (or one server): domain, PHP version, WordPress flag, HTTPS, page cache, backups, pending WordPress core/theme/plugin updates, git deploy settings and status. Deploy-trigger URLs are hidden. GET /sites.

tools.name: spinupwp_get_site
tools.title: Get site
tools.description: One site by id with its full settings: domains, PHP version, page cache, HTTPS, nginx options, database reference, backup schedule and storage, WordPress update counts, git repo/branch/deploy script, basic-auth username, cron and SpinupWP subdomain. The git deploy-trigger URL is hidden. GET /sites/{id}.

tools.name: spinupwp_list_site_domains
tools.title: List site domains
tools.description: The additional domains of a site, with their redirect settings (enabled, type, destination). GET /sites/{id}/domains.

tools.name: spinupwp_list_site_path_redirects
tools.title: List site path redirects
tools.description: The path redirects configured on a site (from, to, type permanent/redirect). GET /sites/{id}/path-redirects.

tools.name: spinupwp_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List recent events (the activity log: provisioning, restarts, deploys, cache purges) with who started them, status (queued, creating, updating, deleting, deployed, failed) and timestamps. Long command output is shortened; read one event for its full output. GET /events.

tools.name: spinupwp_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event by id, with status and command output. Use it to see whether a purge, restart or deploy (which reply with an event_id) has finished or failed. GET /events/{id}.

tools.name: spinupwp_list_storage_providers
tools.title: List backup storage providers
tools.description: The backup storage providers connected to the team (id, service, name). GET /storage-providers.

tools.name: spinupwp_list_team_ssh_keys
tools.title: List team SSH keys
tools.description: The team's saved SSH public keys (id, name, fingerprint, public key). Public keys only; read-only. GET /ssh-keys.

tools.name: spinupwp_purge_page_cache
tools.title: Purge page cache
tools.description: WRITE: purge the nginx page cache of one site. Pages are rebuilt on the next visit, so the site may be slower for a moment; nothing is lost. Asynchronous: returns an event_id. POST /sites/{id}/page-cache/purge.

tools.name: spinupwp_purge_object_cache
tools.title: Purge object cache
tools.description: WRITE: flush the Redis object cache of one site (the site must have object caching). The cache refills on demand. Asynchronous: returns an event_id. POST /sites/{id}/object-cache/purge.

tools.name: spinupwp_correct_file_permissions
tools.title: Correct file permissions
tools.description: WRITE: reset a site's files and folders to the permissions and ownership SpinupWP recommends (usually after a manual upload as the wrong user). Can take a while on big sites. Asynchronous: returns an event_id. POST /sites/{id}/file-permissions/correct.

tools.name: spinupwp_deploy_site_git
tools.title: Run site git deploy
tools.description: WRITE: pull the latest commit of the site's connected git branch and run its deploy script on the server. This changes the live site's files (and may run build/migration commands); it fails if git is not connected. Asynchronous: returns an event_id. POST /sites/{id}/git/deploy.

tools.name: spinupwp_restart_nginx
tools.title: Restart nginx
tools.description: WRITE: restart nginx (web server) on one server. Visitors may see a brief interruption. Asynchronous: returns an event_id. POST /servers/{id}/services/nginx/restart.

tools.name: spinupwp_restart_php
tools.title: Restart php
tools.description: WRITE: restart PHP-FPM (every PHP version) on one server. Running PHP requests can fail or be cut off while it restarts. Asynchronous: returns an event_id. POST /servers/{id}/services/php/restart.

tools.name: spinupwp_restart_mysql
tools.title: Restart mysql
tools.description: WRITE: restart MySQL (database) on one server. All sites on the server lose database access for a short time; running queries are interrupted. Asynchronous: returns an event_id. POST /servers/{id}/services/mysql/restart.

tools.name: spinupwp_restart_redis
tools.title: Restart redis
tools.description: WRITE: restart Redis (object cache) on one server. Cached objects are lost and rebuilt on demand. Asynchronous: returns an event_id. POST /servers/{id}/services/redis/restart.

tools.name: spinupwp_reboot_server
tools.title: Reboot server
tools.description: WRITE: reboot a whole server. Every site on it is offline for the duration (typically a minute or two). Use it when spinupwp_get_server shows reboot_required. Asynchronous: returns an event_id. POST /servers/{id}/reboot.
