servers.name: Synchroteam
servers.description: Read Synchroteam jobs, customers, sites, equipment and parts; create, schedule and complete jobs.

login.hint: The domain is the first part of your Synchroteam address (**mycompany** for mycompany.synchroteam.com). Find the key in Synchroteam under **Configuration → Authentication Key**. The key is account-wide and acts with administrator rights. It is used only to call the Synchroteam API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List or search customers (name wildcard, e-mail, active flag, change time). Returns name, address, contact, custom fields, tags. GET /customer/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_customer
tools.title: Get customer
tools.description: One customer by id, myId, exact name or e-mail, with address, contact, custom fields and tags. GET /customer/details.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_sites
tools.title: List sites
tools.description: List or search sites (a customer's locations): by name, customer, active flag, change time. GET /site/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_site
tools.title: Get site
tools.description: One site by id, myId or exact name: address, contact, customer, custom fields, tags. GET /site/details.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_equipment
tools.title: List equipment
tools.description: List or search pieces of equipment (assets) by name, customer, site, active flag, change time. GET /equipment/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_equipment
tools.title: Get equipment
tools.description: One piece of equipment by id, myId or exact name, with its customer and site. GET /equipment/details.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_jobs
tools.title: List jobs
tools.description: List jobs (simplified: no report, parts or time entries) filtered by status, schedule window, technician, team, customer, site, equipment, job type or project. Use synchroteam_get_job for the full record. GET /job/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_job
tools.title: Get job
tools.description: One job by num (the job number shown in the app), id or myId: status, customer/site/equipment, technician(s), schedule, actual times, time entries, parts used, report and custom fields. GET /job/details.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_job_photos
tools.title: Get job photos
tools.description: Photo links of a job (url, file name, comment, report iteration). Image bytes are never returned. GET /job/photos.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_job_types
tools.title: List job types
tools.description: List job types (name, default duration, priority, skills, default report). Use their id or name when creating a job. GET /jobtype/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_users
tools.title: List users (technicians and staff)
tools.description: List users: login, name, profile (technician, manager, administrator), teams, skills, last known location. Passwords are never returned. GET /user/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: One user by login or id. GET /user/details.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: List teams with member counts and tags. GET /team/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_parts
tools.title: List parts and services
tools.description: List the parts and services catalog (reference, name, price, category, tax, tracked/serialized flags, type). GET /part/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_part
tools.title: Get part
tools.description: One part or service by id or reference. GET /part/details.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_depots
tools.title: List stock depots
tools.description: List stock depots (warehouses and technician vans). The part quantities of one depot come from synchroteam_get_depot. GET /depot/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_depot
tools.title: Get depot stock
tools.description: One stock depot by id, with the quantity of each part it holds. GET /depot/details.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_part_requests
tools.title: List part requests
tools.description: List technicians' part requests (urgent, sent, completed, deleted flags). GET /partrequest/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices (read only): number, status, customer, job, lines, totals. Filter by status, customer, site, job or time. GET /invoice/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_invoice
tools.title: Get invoice
tools.description: One invoice by id, reference or number, with its lines. GET /invoice/details.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_quotations
tools.title: List quotations
tools.description: List quotations (read only): number, status, customer, job, lines, totals. GET /quotation/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_get_quotation
tools.title: Get quotation
tools.description: One quotation by id, reference or number, with its lines. GET /quotation/details.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_contracts
tools.title: List contracts
tools.description: List service contracts by name, customer, site, period or active flag. GET /contract/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List projects (groups of jobs) by customer, site, equipment or project type. GET /project/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_list_activities
tools.title: List technician activities
tools.description: List time entries and unavailabilities (travel, at work, clock, unavailable) of technicians. start_date and end_date go together and return anything overlapping that range. GET /activity/list.

tools.name: synchroteam_create_customer
tools.title: Create customer
tools.description: WRITE: create a new customer (name and an address are required). If you pass myId and a customer with that myId already exists, nothing is created and an error is returned (use synchroteam_update_customer). POST /customer/send.

tools.name: synchroteam_update_customer
tools.title: Update customer
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing customer by its numeric id. Only the fields you pass are changed; nothing is cleared. The customer id must exist (an unknown id fails). POST /customer/send.

tools.name: synchroteam_create_site
tools.title: Create site
tools.description: WRITE: create a new site (a location of a customer). Needs a name, an address and the customer (id or myId). If myId already exists nothing is created and an error is returned. POST /site/send.

tools.name: synchroteam_create_equipment
tools.title: Create equipment
tools.description: WRITE: create a new piece of equipment under a site or a customer (give exactly one of site or customer; both is refused). If myId already exists nothing is created and an error is returned. POST /equipment/send.

tools.name: synchroteam_create_job
tools.title: Create job
tools.description: WRITE: create a new job for a customer (status created, not yet scheduled; use synchroteam_schedule_job to assign a technician and time). The customer is required (id, myId or exact name); site, equipment and job type are optional. If myId already exists nothing is created and an error is returned. Synchroteam may send the account's 'job created' notifications (email/SMS/webhook, possibly to the customer), as configured. POST /job/send.

tools.name: synchroteam_schedule_job
tools.title: Schedule job
tools.description: WRITE: schedule a job for a technician between two times (also re-schedules a scheduled or paused job). Synchroteam may notify technicians and/or customers (email/SMS/webhook) as configured in the account's notification settings (SMS uses the account's paid credits). Identify the job by exactly one of id, my_id or num. POST /job/schedule.

tools.name: synchroteam_start_job
tools.title: Start job
tools.description: WRITE: mark a job as started (status started, actual start now). If the job's technician already has another started job, Synchroteam pauses that one. Starting may trigger the account's 'job started' notifications (email/SMS/webhook to managers, technicians or the customer). Identify the job by exactly one of id, my_id or num. POST /job/start.

tools.name: synchroteam_complete_job
tools.title: Complete job
tools.description: WRITE: mark a job as completed, optionally with the real start and end times (give actual_start and actual_end together: Synchroteam may refuse the call with only one of them). Completing may trigger the account's 'job completed' notifications (email/SMS/webhook to managers, technicians or the customer), as configured in Synchroteam. Identify the job by exactly one of id, my_id or num. POST /job/complete.

tools.name: synchroteam_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: synchroteam_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Synchroteam tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: synchroteam_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Synchroteam (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: synchroteam_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Synchroteam Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run synchroteam_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

Find customer Acme Ltd and show their sites and equipment.
Which invoices did we issue recently and what are their totals?
Create a new job for Acme Ltd to fix the air conditioner.

servers.name: Dead Man's Snitch
servers.description: Read Dead Man's Snitch monitors and status; create, tag, pause and unpause snitches.

login.hint: Create a key on the **API Keys** page of your Dead Man's Snitch account (the API needs a paid plan). A separate key for this connection makes it easy to revoke. Your key is used only to call the Dead Man's Snitch API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: deadmanssnitch_list_snitches
tools.title: List snitches
tools.description: List the snitches (cron/heartbeat monitors) of the account with status (pending, healthy, failed, errored, paused), interval, alert type, tags and last check-in. Tokens are masked (the token is also the check-in secret); pass the masked token or the name to the other snitch tools. The API has no paging: all snitches come back. Optionally filter by tags (must have all) or status. GET /v1/snitches.

tools.name: deadmanssnitch_get_snitch
tools.title: Get snitch
tools.description: One snitch with its full details, including the check-in URL (https://nosnch.in/<token>). The check-in URL is a secret: anyone who has it can check in and so silence the alert; share it only where the job runs. GET /v1/snitches/{token}.

tools.name: deadmanssnitch_create_snitch
tools.title: Create snitch
tools.description: WRITE: create a new snitch (monitor). Returns it with its check-in URL (https://nosnch.in/<token>), which the job must call on every run; keep it secret. Fails with 402 when the plan's snitch limit is reached. POST /v1/snitches.

tools.name: deadmanssnitch_update_snitch
tools.title: Update snitch
tools.description: WRITE: change a snitch. Only the fields you pass change. `tags` REPLACES the whole tag list (use deadmanssnitch_add_tags to add) and `alert_email` replaces the alert recipients (an empty list = all team members). Returns the updated snitch with the token masked. PATCH /v1/snitches/{token}.

tools.name: deadmanssnitch_add_tags
tools.title: Add tags
tools.description: WRITE: add one or more tags to a snitch, keeping the existing ones. Returns the snitch's full tag list. POST /v1/snitches/{token}/tags.

tools.name: deadmanssnitch_remove_tag
tools.title: Remove tag
tools.description: WRITE: remove one tag from a snitch (the snitch itself is untouched). Returns the remaining tags. DELETE /v1/snitches/{token}/tags/{tag}.

tools.name: deadmanssnitch_pause_snitch
tools.title: Pause snitch
tools.description: WRITE: pause a snitch, which SILENCES its alerts: a job that stops running goes unnoticed while it is paused. `until` says when alerting resumes: 'healthy' (default: on the next healthy check-in), 'unpaused' (stays paused until deadmanssnitch_unpause_snitch) or a future ISO 8601 time. A snitch that has never checked in (pending) cannot be paused. POST /v1/snitches/{token}/pause.

tools.name: deadmanssnitch_unpause_snitch
tools.title: Unpause snitch
tools.description: WRITE: resume alerting for a paused snitch (safe on a snitch that is not paused). POST /v1/snitches/{token}/unpause.

servers.name: WhatConverts
servers.description: Read WhatConverts leads, calls, forms, accounts and profiles; add leads and update lead value.

login.hint: In WhatConverts open **Tracking → Integrations → API Keys** inside a profile and click Generate API Key (a profile key sees that profile). Agency plans can use **Integrations → API Keys** in the agency dashboard for a master key that also reaches accounts, profiles and users. Your key is used only to call the WhatConverts API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: whatconverts_list_leads
tools.title: List leads
tools.description: List tracked leads (phone calls, web forms, chats, texts, emails, events, transactions) with source/medium/campaign/keyword attribution, contact details, quote and sales values, call duration and transcripts. start_date is REQUIRED because WhatConverts otherwise returns only today's leads; a range is at most 400 days. A Profile key sees its own profile; an Agency key can narrow by account_id/profile_id. GET /leads.

tools.name: whatconverts_get_lead
tools.title: Get lead
tools.description: One lead by id with every field: type, status, attribution (source, medium, campaign, keyword, landing page), contact details, location, device, quote/sales value, call details, transcripts, form/message content, and custom fields. GET /leads/{lead_id}.

tools.name: whatconverts_get_call_recording_info
tools.title: Get call recording info
tools.description: Recording and voicemail facts for a phone-call lead: the recording and voicemail links, call duration, answer status, tracking/caller numbers and the call/voicemail transcripts. Returns links and text only, never audio. Taken from GET /leads/{lead_id} (the audio endpoint GET /recording returns raw MP3 and is not used).

tools.name: whatconverts_update_lead
tools.title: Update lead
tools.description: WRITE: update a lead's sales data in WhatConverts: quotable state, quote value, sales value, the URL where the lead occurred, and/or custom/additional field values. Only the fields you pass change; it overwrites the previous values of those fields. Sends no notifications. At least one field is required. POST /leads/{lead_id}.

tools.name: whatconverts_create_lead
tools.title: Create lead
tools.description: WRITE: add a lead to WhatConverts, for example an offline phone call, a form submission from another system or a sale you want attributed. It appears in reports and counts toward lead totals; send_notification is always off, so no emails go out. Not idempotent: calling twice creates two leads. A Profile key adds to its own profile; an Agency key must pass profile_id. POST /leads.

tools.name: whatconverts_list_accounts
tools.title: List accounts
tools.description: Agency key only: list the accounts (clients) of the agency with their profiles (id, name, date created). Use the ids to filter leads. start_date/end_date filter by creation date (WhatConverts defaults start_date to today, so pass an early start_date to see all). GET /accounts.

tools.name: whatconverts_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: Agency key only: one account by id with its profiles. GET /accounts/{account_id}.

tools.name: whatconverts_list_profiles
tools.title: List profiles
tools.description: Agency key only: list the profiles (websites/campaign sets) of one account. start_date/end_date filter by creation date (WhatConverts defaults start_date to today, so pass an early start_date to see all). GET /accounts/{account_id}/profiles.

tools.name: whatconverts_get_profile
tools.title: Get profile
tools.description: Agency key only: one profile by id (name, date created). GET /accounts/{account_id}/profiles/{profile_id}.

tools.name: whatconverts_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: Agency key only: list WhatConverts users (email, role, whether activation is pending) of the master account or of client accounts. start_date/end_date filter by creation date (WhatConverts defaults start_date to today, so pass an early start_date to see all). GET /users.

tools.name: whatconverts_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: Agency key only: one user by id with role, notification settings and (for account users) the accounts they can access. GET /users/{user_id}.

tools.name: whatconverts_list_roles
tools.title: List roles
tools.description: Agency key only: list user roles (id, name, master-account or account type). GET /roles.

tools.name: whatconverts_get_role
tools.title: Get role
tools.description: Agency key only: one role with its permission levels (none/view/edit) per area. GET /roles/{role_id}.

tools.name: whatconverts_list_phone_numbers
tools.title: List tracking phone numbers
tools.description: List the call-tracking numbers: tracking and destination number, call flow, trigger (source/medium), call recording and messaging flags, last used. A Profile key lists its own profile; an Agency key may filter by account_id/profile_id. GET /tracking/numbers.

tools.name: whatconverts_list_web_forms
tools.title: List tracked web forms
tools.description: List the web forms WhatConverts tracks (id, name, how the form and its submit are matched on the page). A Profile key lists its own profile; an Agency key may filter by account_id/profile_id. GET /tracking/forms.

tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)

Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: AddEvent
servers.description: Read AddEvent calendars, events, RSVPs and subscribers; create and update calendars and events.

login.hint: Find it in the AddEvent dashboard under **Account settings**. API access needs a paid AddEvent plan. The key gives full access to your account's calendars and events; it is used only to call the AddEvent API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: addevent_list_calendars
tools.title: List calendars
tools.description: List the account's calendars (newest first by default) with id, title, timezone, whether it is the default calendar, landing-page links and counts of events and subscribers. GET /calendars.

tools.name: addevent_get_calendar
tools.title: Get calendar
tools.description: One calendar by id: title, timezone, week start, template ids, subscriber and event counts, links, custom data. GET /calendars/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_create_calendar
tools.title: Create calendar
tools.description: WRITE: creates a new calendar in the AddEvent account (a new, empty calendar; nothing existing is changed and nobody is notified). Needs a title. POST /calendars.

tools.name: addevent_update_calendar
tools.title: Update calendar
tools.description: WRITE: changes fields of an existing calendar (only the fields you pass; the rest stay). Title, description and timezone changes show on its landing page and can reach people who subscribe to the calendar feed. Not reversible by this server (no previous values are kept), so read the calendar first. PATCH /calendars/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: Search the account's events (newest created first; by start time when a date filter is used): title, start/end, timezone, location, RSVP settings and stats, landing-page links. Filter by calendar, event ids, text, date window or a custom_data pair. GET /events.

tools.name: addevent_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event by id (evt-...): all fields incl. description, organizer, reminder, recurring rule, RSVP settings and stats, custom data and share links. GET /events/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_create_event
tools.title: Create event
tools.description: WRITE: creates a new event on a calendar (the account's default calendar if calendar_id is omitted). Creates a public event landing page and share links; it does not e-mail anyone, though people subscribed to that calendar's feed will see the event on their next sync. Needs title and datetime_start. POST /events.

tools.name: addevent_update_event
tools.title: Update event
tools.description: WRITE: changes fields of an existing event (only the fields you pass; the rest stay). The change goes live on its landing page and share links, and people who subscribed to the calendar or added the event with a live link are updated on their next calendar sync, so a time or location change can notify real people. No previous values are kept: read the event first. PATCH /events/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_list_rsvp_attendees
tools.title: List RSVP attendees
tools.description: List RSVP attendees (personal data: e-mail addresses and the answers they gave on the RSVP form). Filter by calendar, event or response (going/maybe/not-going). Paged, 20 at most per page: read only what the task needs. IP address and coordinates are removed from the reply. GET /rsvps.

tools.name: addevent_get_rsvp_attendee
tools.title: Get RSVP attendee
tools.description: One RSVP attendee by id (personal data: e-mail and form answers; IP address and coordinates removed). GET /rsvps/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_create_rsvp_attendee
tools.title: Create RSVP attendee
tools.description: WRITE: adds ONE RSVP attendee (one e-mail address, personal data) to an event. This server never asks AddEvent to send the confirmation or organizer notification e-mails, but the event's own reminder and follow-up e-mails (if the event has them) will later go to this address, so only add someone who really RSVP'd. The e-mail must be unique per event. POST /events/{id}/rsvps.

tools.name: addevent_update_rsvp_attendee
tools.title: Update RSVP attendee
tools.description: WRITE: changes ONE RSVP attendee (email, response or form answers; only the fields you pass). The event's reminder and update e-mails go to the e-mail address stored here, so changing it redirects those e-mails to that person. This server never triggers the confirmation or organizer notification e-mails. PATCH /rsvps/{id}.

tools.name: addevent_list_calendar_subscribers

tools.name: addevent_get_calendar_subscriber

tools.name: addevent_list_rsvp_forms

tools.name: addevent_list_event_templates
tools.title: List event landing page templates

tools.name: addevent_list_calendar_templates
tools.title: List calendar templates
tools.description: The account's calendar landing page templates or embeddable calendar templates (id, name), newest first. Use the id as landing_page_template_id / embeddable_calendar_template_id on a calendar. GET /calendars/templates.

tools.name: addevent_list_timezones
tools.title: List timezones

tools.name: addevent_usage_status

servers.name: Helpwise
servers.description: Read Helpwise conversations, contacts, tags and reports; note, tag, assign, close; send one email.

login.hint: Find both in Helpwise under **Settings → Integrations → API** (the API needs a plan that includes API access, Premium and up). Your key and secret are used only to call the Helpwise API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: helpwise_list_conversations

tools.description: List conversations (threads) of one or more inboxes, newest first, with subject, snippet, tags, assignee, read/starred/closed flags and contact. Pick the folder with `folder` (default: all). Page with `next_page_token`. Inbox ids come from helpwise_list_inboxes. GET /conversations.

tools.name: helpwise_get_conversation
tools.title: Get conversation
tools.description: One conversation with its messages, notes, drafts, assignment and contacts. Page long conversations with `page_token` from the previous reply. GET /inboxes/{inbox_id}/conversations/{conversation_id}.

tools.name: helpwise_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts (name, company, job title, emails, phones, id). Page with limit and offset. GET /contacts.

tools.name: helpwise_search_contacts
tools.title: Search contacts
tools.description: Search contacts by a name, email or phone term. Page with limit and offset. GET /contacts/search.

tools.name: helpwise_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact with emails, phones, company, custom fields and recent conversations. GET /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: helpwise_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: All tags (id, name, colour, parent, inbox). Use the ids with helpwise_apply_tags. GET /tags.

tools.name: helpwise_get_tag
tools.title: Get tag
tools.description: One tag by id. GET /tags/{id}.

tools.name: helpwise_get_report

tools.name: helpwise_get_tags_report

tools.name: helpwise_list_inboxes

tools.name: helpwise_list_users

tools.name: helpwise_get_current_user
tools.title: Get current user
tools.description: The Helpwise user the API key belongs to (name, email, id). POST /users/me (V0).

tools.name: helpwise_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: create a new contact in Helpwise (name, company, job title, emails, phones, custom fields). Nothing is sent to the person. Creating the same email twice may create a duplicate. POST /contacts.

tools.name: helpwise_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: change a contact's name, company, job title, emails, phones or custom fields. Helpwise updates with PUT, so this tool first reads the contact and sends the current values together with your changes; a list you pass (emails, phones, custom_fields) REPLACES the old list. Nothing is sent to the person. PUT /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: helpwise_add_note
tools.title: Add note
tools.description: WRITE: add an internal note to a conversation. Visible to your Helpwise team only; it is not sent to the customer. Notes cannot be deleted through this API. POST /notes/add (V0).

tools.name: helpwise_assign_conversation

tools.name: helpwise_close_conversations

tools.name: helpwise_reopen_conversations

tools.name: helpwise_remove_tags

tools.name: helpwise_send_email

servers.name: Qgiv
servers.description: Read Qgiv (Bloomerang Fundraising) donations, refunds, recurring gifts, P2P registrations, events.

login.hint: In Qgiv open **Data Tools > API Access > Create API Token** and select the forms it may read. The token is used only to call the Qgiv API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone. Donor contact details are returned only when you ask for them.

tools.name: qgiv_list_recent_transactions
tools.title: List recent transactions
tools.description: The most recent donations/transactions (newest first as Qgiv returns them): id, status, date, amount, fee, net, donor name and id, form, recurring link, payment type and last four card digits, fund. Donor contact details are left out unless include_contact is set; full card numbers are never returned. POST /reporting/transactions/last/{limit}.

tools.name: qgiv_list_transactions_by_date
tools.title: List transactions by date range
tools.description: Transactions between two dates (inclusive), at most 31 days per call, paged with offset/limit. Same fields as qgiv_list_recent_transactions. Qgiv has no server-side paging, so a busy range is fetched whole and sliced; use a shorter range if it is too large. POST /reporting/transactions/dates/{begin}:{end}.

tools.name: qgiv_list_transactions_after_id
tools.title: List transactions after an id
tools.description: Transactions with an id greater than the given one, sorted by id ascending and paged with limit; next_after_id is the cursor for the next call (use it as after_id). Handy for syncing new gifts. POST /reporting/transactions/after/{id}.

tools.name: qgiv_get_transaction
tools.title: Get transaction
tools.description: One transaction in full: donation lines, fund/restriction, dedication, custom-field answers, event packages, registrations, refunds. Contact details only with include_contact; card data is reduced to the last four digits. POST /reporting/transactions/{id}.

tools.name: qgiv_list_recent_refunds
tools.title: List recent refunds
tools.description: The most recent refunds (read-only): id, original transaction, refund and settle dates, amount, payment type, last four digits, fund. POST /reporting/refunds/last/{limit}.

tools.name: qgiv_list_refunds_by_date
tools.title: List refunds by date range
tools.description: Refunds between two dates (inclusive), at most 31 days per call, paged with offset/limit. POST /reporting/refunds/dates/{begin}:{end}.

tools.name: qgiv_get_refund
tools.title: Get refund
tools.description: One refund in full by id (read-only; this server never issues refunds). POST /reporting/refunds/{id}.

tools.name: qgiv_list_recurring_schedules
tools.title: List recurring gift schedules
tools.description: Recurring donation schedules (read-only): id, start/end date, next billing date, frequency, amount, state, donor name and id, plus Qgiv's 12-month forecast. Filter by status active, paused, expired or deleted. Paged with offset/limit. POST /reporting/recurring/list or /reporting/recurring/{status}.

tools.name: qgiv_get_recurring_schedule
tools.title: Get recurring gift schedule
tools.description: One recurring donation schedule by id (read-only; schedules cannot be changed here). POST /reporting/recurring/{id}.

tools.name: qgiv_list_statements
tools.title: List statements
tools.description: Monthly fee/payout statements: id, date, amount contributed, fees, refunded, debited, credited and the summary totals (without the per-transaction rows; use qgiv_get_statement for those). Paged with offset/limit. POST /reporting/statements/list.

tools.name: qgiv_get_latest_statements
tools.title: Get latest statements
tools.description: The latest statement(s) for the organization or form, with summary totals (per-transaction rows left out). POST /reporting/statements/latest.

tools.name: qgiv_get_statement
tools.title: Get statement
tools.description: One statement by id with its transaction rows (first 100 shown; donor names only). POST /reporting/statements/{id}.

tools.name: qgiv_list_recent_registrations
tools.title: List recent P2P registrations
tools.description: The most recent peer-to-peer (Hobnob) event registrations: id, category, registrant name, team, fundraising goal and amount raised. Contact details only with include_contact. POST /reporting/registrations/last/{limit}.

tools.name: qgiv_list_registrations_by_date
tools.title: List P2P registrations by date range
tools.description: Peer-to-peer registrations between two dates (inclusive), at most 31 days per call, paged with offset/limit. POST /reporting/registrations/dates/{begin}:{end}.

tools.name: qgiv_get_registration
tools.title: Get P2P registration
tools.description: One peer-to-peer registration in full (purchase history, team, totals, child registrations). Contact details only with include_contact. POST /reporting/registrations/{id}.

tools.name: qgiv_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: Events (ticketed/auction events) on the forms the token covers: id, dates and the top-level settings. Set include_details for packages, questions and promo codes. Notification e-mail addresses are never returned. POST /events/list.

tools.name: qgiv_list_pledges
tools.title: List pledge options

tools.name: qgiv_get_pledge
tools.title: Get pledge option

tools.name: qgiv_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List custom fields
tools.description: Custom (additional-question) fields configured on the form(s): id, reference, title, input type, required flags, display flags. POST /customFields/list.

tools.name: qgiv_list_report_mappings
tools.title: List report mappings
tools.description: Report mappings (accounting export mappings) on the form(s): id, identifier, mapping data, export service, type. POST /reporting/mappings/list.

servers.name: Starshipit
servers.description: Read Starshipit orders, tracking, rates and manifests; create and update unshipped orders.

login.hint: Find both in Starshipit under **Settings → API** (the API key is the StarShipIT-Api-Key, the subscription key is the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key; generate them there if they are empty). The keys are used only to call the Starshipit API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: starshipit_list_unshipped_orders
tools.title: List unshipped orders
tools.description: List unshipped (new, not yet printed) orders with full details: addresses, items, packages, carrier. By default only orders updated in the last 24 hours; use since_order_date / since_last_updated to look further back. ids_only=true returns just the order ids. GET /api/orders/unshipped.

tools.name: starshipit_list_shipped_orders
tools.title: List shipped orders
tools.description: List shipped orders (label printed) with tracking number, tracking status, carrier, manifest and shipped date. By default only orders updated in the last 24 hours; use since_last_updated to look further back. Label files are not returned. GET /api/orders/shipped.

tools.name: starshipit_list_printed_orders
tools.title: List printed or unmanifested orders
tools.description: List orders whose label was recently printed, or printed but not yet manifested, with tracking numbers. GET /api/orders/shipments.

tools.name: starshipit_list_delivered_orders
tools.title: List delivered orders by reference
tools.description: List delivered orders that carry a given order reference (the customer reference), with full order details. GET /api/orders/delivered.

tools.name: starshipit_orders_summary
tools.title: Orders summary by status
tools.description: A compact list of orders in one status (new, printed, shipped, archived) with contact, country, carrier, weight, manifest and dates, plus account-wide counts (unprinted, printed, shipped, archived, invalid addresses, returns). Supports filters and sorting. GET /api/orders/summary.

tools.name: starshipit_search_orders
tools.title: Search orders
tools.description: Search orders by order number, tracking number, customer reference or recipient name (phrase), optionally limited to unshipped or shipped orders. Returns id, number, date, name, carrier, tracking number and country. GET /api/orders/search.

tools.name: starshipit_get_order
tools.title: Get one order
tools.description: One order by Starshipit order_id or by the order_number from the source platform. Use include to add sections (Items, Packages, Events, Metadatas, Shipping_Price, ...). Status defaults to Unshipped in Starshipit, so pass status=Shipped or Printed for orders already printed. Label files are not returned. GET /api/orders?order_id= or ?order_number=.

tools.name: starshipit_list_orders
tools.title: List orders with filters
tools.description: List full order details for one status (Unshipped by default, or Shipped / Printed), narrowed by a filter such as `Order:::1419,Country:::Australia` and sorted. Heavier than the summary: use starshipit_orders_summary for overviews. Label files are not returned. GET /api/orders (no id).

tools.name: starshipit_track_shipment

tools.description: Tracking details for a shipped order, by tracking number or by order number: status, carrier, tracking URL, shipment date and the carrier's tracking events. GET /api/track.

tools.name: starshipit_get_rates
tools.title: Quote shipping rates
tools.description: QUOTE ONLY: shipping rates (service name, code, price) for a destination and parcels from the couriers enabled in the account. Nothing is purchased, created or printed. The sender defaults to the account's pickup address. Needs at least one enabled courier. POST /api/rates.

tools.name: starshipit_list_address_book
tools.title: List address book
tools.description: List contacts in the account's address book (name, company, address, phone, email), sorted by a column. GET /api/addressbook/filtered.

tools.name: starshipit_list_manifests
tools.title: List manifests
tools.description: List manifests already submitted to carriers (newest first): number, date, carrier, package and consignment counts. Read only; manifesting is not available here. GET /api/manifests.

tools.name: starshipit_list_products
tools.title: List product catalogue
tools.description: List Product Catalogue records (SKU, title, weight, dimensions, HS code, bin location, price), optionally searching by SKU or title. GET /api/products.

tools.name: starshipit_list_tags
tools.title: List order tags
tools.description: List the account's user-defined order tags, optionally filtered by tag name. GET /api/tags.

tools.name: starshipit_list_pickups

tools.description: List courier pickups already booked for the account. Read only; booking a pickup is not available here. GET /api/pickup.

tools.name: starshipit_create_order
tools.title: Create an unshipped order

tools.name: starshipit_update_order

tools.name: starshipit_add_order_tags

servers.name: Buttondown
servers.description: Read Buttondown subscribers, emails, analytics and automations; add subscribers; write email drafts.

login.hint: Find your key at [buttondown.com/keys](https://buttondown.com/keys). A key with write access to subscribers, emails and tags makes every tool work; a read-only key works for the read tools. Your key is used only to call the Buttondown API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: buttondown_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The Buttondown account this API key belongs to: username and e-mail address. GET /accounts/me.

tools.name: buttondown_list_newsletters
tools.title: List newsletters
tools.description: List the newsletters on the account with name, username, domains, sender, locale and timezone. The newsletter's API key, custom CSS and e-mail templates are never returned. GET /newsletters.

tools.name: buttondown_get_newsletter
tools.title: Get newsletter
tools.description: One newsletter by id (settings and identity only; no API key, CSS or templates). GET /newsletters/{id}.

tools.name: buttondown_list_subscribers
tools.title: List subscribers
tools.description: List or search subscribers (newest first by default) with e-mail, type (regular, unactivated, unsubscribed, premium, ...), tags, notes, metadata, source, open/click rates and dates. Filter by e-mail text, type, tag, signup date or domain. GET /subscribers.

tools.name: buttondown_get_subscriber
tools.title: Get subscriber
tools.description: One subscriber by id or by e-mail address: type, tags, notes, metadata, source, engagement and lifecycle dates. GET /subscribers/{id_or_email}.

tools.name: buttondown_add_subscriber
tools.title: Add a subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: add ONE subscriber by e-mail address. No subscriber type is set, so Buttondown applies the newsletter's normal sign-up rules (double opt-in: the subscriber is typically created as unactivated and Buttondown e-mails THAT ONE address a confirmation message; opt-in is never bypassed, nor is the firewall). Only add people who asked to subscribe. Creating a subscriber (and its tags) can also start the newsletter's own automations, which may e-mail that one subscriber. An existing e-mail is left untouched (error, no overwrite). Optional tags (a tag that does not exist is created, which needs a plan with tags), a private note and metadata. Buttondown limits creation to 100 subscribers per day. POST /subscribers.

tools.name: buttondown_update_subscriber
tools.title: Update a subscriber's tags, notes or metadata
tools.description: WRITE: change ONE subscriber's tags, private note or metadata. Tags are merged (add_tags / remove_tags change only those names; the others stay). A given note or metadata replaces the existing value (destructive for that field). The subscriber's type (unsubscribe, block, ...) and e-mail address cannot be changed here, and this tool sends nothing itself; but a tag, note or metadata change can start the newsletter's own automations (for example a tag-triggered welcome sequence), which may e-mail that one subscriber. PATCH /subscribers/{id_or_email}.

tools.name: buttondown_list_emails
tools.title: List emails
tools.description: List emails (drafts, scheduled and sent), newest first by default, with subject, status, publish date, slug, archive URL and analytics summary. The body is left out unless include_body is set. Filter by status, subject text or date. GET /emails.

tools.name: buttondown_get_email
tools.title: Get email
tools.description: One email by id with its full body, subject, status, publish date, slug, archive settings and analytics summary. GET /emails/{id}.

tools.name: buttondown_get_email_analytics
tools.title: Get email analytics
tools.description: Delivery and engagement numbers for one sent email: recipients, deliveries, opens, clicks, failures, unsubscriptions, complaints, replies, page views. GET /emails/{id}/analytics.

tools.name: buttondown_create_email_draft
tools.title: Create an email draft
tools.description: WRITE: create a DRAFT email (status always "draft"). Nothing is sent or scheduled and no subscriber is e-mailed; to send it, the user must open the draft in Buttondown and send it there. This server has no tool that sends or schedules email. Body is Markdown or HTML. POST /emails.

tools.name: buttondown_update_email_draft
tools.title: Edit an email draft
tools.description: WRITE: edit the subject, body, description, slug or preview image of an email that is still a DRAFT (replaces those fields; the previous text is lost unless Buttondown's email history is used). Refuses any email that is not a draft, and never changes status or publish date, so nothing is sent or scheduled. PATCH /emails/{id}.

tools.name: buttondown_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: List subscriber tags with name, color, descriptions and whether subscribers can edit them. GET /tags.

tools.name: buttondown_get_tag_analytics
tools.title: Get tag analytics
tools.description: Subscribers created, open rate and click rate for one tag. GET /tags/{id}/analytics.

tools.name: buttondown_create_tag
tools.title: Create a tag
tools.description: WRITE: create a subscriber tag (needs a Buttondown plan with tags). An existing tag with the same name is returned as an error and not changed. POST /tags.

tools.name: buttondown_list_automations
tools.title: List automations
tools.description: List automations (welcome sequences and other triggered e-mails) with name, status, trigger, actions and filters (webhook URLs in actions are shown by host only). Read-only: automations are not started or changed. GET /automations.

tools.name: buttondown_get_automation
tools.title: Get automation
tools.description: One automation by id with its trigger, actions and filters. GET /automations/{id}.

tools.name: buttondown_get_automation_analytics
tools.title: Get automation analytics
tools.description: Performance numbers for one automation. GET /automations/{id}/analytics.

tools.name: buttondown_list_surveys
tools.title: List surveys
tools.description: List surveys with question, answers, status and response count. GET /surveys.

tools.name: buttondown_list_survey_responses
tools.title: List survey responses
tools.description: List survey responses (who answered what), optionally for one survey, email or subscriber. GET /survey_responses.

tools.name: buttondown_list_segments
tools.title: List segments
tools.description: List saved subscriber segments with name, description and filters. GET /segments.

tools.name: buttondown_list_forms
tools.title: List forms
tools.description: List sign-up forms with title, slug, status, tags and subscriber counts. GET /forms.

tools.name: buttondown_list_snippets
tools.title: List snippets
tools.description: List reusable content snippets with identifier, name, mode and how often each is referenced. GET /snippets.

tools.name: buttondown_list_webhooks
tools.title: List webhooks
tools.description: List configured webhooks with status and subscribed event types. The signing key is never returned and the URL is shown by host only. GET /webhooks.

tools.name: buttondown_list_events
tools.title: List email events
tools.description: List delivery events (delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, unsubscribed, ...), newest first, optionally for one email or subscriber. GET /events.

tools.name: buttondown_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: buttondown_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Buttondown tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: buttondown_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Buttondown (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: buttondown_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Buttondown Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run buttondown_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: How many subscribers do I have and who joined this week?
How did my last newsletter perform on opens and clicks?
Which drafts and scheduled emails do I have right now?
Write a draft email called June Update with a short intro.

servers.name: SuperFaktura
servers.description: Read SuperFaktura invoices, clients, expenses, bank and stock; create clients, expenses and drafts.

login.hint: In SuperFaktura open **Tools → API access** (Nástroje → API prístup) for the e-mail, API key and company id. **API access is only included in the top SuperFaktura plan** (the price list shows API as not available on the lower plans), so a lower plan cannot connect. The company id is optional (leave it empty for your default company). Pick the instance you log in to (SK, CZ or AT). A dedicated user with the Administrator role is recommended. SuperFaktura allows 1000 API requests per day and 31000 per month per account. Your key is used only to call the SuperFaktura API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: superfaktura_get_company
tools.title: Get the company profile and API limits
tools.description: The company the API key is working in (name, IČO, DIČ, IČ DPH, address, VAT-payer flag, bank accounts) and the remaining API quota (SuperFaktura's fair-use policy is 1000 requests per day and 31000 per month; every tool call here uses one request). Good first call. With all_companies=true also the other companies the user can access (their ids are the company_id of the login). GET /users/getUserCompaniesData.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_invoices
tools.title: List or search invoices
tools.description: List issued documents with client, items, totals and payment status. type selects the document kind (default regular = ordinary invoices; also proforma, estimate = quote, order, cancel = credit note, delivery, draft, reverse_order; several allowed). Without a date filter SuperFaktura returns only the CURRENT YEAR; use created_period='all' or a date range for older ones. status: issued, partially_paid, paid, overdue. search matches client name, number, VS ... Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /invoices/index.json.

tools.name: superfaktura_get_invoice
tools.title: Get an invoice
tools.description: One document (invoice, proforma, quote ...) with its header (number, dates, status, amounts, currency, symbols, comments), client, items, VAT summary, payments and related documents. The public access token and payment links of the document are not returned. GET /invoices/view/{id}.json.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_clients
tools.title: List or search clients
tools.description: List the address book (clients and suppliers) with contact data and totals. search matches name, IČO, DIČ, IČ DPH, bank account, e-mail, address, city, phone, note and tags. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /clients/index.json.

tools.name: superfaktura_get_client
tools.title: Get a client
tools.description: One client with address, tax ids, bank data, default currency/due days/discount and statistics. GET /clients/view/{id}.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_contact_persons
tools.title: List a client's contact persons
tools.description: The contact persons (name, e-mail, phone) stored for one client. GET /contact_people/getContactPeople/{client_id}.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_expenses
tools.title: List or search expenses
tools.description: List received documents (expenses: received invoices, bills, internal documents) with amounts, VAT, supplier and payment status. status: issued (new), partially_paid, paid, overdue. Without a date filter SuperFaktura applies its default period; pass created_period='all' for everything. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /expenses/index.json.

tools.name: superfaktura_get_expense
tools.title: Get an expense
tools.description: One expense with its items, VAT rates, payments and supplier. Attachments are not returned. GET /expenses/view/{id}.json.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_expense_categories
tools.title: List expense categories
tools.description: The expense category tree (id, name, parent) for the category_id of expenses. GET /expenses/expense_categories.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_bank_accounts
tools.title: List bank accounts
tools.description: The company's bank accounts as stored in SuperFaktura (bank name, IBAN, SWIFT, default flag). GET /bank_accounts/index.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_bank_moves
tools.title: List imported bank account moves
tools.description: Bank transactions imported into SuperFaktura (date, amount, currency, variable symbol, counter account, matching state), newest first by default. Filter by date range, credit/debit or amount. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /accounts/index.json.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_cash_registers
tools.title: List cash registers
tools.description: The company's cash registers with currency, number of entries and current balance (read only). GET /cash_registers/getDetails.

tools.name: superfaktura_get_cash_register
tools.title: Get a cash register
tools.description: One cash register with currency, number of entries and current balance (read only). GET /cash_registers/view/{id}.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_stock_items
tools.title: List or search stock items
tools.description: List warehouse items (name, SKU, unit, price, VAT, quantity in stock). search matches name, SKU and description; sku matches the SKU. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /stock_items/index.json.

tools.name: superfaktura_get_stock_item
tools.title: Get a stock item
tools.description: One warehouse item with SKU, price, VAT, purchase price and quantity in stock. GET /stock_items/view/{id}.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_stock_movements
tools.title: List stock movements of an item
tools.description: The stock log of one item (quantity changes, notes, related invoice or expense). Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /stock_items/movements/{id}.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: The tags (id and name) usable on invoices, expenses and clients. GET /tags/index.json.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_sequences
tools.title: List numbering sequences
tools.description: The document numbering sequences per document type (id, name, mask, next formatted number, default flag); sequence ids are used when creating documents. GET /sequences/index.json.

tools.name: superfaktura_list_countries
tools.title: List countries
tools.description: SuperFaktura's country ids with ISO code and EU flag, for the country_id of clients. GET /countries/index/view_full:1.

tools.name: superfaktura_get_response_by_checksum
tools.title: Recover the reply of a create by its checksum
tools.description: If a superfaktura_create_invoice call timed out, fetch the reply of the ORIGINAL request by the checksum it was sent with (kept 3 months), so the document is not created twice. GET /api_logs/getResponseByChecksum/{checksum}.

tools.name: superfaktura_create_client
tools.title: Create a client
tools.description: WRITE: adds a new client to the SuperFaktura address book (only the name is required). Nothing is sent to the client. Not idempotent: calling twice creates two clients, so check superfaktura_list_clients first. POST /clients/create.

tools.name: superfaktura_add_contact_person
tools.title: Add a contact person to a client
tools.description: WRITE: adds a contact person (name and e-mail, optional phone) to an existing client. Nothing is sent to that person. Not idempotent. POST /contact_people/add/api:1.

tools.name: superfaktura_create_tag
tools.title: Create a tag
tools.description: WRITE: adds a new tag name (usable on invoices, expenses and clients in the SuperFaktura app). A duplicate name is refused by SuperFaktura. POST /tags/add.

tools.name: superfaktura_create_expense
tools.title: Record a received expense
tools.description: WRITE: records a received document (expense) with ONE total amount and VAT rate, e.g. a supplier invoice or a bill. It is created unpaid: no payment is recorded and nothing is sent. No attachments. Not idempotent: calling twice records two expenses. POST /expenses/add.

tools.name: superfaktura_create_invoice
tools.title: Create an unsent invoice document
tools.description: WRITE: creates ONE document in SuperFaktura for the user to review: type draft (concept, default), estimate (quote), order or proforma. A final regular invoice cannot be created here. It is NOT sent (no e-mail, no post), NOT marked paid or sent, and has no payment link or discount. Give an existing client_id (its name is read first with one extra GET /clients/view/{id}, so the call uses 2 requests of the daily quota) OR a new client's name (+ optional ico/dic/ic_dph/address...). Items: name, unit price without VAT, VAT rate, quantity. Not idempotent: pass a checksum (max 32 chars) so a timed-out call can be recovered with superfaktura_get_response_by_checksum instead of retried. POST /invoices/create.

tools.name: superfaktura_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: superfaktura_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the SuperFaktura tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: superfaktura_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on SuperFaktura (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: superfaktura_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's SuperFaktura Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run superfaktura_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which of my issued invoices are still unpaid, and how much is owed?
Show the expenses I recorded last month with the amounts.
What is the current balance in my cash register?
Add a new client called Acme Ltd with email billing@acme.com.

servers.name: Accredible
servers.description: Read Accredible credentials, groups, designs, analytics, skills; issue one credential as a draft.

login.hint: Create or copy a key in the Accredible Dashboard ([dashboard.accredible.com](https://dashboard.accredible.com), API keys). An account-wide key sees every department; a department key only its own. Choose the environment your key belongs to: US and EU production accounts use different hosts, and sandbox accounts (Connect and Growth plans) use their own keys. Your key is used only to call the Accredible API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: accredible_get_issuer
tools.title: Get the issuer (account)
tools.description: The Accredible issuer (organization) behind the API key: id, name, e-mail, remaining credential credits (certificate_left), language and URL. Good first call. GET /v1/issuer/details.

tools.name: accredible_search_credentials
tools.title: Search credentials
tools.description: Search issued credentials (badges and certificates) with filters that combine with AND, newest first by default. Returns id, uuid, encoded_id, recipient name/e-mail, group, issued_on, expired_on, published state (approve), whether the recipient opened or engaged, and meta. Paging: size + offset (first 10 000 results) OR cursor: when the reply has next_cursor pass it as cursor for the next page (cursor and offset cannot be combined). POST /v2/credentials/search (a read-only search).

tools.name: accredible_get_credential
tools.title: Get a credential
tools.description: One credential in full: recipient, group, issue and expiry dates, published state, public URL, evidence items, references, custom attributes and skills. The id is the numeric credential id or the custom id your organization set. GET /v1/credentials/{id}.

tools.name: accredible_get_credential_analytics
tools.title: Get a credential's analytics events
tools.description: The analytics events of one credential (recipient views, shares, privacy changes, verification and so on) with timestamps. Read-only despite being a POST. POST /v1/credentials/analytics/{id}.

tools.name: accredible_list_analytics
tools.title: List credential analytics events
tools.description: Account-wide credential analytics events (views, shares, downloads and similar), optionally for a date range, group or department. Paged (default 100 per page). GET /v1/analytics.

tools.name: accredible_search_groups
tools.title: Search groups
tools.description: Search groups (an achievement such as a course or qualification that credentials belong to). Filters combine with AND; name and course_name match partially. Returns id, name, course name and description, design ids, language and dates. Paged: pass meta.next_page as page. POST /v1/issuer/groups/search (a read-only search).

tools.name: accredible_get_group
tools.title: Get a group
tools.description: One group in full: name, course name and description, learning outcomes, design ids, language, skills and dates. GET /v1/issuer/groups/{group_id}.

tools.name: accredible_search_designs
tools.title: Search designs
tools.description: List badge and certificate designs, optionally by kind or meta_data. POST /v1/designs/search (a read-only search).

tools.name: accredible_get_design
tools.title: Get a design
tools.description: One badge or certificate design with its settings. GET /v1/designs/{design_id}.

tools.name: accredible_search_departments
tools.title: Search departments
tools.description: List departments (independent organization units with their own designs, groups and branding). An account-wide key sees all, a department key only its own. Paged: pass meta.next_page as page. POST /v1/departments/search (a read-only search).

tools.name: accredible_get_department
tools.title: Get a department
tools.description: One department: name, description, URL, branding and meta_data. GET /v1/departments/{department_id}.

tools.name: accredible_search_collections
tools.title: Search collections
tools.description: List collections (sets of groups shown together). Filters: ids, name (substring), public. Paged: pass meta.next_page as page. POST /v1/collections/search (a read-only search).

tools.name: accredible_search_attribute_keys
tools.title: Search custom attribute keys
tools.description: List the custom attribute keys (placeholders such as a grade or date that credential designs and e-mails merge in); useful to know which custom_attributes a credential can carry. Paged: pass meta.next_page as page. POST /v1/attribute_keys/search (a read-only search).

tools.name: accredible_list_skill_frameworks
tools.title: List skill frameworks
tools.description: The skills frameworks (O*NET, ESCO, NACE or your own) enabled for a department, each with its published versions. Needs a plan that includes skills frameworks (otherwise HTTP 403 plan_not_entitled). Paged, max 10 per page. GET /v1/skill_frameworks.

tools.name: accredible_search_skills
tools.title: Search skills in a framework version
tools.description: Search the skills of one published skills-framework version by name or the publisher's identifier (partial, case-insensitive, at least 2 characters). Paged, max 50 per page. GET /v1/skill_frameworks/{id}/versions/{version_id}/skills.

tools.name: accredible_list_data_exports
tools.title: List data exports
tools.description: Data exports of the departments the key can access: department, status (scheduled, processing, completed, errored) and download links of completed files. Exports are created in the Accredible Dashboard. GET /v1/data_exports.

tools.name: accredible_get_data_export
tools.title: Get a data export
tools.description: One data export: department, status and, once completed, the download links of its files. GET /v1/data_exports/{id}.

tools.name: accredible_get_team_member
tools.title: Get a team member
tools.description: One team member of the account: name, e-mail and permissions per department. Which members are visible depends on the key (an account-wide key sees all, a department key its own department). GET /v1/team_members/{id}.

tools.name: accredible_issue_credential
tools.title: Issue a credential to ONE recipient
tools.description: WRITE: creates ONE credential (badge or certificate) for ONE recipient in an existing group. By default it is created UNPUBLISHED (a draft: no e-mail is sent and no credit is used); publish it later in the Accredible Dashboard. With publish=true the credential is published immediately: Accredible then SENDS AN E-MAIL to the recipient (as configured in the group's e-mail settings) and uses one credential credit of the account; an account without credits keeps it unpublished. A sandbox-mode setting in the Dashboard overrides publish. Not idempotent: calling twice creates two credentials (set credential_id to your own unique id to be able to find it again). No evidence, references, bulk issuing, edits or deletes. POST /v1/credentials.

Does not count against the meter.
