servers.name: Wincher
servers.description: Read Wincher keyword rankings, SERPs, competitors and history; add keywords, groups and notes.

login.hint: Create it in Wincher → **Account → Personal Access Tokens**. The Wincher API is part of the higher paid plans. The token acts with your user's permissions and is used only to call the Wincher API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: wincher_get_account
tools.title: Get account and plan limits
tools.description: The Wincher account behind the token: id, timezone and the plan limits with current usage (websites, users, keywords, keyword lookups, map-tracking credits, history days). Check keyword usage here before adding keywords. GET /account.

tools.name: wincher_get_user
tools.title: Get current user
tools.description: The Wincher user the token belongs to: id, role, state, project access and profile (name, email, language). GET /user.

tools.name: wincher_list_search_engines
tools.title: List search engines
tools.description: The search engines Wincher can track (id, domain such as google.com, country, languages, default location). GET /search-engines.

tools.name: wincher_search_locations
tools.title: Search tracking locations
tools.description: Search the locations Wincher can track rankings for (code, name, country), most popular first, at most 100. Both are required by the API: an ISO country code and a free-text search (at least 3 characters). GET /locations.

tools.name: wincher_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List projects (folders that group websites): id, name, website_ids, user_ids, and optionally the ranking summary for a period. GET /projects.

tools.name: wincher_list_websites
tools.title: List tracked websites
tools.description: List the websites tracked in Wincher: id, domain, display name, search engine, location, language, mobile flag, keyword/group/competitor counts, competitors and brand keywords. Optionally with the ranking summary for a period. GET /websites.

tools.name: wincher_get_website
tools.title: Get website
tools.description: One tracked website with its settings, competitors, brand keywords, counts and (for the period) ranking summary. GET /websites/{website_id}.

tools.name: wincher_list_keywords
tools.title: List keywords
tools.description: List the keywords tracked for a website with groups, volume, CPC, difficulty, competition, search intents and, with include_ranking, the latest position, traffic, ranking pages, SERP features and best position in the period. Positions are tracked down to the top 30. GET /websites/{website_id}/keywords.

tools.name: wincher_get_keyword
tools.title: Get keyword
tools.description: One tracked keyword with its groups, volume, CPC, difficulty and (default) ranking for the period. GET /websites/{website_id}/keywords/{keyword_id}.

tools.name: wincher_get_keyword_serps
tools.title: Get keyword SERPs
tools.description: The most recent search result pages Wincher stored for a keyword (up to 30): date, search volume, SERP features and the ranking results (position, URL, domain, traffic). GET /websites/{website_id}/keywords/{keyword_id}/serps.

tools.name: wincher_get_keyword_ranking_history
tools.title: Get keyword ranking history
tools.description: Historical position (or estimated traffic) for ONE keyword as time series, optionally split per ranking page or per competitor. GET /websites/{website_id}/keyword/{keyword_id}/ranking-history.

tools.name: wincher_get_ranking_history_bulk
tools.title: Get ranking history for several keywords
tools.description: Historical positions for up to 50 keywords at once (one time series per keyword). This is a read: it uses POST only because the keyword id list goes in the body. POST /websites/{website_id}/ranking-history.

tools.name: wincher_list_groups
tools.title: List keyword groups
tools.description: List the keyword groups of a website: id, name, keyword_ids, average difficulty, search-intent counts and optionally ranking summaries. GET /websites/{website_id}/groups.

tools.name: wincher_get_group
tools.title: Get keyword group
tools.description: One keyword group with its keyword ids and (optionally) ranking summary for the period. GET /websites/{website_id}/groups/{group_id}.

tools.name: wincher_list_competitors
tools.title: List competitors
tools.description: The competitor domains tracked for a website (id, domain, created_at). GET /websites/{website_id}/competitors.

tools.name: wincher_list_competitor_ranking_summaries
tools.title: Competitor ranking summaries
tools.description: Ranking summaries (average position, share of voice, traffic, position distribution, volume) for the website's competitors over a period, for comparison with your own. GET /websites/{website_id}/competitors/ranking-summaries.

tools.name: wincher_list_competitor_keyword_positions
tools.title: Competitor keyword positions
tools.description: For each tracked keyword, the position of your site and of each competitor in the period. GET /websites/{website_id}/competitors/keyword-positions.

tools.name: wincher_list_annotations
tools.title: List annotations
tools.description: The annotations (notes on the ranking graphs: automatic, alert and user-written) for a website, optionally within a period. GET /websites/{website_id}/annotations.

tools.name: wincher_list_segments
tools.title: List segments
tools.description: The saved segments (keyword filters) usable as segment_id in other tools. By default also temporary ones; only_named limits to saved ones. GET /segments.

tools.name: wincher_add_keywords
tools.title: Add keywords to track
tools.description: WRITE: start tracking up to 50 new keywords on ONE website. EACH keyword uses one keyword slot of the plan's keyword quota (see wincher_get_account), and it is tracked and updated from then on; this tool cannot remove keywords again. Each keyword may name a preferred_url (the landing page expected to rank). Invalid or already-tracked keywords are ignored by Wincher (not created). 'groups' are keyword group NAMES to put every keyword in (may be empty; use names from wincher_list_groups, an unknown name may create a new group). POST /websites/{website_id}/keywords/bulk.

tools.name: wincher_create_group
tools.title: Create keyword group
tools.description: WRITE: create a keyword group on a website, optionally containing existing keywords (ids from wincher_list_keywords). Uses no keyword quota. POST /websites/{website_id}/groups.

tools.name: wincher_create_annotation
tools.title: Create annotation
tools.description: WRITE: add a user annotation (a note shown on the ranking graphs, e.g. 'Launched new landing page') for a date, optionally tied to specific keywords; without keyword_ids it is a global note for the website. Visible to everyone with access to the website. Uses no keyword quota. POST /websites/{website_id}/annotations.

tools.name: wincher_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wincher_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Wincher tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wincher_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Wincher (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: wincher_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Wincher Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run wincher_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which of my keywords rank in the top 10 right now?
How did my keyword rankings change over the last month?
Who are my tracked competitors and how do they rank?
Which keyword groups do I have, and how are they ranking on average?

servers.name: Waitwhile
servers.description: Read Waitwhile visits, bookings, customers, services and analytics; add, update and cancel visits.

login.hint: Create it in Waitwhile → **Settings → Developers → API & Webhooks** → Create API key (the API needs the Business plan or higher). Your key is used only to call the Waitwhile API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List the account's locations (businesses/sites): id, name, short name, address, time zone, opening hours and waitlist/booking settings. Use the ids to filter visits, services and resources. GET /locations.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_location
tools.title: Get location
tools.description: One location by id or short name (the part of its public Waitwhile URL). GET /locations/{shortNameOrId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_location_status
tools.title: List location status (live waitlist)
tools.description: Live status of every location: open/closed, number of people waiting and being served, current estimated wait time, and booking counters. GET /location-status.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_location_status
tools.title: Get location status (live waitlist)
tools.description: Live status of one location: open/closed, waiting and serving counts, estimated wait. GET /location-status/{locationId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_visits
tools.title: List visits (waitlist entries and bookings)
tools.description: List visits: waitlist entries (people in line) and bookings (appointments), with customer, state (PENDING, DRAFT, BOOKED, WAITING, SERVING, COMPLETE), tags (e.g. NO-SHOW, CANCELLED, ARRIVED), services, resources, party size, position and timestamps. Filter by location, state, tag, customer, service, resource, booking date (local time) or created/updated date. Cursor-paged. Contains customer contact details. GET /visits.

tools.name: waitwhile_search_visits
tools.title: Search visits
tools.description: Search visits by a prefix match on customer name, phone, e-mail or customer id, optionally filtered by location, state, tag and excluded tags. Page-numbered. Contains customer contact details. GET /visits/search.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_visit
tools.title: Get visit
tools.description: One visit (waitlist entry or booking) by id: customer, state, tags, services, resources, party size, position, estimated wait and all timestamps. GET /visits/{visitId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_booking_slots
tools.title: List booking slots
tools.description: Booking slots of a location for a date range with the free spots per resource and service, so you can see when an appointment can be booked. Dates are local to the location, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm. GET /visits/availability.

tools.name: waitwhile_first_available_slots
tools.title: First available booking slots
tools.description: The first available booking slots of a location (optionally for a party size, services and resources) from a date. Use it to propose appointment times. GET /visits/first-available-slots.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List customers (name, phone, e-mail, tags, last visit per location, created/updated). Cursor-paged, 20 per page by default; filter by location, external id or created/updated date. Contains personal data. GET /customers.

tools.name: waitwhile_search_customers
tools.title: Search customers
tools.description: Search customers by a prefix match on name, phone, e-mail or customer id; optionally narrowed by location, visit state or tag. Page-numbered. Contains personal data. GET /customers/search.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_customer
tools.title: Get customer
tools.description: One customer by id: contact details, tags, per-location state and last visit. Contains personal data. GET /customers/{customerId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_customer_notes
tools.title: List customer notes
tools.description: The staff notes recorded on a customer (content, author, visit and location, timestamps). GET /customers/{customerId}/notes.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_services
tools.title: List services
tools.description: List services (what customers book or queue for): name, duration, price, locations, resources and category structure. GET /services.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_service
tools.title: Get service
tools.description: One service by id. GET /services/{serviceId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_resources
tools.title: List resources (staff, rooms, tables)
tools.description: List resources — the people, rooms, tables or equipment that serve customers: name, locations, services, availability flag and category structure. GET /resources.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_resource
tools.title: Get resource
tools.description: One resource by id. GET /resources/{resourceId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_resources_availability
tools.title: Resource availability
tools.description: Working hours/availability of a location's resources on a date (e.g. who is working today). GET /resources/availability.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_data_fields
tools.title: List data fields (intake form fields)
tools.description: List the custom data fields (intake/booking form questions) with type, options and where they apply. Use the ids to read answers on visits. GET /data-fields.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_data_field
tools.title: Get data field
tools.description: One data field by id. GET /data-fields/{dataFieldId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_users
tools.title: List users (staff)
tools.description: List the staff users of the account: name, e-mail, roles, locations. Password data and tokens are never returned. GET /users.

tools.name: waitwhile_list_messages
tools.title: List messages
tools.description: List the SMS/e-mail messages Waitwhile sent to and received from customers: channel, recipient, body, delivery state (PENDING, BLOCKED, FAILED, DELIVERED, UNCONFIRMED, RECEIVED) and error. Filter by location, visit, customer, state or date. Contains personal data. This only reads; it cannot send. GET /messages.

tools.name: waitwhile_get_message
tools.title: Get message
tools.description: One message by id. Contains personal data. GET /messages/{messageId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_visit_analytics
tools.title: Visit analytics
tools.description: Aggregated visit statistics for a period: visits, waitlisted, bookings, served, no-shows, cancellations, wait and serve duration quantiles, and breakdowns by location, resource, service, party size, user, day of week and hour of day. GET /analytics/visits (JSON).

tools.name: waitwhile_list_audit_entries
tools.title: List audit entries
tools.description: The account's audit log: who changed what and when (visits, customers, locations, services, resources, users, messages). Filter by type, event, entity, location or date. GET /audit-entries.

tools.name: waitwhile_create_visit
tools.title: Add a customer to the waitlist or create a booking
tools.description: WRITE: create ONE visit at a location. Without a date it adds the customer to the waitlist; with a local date-time (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm) it creates a booking. Needs a location and at least a name, phone or e-mail. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two visits. Visit notes are not supported here (the field is deprecated): use waitwhile_add_customer_note. By default the request asks Waitwhile to suppress the customer message; this may only stop the immediate confirmation, and scheduled reminders/follow-ups can still go out per the location's settings. With send_notifications=true Waitwhile may text/e-mail this ONE customer. POST /visits.

tools.name: waitwhile_update_visit
tools.title: Update a visit (state, tags, time, party)
tools.description: WRITE: change ONE visit — its state (e.g. WAITING to SERVING to COMPLETE, or BOOKED), add/remove tags (e.g. ARRIVED, CONFIRMED, NO-SHOW), booking date/duration or party size. Only the fields you pass change. By default the request asks Waitwhile to suppress the customer message; this may only stop the immediate status message, and scheduled reminders/follow-ups can still go out per the location's settings. With send_notifications=true Waitwhile may text/e-mail this ONE customer. Use waitwhile_cancel_visit to cancel. POST /visits/{visitId}.

tools.name: waitwhile_cancel_visit
tools.title: Cancel a visit
tools.description: WRITE: cancel ONE visit (a waitlist entry or booking). Waitwhile sets its state to COMPLETE and adds the CANCELLED tag; the visit is kept, not deleted. By default the request asks Waitwhile to suppress the customer message; this may only stop the immediate cancellation notice, and scheduled reminders/follow-ups can still go out per the location's settings. With send_notifications=true Waitwhile may text/e-mail this ONE customer. POST /visits/{visitId}/cancel.

tools.name: waitwhile_add_customer_note
tools.title: Add a customer note
tools.description: WRITE: add one staff note to a customer's record (optionally tied to a visit and location). Adds only; nothing is edited or sent to the customer. POST /customers/{customerId}/notes.

tools.name: waitwhile_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: waitwhile_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Waitwhile tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: waitwhile_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Waitwhile (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: waitwhile_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Waitwhile Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run waitwhile_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Who is waiting in line at my shop right now?
What bookings do I have tomorrow, and for which customers?
How many visits did we have last week, bookings and walk-ins?
What are the first free appointment slots for the haircut service?

servers.name: Doxis AI.dp (Klippa DocHorizon)
servers.description: Capture invoices, receipts, IDs and bank statements with Doxis AI.dp; split, render, convert files.

login.hint: Find the key in the Doxis AI.dp platform (dochorizon.klippa.com) under **Settings → Project → API → Credentials**. A new account gets EUR 25 of free credit. Keys belong to one project; if you restricted the credential to certain IP addresses, remove that restriction (this server calls from shared Cloudflare addresses). Choose **Germany** only if your project was created in the Germany region. Identity, bank statement and salary slip captures return personal data to your AI client; documents are processed by Doxis AI.dp under your project's data-retention settings. Your key is used only to call the Doxis AI.dp API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: dochorizon_get_key_info
tools.title: Get API key info
tools.description: Check the connected Doxis AI.dp (Klippa DocHorizon) API key: organization, project, credential id, and the services enabled for it. Does not process a document and costs nothing. GET /auth/v1/info.

tools.name: dochorizon_list_models
tools.title: List enabled capturing models
tools.description: List the document capturing models enabled for this project (financial, identity, bank statement, salary slip, generic, e-invoice, ...). Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /document_capturing/v1/enabled_models.

tools.name: dochorizon_list_configurations
tools.title: List capturing configurations
tools.description: List the capturing configurations of a model (name, slug and the enabled components). Pass a slug as configuration_slug to a capture tool to choose which fields are extracted. Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /document_capturing/v1/{model}/configurations.

tools.name: dochorizon_get_model_schema
tools.title: Get a model's JSON schema
tools.description: The JSON schema of what a capturing model returns (every field it can extract), optionally for one configuration. Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /document_capturing/v1/{model}/schema or /{model}/configurations/{slug}/schema.

tools.name: dochorizon_list_prompt_configurations
tools.title: List Prompt Builder configurations
tools.description: List the Prompt Builder (LLM extraction) configurations of the project: name and slug. Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /document_capturing/v1/prompt_builder/configurations.

tools.name: dochorizon_get_prompt_schema
tools.title: Get a Prompt Builder JSON schema
tools.description: The JSON schema of the output of one Prompt Builder configuration. Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /document_capturing/v1/prompt_builder/configurations/{slug}/schema.

tools.name: dochorizon_capture_financial
tools.title: Capture an invoice or receipt
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: extract structured data from an invoice, receipt or other financial document with the Financial model: merchant and customer, dates, totals, VAT, line items, payment details, currency, and more (as the chosen configuration enables). Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). Synchronous; for long documents use dochorizon_submit_async_capture. POST /document_capturing/v1/financial.

tools.name: dochorizon_capture_identity
tools.title: Capture an identity document
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: read an identity document (passport, ID card, driver's licence, visa) with the Identity model: name, date of birth, nationality, document number, expiry, MRZ, validity and fraud checks. WARNING: the result contains personal data of the people on the document; handle it accordingly. It is returned to you only; this server never stores or logs it. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). Images up to 4096 px per side. POST /document_capturing/v1/identity.

tools.name: dochorizon_capture_bank_statement
tools.title: Capture a bank statement
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: extract a bank statement: bank, account holder, period, opening and closing balance and every transaction. WARNING: the result contains personal data of the people on the document; handle it accordingly. It is returned to you only; this server never stores or logs it. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). POST /document_capturing/v1/bank_statement.

tools.name: dochorizon_capture_salary_slip
tools.title: Capture a salary slip
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: extract a salary slip (payslip): employer, employee, period, gross and net pay, deductions. WARNING: the result contains personal data of the people on the document; handle it accordingly. It is returned to you only; this server never stores or logs it. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). POST /document_capturing/v1/salary_slip.

tools.name: dochorizon_capture_generic
tools.title: Capture any document as key-values and tables
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: turn any document into generic structured data: key-value pairs and tables, as JSON. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). POST /document_capturing/v1/generic.

tools.name: dochorizon_capture_einvoice
tools.title: Capture a document as an e-invoice
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: read an invoice with the financial model and return it in the Universal Invoice structure used for e-invoicing (parties, lines, tax subtotals, totals, payment means). Does not send anything to a network. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). POST /document_capturing/v1/einvoice.

tools.name: dochorizon_capture_with_prompt
tools.title: Capture with a Prompt Builder configuration
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: extract data from a document with a Prompt Builder configuration (an LLM extraction prompt you defined in the platform). Output follows that configuration's schema (see dochorizon_get_prompt_schema). The result may contain whatever personal data the document holds. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). POST /document_capturing/v1/prompt_builder/configurations/{slug}.

tools.name: dochorizon_submit_async_capture
tools.title: Submit a document for asynchronous capture
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: queue one document for capturing and return a job_id right away; poll dochorizon_get_async_job, then read dochorizon_get_async_job_result. Use it for long documents and bursts (async jobs are not subject to the concurrent-request limit). No webhook or human review is configured. For identity, salary_slip and bank_statement the result holds personal data. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). POST /document_capturing/v1/{model}/async.

tools.name: dochorizon_list_async_jobs
tools.title: List asynchronous capture jobs
tools.description: List the project's async capture jobs (newest first as returned): job_id, status, created time, with paging. Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /document_capturing/v1/async.

tools.name: dochorizon_get_async_job
tools.title: Get asynchronous job status
tools.description: The status of one async capture job (in_queue, processing, hitl, done, error, closed, rejected). Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /document_capturing/v1/async/{job_id}.

tools.name: dochorizon_get_async_job_result
tools.title: Get asynchronous job result
tools.description: The captured data of a finished async job (status done). The result may contain personal data (identity, salary slip, bank statement). Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /document_capturing/v1/async/{job_id}/result.

tools.name: dochorizon_get_async_job_logs
tools.title: Get asynchronous job logs
tools.description: Status changes and error messages of an async job, to debug a failed one. Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /document_capturing/v1/async/{job_id}/logs.

tools.name: dochorizon_delete_async_job
tools.title: Delete an asynchronous job
tools.description: WRITE: permanently delete an async job, its result and the stored documents from Doxis AI.dp's servers; a job still waiting in the queue is cancelled. Use it to remove personal data you no longer need. Cannot be undone. DELETE /document_capturing/v1/async/{job_id}.

tools.name: dochorizon_document_info
tools.title: Get document info
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: page count, page sizes, content type, metadata and permissions of a PDF or TIFF. Useful to check the page count before capturing. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). POST /document_toolkit/v1/info.

tools.name: dochorizon_document_split
tools.title: Split a PDF
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: split a PDF into several PDFs by page ranges (one output file per range, for example ['1-3','4-6']). Output files are stored in Doxis AI.dp storage and returned as file ids you can pass to any other tool as file_id. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). POST /document_toolkit/v1/split.

tools.name: dochorizon_document_render
tools.title: Render PDF pages as images
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: render pages of a PDF as images, optionally limited in width/height. Each render config gives page_ranges and optional width and height in pixels. Images are stored in Doxis AI.dp storage and returned as file ids (use dochorizon_download_file for small ones). Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Give the document as exactly one of url (public https), data_base64 (small files) or file_id (a stored file). POST /document_toolkit/v1/render.

tools.name: dochorizon_document_merge
tools.title: Merge PDFs
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: merge two or more PDFs into one, in the order given, optionally taking only some pages of each. The merged file is stored in Doxis AI.dp storage and returned as a file id. Uses your own Doxis AI.dp (Klippa) credits: billed per request or per page depending on the service (extra components in a configuration can add cost), at your project's price (Billing → Pricing in the platform); a new account starts with EUR 25 of free credit. Each document is one of url (public https), data_base64 or file_id. POST /document_toolkit/v1/merge.

tools.name: dochorizon_upload_file
tools.title: Upload a file to Doxis AI.dp storage
tools.description: WRITE: store a file in your Doxis AI.dp storage and get a file_id to reuse in other tools (capture the same file several times without sending it again). Give a public https url or small base64 data. The file stays in your project's storage until it expires per your data-retention setting. May use credits per your pricing. POST /storage/v1/files.

tools.name: dochorizon_download_file
tools.title: Download a stored file (small files only)
tools.description: Fetch a stored file by file_id and return it as base64. Only files up to 30 KB are returned inline; for larger files use the file_id in other tools instead. Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /storage/v1/files/{file_id}.

tools.name: dochorizon_validate_einvoice
tools.title: Validate an e-invoice
tools.description: Validate an e-invoice (XML or hybrid PDF) against its standard (EN 16931, XRechnung, Peppol BIS, ...): returns the detected type, valid yes/no, a summary and each broken rule with its XPath location. Nothing is sent to anyone. May use credits per your pricing. POST /einvoicing/v1/tools/validate.

tools.name: dochorizon_convert_einvoice
tools.title: Convert an e-invoice to Universal Invoice JSON
tools.description: Convert an e-invoice (XML or hybrid PDF) to the Universal Invoice JSON structure (parties, lines, taxes, totals). Nothing is sent to anyone. May use credits per your pricing. POST /einvoicing/v1/tools/convert/einvoice.

tools.name: dochorizon_list_einvoice_types
tools.title: List e-invoice types
tools.description: The e-invoice types Doxis AI.dp understands (ids to pass as einvoice_type). Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /einvoicing/v1/tools/einvoice-types.

tools.name: dochorizon_search_peppol_directory
tools.title: Search the Peppol directory
tools.description: Search the public Peppol business directory by company name, identifier or other text: participant identifiers, countries, contacts, websites and the document types each can receive. Public business data; costs nothing. GET /einvoicing/v1/peppol/environments/{environment}/directory.

tools.name: dochorizon_lookup_peppol_participant
tools.title: Look up a Peppol participant
tools.description: Look up one Peppol participant by identifier (for example iso6523-actorid-upis::0106:64111512) in the Peppol network (SML): the document types it can receive. Does not process a document; normally not billed. GET /einvoicing/v1/peppol/environments/{environment}/participants/{participant_identifier}.

tools.name: dochorizon_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: dochorizon_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Doxis AI.dp (Klippa DocHorizon) tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: dochorizon_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Doxis AI.dp (Klippa DocHorizon) (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: dochorizon_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Doxis AI.dp (Klippa DocHorizon) Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run dochorizon_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: TinyURL
servers.description: Create and manage TinyURL short links: aliases, destinations, tags, archive, click analytics.

login.hint: Create a token in TinyURL under **Settings → API** ([tinyurl.com/app/settings/api](https://tinyurl.com/app/settings/api)). Your token is used only to call the TinyURL API on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: tinyurl_get_link
tools.title: Get a short link
tools.description: Details of one short link: destination URL, tiny_url, tags, created/expires dates, archived/deleted flags, analytics settings, total hits and owner. GET /alias/{domain}/{alias}.

tools.name: tinyurl_list_links
tools.title: List short links
tools.description: List the account's short links (type available = active, archived = archived), optionally created within a date range or filtered by alias or tag. The TinyURL API does not page this list: at most `limit` items (default 50, max 200) are returned together with the total, so narrow with from/to/search when truncated is true. GET /urls/{type}.

tools.name: tinyurl_count_links
tools.title: Count short links
tools.description: How many short links the account has (active or archived), optionally within a creation date range or filtered by alias or tag. GET /urls/{type}/count.

tools.name: tinyurl_get_analytics
tools.title: Get click analytics
tools.description: Aggregated click analytics for the account, or for one link (alias) or one tag, from a start date. report: timeline (clicks over time; interval minute/hour/day/week/month), general (browsers, operating systems, devices), weekday and hour (popularity), top_sources (referrers), top_languages, location (countries, or the regions of one country via region = ISO 3166 alpha-2 code). Which reports are available depends on the account's TinyURL plan. Visitor-level raw logs are not exposed. GET /analytics/*.

tools.name: tinyurl_create_link
tools.title: Create a short link
tools.description: WRITE: create ONE new short link for an http(s) destination URL. Optional custom alias (5-30 characters on tinyurl.com), domain (tinyurl.com or a branded domain), tags, expiry and description. Not idempotent: calling it again without an alias creates another link. Returns the new tiny_url. POST /create.

tools.name: tinyurl_update_link
tools.title: Update a short link's alias, tags or settings
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing short link's alias, tags, expiry, description or click-analytics switch. At least one new_* field is required. DESTRUCTIVE for what it replaces: new_tags REPLACES all existing tags, and renaming the alias (new_alias) makes the old short URL stop working. The destination URL is changed with tinyurl_change_destination. PATCH /update.

tools.name: tinyurl_change_destination
tools.title: Change a short link's destination URL
tools.description: WRITE: point an existing short link at a new destination. DESTRUCTIVE: everyone who opens the short link is sent to the new URL from now on and the old destination is overwritten. The new URL must be http(s). PATCH /change.

tools.name: tinyurl_set_link_archived
tools.title: Archive or unarchive a short link
tools.description: WRITE: archive an active short link (archived = true) or restore an archived one (archived = false). Archiving moves the link to the archived list; nothing is deleted and it can be restored. The API's archive endpoint is a toggle, so the link's current state is read first and nothing is changed when it already matches, and the state afterwards is checked. Do not run two archive calls for the same link at once. GET /alias/{domain}/{alias}, then PATCH /archive.

tools.name: tinyurl_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: tinyurl_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the TinyURL tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: tinyurl_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on TinyURL (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: tinyurl_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's TinyURL Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run tinyurl_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: Spoke Dispatch
servers.description: Read Spoke Dispatch plans, stops, routes and drivers; create and optimize plans; send routes.

login.hint: Create a key in Spoke Dispatch under **Settings → Integrations → API**. The key acts for your whole team; keep it secret. Your key is used only to call the Spoke Dispatch API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: spoke_list_plans
tools.title: List plans
tools.description: List route plans (a plan = one day's delivery job: date, depot, drivers, routes), newest first, in pages of up to 20. Filter with e.g. {"title":"Monday run"} or {"startsGte":"2026-10-01"}. GET /plans.

tools.name: spoke_get_plan
tools.title: Get plan
tools.description: One plan: title, start date, depot, driver ids, route ids, whether it is distributed/writable, optimization state and route overrides. GET /plans/{planId}.

tools.name: spoke_list_plan_stops
tools.title: List plan stops
tools.description: List the stops of a plan, in pages of up to 10. Stops include recipient names, phones, e-mails and addresses (personal data): page only as far as needed. GET /plans/{planId}/stops.

tools.name: spoke_get_stop
tools.title: Get stop
tools.description: One stop of a plan with address, recipient, timing, ETA, route and delivery outcome (attempted, succeeded, notes, photo/signature links). Contains personal data. GET /plans/{planId}/stops/{stopId}.

tools.name: spoke_search_stops
tools.title: Search stops
tools.description: Search all stops of the team (planned, unassigned, past) by keyword and/or Spoke's filter language, up to 20 per page. Example filter: address.countryCode = "DE" and deliveryInfo.attempted = false. Filterable: planId, routeId, type, activity, notes, address.*, createdAt, recipient.name/email/phone/externalId, deliveryInfo.state/attempted/succeeded, orderInfo.*. Results include personal data. The search index lags real time by a short while. GET /stops:search.

tools.name: spoke_list_unassigned_stops
tools.title: List unassigned stops
tools.description: List stops that are not on any plan yet (the inbox of imported orders), in pages of up to 20 (default 20). Contains personal data. GET /unassignedStops.

tools.name: spoke_get_unassigned_stop
tools.title: Get unassigned stop
tools.description: One unassigned stop by id. Contains personal data. GET /unassignedStops/{id}.

tools.name: spoke_list_drivers
tools.title: List drivers
tools.description: List the team's drivers (name, e-mail/phone, active flag, depots, route overrides), up to 50 per page. Contains personal data. GET /drivers.

tools.name: spoke_get_driver
tools.title: Get driver
tools.description: One driver by id. Contains personal data. GET /drivers/{driverId}.

tools.name: spoke_list_depots
tools.title: List depots
tools.description: List depots (start/end addresses, working hours, vehicle type, max stops), up to 20 per page. Use the ids when creating plans. GET /depots.

tools.name: spoke_get_depot
tools.title: Get depot
tools.description: One depot by id. GET /depots/{depotId}.

tools.name: spoke_list_routes
tools.title: List routes
tools.description: List routes (one driver's run of a plan: stop count, driver, distributed/started/completed state), up to 20 per page. GET /routes.

tools.name: spoke_get_route
tools.title: Get route
tools.description: One route: title, driver, stop count and state (distributed, started, completed, recipients notified). GET /routes/{routeId}.

tools.name: spoke_list_route_stops
tools.title: List route stops
tools.description: List the stops of one route in driving order, in pages of up to 10. Contains personal data: page only as far as needed. GET /routes/{routeId}/stops.

tools.name: spoke_list_operations
tools.title: List operations
tools.description: List long-running operations (plan optimizations): type, done flag, who started it, result (optimized and skipped stops), up to 20 per page. GET /operations.

tools.name: spoke_get_operation
tools.title: Get operation
tools.description: One operation, e.g. the optimization started by spoke_optimize_plan: poll until done is true. GET /operations/{operationId}.

tools.name: spoke_list_custom_stop_properties
tools.title: List custom stop properties
tools.description: The team's custom stop property definitions (ids and names). Their ids are the keys of customProperties on stops. Needs a subscription that includes custom properties (HTTP 403 otherwise). GET /team/customStopProperties.

tools.name: spoke_create_plan
tools.title: Create plan
tools.description: WRITE: create a new route plan for a date (no stops yet, nothing is sent to drivers). Optionally assign drivers (up to 50, they must be active and share the plan's depot) and a depot (default: the team's main depot). Does not optimize or distribute. POST /plans.

tools.name: spoke_update_plan
tools.title: Update plan
tools.description: WRITE: change a plan's title, date, drivers and/or depot. Only the fields you pass change, but driver_ids REPLACES the plan's whole driver list. Fails if the plan is not writable (already distributed). Nothing is sent to drivers. PATCH /plans/{planId}.

tools.name: spoke_create_stop
tools.title: Create stop
tools.description: WRITE: add one stop to a writable (not yet distributed) plan. Needs an address (text fields or latitude+longitude). The recipient's phone/e-mail are stored on the stop and Spoke may contact the recipient later when the route runs; nothing is sent now. For many stops use spoke_import_stops. POST /plans/{planId}/stops.

tools.name: spoke_import_stops
tools.title: Import stops
tools.description: WRITE: add up to 100 stops to a writable (not yet distributed) plan in one request (better geocoding than one at a time; Spoke limits imports to 30 requests a minute). Returns the created stop ids and any failures. Recipient contact data is stored on the stops; nothing is sent now. POST /plans/{planId}/stops:import.

tools.name: spoke_optimize_plan
tools.title: Optimize plan
tools.description: WRITE: start the route optimization of a plan (orders and assigns its stops to its drivers). Rewrites the plan's routes if it was optimized before, and uses Spoke's optimization quota (30 per minute, 100 per 10 minutes). Does NOT send anything to drivers. Returns an operation: poll spoke_get_operation until done. Needs at least one driver and one stop. POST /plans/{planId}:optimize.

tools.name: spoke_distribute_plan
tools.title: Distribute plan to drivers
tools.description: WRITE (SENDS TO REAL PEOPLE): distribute an optimized plan, which immediately sends each driver of the plan their route on their phone (push notification / message) and locks the plan for edits. Cannot be undone. Only for a plan with 1-10 drivers, and only after the user has explicitly said to send the routes: set confirm_send_to_drivers to true. POST /plans/{planId}:distribute.

tools.name: spoke_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: spoke_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Spoke Dispatch tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: spoke_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Spoke Dispatch (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: spoke_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Spoke Dispatch Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run spoke_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: RunCloud
servers.description: Read RunCloud servers, web apps, databases and logs; deploy, restart services, renew SSL.

login.hint: Create it in RunCloud under **Workspace → Settings → API Management** (the API is available on the Business and Enterprise plans). Leave the key's **IP restriction empty**: requests come from Cloudflare addresses, so a key limited to your own IP would be refused. The key has the access of your workspace; revoke it there at any time. Your key is used only to call the RunCloud API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: runcloud_ping
tools.title: Check API connection
tools.description: Check that the API key works: RunCloud answers with a message ('pong'). GET /ping.

tools.name: runcloud_list_servers
tools.title: List servers
tools.description: List the servers connected to the workspace: id, name, provider, IP address, OS, stack, online/connected state, agent and PHP CLI version, auto-update settings and tags. GET /servers.

tools.name: runcloud_get_server
tools.title: Get server
tools.description: One server by id: provider, IP, OS and version, stack, online state, agent version, update settings, tags. GET /servers/{id}.

tools.name: runcloud_get_server_stats
tools.title: Get server counts
tools.description: How many web applications, databases, cron jobs and supervisor jobs a server has, and its country. GET /servers/{id}/stats.

tools.name: runcloud_get_server_hardware
tools.title: Get server hardware info
tools.description: Kernel version, CPU model and cores, memory and disk totals/free, load average and uptime of a server. GET /servers/{id}/hardwareinfo.

tools.name: runcloud_get_server_health
tools.title: Get latest server health
tools.description: The latest health sample of a server: total/available/used memory and disk space (MB) and load average. GET /servers/{id}/health/latest.

tools.name: runcloud_list_server_logs
tools.title: List server activity logs
tools.description: The server's activity log (what was changed in RunCloud and when), newest first. GET /servers/{id}/logs.

tools.name: runcloud_list_services
tools.title: List server services
tools.description: The services on a server (nginx, php-fpm, mariadb, redis, supervisor...) with real name, running state, CPU, memory and version. The realName is what runcloud_control_service needs. GET /servers/{id}/services.

tools.name: runcloud_list_system_users
tools.title: List system users
tools.description: The system (Linux) users on a server: id, username, whether deletable. Deployment keys and passwords are never returned. GET /servers/{id}/users.

tools.name: runcloud_list_webapps
tools.title: List web applications
tools.description: List the web applications on a server: id, name, root/public path, PHP version, stack, type (wordpress, custom...), default flag, alias. Deployment webhook keys are not returned. GET /servers/{id}/webapps.

tools.name: runcloud_get_webapp
tools.title: Get web application
tools.description: One web application by id (path, PHP version, stack, type, default flag). GET /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}.

tools.name: runcloud_get_webapp_settings
tools.title: Get web application settings
tools.description: PHP and FPM/Nginx settings of a web application (disabled functions, timezone, memory and upload limits, process manager...). GET /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/settings.

tools.name: runcloud_list_webapp_logs
tools.title: List web application activity logs
tools.description: The activity log of a web application (settings changes, PHP version changes, deployments), newest first. GET /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/log.

tools.name: runcloud_list_domains
tools.title: List domain names
tools.description: The domain names of a web application: id, name, type (primary/alias), www, redirection, wildcard, DNS integration, status. GET /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/domains.

tools.name: runcloud_get_domain_dns
tools.title: Get domain DNS setup instructions
tools.description: The DNS records (A, CNAME...) a domain name needs to point at the server. GET /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/domains/{domain}/dns.

tools.name: runcloud_get_webapp_ssl
tools.title: Get web application SSL
tools.description: The web application's SSL certificate (basic / web-app-level SSL): provider, validity, HTTPS settings. Private keys are never returned. GET /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/ssl.

tools.name: runcloud_get_ssl_method
tools.title: Check SSL method and AutoSSL status
tools.description: Whether the web application uses basic (one certificate for the app) or advanced (one per domain) SSL, and its AutoSSL status. Advanced SSL is a Business/Enterprise feature. GET /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/ssl/advanced.

tools.name: runcloud_get_git_deployment
tools.title: Get Git deployment
tools.description: The Git deployment configured on a web application: provider, branch, repository URL, auto-deploy flag, deployment script and whether it is an atomic deployment. The deployment webhook keys are not returned. The id of the result is the git_id for runcloud_deploy_git. GET /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/git.

tools.name: runcloud_list_databases
tools.title: List databases
tools.description: The databases on a server: id, name, collation. No credentials. GET /servers/{id}/databases.

tools.name: runcloud_list_database_users
tools.title: List database users
tools.description: The database users on a server (id, username). Passwords are never returned. GET /servers/{id}/databaseusers.

tools.name: runcloud_list_cronjobs
tools.title: List cron jobs
tools.description: The cron jobs of a server: id, label, user, schedule, command, enabled flag. The id is what runcloud_run_cronjob needs. GET /servers/{id}/cronjobs.

tools.name: runcloud_list_supervisors
tools.title: List supervisor jobs
tools.description: The supervisor (background worker) jobs of a server: id, label, user, process count, auto start/restart, directory, command. GET /servers/{id}/supervisors.

tools.name: runcloud_get_supervisor_status
tools.title: Get supervisor job status
tools.description: The live status (RUNNING, FATAL, BACKOFF...), pid and uptime of every supervisor process, by job label. GET /servers/{id}/supervisors/status.

tools.name: runcloud_list_firewall_rules
tools.title: List firewall rules
tools.description: The firewall rules of a server: type (global/rich), port, protocol, IP address, action. GET /servers/{id}/security/firewalls.

tools.name: runcloud_list_blocked_ips
tools.title: List Fail2Ban blocked IPs
tools.description: The IP addresses Fail2Ban currently blocks on a server. GET /servers/{id}/security/fail2ban/blockedip.

tools.name: runcloud_list_backups
tools.title: List backups
tools.description: The backup instances of the workspace: label, what they cover (web app / database), storage, type, frequency, size, status. Filter by server, storage, status or name. GET /backups.

tools.name: runcloud_list_backup_snapshots
tools.title: List backup snapshots
tools.description: The snapshots of one backup instance: run date, status, type and size. GET /backups/{id}/snapshots.

tools.name: runcloud_list_atomic_projects
tools.title: List atomic deployment projects
tools.description: The atomic Git deployment projects of the workspace: name, provider, repository, branch, auto-deploy, success/failure counts and the latest deployment. Webhook keys are not returned. GET /atomic.

tools.name: runcloud_list_atomic_deployments
tools.title: List atomic deployments
tools.description: The deployments of an atomic project: commit hash, branch, message, committer, release name, status (DEPLOYING, COMPLETED, FAILED), start and end time. GET /atomic/{project}/deployments.

tools.name: runcloud_control_service
tools.title: Start, restart or reload a service
tools.description: WRITE: run systemctl start, restart or reload on one service of a server (for example nginx-rc or php81rc-fpm). A restart briefly interrupts that service and the sites behind it. 'stop' is deliberately not offered. Get the realName from runcloud_list_services. PATCH /servers/{id}/services.

tools.name: runcloud_deploy_git
tools.title: Force a Git deployment
tools.description: WRITE: force a Git deployment of a web application now: RunCloud pulls the configured branch and runs the deployment script, which changes the live site's files. Get git_id from runcloud_get_git_deployment (its id). PUT /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/git/{git}/script.

tools.name: runcloud_force_deploy_atomic
tools.title: Force an atomic deployment
tools.description: WRITE: start an atomic deployment of a project now (builds a new release and switches the live symlink when it succeeds). PUT /atomic/{project}/forcedeploy.

tools.name: runcloud_run_cronjob
tools.title: Run a cron job now
tools.description: WRITE: force-run one cron job of a server once, right now, outside its schedule. The job's command runs on the server with its configured user. Get the id from runcloud_list_cronjobs. POST /servers/{id}/cronjobs/{job}/run.

tools.name: runcloud_reload_supervisor
tools.title: Reload a supervisor job
tools.description: WRITE: reload one supervisor job so its worker processes restart (running processes are interrupted). Get the id from runcloud_list_supervisors. POST /servers/{id}/supervisors/{job}/reload.

tools.name: runcloud_renew_ssl
tools.title: Renew a Let's Encrypt certificate
tools.description: WRITE: redeploy (renew) the Let's Encrypt certificate of a web application, which re-issues it and reloads the web server. Let's Encrypt certificates only. For basic SSL pass the ssl_id from runcloud_get_webapp_ssl; for advanced (per-domain) SSL, which requires advanced SSL mode (check runcloud_get_ssl_method), also pass domain_id. PUT /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/ssl/{ssl} or /domains/{domain}/ssl/{ssl}.

tools.name: runcloud_install_letsencrypt_ssl
tools.title: Issue a Let's Encrypt certificate
tools.description: WRITE: issue and install a free Let's Encrypt certificate for a web application (basic SSL) or for one domain of it (advanced SSL, pass domain_id; this requires advanced SSL mode, see runcloud_get_ssl_method). The web server is reloaded; the domain's DNS must already point at the server. Custom certificates are not supported here. POST /servers/{id}/webapps/{webapp}/ssl or /domains/{domain}/ssl.

tools.name: runcloud_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: runcloud_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the RunCloud tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: runcloud_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on RunCloud (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: runcloud_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's RunCloud Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run runcloud_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which of my servers are online and how much memory is free?
Which websites are hosted on my main server?
When does the SSL certificate for my main website expire?
Which backups ran recently and did they succeed?

servers.name: Status.io
servers.description: Read Status.io components, incidents, maintenance; post incidents, schedule maintenance, set status.

login.hint: Find the API ID and API key in your Status.io **Dashboard → API** tab; the status page id is on the same tab. Each team member has their own pair, and the pair acts with that member's permissions. They are used only to call the Status.io API on your behalf and are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: statusio_get_status_summary
tools.title: Get status summary
tools.description: The current state of the status page in one call: overall status, every component and container with its status code and last update, open incidents and active/upcoming maintenance. Start here. GET /status/summary/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_components
tools.title: List components
tools.description: List the components of the status page and the containers (data centers / locations) attached to each, with ids. Component and container ids are needed to update a status or to say what an incident affects ('<component_id>-<container_id>'). GET /component/list/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_incidents
tools.title: List incident ids
tools.description: The ids of all active and resolved incidents (ids only, no details): a quick way to see which incidents exist. Fetch one with statusio_get_incident. GET /incidents/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_active_incidents
tools.title: List active incidents
tools.description: Active (unresolved) incidents with their messages and affected components. GET /incident/list/active/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_resolved_incidents
tools.title: List resolved incidents
tools.description: Resolved incidents (history) with their messages and affected components. GET /incident/list/resolved/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_get_incident
tools.title: Get incident
tools.description: One incident in full: components, containers, infrastructure affected and all its messages. GET /incident/{statuspage_id}/{incident_id}.

tools.name: statusio_get_incident_message
tools.title: Get incident message
tools.description: One message (update) of an incident: text, state, status, time and the user who posted it. GET /incident/message/{statuspage_id}/{message_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_maintenance_ids
tools.title: List maintenance ids
tools.description: The ids of all active, closed and upcoming maintenance events (ids only). Fetch one with statusio_get_maintenance. GET /maintenances/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_maintenance
tools.title: List maintenance
tools.description: Maintenance events in one state, with messages and affected components: pending (scheduled, not started), active (in progress) or closed (finished). GET /maintenance/list/{pending|active|closed}/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_get_maintenance
tools.title: Get maintenance
tools.description: One maintenance event in full, with all messages and the infrastructure affected. GET /maintenance/{statuspage_id}/{maintenance_id}.

tools.name: statusio_get_maintenance_message
tools.title: Get maintenance message
tools.description: One message of a maintenance event. GET /maintenance/message/{statuspage_id}/{message_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_subscribers
tools.title: List subscribers
tools.description: List the people and endpoints subscribed to the status page (email addresses, phone numbers, webhook hosts) with ids and their granular preferences. This is personal data of your subscribers. Webhook URLs are shortened to their host, because they can carry secrets. GET /subscriber/list/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_update_component_status
tools.title: Update component status
tools.description: WRITE: change the PUBLIC status of one component/container pair (for example to degraded_performance) without creating an incident. It changes what visitors of your status page see right away. Set it back to operational when done. Ids from statusio_list_components. POST /component/status/update.

tools.name: statusio_create_incident
tools.title: Create incident
tools.description: WRITE: open a new incident on the PUBLIC status page. It is visible to every visitor immediately and sets the status of the affected components. No subscriber, Slack, Teams, IRC or Twitter notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). Returns the new incident id. Say what is affected with all_infrastructure_affected or infrastructure_affected pairs. POST /incident/create.

tools.name: statusio_update_incident
tools.title: Update incident
tools.description: WRITE: post a new update message on an existing incident and set its state and component status. The message is public at once. No subscriber or channel notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). To close an incident use statusio_resolve_incident. POST /incident/update.

tools.name: statusio_resolve_incident
tools.title: Resolve incident
tools.description: WRITE: resolve an incident with a closing message. The affected components return to operational and the incident moves to history. No notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). POST /incident/resolve.

tools.name: statusio_schedule_maintenance
tools.title: Schedule maintenance
tools.description: WRITE: schedule a planned maintenance on the PUBLIC status page. It is visible to visitors as upcoming maintenance. Subscribers are told only if you switch on notify_now / notify_72_hr / notify_24_hr / notify_1_hr (all default off). With automation true Status.io starts and ends it by itself at the planned times. Returns the maintenance id. POST /maintenance/schedule.

tools.name: statusio_start_maintenance
tools.title: Start maintenance
tools.description: WRITE: start a scheduled maintenance now; it moves from pending to active and the affected components show planned maintenance. The message is public at once. No notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). POST /maintenance/start.

tools.name: statusio_update_maintenance
tools.title: Update maintenance
tools.description: WRITE: post a new status message on an active maintenance event. The message is public at once. No notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). POST /maintenance/update.

tools.name: statusio_finish_maintenance
tools.title: Finish maintenance
tools.description: WRITE: finish an active maintenance event; it moves to history and the affected components return to operational. The message is public at once. No notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). POST /maintenance/finish.

tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

Does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Status.io (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: statusio_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Status.io Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Which components are on my status page and what is their status?
