servers.name: Homerun
servers.description: Read Homerun vacancies, applications, notes and tags; move an application to a stage or add a note.

login.hint: Create it in Homerun → **Settings → Integrations** (the Public API needs a plan that includes it). Give the key only the scopes you need: vacancies:read, job-applications:read, job-application-notes:read, tags:read and job-application-tags:read for reading; add job-applications:write and job-application-notes:write only if you want to move candidates between stages or add notes. Your key is used only to call the Homerun API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: homerun_list_vacancies
tools.title: List vacancies
tools.description: List job vacancies (draft, private, public, ...) with title, status, type, location type and expiry. Optionally include location, department, hiring stages (their ids are what homerun_move_application_to_stage needs), salary indication and the candidate count. GET /vacancies (scope vacancies:read).

tools.name: homerun_get_vacancy
tools.title: Get vacancy
tools.description: One vacancy by id with description, location, department, hiring stages (id + name), salary indication, candidate count and the public job and application-form URLs. GET /vacancies/{vacancy_id} (scope vacancies:read).

tools.name: homerun_list_applications
tools.title: List applications (candidates)
tools.description: List job applications, newest page first as the API orders them. Each item has name, e-mail, vacancy id, current stage (id + name), rating, created/hired dates and disqualified flag. Personal data: no phone number, date of birth, photo or files are returned here; ask for one application with homerun_get_application. Filter by vacancy, stage name or disqualified state and page through; do not use it to export all candidates. GET /job-applications (scope job-applications:read).

tools.name: homerun_get_application
tools.title: Get application (candidate)
tools.description: One job application in full: contact details (name, e-mail, phone, city, country), links, experience/education, current stage, rating, sources and file names (notes: use homerun_list_notes). Date of birth, photo URL and file download links are never returned. Optionally include the answers to the application-form questions. Personal data: fetch only the candidate you need. GET /job-applications/{job_application_id} (scope job-applications:read).

tools.name: homerun_list_notes
tools.title: List application notes
tools.description: List the notes on one application: id, author display name, text, sensitive flag and timestamps. GET /job-applications/{job_application_id}/notes (scope job-application-notes:read).

tools.name: homerun_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: List the company's candidate tags (id + name). GET /tags (scope tags:read).

tools.name: homerun_list_application_tags
tools.title: List an application's tags
tools.description: The tags attached to one application. GET /job-applications/{job_application_id}/tags (scope job-application-tags:read).

tools.name: homerun_move_application_to_stage
tools.title: Move application to a stage
tools.description: WRITE: move ONE application to another hiring stage of its vacancy (PATCH with only the stage id; nothing else on the application changes). Get stage ids from homerun_get_vacancy. Homerun's own automations for that stage may run (for example automatic e-mails configured in Homerun); this tool sends no e-mail itself and does not reject or delete anyone. PATCH /job-applications/{job_application_id} (scope job-applications:write).

tools.name: homerun_add_note
tools.title: Add a note to an application
tools.description: WRITE: add ONE note (1-2000 characters) to one application. It becomes visible to the hiring team in Homerun and cannot be removed with this server. display_name is free text shown as the author. Nothing is sent to the candidate. POST /job-applications/{job_application_id}/notes (scope job-application-notes:write).

tools.name: homerun_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: homerun_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Homerun tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: homerun_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Homerun (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: homerun_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Homerun Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run homerun_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which of our job vacancies are currently published?
How many applications came in for the barista vacancy?
Show the details and notes on the newest job application.
Show the hiring stages and application counts for the barista vacancy.

servers.name: 17TRACK
servers.description: Track parcels across 3000+ carriers with 17TRACK: register numbers, read tracking events and quota.

login.hint: Find it in the 17TRACK API dashboard under **Settings → Security Key**. Registering a number uses your own tracking quota. Do not enable an IP whitelist for this key: this hosted server has no fixed IP address. Your key is used only to call the 17TRACK API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: track17_get_quota
tools.title: Get tracking quota
tools.description: The account's tracking quota: total, used, remaining, used today, the daily registration limit (0 = no limit) and the free e-mail quota. Each registered tracking number uses 1 quota. POST /getquota.

tools.name: track17_list_tracking_numbers
tools.title: List registered tracking numbers
tools.description: Search the tracking numbers registered on this account (40 per page) with their carrier, status, registration and last-update times, and latest event. Filter by number(s), carrier, tracking state, package status or registration date. Free: it does not use quota. POST /gettracklist.

tools.name: track17_get_tracking
tools.title: Get tracking details
tools.description: Full tracking details (status, sub-status, milestones, every carrier event with time and location, estimated delivery) for up to 10 numbers that are ALREADY registered on this account. Free: it does not use quota. A number that is not registered comes back in `rejected` — register it first with track17_register_numbers, or use track17_realtime_lookup. POST /gettrackinfo.

tools.name: track17_realtime_lookup
tools.title: Real-time lookup of one number
tools.description: WRITE (uses quota): look up ONE tracking number directly at the carrier right now, without registering it. Costs 1 quota per call (standard: carrier data up to 3 hours old). If the number is already registered, a changed result is also pushed to the account. Not supported for USPS, Royal Mail, Australia Post, Direct Freight Express, DHL eCommerce US and DHL Global Forwarding; some accounts are not enabled for real-time lookups. POST /getRealTimeTrackInfo.

tools.name: track17_register_numbers
tools.title: Register tracking numbers
tools.description: WRITE (uses quota): start tracking up to 10 tracking numbers per call. Each ACCEPTED number costs 1 quota from this account (see track17_get_quota); rejected numbers cost nothing. Deleting and re-registering a number costs again. 17TRACK then updates the status itself every 6-12 hours; read it with track17_get_tracking. The carrier is detected automatically unless a carrier code is given. No e-mail notifications are enabled. POST /register.

tools.name: track17_change_carrier
tools.title: Change the carrier of a number
tools.description: WRITE: assign a different carrier to registered tracking numbers (up to 10 per call), for example when auto-detection picked the wrong one. A number can change carrier at most 5 times, and a successful change can be charged as one shipment (see track17_get_quota). POST /changecarrier.

tools.name: track17_change_tag
tools.title: Change the tag of a number
tools.description: WRITE: set the tag (your own label, max 100 characters) of a registered tracking number. It replaces the old tag. Free. POST /changeinfo.

tools.name: track17_stop_tracking
tools.title: Stop tracking numbers
tools.description: WRITE: stop tracking registered numbers (up to 10 per call). The numbers stay in the account for 90 days with their history and can be restarted ONCE each with track17_retrack. Stopping does not refund quota. POST /stoptrack.

tools.name: track17_retrack
tools.title: Restart tracking of stopped numbers
tools.description: WRITE: restart tracking of stopped numbers (up to 10 per call). Each number can be restarted only ONCE in its lifetime, so a second restart is rejected. POST /retrack.

tools.name: track17_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: track17_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the 17TRACK tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: track17_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on 17TRACK (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: track17_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's 17TRACK Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run track17_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which of my tracked parcels have already been delivered?
How much of my tracking quota have I used so far?
List the parcels I am tracking and their current delivery status.
Start tracking these two parcel numbers for me: RR123456789CN and RR987654321CN.

servers.name: Kinsta
servers.description: Read Kinsta sites, environments, backups, logs and analytics; clear caches, restart PHP, back up.

login.hint: Create one in MyKinsta → your user name → **Company settings → API Keys → Create API Key** (company owners, administrators and developers can). The key is shown only once. It acts with the permissions of the role of the person who created it. Your key is used only to call the Kinsta API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: kinsta_get_api_key_info
tools.title: Get API key info
tools.description: Details of the Kinsta API key in use: its name, status, expiry and the company id it belongs to. The key itself is never shown. GET /validate.

tools.name: kinsta_list_available_regions
tools.title: List data center regions
tools.description: The data center regions (name and region code) the company can host sites in. GET /company/{id}/available-regions.

tools.name: kinsta_list_activity_logs
tools.title: List activity logs
tools.description: The company's activity log (who did what: site actions, DNS, migrations, billing, notifications, user management), newest first, with type, status, time, initiator and a description. Page with limit and offset (the reply's total tells how many exist). GET /company/{id}/activity-logs.

tools.name: kinsta_list_sites
tools.title: List sites
tools.description: List the company's WordPress sites (id, name, display name, status, labels). With include_environments the live/staging environment ids, primary domain, PHP version, WordPress version and SSH host/port come too: use those environment ids for the other tools. GET /sites.

tools.name: kinsta_get_site
tools.title: Get site
tools.description: One site by id, with its status and environments. GET /sites/{site_id}.

tools.name: kinsta_list_site_environments
tools.title: List site environments
tools.description: The environments (live, staging, ...) of one site: id, name, PHP engine version, WordPress version, primary domain, edge cache and CDN ids. GET /sites/{site_id}/environments.

tools.name: kinsta_get_site_usage
tools.title: Get site usage this month
tools.description: A site's usage for the current billing month: visits, bandwidth or CDN bandwidth. GET /sites/{site_id}/usage/{metric}/this-month.

tools.name: kinsta_list_environment_domains
tools.title: List environment domains
tools.description: The domains attached to one environment (id, name, whether Kinsta DNS/Cloudflare is used). GET /sites/environments/{env_id}/domains.

tools.name: kinsta_list_company_domains
tools.title: List company domains
tools.description: All domains the company has in Kinsta DNS / hosting, across sites. GET /domains.

tools.name: kinsta_list_backups
tools.title: List backups
tools.description: The backups of one environment (manual, scheduled and system): id, name, note, type and creation time (epoch ms). Backups cannot be restored or deleted from here. GET /sites/environments/{env_id}/backups.

tools.name: kinsta_list_plugins
tools.title: List WordPress plugins
tools.description: The plugins of one environment: name, title, status (active/inactive), version, available update version, vulnerability flags and the auto-update type. GET /sites/environments/{env_id}/wp-plugins.

tools.name: kinsta_list_themes
tools.title: List WordPress themes
tools.description: The themes of one environment: name, title, status, version, available update version and vulnerability flags. GET /sites/environments/{env_id}/wp-themes.

tools.name: kinsta_get_logs
tools.title: Get environment logs
tools.description: Recent lines of an environment's error log, access log or Kinsta cache performance log, optionally within a time range and filtered by a search text. Returns the log as text (the newest lines the API gives). Access logs contain visitor IP addresses. GET /sites/environments/{env_id}/logs.

tools.name: kinsta_get_analytics
tools.title: Get environment analytics
tools.description: Traffic and resource analytics for one environment: visits, bandwidth, CDN bandwidth, disk space, response codes, visit dispersion, or the top countries, cities, browsers, hosts, referrers, user agents or ASNs. Choose a time_span or a from/to date range (yyyy-mm-dd). The company id is filled in automatically. GET /sites/environments/{env_id}/analytics/{metric}.

tools.name: kinsta_get_force_https_status
tools.title: Get force-HTTPS status
tools.description: Whether the environment forces HTTPS (ENABLED_FOR_ALL, ENABLED_REDIRECT_TO_PRIMARY or DISABLED). GET /sites/environments/{env_id}/force-https-status.

tools.name: kinsta_list_redirect_rules
tools.title: List redirect rules
tools.description: The environment's redirect rules (from, to, type, domain, optional country/city targeting), paged. GET /sites/environments/{env_id}/redirect-rules.

tools.name: kinsta_list_denied_ips
tools.title: List denied IPs
tools.description: The IP addresses and ranges blocked from the environment. GET /sites/tools/denied-ips.

tools.name: kinsta_get_operation_status
tools.title: Get operation status
tools.description: The status of an asynchronous operation (cache clear, PHP restart, manual backup, ...) by the operation_id the write tool returned. status 200 = finished, 202 = still running, other = failed. GET /operations/{operation_id}.

tools.name: kinsta_clear_site_cache
tools.title: Clear site cache
tools.description: WRITE: clear the page cache of one environment (the site is briefly slower while the cache warms up; nothing is lost). Returns an operation_id: check it with kinsta_get_operation_status. POST /sites/tools/clear-cache.

tools.name: kinsta_clear_edge_cache
tools.title: Clear edge cache
tools.description: WRITE: clear Kinsta's edge cache for one environment, optionally only for one URL (and its subdirectories). Nothing is lost; pages are cached again on the next visits. Returns an operation_id. POST /sites/edge-caching/clear.

tools.name: kinsta_clear_cdn_cache
tools.title: Clear CDN cache
tools.description: WRITE: clear the CDN cache of one environment (nothing is lost; files are fetched from the origin again). Needs the environment's cdn_cache_id from kinsta_list_sites. Returns an operation_id. POST /sites/cdn/clear-cache.

tools.name: kinsta_restart_php
tools.title: Restart PHP engine
tools.description: WRITE: restart the PHP engine of one environment. Requests in flight fail and the site may be unavailable for a few seconds. Returns an operation_id. POST /sites/tools/restart-php.

tools.name: kinsta_create_manual_backup
tools.title: Create manual backup
tools.description: WRITE: start a manual backup of one environment, with an optional note. Kinsta limits the number of manual backups per environment; when the limit is reached the request fails and nothing is deleted. Returns an operation_id. POST /sites/environments/{env_id}/manual-backups.

tools.name: kinsta_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: kinsta_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Kinsta (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: kinsta_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Kinsta Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run kinsta_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which sites are on my account, and what is each one's status?
How many visits did my main site get this month?
Which plugins on my live site have updates available?
Clear the cache on the live version of my main site.

servers.name: rapidmail
servers.description: Read rapidmail lists, recipients, mailings and stats; add, update or unsubscribe one recipient.

login.hint: Create them in rapidmail under **Settings › API** (my.rapidmail.de) with **Create new API access**. These are separate API credentials, not your rapidmail login e-mail and password. They are used only to call the rapidmail API on your behalf and are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: rapidmail_list_recipientlists
tools.title: List recipient lists
tools.description: List the recipient lists (newsletter audiences) of the rapidmail account with id, name, description, whether unsubscribed recipients are blacklisted, and which is the default. Use the ids for recipients and mailing filters. GET /recipientlists.

tools.name: rapidmail_get_recipientlist
tools.title: Get recipient list
tools.description: One recipient list by id. GET /recipientlists/{id}.

tools.name: rapidmail_get_recipientlist_activity_stats
tools.title: Get recipient list activity stats
tools.description: Subscription activity of one recipient list between two dates (for example new subscriptions and unsubscriptions). The range may be at most one year, must not start before the list was created and must not lie in the future. GET /recipientlists/{id}/stats/activity.

tools.name: rapidmail_list_recipients
tools.title: List recipients
tools.description: List the recipients (subscribers) of ONE recipient list, optionally filtered by e-mail address, external id or status. recipientlist_id is required. The long text fields (extrabig1-10) are only returned with include_extrabig. GET /recipients.

tools.name: rapidmail_get_recipient
tools.title: Get recipient
tools.description: One recipient by id: e-mail, name, status, custom fields and timestamps. GET /recipients/{id}.

tools.name: rapidmail_create_recipient
tools.title: Add recipient
tools.description: WRITE: add ONE recipient (subscriber) to a recipient list. By default double opt-in is used: the recipient is created with status 'new' and rapidmail sends ONE confirmation e-mail to that address; they only receive newsletters after confirming. Set double_opt_in=false only if you hold the person's documented consent: the recipient is then stored as 'active' and no e-mail is sent (refused if the address was unsubscribed before). If a deleted recipient with the same address exists it is re-activated; an existing address returns a conflict error. Never use for bulk imports. POST /recipients.

tools.name: rapidmail_update_recipient
tools.title: Update recipient
tools.description: WRITE: partially update ONE recipient (only the fields you pass change): e-mail, name, custom fields. The status and the recipient list cannot be changed here, and no e-mail is sent. An e-mail address that already exists in the list returns a conflict error. PATCH /recipients/{id}.

tools.name: rapidmail_unsubscribe_recipient
tools.title: Unsubscribe recipient
tools.description: WRITE: remove ONE recipient from their list. rapidmail only soft-deletes the record (status 'deleted', as if the person had unsubscribed) and the statistics count it as an unsubscription. No goodbye e-mail is sent. Single recipient only. DELETE /recipients/{id}.

tools.name: rapidmail_list_mailings
tools.title: List mailings
tools.description: List newsletters (mailings) with status, subject, sender, send time, recipient count and recipient lists. Filter by status, recipient list, created / updated / sent date. Read only: mailings are never created, sent or scheduled by this server. GET /mailings.

tools.name: rapidmail_get_mailing
tools.title: Get mailing
tools.description: One mailing by id: status, subject, sender, destinations (recipient lists), send time, size and attachments. GET /mailings/{id}.

tools.name: rapidmail_get_mailing_stats
tools.title: Get mailing statistics
tools.description: Statistics of one sent mailing (opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscriptions and similar totals). GET /mailings/{id}/stats.

tools.name: rapidmail_list_mailing_activity
tools.title: List mailing recipient activity
tools.description: The recipients a mailing went to and what each did (delivered, opened, clicked, bounced). Detailed event information is only available if the respective plugin is enabled in the rapidmail account. GET /mailings/{id}/stats/activity.

tools.name: rapidmail_get_mailing_recipient_activity
tools.title: Get one recipient's activity in a mailing
tools.description: Delivery and engagement details of one recipient of one mailing. GET /mailings/{id}/stats/activity/{mailingrecipient_id}.

tools.name: rapidmail_list_mailing_folders
tools.title: List mailing folders
tools.description: The folders used to organise mailings, with id and name. GET /mailings/folders.

tools.name: rapidmail_list_blacklist
tools.title: List blacklist entries
tools.description: The account's blacklist: e-mail addresses, domains and patterns that never receive mailings, with their type, source and dates. GET /blacklist.

tools.name: rapidmail_list_transactional_emails
tools.title: List transactional e-mails
tools.description: Transactional (SMTP) e-mails sent through the rapidmail account: sender, recipient, subject, status (queued, delivered, bounced...), delivery diagnostics and open/click counts. Metadata only, no message bodies. Filter by date, status, project or address. GET /trx/emails.

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on rapidmail (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: rapidmail_cancel_subscription

tools.description: Cancel the caller's rapidmail Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). servers.name: smsmode
servers.description: Read smsmode balance, messages, replies, campaigns and usage; send SMS to up to 10 numbers.

login.hint: Create an API key in your smsmode account under **Settings → Developers** ([ui.smsmode.com/settings/dev](https://ui.smsmode.com/settings/dev)). Its role (user, manager or administrator) decides what it can see. Your key is used only to call the smsmode API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: smsmode_get_balance
tools.title: Get the account balance
tools.description: The credit balance of the connected smsmode account (and sub-organisations an administrator key can see): amount and currency (negative = owed on a POST_PAY account), payment type (PRE_PAY / POST_PAY), state, monthly consumption and its limit. Good first call; check it before sending SMS. GET /commons/v1/organisations.

tools.name: smsmode_get_organisation
tools.title: Get an organisation
tools.description: Full details of one organisation: contacts, addresses, company information, balance, monthly limit and consumption. GET /commons/v1/organisations/{id}.

tools.name: smsmode_list_channels
tools.title: List channels
tools.description: List messaging channels (SMS or RCS; flow TRANSACTIONAL / MARKETING / OTP) with default sender, daily and monthly limits and consumption. A channel id is needed to scope messages or consumption to one channel. GET /commons/v1/channels.

tools.name: smsmode_get_channel
tools.title: Get a channel
tools.description: Details of one channel: type, flow, default sender ID and authorized sender IDs, limits and consumption. GET /commons/v1/channels/{id}.

tools.name: smsmode_list_consumptions
tools.title: List consumption statistics
tools.description: Sent-message counts and money spent per month or per day (price amount and currency), optionally for one channel. Default: monthly, the last 3 months. GET /commons/v1/consumptions.

tools.name: smsmode_get_consumption
tools.title: Get a consumption with its breakdown
tools.description: One consumption record broken down by country (mcc) or network (mccMnc) with quantity and price per sub-item, optionally with delivery statuses. GET /commons/v1/consumptions/{id}.

tools.name: smsmode_lookup_number
tools.title: Look up a phone number's network
tools.description: Country and mobile network (mcc/mnc, operator) of a phone number. Only for customers with a premium smsmode subscription and, for now, only French numbers (403 otherwise). GET /commons/v1/lookup/{msisdn}.

tools.name: smsmode_list_messages
tools.title: List sent and received messages
tools.description: Messages with delivery status (SCHEDULED, ENROUTE, DELIVERED, UNDELIVERABLE, UNDELIVERED; status.detail names the cause), recipient, sender, text, parts and price. Default window: the last 10 days. Filter by direction (MT = sent, MO = replies received), recipient, your reference, channel or campaign. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /sms/v1/messages.

tools.name: smsmode_get_message
tools.title: Get a message and its delivery status
tools.description: One message: delivery status and detail, delivery date, recipient network, text, parts and price. GET /sms/v1/messages/{id}.

tools.name: smsmode_list_campaigns
tools.title: List SMS campaigns
tools.description: Existing SMS campaigns (grouped sends) with status SCHEDULED / ONGOING / ENDED, quantity, price and per-status delivery counts. Read only: this server does not send campaigns. GET /sms/v1/campaigns.

tools.name: smsmode_get_campaign
tools.title: Get an SMS campaign
tools.description: One campaign: state, period, recipients count, text, price and delivery counts per status. Use smsmode_list_messages with campaign_id for its individual messages. GET /sms/v1/campaigns/{id}.

tools.name: smsmode_send_sms
tools.title: Send an SMS to 1-10 recipients
tools.description: WRITE, SPENDS CREDIT: sends one SMS text to 1 to 10 recipients (one message each, a batch of unit messages) and texts REAL people immediately, or at send_at. Cost: every message is charged to the account at its destination's price per SMS part (GSM7: 160 characters for 1 part, 306 for 2, 459 for 3...; UNICODE: 70, 134, 201...); the accept reply returns each message's id and status (the price may only appear later on smsmode_get_message / smsmode_list_messages; total_price is given when present). A batch can partly fail: failures lists the refused numbers, which are not charged. A message is never retried: after a timeout or error, check smsmode_list_messages (ref_client) before sending again. Max 10 recipients, no campaigns or lists. Check smsmode_get_balance first. POST /sms/v1/messages.

tools.name: smsmode_cancel_scheduled_message
tools.title: Cancel a scheduled message
tools.description: WRITE: cancels ONE message that is still scheduled (status SCHEDULED, sent with send_at) so it is not sent; smsmode refuses messages already sent. Cannot be undone. DELETE /sms/v1/messages/{id}.

tools.name: smsmode_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smsmode_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the smsmode tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smsmode_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on smsmode (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smsmode_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's smsmode Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run smsmode_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: How much SMS credit do I have left on my account?
How many texts did we send last month and what did they cost?
Show my SMS campaigns and how many messages in each were delivered.
Were yesterday's appointment reminder texts all delivered?

servers.name: Zammad
servers.description: Search and read Zammad tickets, customers and organizations; add notes, replies and ticket updates.

login.hint: **Zammad address:** for Zammad Cloud just the name (`acme` for acme.zammad.com); for a self-hosted Zammad its public `https://` address (`https://support.example.com`). **Access token:** in Zammad open your **Profile → Token Access → Create** and tick the permissions you want (ticket.agent for agents; admin.group only if you want the group list). The token acts with your user's permissions, so a dedicated agent user makes its activity easy to track. It is used only to call your Zammad on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: zammad_get_me
tools.title: Get current user
tools.description: The Zammad user this access token belongs to: id, name, e-mail, roles and groups. Use it to confirm the connection and the token's permissions. GET /api/v1/users/me.

tools.name: zammad_search_tickets
tools.title: Search tickets
tools.description: Search tickets with Zammad's query syntax. With Elasticsearch on the instance you can use fields, e.g. `state.name:open AND group.name:Sales`, `customer.email:"a@b.com"`, `title:invoice`, `number:20001`; a plain word searches ticket text. Replies carry ids plus names (group, state, priority, owner, customer). GET /api/v1/tickets/search?expand=true.

tools.name: zammad_list_tickets
tools.title: List tickets
tools.description: List the tickets the token's user can see (an agent sees the tickets of their groups; a customer only their own). For anything targeted use zammad_search_tickets. GET /api/v1/tickets?expand=true.

tools.name: zammad_get_ticket
tools.title: Get ticket
tools.description: One ticket by its numeric id (not the ticket number): title, group, state, priority, owner, customer, organization, dates, escalation and article count. GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}?expand=true.

tools.name: zammad_list_ticket_articles
tools.title: List ticket articles
tools.description: All articles (messages, internal notes, e-mails, phone notes) of one ticket in order, with sender, type, internal flag, from/to/cc, subject, body and attachment names (attachments are not downloaded). Long bodies are cut at 6000 characters; use zammad_get_ticket_article for the full text. GET /api/v1/ticket_articles/by_ticket/{ticket_id}.

tools.name: zammad_get_ticket_article
tools.title: Get ticket article
tools.description: One article by its id with its full body, headers and attachment names. GET /api/v1/ticket_articles/{id}.

tools.name: zammad_list_ticket_tags
tools.title: List ticket tags
tools.description: The tags on one ticket. GET /api/v1/tags?object=Ticket&o_id={ticket_id}. Needs an agent token.

tools.name: zammad_list_ticket_states
tools.title: List ticket states
tools.description: The ticket states of the instance (new, open, pending reminder, pending close, closed, ...) with ids and whether they are active. Use the names in zammad_update_ticket. GET /api/v1/ticket_states.

tools.name: zammad_list_ticket_priorities
tools.title: List ticket priorities
tools.description: The ticket priorities of the instance (e.g. '1 low', '2 normal', '3 high') with ids. Use the names in zammad_update_ticket. GET /api/v1/ticket_priorities.

tools.name: zammad_list_groups
tools.title: List groups
tools.description: The ticket groups (queues) of the instance, with ids, names and agent ids. Zammad requires the admin.group permission for this list; with an agent-only token it returns an authorization error. GET /api/v1/groups.

tools.name: zammad_search_users
tools.title: Search users
tools.description: Search customers and agents by name, e-mail, login, phone or organization. Returns profile fields (no credentials). Needs an agent token. GET /api/v1/users/search?expand=true.

tools.name: zammad_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: One user (customer or agent) by id: name, e-mail, phone, organization, roles, VIP flag and notes. No credentials. GET /api/v1/users/{id}?expand=true.

tools.name: zammad_search_organizations
tools.title: Search organizations
tools.description: Search customer organizations by name or domain. Needs an agent token. GET /api/v1/organizations/search.

tools.name: zammad_list_organizations
tools.title: List organizations
tools.description: List customer organizations with domain, VIP flag and member ids. Needs an agent token. GET /api/v1/organizations.

tools.name: zammad_get_organization
tools.title: Get organization
tools.description: One organization by id: name, domain, notes, VIP flag, member ids. GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}.

tools.name: zammad_add_internal_note
tools.title: Add internal note
tools.description: WRITE: add an INTERNAL note (visible to agents only, never e-mailed to the customer) to ONE ticket. Needs an agent's token (a customer's token is refused, because Zammad would make the note public). The ticket's other data is not changed. POST /api/v1/ticket_articles with type=note, internal=true.

tools.name: zammad_reply_to_ticket
tools.title: Reply to ticket (e-mails the customer)
tools.description: WRITE: send a customer-visible reply on ONE ticket. THIS E-MAILS A REAL PERSON: the reply is delivered by e-mail to exactly ONE recipient and cannot be recalled. By default the recipient is the ticket's customer (looked up from the ticket); `to` may name one other single address. No cc, no bulk, no attachments. Needs an agent's token (a customer's token is refused). For an internal remark use zammad_add_internal_note. GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}, then POST /api/v1/ticket_articles with type=email, internal=false.

tools.name: zammad_update_ticket
tools.title: Update ticket
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of ONE ticket: state, priority, owner (agent), group and/or title. Use names from zammad_list_ticket_states / zammad_list_ticket_priorities / zammad_list_groups. Pending states need `pending_time`. Never deletes, removes or merges (those states are refused). The instance's own triggers still run, so closing or reassigning a ticket can send the customer or agent a notification e-mail. PUT /api/v1/tickets/{id}.

tools.name: zammad_create_ticket
tools.title: Create ticket
tools.description: WRITE: create ONE new ticket for an EXISTING customer (by e-mail address or user id) in a group, with a first article recorded as written by the customer (type note or phone). It does not send an e-mail by itself, but the instance's triggers may (for example an automatic confirmation to the customer). It never creates new users. POST /api/v1/tickets.

servers.name: TinyPNG
servers.description: Compress, resize and convert images with TinyPNG by URL, and check this month's compression count.

login.hint: Get a free key (500 compressions a month) at **tinify.com/developers**, then copy it from your **API dashboard**. Every compression, resize and conversion counts against your own Tinify quota. Your key is used only to call the Tinify API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: tinypng_compress_image
tools.title: Compress an image from a URL
tools.description: WRITE (uses quota): ask TinyPNG (Tinify) to fetch a public image by URL and compress it (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or JPEG XL). Returns the output_url (Tinify's Location address of the compressed image), the compressed size and type, the savings when the input size is known, and the Compression-Count header (compressions used this month). The image is stored by Tinify for about 48 hours; output_url needs your API key, so use tinypng_download_image to get the bytes and tinypng_transform_image to resize, convert or keep metadata. Each compression counts against the monthly quota of your Tinify API key (the free plan includes 500 per month); resizing and converting count one extra compression each. POST /shrink.

tools.name: tinypng_transform_image
tools.title: Resize, convert or keep metadata of a compressed image
tools.description: WRITE (uses quota): apply a resize, a format conversion and/or metadata preservation to an image compressed earlier (the output_url from tinypng_compress_image, valid about 48 hours). Returns the resulting type, byte size, width, height and Compression-Count; the image itself is returned too when include_image is true and it is under 1 MB. Resize: method scale (give width OR height), or fit / cover / thumb (give width AND height); images are never scaled up. Convert: one or more of image/webp, image/jpeg, image/png, image/avif, image/jxl (several = the smallest is returned) or */* (the smallest of WebP, JPEG, PNG); converting a transparent image to JPEG needs a background colour. Preserve: copyright, creation, location (location is JPEG only) keeps that metadata, which makes the file slightly larger. Each call is a fresh request: resize and convert each count one extra compression on your monthly Tinify quota, preserve is free. Tinify returns the bytes only (no new URL), so only include_image gives you the transformed file, and only when it is under 1 MB. POST /output/{id}.

tools.name: tinypng_download_image
tools.title: Download a compressed image
tools.description: Fetch the compressed image of an earlier tinypng_compress_image (its output_url, valid about 48 hours) and return it as an image with its type, byte size, width and height. Images over 1 MB are described but not returned inline. Downloading does not use extra compression quota. GET /output/{id}.

tools.name: tinypng_get_usage
tools.title: Get compression usage this month
tools.description: How many compressions your Tinify API key has used this calendar month (the Compression-Count header), and whether the key is valid. The check sends an empty request that Tinify refuses, so nothing is compressed and no quota is used. Compare with your Tinify plan (the free plan includes 500 per month). POST /shrink with no body.

servers.name: WakaTime
servers.description: Read your WakaTime coding time: summaries, stats, projects, goals, commits and leaderboards.

login.hint: Find it at **wakatime.com → Settings → Account → Secret API Key** (wakatime.com/settings/api-key). This server only reads your data, but the key itself gives full access to your WakaTime account. Your key is used only to call the WakaTime API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone. You can reset it at any time on the same page.

tools.name: wakatime_get_user
tools.title: Get current user
tools.description: The WakaTime user this key belongs to: id, username, display name, email, timezone, plan, last plugin/project/branch and last heartbeat time. GET /users/current.

tools.name: wakatime_get_summaries
tools.title: Get daily summaries
tools.description: Coding activity as one summary per day for a date range: grand total plus breakdowns by project, language, editor, operating system, category, dependencies and machine, with cumulative total and daily average. Give start and end, or one named range. Use project (and branches) to also get per-branch and per-file entities. GET /users/current/summaries.

tools.name: wakatime_get_stats
tools.title: Get coding stats
tools.description: Aggregated coding stats for a range: total time, daily average, best day, AI vs human line changes, and the full breakdown by language, project, editor, operating system, category, dependencies and machine. If the reply says it is still calculating, call again shortly. GET /users/current/stats/{range}.

tools.name: wakatime_get_all_time_since_today
tools.title: Get all-time total
tools.description: Total coding time since the user's WakaTime account (or one project) was created, with daily average and the range covered. GET /users/current/all_time_since_today.

tools.name: wakatime_get_status_bar_today
tools.title: Get today's coding time
tools.description: Today's coding activity as shown in an editor status bar: grand total plus breakdowns by project, language, editor and more. Cached data only; an empty summary means the cache is still being filled. GET /users/current/status_bar/today.

tools.name: wakatime_get_insight
tools.title: Get insight
tools.description: One WakaTime insight for a range: stats, weekdays (average per weekday), days (per-day totals, optionally one weekday), ai_days, best_day, daily_average, or a breakdown by projects, languages, editors, categories, machines or operating_systems. GET /users/current/insights/{insight_type}/{range}.

tools.name: wakatime_get_durations
tools.title: Get durations for a day
tools.description: The coding sessions (durations) of one day, each with start time, length in seconds and the project (or other slice) it belongs to. Needs the read_heartbeats scope for OAuth tokens. GET /users/current/durations.

tools.name: wakatime_get_heartbeats
tools.title: Get heartbeats for a day
tools.description: The raw heartbeats (activity pings from editor plugins) of one day: entity (file path or domain), type, category, project, branch, language, time, lines and AI line changes. Large days are cut to `limit` heartbeats starting at `offset`; total_heartbeats says how many the day has. Needs the read_heartbeats scope for OAuth tokens. GET /users/current/heartbeats.

tools.name: wakatime_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: The user's WakaTime projects with id, name, repository, color, clients, first and last heartbeat time and badge/public-url flags. Optionally filter by a name search. GET /users/current/projects.

tools.name: wakatime_list_machines
tools.title: List machines
tools.description: The machines (computers) that sent coding activity: id, name, host name, IP, timezone and last-seen time. GET /users/current/machine_names.

tools.name: wakatime_list_user_agents
tools.title: List editors and plugins used
tools.description: The editor and plugin user agents that sent coding activity: editor, version, OS, AI model if any, and last-seen time. GET /users/current/user_agents.

tools.name: wakatime_list_commits
tools.title: List project commits
tools.description: Commits of a WakaTime project with the time spent coding on each (needs a connected repository). Filter by author or branch; paged. Needs the read_heartbeats scope for OAuth tokens. GET /users/current/projects/{project}/commits.

tools.name: wakatime_get_commit
tools.title: Get project commit
tools.description: One commit of a WakaTime project by hash, with the time spent coding on it. Needs the read_heartbeats scope for OAuth tokens. GET /users/current/projects/{project}/commits/{hash}.

tools.name: wakatime_list_goals
tools.title: List goals
tools.description: The user's coding goals: title, type, target seconds, status, chart data per period, languages/projects/editors it covers and who it is shared with. Needs the read_goals scope for OAuth tokens. GET /users/current/goals.

tools.name: wakatime_get_goal
tools.title: Get goal
tools.description: One goal by id with its chart data (cached; an empty chart means the cache is still building, retry shortly). GET /users/current/goals/{goal}.

tools.name: wakatime_list_orgs
tools.title: List organizations
tools.description: The WakaTime organizations the user belongs to: id, name, people count, keystroke timeout and timezone preferences and what the user may do. Needs the read_orgs scope for OAuth tokens. GET /users/current/orgs.

tools.name: wakatime_list_org_dashboards
tools.title: List organization dashboards

tools.name: wakatime_list_org_dashboard_members

tools.name: wakatime_get_org_dashboard_summaries
tools.title: Get dashboard summaries for a day

tools.name: wakatime_get_org_member_summaries

Requires confirm: true. Run wakatime_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: e-Boekhouden
servers.description: Read e-Boekhouden relations, invoices, ledgers, bookings and products; create relations, invoices.

login.hint: Create a token in e-Boekhouden under **Beheer → Inrichting → Koppelingen → e-Boekhouden API** (it is shown only once; you can set an expiry date). Your token is exchanged for a short-lived session on every request and is used only to call the e-Boekhouden API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone. Deactivating the token's user or letting the token expire disconnects this server.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_relations
tools.title: List or search relations
tools.description: List relations (customers and suppliers of the administration), optionally filtered (filters combine with AND). Text filters match exactly unless match is contains or starts_with. Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/relation.

tools.name: eboekhouden_get_relation
tools.title: Get a relation
tools.description: One relation with all its fields (addresses, e-mail addresses, VAT and KvK number, IBAN, payment term, ledger). GET /v1/relation/{id}.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_invoices
tools.title: List or search invoices
tools.description: Search the invoices created in the invoicing module, by invoice number, relation or date (exact, or from/to). Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/invoice.

tools.name: eboekhouden_get_invoice
tools.title: Get an invoice
tools.description: One invoice with its items, amounts and relation. GET /v1/invoice/{id}.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_outstanding_invoices
tools.title: List outstanding invoices
tools.description: Open (unpaid) invoices: debtors (D, sales invoices customers still owe) or creditors (C, purchase invoices still to be paid). Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/mutation/invoice/outstanding.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_mutations
tools.title: List or search mutations (bookings)
tools.description: Search the bookkeeping mutations: type 1 invoice received, 2 invoice sent, 3 invoice payment received, 4 invoice payment sent, 5 money received, 6 money sent, 7 general journal entry. Filter by type, mutation number, description, invoice number or date. Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/mutation.

tools.name: eboekhouden_get_mutation
tools.title: Get a mutation (booking)
tools.description: One mutation with its rows (ledger, VAT code, amount, relation, invoice number). GET /v1/mutation/{id}.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_ledgers
tools.title: List ledgers (chart of accounts)
tools.description: The ledger accounts (grootboekrekeningen): id, code, description and category (BAL balance, VW profit and loss, FIN, DEB, CRED, AF6, AF19, AFOVERIG, VOOR, BTWRC, AF). Use the id as ledger_id in other tools. Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/ledger.

tools.name: eboekhouden_get_ledger
tools.title: Get a ledger
tools.description: One ledger account. GET /v1/ledger/{id}.

tools.name: eboekhouden_get_ledger_balance
tools.title: Get a ledger's balance
tools.description: The balance of one ledger, optionally per cost center and for a period (from/to). GET /v1/ledger/{id}/balance.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_ledger_balances
tools.title: List all ledger balances
tools.description: The balances of all ledgers (a trial balance), optionally per cost center and for a period (from/to). GET /v1/ledger/balances.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products and services (articles) with price, VAT code, ledger and unit, optionally by code or group code. Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/product.

tools.name: eboekhouden_get_product
tools.title: Get a product
tools.description: One product with price, VAT code, ledger, unit and stock setting. GET /v1/product/{id}.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_product_groups
tools.title: List product groups
tools.description: All product groups. GET /v1/product/groups.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_cost_centers
tools.title: List cost centers
tools.description: List cost centers (kostenplaatsen), optionally by parent id or description. Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/costcenter.

tools.name: eboekhouden_get_cost_center
tools.title: Get a cost center
tools.description: One cost center. GET /v1/costcenter/{id}.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_units
tools.title: List units
tools.description: List product units (piece, hour, ...) with their ids. Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/unit.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_invoice_templates
tools.title: List invoice templates
tools.description: List invoice templates (the template_id for eboekhouden_create_invoice), optionally by name, type (E editor, A advanced) or active. Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/invoicetemplate.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_email_templates
tools.title: List e-mail templates
tools.description: List e-mail templates. Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/emailtemplate.

tools.name: eboekhouden_list_members
tools.title: List members (clubs and associations)
tools.description: List members; only available to clubs and associations (others get error MEM_056). Paged: pass next_offset as offset. GET /v1/member.

tools.name: eboekhouden_get_member
tools.title: Get a member (clubs and associations)
tools.description: One member; only available to clubs and associations. GET /v1/member/{id}.

tools.name: eboekhouden_create_relation
tools.title: Create a relation
tools.description: Create a new relation (customer or supplier) in the administration. Only name is required; the code is generated when omitted. Returns the new id and code. POST /v1/relation.

tools.name: eboekhouden_update_relation
tools.title: Update a relation
tools.description: Change fields of an existing relation. The tool first reads the relation, then sends its current values with your changes on top (the API requires name on every update), so fields you do not pass keep their values. This overwrites the current values of the fields you pass. GET + PATCH /v1/relation/{id}.

tools.name: eboekhouden_create_product
tools.title: Create a product
tools.description: Create a product or service. Needs code, description, a sale VAT code and a ledger id, and exactly one of price_excl or price_incl. Returns the new id. POST /v1/product.

tools.name: eboekhouden_create_invoice
tools.title: Create an invoice
tools.description: Create a sales invoice for a relation. PERMANENT: the API cannot change or delete invoices afterwards, and an invoice number is used up. The invoice is created only: it is NOT e-mailed to the customer, NOT booked as a mutation and no direct debit is set. Needs relation_id, template_id (eboekhouden_list_invoice_templates), term_of_payment in days and at least one item with a ledger_id. Returns the new id and invoice number. POST /v1/invoice.

tools.name: eboekhouden_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: eboekhouden_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the e-Boekhouden tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: eboekhouden_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on e-Boekhouden (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: eboekhouden_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's e-Boekhouden Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run eboekhouden_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which customer invoices are still unpaid, and how much is outstanding in total?
Show the invoices we sent to Acme Ltd this year.
What is the balance of each ledger account right now?
Add a new customer called Acme Ltd with the email billing@acme-example.com.

servers.name: Weblate
servers.description: Read Weblate projects, strings, stats and changes; translate, suggest, comment and autotranslate.

login.hint: Create a token in Weblate: your **profile (user menu) → Settings → API access**; it starts with `wlu_` (a project token, `wlp_`, limits the connection to one project). The token acts with your permissions, so a dedicated user makes its activity easy to track. The instance must be a public `https://` address without a path. Your token is used only to call the Weblate API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: weblate_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the projects visible to this token: name, slug, website and settings (review workflow, access control). GET /api/projects/.

tools.name: weblate_get_project
tools.title: Get project
tools.description: One project by slug: name, website, settings, instructions and links. GET /api/projects/{project}/.

tools.name: weblate_list_components
tools.title: List components
tools.description: List translation components (one translatable file set in a repository), with repository, file mask, source language and status flags. Give a project to list only its components. Repository URLs have embedded credentials removed. GET /api/components/ or /api/projects/{project}/components/.

tools.name: weblate_get_component
tools.title: Get component
tools.description: One component: repository, branch, file mask, template, source language, commit and merge settings, lock state. GET /api/components/{project}/{component}/.

tools.name: weblate_list_translations
tools.title: List translations
tools.description: List the translations (one language each) of a component with their statistics: total, translated, fuzzy, percent, last change. GET /api/components/{project}/{component}/translations/.

tools.name: weblate_get_translation
tools.title: Get translation
tools.description: One translation (a component in one language): statistics, language, file name, revision and links. GET /api/translations/{project}/{component}/{language}/.

tools.name: weblate_get_statistics
tools.title: Get translation statistics
tools.description: Translation progress: strings and words total, translated, needing edit, with percentages and checks. Scope by project; add a component for per-language statistics of a component, add a language too for one translation. GET /api/projects/{project}/statistics/, /api/components/{project}/{component}/statistics/ or /api/translations/{project}/{component}/{language}/statistics/.

tools.name: weblate_list_project_languages
tools.title: List project languages
tools.description: Per-language translation statistics for a whole project (code, total, translated, percentages). GET /api/projects/{project}/languages/.

tools.name: weblate_list_languages
tools.title: List languages
tools.description: List the languages known to this Weblate instance: code, name, text direction, plural forms. GET /api/languages/.

tools.name: weblate_list_units
tools.title: List strings (units)
tools.description: List or search translation strings (units): source, target, state (0 untranslated, 10 needs editing, 20 translated, 30 approved, 100 read-only), context, location, failing checks. Search with Weblate's query syntax, for example state:<translated or has:suggestion. Give project + component + language to read one translation; without them all visible strings are searched. GET /api/translations/{project}/{component}/{language}/units/ or /api/units/.

tools.name: weblate_get_unit
tools.title: Get string (unit)
tools.description: One string by id: source and target forms, state, context, location, flags, labels, explanation, suggestions/comments flags, web link. GET /api/units/{id}/.

tools.name: weblate_list_unit_comments
tools.title: List string comments
tools.description: Comments on one string (Weblate 5.15+). GET /api/units/{id}/comments/.

tools.name: weblate_list_suggestions
tools.title: List suggestions
tools.description: List suggestions (proposed translations waiting for review), newest first (Weblate 2026.8+). Give a unit id for one string's suggestions. GET /api/suggestions/ or /api/units/{id}/suggestions/.

tools.name: weblate_list_changes
tools.title: List changes
tools.description: The activity log: who changed or translated what, when, with the action name and the changed text. Scope by project, component or translation (language), or filter by user, action id and time range. GET /api/changes/ or the project/component/translation changes endpoint.

tools.name: weblate_search_memory
tools.title: Search translation memory
tools.description: Browse the translation memory entries visible to the token, filtered by source text (substring), languages or project. GET /api/memory/.

tools.name: weblate_lookup_memory
tools.title: Look up translation memory
tools.description: Find translation memory matches (exact or fuzzy) for up to 20 source strings in one language pair. Read-only: nothing is stored. POST /api/memory/lookup/.

tools.name: weblate_get_repository_status
tools.title: Get repository status
tools.description: Version-control status: pending changes to commit, upstream changes to merge, changes to push, remote commit, merge failure. For a project (summary of all its repositories) or one component. GET /api/projects/{project}/repository/ or /api/components/{project}/{component}/repository/.

tools.name: weblate_update_translation
tools.title: Update a translation
tools.description: WRITE: set the translation of one string (replaces the current target). `target` is the list of plural forms. `state` is required (Weblate rejects a partial update without both): 0 untranslated with an empty target, 10 needs editing, 20 translated or 30 approved (approval needs the review workflow and permission). The number of plural forms must match the language. Changes are committed to the repository by Weblate's normal schedule. PATCH /api/units/{id}/.

tools.name: weblate_add_suggestion
tools.title: Add a suggestion
tools.description: WRITE: propose a translation for one string; normally a reviewer accepts it later, but the author's automatic upvote (or an existing identical suggestion) can reach the project's auto-accept threshold and apply it at once. Needs the Add suggestion permission and suggestions enabled (Weblate 2026.8+). POST /api/units/{id}/suggestions/.

tools.name: weblate_accept_suggestion
tools.title: Accept a suggestion
tools.description: WRITE: apply a suggestion to its string (replaces the current translation). `approve` also marks it approved (review workflow and permission needed). Weblate 2026.8+. POST /api/suggestions/{id}/accept/.

tools.name: weblate_add_unit_comment
tools.title: Add a string comment
tools.description: WRITE: add a comment to one string (Markdown, @username mentions notify users). `scope` is global (all languages), translation (this language) or report (a source-string issue report; needs the review workflow). Weblate 5.12+. POST /api/units/{id}/comments/.

tools.name: weblate_repository_operation
tools.title: Run a repository operation
tools.description: WRITE: commit (write pending translations into the local repository), pull (merge upstream changes) or push (publish committed changes to the remote repository) for a project or one component. Push changes the remote repository. reset and cleanup are not offered. POST /api/projects/{project}/repository/ or /api/components/{project}/{component}/repository/.

tools.name: weblate_autotranslate
tools.title: Run automatic translation
tools.description: WRITE: fill a translation automatically from other components (auto_source others, default) or from machine translation (mt, needs engines). `mode` suggest only adds suggestions (default), translate writes translations, fuzzy marks them needing edit. `q` limits it to strings matching a search (default state:<translated, the strings that are not translated yet); threshold is the minimum match score (default 80). Use background to schedule a task instead of waiting. POST /api/translations/{project}/{component}/{language}/autotranslate/.

tools.name: weblate_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: weblate_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Weblate tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: weblate_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Weblate (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: weblate_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Weblate Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run weblate_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: SmartBill
servers.description: Read SmartBill series, taxes, stock, clients and products; draft and issue invoices and estimates.

login.hint: Find the **Email**, **Token** and **CIF** in SmartBill Cloud under **Integrari → API** ([cloud.smartbill.ro/core/integrari](https://cloud.smartbill.ro/core/integrari/)). The optional **API V3 token** from the same page unlocks the client, supplier, product and warehouse lists. The API is part of selected SmartBill plans. Your credentials are used only to call the SmartBill API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: smartbill_list_series
tools.title: List document series
tools.description: List the document series configured in SmartBill Cloud with their next number. Invoice and proforma tools need a series name from here. type: f = invoice series, p = proforma, c = receipt (chitanta); omit for all. GET /series.

tools.name: smartbill_list_taxes
tools.title: List VAT rates (V1)
tools.description: List the VAT rates configured in the account (name and percentage). Use the name as tax_name and the percentage as tax_percentage on document lines. Works without a V3 token. GET /tax.

tools.name: smartbill_get_stock
tools.title: Get stock levels
tools.description: Stock quantities per warehouse as of a date (needs the SmartBill stock module). Optional filters: warehouse_name (case-sensitive), product_name, product_code. No filters = all products in all warehouses. GET /stocks.

tools.name: smartbill_get_invoice_payment_status
tools.title: Get invoice payment status
tools.description: Whether an invoice is paid and how much remains: invoiceTotalAmount, paidAmount, unpaidAmount and the paid flag. GET /invoice/paymentstatus.

tools.name: smartbill_get_estimate_invoices
tools.title: Get invoices of a proforma
tools.description: Whether a proforma was invoiced and the invoices (series, number) made from it. A draft invoice shows with an empty number. GET /estimate/invoices.

tools.name: smartbill_list_clients
tools.title: List or search clients
tools.description: List clients from the SmartBill client list, optionally filtered by name (partial, case-insensitive), internal code (exact) or CIF (exact). Needs the API V3 token. Cursor paged: pass the reply's next_args as the next call's arguments. GET /v3/companies/{cif}/clients.

tools.name: smartbill_get_client
tools.title: Get a client
tools.description: One client by V3 id (cus_...): name, CIF, address, bank, contact, VAT-payer flag and delivery addresses. Needs the API V3 token. GET /v3/companies/{cif}/clients/{id}.

tools.name: smartbill_list_suppliers
tools.title: List or search suppliers
tools.description: List suppliers, optionally filtered by name (partial), internal code (exact) or CIF (exact). Needs the API V3 token. Cursor paged: pass the reply's next_args as the next call's arguments. GET /v3/companies/{cif}/suppliers.

tools.name: smartbill_get_supplier
tools.title: Get a supplier
tools.description: One supplier by V3 id (sup_...). Needs the API V3 token. GET /v3/companies/{cif}/suppliers/{id}.

tools.name: smartbill_list_products
tools.title: List or search products and services
tools.description: List the product and service catalog (price, unit, VAT rate, currency), optionally filtered by name (whole-word match) or internal code (exact). Needs the API V3 token. Cursor paged: pass the reply's next_args as the next call's arguments. GET /v3/companies/{cif}/products.

tools.name: smartbill_get_product
tools.title: Get a product or service
tools.description: One product or service by V3 id (prod_...). Needs the API V3 token. GET /v3/companies/{cif}/products/{id}.

tools.name: smartbill_list_warehouses
tools.title: List warehouses
tools.description: List warehouses (name, type en gros / en detail, keeper, address). Needs the API V3 token. Cursor paged: pass the reply's next_args as the next call's arguments. GET /v3/companies/{cif}/warehouses.

tools.name: smartbill_list_vat_rates
tools.title: List VAT rates (V3)
tools.description: List VAT rates with ids, name, percentage and reverse-charge flag. Filter by name (partial) or percentage (exact). Needs the API V3 token (smartbill_list_taxes does the same without it). Cursor paged: pass the reply's next_args as the next call's arguments. GET /v3/companies/{cif}/vat-rates.

tools.name: smartbill_create_invoice
tools.title: Create an invoice
tools.description: Create an invoice for a client with product/service lines. By default it is saved as a DRAFT (no number) for review in SmartBill Cloud. With draft=false the invoice is ISSUED: it takes the next number of the series, cannot be deleted or edited through this server, can only be cancelled or reversed (storno), and, depending on the account's e-Factura setup, may be transmitted to ANAF. Confirm every field with the user before draft=false. Returns series, number, documentId, documentUrl (needs login) and documentViewUrl (public PDF link). POST /invoice/v2.

tools.name: smartbill_create_invoice_from_estimate
tools.title: Create an invoice from a proforma
tools.description: Create an invoice from an existing proforma (client and lines are copied from it). Default is a DRAFT; with draft=false the invoice is ISSUED with the next number of the series and may be transmitted to e-Factura / ANAF. Stock is not discharged. POST /invoice/v2 (useEstimateDetails).

tools.name: smartbill_create_estimate
tools.title: Create a proforma
tools.description: Create a proforma (estimate) for a client with product/service lines. Default is a DRAFT (no number); with draft=false it takes the next number of the proforma series. A proforma is not a fiscal invoice. Returns series, number, documentId and links. POST /estimate/v2.

tools.name: smartbill_reverse_invoice
tools.title: Reverse an invoice (storno)
tools.description: ISSUE a storno (credit) invoice that reverses an issued invoice. It takes the next number, an invoice can be reversed only once, and the storno cannot be undone; it may be transmitted to e-Factura / ANAF. Confirm the exact series and number with the user first. POST /invoice/reverse.

tools.name: smartbill_cancel_invoice
tools.title: Cancel an invoice
tools.description: Cancel an existing invoice (it stays in the books as cancelled; smartbill_restore_invoice undoes it). Changes the document's fiscal status, so confirm with the user. PUT /invoice/cancel.

tools.name: smartbill_restore_invoice
tools.title: Restore a cancelled invoice
tools.description: Restore an invoice that was cancelled, making it active again. PUT /invoice/restore.

tools.name: smartbill_cancel_estimate
tools.title: Cancel a proforma
tools.description: Cancel an existing proforma (smartbill_restore_estimate undoes it). PUT /estimate/cancel.

tools.name: smartbill_restore_estimate
tools.title: Restore a cancelled proforma
tools.description: Restore a proforma that was cancelled. PUT /estimate/restore.

tools.name: smartbill_record_invoice_payment
tools.title: Record a payment against invoices
tools.description: Record a collection (incasare) against one or more issued invoices; client and amount are taken from the invoices. With value (single invoice only) a partial payment is recorded. type Chitanta issues a numbered RECEIPT on receipt_series (cannot be undone from this server); the other types (Card, Ordin plata, ...) record the payment without a document. It changes the invoice's paid status in the books: confirm with the user. Fiscal receipts (Bon) are not supported. POST /payment.

tools.name: smartbill_send_document
tools.title: Email an invoice or proforma
tools.description: Send an issued invoice or proforma by email from SmartBill. This EMAILS A THIRD PARTY and cannot be recalled. Without `to` it goes to the client's email on the document; without subject/body_text the account's email template is used. Confirm the recipient with the user first. POST /document/send.

tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on SmartBill (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free).
