servers.name: packagecloud
servers.description: Read packagecloud repos, packages, versions and download stats; create repos, promote and delete.

login.hint: Log in at packagecloud.io and copy the token from [packagecloud.io/api_token](https://packagecloud.io/api_token). The token acts as your whole account, so keep it private. Your token is used only to call the packagecloud API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: packagecloud_list_repositories
tools.title: List repositories
tools.description: List the package repositories of this account: name, fqname (user/repo, used by every other tool), privacy, package count and last push. include_collaborations adds repositories you collaborate on. GET /repos.

tools.name: packagecloud_get_repository
tools.title: Get repository
tools.description: One repository: name, fqname, url, privacy, package count and last push. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}.

tools.name: packagecloud_create_repository
tools.title: Create repository
tools.description: WRITE: create a new, empty package repository in this account (the plan limits how many private ones). Returns the URL of the new repository. POST /repos.

tools.name: packagecloud_list_distributions
tools.title: List distributions
tools.description: The Linux distributions and versions packagecloud supports for deb, dsc and rpm packages, with their index_name (for example ubuntu / jammy) and numeric version ids. GET /distributions.

tools.name: packagecloud_list_packages
tools.title: List all packages
tools.description: List every package file in a repository (not grouped), newest data first as the server orders it. Each item carries ready-made URLs: package_url, versions_url, downloads_*_url, promote_url, destroy_url and download_url; pass those to the other package tools. Paged. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/packages.json.

tools.name: packagecloud_search_packages
tools.title: Search packages
tools.description: Search a repository by package file name. An empty q returns every package. filter limits by type (rpms, debs, dscs, gem, python, node); dist (for example ubuntu or el/6) overrides filter; arch applies to Alpine/RPM/Debian only. Items carry the same ready-made URLs as list_packages. Paged. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/search.json.

tools.name: packagecloud_list_package_groups
tools.title: List package names by type
tools.description: List the packages of one type, grouped by name with a versions_count and a versions_url (pass that to packagecloud_list_package_versions). Narrow by distro, then version, then arch (each needs the previous one; '*' matches any). Examples: type rpm; type deb + distro ubuntu + version jammy + arch amd64; type gem. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/packages/{type}[/{distro}[/{version}[/{arch}]]].json.

tools.name: packagecloud_get_package
tools.title: Get package
tools.description: Details of one package file (size, checksums, dependencies, licenses, download counts and its other URLs). Pass the package_url of an item from list_packages, search_packages or list_package_versions. GET {package_url}.

tools.name: packagecloud_list_package_versions
tools.title: List package versions
tools.description: All versions of one package name (for deb/rpm: per distro, version and architecture). Pass the versions_url of an item from list_package_groups, or derive it from a package object. Paged. GET {versions_url}.

tools.name: packagecloud_get_package_downloads
tools.title: Get package download stats
tools.description: Download statistics of one package version: a count, a time series, or (repository owners only) the detail of each download. Default range is the last 7 days; pass start_date=19700101Z for all time. Pass the package_url of the package; Java and generic files have no download stats. GET {package_url minus .json}/stats/downloads/{count|detail|series/<interval>}.json.

tools.name: packagecloud_get_repository_installs
tools.title: Get repository install stats
tools.description: How often a repository was installed (set up on a machine): a count, a time series, or (owners only) the detail of each install, optionally for one distro or distro+version. Default range is the last 7 days; pass start_date=19700101Z for all time. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/stats/installs[/{distro}[/{version}]]/{count|detail|series/<interval>}.json.

tools.name: packagecloud_list_gpg_keys
tools.title: List GPG keys
tools.description: The GPG keys of a repository (repository signing keys and package signing keys): name, fingerprint, type and the public key download URL. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/gpg_keys.json.

tools.name: packagecloud_get_gpg_key
tools.title: Get GPG key
tools.description: One GPG key of a repository by its key name (as returned by list_gpg_keys, for example user-repo-85D7FBF915DFCBC6.pub.gpg). GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/gpg_keys/{keyname}.json.

tools.name: packagecloud_get_readme
tools.title: Get repository README
tools.description: The Markdown README of a repository. GET /repos/{user}/{repo}/readme.json.

tools.name: packagecloud_create_readme
tools.title: Create repository README
tools.description: WRITE: create the Markdown README of a repository. Use append_readme to add to an existing one. POST /repos/{user}/{repo}/readme.json.

tools.name: packagecloud_append_readme
tools.title: Append to repository README
tools.description: WRITE: append Markdown to the existing README of a repository (existing text is kept). Not idempotent: calling it twice appends twice. PATCH /repos/{user}/{repo}/readme.json.

tools.name: packagecloud_promote_package
tools.title: Promote (move) package
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: MOVE a package file to another repository (for example staging -> production). It no longer exists in the source repository afterwards, and its download statistics are cleared. Pass the promote_url of the package object and the destination as user/repo. POST {promote_url}.

tools.name: packagecloud_delete_package
tools.title: Delete (yank) package
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE: delete one package file from its repository (a gem is yanked). Clients that depend on it will break. Pass the destroy_url of the package object and repeat its file name (the last path segment, for example jake-1.0-2.el6.x86_64.rpm) as confirm_filename. DELETE {destroy_url}.

tools.name: packagecloud_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: packagecloud_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the packagecloud tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: packagecloud_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on packagecloud (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: packagecloud_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's packagecloud Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run packagecloud_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: Cuttly
servers.description: Shorten links with Cuttly, read click stats, and edit, expire, redirect or delete short links.

login.hint: Find it in Cuttly → **Account → Edit Account** (the API key section). Cuttly limits API calls per plan (Free: 3 per minute) and link editing needs the Single plan or higher. Your key is used only to call the Cuttly API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: cuttly_shorten_link
tools.title: Shorten link
tools.description: WRITE: create a Cuttly short link for a long URL, optionally with a custom alias (the part after the slash). Returns the short link, the full link and the page title. It counts against the monthly link limit of the plan. Cuttly rate limit: Free 3 calls per 60 seconds, Starter 6, Single 60. The call is sent once and never retried. GET https://cutt.ly/api/api.php?short=...

tools.name: cuttly_get_link_stats
tools.title: Get link stats
tools.description: Click statistics of one short link: total clicks, clicks by source (Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, other, bots), top referrers, countries, device types, operating systems, browsers, device brands and languages. The date range filter needs the Team plan or higher. Counts as one API call (Free plan 3 per 60 seconds). GET https://cutt.ly/api/api.php?stats=...

tools.name: cuttly_update_link
tools.title: Update link
tools.description: WRITE: change a short link: its alias, destination URL, title, tag or unique-click window. Send only what you want to change. Changing the alias makes the old short link stop working; changing the destination redirects every visitor to the new URL at once. Link editing needs the Single plan or higher. Cuttly sends no previous values back, so ask the user before you change a live link. The call is sent once and never retried. GET https://cutt.ly/api/api.php?edit=...

tools.name: cuttly_set_link_expiration
tools.title: Set link expiration
tools.description: WRITE: set or remove the expiration of a short link. The link expires after a number of clicks or on a date, and can then redirect to another URL. mode 'none' removes an existing expiration. Needs the Single plan or higher. The call is sent once and never retried. GET https://cutt.ly/api/api.php?edit=...&expire=...

tools.name: cuttly_set_device_redirect
tools.title: Set device redirect
tools.description: WRITE: send visitors on one device type to another destination (an app store page or a deep link): Android, iOS or Windows Mobile. platform 'redirect' sets the destination for all other devices. Set `remove: true` instead of a destination to delete the rule. Needs the Single plan or higher. The call is sent once and never retried. GET https://cutt.ly/api/api.php?edit=...&mobile=...

tools.name: cuttly_delete_link
tools.title: Delete link
tools.description: WRITE, IRREVERSIBLE: permanently delete a short link and its statistics. Anyone who opens the short link afterwards gets an error, and Cuttly cannot restore it. Ask the user to confirm the exact link before you call this. Needs the Single plan or higher. The call is sent once and never retried. GET https://cutt.ly/api/api.php?edit=...&delete=1

Does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Cuttly (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). servers.name: Beacon CRM
servers.description: Read and filter Beacon CRM records of any type; create, update, upsert, delete records; run exports.

login.hint: Create the key in Beacon → **Settings → API keys → Create API key** (admins only; the API needs the Standard, Premium or Ultimate plan). The key is shown once. The account id is the number in the Beacon address bar after you log in. The key acts with your account's access, so changes it makes are real changes to your database. Your key is used only to call the Beacon API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: beaconcrm_list_record_types
tools.title: List record types and fields
tools.description: List the record types of this Beacon account (people, organisations, payments, custom types, ...) with their fields (keys, types, options). Call this first: the keys are what the other tools take as `entity` and as field names. GET /entity_types.

tools.name: beaconcrm_list_users
tools.title: List account users
tools.description: List the users of the Beacon account (id, role, name, email). Use the inner user.id for 'link to a user' fields. GET /users.

tools.name: beaconcrm_list_records
tools.title: List records
tools.description: List records of one type (for example person, organization, payment), one page at a time. Use beaconcrm_filter_records to search by field values. GET /entities/{entity}.

tools.name: beaconcrm_get_record
tools.title: Get record
tools.description: One record by type and id, with all its fields. GET /entity/{entity}/{id}.

tools.name: beaconcrm_filter_records
tools.title: Filter records
tools.description: Search records of one type with Beacon filter conditions (read-only; it uses POST because the filter is a body). Each condition is {"field", "operator", "value"}. Operators by field type: text == != starts_with ends_with contains not_contains null not_null; select (value is an array) contains not_contains in not_in null not_null; number == != > < null not_null; date date_on date_after date_before date_between (value e.g. "2026-01-01", "last_month", or ["2026-01-01","2026-06-01"]); checkbox == true; point-to-record (value is an array of ids) contains not_contains. Location parts: address.city etc.; emails: emails.email. Conditions can nest as {"filter_conditions": [...], "filter_strictness": "all"|"any"}. Example: [{"field":"emails.email","operator":"==","value":"a@b.org"}]. POST /entities/{entity}/filter.

tools.name: beaconcrm_create_record
tools.title: Create record
tools.description: WRITE: create ONE new record of the given type in the live Beacon database. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two records (use beaconcrm_upsert_record to avoid duplicates). Beacon workflows may run as a result. Invalid field values are rejected with the rule that failed. POST /entity/{entity}.

tools.name: beaconcrm_update_record
tools.title: Update record
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of ONE existing record. Only the fields you pass are changed; a select or reference field passed as an empty array [] is CLEARED, removing its existing values. The previous values are not kept by this tool. Beacon workflows may run as a result. PATCH /entity/{entity}/{id}.

tools.name: beaconcrm_upsert_record
tools.title: Create or update record by key field
tools.description: WRITE: create a record, or update the existing one whose key field matches. `primary_field_key` names the field used to find the match (for example "emails" for a person, or "external_id"); `fields` must contain a value for it. If a record matches it is UPDATED with the given fields (an empty array leaves an existing value untouched on upsert); otherwise a new record is created. Beacon workflows may run as a result. PUT /entity/{entity}/upsert.

tools.name: beaconcrm_delete_record
tools.title: Delete record
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: delete ONE record. Beacon keeps deleted records as 'archived' (listable with archived=true), but this server has no restore tool, so treat the deletion as irreversible. Related data that depends on the record may be affected. It is sent once and never retried. DELETE /entity/{entity}/{id}.

tools.name: beaconcrm_trigger_export
tools.title: Start an export
tools.description: WRITE: start an export job from an existing export template (created in Beacon). Returns the new export's id with status in_progress; then poll beaconcrm_list_exports with that id until progress is 100 and it carries a download url. Each call starts another job. POST /entity_export/trigger.

tools.name: beaconcrm_list_exports
tools.title: List exports
tools.description: List recent export jobs with status, progress (100 = complete) and, when complete, a signed download url. Pass entity_export_id to check one job started by beaconcrm_trigger_export. GET /entity_exports.

Does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Beacon CRM (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). login.hint: Find it in Emailable → **API** → your API keys (create a private key; do not restrict it to trusted IP addresses, because Cloudflare's IPs change). tools.description: The Emailable account behind this API key: the owner's email and available_credits. Check it before a large batch. GET /v1/account.

tools.name: emailable_verify_email
tools.title: Verify one email address
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: verifies one email address and uses 1 Emailable credit (a test_ API key spends none). Returns state (deliverable, undeliverable, risky, unknown), reason, score (0-100), and flags: disposable, free, role, accept_all, no_reply, mailbox_full, plus did_you_mean (a typo fix), the detected user/domain/tag, mx_record and smtp_provider. A credit is returned for an unknown result. The call is never retried automatically. If the reply is {status: "try_again"}, the check took longer than the timeout: call again with the same email; repeats within 5 minutes are not charged. Emailable's terms allow verification of opt-in subscribers' addresses. GET /v1/verify.

tools.name: emailable_create_batch

tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS: starts a bulk verification of up to 5000 email addresses. tools.name: emailable_get_batch

tools.description: Status and results of a batch made with emailable_create_batch: message, progress (processed/total), reason_counts and total_counts (deliverable, undeliverable, risky, unknown). Batches of up to 1,000 emails also return the results inline in `emails` (30 days). servers.name: Teamup Calendar
servers.description: Read and search Teamup Calendar events and sub-calendars; create, update, delete and undo events.

login.hint: The **API key** is free and personal: request your own at [teamup.com/api-keys/request](https://teamup.com/api-keys/request) (Teamup uses it to know who runs an app, it gives no access to a calendar). The **calendar key** is the last part of a calendar link: open the calendar, go to **Settings → Sharing**, create a link with the permission you want the AI to have (read-only, add only, modify or admin), and paste the link or its key (it starts with `ks`). Both are used only to call the Teamup API on your behalf and are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: teamup_get_calendar
tools.title: Get calendar
tools.description: The calendar this connection points at: title, timezone and date settings, custom event fields, sub-calendars, the permission of the calendar key in use and the plan's features. Call this first to learn the sub-calendar ids and the timezone. The calendar key itself is never returned. GET /{calendarKey}/configuration.

tools.name: teamup_list_subcalendars
tools.title: List sub-calendars
tools.description: List the sub-calendars (the colored lanes that events belong to, such as people, rooms or resources). A key with admin permission also sees inactive ones. GET /{calendarKey}/subcalendars.

tools.name: teamup_get_subcalendar
tools.title: Get sub-calendar
tools.description: One sub-calendar by id: name, color, overlap rule, active state and which links may use it. GET /{calendarKey}/subcalendars/{id}.

tools.name: teamup_list_access_keys
tools.title: List access keys
tools.description: List the calendar's access keys (sharing links and user accesses) with name, role, active state and per-sub-calendar permission. Needs a key with admin permission. The secret key values are never returned (they are secrets); use the id and name to tell links apart. GET /{calendarKey}/keys.

tools.name: teamup_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List the events in a date range, optionally only on some sub-calendars. Recurring events are expanded: every occurrence in the range is returned with its own id (series id + -rid- + start). Notes come as markdown. Times use the calendar's timezone unless tz is set. GET /{calendarKey}/events.

tools.name: teamup_search_events
tools.title: Search events
tools.description: Search events by keyword (2-100 characters) within a date range (default: today only, so always pass the range you mean). Recurring events are expanded. Paged with limit and offset. GET /{calendarKey}/events?query=.

tools.name: teamup_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event by id: title, times, sub-calendars, location, who, notes (markdown), recurrence rule, custom fields, signups, comments, attachments (metadata), version, change history and reminders. Use the occurrence id (123-rid-<unix start>) for one occurrence of a recurring event. GET /{calendarKey}/events/{id}.

tools.name: teamup_list_changed_events
tools.title: List changed events
tools.description: Events created, changed or deleted since a Unix timestamp (at most 30 days back), for syncing. A recurring event comes back once, as its series, not as occurrences. Deleted events carry delete_dt. Pass the reply's timestamp as since_timestamp next time so nothing is missed. GET /{calendarKey}/events?modifiedSince=.

tools.name: teamup_list_event_signups
tools.title: List event signups
tools.description: The people signed up for an event (name, email, id). Signups must be enabled on the event. GET /{calendarKey}/events/{id}/signups.

tools.name: teamup_create_event
tools.title: Create event
tools.description: WRITE: create an event. Needs a calendar key with add or modify permission. Give at least subcalendar_ids, start and end. Not idempotent: a repeated call creates a second event. The reply holds the new event and an undo_id; teamup_undo_event_action removes the event again within one hour. POST /{calendarKey}/events.

tools.name: teamup_update_event
tools.title: Update event
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an event; fields you leave out keep their value (the event is read first and sent back with its version, so a concurrent edit is refused instead of overwritten; an event without a version is not changed). Needs modify permission. For a recurring event pass redit; use the occurrence id (123-rid-<unix start>) with single or future. Attachments are not touched. The reply holds the event and an undo_id for one hour (teamup_undo_event_action). PUT /{calendarKey}/events/{id}.

tools.name: teamup_delete_event
tools.title: Delete event
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: delete an event, or for a recurring event the chosen occurrences. Needs modify permission. Not retried. The reply holds an undo_id; teamup_undo_event_action restores the event within one hour, after that the deletion is permanent. For one occurrence use the occurrence id (123-rid-<unix start>) and redit single (the default); redit all deletes the whole series. DELETE /{calendarKey}/events/{id}.

tools.name: teamup_undo_event_action
tools.title: Undo event change
tools.description: WRITE: undo a recent event creation, update or deletion with the undo_id from that call. Works for one hour only and is refused if someone else changed the event since. PUT /{calendarKey}/events/undo/{undo_id}.

tools.name: teamup_create_subcalendar
tools.title: Create sub-calendar
tools.description: WRITE: create a sub-calendar. Needs a calendar key with admin permission, and the plan may limit how many exist. Not idempotent: a repeated call creates a second one. POST /{calendarKey}/subcalendars.

tools.name: teamup_update_subcalendar
tools.title: Update sub-calendar
tools.description: WRITE: change a sub-calendar's name, color, overlap rule or active state; fields you leave out keep their value. Needs admin permission. Making a sub-calendar inactive hides it from users without admin rights. PATCH /{calendarKey}/subcalendars/{id}.

tools.name: teamup_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: teamup_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Teamup Calendar tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: teamup_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Teamup Calendar (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: teamup_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Teamup Calendar Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run teamup_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: What is on the shared team calendar this week, day by day?
Find all events mentioning 'inspection' in the next two months.
Who is signed up for the Saturday workshop?
Add a team meeting to the shared calendar next Monday from 10:00 to 11:00.

servers.name: Fieldwire
servers.description: Read Fieldwire projects, tasks, plans, forms, RFIs and submittals; create and update tasks.

login.hint: Account Owners and Managers create the token in Fieldwire under **Account → API Settings**. API access is not on every plan: Fieldwire sells it with the Premier plan or as an add-on to Pro and Business, so ask Fieldwire sales if the section is missing. The token acts as its user. The region is the one your projects live in (US, EU or Canada). Your token is used only to call the Fieldwire API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: fieldwire_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The Fieldwire account this API token belongs to: id, company name and address, enabled modules (submittals, change orders, RFIs, specs, BIM) and the owner. GET /account on the account host.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_account_users
tools.title: List account users
tools.description: All users on the account (and users invited to its projects) with name, company, email, account role and the number of projects each is in. User ids are what tasks use for owner and assignees. GET /account/users on the account host.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: Projects the token's user can access in the region chosen at login: id, name, code, address, time zone, plan and archive state. Filter by name, code, archive state or update time. Use the id in every other tool. GET /api/v3/projects.

tools.name: fieldwire_get_project
tools.title: Get project
tools.description: One project by id: name, code, address, time zone, currency, plan, enabled features and owner email. GET /api/v3/projects/{id}.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_project_users
tools.title: List project users
tools.description: Users on one project with name, company, job title, email and phone. The integer id is what tasks use for owner_user_id and user_ids. Filter by email, name or company. GET /api/v3/account/projects/{project_id}/users.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: Tasks (punch items, issues) in a project: name, status_id, team_id, location_id, floorplan_id, owner and assignee user ids, priority, dates and cost. Filter by status, team, location, plan, owner, name, tag and dates. Resolve ids with fieldwire_list_task_statuses, _list_teams, _list_locations and _list_project_users. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/tasks.

tools.name: fieldwire_get_task
tools.title: Get task
tools.description: One task by id with all its fields. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/tasks/{id}.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_task_statuses
tools.title: List task statuses
tools.description: The task statuses of a project (id, name, order, kind open/tracked/verified, default flag). Use the id as status_id on tasks. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/statuses.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_teams
tools.title: List teams (task categories)
tools.description: Teams of a project (id, name, handle). The Fieldwire app calls them 'categories' on tasks; tasks carry a team_id. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/teams.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: Locations of a project (id, name, parent location_id). Tasks carry a location_id. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/locations.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_task_check_items
tools.title: List task checklist items
tools.description: Checklist items of all tasks in a project: name, checked flag, state (empty/yes/no/not_applicable) and task_id (match it to the task). GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/task_check_items.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_floorplans
tools.title: List plans (floorplans)
tools.description: Plans (floorplans) of a project: id, name, description, folder and sheet count. Filter by name, tag or dates. Set with_current_sheet to include each plan's current sheet. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/floorplans.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_sheets
tools.title: List sheets
tools.description: Sheets (plan versions) of a project: id, name, file name, version, floorplan_id and file URLs. Filter by plan, folder, name or dates. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/sheets.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_attachments
tools.title: List attachments
tools.description: Files, photos, videos and 360 photos attached in a project: id, name, kind, size, capture time and file URLs. Filter by kind. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/attachments.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_forms
tools.title: List forms
tools.description: Forms (inspections, daily reports, checklists) of a project: id, name, template, status, owner, dates. Forms need a Business plan. Use fieldwire_get_form_full for the filled-in values. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/forms.

tools.name: fieldwire_get_form
tools.title: Get form
tools.description: One form by id (header data only, not the filled-in values). GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/forms/{id}.

tools.name: fieldwire_get_form_full
tools.title: Get form with all values
tools.description: A form with its sections, inputs and filled-in values. Two steps: call without jid to start the job (Fieldwire answers with a jid); then call again with that jid until the form comes back (answer 'pending' means not ready, retry). GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/forms/{id}/full.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_form_templates
tools.title: List form templates
tools.description: Form templates of a project: id, name, version, publish state. Use the id to filter forms. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/form_templates.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_rfis
tools.title: List RFIs
tools.description: RFIs (requests for information) of a project: number, name, question, answer, status, assignee, due date. Needs the RFI module. Filter by status, assignee, text, overdue or dates. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/rfis.

tools.name: fieldwire_list_submittals
tools.title: List submittals
tools.description: Submittals of a project: number, name, status, revision, key dates. Needs the submittals module. Filter by status, assignee, text, overdue or dates. GET /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/submittals.

tools.name: fieldwire_create_task
tools.title: Create task
tools.description: WRITE: creates a new task in a project. It is sent once and never retried; if the reply is an error, check fieldwire_list_tasks before creating it again, or you may get a duplicate. owner_user_id and priority are required; creator_user_id defaults to the owner. Find user ids with fieldwire_list_project_users. POST /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/tasks.

tools.name: fieldwire_update_task
tools.title: Update task
tools.description: WRITE: changes fields of one task (only the fields you pass; user_ids replaces the whole assignee list; null clears a field that allows it). Use it to set the status, owner, assignees, priority or dates. It does not delete the task. Sent once, never retried. PATCH /api/v3/projects/{project_id}/tasks/{id}.

tools.name: fieldwire_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: fieldwire_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Fieldwire tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: fieldwire_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Fieldwire (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: fieldwire_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Fieldwire Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run fieldwire_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: List my construction projects and where each one is located.
Show all open tasks on the Maple Street project.
Which RFIs on the Maple Street project are still waiting for an answer?
Create a task on the Maple Street project: patch drywall in unit 4.

servers.name: CashCtrl
servers.description: Read CashCtrl accounts, journal, orders, people, articles, salaries and reports; book and create.

login.hint: Create the key in CashCtrl under **Settings → Users & Roles → Add → Add API user** (the API needs a PRO account; one API user per organization). The role of the API user decides what this server can read and change, so a read-only role makes it read-only. The organization is the "myorg" part of myorg.cashctrl.com. Your key is used only to call the CashCtrl API of that organization on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_accounts
tools.title: List accounts
tools.description: The chart of accounts: number, name, category and the balance for the fiscal period. Not paged. GET /account/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_get_account
tools.title: Get an account
tools.description: One account of the chart of accounts by id. GET /account/read.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_get_account_balance
tools.title: Get an account balance
tools.description: The balance of one account at the end of a day (default: the last day of the current fiscal period). GET /account/balance.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_account_categories
tools.title: List account categories
tools.description: The categories of the chart of accounts (assets, liabilities, expenses, revenue and their sub-categories). GET /account/category/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_bank_accounts
tools.title: List bank accounts
tools.description: The bank accounts set up in CashCtrl (name, IBAN, linked ledger account). GET /account/bank/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_journal
tools.title: List journal entries
tools.description: Book entries of the journal (date, title, debit and credit account, amount, reference), newest first, for the current fiscal period unless fiscal_period_id is set. GET /journal/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_get_journal_entry
tools.title: Get a journal entry
tools.description: One book entry by id, with its items for a collective entry. GET /journal/read.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_orders
tools.title: List orders
tools.description: Sales or purchase documents (quotes, order confirmations, invoices, delivery notes, credit notes, vendor bills) with number, date, customer, status and total. Newest first. GET /order/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_get_order
tools.title: Get an order
tools.description: One order (invoice, quote, purchase document) by id, with its items, totals and status. GET /order/read.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_order_categories
tools.title: List order categories
tools.description: The order categories (Quote, Invoice, Credit note, Purchase invoice and so on) with their statuses (Draft, Open, Paid) and the default accounts and sequence numbers. Use it to find category_id and status_id (type PURCHASE for purchase documents). GET /order/category/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_persons
tools.title: List people
tools.description: Customers, vendors, employees and other contacts (name, company, number, roles, addresses). GET /person/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_get_person
tools.title: Get a person
tools.description: One person or company by id, with addresses, contact data and bank accounts. GET /person/read.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_articles
tools.title: List inventory articles
tools.description: Inventory articles (products and services) with number, name, price, stock and accounts. GET /inventory/article/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_get_article
tools.title: Get an inventory article
tools.description: One inventory article by id. GET /inventory/article/read.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_salary_statements
tools.title: List salary statements
tools.description: Payroll statements (employee, date, status, gross and net amounts), newest first. Sensitive personal data. GET /salary/statement/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_get_salary_statement
tools.title: Get a salary statement
tools.description: One payroll statement by id, with its salary items. Sensitive personal data. GET /salary/statement/read.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_fiscal_periods
tools.title: List fiscal periods
tools.description: All fiscal periods (id, name, start, end, current flag). The id is the fiscal_period_id of the other tools. GET /fiscalperiod/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_tax_codes
tools.title: List tax codes
tools.description: The VAT tax codes (id, code, name, rates). The id is the tax_id of the write tools. GET /tax/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_sequence_numbers
tools.title: List sequence numbers
tools.description: The number sequences (for journal references, order numbers, customer numbers). The id is the sequence_number_id of the write tools. GET /sequencenumber/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_list_currencies
tools.title: List currencies
tools.description: The currencies set up in CashCtrl with their exchange rates. GET /currency/list.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_get_report_tree
tools.title: Get the report tree
tools.description: The reports set up in CashCtrl (balance sheet, income statement, and so on) as a tree of collections and elements. The element id is the input of cashctrl_get_report_data. GET /report/tree.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_get_report_data
tools.title: Get report data
tools.description: The data of one report element (for example the balance sheet or the income statement) for a fiscal period or a date range. GET /report/element/data.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_create_journal_entry
tools.title: Create a journal entry
tools.description: WRITE: changes the accounting records. Makes one request that is never repeated; check the result before trying again. Creates a manual book entry in the journal. Either a simple entry (debit_account_id, credit_account_id, amount) or a collective entry (items, whose debit and credit sums must match). POST /journal/create.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_delete_journal_entries
tools.title: Delete journal entries
tools.description: WRITE: changes the accounting records. Makes one request that is never repeated; check the result before trying again. DELETES manual journal entries by id (entries created by orders or salary statements cannot be deleted this way). Deleted entries are gone from the books; confirm the ids with the user first. POST /journal/delete.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_create_order
tools.title: Create an order
tools.description: WRITE: changes the accounting records. Makes one request that is never repeated; check the result before trying again. Creates ONE order document for ONE customer or vendor: a quote, invoice, credit note, purchase bill and so on, depending on category_id. Without status_id the first status of the category is used; a booking status (for example Open) also creates journal entries, so use a draft status unless the user asks otherwise. No e-mail is sent. POST /order/create.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_update_order_status
tools.title: Change the status of orders
tools.description: WRITE: changes the accounting records. Makes one request that is never repeated; check the result before trying again. Sets the status of 1-20 orders (for example Draft to Open, or Open to Paid). A status can book journal entries or move stock, so the books change. POST /order/update_status.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_delete_orders
tools.title: Delete orders
tools.description: WRITE: changes the accounting records. Makes one request that is never repeated; check the result before trying again. DELETES orders (invoices, quotes, purchase documents) by id, with the journal entries they created. Deleted documents are gone; confirm the ids with the user first. POST /order/delete.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_create_person
tools.title: Create a person or company
tools.description: WRITE: changes the accounting records. Makes one request that is never repeated; check the result before trying again. Creates a customer, vendor or other contact. Give company, first_name or last_name (at least one). Search first with cashctrl_list_persons so no duplicate is created. POST /person/create.json.

tools.name: cashctrl_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the CashCtrl tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: cashctrl_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on CashCtrl (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: cashctrl_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's CashCtrl Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run cashctrl_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

What is our income statement for the current fiscal year?
Show the bookkeeping entries from last month.
Add a new customer called Acme Ltd to my contacts.

servers.name: Zenserp
servers.description: Search Google, images, news, maps, shopping, YouTube, jobs, hotels, flights and trends with Zenserp.

login.hint: Find it in your Zenserp dashboard at **app.zenserp.com** (the key is shown after you log in). Every search the AI runs spends requests from your Zenserp plan's monthly quota. Your key is used only to call the Zenserp API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: zenserp_get_status
tools.title: Get remaining requests
tools.description: The number of search requests left on this Zenserp key's plan (remaining_requests). Free: it spends no quota. GET /v2/status.

tools.name: zenserp_search
tools.title: Search the web (SERP)
tools.description: Live search-engine result page as JSON: organic results, ads (paid_results), featured snippets, related questions and searches, knowledge graph. Google by default; set search_engine for Bing, Yandex or DuckDuckGo. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. ai_overview=true also returns Google's AI Overview and costs 3 requests when one is returned (Small plan or higher). GET /v2/search.

tools.name: zenserp_image_search
tools.title: Search Google Images
tools.description: Google image results (thumbnails, source pages, sizes). SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. Each page holds 100 images. GET /v2/search (tbm=isch).

tools.name: zenserp_news_search
tools.title: Search Google News
tools.description: Google News results for a query: title, source, date, snippet. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v2/search (tbm=nws).

tools.name: zenserp_video_search
tools.title: Search Google Videos
tools.description: Google video results for a query (title, channel, length, link). SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v2/search (tbm=vid).

tools.name: zenserp_maps_search
tools.title: Search Google local and maps
tools.description: Google local/maps results: shops, cafes and other businesses with address, rating, phone and coordinates. Set location for accurate results. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v2/search (tbm=lcl).

tools.name: zenserp_shopping_search
tools.title: Search Google Shopping
tools.description: Google Shopping listings for a query: product, price, merchant, rating, and the product_id for zenserp_shopping_product. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v2/search (tbm=shop).

tools.name: zenserp_youtube_search
tools.title: Search YouTube
tools.description: YouTube search results (videos, channels, ads) for a query, optionally by location. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v2/search (search_engine=youtube.com).

tools.name: zenserp_reverse_image_search
tools.title: Reverse image search
tools.description: Pages and sources that contain a given image (Google reverse image search). SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v2/search (image_url).

tools.name: zenserp_jobs_search
tools.title: Search Google Jobs
tools.description: Google Jobs listings for a query (jobs_results: title, company, location, source, apply url). Google returns one page; there is no paging. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v2/search (ibp=htl;jobs).

tools.name: zenserp_shopping_product
tools.title: Get Google Shopping product page
tools.description: Product page data from Google Shopping: description, merchant offers, variations. product_id comes from zenserp_shopping_search. With gpc_id (from the same result) it returns the whole product cluster across merchants. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v1/shopping.

tools.name: zenserp_hotels
tools.title: Search Google Hotels
tools.description: Google Hotels offers for a hotel or place. Send check_in and check_out together, or Google falls back to today's rates. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v1/hotels.

tools.name: zenserp_flights
tools.title: Search Google Flights
tools.description: Google Flights options. Best: origin and destination as 3-letter airport codes plus departure_date (dates and curr are honoured only then). A free-text q or a tfs string from a Google Flights URL also works. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v1/flights.

tools.name: zenserp_trends
tools.title: Get Google Trends
tools.description: Trending searches from Google Trends for a country, optionally narrowed to given keywords or a category. Trending data covers at most the past 7 days. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v1/trends.

tools.name: zenserp_answer_engine
tools.title: Ask an AI answer engine
tools.description: Send a prompt to an AI answer engine (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Copilot) and get its answer_text with citations; with brand it also reports whether and where that brand was cited. SPENDS quota at Zenserp's premium per-answer rate (see Zenserp pricing), is slow (seconds to a minute), and must not be repeated needlessly. Plan gate: Medium unlocks ChatGPT, Large adds Perplexity, Premium adds Gemini, Enterprise adds Copilot. GET /v1/answer-engine.

tools.name: zenserp_list_search_engines
tools.title: List search engines
tools.description: The search engine hosts Zenserp supports (values for search_engine). GET /v2/search_engines. The docs do not say whether helper lists are charged; they are not searches.

tools.name: zenserp_list_languages
tools.title: List languages (hl)
tools.description: The supported interface language codes (values for hl). GET /v2/hl.

tools.name: zenserp_list_countries
tools.title: List countries (gl)
tools.description: The supported country codes (values for gl). GET /v2/gl.

tools.name: zenserp_search_locations
tools.title: Search geo locations
tools.description: The supported geo locations (values for location), as Google's canonical names. The list is long: pass query to keep only entries that contain it, and limit to cap the count. GET /v2/locations.

tools.name: zenserp_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: zenserp_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Zenserp tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: zenserp_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Zenserp (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: zenserp_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Zenserp Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run zenserp_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: What are the top search results for 'best coffee roaster Prague'?
Find coffee shops near Leeds city centre with their ratings and phone numbers.
What is the latest news about electric delivery vans?
How many search requests do I have left on my plan?

login.hint: Create it in Bill4Time under **Settings → API** tab. Use a v1 key. The key gives read access to your firm's billing data; this server only reads, and returns no private notes unless you ask. Your key is used only to call the Bill4Time API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone. Delete the key in Bill4Time to disconnect.

tools.name: bill4time_list_clients
tools.title: List clients
tools.description: List clients (id, name, billing name, email, phone, city, account manager, status, billing rate type, currency). Filter by status, exact client name, id or creation date. Street addresses and tax ids are not returned. GET /clients.

tools.name: bill4time_list_projects
tools.title: List projects (matters)
tools.description: List projects (matters): id, name, client, status, billing method, rate overrides, assigned user, created/closed/due dates. Filter by status, billing method, client, id or creation date. GET /projects.

tools.name: bill4time_list_time_entries
tools.title: List time entries
tools.description: List time entries: client, project, user, entry date, billable and labor time, billable amount, rate, activity, ABA litigation code, billing status, invoice id, public description. Filter by client, project, user, invoice, entry date range or billing status. Private notes and contractor pay rates are not returned unless include_private_notes is set. GET /timeEntries.

tools.name: bill4time_list_expenses
tools.title: List expenses
tools.description: List expenses: client, project, user, expense date, cost and sell price, quantity, type, billing status, invoice id, public description. Filter by client, project, user, invoice, expense date range, billing status or exact expense type. Private notes are not returned unless include_private_notes is set. GET /expenses.

tools.name: bill4time_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices: client, project, invoice date, status (prebill or finalized), paid status, totals (invoice, labor, expense, late fee), terms and notes. Filter by status, paid status, client, project, id or invoice date range. GET /invoices.

tools.name: bill4time_list_payments
tools.title: List payments
tools.description: List payments: client, project, amount, date, type, method, public note. Filter by client, project, id or payment date range. Check numbers are not returned; the private note only with include_private_notes. GET /payments.

tools.name: bill4time_list_users
tools.title: List users (timekeepers)
tools.description: List the firm's users: name, email, user type, status, department, position, billing and overtime rate. Birth dates, addresses, phone numbers and contractor pay rates are not returned. Filter by status or id. GET /users.

tools.name: bill4time_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts: name, email, work and mobile phone, city, status, creation date. Filter by status, id or creation date. Street addresses, home phone and notes are not returned. GET /contacts.

servers.name: Notifyre
servers.description: Read Notifyre SMS, replies, faxes, numbers, prices and contacts; send SMS to up to 10 numbers.

login.hint: Create a token in the Notifyre dashboard under **Settings > Developer** > **New**. The token acts with its role's permissions; use a role that can send and receive, not the Developer role. Sending SMS through this server spends the prepaid balance of your account. Your token is used only to call the Notifyre API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: notifyre_list_sent_sms
tools.title: List sent SMS
tools.description: List SMS messages sent from the account, newest first by default, with recipient, status and cost. Without from_date the window is the last 30 days. Filter by status (processing, submitted, sent, failed), numbers, or a message id in search. Page with skip = next_skip. Notifyre API: GET /sms/send.

tools.name: notifyre_get_sent_sms
tools.title: Get a sent SMS
tools.description: Get one sent SMS message with every recipient: status, delivery status, message parts, cost. Use the id from notifyre_list_sent_sms or notifyre_send_sms. Notifyre API: GET /sms/send/{id}.

tools.name: notifyre_get_sms_recipient
tools.title: Get an SMS recipient message
tools.description: Get the text and delivery details of one recipient of a sent SMS (status, parts, cost). Notifyre API: GET /sms/send/{messageId}/recipients/{recipientId}.

tools.name: notifyre_list_sms_replies
tools.title: List SMS replies
tools.description: List SMS replies received on the account's numbers. Without from_date the window is the last 30 days. from_number and to_number must be given together. include_reply_content adds the reply texts (then at most 20 per page). Page with skip = next_skip. Notifyre API: GET /sms/received.

tools.name: notifyre_get_sms_reply
tools.title: Get an SMS reply
tools.description: Get one received SMS reply with its text, sender and receiving number. Use the replyID from notifyre_list_sms_replies. Notifyre API: GET /sms/received/{id}.

tools.name: notifyre_list_sms_numbers
tools.title: List SMS numbers and sender IDs
tools.description: List the account's SMS numbers (E.164, status, 10DLC campaign) and approved alphanumeric sender IDs. Use one of them as `from` when sending. Notifyre API: GET /sms/numbers.

tools.name: notifyre_list_sms_prices
tools.title: List SMS prices
tools.description: List the price of one SMS per destination country (country code, calling prefix, price, currency). Check it before sending: the cost of a send is price x message parts x recipients. Notifyre API: GET /sms/send/prices.

tools.name: notifyre_list_sent_faxes
tools.title: List sent faxes
tools.description: List faxes sent from the account (recipient, pages, quality, status, failure reason). Without from_date the window is the last 30 days. Filter by status (accepted, successful, in_progress, failed, queued). Page with skip = next_skip. Notifyre API: GET /fax/send.

tools.name: notifyre_list_received_faxes
tools.title: List received faxes
tools.description: List faxes received on the account's fax numbers (sender, number, time, pages, duration, read flag). The fax documents are not downloaded. Without from_date the window is the last 30 days. Page with skip = next_skip. Notifyre API: GET /fax/received.

tools.name: notifyre_list_fax_numbers
tools.title: List fax numbers
tools.description: List the account's fax numbers (E.164, region, status). Notifyre API: GET /fax/numbers.

tools.name: notifyre_list_fax_prices
tools.title: List fax prices
tools.description: List the price of sending a fax per destination country (country code, calling prefix, price, currency). Notifyre API: GET /fax/send/prices.

tools.name: notifyre_list_fax_cover_pages
tools.title: List fax cover pages
tools.description: List the fax cover page templates of the account (name and whether it is the default). The HTML of each template is left out. Notifyre API: GET /fax/coverpages.

tools.name: notifyre_list_contacts
tools.title: List address book contacts
tools.description: Search the address book. search_query matches the name; type FaxNumber or MobileNumber keeps contacts that have that number; group_ids limits to groups. Page numbers start at 0. Contacts that unsubscribed are left out unless include_unsubscribed is true. The unsubscribe key of a contact is never shown. Notifyre API: POST /addressbook/contacts/search (a read).

tools.name: notifyre_get_contact
tools.title: Get an address book contact
tools.description: Get one contact: names, organization, email, fax and mobile number, groups, custom fields, unsubscribed flag. Notifyre API: GET /addressbook/contacts/{id}.

tools.name: notifyre_list_groups
tools.title: List address book groups
tools.description: List the address book groups with their contact counts. Notifyre API: GET /addressbook/groups.

tools.name: notifyre_list_brands
tools.title: List 10DLC brands
tools.description: List the account's registered 10DLC brands (US SMS sender registration). Notifyre API: GET /numbers/brands.

tools.name: notifyre_list_campaigns
tools.title: List 10DLC campaigns
tools.description: List the account's 10DLC campaigns (US SMS use-case registrations) and their status. Notifyre API: GET /numbers/campaigns.

tools.name: notifyre_send_sms
tools.title: Send SMS
tools.description: WRITE: SENDS REAL SMS to real people and SPENDS the prepaid balance of the user's Notifyre account; it cannot be undone or recalled and is never retried. One text to 1 to 10 mobile numbers in international format with "+" (e.g. +61412345678); no contacts, no groups, no scheduling. Cost = price per message part (see notifyre_list_sms_prices; it depends on the destination country) x number of parts x number of recipients; the text may be up to 640 characters (160 per part, 70 with emoji or non-GSM characters, a little less per part when it is longer). Only send what the user explicitly asked for: confirm the exact text, the recipients and the sender first. Recipients must have agreed to receive messages. A commercial SMS needs an opt-out (Australia: Spam Act 2003; Notifyre Terms and Conditions 13.5): set add_unsubscribe_link true to append Notifyre's opt-out link, or put your own opt-out instruction in the text. The default is false, so the requirement is yours to meet. US numbers need a registered 10DLC campaign. Omit `from` to send from a Notifyre shared number. An unclear result (timeout, HTTP 5xx) means the message may still have been sent: check notifyre_list_sent_sms before trying again. Notifyre API: POST /sms/send.

tools.name: notifyre_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: WRITE: adds one contact to the Notifyre address book. Give at least a name or a number. Numbers in international format (e.g. +61412345678). groups takes existing group ids; group_name puts the contact in that group and CREATES the group if it does not exist. Creating the same contact twice may make a duplicate. Notifyre API: POST /addressbook/contacts.

tools.name: notifyre_create_group
tools.title: Create a contact group
tools.description: WRITE: creates one address book group with the given name. Notifyre API: POST /addressbook/groups.

tools.name: notifyre_add_contacts_to_groups
tools.title: Add contacts to groups
tools.description: WRITE: adds existing contacts to existing groups (up to 100 contacts and 20 groups). Contacts keep their other groups. Adding a contact to a group does not send anything, but a later send to that group reaches it. Notifyre API: POST /addressbook/groups/contacts.

servers.name: Lessonspace
servers.description: Read Lessonspace sessions, recordings, transcripts, spaces and users; launch spaces, edit sessions.

login.hint: Create it in Lessonspace → **Settings → Developer** (owner or Developer role, two-factor sign-in required). Lessonspace shows the key once, so copy it right away. The key acts for your whole organisation, so use a key made for this connection and delete it in Lessonspace to disconnect. Your key is used only to call the Lessonspace API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: lessonspace_list_sessions
tools.title: List sessions
tools.description: List the organisation's sessions (a session is one meeting held in a space): name, uuid, start/end time, space, participants (name, email, role), guests, billable seconds, tags, summary and recording state. Filter by time, duration, participant, space, launch id or tags. Newest first as Lessonspace orders them. Each session's playback_url is an access link to its recording, and participant emails are personal data: treat both as sensitive and share them only with someone entitled to see them. GET /organisations/sessions/.

tools.name: lessonspace_get_session
tools.title: Get session
tools.description: One session by uuid, with its space, participants, guests, tags, summary and recording state. GET /organisations/sessions/{session}/.

tools.name: lessonspace_get_session_recording
tools.title: Get session recording URL
tools.description: The playback URL of a session's recording. status 'ready' = the URL works now; 'preparing' = Lessonspace is still creating it (ask again in a minute); 'no_recording' = recording was disabled, so none exists. The URL is an access link: give it only to someone entitled to watch the recording. GET /organisations/sessions/{session}/playback/.

tools.name: lessonspace_get_session_transcript
tools.title: Get session transcript URL
tools.description: A signed download URL for a session's transcript. Only works if transcription was switched on for the session (launch with transcribe=true). The URL is an access link: give it only to someone entitled to read the transcript. GET /organisations/sessions/{session}/transcript/.

tools.name: lessonspace_update_session
tools.title: Rename session / set recording access
tools.description: WRITE: rename a session and optionally set who may watch its recording (a list of participant, admin, teacher, student; an empty list falls back to the organisation policy). The name is always sent (Lessonspace requires it). PATCH /organisations/sessions/{session}/.

tools.name: lessonspace_list_spaces
tools.title: List spaces
tools.description: List the organisation's spaces (persistent rooms): id, name, slug, alias, url, tags, lock state, region and recording/transcription settings. The url of a space is a way in; treat it as sensitive. GET /organisations/spaces/.

tools.name: lessonspace_list_space_sessions
tools.title: List sessions of a space
tools.description: Sessions held in one space, with the join/leave log (who joined, left or went idle, and when) and the users connected now. Same filters as lessonspace_list_sessions. GET /spaces/{space}/sessions/.

tools.name: lessonspace_launch_space
tools.title: Launch a space (create a join link)
tools.description: WRITE: create a space, or reuse the one with the same `id`, and get a join link (client_url) for one participant. The link is a live credential for a real person: share it only with that person and never post it elsewhere. Calling again with the same id reuses the space but issues a new link; it is not safe to repeat blindly. Lessonspace's own `secret` is never returned. POST /spaces/launch/.

tools.name: lessonspace_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the organisation's users: Lessonspace user id, name, email, role (teacher, student, admin), active state and external id. Names and emails are personal data. GET /organisations/users/.
