servers.name: Clio
servers.description: Read Clio matters, contacts, time, tasks, calendar and bills; add matters, time entries, notes.

login.hint: This server reads your firm's matters, contacts, time and expense entries, tasks, calendar, bills, document details (names and metadata, never file contents), notes, logged phone calls and emails, and custom fields. It can create contacts, matters, time entries, tasks, notes and calendar entries, log a phone call or email (it never sends one) and update tasks when you ask it to; it never deletes anything, changes a bill or touches payments or trust accounts. It can do only what your Clio user is allowed to do. This server is for Clio accounts in the US region. You can revoke access any time in Clio.

tools.name: clio_who_am_i
tools.title: Who am I
tools.description: Fetch the Clio user this access token belongs to — name, email, subscription type, time zone and default_calendar_id (needed to create calendar entries). A cheap way to confirm the token and region are right. Clio: GET /users/who_am_i.json.

tools.name: clio_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the firm's Clio users (attorneys and staff) — use their ids for responsible attorneys, time entries and task assignees. Clio: GET /users.json.

tools.name: clio_list_matters
tools.title: List matters
tools.description: Search and list matters (the firm's cases) with their client, practice area, responsible attorney and status. `query` wildcard-matches matter number or description and the client's name; custom_field_id + custom_field_value filter by one of the firm's custom fields (e.g. a court case number). Clio: GET /matters.json.

tools.name: clio_get_matter
tools.title: Get one matter
tools.description: Fetch a single matter by id, with its client, practice area, stage, attorneys and custom field values (field_name + value; a picklist value is an option id, see clio_list_custom_fields). Clio: GET /matters/{id}.json.

tools.name: clio_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: Search and list contacts — clients, prospective clients, companies, opposing parties and co-counsel. `query` wildcard-matches name, email, phone, address and more; custom_field_id + custom_field_value filter by one of the firm's custom fields. Clio: GET /contacts.json.

tools.name: clio_get_contact
tools.title: Get one contact
tools.description: Fetch a single contact by id with all email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses, web sites and custom field values (field_name + value; a picklist value is an option id, see clio_list_custom_fields). Clio: GET /contacts/{id}.json.

tools.name: clio_list_activities
tools.title: List activities (time and expenses)
tools.description: List activities — time entries, expense entries and fixed fees — with hours, rate, total and billing status. Filter by matter, user, type, status or date range. `quantity` is in seconds; `quantity_in_hours` is hours. Clio: GET /activities.json.

tools.name: clio_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List tasks with status, priority, due date, matter and assignee. Filter by matter, assignee, status, priority or a due-date range — e.g. what is due this week. Clio: GET /tasks.json.

tools.name: clio_list_calendar_entries
tools.title: List calendar entries
tools.description: List calendar entries (hearings, meetings, deadlines) in a time window, optionally for one matter or calendar. Set expanded=true to get each occurrence of recurring events. Clio: GET /calendar_entries.json.

tools.name: clio_list_bills
tools.title: List bills
tools.description: List bills (invoices) with state, totals, amount due and dates. Filter by client, matter, state, overdue, or issue/due date. Clio: GET /bills.json.

tools.name: clio_get_bill
tools.title: Get one bill
tools.description: Fetch a single bill by id with its state, totals, balance, client and matters. Clio: GET /bills/{id}.json.

tools.name: clio_list_documents
tools.title: List documents
tools.description: List documents (metadata only: name, file name, type, size, category, dates) for a matter, a contact or a folder, or search them by name. Clio: GET /documents.json.

tools.name: clio_list_notes
tools.title: List notes
tools.description: List notes on a matter or a contact, with subject, body, date and author. Clio requires type; narrow to one matter or contact with matter_id or contact_id. Clio: GET /notes.json.

tools.name: clio_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List custom fields
tools.description: List the firm's custom fields for matters or contacts — name, type, whether required, and the options of picklist fields (option id + text). Use the ids to filter clio_list_matters / clio_list_contacts and to read the values that clio_get_matter / clio_get_contact return. Clio: GET /custom_fields.json.

tools.name: clio_list_communications
tools.title: List communications
tools.description: List logged communications — phone calls and emails recorded on matters — with subject, body, date, senders and receivers. Filter by matter, contact, user, type or date range, or search subject and body. Clio: GET /communications.json.

tools.name: clio_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: WRITE: Create a contact — a person (give first_name and/or last_name) or a company (give name) — optionally with an email address and phone number. Clio: POST /contacts.json.

tools.name: clio_create_matter
tools.title: Create a matter
tools.description: WRITE: Open a new matter for an existing client contact. Requires the client's contact id and a description. Clio: POST /matters.json.

tools.name: clio_create_time_entry
tools.title: Record a time entry
tools.description: WRITE: Record billable (or non-billable) time on a matter. Give hours as a decimal (1.5 = 90 minutes); it is sent to Clio as seconds. If price (hourly rate) is omitted Clio applies the firm's rate hierarchy; if user_id is omitted it records for the token's user. Clio: POST /activities.json with type TimeEntry.

tools.name: clio_create_task
tools.title: Create a task
tools.description: WRITE: Create a task and assign it to a firm user or a contact, optionally on a matter with a due date and priority. Clio: POST /tasks.json.

tools.name: clio_update_task
tools.title: Update a task
tools.description: WRITE: Update a task — mark it complete, change its status, due date, priority, name or description, or reassign it. Only the fields given are changed. Clio: PATCH /tasks/{id}.json.

tools.name: clio_create_note
tools.title: Create a note
tools.description: WRITE: Add a note to a matter (type Matter + matter_id) or to a contact (type Contact + contact_id). Clio: POST /notes.json.

tools.name: clio_log_communication
tools.title: Log a phone call or email
tools.description: WRITE: Record a phone call or an email on Clio's communication log, optionally on a matter, with who it was from and to. This only records it: Clio sends nothing. To bill the time, also use clio_create_time_entry. Clio: POST /communications.json.

tools.name: clio_create_calendar_entry
tools.title: Create a calendar entry
tools.description: WRITE: Put an event on a Clio calendar — a hearing, meeting or deadline — optionally linked to a matter. calendar_id is the calendar to put it on (the token user's own is default_calendar_id from clio_who_am_i). Clio: POST /calendar_entries.json.

tools.name: clio_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: clio_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Clio tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: clio_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Clio (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: clio_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Clio Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run clio_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which of my matters are open, and who is the responsible attorney on each?
What tasks are due this week across the firm?
Show unbilled time for the Smith matter and which bills are overdue.
Add a note to the Jones matter: spoke with the client, filing due Friday.
Log my call with Jane Smith on the Smith matter: we discussed the settlement offer.

servers.name: Chatra
servers.description: Read and update Chatra visitors; send, edit and delete chat and pushed messages.

login.hint: Find both keys in Chatra under **Settings → Preferences → API keys**. The keys act for your whole Chatra account and messages you send reach real visitors. They are used only to call the Chatra API on your behalf and are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: chatra_get_visitor
tools.title: Get visitor
tools.description: A chat visitor by id: name and contact details (basicInfo, integrationData and the merged `info`), custom form answers, location, browser, the link to the chat in the Chatra dashboard, the agent group, and the pages viewed in the latest visit. The id is the `clientId` your website passed to the widget or the visitor id from a Chatra webhook; Chatra has no endpoint to list or search visitors. GET /clients/{id}.

tools.name: chatra_update_visitor
tools.title: Update visitor
tools.description: WRITE: edit a visitor's basic info (name, email, phone, notes) exactly as if an agent edited it in the Chatra dashboard. Only the fields you pass change; `null` removes a value. Returns the updated visitor. PUT /clients/{id}.

tools.name: chatra_get_message
tools.title: Get message
tools.description: One chat message by id (a visitor's or an agent's): type (agent or client), text, visitor id, agent id, timestamp (ms) and receivedFrom. Chatra has no endpoint to list a conversation, so the id must come from a send call or a webhook. GET /messages/{id}.

tools.name: chatra_send_message
tools.title: Send message as an agent
tools.description: WRITE: send a chat message to a visitor as a Chatra agent. The visitor sees it immediately in their chat window as if the agent typed it, so only call it with text the user asked you to send. It cannot be unsent except by deleting it. Say which agent writes: agent_id, or agent_email + agent_name + received_from (a dummy agent is created in Chatra when the email is unknown). For automated notices (order status, announcements) use chatra_push_message instead. Returns the new message with its id. POST /messages/.

tools.name: chatra_edit_message
tools.title: Edit agent message
tools.description: WRITE: replace the text of an agent message that was sent earlier. Only agents' messages can be edited, not visitors'. The visitor sees the edited text. Returns the updated message. PUT /messages/{id}.

tools.name: chatra_delete_message
tools.title: Delete agent message
tools.description: WRITE, IRREVERSIBLE: delete an agent message from the conversation. Only agents' messages can be deleted, not visitors'. Returns the deleted message. DELETE /messages/{id}.

tools.name: chatra_get_pushed_message
tools.title: Get pushed message
tools.description: One pushed (automated) message sent earlier by id: text, visitor id, agent id, timestamp (ms), isPushed. GET /pushedMessages/{id}.

tools.name: chatra_push_message
tools.title: Push message to a visitor
tools.description: WRITE: send an automated message (order status, product update, announcement) to a visitor whose account is bound to Chatra through a clientId. It is delivered into the visitor's chat on behalf of a random agent, a given agent (agent_id) or a random agent of a group (group_id). It reaches a real customer and cannot be unsent except by deleting it, so only call it with text the user asked you to send. Returns the new message with its id. POST /pushedMessages/.

tools.name: chatra_edit_pushed_message
tools.title: Edit pushed message
tools.description: WRITE: replace the text of a pushed message sent earlier; the visitor sees the edited text. Returns the updated message. PUT /pushedMessages/{id}.

tools.name: chatra_delete_pushed_message
tools.title: Delete pushed message
tools.description: WRITE, IRREVERSIBLE: delete a pushed message sent earlier. Returns the deleted message. DELETE /pushedMessages/{id}.

tools.name: chatra_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: chatra_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Chatra tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: chatra_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Chatra (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: chatra_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Chatra Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run chatra_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: Corsizio
servers.description: Read Corsizio events, attendees and registrations, including payment status. Read-only.

login.hint: In Corsizio open **Account → Integrations**, enable the **API** integration and copy the **API Secret Access Key** ([how to find it](https://help.corsizio.com/article/37-api-endpoint-authentication)). Grant the key the permissions you want available, such as attendees. Your key is used only to call the Corsizio API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: corsizio_get_account
tools.title: Get account details
tools.description: Get the Corsizio account behind the API key: name, alias, time zone, currency, site URL, contact, and the configured locations, categories, age groups, genders, levels and price ranges (their ids are the filters for corsizio_list_events). Good first call. API: GET /account.

tools.name: corsizio_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List the account's events (classes, workshops, camps) with dates, location, prices and page URLs, newest start first by default. Only published events unless status says otherwise. Filter by status, date range, price range, category/location/age/gender/level id (from corsizio_get_account) or a name word. API: GET /events.

tools.name: corsizio_get_event
tools.title: Get event details
tools.description: Get one event in full: dates, location, ticket prices and early-bird prices, descriptions, max spots, contact and instructors. Use include=stats for registration counts. For the attendee list use corsizio_list_attendees with the event id (or corsizio_get_event_with_attendees). API: GET /events/{id}.

tools.name: corsizio_get_event_with_attendees
tools.title: Get event with its attendees
tools.description: Get one event together with its attendees (and optionally each attendee's payment) in a single call. Returns personal data of registrants (names, emails, phones, notes); only use it when you need the roster, otherwise prefer corsizio_get_event or corsizio_list_attendees with a limit. API: GET /events/{id}?include=attendees[,payment].

tools.name: corsizio_list_attendees
tools.title: List attendees (registrations)
tools.description: List attendee registrations across the account, or for one event (event filter): name, email, phone, status, registration answers and dates. Default status is active. Filter by status (e.g. owing,!canceled), created-date range, event id, coupon code or a search word (name, email, phone). Returns personal data. The API key needs the attendees permission. API: GET /attendees.

tools.name: corsizio_get_attendee
tools.title: Get attendee details
tools.description: Get one attendee registration in full: contact data, registration answers, internal remark, status, and with include=payment the amount, fees, taxes, refunds and transactions (card brand and last 4 digits). Returns personal data. The API key needs the attendees permission. API: GET /attendees/{id}.

servers.name: DialMyCalls
servers.description: Manage DialMyCalls contacts and groups; read broadcasts; send text and voice broadcasts on approval.

login.hint: Log in to DialMyCalls and open [account management](https://www.dialmycalls.com/members/v2/management.php) and find **API Info** to copy your API key. Your key is used only to call the DialMyCalls API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: dialmycalls_get_account
tools.title: Get DialMyCalls account
tools.description: Get the account: credits available (calls and texts spend credits) and the account creation date.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts in the account (name, phone, email, groups), 100 per page.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_contacts_in_group
tools.title: List contacts in a group
tools.description: List the contacts that belong to one contact group (from dialmycalls_list_groups), 100 per page.

tools.name: dialmycalls_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: Get one contact by id.

tools.name: dialmycalls_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: Add a contact (phone number required) to the contact list, optionally into contact groups. Sends nothing to the contact.

tools.name: dialmycalls_update_contact
tools.title: Update a contact
tools.description: Update a contact. DialMyCalls requires the phone number on every update. Fields you omit are left as they are; if you pass group_ids the contact's groups are REPLACED by that list.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_groups
tools.title: List contact groups
tools.description: List contact groups with their contact counts, 100 per page.

tools.name: dialmycalls_get_group
tools.title: Get a contact group
tools.description: Get one contact group (name, contacts_count) by id.

tools.name: dialmycalls_create_group
tools.title: Create a contact group
tools.description: Create an empty contact group. Sends nothing.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_recordings
tools.title: List voice recordings
tools.description: List voice recordings (the messages a call broadcast can play): id, name, type, length, processed. A call needs a processed recording.

tools.name: dialmycalls_get_recording
tools.title: Get a recording
tools.description: Get one voice recording by id (includes its audio file url and whether it is processed and ready).

tools.name: dialmycalls_create_recording_tts
tools.title: Create a text-to-speech recording
tools.description: Create a voice recording from text (text-to-speech) that a call broadcast can then play. Makes no call and sends nothing.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_caller_ids
tools.title: List caller IDs
tools.description: List caller ID phone numbers on the account (id, name, phone, approved). A call broadcast needs an approved caller ID.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_keywords
tools.title: List text keywords
tools.description: List text-message keywords (id, keyword, status). A text broadcast must be tied to one active keyword.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_shortcodes
tools.title: List shortcodes
tools.description: List shortcodes available to send texts from.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_do_not_contacts
tools.title: List do-not-contact numbers
tools.description: List phone numbers on the account's do-not-contact lists (type call or text); these opted out.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_calls
tools.title: List call broadcasts
tools.description: List voice call broadcasts (name, recording, recipients, credit cost, send time), 100 per page.

tools.name: dialmycalls_list_text_recipients

tools.name: dialmycalls_get_incoming_text

servers.name: Namely
servers.description: Read Namely employee profiles, groups, teams, jobs and reports; update profiles, post to the feed.

login.hint: The site name is the first part of your Namely address: **acme** for acme.namely.com. In Namely open the **API** menu (ask your Namely administrator if you do not see it), tab **Personal Access Tokens**, and create a token. The token acts with the permissions of the profile that created it, so use an account that may see the HR data you want to ask about; it is valid for 2 years. It is used only to call the Namely API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: namely_get_me
tools.title: Get my profile
tools.description: Get the profile of the user the connected token belongs to (name, email, job title, manager, access role). Namely API: GET /profiles/me.

tools.name: namely_list_profiles
tools.title: List employee profiles
tools.description: List employee profiles (active, pending and inactive unless filtered) with paging, sorting and filters. Returns {profiles, meta:{count}, linked}. Use format=short for a smaller record (ids, names, email, status, job title); the full record includes every custom field the token may see (compensation, addresses and other sensitive HR data). An empty page means the end. Namely API: GET /profiles (limit 100 requests per minute).

tools.name: namely_get_profile
tools.title: Get employee profile
tools.description: Get one employee's full profile by id: personal and job data, manager, groups, teams and the custom fields the token may see (can include compensation and other sensitive HR data). Namely API: GET /profiles/{id}.

tools.name: namely_list_profile_fields
tools.title: List profile fields
tools.description: List the fields of the employee profile as configured at this company (standard and custom), with their labels, sections and the valid format of each value. Namely API: GET /profiles/fields.

tools.name: namely_list_groups
tools.title: List groups
tools.description: List all groups (departments, office locations and other company groups). Every group belongs to one group type. Namely API: GET /groups.

tools.name: namely_get_group
tools.title: Get group
tools.description: Get one group by id, with the profiles (members) linked to it. Namely API: GET /groups/{id}.

tools.name: namely_list_group_types
tools.title: List group types
tools.description: List the group types (the containers of groups, such as Department or Office). Namely API: GET /group_types.

tools.name: namely_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: List all teams with their team categories. Namely API: GET /teams.

tools.name: namely_get_team
tools.title: Get team
tools.description: Get one team by id, with the profiles (members) linked to it. Namely API: GET /teams/{id}.

tools.name: namely_list_job_titles
tools.title: List job titles
tools.description: List all job titles; each belongs to one job tier. Namely API: GET /job_titles.

tools.name: namely_list_job_tiers
tools.title: List job tiers
tools.description: List all job tiers (the levels that group job titles). Namely API: GET /job_tiers.

tools.name: namely_list_events
tools.title: List feed events
tools.description: List events of the company home feed (announcements, birthdays, work anniversaries, new arrivals), newest first by default, with limit and after (an event id) for paging. Namely API: GET /events.

tools.name: namely_list_event_comments
tools.title: List event comments
tools.description: List the comments on a feed event. Namely API: GET /events/{event-id}/comments.

tools.name: namely_get_report
tools.title: Get report
tools.description: Run a saved Namely report by id and return its columns and rows (live data; each row is a list in column order). Find the id in the URL of the report in Namely. Reports can contain sensitive HR data such as salary history. Namely API: GET /reports/{id}.

tools.name: namely_update_profile
tools.title: Update employee profile
tools.description: Change standard fields of an employee profile (name, emails, start date, status, manager, job title). WRITES live HR data. Send only the fields to change. Setting user_status to pending needs a personal_email. Namely API: PUT /profiles/{id}.

tools.name: namely_create_announcement
tools.title: Post announcement
tools.description: Post an announcement to the company home feed, visible to every employee. Markdown; to mention a person write [Full Name](/people/<profile_id>). With is_appreciation, mentioned people are appreciated. email_all=true ALSO EMAILS every active employee at their company address (needs the permission) and cannot be undone: set it only when the user explicitly asks. Namely API: POST /events.

tools.name: namely_create_event_comment
tools.title: Comment on event
tools.description: Add a comment to a feed event, posted as the token's user and visible to employees who see the event. Markdown; mention a person with [Full Name](/people/<profile_id>). Namely API: POST /events/{id}/comments.

tools.name: namely_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Namely (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: namely_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription

List everyone in the Sales department with their start dates.
Which employees have a work anniversary or birthday coming up?
Post an announcement welcoming our new hire to the company feed.

servers.name: Papershift
servers.description: Read Papershift absences, vacation, time tracking and shifts; request and review absences.

login.hint: Create it in Papershift → gear icon → **Account settings → API** (Account Admin only; the paid Papershift API add-on must be active). New keys can read and write; edit the key's permissions to make it read-only if you only want to look things up. Your key is used only to call the Papershift API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: papershift_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The Papershift account this API key belongs to (id and name). A quick way to check the connection. GET /accounts.

tools.name: papershift_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List all locations (sites/companies inside the account) with id, name and status. Most other tools need a location id from here. GET /locations.

tools.name: papershift_get_location
tools.title: Get location
tools.description: One location by id. GET /locations?id=.

tools.name: papershift_list_working_areas
tools.title: List working areas
tools.description: List working areas (departments/stations shifts are planned in), optionally for one location. Use the ids for shifts and time trackings. GET /working_areas.

tools.name: papershift_list_users
tools.title: List employees
tools.description: List employees (users) with name, email, status, contract basics and their location, working-area and tag ids. Filter by location, working area or tag. 25 per page. GET /users.

tools.name: papershift_get_user
tools.title: Get employee
tools.description: One employee by id: contact data, status, locations, working areas, tags and profile fields. GET /users?id=.

tools.name: papershift_list_tags
tools.title: List tags
tools.description: List the tags of a location (labels on shifts, time trackings and employees). GET /filters.

tools.name: papershift_list_absence_types
tools.title: List absence types
tools.description: List the absence types of a location (vacation, sick leave, ...) with id, title and rules. Use the ids to create absences. GET /absence_types.

tools.name: papershift_list_absences
tools.title: List absences
tools.description: List absences (vacation, sick leave, ...) that fall between two dates, optionally for one employee or location. Shows type title, times, hours, vacation days and whether it is confirmed. 25 per page. GET /absences.

tools.name: papershift_get_absence
tools.title: Get absence
tools.description: One absence by id, with its status, confirmation, hours and vacation days. GET /absences?id=.

tools.name: papershift_list_vacation_entitlements
tools.title: List vacation entitlements
tools.description: An employee's vacation entitlements (planned days, spent days, expiry, carry-over) for the given period. Use it to answer 'how many vacation days does X have left'. 25 per page. GET /vacation_entitlements.

tools.name: papershift_list_time_trackings
tools.title: List time trackings
tools.description: List worked-time entries (clock-ins) from a start date, optionally to an end date and for one employee. Shows start, end, break time, location, employee and whether confirmed. 25 per page. GET /working_sessions.

tools.name: papershift_get_time_tracking
tools.title: Get time tracking
tools.description: One worked-time entry by id, with its breaks, tags and break total. GET /working_sessions?id=.

tools.name: papershift_list_evaluations
tools.title: List evaluations (daily hours)
tools.description: An employee's daily evaluations: target, planned and actual hours, vacation and compensation per day. Use it for overtime and balance questions. 25 per page. GET /evaluations.

tools.name: papershift_list_target_hours
tools.title: List target hours
tools.description: An employee's contractual target hours (weekly/monthly rhythm and hours per weekday) over time. 25 per page. GET /target_hours.

tools.name: papershift_list_payrolls
tools.title: List payrolls
tools.description: An employee's payroll entries (paid hours, salary, bonus, time-account start/end per period). Sensitive pay data. 25 per page. GET /payrolls.

tools.name: papershift_list_shifts
tools.title: List shifts
tools.description: List planned shifts of a location between two dates, optionally for one working area or tags. Shows start, end, number of employees needed, note and visibility. Assigned employees: papershift_list_shift_assignments. 25 per page. GET /shifts.

tools.name: papershift_get_shift
tools.title: Get shift
tools.description: One shift by id. GET /shifts?id=.

tools.name: papershift_list_shift_assignments
tools.title: List shift assignments
tools.description: Who is assigned to a shift and who has applied for it (user id and name). GET /assignments?shift_id=.

tools.name: papershift_list_availabilities
tools.title: List availabilities
tools.description: The times an employee has marked as available between two dates. 25 per page. GET /availabilities.

tools.name: papershift_create_absence
tools.title: Create absence
tools.description: WRITE: record an absence (vacation, sick leave, ...) for an employee. Get the absence type id from papershift_list_absence_types and the user id from papershift_list_users. Whether it counts immediately or waits for approval depends on the absence type and the account's approval rules; the employee may be notified. Papershift calculates the paid hours and vacation days. POST /absences.

tools.name: papershift_review_absence
tools.title: Confirm, reject or reset an absence
tools.description: WRITE: decide on an absence request. action 'confirm' approves it (it then counts against vacation days and the plan), 'reject' declines it, 'reset' puts a decided absence back to pending. The employee is typically notified of the decision. Find ids with papershift_list_absences. PUT /absences/{confirm|reject|reset}.

tools.name: papershift_create_time_tracking
tools.title: Create time tracking
tools.description: WRITE: add a worked-time entry for an employee after the fact (start, end and break minutes) in a location and working area. It changes the employee's recorded hours and balance. Ids from papershift_list_locations, papershift_list_working_areas and papershift_list_users. POST /working_sessions.

tools.name: papershift_confirm_time_tracking
tools.title: Confirm time tracking
tools.description: WRITE: confirm (approve) a worked-time entry so it counts as final for payroll and balances. Find ids with papershift_list_time_trackings. PUT /working_sessions/confirm.

tools.name: papershift_create_shift
tools.title: Create shift
tools.description: WRITE: plan a new shift in a location and working area for a number of employees. Set visible to true only if employees should see it right away (default: left to the account's setting). Assign people afterwards with papershift_assign_user_to_shift. POST /shifts.

tools.name: papershift_assign_user_to_shift
tools.title: Assign employee to shift
tools.description: WRITE: put an employee on a shift (or, with application true, record them as having applied for it). The employee is typically notified of the assignment. An already assigned user is re-assigned. Returns the shift's assigned and applied users. POST /assignments.

servers.name: Robly
servers.description: Find Robly contacts and lists; subscribe, update and move contacts between lists.

login.hint: Both are shown in Robly under **My Account**. If there is no key yet, or you need a new one, email support@robly.com from your login address. Use the API ID and key, never your Robly password. They are used only to call the Robly API on your behalf and are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: robly_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts (members) of the Robly account, newest first as Robly orders them: id, email, subscribed/deleted flags, subscription date, sign-up source, timestamps. Filter by status, by list, or by last-updated time; optionally include each contact's lists and data fields. Pages with limit (max 100) and offset: pass next_offset from the previous reply. Robly does not return a total. GET /api/v1/contacts/show.

tools.name: robly_find_contact
tools.title: Find contact
tools.description: Look up one contact by email address or member id: status, subscription date, sign-up source and, on request, the lists and data fields. Returns found: false when Robly has no such contact. GET /api/v1/contacts/search.

tools.name: robly_check_list_membership
tools.title: Check list membership
tools.description: Whether one contact (by email or member id) is on one list. GET /api/v1/contacts/exists_in_sub_list.

tools.name: robly_list_sub_lists
tools.title: List sub lists
tools.description: List the account's sub lists (the lists contacts belong to): id, name, position, timestamps. Public lists only unless include_all is true. Use the ids for list filters and for adding contacts. GET /api/v1/sub_lists/show.

tools.name: robly_list_fields
tools.title: List data fields
tools.description: List the contact data fields (First Name, Last Name, custom fields): id, label, type, required flag and the user_tag that robly_subscribe_contact and robly_update_contact use as the field key. GET /api/v1/fields/show.

tools.name: robly_get_signup_form
tools.title: Get sign-up form
tools.description: The data fields and sub lists a new subscriber can be given through the sign-up API (public ones unless include_all is true). GET /api/v1/sign_up/show.

tools.name: robly_subscribe_contact
tools.title: Subscribe contact
tools.description: WRITE: add a new subscribed contact (or re-submit an existing one through the sign-up form). With double_opt_in Robly EMAILS the contact a confirmation link first; with welcome_email it EMAILS the welcome message right away; with include_autoresponder it triggers matching autoresponders, which email the contact. Only subscribe people who agreed to receive email. Field values go in `fields`, keyed by the user_tag from robly_list_fields (for example fname, lname). POST /api/v1/sign_up/generate.

tools.name: robly_add_contact_to_list
tools.title: Add contact to list
tools.description: WRITE: put an existing contact on a list. With include_autoresponder Robly triggers autoresponders matching the newly listed contact, which EMAIL the contact. POST /api/v1/contacts/add_sub_list.

tools.name: robly_remove_contact_from_list
tools.title: Remove contact from list
tools.description: WRITE: take a contact off one list (the contact itself is kept). POST /api/v1/contacts/remove_sub_list.

tools.name: robly_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing contact's data fields and/or list memberships in one call. Name the contact by member_id (look it up with robly_find_contact). `fields` are keyed by user_tag (robly_list_fields); the email address cannot be changed here. add_to_list_ids puts the contact on those lists, remove_from_list_ids takes it off them. remove_from_all_other_lists also removes the contact from every list NOT named in add_to_list_ids (requires add_to_list_ids). include_autoresponder triggers autoresponders that EMAIL the contact. POST /api/v1/contacts/update_full_contact.

tools.name: robly_unsubscribe_contact
tools.title: Unsubscribe contact
tools.description: WRITE: unsubscribe a contact so Robly stops emailing it. Robly's API cannot undo this: an unsubscribed contact can only come back through a sign-up form. Use it for a contact that asked to stop. POST /api/v1/contacts/unsubscribe.

tools.name: robly_rename_sub_list

servers.name: Seal Subscriptions
servers.description: Manage Seal Subscriptions on Shopify: subscriptions, billing attempts, items, discounts, rules.

login.hint: Find it in your Shopify admin → **Apps → Seal Subscriptions → Settings → General Settings → API**. Use the **API token**, not the API secret. The token belongs to one shop and can manage its subscriptions; your token is used only to call the Seal Subscriptions API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_list_subscriptions
tools.title: List subscriptions
tools.description: List or search the shop's subscriptions (50 per page): status, customer, interval, total value, shipping address and card brand/last digits. Search by customer email, first or last name; filter by status; optionally include the items and the billing attempts of each. GET /subscriptions.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_list_subscriptions_by_billing_date
tools.title: List subscriptions by billing date
tools.description: Subscriptions that have at least one billing attempt scheduled between two UTC date-times: the way to see what will be charged tomorrow or this week. Each subscription carries a cursor; pass the last one's cursor as `cursor` to get the next page. GET /subscriptions-by-billing-date.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_get_subscription
tools.title: Get subscription
tools.description: One subscription with everything Seal knows: customer, shipping and billing address, status, intervals, delivery method, items with discounts, billing attempts (with status and error messages), fulfillment orders, invoices, tags and the activity log. Private customer links are removed. GET /subscription?id=.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_list_subscription_rules
tools.title: List subscription rules
tools.description: List the subscription rules (plans) of the shop: name, payment type, the products and variants they apply to and their selling plans. GET /subscription-rules.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_get_subscription_rule
tools.title: Get subscription rule
tools.description: One subscription rule by id, with its products, variants and selling plans. GET /subscription-rule?id=.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_list_webhooks
tools.title: List webhooks
tools.description: List the webhooks registered for this shop through the API (topic and address). GET /webhooks.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_pause_subscription
tools.title: Pause subscription
tools.description: WRITE: Pause an active subscription: no further charges or shipments until it is resumed. Undo with sealsubscriptions_resume_subscription. PUT /subscription action=pause.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_resume_subscription
tools.title: Resume subscription
tools.description: WRITE: Resume a paused subscription so charges and shipments continue on the schedule. PUT /subscription action=resume.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_reactivate_subscription
tools.title: Reactivate subscription
tools.description: WRITE: Reactivate a cancelled subscription (the effect is the same as resume; use this for cancelled ones). Charges restart on the schedule, so the customer may be billed. PUT /subscription action=reactivate.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_cancel_customer_subscription
tools.title: Cancel subscription
tools.description: WRITE: Cancel a subscription now: all future charges and shipments stop and the customer may get Seal's cancellation email. It can be brought back with sealsubscriptions_reactivate_subscription. For a later cancellation use sealsubscriptions_schedule_cancellation. PUT /subscription action=cancel.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_schedule_cancellation
tools.title: Schedule subscription cancellation
tools.description: WRITE: Schedule the cancellation of a subscription for a future date and time (it stays active until then). PUT /subscription-schedule-cancellation.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_add_items
tools.title: Add items to subscription
tools.description: WRITE: Add products to a subscription. Prices are in the subscription's currency and change what the customer pays on the next charge. An item with one_time=true is removed after the next renewal. PUT /subscription action=add_items.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_edit_items
tools.title: Edit subscription items
tools.description: WRITE: Change existing items of a subscription: variant, quantity (> 0), price (>= 0), SKU, one-time flag, properties. Changes what the customer pays on the next charge. PUT /subscription action=edit_items.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_remove_items
tools.title: Remove items from subscription
tools.description: WRITE: Remove items from a subscription by item id. The customer stops receiving and paying for them. PUT /subscription action=remove_items.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_edit_subscription
tools.title: Edit subscription
tools.description: WRITE: Edit a subscription's schedule and details: delivery and billing interval (a billing interval longer than the delivery interval makes it prepaid), min/max number of payments, note attributes (an empty list removes them), delivery method and price, and the shipping address. Only the fields you pass change. To change items use the item tools. PUT /subscription action=edit.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_reschedule_billing_attempt
tools.title: Reschedule billing attempt
tools.description: WRITE: Move a billing attempt that has not been processed yet to another date and time. With reset_schedule=true the later attempts are rebuilt from the new date. PUT /subscription-billing-attempt action=reschedule.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_skip_billing_attempt
tools.title: Skip billing attempt
tools.description: WRITE: Skip one upcoming billing attempt so the customer is not charged for that cycle. Undo with sealsubscriptions_unskip_billing_attempt. PUT /subscription-billing-attempt action=skip.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_unskip_billing_attempt
tools.title: Unskip billing attempt
tools.description: WRITE: Bring back a skipped billing attempt, so it is charged on its date again. PUT /subscription-billing-attempt action=unskip.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_delete_billing_attempt
tools.title: Delete billing attempt
tools.description: WRITE: Delete a billing attempt that has not been processed. Seal keeps 65 days of attempts scheduled, so a deleted one is recreated within hours unless the schedule is moved first (see sealsubscriptions_reschedule_billing_attempt). DELETE /subscription-billing-attempt.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_reschedule_fulfillment_order
tools.title: Reschedule fulfillment order
tools.description: WRITE: Move a fulfillment order of a prepaid subscription to another date and time. PUT /subscription-fulfillment-order action=reschedule.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_create_charge_now
tools.title: Charge subscription now
tools.description: WRITE: CHARGES THE CUSTOMER'S PAYMENT METHOD IMMEDIATELY for the next billing attempt of the subscription and creates a Shopify order; it does not wait for the scheduled date. Only call it when the user clearly asked for an immediate charge. With reset_schedule=true the later attempts are rebuilt from today. PUT /subscription-create-charge-now.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_process_charge
tools.title: Process a specific charge
tools.description: WRITE: CHARGES THE CUSTOMER'S PAYMENT METHOD NOW for one specific billing attempt (for example a failed or upcoming one) and creates a Shopify order. Only call it when the user clearly asked for that charge. PUT /subscription-process-charge.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_apply_discount_code
tools.title: Apply discount code
tools.description: WRITE: Apply a Shopify discount code to an auto-charging subscription (not to recurring-invoice subscriptions); it lowers what the customer pays on the next charges. PUT /subscription-discount-code action=apply.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_remove_discount_code
tools.title: Remove discount code
tools.description: WRITE: Remove a discount code from a subscription. Use the discount code id from the subscription's items[].discount_codes[].id (a uuid), not the code text. DELETE /subscription-discount-code.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_send_payment_method_update_email
tools.title: Email customer to update payment method
tools.description: WRITE: SENDS AN EMAIL TO THE CUSTOMER of the subscription with a link to update their payment method (for example after failed charges). Only call it when the user clearly asked to contact the customer. PUT /subscription action=send_payment_method_update_email.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_edit_subscription_rule
tools.title: Edit subscription rule
tools.description: WRITE: Edit a subscription rule: its name, the plan selector label (`options`, e.g. "Deliver every") and the products it applies to. product_variants REPLACES all products and variants linked to the rule: to add some without removing the others use sealsubscriptions_append_rule_product_variants. PUT /subscription-rule.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_append_rule_product_variants
tools.title: Add products to subscription rule
tools.description: WRITE: Add products or variants to a subscription rule without touching the ones already linked. PUT /subscription-rule/append-product-variants.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Seal Subscriptions tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Seal Subscriptions (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sealsubscriptions_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Seal Subscriptions Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run sealsubscriptions_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which subscriptions are scheduled to be charged tomorrow?
Show the subscriptions of john@example.com and their next billing dates.
Skip the next billing attempt of subscription 568185.
Which of my subscriptions have failed charges this week?

servers.name: SuiteDash
servers.description: Read and update SuiteDash contacts, companies and projects; create leads and clients.

login.hint: An account admin finds both in SuiteDash → **Integrations → Secure API** (create a Secret Key there if you have none). The pair acts with full API access to your account and counts against its monthly API-call quota. Your credentials are used only to call the SuiteDash API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: suitedash_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List CRM contacts (leads, prospects, clients) 10 per page: name, emails, phones, role, tags, companies, address and custom fields. Filter by creation time and sort by name or creation date. GET /contacts.

tools.name: suitedash_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One CRM contact by UID or primary email, with companies, tags, address and custom fields. GET /contact/{identifier}.

tools.name: suitedash_get_contact_fields
tools.title: Get contact field schema
tools.description: The contact field schema of this account: every default and custom field with its type, whether it is required, and which actions (read/create/update) allow it. Custom fields appear under their UID: use these UIDs in custom_fields. GET /contact/meta.

tools.name: suitedash_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: create a CRM contact in SuiteDash. role and names are required; email is required except for a Lead. Optionally link the contact to a company by name (set create_company_if_not_exists to create it). If send_welcome_email is true SuiteDash EMAILS the contact a portal access invitation: leave it false unless the user asked for that. POST /contact.

tools.name: suitedash_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: update fields of an existing CRM contact (found by UID or email); only the fields you pass change, and null clears a field. Tags and custom fields passed here replace the current values. If send_welcome_email is true SuiteDash EMAILS the contact a portal invitation (only if none was sent before): leave it unset unless the user asked. PUT /contact/{identifier}.

tools.name: suitedash_list_companies
tools.title: List companies
tools.description: List CRM companies 10 per page (idle companies are not available): name, role, category, phones, website, address, tags, primary contact and custom fields. Filter by creation time and sort by name or creation date. GET /companies.

tools.name: suitedash_get_company
tools.title: Get company
tools.description: One CRM company by UID or exact name, with primary contact, category, tags, address and custom fields. GET /company/{identifier}.

tools.name: suitedash_get_company_fields
tools.title: Get company field schema
tools.description: The company field schema of this account: every default and custom field (public, private and target custom fields under their UIDs) with type, required flag and the actions allowed. GET /company/meta.

tools.name: suitedash_create_company
tools.title: Create company
tools.description: WRITE: create a CRM company (name and role are required) with an optional primary contact. With create_primary_contact_if_not_exists the primary contact is created from the given names/email when no contact has that email. If send_welcome_email is true SuiteDash EMAILS the primary contact a portal invitation: leave it false unless the user asked. POST /company.

tools.name: suitedash_update_company
tools.title: Update company
tools.description: WRITE: update fields of an existing CRM company (found by UID or name); only the fields you pass change, and null clears a field. Tags and custom fields passed here replace the current values. PUT /company/{identifier}.

tools.name: suitedash_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List projects 10 per page: name, status, start/end dates, due time. Filter by creation time and sort by name, creation, start or end date. Use suitedash_get_project for the client, team and economics. GET /projects.

tools.name: suitedash_get_project
tools.title: Get project
tools.description: One project with its description, client and secondary clients, teammates, team, leader, economics (estimated value, currency, sector) and custom fields. Find it by UID (default), exact name, a name fragment, or the most recent one. GET /project/{type}/{identifier}.

tools.name: suitedash_get_project_fields
tools.title: Get project field schema
tools.description: The project field schema of this account: default and custom fields (under their UIDs) with type, required flag and allowed actions. GET /project/meta.

tools.name: suitedash_update_project
tools.title: Update project
tools.description: WRITE: update fields of an existing project (found by UID, name, name fragment or most recent); only the fields you pass change. The status must be one of the account's project statuses (see suitedash_get_project_fields). The description and client text accept HTML. PUT /project/{type}/{identifier}.

tools.name: suitedash_subscribe_to_marketing
tools.title: Subscribe contacts to marketing audiences
tools.description: WRITE: subscribe people (by email) to one or more marketing audiences (numeric audience ids from SuiteDash > Marketing). Unknown emails may be created as marketing contacts. This enrolls real people in email marketing and can start campaigns or automations tied to those audiences: only do it for people who have consented, and only when the user asked. The reply holds the outcome per person. POST /marketing/subscribe.

tools.name: suitedash_list_worlds
tools.title: List worlds
tools.description: List the account's Worlds (client groupings), 10 per page. Only available with the WORLDS Power-Up; otherwise SuiteDash answers 403. GET /worlds.

tools.name: suitedash_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: suitedash_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the SuiteDash tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: suitedash_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on SuiteDash (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: suitedash_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's SuiteDash Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run suitedash_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: List the contacts created in the last 7 days and tell me which ones are still leads.
Show everything SuiteDash has on the company Acme Corp, including custom fields.
Create a Lead for Jane Doe (jane@example.com) and tag her 'webinar'.
Which projects end this month, and what status are they in?

servers.name: UpKeep
servers.description: Read UpKeep work orders, assets, parts and meters; create requests and work orders.

login.hint: An UpKeep admin creates it under **Settings > API Tokens > Create token** (it starts with `uk_pat_` and is shown only once). The token acts with the role you choose for it, so pick the narrowest role that fits; changes it makes are attributed to the token's name. The UpKeep API is available on the Enterprise plan. Your token is used only to call the UpKeep API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: upkeep_get_account
tools.title: Check API token
tools.description: Confirm the UpKeep API token is active: returns the company id, the token's name, when it was created and when it was last used. GET /api/v1/organization-api-tokens/introspect.

tools.name: upkeep_list_work_orders
tools.title: List work orders
tools.description: List work orders (reactive and preventive), newest first, with status, priority, due date, asset, location, assignee, parts, time and cost. Filter by status, completion, priority, category, asset, location, assignee, title or date ranges. GET /work-orders.

tools.name: upkeep_get_work_order
tools.title: Get work order
tools.description: One work order by id with its checklist items, custom fields, time log, parts and files. GET /work-orders/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_list_assets
tools.title: List assets
tools.description: List assets (equipment) with name, model, serial and barcode, location, status, downtime status, warranty and number of open work orders. Filter by name, serial number, barcode, location, status, category or assignee. GET /assets.

tools.name: upkeep_get_asset
tools.title: Get asset
tools.description: One asset by id with purchase and warranty details, custom fields and (optionally) assigned users, teams, vendors, parts, files and sub-assets. GET /assets/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List locations (sites, buildings, rooms) with address, barcode, parent location and hierarchy level. GET /locations.

tools.name: upkeep_get_location
tools.title: Get location
tools.description: One location by id. GET /locations/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_list_parts
tools.title: List parts (inventory)
tools.description: List spare parts with quantity on hand, minimum quantity, cost, category, location and part number. Compare quantity with minimumQuantity to find parts to reorder. GET /parts.

tools.name: upkeep_get_part
tools.title: Get part
tools.description: One part by id with quantity, cost, location and custom fields. GET /parts/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_list_meters
tools.title: List meters
tools.description: List meters (usage counters such as hours, mileage, temperature) with units, reading frequency and the asset or location they belong to. GET /meters.

tools.name: upkeep_get_meter
tools.title: Get meter
tools.description: One meter by id. GET /meters/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_list_meter_readings
tools.title: List meter readings
tools.description: Readings recorded for one meter (value, date, who recorded it), newest first. GET /meters/{id}/readings.

tools.name: upkeep_add_meter_reading
tools.title: Add meter reading
tools.description: WRITE: record a new reading on a meter (for example engine hours or mileage). A reading cannot be removed with this server, and a meter notification can create a work order automatically when its condition is met. POST /meters/{id}/readings.

tools.name: upkeep_list_requests
tools.title: List work requests
tools.description: List work requests submitted by staff or through the request portal (before they become work orders), with status open/approved/rejected. GET /requests.

tools.name: upkeep_get_request
tools.title: Get work request
tools.description: One work request by id with its form fields and, once approved, the linked work order id. GET /requests/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_create_request
tools.title: Create work request
tools.description: WRITE: submit a new work request for the maintenance team to approve (it appears in UpKeep's Requests list and may notify the approvers or the assignee). It is not a work order until approved. If the account has a request form configured, pass its field labels in `fields`. POST /requests.

tools.name: upkeep_approve_request
tools.title: Approve work request
tools.description: WRITE: approve a pending work request, which converts it into a work order (it may notify the assignee). Needs a token whose role may approve requests. Approving a request that is already approved or declined fails with HTTP 409. POST /requests/{id}/approve.

tools.name: upkeep_create_work_order
tools.title: Create work order
tools.description: WRITE: create a new work order (it may notify the assignee and appears in UpKeep's work order board). Ids for asset, location and assignee come from the list tools. POST /work-orders.

tools.name: upkeep_update_work_order
tools.title: Update work order
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing work order: status (open, onHold, inProgress, complete), title, description, priority, due date or assignee. Only the fields you pass change; completing a work order may trigger the account's integrations (for example Zapier). Archiving and deleting are not offered. PATCH /work-orders/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_add_work_order_message
tools.title: Add work order message
tools.description: WRITE: post a message (comment) on a work order's activity thread; people following the work order may be notified. POST /work-orders/{id}/update-messages.

tools.name: upkeep_update_part_quantity
tools.title: Update part quantity
tools.description: WRITE: set the quantity on hand (and optionally the minimum quantity that triggers a low-stock notification) of a part. This overwrites the stored number: read the part first and pass the new total, not the difference. PATCH /parts/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List UpKeep users (technicians, admins, requesters) with account type, job title, status and last login. Use the ids to assign work orders. GET /users.

tools.name: upkeep_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: One user by id. GET /users/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: List teams with name and description. Use the ids to assign work. GET /teams.

tools.name: upkeep_list_vendors
tools.title: List vendors
tools.description: List vendors (suppliers and contractors) with contact details. GET /vendors.

tools.name: upkeep_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List customers (the parties whose assets or locations you maintain) with contact details. GET /customers.

tools.name: upkeep_list_purchase_orders
tools.title: List purchase orders
tools.description: List purchase orders with status (awaiting, approved, declined, fulfilled), vendor, dates, total cost and quantities. GET /purchase-orders.

tools.name: upkeep_get_purchase_order
tools.title: Get purchase order
tools.description: One purchase order by id with its parts, quantities, costs and shipping details. GET /purchase-orders/{id}.

tools.name: upkeep_list_preventive_maintenance
tools.title: List preventive maintenance plans
tools.description: List preventive maintenance (PM) templates, the recurring work that generates scheduled work orders, with their schedules. Filter by text, asset, location, assignee, team or priority. Pages are 1-based. GET /pm.

tools.name: upkeep_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: upkeep_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the UpKeep tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: upkeep_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on UpKeep (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: upkeep_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's UpKeep Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run upkeep_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which work orders are overdue and who are they assigned to?
List the open high-priority work orders for the Boiler Room location.
Which spare parts are below their minimum quantity?
Create a work order to inspect the forklift, due Friday, assigned to Sam.

servers.name: AgendaPro
servers.description: Read AgendaPro bookings, slots, clients, services and sales; create, update and cancel bookings.

login.hint: API access needs the **Pro plan**. Create the key in AgendaPro → **Configuraciones → Integraciones** (it is shown only once, and a company can have 2 active keys, so a dedicated key for this connection is easy to revoke). A key limited to some scopes limits the tools in the same way, and it needs at least one of the scopes locations:read, providers:read or services:read (they identify your company). Your key is used only to call the AgendaPro API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: agendapro_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List the business's locations (sucursales / locales): id, name, address, phone, email, timezone, opening hours and country. Location ids are needed for bookings, slots and sales filters. GET /v3/locations.

tools.name: agendapro_get_location
tools.title: Get location
tools.description: One location by id, with address, coordinates, timezone and weekly opening hours. GET /v3/locations/{id}.

tools.name: agendapro_list_services
tools.title: List services
tools.description: List the services (treatments, classes, sessions) the business offers: id, name, price, duration, type, category, whether online booking/payment is on, and the location. Service ids are needed to book. GET /v3/services.

tools.name: agendapro_get_service
tools.title: Get service
tools.description: One service by id, including its category, images and the providers who perform it. GET /v3/services/{id}.

tools.name: agendapro_list_service_categories
tools.title: List service categories
tools.description: List service categories, ordered as the business arranges them. GET /v3/categories.

tools.name: agendapro_list_providers
tools.title: List providers
tools.description: List service providers (the staff who take bookings): id, public name, location, active flag, online-booking flag and working hours. Provider ids are needed to book. GET /v3/providers.

tools.name: agendapro_get_provider
tools.title: Get provider
tools.description: One service provider by id, with biography, images and working hours including breaks. GET /v3/providers/{id}.

tools.name: agendapro_list_bookings
tools.title: List bookings
tools.description: List bookings (reservas / appointments) with time, status, service, provider, client id, location, price and the linked sale. AgendaPro requires at least ONE of client_id, location_id, service_id or service_provider_id; dates only narrow the result. A sale may be a membership covering several bookings, so do not total amounts by sale id. GET /v3/bookings.

tools.name: agendapro_get_booking
tools.title: Get booking
tools.description: One booking by id with status, service, provider, client id, location, prices, notes and the linked sale. GET /v3/bookings/{id}.

tools.name: agendapro_list_available_slots
tools.title: List available slots
tools.description: Free booking time windows at a location on one date (optionally for one service and/or provider): start/end time, provider, plus a metadata summary (service duration, slot count). Use before creating a booking. GET /v3/available_slots.

tools.name: agendapro_create_booking
tools.title: Create booking
tools.description: WRITE: create a booking for an existing client, service, provider and location. Check agendapro_list_available_slots first. status_id must be a non-cancelled status: copy the status.id of an existing booking (agendapro_list_bookings). AgendaPro does NOT send email/SMS/WhatsApp notifications for bookings created through the API. Not idempotent: calling twice books twice. POST /v3/bookings.

tools.name: agendapro_update_booking
tools.title: Update booking
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing booking (partial update: only the fields you pass change): move it, switch service/provider/location, change status, price or notes. The merchant's customer policy applies: a change too close to the start time, or past the maximum number of changes, is refused with HTTP 422 and must not be retried. PATCH /v3/bookings/{id}.

tools.name: agendapro_cancel_booking
tools.title: Cancel booking
tools.description: WRITE: cancel a booking. This cannot be undone through the API. The merchant's customer policy applies: a cancellation that is disabled, too close to the start time or past the maximum number of changes is refused with HTTP 422 (tell the user the merchant does not allow it; do not retry). Confirm with the user before calling. PATCH /v3/bookings/{id}/cancel.

tools.name: agendapro_list_clients
tools.title: List clients
tools.description: List the business's clients (customers) page by page: name, email, phone, identification number, address, birth date, record number, active flag. Personal data: only use it for the task at hand. To find one person use agendapro_search_clients. GET /v3/clients.

tools.name: agendapro_search_clients
tools.title: Search clients
tools.description: Find clients by free text (name, email, phone, identification number or record number): a short ranked list with id, full name, email, phone. The fastest way to get a client_id. GET /v3/clients/quick-search.

tools.name: agendapro_get_client
tools.title: Get client
tools.description: One client by id with contact details, address, birth date, record number and active flag. GET /v3/clients/{id}.

tools.name: agendapro_list_client_custom_attributes
tools.title: List a client's custom attributes
tools.description: The custom attribute values stored for one client (id, name, datatype, value). GET /v3/clients/{id}/custom_attributes.

tools.name: agendapro_list_custom_attributes
tools.title: List custom attribute templates
tools.description: The custom client fields the business defined (id, name, datatype, mandatory, group, choices). Use the template ids when setting custom_attributes on a client. GET /v3/custom_attributes.

tools.name: agendapro_create_client
tools.title: Create client
tools.description: WRITE: create a new client. first_name is required and at least one of last_name, email or phone must also be given (AgendaPro's rule). Search first (agendapro_search_clients) to avoid duplicates; not idempotent. No message is sent to the client. POST /v3/clients.

tools.name: agendapro_update_client
tools.title: Update client
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing client (partial update: only the fields you pass change; it overwrites the stored value). PATCH /v3/clients/{id}.

tools.name: agendapro_list_sales
tools.title: List sales
tools.description: List sales (ventas): status (partially_paid, paid, canceled, refunded), paid and pending amounts, paid-at time, location, client id and the payment transactions. Filter by paid date range, location or client. GET /v3/sales.

tools.name: agendapro_get_sale
tools.title: Get sale
tools.description: One sale by id with amounts, status, location and its payment transactions (amount, paid-at, payment method). GET /v3/sales/{id}.

tools.name: agendapro_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List retail products in the catalog: name, SKU, price, active flag, category, brand and display. GET /v3/products.

tools.name: agendapro_get_product
tools.title: Get product
tools.description: One catalog product by id with description, SKU, price, category, brand and display. GET /v3/products/{id}.

tools.name: agendapro_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: agendapro_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the AgendaPro tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: agendapro_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on AgendaPro (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: agendapro_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's AgendaPro Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run agendapro_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.
