servers.name: CiviCRM
servers.description: Work with your own CiviCRM: contacts, contributions, memberships, events; log activities.

login.hint: **Site address:** the https address you log in at, for example `https://crm.example.org` (a WordPress, Drupal or Joomla site with CiviCRM inside works too; give the site's own address, or your `/wp-admin/` or `/administrator/` address if CiviCRM has no clean URLs there). **API key:** a key attached to one CiviCRM contact (**Contacts → edit the contact → API Key** with the API Key extension, or via the APIv4 Explorer). Use a dedicated contact whose role has only the permissions you want the AI to have, plus authenticate with api key. An administrator must also allow API keys under **Administer → System Settings → Authentication** (CiviCRM 5.47 or newer; AuthX in 5.36–5.46). The key is used only to call your CiviCRM on your behalf and to derive a private account id; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: civicrm_whoami
tools.title: Get current contact
tools.description: The CiviCRM contact this API key belongs to (contact id, display name, contact type) and how it authenticated. Everything the other tools do is limited to that contact's permissions. GET /civicrm/authx/id, then APIv4 Contact.get.

tools.name: civicrm_search_contacts
tools.title: Search contacts
tools.description: Find contacts (people, organizations, households) by a word in their name, e-mail address or phone number, optionally of one contact type. Trashed contacts are left out. Returns id, display name, type, primary e-mail and phone. APIv4 Contact.get.

tools.name: civicrm_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact by id: name, type, job title, source, communication preferences (do not e-mail, opted out, ...), dates, plus all their e-mail addresses, phone numbers and postal addresses. APIv4 Contact.get, Email.get, Phone.get, Address.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_contact_notes
tools.title: List contact notes
tools.description: The notes recorded on one contact (subject, text, who wrote it, when), newest first. APIv4 Note.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_relationships
tools.title: List contact relationships
tools.description: The relationships of one contact (employee of, spouse of, volunteer for, ...) with the other contact, start and end date and whether it is active. APIv4 Relationship.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_contributions
tools.title: List contributions
tools.description: Contributions (donations, membership dues, event fees) with contact, amount, currency, financial type, status, payment method, date and source, newest first. Filter by contact, status, financial type, date range and minimum amount. Test contributions are left out. APIv4 Contribution.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_memberships
tools.title: List memberships
tools.description: Memberships with contact, membership type, status (New, Current, Grace, Expired, ...), join, start and end date. Filter by contact, status, type, or those ending before a date (renewal follow-up). Test memberships are left out. APIv4 Membership.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: Events with title, type, start and end date, whether active and public, maximum participants and summary. Upcoming events first when upcoming_only is set. Template events are left out. APIv4 Event.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_participants
tools.title: List event participants
tools.description: Event registrations with event, contact, status (Registered, Attended, Cancelled, ...), role, registration date and fee. Filter by event, contact or status. Test registrations are left out. APIv4 Participant.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_activities
tools.title: List activities
tools.description: Activities (meetings, phone calls, e-mails, follow-ups, ...) with type, subject, status, date and details, newest first. With contact_id: the activities that contact took part in, with their role (source, target or assignee). Otherwise all activities, optionally of one type or status. APIv4 ActivityContact.get / Activity.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_cases
tools.title: List cases
tools.description: Cases (CiviCase) with subject, case type, status and dates. With contact_id: the cases that contact is a client of. Needs the CiviCase component to be enabled. APIv4 CaseContact.get / Case.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_groups
tools.title: List groups
tools.description: Contact groups (mailing lists, static groups, smart groups) with title, description, visibility and type. APIv4 Group.get.

tools.name: civicrm_list_group_contacts
tools.title: List group members
tools.description: The members of one static group (or the groups one contact belongs to): contact, group and membership status (Added, Removed, Pending). Smart groups are computed by CiviCRM and not listed here. APIv4 GroupContact.get.

tools.name: civicrm_get_fields
tools.title: Describe an entity's fields
tools.description: The fields of one CiviCRM entity (Contact, Contribution, Event, ...) including custom fields: name, label, data type, whether required, and the allowed options for a pick-list field. Use it to find the right field names for civicrm_query and the right option names for the filters and write tools. APIv4 <Entity>.getFields.

tools.name: civicrm_list_entities
tools.title: List API entities
tools.description: The APIv4 entities this CiviCRM site offers (Contact, Contribution, Event, plus those of installed extensions), with a short description. Use the names with civicrm_get_fields and civicrm_query. APIv4 Entity.get.

tools.name: civicrm_query
tools.title: Query any entity
tools.description: Read records of ANY CiviCRM entity with APIv4 Entity.get: choose fields, filter, sort and page. Use civicrm_list_entities and civicrm_get_fields for the names. Field names may be joined (`contact_id.display_name`, `email_primary.email`) or ask for an option's text (`status_id:label`). Examples: entity Tag; entity Campaign with where [{field:'is_active',op:'=',value:true}]; entity Contribution with select ['id','total_amount'] and where [{field:'total_amount',op:'>=',value:1000}]. Read-only; credential fields and system entities (settings, payment processors, mailings, users) are refused.

tools.name: civicrm_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: creates ONE new contact (an individual, organization or household) and optionally its first e-mail address and phone number. Does not check for duplicates: search first with civicrm_search_contacts. Sends nothing. APIv4 Contact.create, Email.create, Phone.create.

tools.name: civicrm_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: changes basic fields of ONE existing contact (name, job title, source, preferred language) and/or its communication preferences (do not e-mail, do not phone, do not mail, do not SMS, opted out of bulk mail). Only the fields you give are changed. Setting a do-not flag to false re-enables contact the person may have declined, so only do that on the person's request. APIv4 Contact.update.

tools.name: civicrm_add_contact_note
tools.title: Add contact note
tools.description: WRITE: adds ONE note to a contact's record, written by the contact this API key belongs to. Sends nothing. APIv4 Note.create.

tools.name: civicrm_log_activity
tools.title: Log activity
tools.description: WRITE: records ONE activity (a meeting, phone call, e-mail, follow-up, ...) with one or more contacts. It only STORES the record: an activity of type Email does not send an e-mail. Added by the contact this API key belongs to unless source_contact_id is given. APIv4 Activity.create.

tools.name: civicrm_record_contribution
tools.title: Record contribution
tools.description: WRITE: records ONE contribution (a donation, a payment received elsewhere) for a contact. It only STORES the financial record: no card is charged, no receipt is e-mailed, and the amount shows up in CiviCRM's reports and the contact's giving history. Check civicrm_list_contributions first to avoid a duplicate. APIv4 Contribution.create.

tools.name: civicrm_create_membership
tools.title: Create membership
tools.description: WRITE: gives ONE contact a membership of a type. CiviCRM works out the dates and status from the type unless you give dates. It does NOT record a payment (use civicrm_record_contribution for that) and sends nothing. APIv4 Membership.create.

tools.name: civicrm_add_contact_to_group
tools.title: Add contact to group
tools.description: WRITE: adds ONE contact to ONE static group. If the group is used as a mailing list, the contact will receive future mailings sent to it, so only add people who agreed. Sends nothing by itself. Adding a contact who is already in the group changes nothing; a contact who was removed from it (or is pending) is set back to Added. APIv4 GroupContact.save matched on group and contact.

tools.name: civicrm_register_participant
tools.title: Register participant
tools.description: WRITE: registers ONE contact for ONE event (a participant record). It does not check the event's capacity or fee, does not take payment and sends no confirmation e-mail. APIv4 Participant.create.

tools.name: civicrm_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: civicrm_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the CiviCRM tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: civicrm_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on CiviCRM (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: civicrm_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's CiviCRM Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run civicrm_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Find the contact for jane@example.org and show her donations and memberships.
Which memberships expire in the next 30 days?
List the donations over 500 received this month, newest first.
Log a phone call with contact 1042: she will renew in November.

servers.name: CustomCat
servers.description: Browse the CustomCat catalog, your products and designs; check shipping; create and cancel orders.

login.hint: Find it in the CustomCat app (customcat-beta.mylocker.net) → **Settings**: CustomCat creates two keys, a **Read** key and a **Write** key. Use the Read key for look-ups only; use the Write key if you want the assistant to place or cancel orders (an order charges the payment method on your CustomCat account). Your key is used only to call the CustomCat API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: customcat_list_products
tools.title: List your products
tools.description: List the products you set up in CustomCat (a design on one or more catalog items) with variants, SKUs, cost, price, stock flag and design images. Use the variant SKUs when placing an order for these products. GET /product.

tools.name: customcat_get_product
tools.title: Get one of your products
tools.description: One of your CustomCat products by id (e.g. 22-2580581): variants, SKUs, cost, price, options, designs. GET /product/{product_id}.

tools.name: customcat_list_designs
tools.title: List your designs
tools.description: List the designs uploaded to your CustomCat account: id, name, tags, image URLs, default product and last-updated time. GET /design.

tools.name: customcat_list_catalog_categories
tools.title: List catalog categories
tools.description: The CustomCat catalog categories (Digisoft, Sublimation) and their subcategories (e.g. T-Shirts, Sweatshirts, Bags), to narrow customcat_list_catalog. GET /catalogcategory.

tools.name: customcat_list_catalog
tools.title: List the blank-product catalog
tools.description: Browse the full CustomCat catalog of printable blank products (the items you can order with your own artwork). Filter by category and subcategory from customcat_list_catalog_categories. The reply carries the total in `total`. GET /catalog.

tools.name: customcat_get_catalog_product
tools.title: Get a catalog product
tools.description: One catalog product by numeric id with its colors, sizes and SKUs. GET /catalog/{catalog_product_id}.

tools.name: customcat_get_catalog_sku
tools.title: Get a catalog SKU (stock check)
tools.description: One catalog SKU with its price and stock status. Use it before ordering: a SKU that is out of stock, discontinued or invalid makes the order fail. GET /catalog/sku/{catalog_sku_id}.

tools.name: customcat_list_shipping_methods
tools.title: List shipping methods
tools.description: The shipping methods CustomCat offers for a destination country (ids and names). The method name is required when placing an order. GET /shipping.

tools.name: customcat_get_shipping_cost
tools.title: Get the shipping cost for items
tools.description: Calculate the shipping cost of one shipping method for a destination and a list of catalog SKUs with quantities. Read-only quote: it places nothing. POST /shipping/{shipping_id} (shipping_id from customcat_list_shipping_methods).

tools.name: customcat_get_order_status
tools.title: Get order status
tools.description: Status of an order by YOUR order id: order status (Pending, Verified, Shipped), per-item production status, shipments with tracking ids, totals and the ship-to address. Set sandbox=true to look up a sandbox test order. GET /order/status/{order_id}.

tools.name: customcat_create_order
tools.title: Place an order
tools.description: WRITE: place an order for CustomCat to print and ship. This CHARGES the payment method on file in your CustomCat account (product cost + shipping; a front+back print adds $5 per line item) unless sandbox=true, which only validates the order. A real order (sandbox=false) also needs confirm=true, set only after the user confirmed it. The order id is yours and must be new (a duplicate is rejected). Needs the Write API key. Check stock with customcat_get_catalog_sku and the method name with customcat_list_shipping_methods first, and confirm the details with the user before calling. POST /order/{order_id}.

tools.name: customcat_cancel_order
tools.title: Cancel an order
tools.description: WRITE: cancel (delete) an order by YOUR order id. CustomCat can only cancel an order that has not gone into production; one already printed or shipped is refused. Needs the Write API key. Confirm with the user first. DELETE /order/{order_id}.

tools.name: customcat_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: customcat_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the CustomCat tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: customcat_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on CustomCat (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: customcat_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's CustomCat Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run customcat_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: What is the status of order 101-102938 and has it shipped?
List the products I set up in CustomCat and their variant SKUs.
Is catalog SKU 39515 in stock, and what would shipping to Detroit cost?
Place a sandbox test order for two of my Red / Large shirts to Joe Testing in Detroit.

servers.name: Farmbrite
servers.description: Read Farmbrite livestock, crops, tasks, inventory and orders; log records and tasks.

login.hint: Find it in Farmbrite under your **user profile → API Key** (Farmbrite enables API access on request: see developers.farmbrite.com). The key acts with that user's permissions, so Farmbrite recommends a separate user for integrations. Your key is used only to call the Farmbrite API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_animals
tools.title: List animals
tools.description: List livestock records (name, type, tag number, gender, breed, status, weight, group, purchase/sale data). Farmbrite returns only active-status animals unless you filter by status (Sold, Deceased, Culled, Butchered, Archived...). GET /animals.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_animal
tools.title: Get animal
tools.description: One animal by id, with its current location and custom fields. GET /animals/{animal_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_livestock_groups
tools.title: List livestock groups
tools.description: List livestock groups (id, name, type). GET /livestock_groups.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_livestock_group
tools.title: Get livestock group
tools.description: One livestock group by id with its member count, filters and member animals. GET /livestock_groups/{group_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_animal_measurements
tools.title: List animal measurements
tools.description: Weight, height, temperature, condition score and fecal-count records of one animal, newest data included. GET /animals/{animal_id}/measurements.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_feedings
tools.title: List feedings
tools.description: Feeding records (amount, cost, date, feed type, inventory used) of one animal or livestock group. GET /{animals|livestock_groups}/{id}/feedings.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_grazing_summary
tools.title: List grazing summary
tools.description: Grazing status per field/pasture: animals present, days rested, rest days required, last grazed. GET /grazings.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_plants
tools.title: List plant types
tools.description: List plant types/varieties (days to maturity, spacing, market price, harvest unit). GET /plants.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_crops
tools.title: List crop plantings
tools.description: List crop plantings (plant, field/plot, bed, quantity, planting and expected harvest dates, growth stage). GET /crops.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_crop
tools.title: Get crop planting
tools.description: One crop planting by id. GET /crops/{crop_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_plots
tools.title: List fields (plots)
tools.description: List fields/grow locations (title, type, size, status, grazing rest days). GET /plots.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_plot
tools.title: Get field (plot)
tools.description: One field/grow location by id. GET /plots/{plot_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_harvests
tools.title: List harvests
tools.description: Harvest records (quantity, unit, grade, price, date, inventory added) of one animal or crop planting. GET /{animals|crops}/{id}/harvests.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_treatments
tools.title: List treatments
tools.description: Treatment records (type, product, amount, cost, date, withdrawal date, technician) of one animal, field or crop planting. GET /{animals|plots|crops}/{id}/treatments.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_notes
tools.title: List notes
tools.description: Notes (description, category, date, keywords) attached to an animal, field, plant type, crop planting or inventory type. GET /{animals|plots|plants|crops|inventory_types}/{id}/notes.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts (customers, suppliers, vendors): name, company, email, phone, type, label. GET /contacts.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact by id, with address. GET /contacts/{contact_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List tasks (title, description, status, priority, assignee, due/end time, checklist, linked animal/field/crop). GET /tasks.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_task
tools.title: Get task
tools.description: One task by id with its checklist. GET /tasks/{task_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_activities
tools.title: List schedule activities
tools.description: List calendar/schedule activities (title, start and end time, all-day flag, linked animal or field). GET /activities.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_inventory_types
tools.title: List inventory items
tools.description: List inventory item types (feed, supplies, harvested products) with the quantity remaining, unit, value and low-stock alert level. GET /inventory_types.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_inventory_type
tools.title: Get inventory item
tools.description: One inventory item type by id with quantity remaining and projected empty date. GET /inventory_types/{inventory_type_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_inventory_locations
tools.title: Get inventory by location
tools.description: Where one inventory item is stored: warehouse and bin ids and names, capacity and quantity remaining in each. Use the ids with farmbrite_add_inventory / farmbrite_remove_inventory. GET /inventory_types/{inventory_type_id}/inventory.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_warehouses
tools.title: List storage locations
tools.description: List storage locations (warehouses) for inventory: name, description, internal id. Use the ids when adding or removing inventory. GET /warehouses.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_orders
tools.title: List orders
tools.description: List sales orders (status, payment status, total, dates, contact, delivery type, invoice number). GET /orders.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_order
tools.title: Get order
tools.description: One order by id with its line items, customer contact, delivery address and totals. GET /orders/{order_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_list_transactions
tools.title: List transactions
tools.description: List income and expense transactions (type, amount, date, vendor, category, linked animal/field/plant, description). GET /transactions.

tools.name: farmbrite_get_transaction
tools.title: Get transaction
tools.description: One transaction by id. GET /transactions/{transaction_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: create a contact (customer, supplier, vendor). Nothing is emailed or sent to the contact. Creating twice makes two contacts. POST /contacts.

tools.name: farmbrite_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing contact (only the fields you pass are sent). Overwrites the previous values. PUT /contacts/{contact_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_create_task
tools.title: Create task
tools.description: WRITE: create a task, optionally linked to an animal, equipment, plant, location or planting. May notify the assigned Farmbrite user according to your account settings. Creating twice makes two tasks. POST /tasks.

tools.name: farmbrite_update_task
tools.title: Update task
tools.description: WRITE: change a task (only the fields you pass are sent); set complete=true to mark it done. Overwrites previous values. PUT /tasks/{task_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_create_transaction
tools.title: Create transaction
tools.description: WRITE: record an income or expense transaction in the farm's books. Creating twice records it twice. POST /transactions.

tools.name: farmbrite_create_note
tools.title: Add note
tools.description: WRITE: add a note to an animal, livestock group, field, plant type, crop planting or inventory item. Notes cannot be removed with this server. POST /{parent}/{id}/notes.

tools.name: farmbrite_add_inventory
tools.title: Add inventory
tools.description: WRITE: add stock to an inventory item in a storage location (warehouse, optionally a bin). Raises the quantity remaining; not idempotent: repeating adds again. Find ids with farmbrite_list_inventory_types, farmbrite_get_inventory_locations and farmbrite_list_warehouses. PUT /inventory_types/{id}/inventory/add.

tools.name: farmbrite_remove_inventory
tools.title: Remove inventory
tools.description: WRITE: take stock out of an inventory item in a storage location (use, loss, sale). Lowers the quantity remaining; not idempotent: repeating removes again. It cannot be undone with this server except by adding stock back. PUT /inventory_types/{id}/inventory/remove.

tools.name: farmbrite_create_order
tools.title: Create order
tools.description: WRITE: create a sales order with line items (status defaults to Draft and payment_status to Due unless you set them; memo is internal, note is customer-facing). Farmbrite may email the customer or generate an invoice depending on the account's settings and the status chosen; the API reference does not say, so use Draft unless the user asks otherwise and only pass email when told to. Orders are entered as back-office orders (is_admin). Creating twice makes two orders. POST /orders.

tools.name: farmbrite_update_order
tools.title: Update order status
tools.description: WRITE: change an order's status and/or payment status (for example mark it Paid or Delivered). Farmbrite may send customer notifications on some status changes, depending on the account settings. PUT /orders/{order_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_create_animal
tools.title: Create animal
tools.description: WRITE: add an animal (or a group when is_group=true with group_qty) to the herd. type (e.g. Cattle, Sheep) and status are required. Creating twice makes two animals. POST /animals.

tools.name: farmbrite_update_animal
tools.title: Update animal
tools.description: WRITE: change an animal's fields (only the fields you pass are sent), including its status (Sold, Deceased, Culled...). Statuses Butchered, Culled and Deceased need death_date. Overwrites previous values. PUT /animals/{animal_id}.

tools.name: farmbrite_add_animal_measurement
tools.title: Add animal measurement
tools.description: WRITE: record a measurement for one animal (weight, height, temperature, condition score, fecal egg count). Adds a record each time. POST /animals/{animal_id}/measurements.

tools.name: farmbrite_create_feeding
tools.title: Record feeding
tools.description: WRITE: record a feeding for an animal or livestock group. Either name the feed type, or give inventory_id + inventory_location_id to draw it from inventory (which lowers that inventory's quantity). Adds a record each time. POST /{animals|livestock_groups}/{id}/feedings.

tools.name: farmbrite_create_harvest
tools.title: Record harvest
tools.description: WRITE: record a harvest (quantity and unit) for an animal or crop planting. Adds a record each time. POST /{animals|crops}/{id}/harvests.

tools.name: farmbrite_create_treatment
tools.title: Record treatment
tools.description: WRITE: record a treatment (vaccine, dewormer, spray, fertilizer...) for an animal, livestock group, field or crop planting. Adds a record each time. POST /{animals|livestock_groups|plots|crops}/{id}/treatments.

tools.name: farmbrite_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: farmbrite_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Farmbrite tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: farmbrite_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Farmbrite (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: farmbrite_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Farmbrite Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run farmbrite_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which animals are currently sick or quarantined, and what treatments have they had?
List my open tasks due this week and mark the fence repair as done.
How much layer feed is left in inventory, and where is it stored?
Record an expense of 240 for hay from Smith Farm Supply dated today.

servers.name: intelliHR
servers.description: Read intelliHR people, jobs, leave, skills and training; create and update people records.

login.hint: The tenant is the first part of your intelliHR address (acme for acme.intellihr.io). Create the key in intelliHR under **Settings → Public API Access Keys**. intelliHR keys have no scopes: a key acts as a full system administrator, so create one just for this connection and delete it in intelliHR when you stop using it. Your key is used only to call the intelliHR API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: intellihr_list_people
tools.title: List people
tools.description: List the people (employees) in intelliHR as at today: name, employee number, email, phone, addresses, emergency contact, employment status, their jobs (summary) and custom fields. Filter by name (matches any part of the name), email, employee number, job id, recently updated, or who is on extended leave. Health information is never returned. GET /people.

tools.name: intellihr_get_person
tools.title: Get person
tools.description: One person's full record by id: names, date of birth, gender, employee number, contact details, addresses, emergency contact, employment status, jobs, work rights, user account and custom fields. Health information is never returned. GET /people/{id}.

tools.name: intellihr_list_person_documents
tools.title: List a person's documents
tools.description: The documents stored on a person's record (file name, type, size, upload status and a download link). Contents are not read. GET /people/{personId}/documents.

tools.name: intellihr_list_person_skills
tools.title: List a person's skills
tools.description: The skills assigned to a person (with their level and review details as intelliHR returns them). The whole list comes back at once. GET /people/{personId}/skills.

tools.name: intellihr_list_person_tasks
tools.title: List a person's tasks
tools.description: Tasks (forms, reviews, check-ins, onboarding steps) for a person, by tab: DUE (default), ABOUT_ME, ABOUT_OTHERS, DONE or IGNORED. GET /people/{personId}/tasks.

tools.name: intellihr_list_jobs
tools.title: List jobs
tools.description: List jobs (roles people hold, past, current and future) as at today: person, position title, location, business unit and entity, supervisor, work type, FTE, remuneration schedule, start/end dates and status. Filter by person, job title, status (Current Job, Future Job, Ending Job, Past Job), work type, primary job, or upcoming/recent end dates. GET /jobs.

tools.name: intellihr_get_job
tools.title: Get job
tools.description: One job by id with its person, position title, location, business unit, supervisor, pay grade, remuneration and dates. GET /jobs/{id}.

tools.name: intellihr_get_job_timeline
tools.title: Get job timeline
tools.description: The upcoming changes and current information about a job (scheduled changes, end date). GET /jobs/{jobId}/timeline.

tools.name: intellihr_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: The organisation's locations (sites) with parent location, code, address, enabled flag and representatives. GET /locations.

tools.name: intellihr_list_business_units
tools.title: List business units
tools.description: The organisation's business units (departments, teams). Filter by name or identifier. GET /business-units.

tools.name: intellihr_list_business_entities
tools.title: List business entities
tools.description: The organisation's business entities (legal employers). GET /business-entities.

tools.name: intellihr_list_position_titles
tools.title: List position titles
tools.description: The position titles (job names) defined in intelliHR. Filter by name. GET /position-titles.

tools.name: intellihr_list_pay_grades
tools.title: List pay grades
tools.description: The pay grades and their rates, optionally as at a date. GET /pay-grades.

tools.name: intellihr_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: The user accounts that can sign in to intelliHR: username, enabled flag, permission groups and the linked person. GET /users.

tools.name: intellihr_list_custom_field_definitions
tools.title: List custom field definitions
tools.description: The custom fields defined in intelliHR (what each field on a person, job or location means and its type). GET /custom-field-definitions.

tools.name: intellihr_list_reference_data
tools.title: List reference data
tools.description: Look up one of intelliHR's reference lists: employment_conditions, work_classes, work_types, work_rights, recruitment_sources, extended_leave_types, job_change_reasons, skill_disciplines, training_types, training_providers, qualification_types, qualification_library_items, onboarding_templates, permission_groups or representative_types. Use it to find the ids and names other tools need.

tools.name: intellihr_list_skills
tools.title: List skills
tools.description: The skills catalogue, optionally only business-critical skills or one discipline. GET /skills.

tools.name: intellihr_list_qualifications
tools.title: List qualifications
tools.description: Qualification records held by people (licences, certificates) with status and dates. Filter by person, employee number or library item. GET /qualifications.

tools.name: intellihr_list_trainings
tools.title: List trainings
tools.description: Training records completed or booked by people, with provider, type and dates. Filter by training name, provider, type, employee number or email. GET /trainings.

tools.name: intellihr_create_person
tools.title: Create person
tools.description: WRITE: create a new person record in intelliHR (last name required). It creates the person only: no job, no user account and no welcome email is sent. A job is added separately in intelliHR. Check with list_people first to avoid duplicates. POST /people.

tools.name: intellihr_update_person
tools.title: Update person
tools.description: WRITE: change fields on an existing person (only the fields you pass change): names, date of birth, gender, employee number, title and emergency contact. Contact details, addresses and jobs are not changed by this tool. PATCH /people/{id}.

tools.name: intellihr_create_extended_leave
tools.title: Create extended leave
tools.description: WRITE: record extended leave (parental, long service, unpaid, etc.) on an existing job. It changes the person's employment record and can trigger intelliHR workflows. The leave is created with the end date you give as expected; finalise it in intelliHR when the person returns. Find leave types with list_reference_data kind extended_leave_types. POST /extended-leave.

tools.name: intellihr_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: intellihr_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the intelliHR tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: intellihr_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on intelliHR (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: intellihr_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription

servers.name: Lawcus

fields.label: Where is your Lawcus firm hosted?

tools.name: lawcus_list_team_members

tools.name: lawcus_search

tools.description: Lawcus: global search across contacts, matters and leads for a keyword.

tools.name: lawcus_list_contacts

tools.name: lawcus_get_contact

tools.name: lawcus_create_contact

tools.name: lawcus_list_matters
tools.title: List matters
tools.description: Lawcus: list matters (cases) with status, client, billing type, trust and retainer balances. Filter by status, name, number, client or dates. Paged with skip/take; the reply also carries opened/closed counts.

tools.name: lawcus_get_matter

tools.name: lawcus_list_leads

tools.name: lawcus_get_lead

tools.name: lawcus_list_lead_sources

tools.name: lawcus_list_workflows

tools.name: lawcus_list_workflow_stages

tools.name: lawcus_list_tasks

tools.name: lawcus_create_task

servers.name: myPhoner
servers.description: Work myPhoner calling lists and leads: search, log call outcomes, add, update and assign leads.

login.hint: The subdomain is the first part of your myPhoner address (`acme` for acme.myphoner.com). The account key is in myPhoner under **Manage → Configure → Integrations**; a user's personal key is on their preferences page under Credentials and acts with that user's rights. Your key is used only to call the myPhoner API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: myphoner_list_lists
tools.title: List calling lists
tools.description: All calling lists (campaigns) in the account: id, name, creation date, number of leads and whether the list guarantees the default fields. Start here to find a list id. GET /lists.

tools.name: myphoner_get_list
tools.title: Get a calling list
tools.description: One calling list with its lead count and its call back / winner / loser / archive / skip categories. GET /lists/{id}.

tools.name: myphoner_list_columns
tools.title: List the fields of a list
tools.description: The fields (columns) of a list. The `key` of each is the name to use when creating, updating or finding leads. GET /lists/{id}/columns.

tools.name: myphoner_get_list_stats
tools.title: Get list statistics
tools.description: Lead counts of a list by state (new, call back, won, lost, archived) and by category within each state. Use it for campaign progress and conversion questions. GET /lists/{id}/stats.

tools.name: myphoner_create_list
tools.title: Create a calling list
tools.description: Create a new, empty calling list with its fields. Creates data in the account (nothing is sent to anyone). Field kinds: none (text), phone, email, url, boolean, integer, date, text (multi-line), options, address. POST /lists.

tools.name: myphoner_list_leads
tools.title: List the leads in a list
tools.description: Leads of one list, newest first by creation date (or most recently updated first with order=last_updated_first). Each lead has its state (new, call_back, won, lost, archived), category, scheduled call back, who claimed it and its lead_data fields. GET /lists/{id}/leads.

tools.name: myphoner_get_lead
tools.title: Get a lead
tools.description: One lead with its state, category, claim, duplicates and all lead_data fields. GET /leads/{id}.

tools.name: myphoner_find_leads
tools.title: Find leads by field
tools.description: Exact match on one or more fields of a list, for example a phone number or an email address (to check whether a lead already exists). All fields must match unless match_all is false. GET /lists/{id}/leads/find.

tools.name: myphoner_search_leads
tools.title: Search leads
tools.description: Free-text search across lead data and activity logs (comments, events), like the search box in myPhoner; optionally limited to some lists. Returns the total hit count and one page of leads. GET /leads/search.

tools.name: myphoner_create_lead
tools.title: Create a lead
tools.description: Add a new lead to a list. Keys of `fields` are the list's column keys (myphoner_list_columns). Creates data only; nothing is sent to the lead. Duplicate detection runs in the background a few minutes later (check detected_duplicates on the lead afterwards). POST /lists/{id}/leads.

tools.name: myphoner_update_lead
tools.title: Update lead data
tools.description: Change field values of an existing lead (only the fields you pass change). Keys of `fields` are the list's column keys (myphoner_list_columns). Overwrites the old values; use null to clear one. PATCH /leads/{id}.

tools.name: myphoner_mark_lead_winner
tools.title: Mark a lead as winner
tools.description: Mark a lead as a winner (a won deal). The lead moves to that state and an event is logged on it; nothing is sent to the lead. Optionally add a comment and an existing winner category. POST /leads/{id}/winner.

tools.name: myphoner_mark_lead_loser
tools.title: Mark a lead as loser
tools.description: Mark a lead as a loser (not interested / lost). The lead moves to that state and an event is logged on it; nothing is sent to the lead. Optionally add a comment and an existing loser category. POST /leads/{id}/loser.

tools.name: myphoner_mark_lead_call_back
tools.title: Mark a lead for call back
tools.description: Schedule a lead for a call back. The lead moves to that state and an event is logged on it; nothing is sent to the lead. Set when with call_back_in (minutes) or scheduled_for; optionally a comment and an existing call back category. POST /leads/{id}/call_back.

tools.name: myphoner_archive_lead
tools.title: Archive a lead
tools.description: Archive a lead (it leaves the calling queue). The lead moves to that state and an event is logged on it; nothing is sent to the lead. Optionally add a comment and an existing archive category. POST /leads/{id}/archive.

tools.name: myphoner_delegate_lead
tools.title: Delegate or claim a lead
tools.description: Give the claim on a lead to a user (the lead then shows up in that agent's queue), identified by user id or email. PATCH /leads/{id}/delegate.

tools.name: myphoner_move_lead
tools.title: Move a lead to another list
tools.description: Move a lead to another list. The destination may be the lead's current list, which with release_claim=true just releases a claimed lead. PATCH /leads/{id}/migrate.

tools.name: myphoner_get_call
tools.title: Get a call
tools.description: One call made from myPhoner: who called, the number dialed, duration (0 = unanswered), direction, disposition (normal, voicemail, no_answer, busy ...), state, the lead and list it belongs to, and recording links. GET /calls/{id}.

servers.name: Pobuca Connect
servers.description: Read and update Pobuca Connect contacts and organizations; look up teams and custom fields.

login.hint: Create it in Pobuca Connect → **Settings → Data Management → API Keys → Manage → Create API Key** (API keys are an Enterprise-plan feature). The key acts as the coworker it impersonates; a dedicated coworker makes its activity easy to track. Your key is used only to call the Pobuca Connect API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: pobuca_get_me
tools.title: Get current user
tools.description: The Pobuca Connect user this API key acts as: id, first name, last name and email. GET /api/v1/Users/Me.

tools.name: pobuca_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts (people) with names, phones, emails, addresses, organization, team, tags and custom fields. Paged: 50 per call at most; pass next_skip as skip for the next page. Supports OData $filter and $orderby. To find recently changed contacts use $filter like "updatedat ge 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z". GET /api/v1/Contacts.

tools.name: pobuca_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact by id, with all phone numbers, emails, addresses, organization, team, tags and custom fields. GET /api/v1/Contacts/{id}.

tools.name: pobuca_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: create a new contact in the Pobuca Connect address book. Needs at least a first name, last name or email. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two contacts, so search with pobuca_list_contacts first. POST /api/v1/Contacts.

tools.name: pobuca_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing contact; only the fields you pass are sent. Overwrites the previous values (tags and customFields are replaced as given). Look the contact up first and confirm the right one. PATCH /api/v1/Contacts/{id}.

tools.name: pobuca_list_organizations
tools.title: List organizations
tools.description: List organizations (companies) with phone, email, website, billing and shipping addresses, type, industry, tags and custom fields. Paged: 50 per call at most; pass next_skip as skip for the next page. Supports OData $filter and $orderby. GET /api/v1/Organizations.

tools.name: pobuca_get_organization
tools.title: Get organization
tools.description: One organization by id, with addresses, type, industry, primary contact, tags and custom fields. GET /api/v1/Organizations/{id}.

tools.name: pobuca_create_organization
tools.title: Create organization
tools.description: WRITE: create a new organization (company) in Pobuca Connect. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two organizations, so search with pobuca_list_organizations first. POST /api/v1/Organizations.

tools.name: pobuca_update_organization
tools.title: Update organization
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing organization; only the fields you pass are sent. Overwrites the previous values (tags and customFields are replaced as given). Look the organization up first and confirm the right one. PATCH /api/v1/Organizations/{id}.

tools.name: pobuca_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: List teams (the groups that own and share contacts). Paged: 50 per call at most; pass next_skip as skip for the next page. Supports OData $filter and $orderby. GET /api/v1/Teams.

tools.name: pobuca_get_team
tools.title: Get team
tools.description: One team by id. GET /api/v1/Teams/{id}.

tools.name: pobuca_list_team_members
tools.title: List team members
tools.description: List which users belong to which team, with their role in the team. Paged: 50 per call at most; pass next_skip as skip for the next page. Supports OData $filter and $orderby. GET /api/v1/UserTeams.

tools.name: pobuca_list_departments

tools.description: List departments (ids for the departmentId of a contact). Paged: 50 per call at most; pass next_skip as skip for the next page. Supports OData $filter and $orderby. GET /api/v1/Departments.

tools.name: pobuca_list_industries
tools.title: List industries
tools.description: List industries (ids for the industryId of an organization). Paged: 50 per call at most; pass next_skip as skip for the next page. Supports OData $filter and $orderby. GET /api/v1/Industries.

tools.name: pobuca_list_organization_types
tools.title: List organization types
tools.description: List organization types (ids for the organizationTypeId of an organization). Paged: 50 per call at most; pass next_skip as skip for the next page. Supports OData $filter and $orderby. GET /api/v1/OrganizationTypes.

tools.name: pobuca_list_countries
tools.title: List countries
tools.description: List countries with their codes. Paged: 50 per call at most; pass next_skip as skip for the next page. Supports OData $filter and $orderby. GET /api/v1/Countries.

tools.name: pobuca_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List custom fields
tools.description: List the custom fields defined for contacts, organizations ('Group') or users, with type (Text or Dropdown) and, for dropdowns, the available options. Use the ids and option ids in the customFields of a contact or organization. GET /api/v1/CustomFields/{entityType}.
