servers.name: Bind ERP
servers.description: Read Bind ERP clients, products, inventory, invoices, orders; create prospects, clients, orders.

login.hint: In Bind ERP click your **user name** (top right) -> **Perfil** -> tab **Integraciones**, enter your password and click **Generar API Key**. The key acts with that user's permissions and is subject to Bind's API limits (150 requests per 5 minutes). Your key is used only to call the Bind ERP API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: binderp_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The Bind ERP user and company this API key belongs to: user name, email, roles, branches (locations), company name, RFC (tax id), legal/commercial name, fiscal type and address. GET /api/UserProfile and /api/CompanyProfile.

tools.name: binderp_list_catalog
tools.title: List catalog (branches, warehouses, price lists, currencies, bank accounts, users, categories)
tools.description: List one of the reference catalogs whose ids other tools need: locations (branches), warehouses, price_lists, currencies, bank_accounts (with balances), users (employees) or categories. GET /api/Locations, /api/Warehouses, /api/PriceLists, /api/Currencies, /api/BankAccounts, /api/Users, /api/Categories.

tools.name: binderp_list_clients
tools.title: List clients
tools.description: List customers: id, number, name, legal name, RFC, email, phone, next contact date and branch. Filter with OData, e.g. substringof('acme', ClientName). GET /api/Clients.

tools.name: binderp_get_client
tools.title: Get client
tools.description: One customer with credit terms (days and limit), payment method, price list, branch, sales and credit contacts, discount, account number and addresses. GET /api/Clients/{id}.

tools.name: binderp_get_client_addresses
tools.title: Get client addresses
tools.description: The addresses of a customer, with the ids that an order needs as address_id. GET /api/Clients/{id}/Addresses.

tools.name: binderp_list_prospects
tools.title: List prospects
tools.description: List sales prospects (leads): id, name, company, email, phone and salesperson. GET /api/Prospects.

tools.name: binderp_get_prospect
tools.title: Get prospect
tools.description: One prospect: name, company, email, phone, comments, creation date and owner. GET /api/Prospects/{id}.

tools.name: binderp_list_providers
tools.title: List providers (suppliers)
tools.description: List suppliers: id, number, name, legal name, RFC, email, phone and city. GET /api/Providers.

tools.name: binderp_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products: id, code, title, SKU, cost, current inventory, VAT flag, unit, currency and categories. Filter with OData, e.g. substringof('tornillo', Title). GET /api/Products.

tools.name: binderp_get_product
tools.title: Get product
tools.description: One product with prices per price list, inventory per warehouse, categories and alternative units. GET /api/Products/{id}.

tools.name: binderp_list_products_with_price_and_stock
tools.title: List products with price and stock
tools.description: Products with the price (from one price list) and stock (in one warehouse), VAT/IEPS, min/max and volume prices: the view a point-of-sale or quote needs. Get the ids from binderp_list_catalog. GET /api/ProductsPriceAndInventory.

tools.name: binderp_get_inventory
tools.title: Get inventory by warehouse
tools.description: Stock of every product in one warehouse: current inventory, balance, quantity on client orders and on purchase orders, value and SKU. Filter with OData, e.g. CurrentInventory lt 5 for low stock. GET /api/Inventory?warehouseID=.

tools.name: binderp_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices (sales)
tools.description: List sales invoices, with series, number, date, client, RFC, subtotal, discount, taxes, total, payments received, credit notes, expiration date and status. Open balance = Total - Payments - CreditNotes (filter Total gt Payments, then subtract CreditNotes from the rows). GET /api/Invoices.

tools.name: binderp_get_invoice
tools.title: Get invoice
tools.description: One sale with client, status, payment terms, branch, warehouse, currency, totals, payments, credit notes and its product and service lines. Takes the invoice GUID or its number. GET /api/Invoices/{idOrNumber}.

tools.name: binderp_list_invoice_payments
tools.title: List invoice payments
tools.description: The payments registered against one invoice: date, account, amount, status and who registered them. GET /api/Invoices/Payment/{invoiceID}.

tools.name: binderp_list_orders
tools.title: List sales orders
tools.description: List customer orders (pedidos): number, date, client, branch, warehouse, salesperson, currency, subtotals, taxes, total and status. GET /api/Orders.

tools.name: binderp_get_order
tools.title: Get order
tools.description: One customer order with address, status, totals and its product and service lines. GET /api/Orders/{id}.

tools.name: binderp_list_quotes
tools.title: List quotes
tools.description: List quotes (cotizaciones): number, date, client, branch, comments, total, currency and status. GET /api/Quotes.

tools.name: binderp_get_quote
tools.title: Get quote
tools.description: One quote with client or prospect, totals and its line items. GET /api/Quotes/{id}.

tools.name: binderp_list_purchase_orders
tools.title: List purchase orders
tools.description: List purchase orders to suppliers: number, warehouse, provider, date, status, quantity ordered and still missing, total and currency. GET /api/Purchases/GetPurchaseOrders.

tools.name: binderp_get_purchase_order
tools.title: Get purchase order
tools.description: One purchase order with its product lines, quantities received and totals. GET /api/Purchases/{id}.

tools.name: binderp_list_activities
tools.title: List activities
tools.description: List CRM activities (calls, meetings, tasks): title, start and end, owner, done flag, type and the client or prospect they belong to. GET /api/Activities.

tools.name: binderp_create_prospect
tools.title: Create prospect
tools.description: Create a sales prospect (lead) in Bind ERP. Writes a new record visible to the whole team; it is not deduplicated, so check binderp_list_prospects first. No message is sent to the prospect. POST /api/Prospects.

tools.name: binderp_create_client
tools.title: Create client
tools.description: Create a customer in Bind ERP. Writes a new customer record (with credit terms) and is not deduplicated: check binderp_list_clients for the RFC first. The RFC must be valid for the tax authority (use XAXX010101000 for a generic public customer). No message is sent. Get price_list_id and location_id from binderp_list_catalog. POST /api/Clients.

tools.name: binderp_add_comment
tools.title: Add comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a Bind ERP record (client, prospect, order, ...) identified by its GUID. The comment becomes part of that record's history and cannot be removed through this API. POST /api/Comments.

tools.name: binderp_create_order
tools.title: Create sales order
tools.description: Create a customer order (pedido, not an invoice: nothing is stamped or invoiced and no email is sent) with product and/or service lines. It reserves stock and shows up in the sales pipeline, so confirm client, prices and quantities first. Get ids from binderp_list_clients, binderp_get_client_addresses, binderp_list_catalog and binderp_list_products. POST /api/Orders.

tools.name: binderp_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: binderp_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Bind ERP tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: binderp_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Bind ERP (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: binderp_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Bind ERP Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run binderp_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which invoices are overdue and how much is still unpaid per client?
Which products in my main warehouse have fewer than 5 units left?
Show last month's sales orders for the client Acme.
Add a prospect: Maria Lopez from Acme, maria@acme.mx.

servers.name: Click2Mail
servers.description: Read Click2Mail credit, jobs, costs and tracking; upload documents, create and submit mail jobs.

login.hint: Use the login of your **Business** Click2Mail account (production, not the stage site) and switch on API access first: **Profile & Preferences → API access**. The API accepts only the account's username and password, so a dedicated account makes its activity easy to track. Submitting a job spends postage from your account, and this server only does that when you explicitly confirm. Your login is used only to call the Click2Mail API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: click2mail_get_credit
tools.title: Get account credit
tools.description: The prepaid credit balance of the Click2Mail account (`balance`) and whether the balance may go negative (`allowNegative`). Check it before submitting a job paid with User Credit. GET /molpro/credit.

tools.name: click2mail_list_return_addresses
tools.title: List saved account addresses
tools.description: The addresses of one type saved on the account (return addresses, billing, business reply, courtesy reply, EDDM mailer addresses) with their ids; use an id as `return_address_id` when creating a job. GET /molpro/account/addresses.

tools.name: click2mail_get_product_options
tools.title: Get product options
tools.description: The mail products and valid option combinations (document class, layout, production time, envelope, color, paper, print option, mail class) for the account. Use the exact strings from this reply in click2mail_create_job and click2mail_estimate_cost. GET /molpro/productOptions.

tools.name: click2mail_estimate_cost
tools.title: Estimate mailing cost
tools.description: Estimate the cost of a mailing from its print options and quantity without creating anything (nothing is charged). Use the exact option strings from click2mail_get_product_options. GET /molpro/costEstimate.

tools.name: click2mail_list_documents
tools.title: List documents
tools.description: List the documents uploaded to the account (id, name, class, pages), most recent first. Use a document id when creating a job. GET /molpro/documents.

tools.name: click2mail_get_address_list
tools.title: Get address list status
tools.description: Status of an uploaded address list: processing state (3 = CASS-standardized and ready for a job), name and counts. GET /molpro/addressLists/{id}.

tools.name: click2mail_get_address_list_info
tools.title: Get address list details
tools.description: Details of an address list: its addresses with the standardization result of each. Click2Mail returns 10 addresses by default: page with limit and offset. GET /molpro/addressLists/info.

tools.name: click2mail_check_addresses
tools.title: Check and correct addresses
tools.description: Validate and standardize up to 100 US postal addresses (USPS/CASS correction) before mailing. Read-only: nothing is saved or sent. POST /molpro/addressCorrection.

tools.name: click2mail_create_address_list
tools.title: Create address list
tools.description: WRITE: upload a recipient address list (up to 500 addresses) to the account. The list is standardized (CASS) by Click2Mail; poll click2mail_get_address_list until status 3, then use its id in click2mail_create_job. Creates data only; nothing is mailed or charged. POST /molpro/addressLists.

tools.name: click2mail_upload_document_from_url
tools.title: Upload document from URL
tools.description: WRITE: have Click2Mail fetch a PDF (or other supported file) from a public http(s) URL and store it as a document on the account. Returns the document id for click2mail_create_job. Creates data only; nothing is mailed or charged. POST /molpro/documents/url.

tools.name: click2mail_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the account's projects (jobs are grouped by project; jobs without one are grouped by month, e.g. "March 2022"), most recently updated first. Use a project name with click2mail_list_project_jobs. GET /molpro/projects.

tools.name: click2mail_list_project_jobs
tools.title: List jobs in a project
tools.description: List the mailing jobs of one project (id, status, description). This is how to see the account's jobs: pick a project from click2mail_list_projects. GET /molpro/projects/jobs.

tools.name: click2mail_list_jobs_by_app_signature
tools.title: List jobs by app signature
tools.description: List the jobs that were created with a given `appSignature` (the label an integration puts on its jobs; click2mail_create_job sets it). GET /molpro/jobs/appSignature.

tools.name: click2mail_get_job_status
tools.title: Get job status
tools.description: Status of a job: numeric `status` and its `description` (for example 9 = Editing) plus the status URL. GET /molpro/jobs/{id}.

tools.name: click2mail_get_job_info
tools.title: Get job details
tools.description: Full details of a job: print options, document, address list, dates, cost and payment. GET /molpro/jobs/info/{id}.

tools.name: click2mail_get_job_tracking
tools.title: Get job tracking
tools.description: USPS tracking for a submitted job: per mail piece barcode, address, status, date and location. Tracking updates once a day, so one call per day is enough; nothing is tracked on staging. GET /molpro/jobs/{id}/tracking.

tools.name: click2mail_get_job_cost
tools.title: Get job cost
tools.description: The exact cost of a created job (postage, printing, fees) for a payment type. Read it before click2mail_submit_job. GET /molpro/jobs/{id}/cost.

tools.name: click2mail_create_job
tools.title: Create job (draft)
tools.description: WRITE: create a mailing job from an uploaded document and an address list. The job stays a draft (status Editing): nothing is printed, mailed or charged until click2mail_submit_job. Use the exact option strings from click2mail_get_product_options. Returns the job id. POST /molpro/jobs.

tools.name: click2mail_request_job_proof
tools.title: Request job proof
tools.description: WRITE: ask Click2Mail to render a proof (preview PDF) of a draft job. Free; nothing is mailed or charged. The reply names the proof; it takes a moment to render. POST /molpro/jobs/{id}/proof.

tools.name: click2mail_submit_job
tools.title: Submit job (spends money)
tools.description: WRITE, SPENDS MONEY, NOT REVERSIBLE: submit a draft job for printing and USPS mailing. This charges postage and printing to the account (User Credit = prepaid balance, or Invoice) and the physical mail is sent to every recipient. Before calling: read click2mail_get_job_cost and click2mail_get_credit, and get the user's explicit go-ahead for this job and amount. `confirm` must be true. Cancellation is only possible for Invoice jobs, before processing starts. POST /molpro/jobs/{id}/submit.

tools.name: click2mail_cancel_job
tools.title: Cancel submitted job
tools.description: WRITE: cancel a SUBMITTED job. The vendor documents this only for jobs paid by invoice and only before processing for mailing has started; otherwise it fails. The mailing is stopped for good, so get the user's explicit go-ahead first; `confirm` must be true. To remove a draft use click2mail_delete_job. POST /molpro/jobs/{id}/cancel.

tools.name: click2mail_delete_job
tools.title: Delete draft job
tools.description: WRITE: delete a job that has not been submitted (status Editing or PendingProofAcceptence). Submitted jobs cannot be deleted; use click2mail_cancel_job. POST /molpro/jobs/{id}/delete.

tools.name: click2mail_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Click2Mail tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: click2mail_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Click2Mail (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: click2mail_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Click2Mail Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run click2mail_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: What is my Click2Mail credit balance?
Show the tracking for job 195795.
Which of my mailing jobs from March are still in editing status?
Upload this PDF from a link, build a postcard job for my address list and tell me the cost before I send it.

servers.name: CXT Software
servers.description: Track and search CXT courier orders, check drivers, propose and save order and route plans.

login.hint: Your account id is the 4 digits in your CXT address: for **09870.cxtsoftware.net** it is **0987** (drop the trailing 0). If X Dispatch runs on your own domain, leave it empty and fill in the server address. Type the user name without the XDISPATCH- or INET- prefix. An **Operations App user** can look up orders and plan routes (route planning needs the Itinerary Planning permission); an **internet user** (with "Allow Web Service API" on) sees the orders of its customer account. A dedicated user with only the permissions you want makes its activity easy to track. CXT bills API calls to your account (the first 5,000 credits a month are free) and the web service needs the integrations option on your plan. Your password is used only to call the CXT Software API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: cxt_track_shipments
tools.title: Track shipments
tools.description: Track orders and route stops by tracking number: matches a parcel reference, a parcel item barcode, or Reference1/Reference2 of an order or route stop. Returns shipment summaries with status events and proof of delivery as far as the caller's permissions allow: an INET login sees the most detail; with an Operations App login this endpoint is called without credentials (CXT lists only internet users and anonymous callers for it), which returns the limited public tracking view. Costs 1 API credit with the vendor. POST /v2/Shipments/Summaries.

tools.name: cxt_search_shipments
tools.title: Search orders and route stops
tools.description: Search orders and route stops by place, address, city, state, postal code, order template, or only by date range. tracking_type says which field search_criteria is matched against: Location (origin/destination or stop name), Address, City, State, Postal (zip or zip+4), Template (order template name), Tracking (references/barcodes) or DateOnly (no criteria: everything between begin_date and end_date). Returns shipment summaries, up to 1000 per page. An INET login sees the most detail; with an Operations App login this endpoint is called without credentials (CXT lists only internet users and anonymous callers for it), so the view is limited. Costs 1 API credit with the vendor. POST /v2/Shipments/Summaries.

tools.name: cxt_list_recent_orders
tools.title: List recent orders
tools.description: The most recent orders of the signed-in INTERNET user (user type INET; the orders of their account). Costs 1 API credit with the vendor. POST /v2/Shipments/Summaries with numRecentOrders.

tools.name: cxt_get_order
tools.title: Get order (internet user)
tools.description: One on-demand order with its status, confirmation, pickup, delivery and proof-of-delivery details, as an INTERNET user sees it (sign in with user type INET). Optionally with the itemized charges. Operations App users should use cxt_get_dispatch_order. Costs 1 API credit with the vendor. GET /v2/Orders/{orderId}/{includeItemizedCharges}.

tools.name: cxt_get_dispatch_order
tools.title: Get order (Operations App user)
tools.description: One on-demand order with itemized charges, as an OPERATIONS APP (X Dispatch) user sees it (sign in with user type XDISPATCH): addresses, times, driver, status events, proof of delivery. Costs 1 API credit with the vendor. GET /v2/Dispatch/Orders/{onDemandOrderId}.

tools.name: cxt_get_planning_limits
tools.title: Get itinerary planning limits
tools.description: The itinerary planning limits of this X Dispatch system: maxAllowedStops (shipments x 2), maxAllowedLocations and maxAllowedPlaceholders. Needs an Operations App user with the ITINERARY_PLANNING_ACCESS permission. GET /v3/ItineraryPlanning/Settings.

tools.name: cxt_validate_drivers
tools.title: Validate drivers for planning
tools.description: Check whether drivers are available to be planned: for each driver id, vehicle violations (for example an expired inspection) and HR violations (for example not scheduled), each with isBypassable. Changes nothing. Needs ITINERARY_PLANNING_ACCESS. POST /v3/ItineraryPlanning/Orders/Drivers/Validate.

tools.name: cxt_validate_driver_for_orders
tools.title: Validate a driver for orders
tools.description: Check one driver against specific orders: vehicle violations, HR violations and capability violations (for example Hazmat or Lift Gate that the driver lacks). Changes nothing. Needs ITINERARY_PLANNING_ACCESS. POST /v3/ItineraryPlanning/Orders/Drivers/{driverId}/Validate.

tools.name: cxt_plan_orders
tools.title: Plan orders onto drivers
tools.description: Generate a proposed itinerary that assigns on-demand orders to drivers (pickup and delivery stops in sequence, with times, distance and unassigned stops). This only PROPOSES a plan: nothing is dispatched until cxt_save_order_plan is called. Needs ITINERARY_PLANNING_ACCESS. Check the limits with cxt_get_planning_limits first. POST /v3/ItineraryPlanning/Orders.

tools.name: cxt_optimize_order_plan
tools.title: Re-optimize one driver's order plan
tools.description: Re-optimize a single driver's plan after manual changes (proposal only: nothing is dispatched until cxt_save_order_plan). Needs ITINERARY_PLANNING_ACCESS. POST /v3/ItineraryPlanning/Orders/Optimize.

tools.name: cxt_plan_routes
tools.title: Plan route stops
tools.description: Generate a proposed re-sequencing of the stops of existing routes for one route date (stops move between the output routes, with times, distance and unassigned stops). Proposal only: nothing changes until cxt_save_route_plan is called. Needs ITINERARY_PLANNING_ACCESS. POST /v3/ItineraryPlanning/Routes/{postDate}.

tools.name: cxt_optimize_route_plan
tools.title: Re-optimize one route
tools.description: Re-optimize a single route after manual changes (proposal only: nothing changes until cxt_save_route_plan). Needs ITINERARY_PLANNING_ACCESS. POST /v3/ItineraryPlanning/Routes/{postDate}/Optimize.

tools.name: cxt_save_order_plan
tools.title: Save order plan (dispatch orders to drivers)
tools.description: COMMIT an order plan: assigns the orders to the drivers and DISPATCHES them (drivers receive the work in the driver app; customers may be notified by the system's own status rules). Use only after the user has seen and approved the plan from cxt_plan_orders / cxt_optimize_order_plan. Pass each driver's stops from the plan reply: id, type (PICKUP or DELIVERY), sequence and from (the scheduled time). Response is empty on success (204). Needs ITINERARY_PLANNING_ACCESS. POST /v3/ItineraryPlanning/Orders/Save.

tools.name: cxt_save_route_plan
tools.title: Save route plan (reassign route stops)
tools.description: COMMIT a route plan for one route date: moves and re-sequences route stops as in the plan and DISPATCHES the changed routes to drivers. Use only after the user has seen and approved the plan from cxt_plan_routes / cxt_optimize_route_plan. Pass each route's stops from the plan reply: id, sequence and from (the scheduled time). Response is empty on success (204). Needs ITINERARY_PLANNING_ACCESS. POST /v3/ItineraryPlanning/Routes/{postDate}/Save.

tools.name: cxt_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the CXT Software (X Dispatch) tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: cxt_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on CXT Software (X Dispatch) (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: cxt_cancel_subscription

tools.description: Cancel the caller's CXT Software (X Dispatch) Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). examples: Track shipment ABC123 and tell me when it was picked up and delivered.
Show all orders for postal code 10001 between October 1 and October 7.
Validate drivers 101, 102 and 103 for planning and tell me who is unavailable.
Plan orders 900001 to 900010 onto drivers 101 and 102 for today, 8am to 6pm, and show me the proposal.

servers.name: Device Magic
servers.description: Read Device Magic forms, submissions, devices and groups; send and revoke dispatches.

login.hint: Find the token in Device Magic under **Account Settings → API Access** (resetting it creates a new one). The organization id is the number in your dashboard URL (app.devicemagic.com/organizations/**12345**/...). Dispatching needs the Enterprise plan. Your token is used only to call the Device Magic API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: devicemagic_list_forms
tools.title: List forms
tools.description: List the organization's forms: id, namespace (the form's unique id used for dispatching), version, description and group. GET /organizations/{org}/forms.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_get_form
tools.title: Get form definition
tools.description: One form's definition: title and its questions/pages with identifiers and types (the identifiers are the keys inside submissions and dispatch payloads). Optionally a specific version. GET /organizations/{org}/forms/{id}.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_list_submissions
tools.title: List form submissions
tools.description: Submitted data of one form, newest data as stored in the form's Device Magic Database destination (it must be active on that form). Each record has form info, metadata (device, user, submitted_at, received_at, submission_id) and the answers. The reply says current_page, total_pages and total_count. Filter by from_date/to_date (yyyy-mm-dd). GET /api/forms/{id}/device_magic_database.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_list_devices
tools.title: List devices
tools.description: List the organization's devices (phones, tablets, web-form users): id, identifier, owner, description, group and whether approval is pending. GET /organizations/{org}/devices.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_get_device
tools.title: Get device
tools.description: One device: id, identifier, owner, description, pending_approval, groups and custom attributes. GET /organizations/{org}/devices/{id}.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_list_groups
tools.title: List groups
tools.description: List the organization's groups (which devices see which forms), optionally narrowed by a name filter or by tags. GET /api/v2/organizations/{org}/groups.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_list_resources
tools.title: List resources
tools.description: List the organization's resources (lookup tables and files used by forms): id, original filename, version, description. GET /api/resources.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_describe_resource
tools.title: Describe resource
tools.description: Metadata of one resource: status, version and, for spreadsheets, its tables and columns. The file content itself is not downloaded. GET /api/resources/{id}/describe.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_list_destinations
tools.title: List form destinations
tools.description: List where one form's submissions are sent (e-mail, Dropbox, database, ...): id, active flag, format and transport types, timestamps. GET /api/forms/{id}/destinations.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_get_destination
tools.title: Get form destination
tools.description: One destination of a form. Credentials and tokens of the destination are never returned. GET /api/forms/{form_id}/destinations/{id}.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_list_dispatches
tools.title: List outstanding dispatches
tools.description: Outstanding dispatches (prefilled forms pushed to devices and not yet completed) of the whole organization: id, form name and namespace, device, scheduled time. Dispatch is an Enterprise-plan feature. GET /api/v2/organizations/{org}/dispatches.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_list_device_dispatches
tools.title: List a device's outstanding dispatches
tools.description: Outstanding dispatches of one device. GET /api/v2/devices/{identifier}/dispatches.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_get_dispatch
tools.title: Get dispatch with prefilled values
tools.description: One dispatch of a device including the values it was prefilled with. GET /api/v3/devices/{identifier}/dispatches/{id}.json?include_inputs=true.

tools.name: devicemagic_list_dispatch_recipients
tools.title: List dispatch recipients
tools.description: Devices and web-forms users a dispatch can be sent to (first 100 by default; use items and page for more). GET /api/v3/dispatch_authors.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_send_dispatch
tools.title: Send a form to a device (dispatch)
tools.description: WRITE: pushes a form, optionally prefilled, to one device where its user will see it (like assigning a job). Not idempotent: calling it twice sends two dispatches. Needs the Enterprise plan. The form is named by its namespace (list_forms); `payload` maps question identifiers (get_form) to prefilled values (subforms = nested objects, repeat groups = arrays). POST /api/v2/devices/{identifier}/dispatches.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_revoke_dispatch
tools.title: Revoke a dispatch
tools.description: WRITE: withdraws one outstanding dispatch from a device (the form disappears from the device). It cannot be undone, but the dispatch can be sent again. DELETE /api/v2/devices/{identifier}/dispatches/{id}.json.

tools.name: devicemagic_approve_device
tools.title: Approve a pending device
tools.description: WRITE: approves a device that is waiting for approval (pending_approval is true) so it can receive forms. Approving an approved device has no effect. POST /organizations/{org}/devices/{id}/approve.

tools.name: devicemagic_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: devicemagic_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Device Magic tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: devicemagic_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Device Magic (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: devicemagic_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Device Magic Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run devicemagic_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: List my forms and show the submissions of the Site Inspection form from last week.
Which devices are waiting for approval?
Show the outstanding dispatches for the whole team.
Send the Safety Check form to Anna's tablet, prefilled with site 'Warehouse 3'.

servers.name: Enginemailer
servers.description: Read Enginemailer subscribers, lists and campaigns; add subscribers, create and send campaigns.

login.hint: In Enginemailer open **Manage account → API Keys** and copy a key (you can create a separate key for this connection and revoke it any time). The key acts on your whole account, including sending email, so use it only with an assistant you trust. The Campaign tools need a paid Enginemailer plan. Your key is used only to call the Enginemailer API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: enginemailer_get_subscriber
tools.title: Get subscriber
tools.description: One subscriber by email: id, status and all custom field values. GET /restapi/subscriber/emsubscriber/getSubscriber.

tools.name: enginemailer_list_subscriber_categories
tools.title: List subscriber categories
tools.description: The subscriber category tree: each category with its subcategories (ids, names). Use the subcategory ids when adding or updating subscribers and when assigning campaign recipients. GET /restapi/subscriber/emsubscriber/getSubCategory.

tools.name: enginemailer_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List custom fields
tools.description: The subscriber custom field definitions (key, name, type). Use the keys when adding or updating subscribers. GET /restapi/subscriber/emsubscriber/getCustomField.

tools.name: enginemailer_add_subscriber
tools.title: Add subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: add a subscriber to the account (optionally into subcategories, with custom field values). Only add people who consented to marketing email. Free accounts may insert 50 subscribers a day, paid accounts 10,000. POST /restapi/subscriber/emsubscriber/insertSubscriber.

tools.name: enginemailer_update_subscriber
tools.title: Update subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing subscriber's subcategories and/or custom fields. subcategories_mode: append (default), remove (drop the given subcategories) or replace (the given list becomes the full list). custom_fields_mode: update_given (change only the given fields) or replace_all (default; fields not given are cleared). POST /restapi/subscriber/emsubscriber/updateSubscriber.

tools.name: enginemailer_unsubscribe_subscriber
tools.title: Unsubscribe subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: unsubscribe a subscriber so they no longer receive campaigns. Reversing it needs the subscriber to opt in again in Enginemailer. GET /restapi/subscriber/emsubscriber/unSubSubscriber.

tools.name: enginemailer_save_subscriber_category
tools.title: Create or update subscriber category
tools.description: WRITE: create a subscriber category (category_id 0) or update one (its id), with subcategories (subcategory_id 0 creates one). Names and descriptions max 128 characters. POST /restapi/subscriber/emsubscriber/updateCategory.

tools.name: enginemailer_list_campaigns
tools.title: List undelivered campaigns
tools.description: List campaigns that have NOT been delivered yet (drafts and scheduled ones): id, name, subject, sender and schedule. Delivered campaigns are not listed by the API; use enginemailer_get_campaign_stats with a known id. Needs a paid account. GET /restapi/campaign/emcampaign/ListCampaign.

tools.name: enginemailer_get_campaign_stats
tools.title: Get campaign delivery stats
tools.description: Delivery results of a DELIVERED campaign: emails sent, delivered, bounces, opens, unique opens, clicks, unique clicks, unsubscribes, spam complaints. Needs a paid account. GET /restapi/campaign/emcampaign/getcampaigndeliverystatus.

tools.name: enginemailer_list_campaign_categories
tools.title: List campaign categories
tools.description: The categories that campaign recipients can be filtered by (id, name, description). Needs a paid account. GET /restapi/campaign/emcampaign/GetCategoryList.

tools.name: enginemailer_list_campaign_subcategories
tools.title: List campaign subcategories
tools.description: The subcategories of one campaign category (id, name, description); use these ids in enginemailer_assign_campaign_recipients. Needs a paid account. GET /restapi/campaign/emcampaign/GetSubCategoryList.

tools.name: enginemailer_create_campaign
tools.title: Create campaign (draft)
tools.description: WRITE: create a campaign DRAFT. Nothing is sent: assign recipients with enginemailer_assign_campaign_recipients, then send with enginemailer_send_campaign. The sender domain must be verified in Enginemailer; max 200 campaigns per account. Needs a paid account. POST /restapi/Campaign/EMCampaign/CreateCampaign.

tools.name: enginemailer_assign_campaign_recipients
tools.title: Assign campaign recipients
tools.description: WRITE: set who a campaign will go to: all subscribers, or the subscribers in the given subcategory ids (match_type any = OR, all = AND). Does not send anything. Needs a paid account. POST /restapi/campaign/emcampaign/AssignRecipientList.

tools.name: enginemailer_send_campaign
tools.title: Send campaign NOW
tools.description: WRITE, SENDS EMAIL TO CUSTOMERS NOW and cannot be undone: delivers the campaign to its assigned recipients immediately. The campaign needs at least one recipient and must not be scheduled or already delivered. Show the user the campaign and its audience and get their go-ahead first; set confirm to true only then. Needs a paid account. GET /restapi/campaign/emcampaign/SendCampaign.

tools.name: enginemailer_send_transactional_email
tools.title: Send transactional email
tools.description: WRITE, SENDS ONE EMAIL NOW and cannot be undone: submits a transactional email to one recipient (plus optional CC/BCC). Needs a sender address on a verified domain; give either subject + content_html, or a template_id from the Enginemailer portal (the template supplies subject and sender name). Total message incl. attachments max 5 MB. Confirm the recipient and text with the user first; set confirm to true only then. POST /RESTAPI/V2/Submission/SendEmail.

tools.name: enginemailer_start_transactional_report_export
tools.title: Start transactional report export
tools.description: Start a CSV export of the transactional email delivery report for a period (start date at most 60 days back). Returns an export id; poll it with enginemailer_check_transactional_report_export. Creates a report file only; nothing is sent. POST /RESTAPI/V2/Submission/Report/Export.

tools.name: enginemailer_check_transactional_report_export
tools.title: Check transactional report export
tools.description: Status of a report export (Processing or Complete); when complete it includes the CSV download URL. POST /RESTAPI/V2/Submission/Report/CheckExport (read-only).

tools.name: enginemailer_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: enginemailer_request_feature

tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Enginemailer tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Enginemailer (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: enginemailer_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Enginemailer Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run enginemailer_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Look up the subscriber jane@example.com and show her custom fields and lists.
Add john@example.com to my Newsletter list with the source 'Signup from website'.
How did my last delivered campaign perform: opens, clicks, bounces?
Export the transactional email report for the last 30 days and give me the download link.

servers.name: Eventee
servers.description: Read an Eventee event's program, participants and reviews; create sessions, speakers; invite.

login.hint: Find it in the Eventee admin, in the **settings of the event** (API access is part of selected plans). Every event has its own token, so connect one event at a time; generating a new token invalidates the old one. The token can read and change that event: it is used only to call the Eventee API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: eventee_get_program
tools.title: Get event program
tools.description: The whole program of the event the API token belongs to: halls, event days, sessions (`lectures`, type 0), workshops (type 1, with capacity and bookings), breaks (`pauses`), speakers and labels (`tracks`). Use it to read back ids (hall_id, speaker ids, label ids, session ids) before changing anything. Replies are compact: long texts are clipped (description_max), each part is paged (limit/offset, `more` maps each part with further rows to the offset to continue from; the reply is cut to a size budget, so for big events read one part at a time with `parts`) and `parts` selects what to read. Times are in the event's time zone. GET /public/api/v1/content.

tools.name: eventee_list_participants
tools.title: List participants
tools.description: Participants of the event (attendees, speakers, moderators, admins) with role, group, tickets, check-in time and registration time. `role`: a = admin, m = moderator, l = speaker, e = attendee. `checked_at` is null until checked in. Anonymous participants and deleted accounts have a placeholder email without '@'. The personal app link of each participant is not returned. Filters apply after the full list is read; use limit/offset for large events. GET /public/api/v1/participants.

tools.name: eventee_list_registrations
tools.title: List registrations
tools.description: Registrations of the event (people who registered or were pre-registered) with status (pending / confirmed / declined), group, contact details and registration-form answers. Filters apply after the full list is read; use limit/offset for large events. GET /public/api/v1/registrations.

tools.name: eventee_list_groups
tools.title: List attendee groups
tools.description: Attendee groups of the event with the app features enabled for each (agenda, questions, polling, networking, ratings, ...), the ticket names that put people into the group automatically, and which group is the default. Use the ids as group_id when inviting or registering people. GET /public/api/v1/groups.

tools.name: eventee_list_reviews
tools.title: List session reviews
tools.description: Session ratings left by attendees (1-5 stars with optional comment), each with the rated session, plus a per-session summary (count and average stars; the 50 most reviewed sessions, `summary_truncated` says if more exist: use session_id for a specific one). Filters apply after the full list is read. GET /public/api/v1/reviews.

tools.name: eventee_list_partners
tools.title: List partners
tools.description: Partners (sponsors and exhibitors) of the event with company details, contact data, code and page sections. GET /public/api/v1/partners.

tools.name: eventee_create_session
tools.title: Create session
tools.description: WRITE: add a session (lecture or workshop) to the event program. It appears in the event app for attendees. The event day is taken from `start` and created if missing. The hall, speakers and labels must already exist (create them first and pass their ids). POST /public/api/v1/lecture.

tools.name: eventee_update_session
tools.title: Update session
tools.description: WRITE: replace a session (full update, not a patch). Eventee RESETS what is omitted: speakers, labels, type, capacity and the Q&A / moderation / polling switches, so `type`, `speaker_ids`, `label_ids`, `capacity`, `discussion`, `moderating` and `polling` are required here; read the session first with eventee_get_program and pass its current values (an empty list removes all). The hall and live stream are kept when omitted. `start` must fall on an existing day of the event. PATCH /public/api/v1/lecture/{session_id}.

tools.name: eventee_delete_session
tools.title: Delete session
tools.description: WRITE, IRREVERSIBLE: delete a session (lecture or workshop) together with its questions, polls, workshop bookings and ratings. Needs confirm: true (without it: a preview, nothing deleted). DELETE /public/api/v1/lecture/{session_id}.

tools.name: eventee_create_hall
tools.title: Create hall
tools.description: WRITE: add a hall (room, stage or virtual space) to the event. Use the returned id as hall_id for sessions. POST /public/api/v1/hall.

tools.name: eventee_create_break
tools.title: Create break
tools.description: WRITE: add a break (coffee, lunch...) to the event program on the day of `start` (created if missing). POST /public/api/v1/pause.

tools.name: eventee_create_label
tools.title: Create label
tools.description: WRITE: add a label (track) for sessions, with a colour. Use the returned id in label_ids of a session. POST /public/api/v1/label.

tools.name: eventee_create_speaker
tools.title: Create speaker
tools.description: WRITE: add a speaker profile to the event (shown in the event app). Use the returned id in speaker_ids of a session. The photo, if given, is downloaded by Eventee from the URL. POST /public/api/v1/speaker.

tools.name: eventee_invite_attendees
tools.title: Invite attendees
tools.description: WRITE: add up to 100 people to the event as attendees, optionally with a group and tickets. People who already have an Eventee account are added directly; others get a profile that links when they sign up with the same email. With send_email=true Eventee SENDS AN INVITATION EMAIL to every person listed (default false: no email); sending needs confirm: true (without it: a preview, nothing sent or added). Invalid entries and the event's admins/moderators are skipped silently by Eventee, so re-read eventee_list_participants to confirm. The first 25 are processed immediately, the rest in the background. Tickets replace the person's existing tickets. PUT /public/api/v1/attendee/invite.

tools.name: eventee_register_people
tools.title: Pre-register people
tools.description: WRITE: pre-register up to 100 people for the event (an existing registration with the same email is updated, not duplicated). With send_email=true Eventee SENDS A REGISTRATION EMAIL to every person listed (default false: no email); sending needs confirm: true (without it: a preview, nothing sent or registered). Invalid entries are skipped silently by Eventee, so re-read eventee_list_registrations to confirm. PUT /public/api/v1/registration/invite.

tools.name: eventee_check_in_attendee
tools.title: Check in attendee
tools.description: WRITE: check a participant in at the event (sets checked_at to now) or undo the check-in. Use the participant `id` from eventee_list_participants. Fails if the person is not a participant of the event. PATCH /public/api/v1/attendee/{attendee_id}/checkin.

tools.name: eventee_remove_attendee
tools.title: Remove attendee
tools.description: WRITE, IRREVERSIBLE: remove the person with this email from the event: their participation, invitation and tickets for this event are deleted (their Eventee account is not). Eventee reports success even when nobody had that email. Needs confirm: true (without it: a preview, nothing removed). DELETE /public/api/v1/attendee?email=.

tools.name: eventee_remove_registration
tools.title: Remove registration
tools.description: WRITE, IRREVERSIBLE: delete the registration with this email. Eventee reports success even when no such registration exists. Needs confirm: true (without it: a preview, nothing deleted). DELETE /public/api/v1/registration?email=.

tools.name: eventee_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: eventee_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Eventee tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: eventee_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Eventee (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: eventee_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Eventee Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run eventee_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Show me the program for the second day of the conference.
Which sessions got the best ratings, and what did people comment on the lowest-rated ones?
Who has registered but is still pending, and who has not checked in yet?
Add a workshop on Friday 14:00-15:30 in the Main Hall with 30 seats.

servers.name: GivingFuel
servers.description: Read GivingFuel forms, donations, transactions, recurring gifts and donors; manage coupons.

login.hint: Create it in your GivingFuel dashboard under **Account settings → Integrations**. The key gives access to your whole account's data (donor names, emails and addresses included), so only connect an AI assistant you trust. Your key is used only to call the GivingFuel API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: givingfuel_list_forms
tools.title: List donation forms
tools.description: List the account's GivingFuel forms (donation / fundraising pages): id, name, status (open or closed), created and updated dates. Use the form ids to filter orders, transactions and subscriptions. GET /forms.

tools.name: givingfuel_get_form
tools.title: Get donation form
tools.description: One form by id: name, status, accounting reference, time zone and its field layout. GET /forms/{id}.

tools.name: givingfuel_get_form_inventory
tools.title: Get form inventory
tools.description: Inventory items of a form (limited-quantity items): path, name, sold and remaining quantity. GET /forms/{id}/inventory.

tools.name: givingfuel_list_orders
tools.title: List donation orders
tools.description: List donation orders (one per checkout): order number, donor billing name and address, form, total, currency and status, newest or oldest first. Filter by form, status, donor email, customer id, order number or dates. GET /search/orders.

tools.name: givingfuel_get_order
tools.title: Get donation order
tools.description: One order by id with the donor's billing details, form, totals and status. Set include_transactions to embed the payments (charges and refunds) of the order. GET /search/orders/{id}.

tools.name: givingfuel_list_transactions
tools.title: List transactions
tools.description: List payment transactions (money movements): amount, deductible amount, currency, type (charge, refund, voucher), payment method, masked card, status, form and donor email. Filter by type, method, form, order, donor or dates. GET /search/transactions.

tools.name: givingfuel_get_transaction
tools.title: Get transaction
tools.description: One transaction by id: amounts, type, payment method, masked card, gateway message and status. GET /search/transactions/{id}.

tools.name: givingfuel_list_subscriptions
tools.title: List recurring gifts
tools.description: List recurring donations (subscriptions): amount, schedule, status, last and next payment date, payments remaining, form and donor email. Filter by form, status, donor, or next/last payment date. GET /search/subscriptions.

tools.name: givingfuel_get_subscription
tools.title: Get recurring gift
tools.description: One recurring donation by id: amount, schedule, status, last and next payment, payments remaining. GET /search/subscriptions/{id}.

tools.name: givingfuel_list_customers
tools.title: List donors
tools.description: List customer records (donors): id, email, billing name and address, lifetime amount, created and updated dates. Filter by email or dates. New donors can take up to 5 minutes to appear. GET /search/customers.

tools.name: givingfuel_get_customer
tools.title: Get donor
tools.description: One donor (customer record) by id: email, billing details and total amount. GET /search/customers/{id}.

tools.name: givingfuel_list_coupons
tools.title: List coupons
tools.description: List GivingFuel coupons: account-wide ones, or only those of one form when form_id is given. Shows discounts, codes, availability, redeemed count and expiry. GET /coupons/global or /coupons/forms/{id}.

tools.name: givingfuel_get_coupon
tools.title: Get coupon

tools.name: givingfuel_create_coupon

tools.description: WRITE: create a discount coupon in the live GivingFuel account (it can be redeemed by donors right away). One discount (fixed amount or percent) and one or more codes; optionally limited to one form, to a number of uses, and to an expiry date. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two coupons. POST /coupons.

tools.name: givingfuel_delete_coupon

tools.description: WRITE: permanently delete a coupon from the live GivingFuel account; its codes stop working immediately and this cannot be undone. Show the coupon (givingfuel_get_coupon) and get the user's approval first, then call with confirm: true. GET /coupons/{id}, then DELETE /coupons/{id}.

Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: Lalamove
servers.description: Read Lalamove cities, vehicles, quotations and orders; quote, place, tip and cancel deliveries.

login.hint: Find them in the **Lalamove Partner Portal** (partnerportal.lalamove.com) under the **Developers** tab; switch the environment at the top right to see the sandbox or the production pair. Production keys (pk_prod / sk_prod) need a topped-up wallet. Choose the market the keys were issued for. Your secret is used only to sign requests to the Lalamove API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: lalamove_list_cities
tools.title: List cities, vehicles and special requests
tools.description: The cities of the connected market with the vehicle types (serviceType keys such as MOTORCYCLE or CAR), their size and load, and the special requests each vehicle accepts. Use these exact keys in lalamove_create_quotation. GET /v3/cities.

tools.name: lalamove_get_quotation
tools.title: Get quotation
tools.description: A quotation by id: stops (with stopId), vehicle, price breakdown, currency, distance and expiresAt (a quotation can be ordered for 5 minutes). GET /v3/quotations/{quotationId}.

tools.name: lalamove_get_order
tools.title: Get order
tools.description: One delivery order: status (ASSIGNING_DRIVER, ON_GOING, PICKED_UP, COMPLETED, CANCELED, REJECTED, EXPIRED), price breakdown, driver id, share link, distance, stops with proof of delivery and metadata. Only orders from the last 60 days can be read. GET /v3/orders/{orderId}.

tools.name: lalamove_get_driver
tools.title: Get driver and location
tools.description: The driver of an order: name, phone, masked plate number, photo and last known coordinates (updated about every 10 seconds). Lalamove only shares this from 1 hour before the scheduled pickup (or the driver's arrival, whichever is earlier) until the order is completed; outside that window it answers 403. GET /v3/orders/{orderId}/drivers/{driverId}.

tools.name: lalamove_track_order
tools.title: Track order
tools.description: Where is my delivery: the order status, stop-level proof of delivery and share link, plus (when a driver has the order and it is on its way) the driver's name and live coordinates. Two reads: GET /v3/orders/{orderId} and, if a driver is assigned and the order is ON_GOING or PICKED_UP, GET /v3/orders/{orderId}/drivers/{driverId}.

tools.name: lalamove_create_quotation
tools.title: Get a delivery quotation
tools.description: Price a delivery: 2-16 stops (the first is the pickup, the rest are drop-offs), a vehicle type and optional extras. Returns quotationId, per-stop stopId, the price breakdown and currency, distance and expiresAt (about 5 minutes). It creates a quotation only: nothing is ordered and nothing is charged. Get the vehicle keys from lalamove_list_cities. Show the price to the user before placing an order. POST /v3/quotations.

tools.name: lalamove_place_order
tools.title: Place delivery order (charges the wallet)
tools.description: WRITE, SPENDS MONEY: order a delivery from a quotation. In production the total price is charged to the prepaid Lalamove wallet and a driver is dispatched; cancellation is only free within Lalamove's policy. Only call it after the user has seen the quotation price and said yes. confirm_total must equal the quotation total (it is checked against Lalamove, and an expired quotation is refused). The recipients are given in stop order and matched to the quotation's drop-off stops by the tool. The order is placed once: do not retry after an error without checking lalamove_get_order. POST /v3/orders.

tools.name: lalamove_add_priority_fee
tools.title: Add priority fee (tip, charges the wallet)
tools.description: WRITE, SPENDS MONEY: add a priority fee (tip) to an order to attract a driver. Only possible before a driver accepts the order. The amount replaces the earlier fee and must be higher than it; the difference is charged to the wallet. Amount in the market's currency (see the order's priceBreakdown.currency). POST /v3/orders/{orderId}/priority-fee.

tools.name: lalamove_cancel_order
tools.title: Cancel order
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: cancel a delivery order. Lalamove only allows it while the order is ASSIGNING_DRIVER, or less than 5 minutes after a driver accepted it; otherwise it answers ERR_CANCELLATION_FORBIDDEN. A cancelled order cannot be revived, only re-placed from a new quotation. DELETE /v3/orders/{orderId}.

tools.name: lalamove_change_driver
tools.title: Change driver
tools.description: WRITE: ask Lalamove to replace the driver of an order (no extra fee). Allowed 15 minutes after the driver was matched and before pickup; the order goes back to ASSIGNING_DRIVER and a new driver is looked for. Needs the current driver id from lalamove_get_order. DELETE /v3/orders/{orderId}/drivers/{driverId}.

tools.name: lalamove_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lalamove_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Lalamove tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lalamove_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Lalamove (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: lalamove_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Lalamove Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run lalamove_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: How much would a motorcycle delivery from our shop in Kowloon Tong to Central cost right now?
Where is order 107900701184 and which driver has it?
Which vehicle types does Lalamove offer in Bangkok?
Place the delivery with that quotation (the price is fine) and add a 20 priority fee if no driver accepts it.

servers.name: HotelRunner
servers.description: Read HotelRunner reservations, rooms, channels; update availability and prices; confirm or cancel.

login.hint: In the HotelRunner property panel open **My Property** and create an app key (HotelRunner Apps); the page shows the **HR_ID** (your property id) and the **TOKEN**. HotelRunner limits each property to 250 API requests a day and 5 a minute, so ask for what you need rather than browsing. Your credentials are used only to call the HotelRunner API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: hotelrunner_list_rooms
tools.title: List rooms and rates
tools.description: List the property's room types and rates with their inv_code and rate_code, capacity, pricing type, sales currency, connected channel codes and whether availability, restrictions and prices can be updated through the API. Use the inv_code with hotelrunner_update_room_calendar. Counts as one of the property's 250 requests per day (5 per minute). GET /api/v2/apps/rooms.

tools.name: hotelrunner_list_reservations
tools.title: List reservations
tools.description: List reservations of the property (new, modified, canceled), newest data first as HotelRunner returns them, 1-50 per page. By default ALL reservations created in the window are returned (this tool sets undelivered=false, so reading does not depend on a PMS having fetched them). from_date is the creation date (HotelRunner keeps at most 30 days back; default 10 days); from_last_update_date finds reservations changed since a date. detail 'summary' (default) gives guest, dates, rooms, totals, payment state and contact; 'full' returns the whole vendor record including billing address, national id, daily prices and extras. Reply: items, count, page, pages, next_page. Counts as one of the property's 250 requests per day (5 per minute). GET /api/v2/apps/reservations.

tools.name: hotelrunner_get_reservation
tools.title: Get reservation
tools.description: One reservation by its HotelRunner code (hr_number, e.g. R377873409) or the sales channel's own reservation code, with the full vendor record (rooms, daily prices, extras, payments, guest and billing details, next_states). If the reservation is older than HotelRunner's lookup window, pass from_date. Counts as one of the property's 250 requests per day (5 per minute). GET /api/v2/apps/reservations?reservation_number=.

tools.name: hotelrunner_list_channels
tools.title: List sales channels
tools.description: All sales channels HotelRunner supports (name and code, e.g. bookingcom, expedia, hrs, online). The code is what hotelrunner_update_room_calendar takes in channel_codes. Counts as one of the property's 250 requests per day (5 per minute). GET /api/v2/apps/infos/channels.

tools.name: hotelrunner_list_connected_channels
tools.title: List connected channels
tools.description: The channels this property is connected to, each with counts of calendar update processes in progress, succeeded and failed. Counts as one of the property's 250 requests per day (5 per minute). GET /api/v2/apps/infos/connected_channels.

tools.name: hotelrunner_get_transaction_details
tools.title: Get calendar update status
tools.description: Per-channel status of a calendar update: pass the transaction_id returned by hotelrunner_update_room_calendar. Shows succeeded / failed / in-progress counts and each channel's state and error message. Counts as one of the property's 250 requests per day (5 per minute). GET /api/v2/apps/infos/transaction_details.

tools.name: hotelrunner_update_room_calendar
tools.title: Update room availability, prices and restrictions
tools.description: WRITE: change availability, price, minimum/maximum stay, stop-sale, closed-to-arrival (cta) or closed-to-departure (ctd) for ONE room type (inv_code) over a date range of at most 90 days, optionally only on some weekdays and only on some channels. Only the fields you pass are changed. This is LIVE inventory: HotelRunner pushes it to every connected channel (Booking.com, Expedia, your own booking engine, ...) and it changes what guests can book and pay. The price is the base-rate price in the property's sales currency; guest-based prices derive from it. Only rooms whose availability_update / restrictions_update / price_update flag is true (hotelrunner_list_rooms) accept that kind of change. HotelRunner answers asynchronously: the reply has a transaction_id; check per-channel results with hotelrunner_get_transaction_details. Send one change per call, not a full refresh. Counts as one of the property's 250 requests per day (5 per minute). PUT /api/v2/apps/rooms/daily.

tools.name: hotelrunner_update_reservation_state
tools.title: Confirm or cancel a reservation
tools.description: WRITE: move ONE reservation to the next state: event 'confirm' (hotelier accepts it) or 'cancel' (cancels it; cancel_reason is required: customer, no_room, no_show or invalid_price). Cancel is not reversible through this API and releases the room; HotelRunner may notify the guest or the sales channel (Booking.com, Expedia, ...), so only cancel when the user clearly asked for it, and pass confirm=true for a cancel. Only possible when the reservation's requires_response is true and the event is in its next_states (see hotelrunner_get_reservation); otherwise HotelRunner answers state_change_is_not_available. Counts as one of the property's 250 requests per day (5 per minute). PUT /api/v2/apps/reservations/fire.

tools.name: hotelrunner_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: hotelrunner_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the HotelRunner tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: hotelrunner_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on HotelRunner (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: hotelrunner_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's HotelRunner Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run hotelrunner_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

Show reservation R377873409 with its payments and guest note.
