Set the price of Family Room to 140 for every weekend in November.

servers.name: Jet HR
servers.description: Read Jet HR employees, absences, clockings, payroll; create, approve, delete leave; create expenses.

login.hint: A Jet HR admin creates the token in Jet HR under **Company Settings (Impostazioni azienda) → API → + Nuova**. Choose Accessible resources: All (or pick the resources you want to use; read-only is fine for reports), then copy the token (it starts with `T_` and is shown only once). Your token is used only to call the Jet HR API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: jethr_list_employees
tools.title: List employees
tools.description: List the company's employees with the full record: name, fiscal code, work and personal email, job title and level, contract kind and dates, annual gross salary (RAL), manager, headquarters and custom fields. Contains personal data; for a lighter list use jethr_list_employee_overviews. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/employees/.

tools.name: jethr_get_employee
tools.title: Get an employee
tools.description: One employee's full record (contract, salary, manager, headquarters, custom fields). GET /public-api/v1/employees/{uuid}/.

tools.name: jethr_list_employee_overviews
tools.title: List employees (overview)
tools.description: List employees with the lighter overview record: name, fiscal code, work email, job title, contract dates, probation end, manager, headquarters and custom fields (no salary or personal contact data). Needs only the employee_overview:read scope. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/employee-overviews/.

tools.name: jethr_get_employee_overview
tools.title: Get an employee (overview)
tools.description: One employee's overview record (job title, contract dates, manager, headquarters, custom fields). GET /public-api/v1/employee-overviews/{uuid}/.

tools.name: jethr_list_terminations
tools.title: List terminations
tools.description: List employee terminations (resignations and dismissals recorded in Jet HR). Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/terminations/.

tools.name: jethr_list_hirings
tools.title: List hirings
tools.description: List hiring processes (drafts and onboarding in progress), optionally by status (for example INCOMPLETE or COMPLETED). Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/hirings/.

tools.name: jethr_get_hiring
tools.title: Get a hiring
tools.description: One hiring process with its status and data. GET /public-api/v1/hirings/{uuid}/.

tools.name: jethr_list_contractors
tools.title: List contractors
tools.description: List external contractors (collaborators) and their collaborations, optionally filtered by contractor, linked employee or a collaboration date window. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/contractors/.

tools.name: jethr_get_contractor
tools.title: Get a contractor
tools.description: One contractor with their collaborations. GET /public-api/v1/contractors/{uuid}/.

tools.name: jethr_list_absence_requests
tools.title: List presence and absence requests
tools.description: List leave, sickness, remote-work and other presence/absence requests with status (APPROVED, REJECTED, PENDING), kind, dates, hours, note and approver. Filters combine with AND. Use status filtering on the result for pending requests. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/presence-absence-requests/.

tools.name: jethr_list_absence_policies
tools.title: List absence policies
tools.description: List the company's absence policies with their active request kinds (codename, name, approval and attachment rules) and the employees assigned to each. The codename is what jethr_create_absence_request needs. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/company-absence-policies/.

tools.name: jethr_get_absence_request_kind
tools.title: Get an absence request kind
tools.description: One absence request kind setting: codename, whether it needs approval or a note, whether it can be requested in hours or days, duration limits. GET /public-api/v1/company-absence-request-kinds/{uuid}/.

tools.name: jethr_list_clockings
tools.title: List clockings
tools.description: List time-clock events (in, out, work and break start/end, overtime) with employee, timestamp, method (web, mobile, badge, QR code), workplace and location. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/clockings/.

tools.name: jethr_list_payrolls
tools.title: List payrolls
tools.description: List the company's monthly payrolls (year and month, status and totals). Sensitive financial data. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/payrolls/.

tools.name: jethr_list_payslips
tools.title: List payslips
tools.description: List employee payslips, optionally for one employee, year or month. Sensitive payroll data. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/payslips/.

tools.name: jethr_list_bonuses
tools.title: List bonuses
tools.description: List payroll bonuses (employee, payroll month, amount, kind, note), optionally for one employee, year or month. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/bonuses/.

tools.name: jethr_list_bonus_kinds
tools.title: List bonus kinds
tools.description: List the bonus kinds (categories) the company can use in payroll. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/bonus-kinds/.

tools.name: jethr_list_fringe_benefits
tools.title: List fringe benefits
tools.description: List fringe benefits assigned in payroll (employee, payroll month, amount, kind), optionally for one employee, year or month. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/fringe-benefits/.

tools.name: jethr_list_fringe_benefit_kinds
tools.title: List fringe benefit kinds
tools.description: List the fringe benefit kinds (categories) available in payroll. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/fringe-benefit-kinds/.

tools.name: jethr_list_payslip_extra_deductions
tools.title: List payslip extra deductions
tools.description: List extra deductions applied to payslips (employee, payroll month, amount, kind), optionally for one employee, year or month. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/payslip-extra-deductions/.

tools.name: jethr_list_payslip_extra_deduction_kinds
tools.title: List payslip extra deduction kinds
tools.description: List the extra deduction kinds (categories) available on payslips. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/payslip-extra-deduction-kinds/.

tools.name: jethr_list_documents
tools.title: List documents
tools.description: List documents stored in Jet HR (payslips, contracts and other files): metadata per document, optionally by employee, kind name, payroll period or last-update window. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/documents/.

tools.name: jethr_list_expenses
tools.title: List expense reimbursement requests
tools.description: List expense reimbursement requests (employee, amount, currency, kind, description, payment date, receipts, status). Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/expenses/.

tools.name: jethr_list_expense_policies
tools.title: List expense policies
tools.description: List the company's expense policies (which expense kinds and limits apply to which employees). Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/company-expense-policies/.

tools.name: jethr_list_devices
tools.title: List devices
tools.description: List company devices (laptops, phones...) and the employee each is assigned to, optionally by employee or device uuid. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/devices/.

tools.name: jethr_get_device
tools.title: Get a device
tools.description: One company device with its assignment. GET /public-api/v1/devices/{uuid}/.

tools.name: jethr_list_company_headquarters
tools.title: List company headquarters
tools.description: List the company's headquarters (legal and operative sites), optionally by kind. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/company-headquarters/.

tools.name: jethr_list_company_ccnl
tools.title: List company CCNL
tools.description: List the national collective labour agreements (CCNL) the company applies. Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/company-ccnl/.

tools.name: jethr_list_trip_refund_policies
tools.title: List trip daily refund policies
tools.description: List the company's business-trip daily refund policies (needed as trip_name for trip absence requests). Paged: pass next_page as page. GET /public-api/v1/company-trip-daily-refund-policies/.

tools.name: jethr_create_absence_request
tools.title: Create a presence or absence request
tools.description: Create a leave, sickness, remote-work or other presence/absence request for an employee. WRITES to the company's HR records. codename is the request kind (from jethr_list_absence_policies); give start_date and end_date for day requests, or start_date + start_time + time_duration for hourly requests. send_notification=true makes Jet HR notify the people involved (approvers/employee) and needs confirm_notification=true; default false. Some kinds need extra fields (child data, trip data, sickness certificate): Jet HR answers with a validation error naming them. POST /public-api/v1/presence-absence-requests/.

tools.name: jethr_update_absence_request
tools.title: Update, approve or reject an absence request
tools.description: Change a presence/absence request: dates, hours, note, or its status (APPROVED, REJECTED, PENDING; give rejection_reason when rejecting). WRITES to the company's HR records; approving or rejecting is visible to the employee, and send_notification=true notifies the people involved (default false; needs confirm_notification=true). Only the fields you pass change. PATCH /public-api/v1/presence-absence-requests/{uuid}/.

tools.name: jethr_delete_absence_request
tools.title: Delete a presence or absence request
tools.description: Permanently delete a presence/absence request (it disappears from the employee's calendar and balance). Cannot be undone; needs confirm=true. DELETE /public-api/v1/presence-absence-requests/{uuid}/.

tools.name: jethr_create_expense
tools.title: Create an expense reimbursement request
tools.description: Create an expense reimbursement request for an employee (no receipt files; those are uploaded in Jet HR). WRITES to the company's records as a reimbursement request. amount is the EUR amount; amount_total is the amount in amount_total_currency (the same value for EUR). POST /public-api/v1/expenses/.

servers.name: kiwiHR
servers.description: Read kiwiHR employees, time off, timesheets, projects; create and update employees, timesheets.

login.hint: Create it in the Tellent HR (kiwiHR) web app under **Company Settings** (API key). The key acts as the first Administrator of your company, so it can read and change everything an admin can: share it only if you are happy for your AI assistant to have that access. It is used only to call the kiwiHR API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_users
tools.title: List employees
tools.description: List or search employees (kiwiHR 'users') with name, work email, active flag, employee number, employment dates, position, team, location and manager. Filter by active state, team, location, position, e-mail or name. Payroll, bank, tax and insurance data are never included. GraphQL query users.

tools.name: kiwihr_get_user
tools.title: Get employee
tools.description: One employee by id: the list fields plus probation end, about-me, language, invitation status, work phones, all teams, work schedule and custom field values. With include_personal=true it also returns birth date, private e-mail and phone, nationality, gender, pronouns, home address, emergency contact and custom fields of the personal sections. Payroll, bank (IBAN/BIC), tax and insurance data are never returned. GraphQL query user.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_teams
tools.title: List teams
tools.description: List teams and departments (id, name, kind GROUP or DEPARTMENT). Use the ids to filter employees. GraphQL query teams.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List office locations (id, name). Use the ids to filter employees. GraphQL query locations.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_positions
tools.title: List positions
tools.description: List job positions (id, name). Use the ids to filter employees. GraphQL query positions.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List custom fields
tools.description: List the company's custom employee profile fields (id, name, section, data type, choice options). Payroll and bank sections are listed by name only; their values are never returned by any tool. GraphQL query customFields.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_time_off_types
tools.title: List time off types
tools.description: List time off (absence) types such as vacation or sick leave: id, name, colour, visibility to team members. Use the ids with kiwihr_get_time_off_usage and kiwihr_list_time_off_balances. GraphQL query timeOffTypes.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_time_off_balances
tools.title: List time off balances
tools.description: Time off balances of all employees: per employee and time off rule the allowance, accrued, used, requested, planned and available days, carry-over and the accrual/usage periods. Filter by time off type, active state and usage period. The API has no per-employee filter or paging for this query; read the result per user. GraphQL query timeOffBalances.

tools.name: kiwihr_get_time_off_usage
tools.title: Get time off usage
tools.description: Who took (or requested) how much time off in a date range: per employee the request count and used days for each time off rule of the chosen time off types. Use it for absence reports ('who was off in March?'). Optional employee filters as in kiwihr_list_users. GraphQL query timeOffRequestUsageStatements.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_timesheets
tools.title: List timesheets
tools.description: Daily timesheets of one employee (or the key's admin user when user_id is omitted) in a date range: expected, tracked, time off, holiday and break time in SECONDS, approval flag, time offs, holidays, entries (start/end, type, note, project) and break-rule violations. GraphQL query timesheets.

tools.name: kiwihr_get_timesheet
tools.title: Get timesheet
tools.description: The timesheet of ONE employee for ONE day (user_id omitted = the admin user the key acts as), with all entries and their ids (needed to update or delete an entry). Times in seconds. GraphQL query timesheet.

tools.name: kiwihr_get_attendance_statement
tools.title: Get attendance statement
tools.description: Attendance summary of ONE employee over a date range: expected, tracked, total, time off and holiday time (seconds) and days, balance, overtime, meal vouchers, and tracked time per project. GraphQL query attendanceStatement.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_attendance_statements
tools.title: List attendance statements
tools.description: Attendance summaries of ALL employees over a date range (expected vs tracked time, time off, holidays, balance, overtime, tracked time per project). Optionally only employees with time tracked on a project, or with uncategorized time; inactive employees can be included. GraphQL query attendanceStatements.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_overtime_balances
tools.title: List overtime balances
tools.description: Current overtime balance (seconds) per employee. GraphQL query overtimeBalanceStatements.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List time-tracking projects (id, name, status ACTIVE or INACTIVE). GraphQL query projects.

tools.name: kiwihr_get_project
tools.title: Get project
tools.description: One time-tracking project by id (name, status). GraphQL query project.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_journeys
tools.title: List journeys
tools.description: List onboarding/offboarding journeys (id, name, status DRAFT/ONGOING/COMPLETED/CANCELLED, assignee, journey type, custom date). Filter by status, assignee, type or team. GraphQL query journeys.

tools.name: kiwihr_get_journey
tools.title: Get journey
tools.description: One journey by id with its steps (name, description, fixed start and due dates). With include_personal=true it also returns the private e-mail address stored on the journey. GraphQL query journey.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_journey_templates
tools.title: List journey templates
tools.description: List journey templates (id, name, description, type). Use a template id with kiwihr_create_journey. GraphQL query journeyTemplates.

tools.name: kiwihr_list_journey_types
tools.title: List journey types
tools.description: List journey types such as pre-onboarding, onboarding or offboarding (id, name, key, archived date). GraphQL query journeyTypes.

tools.name: kiwihr_create_timesheet_entry
tools.title: Create timesheet entry
tools.description: WRITE: add a time entry to the timesheet of one employee on one day (user_id omitted = the admin user the key acts as). type MANUAL = worked time (give start_at and end_at as HH:mm:ss, or a part_of_day), BREAK = a break. Optional project and note. Creates a new entry each call (not idempotent). Returns the updated day. GraphQL mutation createTimesheetEntry.

tools.name: kiwihr_update_timesheet_entry
tools.title: Update timesheet entry
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing timesheet entry (get its id from kiwihr_get_timesheet): times, part of day, project or note. Only the fields you pass are changed. Setting the same values again gives the same result. Returns the updated day. GraphQL mutation updateTimesheetEntry.

tools.name: kiwihr_delete_timesheet_entry
tools.title: Delete timesheet entry
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: permanently delete one timesheet entry by id (get it from kiwihr_get_timesheet). This cannot be undone. Returns true when deleted. GraphQL mutation deleteTimesheetEntry.

tools.name: kiwihr_create_project
tools.title: Create project
tools.description: WRITE: create a time-tracking project (name, status ACTIVE or INACTIVE; default ACTIVE). Creates a new project each call (not idempotent). GraphQL mutation createProject.

tools.name: kiwihr_update_project
tools.title: Update project
tools.description: WRITE: rename a project or switch it ACTIVE/INACTIVE (INACTIVE projects can no longer be used for time tracking). Only the fields you pass are changed. GraphQL mutation updateProject.

tools.name: kiwihr_create_user
tools.title: Create employee
tools.description: WRITE: add a new employee record (first name, last name and work e-mail are required; optional start date, manager, teams, position, location and phones). Creates a new employee each call (not idempotent). No invitation is sent by this tool. Payroll and bank data cannot be set. GraphQL mutation createUser.

tools.name: kiwihr_update_user
tools.title: Update employee
tools.description: WRITE: change an employee's work profile: name, start date, about-me, work phones, position, team(s), location, manager. Only the fields you pass are changed (team_ids replaces the whole team list). Private, payroll and bank data cannot be changed with this tool. GraphQL mutation updateUser.

tools.name: kiwihr_deactivate_user
tools.title: Deactivate employee
tools.description: WRITE, ACCESS-CHANGING: deactivate an active employee (typically after they leave): they lose access to kiwiHR and drop out of active lists. Reversible with kiwihr_activate_user. GraphQL mutation deactivateUser.

tools.name: kiwihr_activate_user
tools.title: Activate employee
tools.description: WRITE: re-activate a deactivated employee so they appear in active lists and can use kiwiHR again. GraphQL mutation activateUser.

tools.name: kiwihr_create_journey
tools.title: Create journey
tools.description: WRITE: create an onboarding/offboarding journey for an employee from a journey type and optionally a template (ids from kiwihr_list_journey_types / kiwihr_list_journey_templates). Creates a new journey each call (not idempotent). It does not publish it; check the status in the reply. GraphQL mutation createJourney.

tools.name: kiwihr_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: kiwihr_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the kiwiHR tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: kiwihr_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on kiwiHR (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: kiwihr_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's kiwiHR Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run kiwihr_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Who is off next week, and what time off do they have left?
List the active employees in the Sales team with their managers.
Show Anna Novak's timesheets for last week and add a missing 09:00-17:00 entry for Monday.
Start an onboarding journey for our new hire from the standard template.

servers.name: MoonClerk
servers.description: Read MoonClerk payment forms, customers (plans with subscriptions) and payments. Read-only.

login.hint: Get the key in MoonClerk under **Settings → API Key** ([app.moonclerk.com/settings/api-key](https://app.moonclerk.com/settings/api-key)). It gives read access to all customer and payment data of the account. Your key is used only to call the MoonClerk API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: moonclerk_list_forms
tools.title: List payment forms
tools.description: List the MoonClerk payment forms: id, title, currency, payment_volume (cents), successful_checkout_count and created/updated times. Use the form ids to filter customers (plans) and payments. Read-only. GET /forms.

tools.name: moonclerk_get_form
tools.title: Get payment form
tools.description: One payment form by id: title, currency, payment volume and checkout count. Read-only. GET /forms/{id}.

tools.name: moonclerk_list_customers
tools.title: List customers (plans)
tools.description: List MoonClerk customers, which the MoonClerk web app calls "Plans": each is one payer with their subscription (status, plan amount and interval, next payment date, trial and cancel dates), payment method (brand, last 4), coupon discount, custom form fields and the form they used. Filter by form, status (active, canceled, expired, past_due, pending, unpaid), sign-up date range or next-payment date range, e.g. past_due plans or renewals due this month. The payer's management link and checkout token are never returned. Read-only. GET /customers.

tools.name: moonclerk_get_customer
tools.title: Get customer (plan)
tools.description: One MoonClerk customer (plan) by id with the full subscription, payment method, discount, checkout amounts (subtotal, fee, total, upfront amount, trial days) and custom field answers. The payer's management link and checkout token are never returned. Read-only. GET /customers/{id}.

tools.name: moonclerk_list_payments
tools.title: List payments
tools.description: List MoonClerk payments (charges): date, status (successful, refunded, failed), amount, Stripe fee and amount refunded in cents, currency, payer name and email, payment method, form, customer id (recurring payments only), coupon and custom fields. Filter by form, customer, status or charge-date range, e.g. failed payments this month or refunds for one plan. Amounts are in cents. Read-only. GET /payments.

tools.name: moonclerk_get_payment
tools.title: Get payment
tools.description: One MoonClerk payment by id with amounts (cents), Stripe fee, refunds, payer, payment method, Stripe references (charge, customer, invoice), coupon, custom fields and one-time checkout data. The checkout token is never returned. Read-only. GET /payments/{id}.

tools.name: moonclerk_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: moonclerk_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the MoonClerk tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: moonclerk_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on MoonClerk (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: moonclerk_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's MoonClerk Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run moonclerk_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which MoonClerk plans are past due right now?
List the payments that failed this month.
Which subscriptions are due to bill next week?
How much has each of my payment forms collected?

servers.name: ReferralHero
servers.description: Read ReferralHero campaigns, subscribers, referrals and rewards; add subscribers and points.

login.hint: Find it in ReferralHero → **Account → API**. The token gives access to every campaign in the account. Your token is used only to call the ReferralHero API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: referralhero_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: List the active ReferralHero campaigns (lists) in the account: uuid, name, subscriber count and creation time. The uuid is needed by every other tool. 10 per page. GET /lists.

tools.name: referralhero_get_leaderboard
tools.title: Get campaign leaderboard
tools.description: The leaderboard of a campaign: its top subscribers (10 to 100) with referral counts, points and position. GET /lists/{uuid}/leaderboard.

tools.name: referralhero_list_campaign_rewards
tools.title: List campaign rewards
tools.description: The rewards configured for a campaign (title, description, referrals needed to win each). This is the reward setup, not who earned what: see referralhero_list_unlocked_rewards for that. GET /lists/{uuid}/bonuses.

tools.name: referralhero_create_campaign
tools.title: Create campaign
tools.description: WRITE: create a new ReferralHero campaign (list) with a name and a default referral URL. It adds a campaign and changes nothing existing. POST /lists.

tools.name: referralhero_list_subscribers
tools.title: List subscribers
tools.description: List the subscribers of a campaign, 50 per page, with referral code, referral link, points, position, people referred, status and referrer. Sort and filter by the extra fields. GET /lists/{uuid}/subscribers.

tools.name: referralhero_get_subscriber
tools.title: Get subscriber
tools.description: One subscriber by id: contact data, referral code and link, points, position, referrals by level, status, fraud risk level, tags. Only verified subscribers are found. GET /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}.

tools.name: referralhero_get_subscriber_by_email
tools.title: Find subscriber by email
tools.description: Find one subscriber of a campaign by email. Only verified subscribers are found. GET /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/retrieve_by_email.

tools.name: referralhero_get_subscriber_by_referral_code
tools.title: Find subscriber by referral code
tools.description: Find the subscriber who owns a referral code (the mwr value in a referral link). Only verified subscribers are found. GET /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/retrieve_by_mwr.

tools.name: referralhero_search_subscribers_by_name
tools.title: Search subscribers by name
tools.description: Search subscribers by name across all campaigns of the account, 50 per page. GET /subscribers/search_by_name.

tools.name: referralhero_list_referrals
tools.title: List a subscriber's referrals
tools.description: The people a subscriber referred, 50 per page. scope: all (pending, unconfirmed and confirmed, default), level_1_confirmed, level_2_confirmed, level_3_confirmed (confirmed only, by referral level), level_2_all or level_3_all (every status at that level). GET /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}/{referred|level_N_referrals|level_N_all_referrals}.

tools.name: referralhero_list_unlocked_rewards
tools.title: List earned rewards (campaign-wide)
tools.description: Rewards unlocked by subscribers across a whole campaign: reward name, status (sent, resent, canceled, pending, flagged), value, subscriber email and id, coupon code, transaction. Filter by status to find rewards still to pay out. GET /lists/{uuid}/rewards.

tools.name: referralhero_list_subscriber_rewards
tools.title: List a subscriber's rewards
tools.description: Rewards one subscriber has unlocked, with status, value and coupon code. The reward id is what referralhero_update_reward_status needs. GET /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}/rewards.

tools.name: referralhero_list_coupon_groups
tools.title: List coupon groups
tools.description: Coupon groups of a campaign (id, name, active flag, coupons with availability), 50 per page. GET /lists/{uuid}/coupon_groups.

tools.name: referralhero_get_coupon_group
tools.title: Get coupon group
tools.description: One coupon group with all its coupons (code, available, sent_at). GET /lists/{uuid}/coupon_groups/{id}.

tools.name: referralhero_add_subscriber
tools.title: Add subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: add a subscriber (or a referred person) to a campaign. Give the campaign's unique identifier (email, phone, wallet or custom id). By default ReferralHero sends the subscriber a confirmation (double opt-in) email and any welcome automation of the campaign: set double_optin=false to suppress the confirmation email. Set referrer (a referral code or the referrer's email) to credit a referral. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers.

tools.name: referralhero_update_subscriber
tools.title: Update subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of a subscriber (overwrites the given fields): name, contact identifiers, extra fields, points (contest campaigns), tags, address, referral status (qualified/unqualified). Only fields you pass change. Only verified subscribers can be updated. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}.

tools.name: referralhero_delete_subscriber
tools.title: Delete subscriber
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: permanently delete a subscriber from a campaign, with their referral standing. This cannot be undone. DELETE /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}.

tools.name: referralhero_add_points
tools.title: Add points to a subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: add points to an existing subscriber (not idempotent: each call adds again). May unlock point-based rewards. The subscriber is identified by the campaign's unique identifier. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/add_points.

tools.name: referralhero_track_transaction
tools.title: Track a transaction
tools.description: WRITE: record a purchase/transaction for a subscriber (amount required) so revenue-based rewards and reports count it (not idempotent unless a transaction_id is reused). The subscriber is identified by the campaign's unique identifier. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/add_transactions.

tools.name: referralhero_confirm_referral
tools.title: Confirm a referral
tools.description: WRITE: confirm a verified referral when its third conversion event happens (campaigns whose goal tracks three events; otherwise ReferralHero returns an error). Confirming can unlock the referrer's rewards and send reward emails. Identify the referral by subscriber_id, or by the campaign's unique identifier. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}/confirm or /subscribers/confirm.

tools.name: referralhero_track_conversion_event
tools.title: Track a referral conversion event
tools.description: WRITE: report a conversion event for a referral (campaigns whose goal tracks two or three events). Updates the referral from pending to confirmed (two events) or unconfirmed (three). If the referral is unknown but a referrer is given, the referral is created. May unlock rewards. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/track_referral_conversion_event.

tools.name: referralhero_qualify_referral
tools.title: Mark referral qualified
tools.description: WRITE: mark a referral as qualified, so it counts toward the referrer's rewards. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}/qualify.

tools.name: referralhero_unqualify_referral
tools.title: Mark referral unqualified
tools.description: WRITE: mark a referral as unqualified (for example fraud or a refund), so it no longer counts toward the referrer's rewards. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}/unqualify.

tools.name: referralhero_promote_subscriber
tools.title: Promote subscriber (winner)
tools.description: WRITE: promote a subscriber to the campaign's winners list (contests and giveaways). Only verified subscribers can be promoted; an already promoted subscriber returns an error. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}/promote.

tools.name: referralhero_unlock_promoted_reward
tools.title: Trigger a manual reward
tools.description: WRITE: unlock a promoted-winner or one-off reward for a subscriber. This delivers the reward and may email the subscriber and use coupon codes. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/{id}/unlock_promoted_reward.

tools.name: referralhero_update_reward_status
tools.title: Update reward status
tools.description: WRITE: set the status of an unlocked reward to sent, resent or canceled. Marking sent/resent can trigger the reward delivery email to the subscriber. Get the reward_id from referralhero_list_subscriber_rewards or referralhero_list_unlocked_rewards. POST /lists/{uuid}/subscribers/update_reward_status.

tools.name: referralhero_create_coupon_group
tools.title: Create coupon group
tools.description: WRITE: create a coupon group for a campaign, optionally with its first coupon codes. It only adds a group. POST /lists/{uuid}/coupon_groups.

tools.name: referralhero_add_coupons
tools.title: Add coupons to a group
tools.description: WRITE: add coupon codes to an existing coupon group. It only adds codes. POST /lists/{uuid}/coupons.

tools.name: referralhero_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: referralhero_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the ReferralHero tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: referralhero_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on ReferralHero (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: referralhero_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's ReferralHero Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run referralhero_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Show the top 20 on the leaderboard of my launch campaign.
Which referral rewards are still pending and need to be sent?
Who referred jane@example.com and how many of her referrals are confirmed?
Add 50 bonus points to john@example.com in my contest campaign.

servers.name: Revamp CRM
servers.description: Read Revamp CRM contacts, deals, notes and orders; create and update contacts, deals and notes.

login.hint: Revamp CRM's API signs in with your account email and API key (never the account password). The key acts with that user's permissions; a dedicated user makes its activity easy to track. Your credentials are used only to call the Revamp CRM API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: revampcrm_get_current_user
tools.title: Get current user
tools.description: The Revamp CRM user the credentials belong to: id, name, email and role. Use the id as owner_user_id / assigned_user_id. GET /User/WhoAmI.

tools.name: revampcrm_list_contact_stages
tools.title: List contact stages
tools.description: The contact (lead) stage names configured in the account, in order. Use them as contact_stage filters and values. GET /Account/ContactStage.

tools.name: revampcrm_list_deal_currencies
tools.title: List deal currencies
tools.description: The currencies that deals in this account can use (name, value, symbol). GET /Account/DealCurrencies.

tools.name: revampcrm_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List contact custom fields
tools.description: The contact custom fields defined in the account: CustomFieldName (the property name, e.g. CustomField3), DisplayName, Type and list options. Read this to interpret CustomFieldN values on contacts and to set them. GET /Account/getAccountCustomFields.

tools.name: revampcrm_list_contacts
tools.title: List or search contacts
tools.description: Search and list contacts (people and organizations), newest filters first. With no filter it lists all contacts. Each item has name, organization, email/phone (ContactInfo), tags, stage, owner, last-contacted info and e-commerce order summary. resultsInfo carries totalCount and hasNext/nextIndex: pass nextIndex as `page` for the next page. GET /Contacts.

tools.name: revampcrm_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact by id with full details: contact info, address, tags, stage, custom fields, owner, previous/next task, deal totals (won/lost/open per currency), e-commerce order summary and order details. GET /Contacts/GetSingleContact/{id}/true.

tools.name: revampcrm_list_contact_deals
tools.title: List a contact's deals
tools.description: All deals of one contact (name, stage, status, value, currency, expected closing date, owner). GET /Contacts/{id}/Deals.

tools.name: revampcrm_list_deals
tools.title: List deals
tools.description: List deals with optional filters (status, pipeline, owner, contact, currency, created / expected-closing / closed date ranges). Each deal has name, stage, status, value, probability, forecasted sale, expected closing date, contact, owner and tags. The deal endpoints have no paging: the reply is cut to `limit` and says how many matched. GET /Deals/List.

tools.name: revampcrm_search_deals
tools.title: Search deals
tools.description: Search deals by name, status, stage, contact, owner, pipeline, product, sales region or deal source (text match as Revamp CRM defines it). Revamp CRM applies `limit` itself and gives no total: may_have_more is true when a full page came back. GET /Deals/Search.

tools.name: revampcrm_list_deals_by_stage
tools.title: List deals grouped by stage
tools.description: The deal pipeline board: deals grouped by stage (with the stage names in CurrentStages). Same filters as revampcrm_list_deals. At most `limit` deals are shown per stage. GET /Deals/ByStage.

tools.name: revampcrm_get_note
tools.title: Get note
tools.description: One note or timeline entry by id: text/message, type, author, related contact and deal, created date. GET /Notes/getNote/{id}.

tools.name: revampcrm_get_order
tools.title: Get e-commerce order
tools.description: One synced e-commerce order (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce ...) by the store's own order id: totals, tax, discount, shipping, financial and shipping status, line items and customer. Needs the provider name and store name exactly as Revamp CRM stores them (see ExternalProviders / Shop on a contact). GET /Orders/Get/{provider}/{store}/{id}.

tools.name: revampcrm_count_orders
tools.title: Count e-commerce orders
tools.description: How many orders Revamp CRM has synced for one store. GET /Orders/Count/{provider}/{store}.

tools.name: revampcrm_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: create a new contact (person or organization) in the Revamp CRM account. It does not email or message the contact. Search first (revampcrm_list_contacts with keyword/email) so you do not create a duplicate: this tool does not check. Returns Revamp CRM's import result (status, message, the new id in ImportingIntoId). POST /Contacts/New.

tools.name: revampcrm_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing contact. Only the fields you pass change: the tool reads the stored contact first and sends it back with your changes (Revamp CRM's update replaces the whole record). `tags` replaces the contact's tags; passing a field overwrites its old value. It does not email or message the contact. PUT /Contacts/Edit.

tools.name: revampcrm_create_deal
tools.title: Create deal
tools.description: WRITE: create a new deal (opportunity) in the Revamp CRM account, optionally linked to a contact. It does not message anyone. Use revampcrm_list_deals_by_stage (CurrentStages) for valid stage names and revampcrm_list_deal_currencies for currencies. POST /Deals.

tools.name: revampcrm_add_note
tools.title: Add note to a contact or deal
tools.description: WRITE: add a note to a contact or a deal timeline in Revamp CRM. It is an internal note: nothing is sent to the contact. Adding twice creates two notes. POST /Notes/{Contact|Deal}/{id}/Add.

tools.name: revampcrm_mark_deal_won
tools.title: Mark deal won
tools.description: WRITE: mark a deal as Won in Revamp CRM (its status changes and it counts in won-deal reports). It does not message the contact. Check the deal first with revampcrm_search_deals. POST /Deals/Won.

tools.name: revampcrm_mark_deal_lost
tools.title: Mark deal lost
tools.description: WRITE: mark a deal as Lost in Revamp CRM with a reason (its status changes and it counts in lost-deal reports). It does not message the contact. Check the deal first with revampcrm_search_deals. POST /Deals/Lost.

tools.name: revampcrm_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: revampcrm_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Revamp CRM tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: revampcrm_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Revamp CRM (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: revampcrm_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Revamp CRM Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run revampcrm_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which open deals are expected to close this month, and what are they worth?
Find the contact with email anna@example.com and show her deals and last order.
Add a note to deal 66a1f0c2: customer wants a revised quote by Friday.
Create a contact for Jan Novak at Acme Ltd, tag him 'webinar' and put him in my first contact stage.

servers.name: Rinkel
servers.description: Read Rinkel calls, voicemails, contacts and numbers; add call notes, edit contacts, block numbers.

login.hint: Create it in **My Rinkel → Settings → Integrations** (API access is included in the Professional and Expert plans). The key gives access to the call data of your whole Rinkel account. It is used only to call the Rinkel API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone; you can delete it in My Rinkel at any time.

tools.name: rinkel_list_calls
tools.title: List calls
tools.description: List call detail records (inbound and outbound calls) with date, direction, status (ANSWERED, MISSED, VOICEMAIL, ANSWERING_SERVICE), duration, external and internal number, the users involved, notes, and (when the account has Rinkel AI insights) the AI summary and sentiment. Use for 'who called today', 'which calls did we miss this week', 'calls longer than 5 minutes'. Newest first by default. Rinkel API: GET /call-detail-records.

tools.name: rinkel_get_call
tools.title: Get a call
tools.description: Get one call detail record by its Rinkel id (the `id` field of rinkel_list_calls): numbers, users, status, duration, notes, voicemail and call-recording ids, AI insights. Rinkel API: GET /call-detail-records/{id}.

tools.name: rinkel_get_call_by_network_id
tools.title: Get a call by network call id
tools.description: Get one call detail record by its network `callId` (the id Rinkel sends in webhook events), optionally with insights and notes. Rinkel API: GET /call-detail-records/by-call-id/{callId}.

tools.name: rinkel_get_call_transcription
tools.title: Get a call transcription
tools.description: Get the raw transcription of a call by its network `callId` (needs Rinkel AI insights on the account; 404 when the call has none). Rinkel API: GET /call-detail-records/by-call-id/{callId}/transcription.

tools.name: rinkel_get_call_recording_url
tools.title: Get a call recording URL
tools.description: Get a temporary URL (valid 3 hours) to stream or download a call recording. The id is `callRecording.id` of a call record. Append `download` as a query parameter to the URL to download instead of stream. Rinkel API: GET /call-recordings/{id}/stream.

tools.name: rinkel_list_voicemails
tools.title: List voicemails
tools.description: List voicemail messages (call records with status VOICEMAIL): caller, date, duration, whether new, and the voicemail id. Newest first. With is_new=true Rinkel ignores every other filter and returns only unplayed voicemails. Rinkel API: GET /voicemails.

tools.name: rinkel_count_new_voicemails
tools.title: Count new voicemails
tools.description: Number of voicemails that have not been played yet. Rinkel API: GET /voicemails/new-count.

tools.name: rinkel_get_voicemail_url
tools.title: Get a voicemail URL
tools.description: Get a temporary URL (valid 3 hours) to stream or download a voicemail. The id is `voicemail.id` of a call or voicemail record. Rinkel API: GET /voicemails/{id}/stream.

tools.name: rinkel_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List the contacts shared with everyone in the account (plus the Rinkel system contact, tag 'system'): names, company, phone numbers, email. Rinkel API: GET /contacts.

tools.name: rinkel_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: Get one contact by id. Rinkel API: GET /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: rinkel_find_contact_by_number
tools.title: Find a contact by phone number
tools.description: Find the contact that owns a phone number (E.164 such as +31612345678 works best). 404 when there is none. Rinkel API: GET /contacts/find-by-number/{number}.

tools.name: rinkel_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the account's users: name, email, phone number, role (ADMIN, USER, ANSWERINGSERVICE), availability schedule and status, and `fixed`/device info (`deviceId` is needed to start a call). Rinkel API: GET /users.

tools.name: rinkel_get_user
tools.title: Get a user
tools.description: Get one user by id, including preferences, notification settings, schedule and `deviceId`. Rinkel API: GET /users/{id}.

tools.name: rinkel_list_numbers
tools.title: List phone numbers
tools.description: List the account's Rinkel phone numbers: id, label, number, status (ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, PENDING_PORTING_IN ...), activation date and the users assigned. Rinkel API: GET /numbers.

tools.name: rinkel_get_number
tools.title: Get a phone number
tools.description: Get one Rinkel number with its full dial plan: greeting, business hours schedule, call forwarding targets and ring logic, voice menu, call recording and caller-id settings. Rinkel API: GET /numbers/{id}.

tools.name: rinkel_list_recordings
tools.title: List greeting recordings
tools.description: List the uploaded audio recordings used in the dial plan (greetings, announcements, voice-over scripts): name, description, duration and where each is used. Not call recordings. Rinkel API: GET /recordings.

tools.name: rinkel_list_webhooks
tools.title: List webhooks
tools.description: List the webhook subscriptions (events incomingCall, outgoingCall, callStart, callEnd, callInsights) with URL and active flag. Webhooks need the Expert plan. Rinkel API: GET /webhooks.

tools.name: rinkel_validate_phone_number
tools.title: Validate a phone number
tools.description: Check a phone number for a country and return its normalised form. With check_inventory=true Rinkel also checks whether the number is available to order. Rinkel API: GET /misc/validate-phone-number.

tools.name: rinkel_add_call_note
tools.title: Add a call note
tools.description: WRITE: add a note to a call record (visible to everyone in the account who sees the call). The id is the call record's `id`; if Rinkel answers 404, retry with the record's `callId`. Rinkel API: PUT /call-detail-records/{callId}/note.

tools.name: rinkel_update_call_note
tools.title: Update a call note
tools.description: WRITE: replace the text of an existing note on a call record (the note id is in `notes[].id` of the call record). Rinkel API: PATCH /call-detail-records/{callId}/note/{noteId}.

tools.name: rinkel_delete_call_note
tools.title: Delete a call note
tools.description: WRITE, irreversible: delete one note from a call record. Needs confirm=true after the user approved it. Rinkel API: DELETE /call-detail-records/{callId}/note/{noteId}.

tools.name: rinkel_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: WRITE: create a contact. It is shared with everyone in the Rinkel account (all users see it and calls from its numbers show its name). Rinkel API: POST /contacts.

tools.name: rinkel_update_contact
tools.title: Update a contact
tools.description: WRITE: update a contact (PUT semantics). `numbers` is required and REPLACES all stored numbers, and an omitted default_outbound_number_id CLEARS it; omitted names, company and email keep their stored value. Read the contact first (rinkel_get_contact) and resend what must stay. The system contact cannot be changed. Rinkel API: PUT /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: rinkel_delete_contact
tools.title: Delete a contact
tools.description: WRITE, irreversible: delete a contact for the whole account. Needs confirm=true after the user approved it. The Rinkel system contact cannot be deleted. Rinkel API: DELETE /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: rinkel_block_number
tools.title: Block a number
tools.description: WRITE: block a number from calling ANY of the account's numbers. Accepts an E.164 number, 'anonymous', or a prefix wildcard such as '+31*' (a wildcard must end the value and include a country code; a broad wildcard blocks every caller from that country). Undo with rinkel_unblock_number. Rinkel API: POST /privacy/block-number.

tools.name: rinkel_unblock_number
tools.title: Unblock a number
tools.description: WRITE: remove a number (or the same wildcard pattern that was blocked) from the block list so it can call again. Rinkel API: DELETE /privacy/unblock-number.

tools.name: rinkel_start_call
tools.title: Start an outgoing call
tools.description: WRITE, COSTS CALL MINUTES: starts a real phone call. Rinkel rings the given user device first and, once it is answered, dials `to` using the chosen Rinkel number as caller id, so call charges apply to the account and the person called sees the number. Needs confirm=true, set only after the user explicitly asked to place this call. Get device_id from rinkel_list_users (`fixed`/device info or `deviceId`) and number_id from rinkel_list_numbers. Rinkel API: POST /dial.

tools.name: rinkel_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Rinkel tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: rinkel_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Rinkel (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: rinkel_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Rinkel Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). servers.name: Safefood 360
servers.description: Read Safefood 360 documents, complaints, suppliers, materials; create complaints, update documents.

login.hint: Safefood 360 (Ideagen Food & Beverage) gives its API to customers through [developers.safefood360.com](https://developers.safefood360.com/): sign up there, subscribe to a product (access is approved by Safefood 360) and copy the **primary key** from your profile. The API signs in with a user's email and password plus the site id, so create a **dedicated user** for this connection with only the permissions you want to give. The password cannot contain a colon. Everything is stored encrypted and used only to call the Safefood 360 API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone. The Trial product allows 5 calls per minute and 100 per week; each question uses two or more calls.

tools.name: safefood360_list_documents
tools.title: List documents
tools.description: List controlled documents of the Safefood 360 site (title, description, version, folder, responsible person, review/approval workflow, created/modified). Supports OData $filter, $orderby, $top, $skip and $count. GET /documents/sites/{siteId}/v1/documents/.

tools.name: safefood360_get_document
tools.title: Get document
tools.description: One controlled document by its identifier: title, description, version, folder, responsible person and workflow. GET /documents/sites/{siteId}/v1/documents/{identifier}.

tools.name: safefood360_list_document_reviews
tools.title: List document reviews
tools.description: List document reviews (the periodic review records of controlled documents). Supports OData $filter, $orderby, $top, $skip and $count; use it to find reviews that are due or overdue. GET /documents/sites/{siteId}/v1/documentreviews/.

tools.name: safefood360_get_document_review
tools.title: Get document review
tools.description: One document review by its review number. GET /documents/sites/{siteId}/v1/documentreviews/{no}.

tools.name: safefood360_list_complaints
tools.title: List complaints
tools.description: List customer complaints (number, name, risk, date, company, source, contact person, product/material, description, created/modified). Supports OData $filter, $orderby, $top, $skip and $count. GET /complaints/sites/{siteId}/v1/complaints.

tools.name: safefood360_get_complaint
tools.title: Get complaint
tools.description: One complaint by its id (GUID). GET /complaints/sites/{siteId}/v1/complaints/{id}.

tools.name: safefood360_list_suppliers
tools.title: List suppliers
tools.description: List suppliers (name, code, addresses, contacts, approval status, risk, establishment numbers). Paged with start_index and limit; the reply carries recordCount and next_start_index. GET /v1/suppliers/?siteId=.

tools.name: safefood360_get_supplier
tools.title: Get supplier
tools.description: One supplier by its external id. GET /v1/suppliers/{externalId}?siteId=.

tools.name: safefood360_list_materials
tools.title: List materials
tools.description: List materials/ingredients (name, our code, supplier code, description, category, countries of origin, risk, archived flag). Paged with start_index and limit; the reply carries recordCount and next_start_index. GET /v1/materials/?siteId=.

tools.name: safefood360_get_material
tools.title: Get material
tools.description: One material by its external id. GET /v1/materials/{externalId}?siteId=.

tools.name: safefood360_get_customer
tools.title: Get customer
tools.description: One customer by its identifier (name, addresses, phone, notes). The vendor offers no customer list. GET /customers/sites/{siteId}/v1/customers/{identifier}.

tools.name: safefood360_get_employee
tools.title: Get employee
tools.description: One employee record by its identifier (training/HR master data of the site). Contains personal data: use it only for the question asked. The vendor offers no employee list. GET /employees/sites/{siteId}/v1/employees/{identifier}.

tools.name: safefood360_get_final_product
tools.title: Get final product
tools.description: One final (finished) product by its identifier: name, folder, categories, barcode, specifications and the materials it is made of. The vendor offers no final-product list. GET /finalproducts/sites/{siteId}/v1/finalproducts/{identifier}.

tools.name: safefood360_get_batching_record
tools.title: Get batching record
tools.description: One batching (traceability) record by its id (GUID). GET /batching/sites/{siteId}/v1/batching/records/{recordId}.

tools.name: safefood360_update_document

tools.description: WRITE: change the title, description and/or folder of a controlled document in Safefood 360 (JSON patch; fields you leave out stay as they are). It does not publish a new version or change the review workflow. Returns the updated document. PATCH /documents/sites/{siteId}/v1/documents/{identifier}.

tools.name: safefood360_update_customer
tools.title: Update customer
tools.description: WRITE: change the name, phone, mobile and/or notes of a customer in Safefood 360 (JSON patch of those fields; others stay as they are). notes REPLACES the existing notes. PATCH /customers/sites/{siteId}/v1/customers/{identifier}.

tools.name: safefood360_create_complaint

tools.description: WRITE: record a NEW complaint in Safefood 360 (it may trigger the site's complaint workflow and notifications). Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two complaints. Safefood 360 validates the fields (ids such as source, company and recorded_by are GUIDs from your site's lists) and rejects a request that lacks required ones. POST /complaints/sites/{siteId}/v1/complaints/.

servers.name: Schedule it
servers.description: Read Schedule it events, resources, groups and labels; create and update events and resources.

login.hint: Schedule It's API signs in with a normal account login: the user name is **<account number>_<login name>** (shown in your Schedule It account settings) and its password. A dedicated login for the AI assistant keeps its activity easy to track and limits what it can see. Your login is used only to call the Schedule It API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: scheduleit_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List scheduled events and tasks (bookings, shifts, jobs). Without date_from/date_to Schedule It uses its default date range. Schedule It returns only a short summary of each event unless you name the fields you want: pass `fields` such as id,title,date_start,date_end,owner,notes,completed,priority,custom1 (get_event returns ALL fields of one event). `owner` holds the ids of the resources (people, rooms, equipment) the event is linked to. There is no paging: the reply holds up to `limit` events (default 100), so narrow with the filters instead. Do not call this repeatedly to watch for changes (use modified_after to fetch only what changed). GET /api/events.

tools.name: scheduleit_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event or task by id with ALL its fields (title, dates, linked resources, notes, completion, priority, custom fields). GET /api/events/{id}.

tools.name: scheduleit_create_event
tools.title: Create event
tools.description: WRITE: create a new event (booking, shift, job or task) in the Schedule It account, optionally linked to resources. It becomes visible to everyone with access to the schedule, and Schedule It may notify the linked resources according to the account's own notification settings. Confirm the title, dates and resources with the user first. POST /api/events.

tools.name: scheduleit_update_event
tools.title: Update event
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing event; only the fields you pass are changed, the rest stay as they are. Passing resource_ids replaces the whole list of linked resources; an empty string clears notes or a custom field. Changing dates or resources may notify people per the account's notification settings. POST /api/events/{id}.

tools.name: scheduleit_delete_event
tools.title: Delete event
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: permanently delete one event or task. It cannot be undone through the API. Only call this when the user clearly asked for this event to be deleted. DELETE /api/events/{id}.

tools.name: scheduleit_list_resources
tools.title: List resources
tools.description: List resources: the people, rooms, equipment or vehicles that events are scheduled against. Schedule It returns only a short summary unless you pass `fields` (for example id,name,email,data1; get_resource returns ALL fields of one). Resources belong to groups (`owner` = group ids). There is no paging; the reply holds up to `limit` resources (default 100). GET /api/resources.

tools.name: scheduleit_get_resource
tools.title: Get resource
tools.description: One resource by id with ALL its fields (name, email, groups, details 1-10, colours, skills). GET /api/resources/{id}.

tools.name: scheduleit_create_resource
tools.title: Create resource
tools.description: WRITE: add a new resource (a person, room, piece of equipment) to the Schedule It account. It may count toward the account's licensed resources or users. Confirm the details with the user first. POST /api/resources.

tools.name: scheduleit_update_resource
tools.title: Update resource
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing resource; only the fields you pass are changed. Passing group_ids replaces the whole list of groups; an empty string clears email or a detail field. POST /api/resources/{id}.

tools.name: scheduleit_list_groups
tools.title: List groups
tools.description: List resource groups (the categories resources are organised in, e.g. Staff, Rooms, Vehicles). Pass `fields` (e.g. id,name) for more than the short summary. GET /api/groups.

tools.name: scheduleit_get_group
tools.title: Get group
tools.description: One resource group by id with ALL its fields. GET /api/groups/{id}.

tools.name: scheduleit_create_group
tools.title: Create group
tools.description: WRITE: add a new resource group to the Schedule It account. POST /api/groups.

tools.name: scheduleit_update_group
tools.title: Update group
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing resource group; only the fields you pass are changed. POST /api/groups/{id}.

tools.name: scheduleit_list_labels
tools.title: List labels
tools.description: List the labels that can be put on events (for example Confirmed, Urgent). Pass `fields` (e.g. id,name) for more than the short summary. GET /api/labels.

tools.name: scheduleit_list_label_groups
tools.title: List label groups
tools.description: List label groups (the categories that labels are organised in). Pass `fields` (e.g. id,name) for more than the short summary. GET /api/labelgroups.

tools.name: scheduleit_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.
