Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: scheduleit_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Schedule It Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run scheduleit_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: What is on the schedule this week, and who is it assigned to?
Create an event 'Site visit - Harper' tomorrow 09:00-11:00 for resource 220.
Which events changed since yesterday?
List all resources in the Vehicles group with their email addresses.

servers.name: splose
servers.description: Read splose patients, appointments, invoices, cases; book and cancel appointments, record payments.

login.hint: The workspace owner requests API access from splose Support (paid plans only), then creates the key in splose under **My account, API**. The key acts with the permissions of the user who owns it. Pick the region your splose account is hosted in (Australia, or the UK for api-uk.splose.com). Patient records are health data: your key is used only to call the Splose API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: splose_get_account
tools.title: Get the account behind the API key
tools.description: The organisation and the practitioner who owns the API key, plus the key's expiry date. Good first call. GET /me.

tools.name: splose_list_patients
tools.title: List patients
tools.description: Patients (clients) of the practice, filtered, in id order, as short rows: id, name, email, birthdate, phones, tags, alert, archived. Use splose_get_patient for the full record. HEALTH DATA: only look people up when the user asks. GET /patients.

tools.name: splose_get_patient
tools.title: Get a patient
tools.description: One patient in full: contact details, address, NDIS number and plan info, Medicare/health fund, emergency contact, tags and custom fields. HEALTH DATA. GET /patients/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_appointments
tools.title: List appointments
tools.description: Appointments in id order: start/end (UTC), service, location, practitioner, price, note and the per-patient status (Arrived, Did not arrive, Cancelled, Completed, cancellation reason, invoice id). Filter by time window, patient, practitioner or status. GET /appointments.

tools.name: splose_get_appointment
tools.title: Get an appointment
tools.description: One appointment in full, with each patient's status, case, invoice and cancellation details. GET /appointments/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_practitioners
tools.title: List practitioners
tools.description: Practitioners (staff): name, email, profession, role, active flag, online-booking flag, timezone and their location/service connections. GET /practitioners.

tools.name: splose_get_practitioner
tools.title: Get a practitioner
tools.description: One practitioner in full, including provider numbers and connections. GET /practitioners/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: Practice locations: title, address, phone, email, timezone, online-booking flag and the ids of the services offered there. GET /locations.

tools.name: splose_get_location
tools.title: Get a location
tools.description: One location in full. GET /locations/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_services
tools.title: List services
tools.description: The service catalogue: name, type, code, duration (minutes), unit (Hour or Each), price, tax type, group size and tags. GET /services.

tools.name: splose_get_service
tools.title: Get a service
tools.description: One service in full, including provider-travel pricing. GET /services/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: Contacts (GPs, plan managers, referrers, invoice recipients): name, type, email, address, phones and the ids of their patients, invoices and cases. GET /contacts.

tools.name: splose_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: One contact in full. GET /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_cases
tools.title: List cases
tools.description: Cases (funding referrals and plans): case number, budget, hours or appointment allowance, issue and expiry dates, tracking type, open flag and utilisation alert. HEALTH/FUNDING DATA. GET /cases.

tools.name: splose_get_case
tools.title: Get a case
tools.description: One case in full, with its appointment connections. GET /cases/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: Invoices: number, issue/due dates, patient, contact, location, practitioner, subtotal, tax, total, paid amount, status (Draft, Awaiting Payment, Paid), line items and payment ids. Use status=Awaiting Payment for what is owed. GET /invoices.

tools.name: splose_get_invoice
tools.title: Get an invoice
tools.description: One invoice in full with its line items and payments. GET /invoices/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_payments
tools.title: List payments
tools.description: Payments received: payment number, amount, date, patient, location, payment method, the invoices each payment settles and credit allocations. GET /payments.

tools.name: splose_get_payment
tools.title: Get a payment
tools.description: One payment in full. GET /payments/{id}.

tools.name: splose_list_payment_methods
tools.title: List payment methods
tools.description: Payment methods (cash, card, bank transfer and so on) with their ids, needed to record a payment. GET /payment-methods.

tools.name: splose_list_credit_notes
tools.title: List credit notes
tools.description: Credit notes: number, invoice, patient, subtotal, tax, total, sent status, items and allocations. GET /credit-notes.

tools.name: splose_list_waitlist
tools.title: List waitlist items
tools.description: Waitlist entries: patient, practitioner, location, wanted services, preferred days and time, tags and active flag. GET /waitlists.

tools.name: splose_list_patient_forms
tools.title: List patient forms
tools.description: Forms sent to patients: title, status (Incomplete, In progress, Completed), patient, appointment, template and submission time. The form content is included. GET /patient-forms.

tools.name: splose_list_support_activities
tools.title: List support activities
tools.description: Non-appointment billable activities (NDIS support activities): patient, practitioner, service, item code, quantity, price, invoice id. GET /support-activities.

tools.name: splose_list_busy_times
tools.title: List busy times
tools.description: Blocked-out time in practitioner calendars (leave, admin time): start/end, location, practitioners, type and note. GET /busy-times.

tools.name: splose_list_cancellation_reasons
tools.title: List cancellation reasons
tools.description: Cancellation reasons with their ids, needed to cancel an appointment. GET /cancellation-reasons.

tools.name: splose_list_custom_fields
tools.title: List patient custom fields
tools.description: The custom fields defined for patients: id, name, type (short text, dropdown, date and so on), required flag and options. GET /custom-field/.

tools.name: splose_get_practitioner_availability
tools.title: Get a practitioner's availability
tools.description: A practitioner's working-hours availability per date and location (start/end time, weekly or fortnightly repeat). The window is at most 100 days. This is the roster, not the open slots: use splose_find_free_slots for bookable times. GET /availabilities/{practitionerId}.

tools.name: splose_find_free_slots
tools.title: Find free appointment slots
tools.description: Bookable free slots for one or more practitioners at a location for one patient service, between from and to (the window is at most 7 days). Returns, per practitioner, the start/end of each open slot in UTC. Read-only. GET /free-slots.

tools.name: splose_create_appointment
tools.title: Create an appointment
tools.description: WRITE: books ONE appointment for one patient with one practitioner, service and location, from start to end (UTC). Splose may send the patient its normal booking confirmation or reminders according to the practice's settings, and the appointment can later be invoiced. Check splose_find_free_slots first. Not idempotent: calling twice books twice. POST /appointments.

tools.name: splose_update_appointment
tools.title: Update (reschedule) an appointment
tools.description: WRITE: changes the time, service, location, practitioner, case or patient of ONE existing appointment; send only the fields to change. Splose may notify the patient of a change according to the practice's settings. Same input twice gives the same result. PUT /appointments/{id}.

tools.name: splose_cancel_appointment
tools.title: Cancel an appointment
tools.description: WRITE: cancels ONE appointment with a cancellation reason (ids from splose_list_cancellation_reasons) and an optional note. The reason's billable rate may create a cancellation charge, and the patient may be notified per the practice's settings. For a group appointment pass patient_id to cancel only that patient's place; without it the whole appointment is cancelled. Cannot be undone through this server: confirm with the user first and pass confirm: true. POST /appointments/{id}/cancellation or /appointments/{id}/patients/{patientId}/cancellation.

tools.name: splose_mark_patient_arrived
tools.title: Mark a patient as arrived
tools.description: WRITE: marks the patient of ONE appointment as arrived (check-in). For a group appointment pass patient_id to mark just that patient. Marking twice has the same effect. POST /appointments/{id}/arrival or /appointments/{id}/patients/{patientId}/arrival.

tools.name: splose_create_patient
tools.title: Create a patient
tools.description: WRITE: adds ONE new patient record (first and last name required). Search with splose_list_patients first to avoid a duplicate. Patient messaging follows the practice's settings and communicationPreference. Not idempotent: calling twice creates two patients. HEALTH DATA: only enter what the user supplied. POST /patients.

tools.name: splose_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: WRITE: adds ONE contact (GP, plan manager, referrer, payer). type, name and email are required (type is Splose's contact type, e.g. Standard; see splose_list_contacts for the values in use). Not idempotent: calling twice creates two contacts. POST /contacts.

tools.name: splose_record_payment
tools.title: Record a payment against an invoice
tools.description: WRITE, MONEY: records ONE payment received (cash, card, transfer) against ONE invoice; it moves the invoice towards Paid and is shown in the patient's account. It does NOT charge anyone's card. amount must not exceed what is owed (check splose_get_invoice). Not idempotent: calling twice records two payments, and this server cannot delete a payment, so confirm the details with the user first and pass confirm: true. Ids come from splose_get_invoice and splose_list_payment_methods. POST /payments.

tools.name: splose_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: splose_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Splose tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: splose_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Splose (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: splose_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Splose Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run splose_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which appointments does the clinic have tomorrow, and with whom?
Which invoices are still awaiting payment, oldest first?
Find the next free slot this week for an initial assessment with Dr Smith.
Which funding cases expire in the next 30 days?

servers.name: StoreRocket
servers.description: Read StoreRocket projects and store-locator locations; create and update locations.

login.hint: Create it at **storerocket.io → API Tokens** (storerocket.io/app/api-tokens). Choose only the permissions you want the AI to have: location:read to look things up, location:update to edit, location:create to add; leave location:delete off. The API needs a project on the Business plan. Your token is used only to call the StoreRocket API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: storerocket_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: The StoreRocket user the API token belongs to: id, name, email and company. GET /user.

tools.name: storerocket_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the StoreRocket projects (store locators) the token's user belongs to: public id, name, number of locations, status and plan. Use the id as project_id in every location tool. Location tools need a project on the Business plan (API access). GET /projects.

tools.name: storerocket_list_locations
tools.title: List locations
tools.description: List the locations of a project (name, address, city, coordinates, phone, visibility, location type, marker, cover image), 25 per page by default, with optional filters on name, address, city, state, country and postal code and optional hours/filters/custom fields/calls to action. Needs the location:read permission. GET /projects/{project_id}/locations.

tools.name: storerocket_get_location
tools.title: Get location
tools.description: One location by id, optionally with its opening hours, search filters, custom fields and calls to action. Needs the location:read permission. GET /projects/{project_id}/locations/{location_id}.

tools.name: storerocket_create_location
tools.title: Create location
tools.description: WRITE: add a location to a project's store locator. name and city are required; supply lat and lng for a precise pin (otherwise StoreRocket geocodes the address, which can be off). It appears on the live locator immediately unless visible is false, so set visible=false for a coming-soon or draft location. Opening hours: omit, or give all seven days. Creating twice makes two locations, so check storerocket_list_locations before retrying after an error. Needs the location:create permission. POST /projects/{project_id}/locations.

tools.name: storerocket_update_location
tools.title: Update location
tools.description: WRITE: change selected fields of one location with a partial update (PATCH): only the fields you send change, everything else is kept. The change shows on the live locator at once. Use null to clear phone, email, url, socials or cover; hours accepts single days (hours:{mon:'09:00-17:00'}), null for a day clears it, hours:null removes the whole schedule; fields and calls_to_action merge by name (a null value removes that entry); filters REPLACES the list ([] clears it). To take a location off the locator without deleting it, set visible=false. An invalid value saves nothing. Needs the location:update permission. PATCH /projects/{project_id}/locations/{location_id}.

tools.name: storerocket_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: storerocket_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the StoreRocket tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: storerocket_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on StoreRocket (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: storerocket_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's StoreRocket Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run storerocket_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: List all my StoreRocket locations in Texas.
Hide the Downtown Seattle location from the store locator.
Change the phone number and Monday opening hours of my Portland store.
Add a coming-soon location in Austin, hidden until it opens.

servers.name: vintrace
servers.description: Read vintrace vessels, batches, work orders, lab results, stock; assign work orders, add notes.

login.hint: The URL is the address you log in to vintrace with, for example **https://us36.vintrace.net/yourcode/1.app** (it holds your server and customer code). A vintrace admin creates the token in vintrace under **API tokens** (permission: Local vintrace Admin); the token acts with the permissions of the user it is created for, so a dedicated user with only the access you want shared works best. The token is used only to call the vintrace API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: vintrace_list_work_orders
tools.title: List work orders
tools.description: List winery work orders (cellar jobs such as transfers, additions, bottling) with their jobs, assignee, status and scheduled time. Filter by scheduled time range, status and operation type. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/operation/work-orders.

tools.name: vintrace_list_wine_batches
tools.title: List wine batches
tools.description: List wine batches (the named lots of wine) with volume, variety, vintage and owner. Use include=vessels,allocations to add where each batch sits. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/operation/wine-batches.

tools.name: vintrace_get_vessel_details_report
tools.title: Vessel contents report
tools.description: The bulk wine report: every vessel (tank, barrel, bin, press, tanker) with its contents, volume, batch, owner and winery as at a date. Use extra_fields=composition,allocations,liveMetrics to add them. Covers every winery the token's user may access unless wineryId/wineryName narrows it. GET /v7/report/vessel-details-report.

tools.name: vintrace_get_vessel
tools.title: Get vessel
tools.description: One vessel by id: a tank, barrel, barrel group, tanker or bin, with its details, dimensions and contents. GET /v7/vessel/<tanks|barrels|barrel-groups|tankers|bins>/{id}.

tools.name: vintrace_list_lab_requests
tools.title: List lab requests
tools.description: The lab console: analysis tasks (samples to measure) with lab, template, vessel, batch, status and arrival. Completed tasks are left out unless status includes Completed. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/lab/lab-requests.

tools.name: vintrace_list_trial_blends
tools.title: List trial blends
tools.description: List trial blends (planned blend trials) with status and composition. Use composition_summary_by=variety,vintage to summarise. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/operation/trial-blends.

tools.name: vintrace_search_transactions
tools.title: Search winemaking transactions
tools.description: Winemaking operations completed in a date range (transfers, additions, blends, racking...) with the from/to vessels and before/after volumes. Defaults to today when no dates are given. GET /v6/transaction/search.

tools.name: vintrace_list_barrel_treatments
tools.title: List barrel treatments
tools.description: Barrel move shipments / barrel treatments recorded in vintrace, with barrel states and treatment types. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/operation/barrel-treatments.

tools.name: vintrace_list_blocks
tools.title: List vineyard blocks
tools.description: List vineyard blocks (grower, vineyard, region, variety). To see fruit placements for a vintage pass include=fruitPlacements together with vintage. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/harvest/blocks.

tools.name: vintrace_list_block_assessments
tools.title: List block assessments
tools.description: List vineyard block assessments (vine and fruit assessments by the viticulture team). Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/harvest/assessments.

tools.name: vintrace_list_bookings
tools.title: List fruit bookings
tools.description: List active fruit bookings (grape deliveries planned for a vintage) for one or more wineries: grower, block, variety, expected pick time and quantity. vintage and winery_ids are required. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/operation/bookings.

tools.name: vintrace_list_bulk_intakes
tools.title: List bulk intakes
tools.description: List bulk wine/juice intakes (wine bought or received in bulk) with batch, volume, owner and cost. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/operation/bulk-intakes.

tools.name: vintrace_search_fruit_intakes
tools.title: Search fruit intakes
tools.description: Fruit intake operations (grape deliveries weighed in at the winery): weights, grower, block, vineyard, vintage, docket numbers and metrics. Filter by vintage, grower, vineyard, block or recorded time. Page with first_result and max_results. GET /v6/intake-operations/search.

tools.name: vintrace_list_stock_dispatches
tools.title: List stock dispatches
tools.description: List stock dispatch actions (bottled goods and dry goods sent out) with routes, items and shipping information. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/stock/dispatches.

tools.name: vintrace_list_shipments
tools.title: List bulk shipments
tools.description: List shipments created by Bulk Dispatch and inter-winery dispatch operations, with destination and wine details. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/operation/shipments.

tools.name: vintrace_list_cost_transactions
tools.title: List bulk wine cost movements
tools.description: Bulk wine cost movements between two times (cost of wine moved between batches and wineries), optionally for one winery or business unit. Needs the vintrace permission to view costs. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/costs/business-unit-transactions.

tools.name: vintrace_list_brand_allocations
tools.title: List brand allocations
tools.description: List brand allocations of bulk wine (how much of a wine is promised to which brand), by status and vintage. Reply: results plus next_offset. GET /v7/allocations/brand-allocations.

tools.name: vintrace_get_purchase_order
tools.title: Get purchase order
tools.description: One purchase order with its lines, state and fulfilment. GET /v7/account/purchase-orders/{id}.

tools.name: vintrace_list_inventory
tools.title: List stock inventory
tools.description: Stock on hand (bottled wine, dry goods, additives) up to a date: quantity, committed, on order and available per item, location, owner, tax class. breakout_costing needs the view-costs permission. GET /v6/inventory.

tools.name: vintrace_lookup_stock_item
tools.title: Look up stock item
tools.description: Find one stock item by code (matched against the start of the code) or by id: type, unit, owner, accounts, tax class and sub-components. Give code or id. GET /v6/stock/lookup.

tools.name: vintrace_get_stock_item
tools.title: Get stock item details
tools.description: One stock item by id with optional detail parts: expand=fields,distributions,notes,historyItems,rawComponents,bulkInfo. GET /v6/mrp/stock/{id}.

tools.name: vintrace_list_stock_item_notes
tools.title: List stock item notes
tools.description: The notes recorded on a stock item. GET /v6/mrp/stock/{id}/notes.

tools.name: vintrace_list_products
tools.title: List products (wines in vessels)
tools.description: List wine products as they sit in vessels: batch code, vessel, volume, colour, state and the latest lab metrics (TSO2, pH, Brix...). skip_metrics=true makes it faster. barcode matches a vessel code or asset id. GET /v6/products/list.

tools.name: vintrace_get_product
tools.title: Get product
tools.description: One wine product by id (or by vessel barcode) with its vessel, volume and metrics. GET /v6/products/{id}.

tools.name: vintrace_list_sales_orders
tools.title: List sales orders
tools.description: List sales orders with customer, status, price list, line items, totals and invoice date. Filter by status, customer, order date range or invoice date range. GET /v6/sales-order/list.

tools.name: vintrace_get_sales_order
tools.title: Get sales order
tools.description: One sales order by id, or by order code (for example VSO20): customer, items, prices, taxes and status. Give exactly one. GET /v6/sales-order/{id} or /v6/sales-order?code=.

tools.name: vintrace_list_parties
tools.title: List parties (customers, growers, owners)
tools.description: List parties: customers, growers, suppliers and owners, individuals or organisations, with address, phone and email. Filter by the start of the name and category. GET /v6/party/list.

tools.name: vintrace_get_party
tools.title: Get party
tools.description: One party (customer, grower, supplier, owner) by id, or by exact name. Give exactly one. GET /v6/party/{id} or /v6/party?name=.

tools.name: vintrace_get_work_order
tools.title: Get work order
tools.description: One work order by id: every job with its steps, summary text, status and assignee. Find the id with vintrace_list_work_orders or vintrace_list_work_orders_v6. GET /v6/workorders/{id}.

tools.name: vintrace_list_work_orders_v6
tools.title: List work orders (operator view)
tools.description: Work orders from the operator's point of view (what is waiting for me / unassigned), with job counts, status and scheduled dates. Defaults to the last 7 days to 3 days ahead. GET /v6/workorders/list.

tools.name: vintrace_search_items
tools.title: Search vintrace items by type
tools.description: Look up names and ids of one kind of item: growers, owners, blocks, varietals, vintages, regions, programs, batches, products, tanks, barrels, bins and more. Use it to find the id or exact name another tool needs. GET /v6/search/list.

tools.name: vintrace_add_stock_item_note
tools.title: Add a note to a stock item
tools.description: WRITE: adds a new note to a vintrace stock item (visible to everyone in the winery, recorded under the token's user). Adding the same note twice creates two notes. POST /v6/mrp/stock/{id}/notes.

tools.name: vintrace_assign_work_order
tools.title: Assign a work order
tools.description: WRITE: assigns a work order to the token's own vintrace user (or to assign_operator_id), so it shows up in that operator's list. With reassign=true it takes over a work order already assigned to someone else. Check the work order first with vintrace_get_work_order. POST /v6/workorders/assign.

tools.name: vintrace_deactivate_booking
tools.title: Deactivate a fruit booking
tools.description: WRITE: deactivates a fruit booking so it no longer counts as an active booking (the record is kept; it is not deleted). Use vintrace_list_bookings to find the booking id first. POST /v7/operation/bookings/{id}/deactivation.

tools.name: vintrace_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)

servers.name: Vision6
servers.description: Read Vision6 lists, contacts, messages and reports; update contacts; send transactional email/SMS.

login.hint: In Vision6 open **Integrations → API Keys**, create a REST-compatible key (choose the lowest access level that covers what you need) and copy the key plus the **REST API Endpoint** shown there (like https://au1.api.vision6.com/v1/). Your key is used only to call the Vision6 API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: vision6_get_account
tools.title: Get API key details
tools.description: Details of the API key this server uses: the scopes it grants (e.g. list.view, contact.create, message.edit, report.view) and its creation/expiry time. Use it to see why a request is refused. GET /v1/.

tools.name: vision6_list_lists
tools.title: List contact lists
tools.description: List the account's contact lists with id, name, creation/modification time and notification settings. Filter by exact name. GET /lists.

tools.name: vision6_get_list
tools.title: Get a contact list
tools.description: One contact list by id. GET /lists/{list_id}.

tools.name: vision6_list_list_fields
tools.title: List a list's fields
tools.description: The fields (columns) of a contact list: label, type (email, mobile, text, dropdown, date ...), allowed values and whether they are mandatory. The lowercase underscore form of a label is the key used for contact values and filters. GET /lists/{list_id}/fields.

tools.name: vision6_list_folders
tools.title: List folders
tools.description: List the account's folders (list folders and message folders) with id, name, type and size. Needed for the folder id when creating a list or message. GET /folders.

tools.name: vision6_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List the contacts of one list: email, mobile, subscribed/blocked status, active flag, double opt-in and the list's custom fields. Filter by email, mobile, active flag, creation/modification time or any custom field (`filters`, e.g. {"city":"Brisbane"} or {"source:ne":"promo"}). GET /lists/{list_id}/contacts.

tools.name: vision6_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: One contact by id within a list, with all fields. GET /lists/{list_id}/contacts/{contact_id}.

tools.name: vision6_list_messages
tools.title: List messages
tools.description: List saved email and SMS messages (templates and campaigns) with id, type, name, subject and sender. Filter by type or exact name/subject. GET /messages.

tools.name: vision6_get_message
tools.title: Get a message
tools.description: One message by id. With include_content=true the HTML and plain-text body is included. GET /messages/{message_id}.

tools.name: vision6_get_message_sender_defaults
tools.title: Get default sender details
tools.description: The account's default from name, from address and reply-to, applied to new email messages when you omit them. GET /message-sender-defaults.

tools.name: vision6_list_reports
tools.title: List send reports
tools.description: Send reports for campaigns, newest first: message name, type, sent, bounced, opened, unique clicks, unsubscribes, complaints, total recipients and last sent time. Filter by message, type, test sends or creation time. Click and domain breakdowns are only returned when requested via `fields`. GET /reports.

tools.name: vision6_get_report
tools.title: Get a send report
tools.description: One send report by id with all delivery and engagement counts, per-link click counts and recipient domain distribution. Optionally includes A/B test results and social click/share statistics. GET /reports/{report_id}.

tools.name: vision6_list_sent_contacts
tools.title: List contacts a message was sent to
tools.description: The contacts one message was sent to, with send time, first/last open time and open type (html, text, sms or not_opened). Use it to see who opened a campaign. GET /messages/{message_id}/sent-contacts.

tools.name: vision6_list_transactional_groups
tools.title: List transactional groups
tools.description: Transactional send groups (one per group name used with vision6_send_transactional) with sent, failed, bounced, delivered, opened, clicked and unsubscribed counts. GET /transactional-groups.

tools.name: vision6_get_transactional_group
tools.title: Get a transactional group
tools.description: One transactional group by id with its delivery statistics. GET /transactional-groups/{group_id}.

tools.name: vision6_create_contact
tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: WRITE: add one contact to a list (needs an email and/or mobile that matches a field of the list). May trigger the list's 'contact created' automations and notification emails. Returns the new contact. POST /lists/{list_id}/contacts.

tools.name: vision6_add_contacts
tools.title: Add several contacts
tools.description: WRITE: add up to 200 contacts to a list in one request (faster than one by one). Each needs an email and/or mobile. Vision6 returns no contact data (HTTP 204), so use vision6_list_contacts to read them back. May trigger automations. POST /lists/{list_id}/contacts.

tools.name: vision6_update_contact
tools.title: Update a contact
tools.description: WRITE: change one contact's email, mobile, custom field values, subscription status (email_subscribed/mobile_subscribed=false unsubscribes), active flag or double opt-in. Only the fields you pass change. May trigger 'contact updated' automations. Returns the updated contact. PATCH /lists/{list_id}/contacts/{contact_id}.

tools.name: vision6_delete_contact
tools.title: Delete a contact
tools.description: WRITE, IRREVERSIBLE: permanently delete one contact from a list (for example for a privacy erasure request). To stop emailing someone but keep the record, use vision6_update_contact with email_subscribed=false instead. Pass confirm=true only after the user agreed to the deletion. DELETE /lists/{list_id}/contacts?id={contact_id}.

tools.name: vision6_create_list
tools.title: Create a contact list
tools.description: WRITE: create a new, empty contact list inside a list folder (see vision6_list_folders with type list). Returns the new list. POST /lists.

tools.name: vision6_create_message
tools.title: Create a message (draft)
tools.description: WRITE: save a new email or SMS message in Vision6. This only stores the message; it is NOT sent (use the Vision6 app to send a campaign, or vision6_send_transactional for a one-off send). Email needs email_type, subject and matching body fields (plain: content_text; html: content_html; plain-html: both; raw_html: content_html or content_html_raw). SMS needs content_sms. The drag-and-drop builder is not supported. POST /messages.

tools.name: vision6_update_message
tools.title: Update a message
tools.description: WRITE: change a saved message's name, subject, sender, folder or body. Only the fields you pass change. It does not send anything. PATCH /messages/{message_id}.

tools.name: vision6_send_transactional
tools.title: Send a transactional email or SMS
tools.description: WRITE: SENDS REAL EMAIL OR SMS to the recipients immediately (asynchronously) and USES ACCOUNT SENDING CREDITS. It cannot be recalled. Up to 100 recipients per call, each identified by exactly one of contact_id, email or mobile, plus optional personalisation values (wildcards %%key%% in the body). Either send a saved message (message_id) or custom content (subject/body_html/body_text, and for SMS body_text + from_address). Unsubscribed addresses are skipped. Email always needs list_id. Results appear in the transactional group (vision6_get_transactional_group). The account owner's email must be confirmed in Vision6 first. Pass confirm_send=true only after the user approved these recipients and this content. POST /transactional-sends.

tools.name: vision6_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: vision6_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Vision6 tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: vision6_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Vision6 (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: vision6_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Vision6 Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run vision6_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: WaiverFile
servers.description: Read WaiverFile waivers, events, forms and SMS opt-ins; create and update events, invite managers.

login.hint: In WaiverFile open **Settings → API → API keys**. Click **Create a Key** if you have none, click **Show** to reveal the key, and copy the **Site ID** shown below it. The key gives access to your signers' personal data and can create events; revoke it there at any time. Your key is used only to call the WaiverFile API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: waiverfile_get_site
tools.title: Get site details
tools.description: Details of the WaiverFile site (WaiverSite) this API key belongs to: name, settings and plan information as WaiverFile reports them. GET /GetSiteDetails.

tools.name: waiverfile_list_waiver_forms
tools.title: List waiver forms
tools.description: List the waiver forms of the site (name, id, which fields they collect: email, address, phone, date of birth, minimum age, signature). Active forms by default; set include_deleted for all forms including deleted ones. Use the form ids when creating or updating events. GET /GetActiveWaiverForms or /GetAllWaiverForms.

tools.name: waiverfile_list_events
tools.title: List events by date range
tools.description: List waiver events (a class, tour, party or session that collects waivers) whose date falls in a range, optionally only one event category. Each event has an id, name, start/end, headcount and spots remaining. Dates are UTC. GET /GetEventsByDateRange or /GetEventsByCategory.

tools.name: waiverfile_list_upcoming_events
tools.title: List upcoming events
tools.description: List upcoming waiver events between two dates (UTC), for example the next 7 days. GET /GetUpcomingEvents.

tools.name: waiverfile_list_event_categories
tools.title: List event categories
tools.description: List the event categories of the site (id and name). Use the ids to filter events or to put a new event in a category. GET /GetEventCategories.

tools.name: waiverfile_get_event_waivers
tools.title: Get waivers for an event
tools.description: The waivers collected for one event: who signed, when, and the participants. Personal data of signers. GET /GetWaiversForEvent.

tools.name: waiverfile_search_waivers
tools.title: Search waivers
tools.description: Search signed waivers by free-text terms (a signer's name, email or phone). Personal data of signers. GET /SearchWaivers.

tools.name: waiverfile_get_waiver
tools.title: Get a waiver
tools.description: One signed waiver by id: signer, date signed, participants, collected form data, event and the agreement text. Set lite for only the collected form data (no agreement text or event info). Signature and image bytes are never returned. GET /GetWaiver or /GetWaiverLite.

tools.name: waiverfile_find_waivers_by_reference
tools.title: Find waivers by reference id
tools.description: Find waivers by the reference ids an outside booking or reservation system attached to them (referenceID1, 2, 3). Give at least one of reference_id_1/2/3, or reference_id_any to match all three fields. GET /GetWaiversByReferenceID.

tools.name: waiverfile_list_waivers
tools.title: List waivers by date range
tools.description: A page of the waivers signed in a date range. Set lite for only the collected form data (smaller). For a flat export with custom form columns use waiverfile_export_waiver_data; for totals use waiverfile_count_waivers. Personal data of signers. GET /GetAllWaiversByDateRange or /GetAllWaiversByDateRangeLite.

tools.name: waiverfile_export_waiver_data
tools.title: Export waiver data
tools.description: A page of flat waiver rows for a date range (the data behind the WaiverFile export): standard fields, optionally every custom form field as a column, and participants either as one comma-separated column or one row each. Personal data of signers. GET /GetWaiverData.

tools.name: waiverfile_count_waivers
tools.title: Count waivers in a date range
tools.description: How many waivers a date range holds: record_count (GetWaiverDataCount, the rows waiverfile_export_waiver_data pages through) and waiver_count (GetAllWaiversByDateRangePageCount, which WaiverFile documents as the number of waivers in the range, used to work out the pages of waiverfile_list_waivers). pages_at_page_size is waiver_count divided by page_size (default 25), rounded up. GET /GetWaiverDataCount and /GetAllWaiversByDateRangePageCount.

tools.name: waiverfile_list_sms_subscribers
tools.title: List SMS subscribers
tools.description: SMS marketing subscribers (phone numbers) that opted in during a date range, or with opted_out set the ones that opted out. Dates are UTC. Personal data. GET /GetSubscribersByDate or /GetOptedOutSubscribersByOptOutDate.

tools.name: waiverfile_create_event
tools.title: Create an event
tools.description: Create a waiver event (a class, tour or session that collects waivers) with a name and a start/end time (UTC). Optionally an all-day flag, category, location, signing cut-off, participant limit and which waiver forms to attach (default: WaiverFile's own choice, see list_waiver_forms). Not idempotent: calling twice creates two events. Sends no email. POST /InsertEvent.

tools.name: waiverfile_update_event
tools.title: Update an event
tools.description: Update an existing event. WaiverFile replaces the whole event, so name, start, end and all_day are required and anything left out is reset: category_id empty = no category, waiver_form_ids empty = ALL active forms are attached. Read the event first (waiverfile_list_events) and send its current values for the fields you do not change. Same input twice gives the same result. POST /UpdateEvent.

tools.name: waiverfile_invite_event_managers
tools.title: Invite event managers
tools.description: SENDS EMAIL: invites people (by email address) to manage one event; they can log in to WaiverFile and see its signers and participants, with the fields set in the account settings. WaiverFile emails each address, with your optional message in the body (skip_email_if_account_exists suppresses the email for people who already have an account). Cannot be undone by this server except with the vendor's own remove-managers action. Requires confirm=true after the user approved it. POST /InviteEventManagers.

tools.name: waiverfile_create_event_category
tools.title: Create an event category
tools.description: Create an event category (a label to group events). Not idempotent: calling twice with the same name creates two categories. POST /InsertEventCategory.

tools.name: waiverfile_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the WaiverFile tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on WaiverFile (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: Instamojo
servers.description: Read Instamojo payment requests, payments and refunds; create payment links and refund payments.

login.hint: Find both on [instamojo.com/integrations](https://www.instamojo.com/integrations/). The keys act on your whole account, so treat them like a password. They are used only to call the Instamojo API on your behalf and are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: instamojo_list_payment_requests
tools.title: List payment requests
tools.description: List the payment requests (payment links) of the account with id, purpose, amount (INR), buyer, status (Pending, Sent, Failed, Completed), short and long URL and timestamps. Paged: use next_page. GET /payment-requests/.

tools.name: instamojo_get_payment_request
tools.title: Get payment request
tools.description: One payment request by id, with its status and the payments made against it (the payment ids go to instamojo_get_payment). GET /payment-requests/{id}/.

tools.name: instamojo_create_payment_request
tools.title: Create payment request
tools.description: WRITE: create a payment request (a payment link) and return its id and URLs (longurl, shorturl) to share with the buyer. Amount is in INR. The buyer is NOT emailed or texted unless send_email / send_sms is true (they then need email / phone). Nothing is charged; the buyer pays on the link. POST /payment-requests/.

tools.name: instamojo_disable_payment_request
tools.title: Disable payment request
tools.description: WRITE: disable a payment request so its link no longer accepts payments (instamojo_enable_payment_request undoes it). Existing payments are not touched. POST /payment-requests/{id}/disable/.

tools.name: instamojo_enable_payment_request
tools.title: Enable payment request
tools.description: WRITE: enable a previously disabled payment request so its link accepts payments again. POST /payment-requests/{id}/enable/.

tools.name: instamojo_get_payment
tools.title: Get payment
tools.description: One payment by its id (MOJO...): status (Credit = paid, Failed), amount, fees, buyer, instrument (card, UPI, netbanking, wallet), failure reason, payout and the payment request it belongs to. GET /payments/{id}/.

tools.name: instamojo_list_refunds
tools.title: List refunds
tools.description: List refunds with id (case id), payment id, status, reason type, refund and total amount (INR) and date. Paged: use next_page. GET /refunds/.

tools.name: instamojo_get_refund
tools.title: Get refund
tools.description: One refund by its id (the case id from instamojo_list_refunds, e.g. C5c0751272). GET /refunds/{id}/.

tools.name: instamojo_create_refund
tools.title: Create refund
tools.description: WRITE (moves money): refund a payment, in full or in part. Instamojo allows only ONE refund per payment, so a partial refund cannot be topped up later. Without confirm: true nothing is sent and the call returns a preview of the refund; ask the user to confirm, then call again with confirm: true. Reason types: RFD = duplicate/delayed payment, TNR = product/service no longer available, QFL = customer not satisfied, QNR = product lost/damaged, EWN = digital download issue, TAN = event was canceled/changed, PTH = problem not described above. POST /refunds/.

Does not count against the meter.

Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). servers.name: Stuart
servers.description: Quote, validate, book and track Stuart courier deliveries; cancel jobs and check zone coverage.

login.hint: Find both in the Stuart admin under **API credentials** (admin.stuart.com for production, admin.sandbox.stuart.com for the sandbox; they are separate). Pick the matching environment below. We exchange the pair for an access token with Stuart; your credentials are used only to call the API on your behalf and are never shown to anyone. Creating a job books a real, charged courier on production: use the sandbox to try things out.

tools.name: stuart_list_jobs
tools.title: List delivery jobs
tools.description: List the delivery jobs of the last 90 days, newest pickup first, with status, deliveries (tracking URLs, courier proof), driver and pricing. Filter by status, active or your client_reference. Paginated: when a page returns per_page rows, ask for the next page. Stuart: GET /v2/jobs.

tools.name: stuart_get_job
tools.title: Get a delivery job
tools.description: One job in full: status, each delivery with tracking URL, pickup/dropoff addresses and contacts, ETA, cancellation, proof of delivery, driver, distance and pricing. Stuart: GET /v2/jobs/{jobId}.

tools.name: stuart_estimate_price
tools.title: Get a delivery price quote
tools.description: Price of a job before you create it: amount excluding and including tax, and currency. Nothing is booked. Needs pickup address, dropoff address and package type. Stuart: POST /v2/jobs/pricing.

tools.name: stuart_validate_job
tools.title: Validate a delivery job
tools.description: Check that a job would be accepted (addresses geocode inside a covered zone, fields valid) without creating it. Returns {valid}. Stuart: POST /v2/jobs/validate.

tools.name: stuart_estimate_pickup_eta
tools.title: Estimate courier arrival at pickup
tools.description: Estimated seconds until a courier could arrive at the pickup address, for the same job body as create. Nothing is booked. Stuart: POST /v2/jobs/eta.

tools.name: stuart_estimate_dropoff_eta
tools.title: Estimate time to dropoff
tools.description: Estimated seconds to reach the destination address for a job (coordinates need the text address too). Nothing is booked. Stuart: POST /v2/jobs/cpt.

tools.name: stuart_validate_address
tools.title: Validate a pickup or dropoff address
tools.description: Check that an address can be geocoded and lies inside a Stuart zone, as a pickup (picking) or a dropoff (delivering). A phone number is needed when the address is approximate. Stuart: POST /v2/addresses/validate.

tools.name: stuart_get_zone_coverage
tools.title: Get a zone's coverage area
tools.description: GeoJSON of the picking or delivery area of an open Stuart zone (for example paris, london). Stuart: GET /v2/areas/{zone}.

tools.name: stuart_get_zone_schedule_slots
tools.title: Get a zone's scheduling slots
tools.description: Available time slots (start and end, 15-minute steps) in a zone for a date, from the time of the request onward. Use a future date. Stuart: GET /v2/jobs/schedules/{zone}/{type}/{date}.

tools.name: stuart_get_courier_phone
tools.title: Get the courier's anonymous phone number
tools.description: Anonymised phone number of the courier assigned to a delivery. Only works once a courier is assigned; expires when the delivery ends. Stuart: GET /v2/deliveries/{deliveryId}/phone_number.

tools.name: stuart_create_job
tools.title: Create a delivery job (dispatches a courier)
tools.description: BOOKS A REAL, CHARGED DELIVERY: creates a job with one pickup and 1-8 dropoffs and starts looking for a courier right away (unless pickup_at schedules it: up to 4 days ahead, 30 for corporate accounts). Get a quote with stuart_estimate_price and check with stuart_validate_job first, and confirm with the user. Use the sandbox environment for tests. Stuart: POST /v2/jobs.

tools.name: stuart_update_job
tools.title: Update delivery details
tools.description: Change allowed details of a delivery in a job: client_reference, package_description, and the pickup/dropoff comment and contact (what is editable depends on the delivery status: once delivered only client_reference). Stuart: PATCH /v2/jobs/{jobId}.

tools.name: stuart_cancel_job
tools.title: Cancel a delivery job
tools.description: Cancels a whole job and all its deliveries. Stuart may charge a cancellation fee once a courier is on the way; confirm with the user first. Give a reason key for reporting. Stuart: POST /v2/jobs/{jobId}/cancel.

tools.name: stuart_cancel_delivery
tools.title: Cancel one delivery
tools.description: Cancels a single delivery (one dropoff) of a multi-drop job. A cancellation fee may apply; confirm with the user first. Stuart: POST /v2/deliveries/{deliveryId}/cancel.

tools.name: stuart_mark_order_ready
tools.title: Signal that an order is ready for pickup
tools.description: Tell Stuart the order is packed and ready for the courier to collect. Pass exactly one of job_id (all orders of the job) or delivery_id (one order). Send it only when the order is really ready. Stuart: POST /v2/jobs/{jobId}/order_ready or /v2/deliveries/{deliveryId}/order_ready.

tools.name: stuart_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: stuart_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Stuart tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: stuart_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Stuart (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: stuart_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Stuart Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run stuart_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: GoCanvas
servers.description: Read GoCanvas forms, submissions, users, dispatches and reference data; create dispatches.

login.hint: In GoCanvas, open your **profile → API Settings** (administrator) and create an **OAuth application**; copy the client ID and the client secret (shown only once). API v3 is included in the Pro and Max plans or available as an add-on. The server acts as the user who owns the application and sees what that user can see. Your credentials are used only to call the GoCanvas API on your behalf and to derive a private account id.

tools.name: gocanvas_get_me
tools.title: Get the connected GoCanvas user
tools.description: The user who owns the connected OAuth application: id, login, company id and name, default department and role. Use it to learn the default department id.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_forms
tools.title: List GoCanvas forms
tools.description: Forms (mobile form definitions) the connected user can see: id, name, status, version, department. Paged, 100 per page. Use gocanvas_get_form for a form's fields (entries).

tools.name: gocanvas_get_form
tools.title: Get a GoCanvas form definition
tools.description: One form definition, including its screens and entries (field ids and labels). Use format 'flat' for the simplest list of fields (what you need to read submissions or create a dispatch), 'nested' (default) for the full structure, 'metadata' or 'minimal' for less.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_form_reports
tools.title: List report definitions of a GoCanvas form
tools.description: The report (PDF) definitions attached to a form: id, name, format, whether emailed by default. Paged.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_submissions
tools.title: List GoCanvas submissions
tools.description: Completed forms (submissions): id, form, number, created time, department, user, status. At least one of form_id, user_id or user_email is required (user_id and user_email cannot be combined). Default status is completed. Dates filter created_at. Paged, 100 per page. Use gocanvas_get_submission for the answers.

tools.name: gocanvas_get_submission
tools.title: Get a GoCanvas submission
tools.description: One submission with all its responses (entry id, label, type, value). Accepts the numeric submission id or the client GUID.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_submission_revisions
tools.title: List revisions of a GoCanvas submission
tools.description: The revision history of a submission (who changed it and when). Paged.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_users
tools.title: List GoCanvas users
tools.description: Users of the company: id, name, email, enabled. Paged, 100 per page.

tools.name: gocanvas_get_user
tools.title: Get a GoCanvas user
tools.description: One user by id: name, login, contact data, default department and role.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_departments
tools.title: List GoCanvas departments
tools.description: Departments of the company: id, name, description. The pseudo department -1 'All' is included.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_department_users
tools.title: List users of a GoCanvas department
tools.description: The users in one department with their department role.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_dispatches
tools.title: List GoCanvas dispatches
tools.description: Dispatches (jobs sent to field workers): id, form, assignee, status, schedule. At least one of user_id, department_id or form_id is required. Dates are ISO-8601. Paged.

tools.name: gocanvas_get_dispatch
tools.title: Get a GoCanvas dispatch
tools.description: One dispatch by id with its pre-filled responses, schedule and status.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_customers
tools.title: List GoCanvas customers
tools.description: Customers (contacts of the Project Management view): individuals or businesses, optionally tied to a site. Paged.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_projects
tools.title: List GoCanvas projects
tools.description: Projects of the Project Management view. Paged.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_sites
tools.title: List GoCanvas sites
tools.description: Sites (job locations) of the Project Management view. Paged.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_reference_data
tools.title: List GoCanvas reference data sets
tools.description: Reference data (lookup tables used by forms): id, name, columns, version. Without department_id the user's default department is used.

tools.name: gocanvas_get_reference_data
tools.title: Get a GoCanvas reference data set
tools.description: One reference data set with its rows.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_groups
tools.title: List GoCanvas groups
tools.description: User groups: id, name, and the forms and users assigned. Paged.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_workflows
tools.title: List GoCanvas workflows
tools.description: Workflows (handoff chains between users) the connected user takes part in, with their handoff states and the count of tasks available to claim. Paged.

tools.name: gocanvas_list_locations
tools.title: List GoCanvas tracker locations
tools.description: GPS location events of field users (needs the tracker feature). start_date and end_date are required and may span at most 7 days. Omit user_id for all users of the company. Paged.

tools.name: gocanvas_create_dispatch
tools.title: Create a GoCanvas dispatch
tools.description: WRITE: creates a dispatch, a job that appears on the assignee's mobile device (immediate_dispatch is sent at once, with a push notification when send_notification is true; scheduled_dispatch needs scheduled_at and scheduled_end). Responses pre-fill the assignee's form (entry ids from gocanvas_get_form). Without assignee_id the dispatch stays unassigned. Not idempotent: calling twice creates two dispatches. Media fields cannot be pre-filled.

tools.name: gocanvas_mark_dispatch_received
tools.title: Mark a GoCanvas dispatch as received
tools.description: WRITE: acknowledges a dispatch (status becomes received). Only works for a dispatch in the assigned state that is assigned to the connected user; repeating it is refused by GoCanvas.

tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.description: Cancel the caller's GoCanvas Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). servers.name: Axis LMS
servers.description: Read Axis LMS users, courses, learning paths, certifications and reports; manage enrollments.

login.hint: The address is the one your learners sign in at, for example **https://training.yourcompany.com** (https only). Create the key in your LMS admin area under **System > Integrations > Axis REST API > Manage API Keys**; the Axis REST API must be enabled for your system. The key can read and change users, enrollments and groups, so create one for this connection and delete it in the same place to disconnect. Your key is used only to call your LMS on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: axislms_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the LMS users (id and username only), active, inactive or all. Not paged: a large LMS returns every user. For names, emails or filters use axislms_search_users. GET /users/list/{status}/.

tools.name: axislms_get_user
tools.title: Get user
tools.description: One user by id with the fields you ask for: profile (name, email, address, phone, custom1-15, role, manager_id, dates), usergroups, enrolled courses, ILT classes, certifications, learning paths, badges, organizations and system variables. Contains personal data. GET /users/{id}/?fields=.

tools.name: axislms_search_users
tools.title: Search users
tools.description: Page through all users, or only those matching a search phrase (for example email~example.com,role=manager), returning the fields you ask for. Contains personal data. GET /users/all/ or /users/filtered/ (page{n}).

tools.name: axislms_count_users
tools.title: Count users
tools.description: Number of users, all or matching a search phrase. GET /users/all/count/ or /users/filtered/count/?user_filter=.

tools.name: axislms_list_courses
tools.title: List courses
tools.description: List the active online courses (id and name), plus the count. GET /courses/list/.

tools.name: axislms_count_courses
tools.title: Count courses
tools.description: Number of active online courses. GET /courses/count/.

tools.name: axislms_get_course
tools.title: Get course
tools.description: One online course: name, catalog id, description, active flag, created/updated dates, keyword tags, passing score, price and whether it is for sale, thumbnail, webhook. GET /courses/{id}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_course_users
tools.title: List users in a course
tools.description: Users enrolled in a course with their access start and end dates (YYYYMMDD): active, expired or all enrollments. GET /courses/{id}/users/{status}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_usergroups
tools.title: List usergroups
tools.description: List usergroups (id and name). GET /usergroups/list/.

tools.name: axislms_get_usergroup
tools.title: Get usergroup
tools.description: One usergroup: name, member counts (active, inactive, total) and owner. GET /usergroups/{id}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_usergroup_members
tools.title: List usergroup members
tools.description: Members of a usergroup (id and username): active, inactive or all. GET /usergroups/{id}/members/{status}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_learningpaths
tools.title: List learning paths
tools.description: List the active learning paths (id and name). GET /learningpaths/list/.

tools.name: axislms_list_learningpath_users
tools.title: List users in a learning path
tools.description: Active enrolled users of a learning path (or one user), with status, start and completion time, completion method, path version, current branch and step, and progress. GET /learningpaths/{id}/users/[{user_id}/].

tools.name: axislms_list_certifications
tools.title: List certification programs
tools.description: List certification programs (id and name): active, inactive or all. GET /certifications/list/{status}/.

tools.name: axislms_get_certification
tools.title: Get certification program
tools.description: One certification program: name, prefix, description, keyword tags, webhook and status. GET /certifications/{program_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_certification_users
tools.title: List certified users
tools.description: Users certified in a certification program (id and username). GET /certifications/{program_id}/users/.

tools.name: axislms_list_user_certificates
tools.title: List a user's certifications
tools.description: The certifications a user holds: program, certification number, issue, renew and expire dates (YYYYMMDD). GET /certifications/certificates/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_user_ceus
tools.title: List a user's CEU credits
tools.description: Continuing-education credits (CEUs) a user earned: type, name, credits and issue date. GET /certifications/ceus/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_ilt_programs
tools.title: List ILT programs
tools.description: List instructor-led training (ILT) programs (id and name). GET /ilt/list/.

tools.name: axislms_get_ilt_program
tools.title: Get ILT program
tools.description: One ILT program: name, catalog id, description and keyword tags. GET /ilt/{program_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_ilt_sessions
tools.title: List ILT sessions
tools.description: Sessions of an ILT program with start and end dates and seats (total, reserved, remaining): current ones or all. GET /ilt/{program_id}/sessions/{current|all}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_ilt_meetings
tools.title: List ILT meetings
tools.description: Meetings of one ILT session: date, time, timezone, duration, GMT start and end, facility. GET /ilt/{program_id}/meetings/{session_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_ilt_completions
tools.title: List ILT completions
tools.description: Users who completed an ILT program, or one session of it (id and username). GET /ilt/{program_id}/completions/[{session_id}/].

tools.name: axislms_list_user_ilt_sessions
tools.title: List a user's ILT sessions
tools.description: ILT sessions a user is part of: program, session, start and end dates and percent attended. GET /ilt/users/{user_id}/sessions/.

tools.name: axislms_list_organizations
tools.title: List organizations
tools.description: List organizations with owner id and user count, all or those owned by one manager (owner id 0 = the partition admin). GET /organizations/list/{all|owner_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_organization_branches
tools.title: List organization branches
tools.description: The branches of an organization (nested branches included). GET /organizations/branches/{organization_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_list_organization_users
tools.title: List organization users
tools.description: Users in an organization (id, username, branch id): active, inactive or all. GET /organizations/users/{organization_id}/{status}/.

tools.name: axislms_course_report
tools.title: Course report
tools.description: Who is doing what in one online course: user, status, progress %, score, start and completion date (YYYYMMDD). Filter by users, status, progress, score and dates. Limited to users currently enrolled who accessed the course or have score data. Paged (100 per page). GET /reports/courses/{course_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_certification_report
tools.title: Certification report
tools.description: Certifications issued in one certification program: user, certification number, how it was earned, issue, renewed and expire date (YYYYMMDD). Filter by users, number, method and dates. Paged (100 per page). GET /reports/certifications/{program_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_learningpath_report
tools.title: Learning path report
tools.description: Learning path enrollments and results for one path: user, status (complete or incomplete), active or archived, start and completion date (YYYYMMDD). Paged (100 per page). GET /reports/learningpaths/{learningpath_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_ilt_report
tools.title: ILT report
tools.description: Attendance and results of one ILT program: user, session, start and end date, meetings and meetings attended, status. Filter by users, status, session and dates. Paged (100 per page). GET /reports/ilt/{program_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_user_report
tools.title: User transcript report
tools.description: A learner's records across the LMS, for one user, for all users, or for users matching a search phrase. kind: courses (status, progress, score, dates), archived (archived and imported course results), certifications, ilt, or learningpaths. Contains personal data; paged (100 per page). GET /reports/users/{user_id|all|filtered}/{kind}/.

tools.name: axislms_enroll_user_in_course
tools.title: Enroll a user in a course
tools.description: WRITE: enroll a user in an online course (optionally with access start and end dates). The user and the course must be active. If the user is already enrolled, send start or end to change the enrollment dates. Depending on the LMS settings the user may be notified. POST /courses/enrollments/{course_id}/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_unenroll_user_from_course
tools.title: Remove a user from a course
tools.description: WRITE: remove a user from an online course. The user loses access to the course. DELETE /courses/enrollments/{course_id}/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_enroll_user_in_learningpath
tools.title: Enroll a user in a learning path
tools.description: WRITE: enroll an active user in a learning path. The user must not already be enrolled. POST /learningpaths/enrollments/{learningpath_id}/users/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_unenroll_user_from_learningpath
tools.title: Remove a user from a learning path
tools.description: WRITE: remove a user from a learning path they are enrolled in. DELETE /learningpaths/enrollments/{learningpath_id}/users/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_enroll_user_in_ilt_session
tools.title: Enroll a user in an ILT session
tools.description: WRITE: enroll a user in a session of an ILT program (takes a seat; check seats_remaining with axislms_list_ilt_sessions first). POST /ilt/enrollments/{program_id}/{session_id}/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_unenroll_user_from_ilt_session
tools.title: Remove a user from an ILT session
tools.description: WRITE: remove a user from a session of an ILT program. DELETE /ilt/enrollments/{program_id}/{session_id}/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_mark_ilt_attendance
tools.title: Mark ILT attendance
tools.description: WRITE: mark a user attended or absent for one ILT meeting. The user must already be enrolled in the meeting. Attendance can count toward completion. PUT /ilt/attendance/{program_id}/{session_id}/{meeting_id}/{user_id}/{attended|absent}/.

tools.name: axislms_create_user
tools.title: Create a user
tools.description: WRITE: create a new LMS user. The username must be 4-40 characters (letters, numbers, @ . _ -) and not in use. Returns the new user id. The temporary password the LMS generates is never shown here: give the person access through the LMS itself (its password reset, invitation or single sign-on). Depending on the LMS settings the user may be notified. POST /users/.

tools.name: axislms_update_user
tools.title: Update a user
tools.description: WRITE: change profile fields of an existing user (only the fields you send are changed; an empty value is not sent, so a field cannot be cleared here). This edits personal data and can change the user's role or manager. PUT /users/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_create_usergroup
tools.title: Create a usergroup
tools.description: WRITE: create a usergroup. The name must be 4-99 characters (letters, numbers, spaces and @ . _ -). Returns its id. POST /usergroups/{name}/.

tools.name: axislms_add_usergroup_member
tools.title: Add a user to a usergroup
tools.description: WRITE: add a user to a usergroup (they must not already be a member). Groups can drive course or path assignments. POST /usergroups/members/{usergroup_id}/{user_id}/.

tools.name: axislms_remove_usergroup_member
tools.title: Remove a user from a usergroup
tools.description: WRITE: remove a user from a usergroup they are a member of. DELETE /usergroups/members/{usergroup_id}/{user_id}/.
