servers.name: Bookingmood
servers.description: Read Bookingmood bookings, availability, guests, payments and invoices; update bookings, contacts.

login.hint: Create the key in your Bookingmood admin dashboard: **Settings** of your organization, **API keys** at the bottom of the page. The key belongs to your organization. Your key is used only to call the Bookingmood API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: bookingmood_get_organization
tools.title: Get organization
tools.description: The Bookingmood organization this API key belongs to: name, company, plan (tier, subscription type, expiry), languages, country, VAT number, custom domain and contact details. Payment-provider ids and secrets are not returned. GET /organizations.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_products
tools.title: List products (rentals)
tools.description: List the rentable products (apartments, rooms, boats, bikes...) with name, currency, timezone, rent period (daily/nightly), booking interaction, fee and deposit. Names and descriptions are objects keyed by language ('default', 'nl-NL', ...). Images are not returned. GET /products.

tools.name: bookingmood_get_product
tools.title: Get product
tools.description: One product by id with its capacities (guest-group min/max limits) embedded. GET /products?id=eq.{id}&select=*,capacities(*).

tools.name: bookingmood_list_bookings
tools.title: List bookings
tools.description: List bookings, newest first: reference, method (request or book), currency, confirmed_at (null = not confirmed yet), created_at. A booking's dates and guests are on its calendar events (bookingmood_list_calendar_events) and contacts. Filter by creation date, confirmation state or reference text. The guest access secret is never returned. GET /bookings.

tools.name: bookingmood_get_booking
tools.title: Get booking with details
tools.description: One booking with everything attached: its calendar events (dates, product, status, occupancy, notes), line items, payments, invoices and the guest contacts linked to it. Five or six read requests. The guest contacts come from the booking-contact link table; if that lookup fails the reply says so instead of failing. GET /bookings, /calendar_events, /line_items, /payments, /invoices, /contact_bookings, /contacts.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_calendar_events
tools.title: List calendar events
tools.description: List calendar events: bookings (type 'booking'), blocked periods and notes, with product_id, booking_id, start_date, end_date, status (TENTATIVE, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED), occupancy, title and notes. Use the date filters for arrivals/departures (e.g. start_date_from = start_date_to = today lists today's arrivals) or active_on for who is in the property on a day. Ordered by start date. GET /calendar_events.

tools.name: bookingmood_check_availability
tools.title: Check availability
tools.description: Availability calendar of up to 5 products: per product a list of intervals {start, end, status} with status available, tentative, unavailable, booked or reserved. One request per product. GET /availability?product_id={id}.

tools.name: bookingmood_search_products
tools.title: Search available products
tools.description: Which products can be booked for a stay: for each product whether it matches the dates, guest numbers and options, its availability and a price range {min, max}. Read-only (a search; nothing is booked). occupancy maps a capacity-group id (from bookingmood_get_product capacities) to a number of guests. POST /search.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts (guests)
tools.description: List contacts (guests and customers): name, email, phone, company, address, language, notes. Search by name, email or company (case-insensitive, contains). Newest first. GET /contacts.

tools.name: bookingmood_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact by id. GET /contacts?id=eq.{id}.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_payments
tools.title: List payments
tools.description: List payments (deposits, balances, offline payments): booking_id, invoice_id, amount and paid (integers; the API reference does not state the unit, normally the smallest currency unit), currency, due_at, completed_at (null = not paid), status, offline. Filter to unpaid payments, a booking or a due date. Ordered by due date, latest first. GET /payments.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices: reference, booking_id, attachment (a custom uploaded file URL, if any), created_at. Filter by booking or creation date. Newest first. GET /invoices.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_line_items
tools.title: List line items
tools.description: List invoice/booking line items: name (per language), amount and quantity (integers; the API reference does not state the unit), item_type (rent, fee...), fee_type (fee or deposit), booking_id, event_id, invoice_id. GET /line_items.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_coupons
tools.title: List coupons
tools.description: List discount coupons: code, description, definition, quota, scope (global, product, service, rent), stackable. Deleted coupons are left out. GET /coupons.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_services
tools.title: List services (extras and fees)
tools.description: List services: the extras, fees and form fields guests can add to a booking, with label, type, fee, deposit and description. GET /services.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List housekeeping/operations tasks attached to calendar events: label, due_at, completed_at (null = open), schedule (manual, arrival, departure), calendar_event_id. Filter to open tasks or a due-date window. Earliest due first. GET /tasks.

tools.name: bookingmood_list_messages
tools.title: List guest messages
tools.description: List the e-mails and SMS Bookingmood sent or scheduled to guests: subject, body, type (email or sms), status (sent, manually-scheduled, scheduled-around-arrival, scheduled-around-departure), send_at, booking_id. The rendered HTML is not returned. Latest first. GET /messages.

tools.name: bookingmood_update_event_notes
tools.title: Set calendar event notes
tools.description: WRITE: replace the internal notes of ONE calendar event (the whole notes text is overwritten, so include the existing text if you want to keep it - read it first with bookingmood_list_calendar_events). Notes are internal; no guest is notified. PATCH /calendar_events?id=eq.{id}.

tools.name: bookingmood_set_event_status
tools.title: Set calendar event status (confirm / cancel)
tools.description: WRITE: change the status of ONE calendar event to CONFIRMED, TENTATIVE or CANCELLED. This changes what the calendar shows as available and can trigger Bookingmood's own automations for the booking (guest e-mails, tasks, payment reminders), so confirm with the user before cancelling or confirming. PATCH /calendar_events?id=eq.{id}.

tools.name: bookingmood_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: create ONE new contact (guest/customer) in Bookingmood. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two contacts, so search with bookingmood_list_contacts first. No message is sent to the contact. POST /contacts.

tools.name: bookingmood_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of ONE existing contact (only the fields you pass are changed; others stay). No message is sent to the contact. PATCH /contacts?id=eq.{id}.

tools.name: bookingmood_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: bookingmood_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Bookingmood tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: bookingmood_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Bookingmood (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: bookingmood_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Bookingmood Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run bookingmood_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Who arrives at my properties this weekend?
Which payments are still open and past their due date?
Is the beach house free from 12 to 19 July for 4 guests, and at what price?
Add a note to this booking: guests arrive late, key in the lockbox.

servers.name: Mail Blaze
servers.description: Manage Mail Blaze lists, subscribers, templates, campaigns and reports; send transactional email.

login.hint: Find it in Mail Blaze → your **Profile menu → API Keys**: create a key and copy the **Public key**. The key acts with full access to your account; you can revoke it there at any time. Your key is used only to call the Mail Blaze API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: mailblaze_list_lists
tools.title: List mailing lists
tools.description: List the account's mailing lists (name, uid, subscriber counts, defaults). Use the list uid in the other tools. Paged: page + per_page.

tools.name: mailblaze_get_list
tools.title: Get a mailing list
tools.description: Get one mailing list by its uid: general settings, default sender, company details and counts.

tools.name: mailblaze_list_list_fields
tools.title: List a list's custom fields
tools.description: List the fields of a mailing list (label, tag, type, required). The tags (EMAIL, FNAME, LNAME, custom ones) are the keys used when adding or updating subscribers.

tools.name: mailblaze_list_segments
tools.title: List a list's segments
tools.description: List the segments defined on a mailing list (uid, name). A segment uid can be used when creating a campaign.

tools.name: mailblaze_list_subscribers
tools.title: List subscribers
tools.description: List the subscribers of a mailing list (sets of 10 per page; use page to go on). Contains personal data (emails, names).

tools.name: mailblaze_get_subscriber
tools.title: Get a subscriber
tools.description: Get one subscriber of a list by subscriber uid (status, fields, dates).

tools.name: mailblaze_find_subscriber_by_email
tools.title: Find a subscriber by email
tools.description: Look up a subscriber in one list by email address. Returns the subscriber (with its uid) or a not-found error.

tools.name: mailblaze_add_subscriber
tools.title: Add a subscriber
tools.description: WRITE, MAY SEND A CONFIRMATION EMAIL: add one subscriber to a mailing list. Depending on the list's settings Mail Blaze may send the person a confirmation (double opt-in) email. Only add people who agreed to receive your email. An email that is already on the list answers with a conflict error.

tools.name: mailblaze_add_subscribers_bulk
tools.title: Add or update subscribers in bulk
tools.description: WRITE, MAY SEND CONFIRMATION EMAILS: add up to 100 subscribers to a mailing list in one request; an email already on the list is updated instead. Depending on the list's settings Mail Blaze may send confirmation emails. Only add people who agreed to receive your email.

tools.name: mailblaze_update_subscriber
tools.title: Update a subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: update a subscriber's name or custom fields. Pass the subscriber's current email (Mail Blaze requires it) plus only the values to change. Does not change subscription status.

tools.name: mailblaze_unsubscribe_subscriber
tools.title: Unsubscribe a subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: set a subscriber's status to unsubscribed so they receive no more campaigns from this list. By default Mail Blaze also adds the address to the account's local blacklist. Do this only when the person asked to stop (or a data-protection request requires it). The subscriber record is kept.

tools.name: mailblaze_resubscribe_subscriber
tools.title: Resubscribe a subscriber
tools.description: WRITE: set a previously unsubscribed subscriber back to subscribed so campaigns reach them again. Only do this when the person asked to be re-added (consent).

tools.name: mailblaze_list_templates
tools.title: List email templates
tools.description: List the account's email templates (uid, name). A template uid is needed to create a campaign.

tools.name: mailblaze_get_template
tools.title: Get an email template
tools.description: Get one email template by uid (name and content).

tools.name: mailblaze_create_template
tools.title: Create an email template
tools.description: WRITE: create an email template from HTML (the tool base64-encodes it). Mail Blaze requires the HTML to contain an unsubscribe link. Sends nothing.

tools.name: mailblaze_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: List the account's email campaigns (uid, name, status, dates). Use the campaign uid for details and reports.

tools.name: mailblaze_get_campaign
tools.title: Get a campaign
tools.description: Get one campaign by uid: sender, subject, list, template, status and schedule.

tools.name: mailblaze_create_campaign
tools.title: Create and schedule a campaign
tools.description: WRITE, SENDS EMAIL TO PEOPLE: create a campaign for a mailing list (or one of its segments) from an existing template and schedule it for send_at. Once it goes out it reaches every subscriber of the list or segment, may use sending credit and cannot be recalled. Confirm the list, segment, subject, template and send time with the user before calling. Needs a template uid (mailblaze_list_templates) and a list uid (mailblaze_list_lists).

tools.name: mailblaze_get_campaign_summaries
tools.title: Get campaign report summaries
tools.description: Bulk report summary (sent, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes) for up to 50 campaigns in one call. Read-only (it is a POST in the API only because of the id list).

tools.name: mailblaze_get_campaign_inbox_breakdown
tools.title: Get a campaign's inbox breakdown
tools.description: Inbox-provider breakdown (e.g. Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo) of a campaign's delivery.

tools.name: mailblaze_list_campaign_events
tools.title: List a campaign's opens, clicks, bounces or unsubscribes
tools.description: List the individual events of a campaign by kind: opens, clicks, bounces or unsubscribes. Cursor-paged: pass the reply's next_cursor back until it is null. For very large campaigns Mail Blaze answers 202 with a job_id; check it with mailblaze_get_report_job.

tools.name: mailblaze_get_subscriber_activity
tools.title: Get a subscriber's activity
tools.description: Email activity (sends, opens, clicks, bounces) of one subscriber by email address, optionally limited to one list. Cursor-paged.

tools.name: mailblaze_get_report_job
tools.title: Get a report job's status
tools.description: Status (and result when finished) of an asynchronous report job, as returned in a 202 reply with a job_id.

tools.name: mailblaze_list_transactional_emails
tools.title: List transactional emails
tools.description: List the transactional emails sent through the account (uid, recipient, subject, status). Paged.

tools.name: mailblaze_get_transactional_email
tools.title: Get a transactional email
tools.description: Get one transactional email by uid: recipient, subject, status and timestamps.

tools.name: mailblaze_send_transactional_email
tools.title: Send a transactional email
tools.description: WRITE, SENDS ONE EMAIL NOW: send a single one-to-one email to one recipient through Mail Blaze. It leaves immediately, uses sending credit and cannot be recalled. Give either html (the body) or template_id (a transactional template, with merge_tags covering every tag in it), not both. Confirm the recipient and content with the user before calling. Not for bulk or marketing mail; use a campaign for that.

tools.name: mailblaze_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: mailblaze_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the MailBlaze tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: mailblaze_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on MailBlaze (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: mailblaze_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's MailBlaze Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run mailblaze_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: How many subscribers are on each of my mailing lists?
Show the open and click rates of my last five campaigns.
Add jane@example.com to my newsletter list as Jane Smith.
Is anna@example.com subscribed, and what did she open recently?

servers.name: Parsley
servers.description: Read Parsley menu items, nutrition, allergens, ingredients and events; record event sales and waste.

login.hint: Generate an API key in your **Parsley account** (the Open API is switched on per account; if you do not see API keys, ask Parsley support at devel@parsleyapp.com). The key acts with the permissions of the user who created it. Your key is used only to call the Parsley API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: parsley_list_menu_items
tools.title: List menu items
tools.description: List the recipes, sub-recipes and ingredients in the Parsley account that can be used on events: id, name, item number, price, tags, active flag, chef and last-modified time. Use the ids with parsley_get_menu_item for nutrition, allergens and ingredients, and on events. The API returns the whole list at once; search/limit/offset slice it here. GET /menu_items.

tools.name: parsley_get_menu_item
tools.title: Get menu item (nutrition, allergens, ingredients)
tools.description: One menu item in full: names, description, price, cost, shelf life, serving size, nutrition facts (nutrients), the allergen flags and allergen text, dietary characteristics (meat, pork, corn, poultry) and the ingredient list. The photo link is returned without its access token. GET /menu_items/{id}.

tools.name: parsley_list_menus
tools.title: List menus
tools.description: List the menus (menu plans) in the account: id, name and last-modified time. Use the id with parsley_get_menu or when creating an event. GET /menus.

tools.name: parsley_get_menu
tools.title: Get menu
tools.description: One menu with its sections and the menu items in each section, and its serving stations. GET /menus/{id}.

tools.name: parsley_list_ingredients
tools.title: List ingredients
tools.description: List the ingredients that can be used in recipes: id, parent id, name, label name, item number, supported units, and whether a recipe uses it. The API returns the whole list at once; search/limit/offset slice it here. GET /ingredients.

tools.name: parsley_get_ingredient
tools.title: Get ingredient (costing and suppliers)
tools.description: One ingredient in full: unit conversions, supported units, tags, the supply options (supplier, SKU, pack size, cost) used for costing and the preparations with yield. Parsley limits this call to 1 request every 3 seconds, so fetch ingredients one at a time. GET /ingredients/{id}.

tools.name: parsley_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List events (a workday, shift, service or catering event) that fall in a date window: id, name, type (standard, cafe-hot-bar, sale, forecast), date, start and end time, menu id. A bare date means the whole day in the account timezone. GET /events.

tools.name: parsley_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event with its metadata and all line items (menu item, amount, unit, station, section). GET /events/{id}.

tools.name: parsley_list_serving_stations
tools.title: List serving stations
tools.description: List the serving stations (id, name) that menu items and event line items can be assigned to. GET /tags/serving_stations.

tools.name: parsley_list_chef_tags
tools.title: List chef tags
tools.description: List the chef tags (id, name) that recipes are attributed to. Only meaningful for accounts with Chef IDs enabled. GET /tags/chefs.

tools.name: parsley_list_chef_users
tools.title: List chef users
tools.description: List the chef users of the account: id, email, join date, active flag, permission level and the chef tag they are tied to. Only meaningful for accounts with Chef IDs enabled. GET /users/chefs.

tools.name: parsley_create_event
tools.title: Create event
tools.description: WRITE: create an event (a workday, shift, service or catering event) in Parsley with its menu items. This changes the account's production plan and is NOT idempotent: calling it twice creates two events. Returns the new event id. Use parsley_list_events first to avoid duplicates. POST /events.

tools.name: parsley_update_event_covers
tools.title: Update event covers
tools.description: WRITE: set the forecast and/or actual number of covers (guests served) on an event. Only the fields you pass change. actual_covers works only on cafe/hot bar events. Setting the same values again has no further effect. PATCH /events/{id}.

tools.name: parsley_record_event_sales
tools.title: Record event sales
tools.description: WRITE: push sold quantities per menu item to a cafe/hot bar event, which feeds Parsley's cost and usage reports. Other event types are refused by Parsley, as is a menu item with no made quantity on the event. Sending the same quantities again overwrites rather than adds. PUT /events/{id}/sales.

tools.name: parsley_record_waste_leftover
tools.title: Record waste and leftover
tools.description: WRITE: push waste and/or leftover quantities per menu item to a cafe/hot bar event. If no sold quantity exists, Parsley derives it as made minus waste minus leftover. Parsley refuses amounts above what was made minus sold. Sending the same quantities again overwrites rather than adds. PUT /events/{id}/waste_leftover.

tools.name: parsley_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: parsley_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Parsley tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: parsley_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Parsley (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: parsley_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Parsley Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run parsley_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which of our recipes contain peanuts or tree nuts?
Show the nutrition facts and ingredient list for the lemon chicken.
What events are on the calendar next week and which menu does each use?
Record 12 portions sold and 2 wasted of the soup of the day on today's cafe event.

servers.name: Placetel
servers.description: Read Placetel calls, recordings, numbers and routing; edit contacts, start calls, send SMS.

login.hint: Find it in Placetel at **Integrations → Web API** (web.placetel.de/integrations/web_api); an API v1 key works too. The key acts with your account's permissions. Your key is used only to call the Placetel API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: placetel_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The Placetel account this API key belongs to: user id, name, email, company, platform (e.g. PROFI), primary SIP user id and the numbers the key may use. GET /me.

tools.name: placetel_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the web users of the account (main account and sub-users) with name, email, login, type, permissions and numbers. Filter by name, email, login or type. GET /users.

tools.name: placetel_list_sip_users
tools.title: List SIP users (extensions)
tools.description: List SIP users (phone extensions, softphones, fax and trunk lines) with extension number (did), caller id, type, online state and registrations. SIP passwords and PINs are never returned. GET /sip_users.

tools.name: placetel_get_sip_user
tools.title: Get SIP user
tools.description: One SIP user (extension) by id: sipuid, extension, caller id, type, linked web user, online state and call settings. The SIP password and PINs are never returned. GET /sip_users/{id}.

tools.name: placetel_list_calls
tools.title: List incoming calls
tools.description: Incoming calls (accepted, missed, blocked, voicemail) on one day, today by default: caller number, called number, duration, matching contact, voicemail file URL and unread flag. For a different day pass date. GET /calls.

tools.name: placetel_get_call
tools.title: Get call
tools.description: One incoming call by id: caller, called number, type, duration, contact, voicemail file URL. GET /calls/{id}.

tools.name: placetel_list_call_detail_records
tools.title: List call detail records
tools.description: Call detail records (billing view) for one day: from, to, answering SIP user, length in seconds, cost amount and description. date is required. GET /call_detail_records.

tools.name: placetel_list_recordings
tools.title: List call recordings
tools.description: Call recordings with direction, from, to, duration, time and the file URL. Filter by direction, number or day. GET /recordings.

tools.name: placetel_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List the shared phone-book contacts with names, company, phone/mobile/fax numbers, emails, tags and blocked flag. Filter by name, company, email, number or update time. search_number finds a contact by any of its numbers. GET /contacts.

tools.name: placetel_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact by id with all its fields. GET /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: placetel_list_numbers
tools.title: List phone numbers
tools.description: List the phone numbers of the account with number, E.164 form, name, description, site, activation state and the routing object id that answers them. GET /numbers.

tools.name: placetel_get_number
tools.title: Get phone number
tools.description: One phone number by id: number, E.164, name, site, carrier, activation state and routing id. GET /numbers/{id}.

tools.name: placetel_list_number_profiles
tools.title: List number profiles
tools.description: The routing profiles of a phone number (for example Standard, Holiday, Night) and which one is active. Needs a Placetel plan with number profiles. GET /numbers/{number_id}/profiles.

tools.name: placetel_list_routings
tools.title: List routings
tools.description: List routing objects (what happens to an incoming call: forward, group, routing plan, IVR, queue, voicemail, API) with their settings and time settings. Filter by update time. GET /routings.

tools.name: placetel_get_routing
tools.title: Get routing
tools.description: One routing object by its id or by the phone number it answers. GET /routings/{number_or_id}.

tools.name: placetel_list_routing_plans
tools.title: List routing plans
tools.description: List routing plans (time-based call distribution plans) with name, description, ring duration and object counts. GET /routing_plans.

tools.name: placetel_list_groups
tools.title: List groups
tools.description: List ring groups (ring_all, hunt, monitoring) with members. Filter by name, description or type. GET /groups.

tools.name: placetel_list_sites
tools.title: List sites
tools.description: List company sites (locations) with address and prefix. GET /sites.

tools.name: placetel_list_faxes
tools.title: List faxes
tools.description: In- and outbound faxes with from/to number, status, pages, duration, type and the file URL. Filter by direction or number. GET /faxes.

tools.name: placetel_get_fax
tools.title: Get fax
tools.description: One fax by id: numbers, status, status info, pages, retries, report and file URL. GET /faxes/{id}.

tools.name: placetel_list_call_center_queues
tools.title: List call center queues
tools.description: List call-center queues with name, ring time, loops and prompts. Use the ids to filter call-center calls. GET /call_center_queues.

tools.name: placetel_list_call_center_agents
tools.title: List call center agents
tools.description: List call-center agents with name, status, extension, priority and last call time. GET /call_center_agents.

tools.name: placetel_list_call_center_calls
tools.title: List call center calls
tools.description: Call-center calls of one day with queue, agent, from/to, answer status, start/end time and time spent in queue. date is required; narrow to queues with queue_ids. GET /call_center_calls.

tools.name: placetel_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: create a contact in the shared Placetel phone book. Give at least a name, company or number. Nothing is sent to the contact. POST /contacts.

tools.name: placetel_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: update the given fields of a contact (omitted fields stay; an empty string clears a text field). tags replaces the whole tag list; blocked=true blocks the caller. PUT /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: placetel_activate_number_profile
tools.title: Activate number profile
tools.description: WRITE: switch the active routing profile of a phone number (for example to Holiday or Night). This changes LIVE call handling for that number immediately: callers are routed differently. Find ids with placetel_list_number_profiles. PUT /numbers/{number_id}/profiles.

tools.name: placetel_initiate_call
tools.title: Initiate call
tools.description: WRITE: start a real phone call. Placetel rings the given SIP user's phone first and, once answered, dials the target number. This places an actual call and call charges apply. Do not use without the user's explicit request. POST /calls.

tools.name: placetel_send_sms
tools.title: Send SMS
tools.description: WRITE: send a real SMS to a phone number from the Placetel account. The recipient receives it immediately and SMS charges apply; it cannot be recalled. Do not use without the user's explicit request and exact text. POST /sms.

tools.name: placetel_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: placetel_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Placetel tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: placetel_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Placetel (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: placetel_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Placetel Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run placetel_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

Show the call detail records for yesterday.

servers.name: FinerWorks
servers.description: Read FinerWorks orders, inventory, catalog, prices and shipping quotes; never submits an order.

login.hint: Log in to your FinerWorks account (finerworks.com, My Account) and open the API credentials: both keys are shown there. The server only reads and quotes: it never submits, changes or deletes an order. Your keys are used only to call the FinerWorks API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: finerworks_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The FinerWorks account these API keys belong to: username, email, billing and business addresses, account credits, shipping preferences and app details. The API keys, payment profile and third-party connection secrets are never returned. GET /v3/test_my_credentials.

tools.name: finerworks_list_orders
tools.title: List orders
tools.description: List submitted print orders, newest first, with status, totals and dates. Filter by free text, production status, FinerWorks order ids, your own order POs (the order numbers from Shopify, Squarespace, etc.) or an order-date range. POST /v3/list_orders.

tools.name: finerworks_get_order
tools.title: Get order
tools.description: One order in full: items, recipient, shipping method, status and totals. Needs the order GUID and the email address on the order. GET /v3/get_order.

tools.name: finerworks_get_order_status
tools.title: Get order production status
tools.description: The current production status of orders (in production, shipped, ...), looked up by your order PO numbers or FinerWorks order ids. An order that is not found returns nothing. POST /v3/fetch_order_status.

tools.name: finerworks_list_order_status_definitions
tools.title: List order status definitions
tools.description: All production statuses an order can have, with their ids. Use the id as the stable reference. GET /v3/list_order_status_definitions.

tools.name: finerworks_list_pending_orders

tools.name: finerworks_list_virtual_inventory

tools.name: finerworks_get_product_details

tools.name: finerworks_get_prices

tools.name: finerworks_list_product_types

tools.name: finerworks_list_media_types

tools.name: finerworks_list_style_types

tools.name: finerworks_list_static_products
tools.title: List static products
tools.description: Non-dynamic products, mostly accessories, that can be added to an order. POST /v3/list_static_products.

tools.name: finerworks_list_frame_collections
tools.title: List frame collections

tools.name: finerworks_get_frame

tools.name: finerworks_list_mats

tools.name: finerworks_list_glazing
tools.title: List glazing
tools.description: The available glazing (glass and acrylic) options. POST /v3/list_glazing.

tools.name: finerworks_get_shipping_options
tools.title: Get shipping options
tools.description: Shipping options and rates for one prospective order: a recipient address plus the SKUs and quantities. Returns the shipping_code values an order would need. Nothing is ordered or billed. POST /v3/list_shipping_options_multiple.

tools.name: finerworks_validate_address

servers.name: Sakari
servers.description: Manage Sakari SMS contacts, conversations, templates and campaigns, and send texts.
examples: Which conversations in my Sakari inbox have unread messages?
How many text messages did we send this week and what is my balance?
Find the contact with mobile ending 4421 and show our last messages.
Draft and send a reminder text to contact 63f1 (after I confirm the wording).

login.hint: Find all three in hub.sakari.io: click the **cog icon** (top right) and scroll to **API Credentials** (click Request Credentials if none are shown). The credentials act on your whole Sakari account, including sending texts that cost balance. They are used only to call the Sakari API on your behalf and are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: sakari_get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: The Sakari account these credentials belong to: name, plan, balance, default country, business info and options. API credentials are never returned. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}.

tools.name: sakari_get_balance
tools.title: Get account balance
tools.description: Prepaid balance, default country, remaining segments and the price per segment. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/balance.

tools.name: sakari_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List or search contacts (partial matches on name, mobile or email; filter by tag). GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/contacts.

tools.name: sakari_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact by id: name, mobile (with validity and line type), email, lists, attributes, opt-in and blocked state. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/contacts/{contactId}.

tools.name: sakari_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: create a contact. If a contact with the same mobile number exists, merge_strategy decides what happens (append, core or remove, per Sakari). A contact is not opted in to messages by this call. POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/contacts.

tools.name: sakari_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: change a contact's name, email or mobile. Sakari's update replaces the contact, so this reads the current contact first and sends it back whole (lists, opt-in, blocked, attributes) with only your changes applied. PUT /v1/accounts/{accountId}/contacts/{contactId}.

tools.name: sakari_list_messages
tools.title: List messages
tools.description: List messages (sent and received) with status, segments, price and timestamps; filter by contact or conversation. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/messages.

tools.name: sakari_get_message
tools.title: Get message
tools.description: One message by id: text, direction, status, segments, price, error. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/messages/{messageId}.

tools.name: sakari_send_message
tools.title: Send text message
tools.description: WRITE: SEND REAL TEXT MESSAGES that cost account balance and cannot be recalled. Recipients: phone numbers (international format), existing contact ids, or conversation ids (max 100 in total). Only text people who opted in; Sakari enforces TCPA/CTIA rules and the sender is responsible. Confirm the recipients and the text with the user first. Placeholders like {{firstName}} are filled per contact. POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/messages.

tools.name: sakari_list_conversations
tools.title: List conversations
tools.description: List conversations (the inbox): contact, last message, unread count, open or closed. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/conversations.

tools.name: sakari_get_conversation
tools.title: Get conversation
tools.description: One conversation by id. Use sakari_list_messages with conversation_id for its messages. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/conversations/{conversationId}.

tools.name: sakari_close_conversation
tools.title: Close conversation
tools.description: WRITE: mark a conversation closed in the Sakari inbox (a new inbound message reopens it). PUT /v1/accounts/{accountId}/conversations/{conversationId}/close.

tools.name: sakari_list_templates
tools.title: List templates
tools.description: List reusable message templates. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/templates.

tools.name: sakari_get_template
tools.title: Get template
tools.description: One message template by id. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/templates/{templateId}.

tools.name: sakari_create_template
tools.title: Create template
tools.description: WRITE: create a reusable SMS template (does not send anything). POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/templates.

tools.name: sakari_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: List message campaigns with schedule, template, status and reporting. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/campaigns.

tools.name: sakari_get_campaign
tools.title: Get campaign
tools.description: One campaign by id. GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/campaigns/{campaignId}.

tools.name: sakari_list_calls

tools.name: sakari_get_call

tools.name: sakari_list_links

tools.name: sakari_list_forms

tools.name: sakari_list_webhooks

tools.name: sakari_list_autoresponders

servers.name: Funraise

tools.name: funraise_list_supporters
tools.title: List supporters

tools.name: funraise_get_supporter

tools.name: funraise_list_donations
tools.title: List donations
tools.description: List donations (transactions) with amount, date, supporter, form, campaign page, allocation, fees and tags. Filter by an exact transactionId, by last N hours, or by a lastUpdated timestamp; use last_id to continue from the last donation id of the previous page. GET /api/v1/crm/donation.

tools.name: funraise_get_donation
tools.title: Get donation
tools.description: One donation by its Funraise id: amount, date, supporter, household, form, allocation, dedication, fees, UTM, subscription. GET /api/v1/crm/donation/{id}.

tools.name: funraise_list_subscriptions
tools.title: List recurring subscriptions
tools.description: List recurring gifts (subscriptions) with status, frequency, amount, next payment date and supporter. The q filter is a Funraise expression (Funraise requires it; default: id > 0 order by id asc), for example: id > 10 and status = "Cancelled" order by id asc. GET /api/v1/crm/subscription.

tools.name: funraise_get_subscription
tools.title: Get recurring subscription
tools.description: One recurring gift by id: status, frequency, amount, last and next payment date, cancel date, supporter. GET /api/v1/crm/subscription/{id}.

tools.name: funraise_list_forms
tools.title: List forms
tools.description: List donation and event forms, filtered by type, status and version. Needs the CREATOR role on the key. GET /api/v1/form.

tools.name: funraise_list_campaign_sites
tools.title: List campaign sites
tools.description: List campaign sites (fundraising pages), active by default or archived. Returns campaignSites with totalPageCount and totalRowCount. GET /api/v1/campaignSite/active or /archived.

tools.name: funraise_get_campaign_site
tools.title: Get campaign site
tools.description: One campaign site by UUID: configuration preview (payment options, goals, form, homepage, fundraiser settings). GET /api/v1/campaignSite/{uuid}.

tools.name: funraise_list_form_custom_questions

tools.name: funraise_get_household
