tools.description: The custom fields (columns) of a contact list: id, caption and type (STRING, BOOL, INT, DATE). Field ids are the keys used when writing contacts. GET /v1/lists/{listId}/fields.

tools.name: sarbacane_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts in a list
tools.description: Contacts of one list (personal data: email, phone, custom fields). Filter by email, phone, a text search across fields, or the modification date. GET /v1/lists/{listId}/contacts.

tools.name: sarbacane_create_contact
tools.title: Add a contact to a list
tools.description: WRITE: add a contact to a contact list. Give an email, a phone number or both, and optional custom field values. Adds a new record; use sarbacane_upsert_contact to update an existing contact. POST /v1/lists/{listId}/contacts.

tools.name: sarbacane_upsert_contact
tools.title: Add or update a contact
tools.description: WRITE: add a contact to a list, or update it when the same email/phone pair already exists (custom field values are overwritten). POST /v1/lists/{listId}/contacts/upsert.

tools.name: sarbacane_list_blacklists
tools.title: List blacklists
tools.description: All blacklists (suppression lists) of the account, with their ids. GET /v1/blacklists.

tools.name: sarbacane_list_blacklist_entries
tools.title: List blacklist entries
tools.description: Entries of a blacklist by kind: bounces (invalid addresses), unsubscribers or complaints (personal data: email, phone). Filter by email, phone or modification date. GET /v1/blacklists/{blacklistId}/{bounces|unsubscribers|complaints}.

tools.name: sarbacane_add_unsubscriber
tools.title: Add an unsubscribed contact to a blacklist
tools.description: WRITE: record an email and/or phone as unsubscribed in a blacklist, so campaigns using that blacklist skip it. Cannot be undone with these tools. POST /v1/blacklists/{blacklistId}/unsubscribers.

tools.name: sarbacane_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: Campaigns of the account (id, name, kind, created/edited, recipient count). Filter by state or a text in the name or subject. GET /v1/campaigns.

tools.name: sarbacane_get_campaign
tools.title: Get campaign details
tools.description: One campaign: state, kind, blacklists, send ids, sent date. The send id is needed to see content. GET /v1/campaigns/{campaignId}.

tools.name: sarbacane_get_campaign_report
tools.title: Get campaign statistics
tools.description: Statistics of a campaign per send: delivered count, opens, openers, clicks, clickers, unsubscribers, devices and operating systems. GET /v1/reports/{campaignId}.

tools.name: sarbacane_list_campaign_recipients
tools.title: List a campaign's recipients
tools.description: Recipients attached to a campaign (personal data: email, phone). GET /v1/campaigns/{campaignId}/recipients.

tools.name: sarbacane_list_webhooks
tools.title: List webhooks
tools.description: Webhook subscriptions of the account: url, display name and subscribed event kinds. GET /v1/webhooks.

tools.name: sarbacane_create_email_campaign
tools.title: Create an email campaign (draft)
tools.description: WRITE: create a new email campaign as a DRAFT. It is never sent by these tools: add content (sarbacane_set_campaign_content or sarbacane_import_campaign_template) and a contact list (sarbacane_set_campaign_list), then send it from Sarbacane. POST /v1/campaigns/email.

tools.name: sarbacane_set_campaign_content
tools.title: Set a draft campaign's content
tools.description: WRITE: set the HTML (and optional plain-text) content of an email campaign's send, replacing what was there. Without send_id the campaign's only send is used (an A/B test campaign has several: pass one). POST /v1/campaigns/{campaignId}/send/{sendId}/content.

tools.name: sarbacane_import_campaign_template
tools.title: Import a template into a draft campaign
tools.description: WRITE: load a saved template's content into an email campaign, replacing its content. POST /v1/campaigns/{campaignId}/content.

tools.name: sarbacane_set_campaign_list
tools.title: Attach a contact list to a draft campaign
tools.description: WRITE: import a contact list's contacts as the recipients of a campaign. It does not send the campaign. POST /v1/campaigns/{campaignId}/list.

tools.name: sarbacane_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sarbacane_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Sarbacane tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sarbacane_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Sarbacane (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: sarbacane_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Sarbacane Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run sarbacane_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: Sellsy
servers.description: Search and read Sellsy companies, contacts, opportunities, invoices and tasks; create records.
examples: Which invoices are late or unpaid, and how much does each customer owe?
Find the company Dupont and list its contacts, open opportunities and latest estimates.
Show my open opportunities in the sales pipeline with their amounts and due dates.
Create a task for tomorrow 9am to call the contact Marie Martin, and add a note on her company.

login.hint: In Sellsy open **Settings → Developer portal → API V2**, create a client of type **Personal** and tick the scopes you want to use (**staffs: read** is required to identify your account; for example also companies, contacts, opportunities, estimates, invoices, items, tasks, comments: read, plus write for the records you want to create). The client acts with the rights of your own Sellsy user and reaches your customers’ names, emails and invoices. Your credentials are used only to call the Sellsy API on your behalf and to derive a private account id from your Sellsy account; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.description: Search companies by name, email, type (prospect/client/supplier), reference, VAT, SIRET, country, postal code, creation or update date. Needs companies.read.

tools.name: sellsy_get_company
tools.title: Get a company
tools.description: Get one company by id. Needs companies.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_company_contacts
tools.title: List a company's contacts
tools.description: List the contacts linked to one company (GET /companies/{id}/contacts). Needs companies.read and contacts.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_individuals
tools.title: List individuals
tools.description: List individuals (private customers, prospects, suppliers) with paging. Needs individuals.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_individuals
tools.title: Search individuals
tools.description: Search individuals by name, email, type, reference, country, postal code, creation or update date. Needs individuals.read.

tools.name: sellsy_get_individual
tools.title: Get an individual
tools.description: Get one individual by id. Needs individuals.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_contacts

tools.description: List contacts (people at companies) with paging. Needs contacts.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_contacts

tools.name: sellsy_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: Get one contact by id. Needs contacts.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_opportunities
tools.title: List opportunities
tools.description: List sales opportunities with paging. Needs opportunities.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_opportunities
tools.title: Search opportunities
tools.description: Search opportunities by name, number, pipeline, step, status (open/won/lost/cancelled/closed/late), amount, owner or due date. Needs opportunities.read.

tools.name: sellsy_get_opportunity
tools.title: Get an opportunity
tools.description: Get one opportunity by id. Needs opportunities.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_opportunity_pipelines
tools.title: List opportunity pipelines
tools.description: List the sales pipelines (needed to create an opportunity: pipeline id and step id). Needs opportunities.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_pipeline_steps
tools.title: List the steps of a pipeline
tools.description: List the steps of one opportunity pipeline. Needs opportunities.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_estimates
tools.title: List estimates
tools.description: List estimates (quotes) with paging. Needs estimates.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_estimates
tools.title: Search estimates
tools.description: Search estimates by status, number, date, currency, owner, contact or related company/individual/opportunity. Needs estimates.read.

tools.name: sellsy_get_estimate
tools.title: Get an estimate
tools.description: Get one estimate by id, with its rows and amounts. Needs estimates.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices with paging. Needs invoices.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_invoices
tools.title: Search invoices
tools.description: Search invoices by status (draft/due/payinprogress/paid/late/cancelled), number, date, currency, owner, or related company/individual/opportunity. Use it for unpaid or late invoices. Needs invoices.read.

tools.name: sellsy_get_invoice
tools.title: Get an invoice
tools.description: Get one invoice by id, with its rows, amounts and status. Needs invoices.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_invoice_payments
tools.title: List an invoice's payments
tools.description: List the payments linked to one invoice. Needs invoices.read and payments.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_orders
tools.title: List orders
tools.description: List orders with paging. Needs orders.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_orders
tools.title: Search orders
tools.description: Search orders by status or delivery status, or related company/individual/opportunity. Needs orders.read.

tools.name: sellsy_get_order
tools.title: Get an order
tools.description: Get one order by id. Needs orders.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_credit_notes
tools.title: List credit notes
tools.description: List credit notes with paging. Needs credit-notes.read.

tools.name: sellsy_get_credit_note
tools.title: Get a credit note
tools.description: Get one credit note by id. Needs credit-notes.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_items
tools.title: List items
tools.description: List catalog items (products, services, shipping, packaging) with paging. Needs items.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_items
tools.title: Search items
tools.description: Search catalog items by name, reference or type. Needs items.read.

tools.name: sellsy_get_item
tools.title: Get an item
tools.description: Get one catalog item by id. Needs items.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_payments
tools.title: Search payments
tools.description: Search payments by status (pending/confirmed/rejected/failed/refund) or related company/individual. Needs payments.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks
tools.description: List tasks with paging. Needs tasks.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_tasks
tools.title: Search tasks
tools.description: Search tasks by status (todo/done), owner, assignee, label, due date or related record. Needs tasks.read.

tools.name: sellsy_get_task
tools.title: Get a task
tools.description: Get one task by id. Needs tasks.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_task_labels
tools.title: List task labels
tools.description: List the task labels (a label id is required to create a task). Needs tasks.read.

tools.name: sellsy_search_comments
tools.title: Search comments (notes)
tools.description: Search comments and notes by author, date, parent comment or the company/individual/contact they are attached to. Needs comments.read.

tools.name: sellsy_list_staffs

tools.description: List the staff members of the account (the list may hold only yourself, depending on the Sellsy plan). Needs staffs.read.

tools.name: sellsy_create_company
tools.title: Create a company
tools.description: WRITE: create a company record in Sellsy (a prospect, client or supplier). Needs companies.write. Nothing is sent to the company.

tools.name: sellsy_create_individual

tools.description: WRITE: create an individual (a private person as prospect, client or supplier) in Sellsy. Needs individuals.write.

tools.title: Create a contact
tools.description: WRITE: create a contact (a person) in Sellsy. It is not linked to a company by this call. Needs contacts.write.

tools.title: Create an opportunity
tools.description: WRITE: create a sales opportunity linked to a company, individual or contact. Needs a pipeline id and one of its step ids (see sellsy_list_opportunity_pipelines and sellsy_list_pipeline_steps). Needs opportunities.write.

tools.name: sellsy_create_comment
tools.title: Add a comment (note)
tools.description: WRITE: add a comment (note) to a company, individual, contact, opportunity or document. Visible to the Sellsy staff, not sent to the customer. Needs comments.write.

servers.name: smallinvoice
servers.description: Read smallinvoice contacts, invoices, offers, projects and hours; create contacts and invoices.
examples: Which invoices are still open, and who owes me the most?
Show all invoices for the contact ACME GmbH from this year.
How many hours did we book on each project last month?
Create a new contact for Muster AG in Bern and draft an invoice for 3 hours of consulting at CHF 150.

login.hint: Create the client yourself in smallinvoice: **Home → Users → API V2**, new client, grant type **Client credentials**, and tick the scopes you want to give the assistant (contact, invoice, offer, order confirmation, delivery note, catalog, configuration, project, working hours, effort, activity, cost unit). Create a client just for this connection, so you can delete it there at any time. The secret is used only to get smallinvoice access tokens and call the API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone. Documents and contacts contain your customers' personal data.

tools.name: smallinvoice_get_owner
tools.title: Get the account owner
tools.description: The smallinvoice account the API client belongs to (the owner's id and details). A cheap check that the connection works. GET /auth/owner.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contacts (customers and suppliers): name, type (company or person), relation, e-mail, currency. Add with=main_address for the address. Needs the "contact" scope. GET /contacts. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_get_contact
tools.title: Get a contact
tools.description: One contact by id, with its fields. Add with=main_address for the main address. Needs the "contact" scope. GET /contacts/{id}.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_contact_addresses
tools.title: List a contact's addresses
tools.description: All addresses of one contact. Needs the "contact" scope. GET /contacts/{contactId}/addresses.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_contact_people
tools.title: List a contact's people
tools.description: The contact persons of one company contact. Needs the "contact" scope. GET /contacts/{contactId}/people.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_contact_groups
tools.title: List contact groups
tools.description: List the contact groups. Needs the "contact" scope. GET /contacts/configuration/groups. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List invoices: number, contact, dates, total, currency, status. Filter by contact_id or a JSON filter. Needs the "invoice" scope. GET /receivables/invoices. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_get_invoice
tools.title: Get an invoice
tools.description: One invoice by id with its positions, totals and status. Needs the "invoice" scope. GET /receivables/invoices/{id}.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_invoice_payments
tools.title: List payments of an invoice
tools.description: The payments recorded on one invoice. Needs the "invoice" scope. GET /receivables/invoices/{invoiceId}/payments.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_offers
tools.title: List offers
tools.description: List offers (quotes). Filter by contact_id or a JSON filter. Needs the "offer" scope. GET /receivables/offers. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_get_offer
tools.title: Get an offer
tools.description: One offer (quote) by id with its positions and totals. Needs the "offer" scope. GET /receivables/offers/{id}.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_order_confirmations
tools.title: List order confirmations
tools.description: List order confirmations. Filter by contact_id or a JSON filter. Needs the "order_confirmation" scope. GET /receivables/order-confirmations. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_get_order_confirmation
tools.title: Get an order confirmation
tools.description: One order confirmation by id. Needs the "order_confirmation" scope. GET /receivables/order-confirmations/{id}.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_delivery_notes
tools.title: List delivery notes
tools.description: List delivery notes. Filter by contact_id or a JSON filter. Needs the "delivery_note" scope. GET /receivables/delivery-notes. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_get_delivery_note
tools.title: Get a delivery note
tools.description: One delivery note by id. Needs the "delivery_note" scope. GET /receivables/delivery-notes/{id}.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_products
tools.title: List catalog products
tools.description: List the catalog's products (articles). Needs the "catalog" scope. GET /catalog/products. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_services
tools.title: List catalog services
tools.description: List the catalog's services. Needs the "catalog" scope. GET /catalog/services. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_units
tools.title: List units
tools.description: List the units (piece, hour, ...) with their ids, which an invoice position's unit_id refers to. Needs the "configuration" scope. GET /catalog/configuration/units. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_bank_accounts
tools.title: List bank accounts
tools.description: List the account's bank accounts (as printed on documents). Needs the "configuration" scope. GET /configuration/bank-accounts. Returns count, total, next_offset (pass it as offset for the next page) and the items.

tools.name: smallinvoice_list_projects

tools.name: smallinvoice_get_project
tools.title: Get a project

servers.name: Smaregi
servers.description: Read Smaregi stores, products, customers, stock and transactions; manage customers, products, stock.
examples: Show yesterday's sales transactions of my Tokyo store.
Which products are low on stock in store 2?
Change the price of product 1042 to 1,980 yen.
Add a new member: Hanako Sato, hanako@example.com.
List my stores and their staff.

login.hint: As the contract administrator (Premium plan or above), open Smaregi **My Page → Settings → Platform API settings**, switch the Platform API on for your own contract and tick the scopes you want to allow (read access to stores, products, customers, transactions, stock and staff; write access to products, customers and stock if you want changes). Copy the **client ID** and **client secret** and your **contract ID**. The credentials are used only to get access tokens and call the Smaregi API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone. Customers and transactions contain your shoppers' personal data.

tools.name: smaregi_list_stores
tools.title: List stores
tools.description: List the stores (shops) of the Smaregi contract: id, code, name, address, phone. Use the ids to filter stock and transactions. GET /stores.

tools.name: smaregi_get_store
tools.title: Get store
tools.description: One store by id. GET /stores/{store_id}.

tools.name: smaregi_list_staffs
tools.title: List staff
tools.description: List staff members: id, code, name, role, e-mail. Passwords are never returned. GET /staffs.

tools.name: smaregi_get_staff
tools.title: Get staff member
tools.description: One staff member by id. GET /staffs/{staff_id}.

tools.name: smaregi_list_stock_changes

tools.name: smaregi_list_transactions

tools.name: smaregi_get_transaction

tools.name: smaregi_create_customer
tools.title: Create customer

tools.name: smaregi_update_customer
tools.title: Update customer
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of one customer (only the fields you pass are changed). Overwrites the old values. PATCH /customers/{customer_id}.

tools.name: smaregi_create_product
tools.title: Create product

tools.name: smaregi_update_product
tools.title: Update product

tools.name: smaregi_set_stock
tools.title: Set stock level

tools.name: smaregi_adjust_stock
tools.title: Adjust stock level

tools.name: smaregi_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smaregi_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Smaregi tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: smaregi_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Smaregi (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). servers.description: Read Upper drivers and stops; create and optimize routes, assign drivers, share routes to the app.
examples: Which stops are not on a route yet?
Create a route for tomorrow called North Loop and add these five addresses to it.
Assign Jordan and Alex to route 18452, optimize it, and tell me when it is done.
List the stops on route 502 with their time windows.

login.hint: Find it in Upper (crew.upperinc.com) under **Settings → Webhooks → API Token** (copy button). The token gives full programmatic access to your Upper account, so treat it like a password. It is used only to call the Upper API on your behalf and is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: upper_list_drivers
tools.title: List drivers
tools.description: List the active drivers on the Upper team that owns the API token: id, name, email and phone. Use the ids with upper_assign_drivers and upper_share_route_to_drivers. GET /ext-get-drivers.

tools.name: upper_list_stops
tools.title: List stops
tools.description: List the team's stops in optimized order: address, coordinates, contact, time window, duration, status, route_id and custom ids. Pass route_id for one route (optionally scheduled=true/false); pass unscheduled=true (without route_id) for stops not on any route; with no filter all active stops are returned. Upper has no paging, so this tool pages locally: `limit` stops (default 100, max 500) starting at `offset`; the reply says if more remain (truncated, next_offset). GET /ext-get-stops.

tools.name: upper_get_optimization_status
tools.title: Get route optimization status
tools.description: Check whether a route is optimized: status is optimized, pending (still running) or not_optimized, plus the queue_id of the last job. Poll this after upper_optimize_route. GET /ext-optimization-status.

tools.name: upper_get_custom_fields
tools.title: Get stop custom fields
tools.description: The workspace's five stop custom-field slots (custom1 - custom5: type, label, enabled, required) and which are enabled. Needs the Custom fields feature in the Upper plan. GET /ext-get-custom-fields.

tools.name: upper_get_capacity_fields
tools.title: Get capacity fields
tools.description: The workspace's five capacity-field slots (capacity1 - capacity5: label, unit, enabled) used for load planning. GET /ext-get-capacity-fields.

tools.name: upper_create_route
tools.title: Create route
tools.description: WRITE: create a new, empty route (name, date, optimization preference, units, pickup sequencing, service time). Omitted settings fall back to the account's defaults. Returns the new route_id; add stops with upper_create_stop. Calling it twice creates two routes. POST /ext-create-route.

tools.name: upper_update_route
tools.title: Update route
tools.description: WRITE: change settings of an existing route (name, date, optimize_for, units, pickup_settings, service_time). Only the fields you pass change. POST /ext-update-route.

tools.name: upper_create_stop
tools.title: Create stop
tools.description: WRITE: create a stop. The address is geocoded by Upper. Pass route_id to put it on a route (the route must not be active/in progress; an optimized route is flagged for re-optimization); omit it for an unscheduled stop. Calling it twice creates two stops. POST /ext-create-stop.

tools.name: upper_update_stop
tools.title: Update stop
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing stop; only the fields you pass change. A new address is re-geocoded (city/state/zipcode you pass with it are ignored); city/state/zipcode apply only without an address. Passing route_id moves the stop to that route. Editing a stop on an optimized route flags the route for re-optimization; stops on an active route cannot be edited. POST /ext-update-stop.

tools.name: upper_assign_drivers
tools.title: Assign drivers to a route
tools.description: WRITE: assign one or more drivers (ids from upper_list_drivers) to a route, replacing the route's drivers. Every id must be an active driver on the team. If the route was already optimized it is reset to unoptimized (needs_optimization: true), so run upper_optimize_route again. POST /ext-assign-drivers.

tools.name: upper_optimize_route
tools.title: Optimize route
tools.description: WRITE: start optimizing a route's stop order. The route needs at least one stop and one assigned driver (upper_assign_drivers). It runs asynchronously: this returns status pending and a queue_id, then poll upper_get_optimization_status. If a job is already running, that job is returned. POST /ext-optimize-route.

tools.name: upper_share_route_to_drivers
tools.title: Share route to drivers
tools.description: WRITE: push a route to the drivers' mobile app NOW, which sends each driver a notification. Without driver_ids the route's assigned drivers are used; with them, every id must be an active driver on the team. Sending twice notifies twice. Confirm with the user before calling. POST /ext-share-to-driver.

tools.name: upper_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: upper_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Upper Route Planner tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: upper_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Upper Route Planner (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: upper_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Upper Route Planner Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run upper_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: spokephone_list_calls
tools.title: List calls
tools.description: List call records (oldest first by default; pass sortOrder descending for the latest calls), with caller, direction, duration, assigned user/team and recording URLs. Filter by time window or the external party's number. Returns { meta: { next }, calls }.

tools.name: spokephone_get_call
tools.title: Get a call
tools.description: Get one call record by call id.

tools.name: spokephone_get_call_recording

tools.name: spokephone_list_call_content_analysis

tools.name: spokephone_list_directory

tools.name: spokephone_get_directory_entry

tools.name: spokephone_list_users

tools.name: spokephone_list_teams

tools.name: spokephone_list_locations

tools.name: spokephone_get_location

tools.name: spokephone_list_location_users

tools.description: List the users assigned to one location.

tools.name: spokephone_list_phonebooks
tools.title: List phonebooks
tools.description: List shared phonebooks (the CRM contact containers used for caller ID), each with its contacts. Use limit 0 to list phonebooks without contacts.

tools.name: spokephone_get_phonebook
tools.title: Get a phonebook
tools.description: Get one phonebook and a page of its contacts. The id may also be a user's email address for that user's personal phonebook.

tools.name: spokephone_get_phonebook_contact
tools.title: Get a phonebook contact
tools.description: Get one contact of a phonebook.

tools.name: spokephone_list_transcripts
tools.title: List transcripts
tools.description: List call and voicemail transcripts. Filter by time window or source.

tools.name: spokephone_get_transcript
tools.title: Get a transcript
tools.description: Get one transcript by id.

tools.name: spokephone_get_transcript_segments
tools.title: Get transcript segments
tools.description: Get the per-speaker segments of one transcript.

tools.name: spokephone_list_content_analysis
tools.title: List AI content analysis
tools.description: List AI content-analysis results (needs the Enlighten entitlement). Filter by time, source, participant or artifact name.

tools.name: spokephone_get_content_analysis
tools.title: Get an AI content analysis
tools.description: Get one content-analysis result by id.

tools.name: spokephone_list_webhooks
tools.title: List webhooks
tools.description: List the webhook subscriptions of the account.

tools.name: spokephone_get_webhook
tools.title: Get a webhook
tools.description: Get one webhook subscription by id.

tools.name: spokephone_list_trunks
tools.title: List SIP trunks
tools.description: List the SIP trunks that overlay a legacy PBX onto Spoke.

tools.name: spokephone_get_trunk
tools.title: Get a SIP trunk
tools.description: Get one SIP trunk by id.

tools.name: spokephone_send_sms
tools.title: Send an SMS
tools.description: WRITE: send a real SMS to a phone number (or a group MMS to several) from a company number or from a Spoke user's conversation number. The message appears in the Spoke conversation. Confirm the recipient and text with the user first. Needs an SMS-enabled number. POST /conversationMessages.

tools.name: spokephone_save_phonebook_contact
tools.title: Add or replace a phonebook contact
tools.description: WRITE: add a contact to a phonebook, REPLACING any contact there with the same contactId (other contacts are untouched). The phonebook id may be a user's email for a personal phonebook. Contacts feed caller ID. PUT /phonebooks/{id}/contacts.

tools.name: spokephone_delete_phonebook_contact

tools.description: WRITE, destructive: delete one contact from a phonebook (it stops showing in caller ID). DELETE /phonebooks/{id}/contacts/{contactId}.

servers.name: Laposta
servers.description: Read Laposta lists, members, campaigns and reports; add members and build campaigns.
examples: How many active subscribers does each of my Laposta lists have?
Show the open and click rates of my last five newsletters.
Find the subscriber maartje@example.com and show what she opened recently.
Add jan@example.com to my newsletter list and unsubscribe piet@example.com.

login.hint: Create it in Laposta under **Account → Integrations → API** (free accounts can have 3 keys). The key gives access to the whole account, so a dedicated key for this connection is easy to revoke later. Your key is used only to call the Laposta API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: laposta_list_lists
tools.title: List mailing lists
tools.description: List all mailing lists of the Laposta account with member counts (active, unsubscribed, cleaned). Use the list_id in the other tools.

tools.name: laposta_get_list
tools.title: Get a mailing list
tools.description: Get one mailing list: name, state, notification addresses and member counts.

tools.name: laposta_list_fields
tools.title: List a list's fields
tools.description: List the custom fields of a mailing list (name, custom_name used as the key in custom_fields, datatype, required, options). Call this before adding or updating a member.

tools.name: laposta_list_segments
tools.title: List a list's segments
tools.description: List the segments of a mailing list (a segment id can be a campaign recipient together with its list).

tools.name: laposta_list_members
tools.title: List members of a list
tools.description: List the members (subscribers) of a mailing list, one page at a time. Filter by state, free-text search (email and field values) or label. Contains personal data: only fetch what the task needs.

tools.name: laposta_get_member
tools.title: Get a member
tools.description: Get one member of a list by member id or email address: state, signup/confirm dates and custom field values.

tools.name: laposta_get_member_history
tools.title: Get a member's event history
tools.description: The event history of one member (subscribed, confirmed, opened, clicked, bounced, unsubscribed, automations ...), newest first by default. Optionally limited to one campaign or a date range. Paged by cursor.

tools.name: laposta_list_campaigns
tools.title: List campaigns
tools.description: List the account's campaigns (name, subject, sender, recipient lists, delivery moments). Use limit/offset to page.

tools.name: laposta_get_campaign
tools.title: Get a campaign
tools.description: Get one campaign: name, subject, preview text, sender, reply-to, recipients, delivery moments and web version URL.

tools.name: laposta_get_campaign_content
tools.title: Get a campaign's content
tools.description: Get the plain-text content of a campaign (and its import_url if it was imported). Set include_html to also get the full HTML (large).

tools.name: laposta_get_campaign_history
tools.title: Get a campaign's event history
tools.description: Recipient events of one campaign (delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, unsubscribed ...), newest first by default, optionally within a date range. Paged by cursor. For totals use laposta_get_report.

tools.name: laposta_list_reports
tools.title: List campaign reports
tools.description: Result figures of all campaigns: sent, accepted, opened, clicked, bounced, unsubscribed, with ratios. Use limit/offset to page.

tools.name: laposta_get_report
tools.title: Get a campaign report
tools.description: Result figures of one campaign: sent, accepted, unique opens and clicks, bounces, complaints, unsubscribes and their ratios.

tools.name: laposta_add_member
tools.title: Add a member to a list
tools.description: WRITE: add one email address to a mailing list (subscribe). On a double opt-in list Laposta sends the confirmation email to that address. The address must have given consent. With upsert, an existing active member's fields are overwritten; an unsubscribed member is re-activated unless suppress_reactivation is set.

tools.name: laposta_update_member
tools.title: Update a member
tools.description: WRITE: change a member's custom field values and/or email address, or unsubscribe the member (state: unsubscribed). Only the fields you pass change. Re-subscribing a person is not offered here: do it in the Laposta app or with laposta_add_member upsert only when they asked for it.

tools.name: laposta_create_campaign
tools.title: Create a campaign draft
tools.description: WRITE: create a new regular campaign (a draft: it is NOT filled, scheduled or sent). Fill it with laposta_set_campaign_content, check it with laposta_send_test_email and send it in the Laposta app. The from_email must be an approved sender address of the account.

tools.name: laposta_set_campaign_content
tools.title: Set a campaign's content
tools.description: WRITE: replace a campaign's content with your HTML, or let Laposta import it from a URL (html wins if both are given). Does not send anything. The reply's report lists problems Laposta found (javascript, missing unsubscribe link, missing images).

tools.name: laposta_send_test_email
tools.title: Send a campaign test email
tools.description: WRITE: send a test copy of a campaign (it must have content and not be sent yet) to ONE email address. Does not send the campaign to its recipients.

servers.name: Appointedd
servers.description: Read Appointedd bookings, customers and availability; create, change and cancel bookings.
examples: What bookings do I have tomorrow, and who are the customers?
Find the next free 30-minute slot for a consultation with any resource this week.
Book Ada Lovelace (ada@example.org) into the first free slot on Monday.
Cancel the 3 pm booking for Sam Jones and mark the other customer as arrived.

login.hint: Find it in Appointedd under **Settings → API** (`app.appointedd.com/management/settings/api`); the API needs a plan that includes it. The key has full access to your organisation. Your key is used only to call the Appointedd API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone. Booking data can include customers' personal details.

tools.name: appointedd_list_bookings
tools.title: List bookings
tools.description: List bookings, newest first by default. Filter by time window (after/before), customer, service, resource, category, status or creation/update time. Each booking has its service, resource, start/end, status and the customers on it (with their notes, questions and statuses). Page with `next`. GET /bookings.

tools.name: appointedd_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List customers in the CRM: name, email, phone/mobile, address, tags, custom fields, marketing opt-in. Page with `next`. GET /customers.

tools.name: appointedd_get_customer
tools.title: Get customer
tools.description: One customer by id. GET /customers/{customer_id}.

tools.name: appointedd_list_resources
tools.title: List resources
tools.description: List resources (the staff members, rooms or equipment that bookings are made for): name, assigned service ids and resource group ids. Page with `next`. GET /resources.

tools.name: appointedd_list_resource_groups
tools.title: List resource groups
tools.description: List resource groups (id and name). Page with `next`. GET /resources/groups.

tools.name: appointedd_list_services
tools.title: List services
tools.description: List services (what can be booked): name, category, durations and prices, buffers, occupancy and booking type. Page with `next`. GET /services.

tools.name: appointedd_get_service
tools.title: Get service
tools.description: One service by id, including its booking questions, durations, prices and buffers. GET /services/{service_id}.

tools.name: appointedd_list_service_categories
tools.title: List service categories
tools.description: List service categories (id and name). Page with `next`. GET /services/categories.

tools.name: appointedd_get_service_category
tools.title: Get service category
tools.description: One service category by id. GET /services/categories/{category_id}.

tools.name: appointedd_find_available_intervals
tools.title: Find available times
tools.description: Find the start times at which a service can be booked in the given ranges, with the free resource ids for each (and existing group bookings with room). Step 1 of making a booking: pick a start, then appointedd_create_reservation. Read-only. POST /availability/intervals/search.

tools.name: appointedd_find_available_dates
tools.title: Find available days
tools.description: Find which days in the given ranges have any availability for a service (a calendar view; use appointedd_find_available_intervals for the times). Read-only. POST /availability/days/search.

tools.name: appointedd_get_reservation
tools.title: Get reservation
tools.description: One reservation (availability slot) by id: its service, resource, times and expiry. GET /availability/slots/{reservation_id}.

tools.name: appointedd_create_customer
tools.title: Create customer
tools.description: WRITE: create a customer in the CRM (first and last name required; email, mobile, phone, tags optional). POST /customers.

tools.name: appointedd_update_customer
tools.title: Update customer
tools.description: WRITE: change a customer's name, email, mobile, phone or tags. Only the fields you pass are sent; `tags` replaces the customer's tag list. PUT /customers/{customer_id}.

tools.name: appointedd_create_reservation
tools.title: Create reservation (hold a time)
tools.description: WRITE: hold a date and time for a booking (step 2). The reservation blocks that slot for `expires_after` minutes (default: the organisation's setting); then call appointedd_create_booking with the returned reservation id. Without resource_id a free resource assigned to the service is picked. POST /availability/slots.

tools.name: appointedd_create_booking
tools.title: Create booking
tools.description: WRITE: turn an active reservation into a booking (step 3) for one or more customers; Appointedd matches each customer to the CRM by name/email/mobile or creates it. Payment requests are NOT sent unless send_payment_request is true. With an empty customers list an empty booking is created. POST /bookings.

tools.name: appointedd_update_booking
tools.title: Update booking
tools.description: WRITE: change a booking's service, resource, label or total spaces, or move it by giving `parts` with new start/end times. Customers are NOT emailed unless send_notifications is true. PUT /bookings/{booking_id}.

tools.name: appointedd_update_booking_customer
tools.title: Update customer on booking
tools.description: WRITE: set the arrival status (Arrived, Complete, No Show, No Status) and/or notes of one customer on a booking. customer_booking_id is the customer's `customer_booking_id` (or `customer_id`) in the booking's customers list. PUT /bookings/{booking_id}/customers/{customer_booking_id}.

tools.name: appointedd_cancel_booking
tools.title: Cancel booking
tools.description: WRITE (cannot be undone): cancel a whole booking. Appointedd may notify the customers according to the organisation's settings. To remove one customer from a group booking use appointedd_cancel_booking_customer. POST /bookings/{booking_id}/cancel.

tools.name: appointedd_cancel_booking_customer
tools.title: Cancel customer on booking
tools.description: WRITE (cannot be undone): cancel one customer's place on a booking (the booking stays for the others). customer_booking_id is the `customer_booking_id` in the booking's customers list. POST /bookings/{booking_id}/customers/{customer_booking_id}/cancel.

servers.name: Ticketsauce
servers.description: Read Ticketsauce events, orders and ticket check-in IDs (read-only).

login.hint: Log in to Ticketsauce, hover **My Account** (top right), click **API**, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret (click **Generate API Keys** if the secret is not shown). They are used only to call the Ticketsauce API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone. The API only reads: this server cannot change your events or orders.

tools.name: ticketsauce_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List the events you own on Ticketsauce with id, name, slug, start/end (local and UTC), venue address, timezone, organization, privacy type, whether tickets are on sale, and the event and ticket-shop URLs. Filter by start/end/created dates (yyyy-mm-dd, UTC), a phrase such as this_weekend, organization or partner. The API has no paging for events. Use the event id for orders and check-ins. GET /v2/events.

tools.name: ticketsauce_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event by id or slug: everything in the list plus summary and description (text and HTML), order_count and ticket_count (tickets sold, not refunded or voided). Replies are cached for an hour. GET /v2/event/{id_or_slug}.

tools.name: ticketsauce_list_orders
tools.title: List orders of an event
tools.description: Orders of one event, oldest first by default (pass sort_dir desc for newest first): order id, status, buyer name, email, phone and address, totals (total_paid, refund_amount, taxes, fees), promo code, ticket_count, paid date. Contains your customers' personal data. Filter by order or modified dates, a phrase, buyer email or last name (exact match), totals, or promo use; optionally embed tickets, questionnaire answers and line-item fees. Paged: per_page up to 500, then pass next_page. Replies are cached for an hour. GET /v2/orders/{event_id}.

tools.name: ticketsauce_get_order
tools.title: Get order
tools.description: One order by id, with its buyer details, totals and its tickets (ticket type, name, price, redeemed state, promo code). Contains personal data. Replies are cached for an hour. GET /v2/order/{order_id}.

tools.name: ticketsauce_list_checkin_ids
tools.title: List ticket check-in ids
tools.description: The ticket check-in ids of one event, for door/scanning reconciliation (the API documents no response fields; the reply is returned as is). Paged: per_page up to 5000, then pass next_page. Replies are cached for 5 minutes. GET /v2/tickets/checkin_ids/{event_id}.

tools.name: ticketsauce_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: ticketsauce_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the Ticketsauce tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: ticketsauce_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on Ticketsauce (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: ticketsauce_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's Ticketsauce Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run ticketsauce_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

examples: Which of my events start this weekend, and how many tickets has each sold?
List the orders for my next event placed in the last 24 hours.
Find the order for jane@example.com on the Summer Fest event and show her tickets.
Which orders over $200 used a promo code?

servers.name: Evenium
servers.description: Read Evenium events, guests, contacts and hotels; register guests and update contacts and statuses.

login.hint: Find it in your Evenium profile: **My account → API key** (Facility accounts on evenium.com), or **Profile → API key** on the evenium.net platform. The key acts with your account's rights. Your key is used only to call the Evenium API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: evenium_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List the events of the Evenium account, with id, title, dates, status and creation date. Filter by title (partial match), status and start/end/creation dates. Use an event id with the guest and session tools. GET /events.

tools.name: evenium_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event by id: title, description, dates, status, site path and its fields (type, your external id, ...). GET /events/{eventId}.

tools.name: evenium_list_guests
tools.title: List guests
tools.description: List the guests (invited contacts) of an event with name, email, company, registration status (e.g. CONFIRMED, DECLINED, UNANSWERED), category and fields. Filter by status, name, email, company or last update. GET /events/{eventId}/guests.

tools.name: evenium_get_guest
tools.title: Get guest
tools.description: One guest of an event, by contact id or by guest code: name, email, status, category and fields (event-only fields flagged). Optionally include REGISTRATION (registrations to sessions), PRESENCE and SIGNATURE data. GET /events/{eventId}/guests/{contactId} or /guests/guestCode/{guestCode}.

tools.name: evenium_get_guest_status
tools.title: Get guest status
tools.description: The registration status of one guest at an event (e.g. CONFIRMED, DECLINED, CANCELED). GET /events/{eventId}/guests/{contactId}/status.

tools.name: evenium_get_guest_post_status
tools.title: Get guest attendance
tools.description: The attendance (post) status of one guest after the event: UNKNOWN, NO_SHOW or PRESENT. GET /events/{eventId}/guests/{contactId}/postStatus.

tools.name: evenium_get_guest_accommodations
tools.title: Get guest accommodations
tools.description: The hotel room bookings of one guest at an event: room id, check-in and check-out dates, status. Not available on the evenium.net platform. GET /events/{eventId}/guests/{contactId}/accommodations.

tools.name: evenium_list_hotels
tools.title: List hotels
tools.description: The hotels of an event with name, group, stars, contact details and, if asked, full location and rooms. Not available on the evenium.net platform. GET /events/{eventId}/hotels.

tools.name: evenium_create_guest
tools.title: Create guest
tools.description: WRITE: invite a person to an event. Either invite an existing contact (contact_id) or create a guest from scratch (first_name, last_name, email, ...), which may also create a new contact. The optional status sets the registration status (the invitation emails of the event may follow Evenium's own rules). POST /events/{eventId}/guests.

tools.name: evenium_update_guest_status
tools.title: Update guest status
tools.description: WRITE: set the registration status of a guest at an event (e.g. CONFIRMED, DECLINED, CANCELED). Can trigger Evenium's own workflows for that status. Read the current value first with evenium_get_guest_status. PUT /events/{eventId}/guests/{contactId}/status.

tools.name: evenium_update_guest_post_status
tools.title: Update guest attendance
tools.description: WRITE: set the attendance (post) status of a guest: PRESENT, NO_SHOW or UNKNOWN (for example after check-in). PUT /events/{eventId}/guests/{contactId}/postStatus.

tools.name: evenium_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List the contacts of the address book (id, your custom id, name, email, company and fields). Filter by name, email, company or last update. GET /contacts.

tools.name: evenium_get_contact
tools.title: Get contact
tools.description: One contact by Evenium id or `ext:<customId>`: name, gender, email, company and fields. GET /contacts/{contactId}.

tools.name: evenium_get_contact_events
tools.title: Get contact events
tools.description: The events a contact is invited to, with the contact's registration (status, post status, category) in each. Filter by event start, end or creation date. GET /contacts/{contactId}/events.

tools.name: evenium_create_contact
tools.title: Create contact
tools.description: WRITE: add a contact to the address book (name, email, company, optional custom id and fields). Does not invite them to an event (use evenium_create_guest). May create a duplicate of an existing person: search with evenium_list_contacts first. POST /contacts.

tools.name: evenium_update_contact
tools.title: Update contact
tools.description: WRITE: change a contact's email, company or fields (only what you pass is sent). The change applies to the contact everywhere, including its guest records. PUT /contacts/{contactId}.

tools.name: evenium_list_event_parts
tools.title: List event sessions
tools.description: List the event parts (sessions, workshops, activities) of an event with title, dates, nature, code and location. Filter by title and start/end/update dates. GET /events/{eventId}/eventParts.

tools.name: evenium_get_event_part
tools.title: Get event session
tools.description: One event part (session) by id: title, dates, nature, code, location and fields. GET /events/{eventId}/eventParts/{eventPartId}.

tools.name: evenium_list_event_part_registrations
tools.title: List session registrations
tools.description: The registrations to one session: contact id, status, attendance, category and dates. With include_deleted, deleted registrations are returned too (status DELETED). GET /events/{eventId}/eventParts/{eventPartId}/registrations.

Does not count against the meter.

Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: GoFormz
servers.description: Read GoFormz templates, forms, groups and data sources; create and update forms and rows.

login.hint: In the GoFormz web app open **Settings**, then **API Access**. Copy the Client ID and the Client Secret (the secret is shown once; use Regenerate if you lost it). API access depends on your GoFormz plan and has a daily call quota; ask your GoFormz account manager if the API Access page is missing. They are used only to call the GoFormz API on your behalf; they are never shown to anyone.

tools.name: goformz_list_templates
tools.title: List templates
tools.description: List the form templates of the account (id, name). Use a template id to list its forms or to create a form. GET /v2/templates.

tools.name: goformz_get_template
tools.title: Get a template
tools.description: Get one template by id. GET /v2/templates/{id}.

tools.name: goformz_list_forms
tools.title: List forms
tools.description: List forms (filled-in instances of templates) with name, status (draft or complete), last update date and assignment. Field values are NOT included: call goformz_get_form for those. Filter by name prefix, status or last-updated date. GET /v2/formz.

tools.name: goformz_list_template_forms
tools.title: List forms of a template
tools.description: List the forms created from one template (name, status, last update date). Field values are not included. GET /v2/templates/{templateId}/formz.

tools.name: goformz_get_form
tools.title: Get a form
tools.description: Get one form with all its field values (text, numbers, dates, checkboxes, table rows, signature/image references), status, assignment and template version. GET /v2/formz/{id}.

tools.name: goformz_list_groups
tools.title: List groups
tools.description: List user groups (forms can be assigned to a group). GET /v2/groups.

tools.name: goformz_get_group
tools.title: Get a group
tools.description: Get one group by id. GET /v2/groups/{id}.

tools.name: goformz_list_users
tools.title: List users
tools.description: List the account's users (id, username, first and last name). A user id is needed to assign a new form. GET /v2/users.

tools.name: goformz_get_user
tools.title: Get a user
tools.description: Get one user by id. GET /v2/users/{id}.

tools.name: goformz_list_datasources
tools.title: List data sources
tools.description: List data sources (lookup tables that feed dropdown and database fields in templates). GET /v2/datasources.

tools.name: goformz_get_datasource
tools.title: Get a data source
tools.description: Get one data source: its name, columns and indexed columns. GET /v2/datasources/{id}.

tools.name: goformz_list_datasource_rows
tools.title: List data source rows
tools.description: List the rows of a data source. Each row has an id, a keyColumn (the lookup key) and a value (a JSON-encoded array of the column values). GET /v2/datasources/{dataSourceId}/rows.

tools.name: goformz_get_datasource_row
tools.title: Get a data source row
tools.description: Get one data source row by id. GET /v2/datasources/{dataSourceId}/rows/{rowId}.

tools.name: goformz_list_webhooks
tools.title: List webhooks
tools.description: List the webhooks that call a URL when a form of a template is completed (event form.complete). Read-only. GET /v2/webhooks.

tools.name: goformz_get_queue_item
tools.title: Get an async job status
tools.description: Check a queued job, for example the PDF export started by goformz_export_form_pdf. Returns status (and progressIndicator); when it is Completed, redirectUrl points at the result (a /v2/files/{id} URL: pass that id to goformz_get_file). GET /v2/queue/{id}.

tools.name: goformz_get_file
tools.title: Get a file
tools.description: Get a file summary: type, created date and a temporary download `link` (it expires; see linkExpiration). Use it for an exported PDF or a form image/signature. The file itself is not downloaded here. GET /v2/files/{id}.

tools.name: goformz_get_pdf_export
tools.title: Get a PDF export
tools.description: Get the metadata of a PDF export of a form, including the temporary download `link` once the PDF is ready. GET /v2/formz/{formId}/exports/{exportId}.

tools.name: goformz_export_form_pdf
tools.title: Export a form to PDF
tools.description: WRITE: start a PDF export of a form (the form is not changed; GoFormz creates a PDF file). The reply gives the queue_id of the job: poll goformz_get_queue_item until Completed, then read the file with goformz_get_file using the id in redirectUrl. POST /v2/formz/{formId}/exports.

tools.name: goformz_create_form
tools.title: Create a form
tools.description: WRITE: create a new draft form from a template, optionally pre-filled and assigned to a user or group (assignment is only possible at creation). Field keys are the template's field names (or ids) and the values are field objects such as {"text": "Acme"}; see goformz_get_form on an existing form of the template for each field's shape. Each call creates another form. POST /v2/formz.

tools.name: goformz_update_form
tools.title: Update a form
tools.description: WRITE: change a form's name and/or field values (partial update: only the fields given change; a null value clears a field). Does NOT change the status and does not trigger workflows; to re-run completion workflows use goformz_set_form_status draft, update, then complete. PATCH /v2/formz/{id}.

tools.name: goformz_set_form_status
tools.title: Complete or re-open a form
tools.description: WRITE: mark a form complete (this can trigger the template's completion workflows and webhooks) or re-open it as a draft so it can be edited. POST /v2/formz/{id}/status.

tools.name: goformz_create_datasource_row
tools.title: Add a data source row
tools.description: WRITE: add a row to a data source. key_column is the lookup key; values are the column values in the data source's column order (see goformz_get_datasource). Each call adds another row. POST /v2/datasources/{dataSourceId}/rows.

tools.name: goformz_update_datasource_row
tools.title: Update a data source row
tools.description: WRITE: replace a data source row's key and values (the whole row is replaced; send every column). PATCH /v2/datasources/{dataSourceId}/rows/{rowId}.

tools.name: goformz_usage_status
tools.title: Usage status (free-tier meter)
tools.description: Report the caller's current usage: the plan, calls used this month, the limit of the plan (the free monthly cap or the Pro fair use limit), remaining, and whether the limit is reached. Read-only; does not count against the meter.

tools.name: goformz_request_feature
tools.title: Request a missing feature
tools.description: Tell usefulapi that the user needs something the GoFormz tools cannot do yet (a missing tool, field or filter). Call it only when the user asks for something none of the tools can do, and tell the user that you send the request. Do not call it for errors or for normal requests. Do not include personal data, credentials or customer records. Stored with the product name and the client type (for example Claude or Cursor), without the user's account. At most 5 requests per day. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: goformz_upgrade
tools.title: Upgrade to Pro (unlimited*)
tools.description: Get Pro: unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month) on GoFormz (the free tier caps monthly usage). Plans: "monthly" — $9/month; "yearly" — $90/year (2 months free). Cancel any time: Pro then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. *A fair use limit applies. For heavy use (near Pro's limit): "plus" or "plus_yearly" — Pro+, $39/month or $390/year, unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 100,000 a month); an existing Pro subscription changes to Pro+ in place (needs confirm: true; the price difference for the rest of the period is charged at once). Otherwise returns a short link to open in your browser (it opens Stripe Checkout); after payment the account upgrades automatically. Does not count against the meter.

tools.name: goformz_cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel the Pro subscription
tools.description: Cancel the caller's GoFormz Pro subscription at the end of the paid period (no refund for the current period; Pro continues until then, then the free tier applies). Requires confirm: true. Run goformz_upgrade later to undo the cancel before the period ends. Does not count against the meter.

servers.name: FastBill
servers.description: Read FastBill customers, invoices, estimates, expenses; create customers, invoices, projects.

login.hint: Find the API key in FastBill under **Einstellungen (Settings) → Integrationen / API**. The e-mail address is the one you log in to FastBill with. FastBill limits API calls per hour by plan (Solo 50, Solo-Plus 100, Pro 500, Premium 1000), so every tool call counts against it. Your key is used only to call the FastBill API on your behalf; it is never shown to anyone.

tools.name: fastbill_list_customers
tools.title: List customers
tools.description: List customers (name, address, e-mail, VAT id, payment terms and bank details as stored in FastBill). Filter by search term (organization, name, address, zip, e-mail or tags), customer number, country or city. customer.get.

tools.name: fastbill_get_customer
tools.title: Get customer
tools.description: One customer by FastBill customer id. customer.get with CUSTOMER_ID.

tools.name: fastbill_list_contacts
tools.title: List contacts
tools.description: List contact persons of customers (name, position, e-mail, phone). Filter by customer, search term or contact id. contact.get.

tools.name: fastbill_list_invoices
tools.title: List invoices
tools.description: List outgoing invoices, drafts and credit notes with totals, state (draft, unpaid, overdue, paid, canceled), dates and line items. Filter by customer, number, type, date ranges (invoice date, due date, paid date, last update). invoice.get.

tools.name: fastbill_get_invoice
tools.title: Get invoice
tools.description: One invoice by FastBill invoice id, with all line items, VAT, payments and the document URL. invoice.get with INVOICE_ID.

tools.name: fastbill_list_recurring_invoices
tools.title: List recurring invoices
tools.description: List recurring invoice templates (customer, interval data, totals, items). recurring.get.

tools.name: fastbill_list_estimates
tools.title: List estimates
tools.description: List estimates (quotes) with state (a created, b sent, c negotiation, d accepted, e rejected, f invoiced), totals and items. estimate.get.

tools.name: fastbill_list_expenses
tools.title: List expenses
tools.description: List expense entries (supplier, category, net/VAT/gross, dates, document URL). Filter by invoice number or date ranges. expense.get.

tools.name: fastbill_list_revenues
tools.title: List revenues
tools.description: List revenue entries (income booked in FastBill: customer, totals, dates, payments). Takes the same filters as invoices. revenue.get.

tools.name: fastbill_list_articles
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products and services (article number, type, title, unit price, VAT, unit). article.get.

tools.name: fastbill_list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List projects (name, customer, hourly rate, VAT, start/end date). project.get.

tools.name: fastbill_list_time_entries
tools.title: List time entries
tools.description: List work time entries (customer, project, date, minutes, billable minutes, comment, invoice). Without filters FastBill returns the latest entries of the current month. time.get.

tools.name: fastbill_list_templates
tools.title: List document templates
tools.description: List the invoice/estimate templates (template id, name, hash). Use a template id with the create tools. Ids change whenever a template is edited. template.get.

tools.name: fastbill_create_customer
tools.title: Create customer
tools.description: WRITE: create a customer. customer_type is required; a business needs organization, a consumer needs last_name. Bank details are not accepted by this tool. FastBill does not check for duplicates, so search with fastbill_list_customers first. customer.create.

tools.name: fastbill_update_customer
tools.title: Update customer
tools.description: WRITE: update fields of an existing customer; only the fields you pass change. Bank details are not accepted by this tool. customer.update.

tools.name: fastbill_create_invoice
tools.title: Create invoice
tools.description: WRITE: create an invoice for a customer from line items. FastBill stores it as a draft; it gets its number and becomes final only with fastbill_complete_invoice, and it is never sent by this tool. Check the result with fastbill_get_invoice. invoice.create.

tools.name: fastbill_complete_invoice
tools.title: Finalize invoice
tools.description: WRITE, NOT REVERSIBLE: turn a draft invoice into a final invoice. FastBill assigns the invoice number and PDF; a final invoice can no longer be edited (it can only be canceled in FastBill). Nothing is sent to the customer. Only call this after the user confirmed the draft. invoice.complete.

tools.name: fastbill_set_invoice_paid
tools.title: Mark invoice paid
tools.description: WRITE: mark a final invoice as paid, with the payment date and method. invoice.setpaid.

tools.name: fastbill_create_estimate
tools.title: Create estimate
tools.description: WRITE: create an estimate (quote) for a customer from line items. It is not sent. estimate.create.

tools.name: fastbill_create_article
tools.title: Create product
tools.description: WRITE: create a product or service (article number, title and unit price are required). article.create.

tools.name: fastbill_create_project
tools.title: Create project
tools.description: WRITE: create a project for a customer (name and customer are required). project.create.

tools.name: fastbill_create_time_entry
tools.title: Create time entry
tools.description: WRITE: book a work time entry on a project (customer, project and start time are required). time.create.
